subject: A conforming implementation
notes: Rule: §4.2.10 'Nonstandard extensions are language elements or functionality in an implementation that consist of any of the following: 1) documented language elements not defined in this Working Draft International Standard;' (cite.py --check 4.2.10 'documented language elements not defined in this Working Draft International Standard' -> OK §4.2.10 1)). The class is definitional, but its obligations - 'Documentation associated with an implementation shall identify nonstandard extensions for which support is claimed' and 'An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate use of a nonstandard extension' (both cite.py OK §4.2.10 3), the catalog attaches them to GR-4.2.10-3) - are what make a class-1 element a CONFORMING extension, and neither holds. MEASURED on pinned 0caa7d5: probe/ext1.cob (PIC S9(5) COMP-3, PIC S9(5) COMP-5, COMP-2 - usages ISO defines at no edition) compiles and runs with ZERO diagnostics at --std 85 and --std 2023; `cobol --help` offers no extension-flagging option (only --permissive, which moves REMOVED ISO constructs, and --sign-encoding); the >>FLAG-02/-14 pass (FlagConformancePass) flags ISO migration items, not extensions; grep of src for a nonstandard-extension warning finds none. DOCUMENTATION: docs/CONFORMANCE.md names the vendor words only as RESERVED WORDS (D-RW1: CHANNEL, COMP-1..5, COMPUTATIONAL-1..5, END-INVOKE, ... pinned by CobolWordsDriftTests) and COMP-4 only as a synonym inside DOC-A.1-208; no section identifies which nonstandard extensions are CLAIMED (e.g. COMP-1/-2/-3/-5, END-INVOKE per PB758, order-free OPTIONS per PB1508, COLLATING-less SORT/MERGE per PB1139, qualifier/subscript interleaving per PB1455). Other extensions ARE refused by name (ENTRY and INSPECT ... TRAILING draw COBOLNET2269 - probe/ext2.cob, ext1 variant), which is conforming for those. Harm: silent - a user asking for portability has no way to learn that COMP-3 is not ISO. NEW mechanism finding 'no-4.2.10-extension-warning-or-register' (findings.json); the per-construct notes PB1139/PB1455/PB1508/PB755/PB756/PB758 each cite §4.2.10 for their own shape but none owns the absent mechanism. || Owning note: kb/Work/PB1525.

subject: Floating indicators
notes: kb/Work PB1493: Rule: 'a space is implied immediately following a floating comment indicator' (cite.py --check 6.2.3.2 OK). The lexer's COMMENT_START '*>' pushes COMMENT_MODE and skips to end of line regardless of what follows (CobolLexer.g4 lines 188, 1157-1160); fixed-form StripInlineComment truncates the source area at the first '*>' outside a literal. Probe p10_inline_ok (--std 2023): `MOVE "ABC" *>comment "unterminated` / `TO X. *>x` compiles and DISPLAYs [ABC         ] - the comment-text begins directly after '*>' with no written space, and an apostrophe/quote in it does not open a literal. No spec-derived test cites the rule (the legacy SpecFixTests InlineComment_* are the legacy engine's tests, not COBOL.NET's). Sibling observed (NOT this rule): '*>' is also accepted at --std 85 (probe n22_inline_85) where the floating comment indicator does not exist - see the edition-gate finding. Probes: E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\floating-indicators\p10_inline_ok || REFUTED: PARTIAL — SR1 governs every stage that analyzes compilation-group text. The lexer (COMMENT_START) and the fixed-form StripInlineComment do honor it: '*>' followed directly by text behaves exactly as '*> text' (probes r1-r4, r6-r8: '*>>SOURCE FORMAT FIXED', '*>COPY NOSUCHBOOK.', '*>REPLACE ==MOVE== BY ==DISPLAY==.', '*>*>"', and '*>' after a >>DISPLAY directive are all commentary). The compiler-directing-statement scanner (CopyProcessor, which parses REPLACE and COPY operands) is a text-analysis stage that does not recognize a floating comment indicator at all. 'REPLACE ==AAA== *>junk BY ==BBB==.' is rejected with COBOLNET1641 in free form (r5a) and in fixed form (r5f); the '*> junk' and '*> ==junk' spellings are rejected the same way (r5c, r5b). SR2 permits the inline comment there, because it is written where a separator space may be. The implied-space half is verified in the lexer stage but is not honored in the directing-statement stage, so the verdict is PARTIAL. The defect sits in comment recognition inside the REPLACE/COPY scanner, which is also the concern of §6.2.3.2 SR2 and should be filed against that scanner. No spec-derived test cites the rule. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (floating indicators are a COBOL-2002 introduction: §6.2.3.1 defines them for both reference formats, 1985 had only the §6.2.2 fixed indicators; Annex E, the 2014->2023 delta, lists no change to them)

subject: Floating indicators
notes: kb/Work PB1493: Rule: 'All the characters forming a multiple-character floating indicator shall be specified on the same line' (cite.py --check 6.2.3.2 OK). The '"-' split (n13) is rejected, but only by the generic COBOL0001 unexpected '-' that every floating continuation gets, so that half is not an enforcement of this rule. The '>>' indicator half was not separately constructed (a directive must begin its line). subject: Fixed-form reference format
notes:
kb/Work PB1493: Rule (§6.3.4 1): "Comment-text of a comment line when the indicator area contains a fixed comment indicator." cite.py --check 6.3.4 "Comment-text of a comment line when the indicator area contains a fixed comment indicator" -> OK §6.3.4 1). Code: ConvertFixedToFree's `case '*' or '/'` rewrites the line's program-text area (cols 8-72) as a `*> ...` floating comment, so the text is never tokenized, and it resets the cross-line literal scanner so quotation symbols in the comment-text cannot affect later lines. Probe ffp12 (a '*' line and a '/' line whose comment-text contains unbalanced ' and " characters, followed by DISPLAY "OK") compiles and prints OK. Out of scope for this row but found at the same dispatch: the switch ALSO turns lines whose column 7 holds S/Y/P/J/H/E/U (and D, which is no longer a fixed indicator in the 2023 §6.2.2 table) into comment lines. Those are not fixed comment indicators; see the SR-6.3.4-2 finding on the indicator dispatch. The comment-line behavior inside a continued literal is broken (ffp1), but that break belongs to §6.3.5 and is recorded under SR-6.3.5-1 and SR-6.3.5-2. No spec-derived test covers the '/' form. l1_margin_r_program_text_area uses '*' comment lines only incidentally, and its derivation is §6.3.1 margin R, so the test-ref is left empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The reference-format arm does turn a '*'/'/' line into a '*>' floating comment, but the comment-text still changes the compile: when a fixed comment line sits between PIC/PICTURE and its character-string, the lexer's PICMODE has no comment rule. Its PIC_STRING token ( ~[ 	
.] ... )+ takes '*>' as the picture string, and the rest of the comment line (or the real X(4) on the next line) is then misparsed. §6.3.7.2 says 'A comment line may be written as any line of a compilation group', and §6.3.7.1 says comments 'have no effect on the meaning of the compilation group'. A fixed comment line inside a REPLACE statement between its pseudo-text operands is rejected as well. Also, a comment line whose sequence area holds letters (e.g. 'ABCDE1*  text') makes auto-detection classify the whole file as free-form, and the '*' is then tokenized. The implied space before a non-continued line holds: ffp11 `DISPLAY "A"` then `"B".` prints AB. (4) UNDER-REJECTS. A mismatched resume quote is accepted: ffp6 ("ABCDE continued by 'FGH") runs and prints [ABCDE ... FGH]. notes: kb/Work PB1491: 'If the line is a comment line or a blank line, that line is logically discarded.' (--check OK §6.5 2)). ConvertFixedToFree does not discard: it rewrites a comment line as '*> text' (line 556) and a blank line as an empty output line, then RESETS inLiteral/pendingQuote (lines 505-506, 557-558). The lexer skips both, so in isolation the effect is 'as though discarded'. But §6.3.5 says 'Comment lines and blank lines may be interspersed among lines containing the parts of a literal' (--check OK §6.3.5) and 'the next line that is not a comment line or a blank line is the continuation line' — and the following '-' line's HandleContinuation joins onto the LAST OUTPUT LINE, i.e. onto the '*>' comment text (swallowing the continuation into a comment) or the blank, with the literal state already cleared. subject: Reference format
notes: kb/Work PB1491: 'If the line contains an inline comment, the inline comment is replaced by spaces and processing of that line continues.' (--check OK §6.5 3)). Fixed form: StripInlineComment truncates the program-text area at a '*>' outside any literal (doubled quotes tracked) BEFORE the cross-line literal scan, so a quote inside the comment cannot disturb continuation; free form: the lexer's COMMENT_START '*>' -> COMMENT_MODE skips to end of line, and a '*>' inside a literal is inside STRINGLIT by maximal munch. Probe rf11.cob: `01 X PIC X(3) VALUE "*>A". *> inline "quote` -> [*>A] (literal kept, comment with a stray quote dropped). Truncation vs replacement-by-spaces is equivalent for the tokens. No spec-derived golden isolates the rule. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — Step 3 applies to EVERY line, and §6.3.7.3 permits an inline comment on any fixed-form line (the only exception is a line carrying a floating literal continuation indicator). ReferenceFormatProcessor.ConvertFixedToFree calls StripInlineComment only in the default (normal-line) arm; the col-7 '-' arm hands the raw sourceArea to HandleContinuation, which appends it with the '*>' text intact. When that continuation line is itself continued, the next continuation's content is appended AFTER the unstripped comment on the same logical line and the lexer's COMMENT_MODE swallows it. A legal program is rejected. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002/2014/2023 (the floating comment indicator is a 2002 introduction — absent from 2023 Annex E, present at 2014)

subject: Text manipulation elements
notes: kb/Work PB1350 (registrar 15a). Rule: "a separator, except for: a space; a pseudo-text delimiter; and the opening and closing delimiters ... In determining which character sequences form text-words, the colon, the right parenthesis, and the left parenthesis characters, in any context except within alphanumeric or national literals, are treated as separators" (cite.py --check 7.2.2.5 -> OK §7.2.2.5 1)). The separator set is §8.3.5: comma/semicolon 'immediately followed by a space' (--check 8.3.5 -> OK 2)), period 'when followed by a space' (--check 8.3.5 -> OK 3)), parentheses, colon. Code: TokenizeTextWords makes '(' and ')' standalone words (correct; probe tw4 control: REPLACE ==WA== BY ==WC== hits WA(1:5), output [ABCDE ]B) but (a) the COLON is NOT a separator at all: 'WA(1:5)' tokenizes as '(' '1:5' ')'; and (b) period/comma/semicolon are classified by 'not followed by a DIGIT' instead of 'followed by a space', so a picture string ZZ.ZZ or Z,ZZ9 is split into several text-words (and the comma inside it is even dropped as a space-equivalent separator). Probe tw1 (all editions incl. --std 85): REPLACE ==5== BY ==2==. ... MOVE WA(1:5) TO WB, WA='ABCDEF' -> observed [ABCDE ]; spec: the text-word 5 is matched and replaced -> WA(1:2) -> expected [AB    ]. Probe tw2: REPLACE ==ZZ== BY ==99==. 01 WA PIC ZZ.ZZ. MOVE 5 -> observed [05.00]; spec: ZZ.ZZ is ONE text-word, no match -> expected [ 5.00]. The comma/semicolon-as-space treatment for MATCHING is §7.2.3.4 GR9 c) 1 and is right for a real separator comma; the defect is the classification. No register note owns this (searched kb/Work for TokenizeTextWords/pseudo-text). Finding F1. || editions (adjudicator): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (text manipulation / COPY-REPLACE text-words exist in every edition; boolean and national literal delimiters from 2002)

subject: Text manipulation elements
notes: kb/Work PB1350 (registrar 15a). Rule: "an alphanumeric, boolean, or national literal including the opening and closing delimiters that bound the literal" (cite.py --check 7.2.2.5 -> OK §7.2.2.5 2)). Opening delimiters per §8.3.5 5): a quotation symbol, B" B' N" N' X" X', BX" BX' NX" NX' (--check 8.3.5 -> OK 5)). Code: the literal arm of TokenizeTextWords starts only at a bare quote/apostrophe and ends at the FIRST matching quote. (a) A prefixed literal splits: the ordinary-word loop stops at the quote, so X"41" is two words 'X' + '"41"', N"PQ" is 'N' + '"PQ"' (same for B, BX, NX). (b) A doubled quote inside the content ends the literal early: "P""Q" becomes '"P"' + '"Q"'. Probe tw3 (--std 2002/2014/2023): REPLACE =="41"== BY =="42"== =="PQ"== BY =="RS"== =="Q"== BY =="Z"==. DISPLAY X"41" / N"PQ" / "P""Q" -> observed [B] [RS] [P"Z]; spec: none of the three literal text-words equals any pseudo-text-1 -> expected [A] [PQ] [P"Q]. Probe tw5 --std 85: REPLACE =="Q"== BY =="Z"==. DISPLAY "P""Q" -> observed [P"Z], expected [P"Q]. The plain "..." and '...' arm without doubled quotes is correct (tw5 'Q"' unchanged). subject: Text manipulation elements
notes: kb/Work PB1350 (registrar 15a). Rule has two halves (cite.py --check 7.2.2.5 "bounded by separators" -> OK §7.2.2.5 3); --check 7.2.2.5 "The implementor may prohibit the use of one or more characters from outside the COBOL character repertoire" -> OK 3)). subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1369 (registrar 15a). Rule: 'The implementor shall define and document any rules restricting the precision and/or magnitude and/or range of permissible values for the intermediate results ... They shall also document which intermediate rounding method is used, if applicable' (--check 7.3.6.2 -> OK §7.3.6.2 2)). Precision/magnitude half: documented (28-29 digits, ~7.9E28) and enforced loudly -- 99999999999999999999999999 * 99999 -> COBOLNET1547 'exceeds the .NET decimal evaluation range ... §7.3.6.2 SR2' (unit Rejects_OverRangeSoleLiteral covers the sole-literal leg). Rounding half: DOCUMENTED WRONG. CONFORMANCE.md says 'division truncates toward the decimal precision'; System.Decimal division rounds the final digit (round-half-even), so CONSTANT AS 2 / 3 * 3 = 2 and 100 / 7 * 7 = 100 where the documented truncation yields 1 and 99 (probe p1.cob). subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: Rule: 'The order of precedence and the rules for evaluation of compile-time arithmetic expressions are shown in 8.8.1' (cite.py --check 7.3.6.3 -> OK §7.3.6.3 1)). Precedence is carried by the shared arithmeticExpression grammar spine (additive > multiplicative > power > unary > primary); EvalArith folds each additive/multiplicative level LEFT TO RIGHT (§8.8.1.2 3) --check OK). Intermediates are not truncated (only the final result, at EvaluateArithmeticOperand). Probed with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/ctae/p1.cob, p2.cob, --std 2002/2014/2023): CONSTANT AS 2 + 3 * 4 = 14; 10 - 3 - 2 = 5; 12 / 2 * 3 = 18; (1 + 2) * 3 = 9; - 2 * - 3 = 6; 5 - 10 / 4 = 2 (2.5 untruncated intermediate); 7 / 2 + 0.5 = 4 (3.5 + 0.5, intermediate not truncated); >>IF 10 - 3 - 2 = 5 AND 12 / 2 * 3 = 18 selects; identical across editions. The unit Theory pins 2+3*4=14 and (2+3)*4-6/2=17 (spec-derived); the same-level left-to-right case has no test (probe only). || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (compile-time arithmetic in DEFINE/EVALUATE/IF directives and constant entries; not 1985)

subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1369 (registrar 15a). Rule: 'The implementor shall define and document which mode of arithmetic is to be used when evaluating compile-time arithmetic' (--check 7.3.6.3 -> OK §7.3.6.3 2)). The code uses .NET System.Decimal (a mode 'unique for processing compile-time arithmetic expressions', which GR2 permits). The documentation exists (docs/CONFORMANCE.md) but is INACCURATE in three ways: (1) it calls the mode 'a standard fixed-point decimal mode ... chosen over the native binary runtime mode for portability (§7.3.6.3 GR2 NOTE)' -- the NOTE's 'standard modes of arithmetic' are standard-binary / standard-decimal (§8.8.1.5.3 --check OK: standard-decimal operations 'are performed as specified in ISO/IEC 60559:2020', decimal128, 34 digits); System.Decimal (96-bit, 28-29 digits, its own rounding) is neither, so the portability claim is false; (2) it states 'division truncates toward the decimal precision', but System.Decimal division ROUNDS the last digit: probe p1.cob CONSTANT AS 2 / 3 * 3 -> 2 and 100 / 7 * 7 -> 100 (truncating division as documented gives 1 and 99), same for >>DEFINE V3 AS 2 / 3 * 3 (>>IF V3 = 2 selects); (3) it names the evaluator 'DataBinder.Constants.cs EvalConstExpr' (no longer exists; the evaluator is CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator) and says 'today a multi-token directive operand binds only its first token -- a recorded Wave-D GAP', which is false (probe p2.cob: >>DEFINE V1 AS 7 / 2 evaluates to 3). A required documentation statement that does not describe the implemented mode does not satisfy 'define and document'. Separate edition note: E.2 6) says the previous standard required a specific mode; the compiler evaluates identically at --std 2014 (probe p2 at 2002/2014/2023), and VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 12 carries that gate as <!-- todo --> -- not this row's verdict, recorded as a dossier gap. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 (Annex E.2 6): the mode 'is now explicitly implementor defined'; earlier editions required a specific mode) || code-location detail: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Expressions/CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.cs#EvalArith; docs/CONFORMANCE.md (Compile-time arithmetic mode determination)

subject: Compile-time arithmetic expressions
notes: Rule: 'The final result of the arithmetic expression shall be truncated to the integer part of the value as specified in 15.49, INTEGER-PART function, and the resultant value shall be considered to be an integer numeric literal' (--check 7.3.6.3 -> OK §7.3.6.3 3)). EvaluateArithmeticOperand applies decimal.Truncate (toward zero = INTEGER-PART) to an expression's final result only, and emits the integer text as the literal; a SINGLE numeric literal is reclassified (§13.10.3 SR1 / §7.3.11.4 GR5) and keeps its value. Probes: CONSTANT AS 7 / 2 -> 3, -7 / 2 -> -3 (toward zero, not floor), 1.5 + 1 -> 2, 0.9 + 0 -> 0; >>DEFINE V2 AS -7 / 2 then >>IF V2 = -3 selects; >>DEFINE V4 AS 1.5 keeps 1.5 (literal) while >>IF V4 + 0 = 1 selects; >>EVALUATE 9 / 4 >>WHEN 2 selects. subject: Compile-time boolean expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1370 (registrar 15a). Rule (cite.py --check 7.3.7.2 OK, SR1): 'Compile-time boolean expressions shall be formed in accordance with 8.8.2, Boolean expressions, except that all operands shall be boolean literals or boolean expressions in which all operands are boolean literals.' The operand-restriction half CONFORMS: BooleanLeaf admits only BOOLLIT (B""/BX"" both decode; probe N5 BX"C" B-OR B"0001" = 1101) and a previously-defined BOOLEAN compilation variable (justified by §7.3.11.4 GR1 'in any compiler directive where a literal of the category associated with the name is permitted', --check OK; probe N6). Rejected with COBOLNET1619 (probes n2,n3,n4,n7,n9,n10,n14,n15): alphanumeric "1", ZERO, numeric 1, ALL B"1" (§7.3.3 SR10), N"1", X"01", an alphanumeric compilation variable, an undefined name; Table 4 (B-NOT,B-NOT) rejected (n8); dangling operator / unbalanced paren rejected (n11,n12). Cause: compileTimeOperand enters booleanExpression only under boolExprAhead(), which needs a B-operator token; with none, the '(B"101")' falls to arithmeticExpression/nonNumericLiteral and fails. (B"1100") B-OR B"0001" works (q1 T-OK). (b) UNDER-REJECTS the shift count — §8.8.2 rule 5 'The second operand shall be an integer operand' (--check OK) and §5.5 2)a) 'if that operand is a literal, it shall be an integer literal' (--check OK); Table 4 row B-SHIFT-* permits only 'Identifier or literal' next, never '(' (§8.8.2 rule 6 --check OK). '>>DEFINE X AS B"1100" B-SHIFT-L 1 + 1', '... B-SHIFT-L 2 * 1' and '... B-SHIFT-L (1)' all compile clean (n5, n20, n6): BooleanShift evaluates suf.arithmeticExpression() through EvaluateDirectiveArithmetic, the grammar's self-described 'permissive-superset' booleanShiftSuffix, with no screen restoring the integer-operand/Table-4 constraint. (A numeric compilation variable as the count, n13, is legal via §7.3.11.4 GR1.) (c) UNDER-REJECTS by edition — at --std 2002 and --std 2014 '>>DEFINE G AS B"1100" B-SHIFT-L 1' and '>>IF B"1100" B-SHIFT-L 1 = B"1000"' compile clean (q3, r3) while the runtime twin 'COMPUTE B1 = B1 B-SHIFT-L 1' at 2014 is COBOLNET0900 (r1). BooleanExpressionGateSiteDriftTests.Exempt exempts compileTimeOperand/cceRelationOrBoolean from the VersionConformancePass gate on a REACHABILITY reason ('the walk never reaches it'), not a spec reason, and nothing in the frontend directive path substitutes the gate. subject: Compile-time boolean expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1370 (registrar 15a). Rule (cite.py --check 7.3.7.3 OK, GR1): 'The order of precedence and the rules for evaluation of compile-time boolean expressions are shown in 8.8.2, Boolean expressions.' EvaluateBoolean folds through the ONE shared BooleanExpressionResolver (same grouping the runtime binder uses, incl. §8.8.2 rule 7b context-inherited shift precedence) over BitString, whose Combine right-zero-extends the shorter operand to the larger length (rules 9/10, --check 8.8.2 'the shorter operand were extended on the right by a sufficient number of boolean zeros' OK), Not preserves length, Shift preserves the first operand's length with zero-fill/rotate (rule 8). Verified by compile-and-run probes with spec-derived expectations (E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2\out\probe\ctbool\p1.cob, q1.cob — all OK): B-NOT B"1100"=0011; (1100 B-AND 0101)=0100; 1100 B-OR 0101 B-AND 0011 = 1101 (B-AND before B-OR, rule 7b); 1100 B-XOR 0110 B-OR 0001 = 1011 (B-XOR before B-OR); 1100 B-SHIFT-R 1 B-OR 0001 = 0111 (unpreceded shift has B-AND precedence, --check 8.8.2 7)b) OK); B"10" B-OR B"0001"=1001 (right extension); 1100 B-SHIFT-L 1 B-SHIFT-R 2 = 0010 (left-to-right, rule 7c); a substituted boolean variable B-AND B-NOT literal; boolean relation and simple boolean condition in >>IF, and a boolean >>EVALUATE subject. Shift count ≥ length / circular periodicity / zero-length handled (unit tests Boolean_Shift, Boolean_HugeShiftCount_NoCrash). No existing test covers the full rule-7b precedence ladder (B-NOT > B-AND > B-XOR > B-OR) for compile-time expressions: CompileTimeBooleanCceTests.Boolean_BinaryAndUnary/Boolean_Shift (Annex A Table A.2 values) and Boolean_ContextInheritedShiftPrecedence cover single operations and the shift-precedence case only, and conformance:2002/directive_expressions exercises one B-OR — so test-ref is left empty (test-needed). Formation defects (parenthesized sole literal, shift-count form, edition gate) are the SR-7.3.7.2-1 row's, not evaluation. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — §8.8.2 rule 7b gives a boolean shift the precedence of the PRECEDING OPERATION, and B-NOT is an operation in that ladder (1st, negation). The shared BooleanExpressionResolver tracks prevPrec only from BINARY operators: a B-NOT is folded inside the factor and never updates prevPrec. So in `A B-AND B-NOT B B-SHIFT-R 1` the shift wrongly takes B-AND precedence and its operand becomes (A B-AND B-NOT B). The spec requires A B-AND ((B-NOT B) B-SHIFT-R 1). Probes confirm the wrong value. The precedence ladder, the right-extension, Not, Combine and Shift semantics otherwise hold (adjudicator's probes plus re-reading BitString). The defect sits in the ONE shared resolver, so the runtime COMPUTE format-2 boolean binder almost certainly carries the same bug (a sibling). || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (shift evaluation 2023 only, §E.2 item 3)

subject: CALL-CONVENTION directive
notes: Rule: "The default for the CALL-CONVENTION directive is '>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL'." (cite.py: OK §7.3.9.3 1)). The compiler holds no call-convention state (DirectiveStateRegistry row: 'every name is processed under the §7.3.9.3 GR1 default (COBOL)'), so with no directive every CALL/CANCEL/program-address/INVOKE name is processed under the COBOL mapping. Probe probe/callconv/A.cob (no directive): CALL "ccsubA" and CALL "CCSUBA" both reach PROGRAM-ID CCSUBA -> 'IN SUB' twice at 2023; same at --std 2002 (B.cob). The explicit '>>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL' (B.cob) is indistinguishable, as GR1 requires. --std 85 rejects the directive with COBOLNET0900 (facility introduced 2002). No spec-derived test asserts the default mapping (tests/conformance/2002/pb725_directive_facility.cob only proves the directive compiles and says 'no call convention varies here'), so test-ref empty. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility; absent in COBOL-85)

subject: CALL-CONVENTION directive
notes: kb/Work PB1383 (registrar 15a). Two halves. (a) 'When COBOL is specified, that program-name or method-name is treated as a COBOL word that maps to the externalized name ... applying the same implementor-defined mapping rules as for a method-name or program-name for which no AS phrase is specified' (cite.py OK §7.3.9.3 2) a)). VERIFIED by probe under >>CALL-CONVENTION COBOL / default: CALL "ccsubg" (lower case) reaches PROGRAM-ID CCSUBG; CANCEL "ccsubg" resets it (IN SUB 1, 2, then 1 after CANCEL); SET PP TO ADDRESS OF PROGRAM "ccsubg" + CALL PP reaches it (G.cob); INVOKE U "hello-m" through a universal OBJECT REFERENCE reaches METHOD-ID HELLO-M (H.cob) -- the case-insensitive no-AS mapping in every construct GR2 lists. The mapping itself is undocumented (A.1 item 68 'Externalized names (formation and mapping rules). This item is required. This item shall be documented', cite.py OK §A.1 68)) -- kb/Work PB661 (open) already owns that documentation debt. (b) 'When call-convention-name-1 is specified, that program-name or method-name is treated as a literal that maps ... in a manner defined by the implementor' (cite.py OK §7.3.9.3 2) b)), and §8.3.2.3.2 'A call-convention-name identifies an implementor-defined convention for mapping a method-name or a program-name to its externalized name' (cite.py OK). COBOL.NET defines NO call-convention-name, yet the operand screen admits ANY COBOL word (ConstructRegistry DirectiveOperand UserWord=true) and the directive has no state: probe C.cob '>>CALL-CONVENTION XYZZY' compiles clean and CALL "ccsubC" still reaches CCSUBC by the case-insensitive COBOL-word mapping -- the name identifies no convention, the program-name is not treated as a literal, and no diagnostic says so. Silent acceptance of an undefined system-name (under-rejects). Half (a) conforms, half (b) diverges -> DIVERGES. Remedy is partly owner latitude (define conventions following GnuCOBOL per the CLAUDE.md rule-1 precedence, or reject every non-COBOL name as undefined); at minimum an undefined call-convention-name must be diagnosed. See finding 'call-convention-name-1 accepted with no defined convention'. The CONFORMANCE.md recognized-and-ignored entry states the single-convention choice but not that an arbitrary name is accepted as COBOL.

subject: CALL-CONVENTION directive
notes: Rule: 'The CALL-CONVENTION directive may also be used by the implementor to determine other details needed to interact with a function, method, or program.' (cite.py OK §7.3.9.3 3)). Permissive ('may'): it grants the implementor latitude and imposes no obligation. COBOL.NET uses no call-convention to select linkage details (single .NET managed calling convention, docs/CONFORMANCE.md recognized-and-ignored directives entry; DirectiveStateRegistry 'NONE HELD'). Declining an optional latitude conforms. Nothing observable to test.

subject: DEFINE directive
notes: kb/Work PB1367 (registrar 15a). cite.py --check 7.3.11.3 "the last previous DEFINE directive referring to compilation-variable-name-1 shall have specified the same value" -> OK SR2. OFF removes the name (so bullet 1 'not declared' and bullet 2 'last previous was OFF' coincide), AssignDefine reports COBOLNET1618 when !OVERRIDE and the stored value differs by category-aware equality. Probes: n4 (1 then 2 -> 1618), q11 (1/1/1.0 accepted; 'A' then 'A ' -> 1618, length-sensitive), t7/q7 (after OFF, redefine accepted), q5 (after an OVERRIDE to 2, a plain '1' -> 1618: the LAST previous value governs), t9 (name case-insensitive), r2 (PARAMETER value differing without OVERRIDE -> 1618). Interpretive edge noted, not a defect: a PARAMETER DEFINE whose environment supplies no value undefines silently and a later plain DEFINE is accepted (u1.cob) - SR2 does not say what value a value-less PARAMETER 'specified'. Also covered by unit:ConditionalCompilationDefineTests.Redefine_SameValue_NoOverride_Accepted / Redefine_AfterOff_Accepted. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — SR2 has three admitting bullets; the implementation checks only a stored-value comparison, and a value-less PARAMETER DEFINE bypasses it entirely. After >>DEFINE PX AS 1, a no-OVERRIDE >>DEFINE PX AS PARAMETER with PX unset in the environment silently removes the name (ApplyDefine: 'if (env is null) { defines.Remove(name); return; }', no AssignDefine call), and a following no-OVERRIDE >>DEFINE PX AS 2 is then accepted as if PX had never been declared. Neither DEFINE meets any SR2 bullet: PX WAS declared previously, the last previous DEFINE was not OFF, and it did not specify the same value (1 vs no value; no value vs 2). The value 1 -> 2 change without OVERRIDE, which SR2 exists to forbid, compiles silently. The adjudicator named this edge and called it interpretive. That leaves the edge unverified, not verified. The ordinary branches hold: 1 then 2 -> 1618; after OFF a redefine is accepted; the last value governs; a program in the same compilation group inherits the value (g1: a DEFINE in program 2 differing from program 1 -> 1618); a DEFINE in an omitted >>IF branch does not count (s1). || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 - §7.3 compiler-directive facility; ISO/IEC 1989:2023 Annex E lists no change to §7.3.11 against 2014 (the 2002 introduction is not stated in the 2023 text itself; below 2002 the directive is COBOLNET0900)

subject: FLAG-14 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1375 (registrar 15a). cite.py --check 7.3.15.4 'If ON is explicitly...' OK (GR1 text read from the clause). The warning mechanism exists: COBOLNET1621 (Warning, never fails the compile), one per flagged construct, and each message names the option and the 2014-to-2023 change with its GR4 sub-rule and Annex E.2 item. Two emitters, one message shape: FlagConformancePass for the bound options, and ConditionalCompilationProcessor.DirectiveDiag.FlagWarn for b/c. It is documented in docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md, which covers Annex B item 80 'shall be documented'. Probes IO/IO2/MX/BZ/GB show the mechanism firing for every one of b-m. Whether each option's COVERAGE is complete is GR4's question, and that rule is DIVERGES. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR1 has two halves: PROVIDE a warning mechanism, and have it FLAG the 2014-to-2023 incompatibilities for the selected option. The first half holds: COBOLNET1621 is a Warning with per-option messages from two emitters in one shape, it is documented, and it is gated per option. The second half does not hold. For options that are selected and ON, the mechanism misses incompatibilities that GR4 names. Numeric-edited items made so by BLANK WHEN ZERO (13.18.8.4 GR2) escape g and l, the constant entry escapes b, EVALUATE-subject FILE STATUS tests escape e and f, and a WRITE with only NOT AT END-OF-PAGE escapes m. It also over-flags d on ACCESS SEQUENTIAL relative/indexed files. The adjudicator split 'the mechanism exists' (GR1 CONFORMS) from 'coverage' (GR4 DIVERGES). But GR1's own text says the mechanism 'flags the incompatibilities ... for the selected option', so a coverage gap is a GR1 gap too. A rule with two halves where only one is verified is PARTIAL. Selection is also incomplete: the implicit-ON and implicit-ALL forms ('>>FLAG-14 VALUE-ZERO', '>>FLAG-14 ALL', '>>FLAG-14 OFF') are rejected with COBOLNET1622 (FMT-7.3.15.2 DIVERGES), so some legal ways to select an option cannot reach the mechanism at all. The test-ref Compile_Flag14ReadPreviousOn_EmitsCobolnet1621 pins only one working branch (h) and asserts only that the code appears.

subject: FLAG-14 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1374 (registrar 15a). cite.py --check 7.3.15.4 'If ON is explicitly or implicitly specified for an option' OK. EXPLICIT ON works: FlagState.IsOnAt folds the last toggle strictly before the site line, so ON applies to the text that follows. ON is sticky until end of the group, until an ALL OFF (Fold_AllOff_ResetsAPreviouslyEnabledOption; probe FH '>>FLAG-14 VALUE-ZERO ON' then '>>FLAG-14 ALL OFF' -> no warning), or until that option's own OFF (probe FG: ALL ON then VALUE-ZERO OFF -> VALUE-ZERO silent, while NUM-ED-ZERO-FIGCONST and VALUE-EDITING still flag). The frontend-inline FlagScanState mirrors the fold for b/c, applies only in emitting branches, and joins PUSH/POP. IMPLICIT ON (the word omitted, 5.2.6.3 default) is rejected with COBOLNET1622 by FlagDirectiveLine.TryParse (probes FA/FB/FD). That half of the rule is unreachable, which is the FMT-7.3.15.2 mechanism.

notes: kb/Work PB1375 (registrar 15a). All twelve options (a-m) have a detector. Verified correct by probes: a ALL fan-out; c >>EVALUATE with WHEN + WHEN OTHER (MX:16); h READ PREVIOUS (IO:39); i ref-mod only while >>REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH is unspecified and EC-BOUND-REF-MOD is on (MX:26, and not after an explicit ON at MX:29); k figurative constant VALUE on a length-less item (BZ:8, BZ:10); m WRITE without END-OF-PAGE on a LINAGE file (IO:46, and not on a non-LINAGE file IO:47); e/f relation and level-88 forms (IO:48-51,53, IO2:36); g/l/j on a PICTURE-numeric-edited item. DEFECTS, each checked with cite.py: (1) b misses the constant entry. cite.py --check 7.3.6.1 'A compile-time arithmetic expression may be specified in the DEFINE and EVALUATE directives, in a constant conditional expression, and in a constant entry' OK, and --check 13.10.3 'Arithmetic-expression-1 shall be formed in accordance with 7.3.6' OK. Probe GB: '01 K1 CONSTANT AS 5 * 2.' under COMPILE-TIME-ARITHMETIC-EXPRESSIONS ON -> no warning, while the >>DEFINE on the line above IS flagged. (2) d over-flags statements that CANNOT be written with INVALID KEY. --check 14.9.10.3 'The INVALID KEY and the NOT INVALID KEY phrases shall not be specified for a DELETE RECORD statement that references a file that is in sequential access mode' OK; --check 14.9.35.3 'Neither the INVALID KEY phrase nor the NOT INVALID KEY phrase shall be specified for a REWRITE statement that references a file with sequential organization or a file with relative organization and sequential access mode' OK. Probe IO2: REWRITE on a RELATIVE ACCESS SEQUENTIAL file (32), DELETE RL (33) and DELETE on an INDEXED ACCESS SEQUENTIAL file (34) are all flagged, because IsKeyed tests organization only and ignores access mode. (3) e/f miss tests that are not a two-operand relation: 'EVALUATE FS WHEN "04"' (IO:52) and 'EVALUATE FS WHEN "07"' (IO2:37) are not flagged, and neither is the abbreviated combined relation 'IF FS = "00" OR "04"' (IO2:35). (4) g/l/j miss numeric-edited items made so by BLANK WHEN ZERO. --check 13.18.8.4 'If the subject of the entry is described by its picture character-string as category numeric, the BLANK WHEN ZERO clause defines the item as numeric-edited' OK. Probe BZ: '01 X PIC 999 BLANK WHEN ZERO VALUE ZERO.' raises no g/l warning, and '01 Y PIC 999 BLANK WHEN ZERO VALUE 12.' raises no j warning, because IsNumericEditedPicture classifies the PICTURE string alone. (5) m misses a WRITE carrying only NOT AT END-OF-PAGE (MX:25), yet 14.9.51.3 SR19 names the END-OF-PAGE and NOT END-OF-PAGE phrases separately. notes: SR6 (cite.py --check 7.3.16.3 OK): 'Text-1 and text-2 may be any kind of source lines, including compiler directives. Text-1 and text-2 may consist of multiple lines.' Render treats every non-directive line as text (block/omitted) and every directive line in a branch through the same switch with ParentActive frames. Probes: p08 nested >>IF/>>ELSE/>>END-IF and a >>DEFINE inside text-1 (N-TT, Z5 correct); p20 non-COBOL garbage, a missing-copybook COPY and >>SOURCE FORMAT FREE in the omitted text-1, and >>TURN + a multi-line DISPLAY in text-2 -> compiles, prints OK1 OK2. The pb1006 golden derives its expected output from §7.2.1 Step 1 and §7.3.16.4 GR2/GR3 with a directive in the false path. || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref EMPTY. The implementation conforms, but pb1006_source_format_in_false_path does not pin SR6: it pins §7.2.1 Step 1 (SOURCE FORMAT processed in the false path) and §7.3.16.4 GR2/GR3, and every text-1/text-2 in it is a single line, so the 'Text-1 and text-2 may consist of multiple lines' half is never exercised. A golden with multi-line texts carrying nested directives (IF, EVALUATE, DEFINE) in both branches would close the row. — Behaviour conforms and survived attack. Probe t2 put a nested >>EVALUATE, a nested IF/ELSE/END-IF and a >>DEFINE in an omitted multi-line text-1, and a nested EVALUATE with WHEN OTHER, >>PAGE, >>DEFINE, a nested IF and a two-line DISPLAY in an included text-2. The false path also tolerated an unterminated literal, an invalid column-7 indicator, a continued literal and an incomplete COPY REPLACING (u1-u4). The refutation is the test-ref only. subject: LEAP-SECOND directive
notes: kb/Work PB1378 (registrar 15a). Rule: 'The LEAP-SECOND directive shall not be specified within a compilation unit.' (cite.py --check 7.3.17.3 OK). The rejecting half CONFORMS: a directive after PROGRAM-ID (probe g_seq.cob, and the negative golden) draws COBOLNET1650. But Process() sets insideUnit=true at the FIRST unit start and never clears it, so a directive written AFTER 'END PROGRAM X.' and before the next unit's IDENTIFICATION DIVISION - not within any compilation unit - is also rejected (probe b_between.cob: two sibling programs, '>>LEAP-SECOND ON' between END PROGRAM LSB1 and the second IDENTIFICATION DIVISION -> 'error COBOLNET1650 ... write it before the first IDENTIFICATION DIVISION of the compilation group'). That message states the COBOL-WORDS rule (§7.3.10.3 SR1 'only before the first IDENTIFICATION DIVISION within a compilation group'), not this one. §7.3.3 SR8 ('A compiler directive may be specified anywhere in a compilation group' except as its own rules restrict) and §7.3.4 GR5 ('A compiler directive applies to all of the source text and library text that follows') make the between-units directive legal and effective for the following unit; the single group-wide bool (BindSession.LeapSecond) cannot represent that. A directive after the last statement of a unit with NO end marker (probe f_endofunit.cob) is textually inside the unit and is correctly rejected. Finding: leap-second-between-units. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 directive facility is absent in 1985; the 2002 edge is DERIVED per docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.21 - Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and does not list LEAP-SECOND, so it predates 2023). The time-form / formatted-time consumers the rule bounds are COBOL-2014 intrinsics (§15.3).

subject: POP directive
notes: kb/Work PB1377 (registrar 15a). Rule: 'If directive-name is specified, the POP directive shall not be specified where directive-name must not be specified.' (cite.py --check 7.3.20.3 -> OK §7.3.20.3 2)). Placement-ruled directives a POP can name: LEAP-SECOND ('shall not be specified within a compilation unit', §7.3.17.3 SR1, --check OK), PROPAGATE ('shall not be specified within a compilation unit', §7.3.21.3 SR1, --check OK), COBOL-WORDS ('may be specified only before the first IDENTIFICATION DIVISION within a compilation group', §7.3.10.3 SR1, --check OK), and TURN (§7.3.25.3 SR5, exception PERFORM - subsumed by §7.3.20.3 SR4, which bans every POP there). Search: no code consults the NAMED directive's placement rule for a POP - DirectiveSiteProcessor records only DirectiveSite(Line, Word, AllForm) and its PositionRuled set {TURN, PUSH, POP} serves the exception-PERFORM ban; PushPopAllPlacementPass handles the ALL form (SR3) only; COBOLNET1650 (LEAP-SECOND) and COBOLNET1623 (COBOL-WORDS) are keyed on their own directive lines, never on a POP naming them. Probes (probe/popdir): p1.cob `>>PUSH LEAP-SECOND` / `>>POP LEAP-SECOND` in the PROCEDURE DIVISION -> compiles clean, runs (A B), while p2.cob `>>LEAP-SECOND ON` at the same place -> COBOLNET1650 error; p5.cob `>>POP PROPAGATE` and `>>POP COBOL-WORDS` inside the procedure division -> clean, while p7.cob `>>COBOL-WORDS` there -> COBOLNET1623. subject: POP directive
notes: kb/Work/PB1005 (2026-09-22): >>POP ALL outside a compilation unit (before the first, or after an END marker) or inside a clause or statement (not at a boundary of a nested one) draws the 4.2.2 warning COBOLNET2344; the directive is still processed (the D20 disposition of the sibling SR4 bans). subject: PROPAGATE directive
notes: kb/Work PB1119 (registrar 15a). Rule: 'When the ON phrase is specified or implied, automatic propagation of exception conditions becomes enabled for functions, methods, and programs that follow in the compilation group ...' (cite.py --check 7.3.21.4 -> OK §7.3.21.4 1)). Code: PropagateDirectiveProcessor.Process only recognizes the line and blanks it (lines[i] = ""); its own doc says 'a well-formed >>PROPAGATE ON is recognized-and-edition-gated but does not yet change EC behavior', and DirectiveStateRegistry declares 'NONE HELD: ... its propagation effect (§7.3.21.4) is not implemented, so no PROPAGATE state exists yet'. No ON/OFF state is computed or carried to the binder/emitter. Probe gr2t.cob (2023): caller PRPMAI3 with >>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING ON and USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-SIZE, CALLs PRPSU3 which is preceded by >>PROPAGATE ON and does ADD 5 TO N (PIC 9 VALUE 9) under EC-SIZE checking with no SIZE ERROR phrase. Expected (§7.3.21.4 GR1+GR2, §14.6.13.1.3 GR6): the fatal EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION is propagated as though GOBACK RAISING LAST, the applicable statement in the caller is the CALL, the caller's declarative runs and displays 'CALLER CAUGHT EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION'. Observed: 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION (fatal)' inside the subprogram — identical to the >>PROPAGATE OFF and no-directive runs. No register note owns the runtime half (PB407/PB794 landed, other halves). Finding: PROPAGATE-RUNTIME-NOT-IMPLEMENTED. || editions (adjudicator): COBOL-2002, 2014, 2023 (§7.3.21 is live in the 2023 text; Annex E.2/E.3 list no 2023 introduction or removal, so it predates 2023; not in COBOL-85 — the §7.3 compiler-directive facility) || code-location detail: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/PropagateDirectiveProcessor.cs#PropagateDirectiveProcessor.Process; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/DirectiveStateRegistry.cs#Entries(PropagateDirective2002)

subject: PROPAGATE directive
notes: kb/Work PB1119 (registrar 15a). Rule: '... any exception condition raised and not handled by either an exception phrase or exception processing procedures in that runtime element shall be propagated as though a GOBACK RAISING LAST statement were executed in a declarative for that exception condition.' (cite.py --check 7.3.21.4 -> OK §7.3.21.4 2)); corroborated by §14.6.13.1.3 GR6 (cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.3 'there is an applicable PROPAGATE ON directive, the exception condition is propagated as if a GOBACK statement with the RAISING LAST EXCEPTION phrase were executed' -> OK). The GOBACK RAISING LAST machinery and the CALL-site propagation pickup exist (CallEmitter), but nothing routes an UNHANDLED condition into it: the fatal-EC default path still terminates the run unit ('14.6.13.1.3 #5/#7') regardless of the directive, because the directive stage holds no state. Probe gr2t.cob as in GR-7.3.21.4-1: expected 'CALLER CAUGHT EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION' from the caller's declarative; observed abnormal run-unit termination in the callee. The nonfatal-EC leg (an unhandled nonfatal condition propagating instead of continuing) is equally absent. Finding: PROPAGATE-RUNTIME-NOT-IMPLEMENTED. || editions (adjudicator): COBOL-2002, 2014, 2023 (§7.3.21 is live in the 2023 text; Annex E.2/E.3 list no 2023 introduction or removal, so it predates 2023; not in COBOL-85 — the §7.3 compiler-directive facility)

subject: PUSH directive
notes: kb/Work PB1377 (registrar 15a). Rule (cite.py --check 7.3.22.3 'Directive-name shall be the name of a compiler directive other than an EVALUATE, IF, PAGE, POP, or PUSH directive.' -> OK §7.3.22.3 1)). Code: the push-directive-2023 row's operand is {Words, Choice=[ALL], DirectiveName=true, ExcludedDirectives=[EVALUATE,IF,PAGE,POP,PUSH]}; CompilerDirectiveCatalog.OperandDirectiveNames admits every catalog Word minus the excluded ROWS (so WHEN/END-EVALUATE/ELSE/END-IF go with their rows). Probed with the pinned cobol.exe at --std 2023 (probe/push-directive/A*.cob): >>PUSH EVALUATE / IF / PAGE / POP / PUSH / WHEN / ELSE / END-IF / END-EVALUATE / FOO / IMP / (no operand) -> COBOLNET1911 citing SR1 (correct); >>PUSH TURN / SOURCE / FLAG-02 / DISPLAY / LISTING / turn (lower case) -> clean (correct). DEFECT: >>PUSH FLAG-85 and >>PUSH FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC compile clean at 2023 (A10, A21 print OK), although both directives were REMOVED in 2023 (cite.py --check E.2 'The following features that were classified as obsolete in the previous COBOL standard, have been removed' -> OK §E.2 21), listing FLAG-85 and FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC) and the compiler itself rejects >>FLAG-85 ON at 2023 with COBOLNET0902 (probe C1). A word naming no 2023 compiler directive is therefore not 'the name of a compiler directive'; OperandDirectiveNames draws from CompilerDirectiveCatalog.Words, which is the edition-INDEPENDENT catalog map, so the two removed-window rows (flag-85-directive-window, flag-native-arithmetic-directive-window, removed 2023) stay admissible and even appear in COBOLNET1911's admissible-name list. Expected (spec): at --std 2023 >>PUSH FLAG-85 is a syntax-rule violation (diagnostic), exactly like >>PUSH FOO. Since PUSH exists only in 2023 the removed rows can never be legal PUSH operands. Edge note: >>PUSH SOURCE FORMAT is rejected as 'more than one operand' — defensible, since directive-name is a single user-defined word (cite.py --check 8.3.2.2.7 'A directive-name identifies a compiler directive whose setting is saved or restored' -> OK) and SOURCE is the directive's word; not reported. OFF written after that line but before the PROCEDURE DIVISION header is ignored. Same mechanism the adjudicator found for GR6 (b), but it was not carried to the OFF sibling. subject: Character sets
notes: kb/Work PB547 (registrar 15b). Rule: "The number of bytes used in the memory of the computer to represent characters in the alphanumeric coded character set shall be the same for all characters in that coded character set; the number of bytes shall be determined at compile time." (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 1)). The byte count IS fixed at compile time (PicInfo.ByteWidth = 1 per DISPLAY position, DOC-A.1-209), but the SET it applies to is not bounded by it: the compiler admits any UTF-16 code unit into an alphanumeric item (DOC-A.1-33/188 declare the alphanumeric repertoire UTF-16) while every byte image carries one byte per position, so a character above U+00FF has no representation of that size. Three different losses measured at the pinned compiler: (a) mixed-usage REDEFINES codec - probe cs1/p2.cob: MOVE "€ABC" TO A1 (PIC X(4)), round trip through a REDEFINES PIC N(2) view, A1 reads back "¬ABC" and compares DIFF; p1.cob shows N1 decoded as U+AC41 U+4243 - CobolBits.NatReadWindow computes (char)((image[hi] << 8) | ...) which drops the code unit's high byte (U+20AC -> 0xAC) silently; (b) the sequential file channel substitutes '?' silently (open kb/Work PB690, PB547); (c) CONVERT ANUM->BYTE substitutes '?' and raises EC-DATA-CONVERSION (the documented disposition). One alphanumeric character, three byte images - the set is not represented in a uniform number of bytes. The file/'?' arm is owned by open kb/Work PB547 (analysis, inventory_rows GR-13.18.60.4-7) and PB690; the REDEFINES low-byte-truncation arm is new (see finding). Expected per spec: either the alphanumeric coded character set is restricted to what one byte represents (a character above U+00FF refused/diagnosed where it enters an alphanumeric item) or the alphanumeric size is widened so every member survives every storage image unchanged. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the alphanumeric/national coded-character-set split and these fixed-size rules arrive with ISO/IEC 1989:2002; 1985 has no national class)

subject: Character sets
notes: Rule: "The number of bytes used in the memory of the computer to represent characters in the national coded character set shall be the same for all characters in that coded character set; the number of bytes shall be determined at compile time." (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 2)). National = one UTF-16 code unit per position, BytesPerNational = 2 (a compile-time const, D-N1); every code unit U+0000-U+FFFF has a total 2-byte UTF-16BE image (PutNat/NatReadWindow are exact inverses for national content). NOTE 3 ("COBOL processes each fixed-size element of a character set as one character", --check OK) edge probed - cs1/p3.cob: LENGTH(N"😀€")=3 BYTE-LENGTH=6 (the surrogate pair is two positions), PIC N(4) BYTE-LENGTH 8; N"€A" in a PIC N(2) redefined as X(4) reads bytes 0x20 0xAC 0x00 0x41 (ORD 33 173 1 66) - uniform, lossless. No spec-derived test pins this rule; test-needed. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (national class introduced in ISO/IEC 1989:2002)

subject: Character sets
notes: kb/Work PB1397 (registrar 15b). Rule sentence 1: "The number of bytes used to represent a character of the national coded character set shall be equal to or greater than the number of bytes used to represent a character of the alphanumeric coded character set." (cite.py --check 8.1.2 -> OK §8.1.2 3)). National 2 >= alphanumeric 1 - holds; pinned by the golden l1_usage_display_character_size (LEQN line compares BYTE-LENGTH of X(1) and N(1)). The row text also carries the trailing implementor obligations: (i) hex literals not converted - probe cs1/p3.cob MOVE X"C1FF" gives ORD 194/256, raw bytes; compile-time = runtime set (UTF-16) so no literal conversion arises (A.1 item 34 conditional, not triggered) - OK; (ii) single SPACE/ZERO values - ' ' and '0' are the one value throughout, OK by reading; (iii) bits per byte (A.1 item 12) = 8, documented only in prose inside the USAGE BIT determination and BitLayout.cs, no DOC-A.1-12 row; (iv) "The implementor shall specify one and only one alphanumeric coded character value associated with each of the following COBOL elements" (--check OK) - A.1 item 32, required + documented - NOT documented anywhere in docs/ (no coded-character-value statement for SPACE/QUOTE/ZERO/editing characters, alphanumeric or national); (v) "the implementor shall specify any such additional characters that are prohibited from use as a currency symbol" (--check OK) - A.1 item 44, required + documented - ValidateCurrencyChar enforces only the §12.3.7.3 SR22/SR27 set (so the implementor-additional set is empty), and that choice is documented nowhere. Documentation halves (iv)/(v) missing => PARTIAL. The premise 'the alphanumeric character is 1 byte' is itself undermined by GR-8.1.2-1's divergence (PB547).

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: kb/Work PB1397 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'The implementor shall define a mapping of each basic letter, basic digit, basic special character, and extended letter of the COBOL character repertoire to one or more coded character sets.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 1)). What the code does: every source and copybook file is read by CompilationInputs.ReadAllText = File.ReadAllText(path) -- .NET BOM detection (UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32), defaulting to UTF-8, decoded into the one UTF-16 in-memory set (the D-N1 substrate). The mapping realized is 'one coded character set containing all characters' (ISO/IEC 10646), so the two-distinct-sets correspondence sentence is vacuous. HALF 1 (a mapping exists) holds for basic letters/digits/special characters. HALF 2 fails twice: (a) the mapping is DEFINED only in code -- docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no row for A.1 item 25 ('COBOL character repertoire (encoding of, mapping of, substitute graphics). This item is required. This item shall be documented', cite.py --check A.1 -> OK A.1 25)); grep of CONFORMANCE.md for source encoding / UTF-8 source / BOM finds nothing (DOC-A.1-25 is the separate catalog row carrying that documentation debt); (b) the rule names EXTENDED LETTERS in the mapping, and the lexer NAME_BODY admits only [a-z0-9_-], so no extended letter maps to a word character (see GR-8.1.3.2-4). Probe out/probe/repertoire/rlat1.cob: a Latin-1 byte 0xE9 inside a literal compiles clean and DISPLAYs EF BF BD (U+FFFD) -- the undocumented UTF-8 default silently replaces a non-UTF-8 byte, exactly what an A.1 item 25 determination must tell the user. No spec-derived test pins the mapping. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to 8.1.3.2 itself; E.2 items 4 and 14 change only the Annex B and Annex C tables 2014->2023)

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: kb/Work PB1397 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'If more than one encoding is permitted in a single compilation group, the implementor shall specify the control functions or other methods used for distinguishing between encodings.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 2)). Sentence 1 (mixed alphanumeric/national coded character sets) is VACUOUS: the repertoire maps to one set (UTF-16 in memory), so there is no shift mechanism to specify -- verified by reading ReadAllText. Sentence 2 IS live: each file (the source, and each copybook via CopyProcessor ~line 430 calling _inputs.ReadAllText independently) is decoded by its own BOM, so more than one encoding is permitted in one compilation group. Probe out/probe/repertoire/rmix.cob (UTF-8, no BOM) COPYing RCPY.cpy written UTF-16LE with BOM: compiles and runs, DISPLAY prints the e-acute correctly. The distinguishing method (per-file byte-order mark; absent a BOM, UTF-8) is nowhere specified in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (A.1 item 26, conditionally required on exactly this support). Sentence 3 (control functions are not part of the syntax) holds: the BOM is consumed by the decoder before the lexer. Mechanism present, specification absent -> PARTIAL. Same documentation mechanism as GR-8.1.3.2-1. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change)

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: kb/Work PB1402 (registrar 15b). Rule a): 'COBOL basic letters, when specified in the non-hexadecimal formats of alphanumeric and national literals, are treated in a case-sensitive manner, unless specific rules require otherwise. COBOL basic letters appearing elsewhere within the compilation group are treated in a case-insensitive manner.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 3) a)). Code: the lexer is caseInsensitive=true; STR_BODY/NAT_BODY capture literal text verbatim; binder name tables compare with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase (63 sites under Binding/). Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): rcase.cob -- data-name declared Abc-Def, referenced aBC-dEF / abc-def / ABC-DEF: one item; MOVE "xY z" displays 'xY z' and IF = "XY Z" takes ELSE (literal case kept); rcase2.cob -- mixed-case paragraph-name PERFORM/GO TO, condition-name SET/IF, index-name, OF-qualified name, lowercase verbs, FUNCTION upper-case all resolve; rlit.cob -- N"aB" and an accented alphanumeric literal keep their case. Half a) VERIFIED. Half b): basic letters/digits/special characters in the alphanumeric set are equivalent to the national ones -- vacuously true on the single UTF-16 set (NOTE 1); basic-letter folding per Annex C is the identity A-Z -> a-z that OrdinalIgnoreCase realizes. The EXTENDED-letter leg of b) cannot be verified because extended letters do not lex at all (GR-8.1.3.2-4 finding) -> two halves, one verified -> PARTIAL. Note for the fixer: OrdinalIgnoreCase is invariant UPPER-casing, not Annex C lower-folding; identical on basic letters, not on extended ones (e.g. U+0130, U+212A), and it is spread over 63 call sites rather than one folding function. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E.2 item 14 / E.3.3 item 6 change only the Annex C table 2014->2023)

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: kb/Work PB1402 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'The set of extended letters consists of characters from the repertoire specified in Annex B ... a) A character in Annex B is included in the set of extended letters if it exists in the implementor-defined compile-time coded character set.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 4) a)); b) uppercase extended letters fold to lowercase per Annex C; c) combining characters count separately toward word length (--check OK 8.1.3.2 4) c)). NOTE 3 makes extended letters optional, BUT docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.4.6 'Extended letters' is **Claimed** (A.4.6 item 1 = 'Extended letters in the COBOL character repertoire (8.1.3)', --check A.4.6 OK) and 8.3.2.1 requires word characters from 'the set of basic letters, basic digits, extended letters, and the basic special characters hyphen and underscore' (--check 8.3.2.1 OK). The compile-time coded character set is UTF-16 (ReadAllText), so every Annex B character exists in it and is an extended letter by a). The lexer: NAME_BODY = [0-9]+ [-_] [a-z0-9] NAME_TAIL? | [0-9]+ [a-z] NAME_TAIL? | [a-z] NAME_TAIL?, NAME_TAIL = [a-z0-9_-]* [a-z0-9] -- no extended letter anywhere. Probes (pinned cobol.exe --std 2023): rext.cob '01 CAF<E-acute> PIC X(3) VALUE "abc".' + 'DISPLAY caf<e-acute>.' -> 'error COBOL0001: cannot parse construct near <E-acute>' + 'COBOL0307 unexpected <e-acute>'; rext2.cob '01 <A-umlaut>RGER ...' -> 'COBOL0307: unexpected <A-umlaut>'. Expected: both compile; rext DISPLAYs 'abc' (by b) the two spellings are one word). Legs b) and c) are unreachable behind the lexer. No kb/Work note owns this (searched kb/Work for 'extended letter', 'Annex B', 'A.4.6': PB661 owns only the 8.3.2.2 externalization determination). REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE under a Claimed optional module. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (extended letters; E.2 item 4 changes Annex B content 2014->2023 -- U+037A deleted, U+30FB barred as first/last character)

subject: COBOL character repertoire
notes: Rule: 'When an implementation does not provide a graphic representation of all characters of the COBOL character repertoire, substitute graphics may be specified by the implementor to replace the characters not represented.' (cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 -> OK 8.1.3.2 5)). A permission conditioned on a missing graphic. The source is decoded to UTF-16, which represents every Table 1 basic letter, digit and special character (all in ISO/IEC 646 IRV) and every Annex B character, so the antecedent is false and no substitute graphic is used or needed -- verified by reading ReadAllText and by the probes (rcase/rcase2 exercise the basic set incl. hyphen, quote, parentheses, period). No latitude exercised. Documenting 'substitute graphics: none' belongs to A.1 item 25 = DOC-A.1-25, the same missing CONFORMANCE.md row noted on GR-8.1.3.2-1; it does not make this permissive rule defective. CONFORMS-but-untested. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change)

subject: COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB301. The prohibition is on ACCEPTING: a word ISO 8.9 reserves at edition E is refused in a user-defined-word slot AND in a system-name slot at E, and admitted at the editions 8.9 leaves it free. The gate is DERIVED, not listed - gen-cobol-words.ps1 computes it from reserved-words.json and CobolWordsDriftTests re-computes it independently, asserting set equality in BOTH directions and across BOTH halves (cobolWord under {userWordHere(W)}? and reservedGatedWord under its inverse), so neither a missing nor a stray gate survives. Words 8.9 reserves that the lexer never tokenizes are caught by the same funnel by NAME (measured: 01 LOCALE PIC X. at --std 2023 draws COBOLNET0901), so the rule holds over the whole 8.9 list and not merely over the token set. The corpus lanes carry both slots the rule names: pb301-screen-words-reserved-from-2002 declares the six words 8.9 adds in 2002 in a data-name slot AND puts CRT in the 12.3.7 implementor-name slot, and its acceptance complement at COBOL-85 is conformance:85/pb301_screen_words_as_user_words; pb301-column-reserved-at-every-edition holds COLUMN, reserved at all four editions. subject: COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB656 (registrar 15b). Rule: `OK  §8.3.2.1 2)` "Compiler-directive words, except those that are also reserved words, may be used as user-defined words and system-names." The §8.12 list (`OK §8.12` "The following words are reserved in compiler directives") was split against tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json: 35 words §8.9 never reserves (CALL-CONVENTION, CHECKING, COBOL-WORDS, COMPILE-TIME-ARITHMETIC-EXPRESSIONS, DE-EDITING, DEFINE, DEFINED, EQUATE, EXTERNAL-FILE-FILE-STATUS, FIXED, FLAG-02/-14, FUNCTION-ARGUMENT, IMP, I-O-DECLARATIVE, I-O-STATUS-04/-07, LEAP-SECOND, LISTING, MOVE-TO-SAME-NAME, NUMVAL, PARAMETER, POP, PROPAGATE, PUSH, READ-PREVIOUS, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH, SUBSTITUTE, TURN, UNDEFINE, VALUE-EDITING, VALUE-FIG-CON-LENGTH, VALUE-ZERO, WRITE-END-OF-PAGE, ZERO-LENGTH) plus the directive-reserved exception-names EC-SIZE / EC-ALL / EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW. The main-program lexer gives none of them a token (directives are consumed by the preprocessor before the parser, CompilerDirectiveCatalog), so each reaches cobolWord as IDENTIFIER and the §8.9 funnel (VersionConformancePass.VisitCobolWord) passes it. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/cdw): cdw.cob declares all 38 as 01-level data-names and DISPLAYs each -> runs at 2023 printing 38 Y; cdw2.cob (the 35-char word dropped, which COBOLNET1567 correctly refuses below 2023 as a §8.3.2.1 length error, not this rule) runs identically at 85/2002/2014. cdw3.cob at 2014 and 2023 puts >>DEFINE DEFINE AS 5 and >>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING ON in the SAME compilation as 01 TURN, 01 DEFINE, 88 CHECKING, 01 PUSH, section UNDEFINE and paragraph POP -> prints 34Q / D5 / CK (the >>IF DEFINE = 5 compilation-variable and the data-name DEFINE coexist). System-name half: cdw4.cob SOURCE-COMPUTER. DEFINE. OBJECT-COMPUTER. PROPAGATE. (computer-name is a system-name, §8.3.2.3) compiles and runs at 85 and 2023. The EXCEPT half: B-AND (a §8.12 word §8.9 reserves from 2002) as a data-name -> COBOLNET0901 at 2014 and 2023, accepted at 85; XOR (§8.9-reserved at 2023 only per the reserved-word table) -> accepted at 85/2014, COBOLNET0901 at 2023. No spec-derived test names this rule (grep of tests/ for the sentence and for 'compiler-directive word' as a user word finds none), so test-ref is empty. (Only one COBOLNET0901 is printed per compilation — the reservation gate reports the first offending use, the PROCEDURE reference — which is a reporting choice, not this rule.) || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator's census of the section 8.12 words that section 8.9 does not reserve is wrong: it lists COBOL-WORDS, which appears in 8.9 only inside a NOTE, and it omits COBOL. COBOL is in the section 8.12 list and is absent from the 2023 section 8.9 list. At 2023, COBOL is accepted as a computer-name, a data-name and a section-name. At 2002 and 2014 the pinned compiler refuses it with COBOLNET0901 ('COBOL is a reserved word in COBOL-2002'). The claimed editions include 2002 and 2014, and the refusal rests on ReservedWords.Table.cs / reserved-words.json flags r2002=true and r2014=true. That row's own provenance string says '1985-reserved, removed post-85 (GnuCOBOL per-standard lists; absent from ISO 2023 section 8.9)', which contradicts those flags. Whether the refusal is correct at 2002 and 2014 therefore depends on edition data that the 2023 text cannot decide and that nobody has verified. That makes one edge unverified, so the verdict is PARTIAL. All the other arms held: 34 other non-reserved directive words and 4 more exception-names (EC-I-O, EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE, EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND, EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE) were accepted at 2002/2014/2023 as program-name, computer-name, mnemonic-name, condition-name (switch status), alphabet-name, class-name, symbolic-character, file-name, record-name, data-name, index-name, level-88 condition-name, section-name and paragraph-name. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (compiler directives and their §8.12 words exist from COBOL-2002; vacuous at 85, where the same words are ordinary user-defined words)

subject: COBOL words
notes: Rule: `OK  §8.3.2.1 4)` "A given word may be used as a system-name and as a user-defined word, subject to the rules specified in 8.3.2.2, User-defined words, and 8.3.2.3, System-names." System-names are held apart from user-defined words by construction: implementor names live in the ONE table ImplementorNames (a SPECIAL-NAMES entry's system-name position), computer-names are read by text in the configuration paragraphs, and none of them is entered into the data-name / procedure-name / mnemonic namespaces, so a data-name, paragraph-name or mnemonic-name spelled like a system-name never collides. PROBE (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/sysuser/su1.cob) at 85 and 2023: SOURCE-COMPUTER. MYBOX. + 01 MYBOX (computer-name = data-name), CONSOLE IS CONSOLE (device-name = its own mnemonic-name), SYSOUT IS OUTDEV + 01 SYSOUT (device-name = data-name), SWITCH-1 IS SW1 + 01 SWITCH-1 (switch-name = data-name), 01 C01 (feature-name = data-name), paragraph SYSERR (device-name = paragraph-name) -> compiles and prints MSWC / K at both editions (DISPLAY UPON OUTDEV and UPON CONSOLE route to the device, the data-names read their own values). The 'subject to 8.3.2.3' half: §8.3.2.3.1's one-type rule for device/feature/switch names holds by construction — ImplementorName carries exactly ONE SystemNameKind per name (ImplementorNamesDriftTests). The 'subject to 8.3.2.2' half defers to §8.3.2.2's own rows; its one-type-of-user-defined-word restriction is unenforced and owned by open kb/Work PB990 (rows SR-8.3.2.2-1/-2/-3), which concerns two USER-DEFINED types and not the system-name/user-word sharing this row permits. No spec-derived test names this row (the dossier's §8.3.2.1 test citations are all rule 1 / rule 3 / rule 5 / word length), so test-ref is empty. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the permission is unchanged across editions; the §8.3.2.3 system-name types it references grew — call-convention-name, entry-convention-name, external-locale-name — but the sharing permission applies to whichever types an edition has)

subject: COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB1228 (registrar 15b). Rule: `OK  §8.3.2.2 1)` "a compilation-variable-name may be the same as any other type of user-defined word" — the first exception to `OK §8.3.2.2` "Within a source element, a given user-defined word may be used as only one type of user-defined word with the following exceptions:". Compilation variables live only in the preprocessor's directive symbol table and are consumed before the parser sees the source element, so no source-element namespace ever meets them. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/onetype/cv.cob) at 2002 and 2023: >>DEFINE ZQ AS 1 / PQ AS 2 / FQ AS 3 beside 01 ZQ (data-name), paragraph PQ, ALPHABET FQ IS NATIVE, and >>IF ZQ = 1 AND PQ = 2 AND FQ = 3 selecting a DISPLAY of the data item ZQ -> prints `CV A` at both (the compilation variables evaluate and the same-spelled data-name reads its own value); out/probe/cdw/cdw3.cob likewise pairs >>DEFINE DEFINE with 01 DEFINE at 2014/2023. The sentence forbids nothing, so it has no rejecting edge to verify; the permission is the whole rule and holds. REGISTER: open kb/Work PB990 lists this row in inventory_rows because the one-type census it owes must encode these exceptions as data — the fixer must keep this permission when the census lands (a regression risk for PB990, not a current defect). No spec-derived test names the exception, so test-ref is empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — [SUPERSEDES the earlier line for this rule: citation corrected to 7.3.11.4 GR1] The permission lets a compilation-variable-name be the same word as any other user-defined word. A compilation-variable-name can be referenced in three places (section 7.3.11.4 GR1): compiler directives, defined conditions, and the constant entry's FROM phrase. Only the first two are consumed by the preprocessor. The adjudicator verified only those two. The FROM phrase is where the permission actually has to be resolved inside the source element: '01 J CONSTANT FROM CQ' beside '>>DEFINE CQ' AND '01 CQ CONSTANT AS ...' must take the compilation variable. The pinned compiler never gets that far, because every CONSTANT ... FROM compilation-variable-name is staged loud as not implemented (COBOLNET0899 in DataBinder.Constants.cs). So this rule's sharing arm in that context is unverifiable, and the rule has two halves of which only one is verified, which makes it PARTIAL. The root cause is section 13.10.4 GR1 staged loud; the fix belongs there, and this row would then need a re-probe. The directive and defined-condition arms do hold: >>IF ZQ = 7 AND PQ = 4 is true beside 01 ZQ and a paragraph named like PQ. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (compilation-variable-names and the >>DEFINE directive exist from COBOL-2002)

subject: COBOL words
notes: Rule: `OK  §8.3.2.2 2)` "a level-number may be the same as a paragraph-name or a section-name". PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/onetype): ex2.cob — paragraphs 01, 05 and 88 beside 01/05-level data, PERFORM 05 / PERFORM 88 -> `05 RAN 7` / `88 RAN` at 85 and 2023; ex2b.cob — `77 SECTION.`, paragraph `01.`, `05 SECTION.` containing paragraph `77.`, beside 77 N and 01 G / 05 X, with PERFORM 05 and GO TO 88 -> `05S 71` / `END` at 85 and 2023. The exception's complement (a level-number spelled like any OTHER type) is unreachable: every other type must contain a letter (§8.3.2.2) and an all-digit word lexes INTEGERLIT, so no other declaration slot can take it. REGISTER: open kb/Work PB990 lists this row in inventory_rows because its one-type census must carry this exception as data (keep it when the census lands). No spec-derived test names the exception; test-ref empty.

subject: Numeric literals
notes: kb/Work PB1445 (registrar 15c). "A literal shall not contain more than one sign character. If a sign is used, it shall appear as the leftmost character of the literal. If the literal is unsigned, the literal is nonnegative." (cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.2 -> OK §8.3.3.3.2 2)); a literal is "a character-string" (lead paragraph, --check OK) and a space is a separator (§8.3.5 1), --check OK), so a sign separated from its digits is not part of the literal. Three halves: (c) UNSIGNED => NONNEGATIVE holds (v1: IF 5 > -6, +0 = -0, 007 stores 7). (a) ONE sign and (b) LEFTMOST/adjacent are enforced only in two places -- SignedIntegerLiteral.Screen (the VALUE Format 2 FROM/TO subscript slot, COBOLNET2155) and SoleOperand.NumericLiteral/SignIsPartOfLiteral (EVALUATE/DEFINE/CONSTANT sole-operand classification). Everywhere else they are not: DIVERGES, two mechanisms. [M1] DataBinder.IsLiteralValueOperand strips ANY number of unary signs with `while (u?.unaryExpression() is { } signed) u = signed;` and never checks adjacency: `01 B PIC S9 VALUE - 5.` (u2), `VALUE +-5` (u1), `VALUE -+5` (u5), `VALUE ++5` (u6), `VALUE -`<newline>`5` (t4), and `88 C1 VALUE - 5` (u9) are all ACCEPTED silently and store -5/+5; `VALUE --5` (u3) passes bind and CRASHES the backend: 'error CS1059: The operand of an increment or decrement operator must be a variable' in the generated C#. Expected: each is refused -- VALUE Format 1 writes literal-1 (§13.18.63.2, --check OK 'IS literal-1') and none of these is a literal. [M2] every procedure-division `literal` slot parses `numericLiteral : signedNumericLiteral : (PLUS | MINUS)? numericLiteralCore` with the sign as a SEPARATE default-mode token and no adjacency screen (GetText() strips the whitespace): `MOVE - 5 TO A` (s2) stores -5.00, `ADD - 5 TO A` (s8) adds -5, `DISPLAY - 5` (u4) prints -5, `MOVE - .5 TO A` (s10) stores -0.50 -- all accepted at --std 85/2002/2014/2023. Correctly refused: MOVE +-5 / MOVE 5- (parse errors, s3/s9); `IF A = - 5` (s7) is legal (a relation operand is an arithmetic expression, so `- 5` is unary minus) and is accepted. Covering tests that exist pin only the screened slots (conformance:negative/pb553-value-subscript-sign-not-adjacent, conformance:negative/pb400-evaluate-signed-sole-literal-pair) and do not cover the diverging arms -> test-ref empty. No kb/Work note owns M1 or M2 (searched open/half notes for adjacency / IsLiteralValueOperand). [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the formation/value rules are unchanged across editions; only the digit ceiling moves: 18 at COBOL-85, 1 through 31 from 2002 per the clause's lead paragraph)]

subject: Numeric literals
notes: kb/Work PB1446 (registrar 15c). "A literal shall not contain more than one decimal point. The decimal point is treated as an assumed decimal point, and may appear anywhere within the literal except as the rightmost character." (cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.2 -> OK §8.3.3.3.2 3)). ONE POINT: DEC_BODY admits exactly one '.', so `MOVE 1.5.5 TO A` is refused (s4: COBOL0001 unexpected '.5'), `VALUE 1.2.3` refused (s6: COBOLNET1585, a literal list); DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA `PERFORM 2,0 TIMES` refused (i3). NOT RIGHTMOST: DEC_BODY requires a digit after the point, so `1.` followed by a space is a separator period -- `COMPUTE A = 1. + 2` refused (d1), `VALUE 1..` refused (d2). ANYWHERE ELSE, incl. LEFTMOST: `.5`, `-.5`, `+.123...` (30 fraction digits), `,5`/`+,5` under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA all accepted with the correct assumed-point value (v1, i4). ASSUMED POINT: the value is aligned by the point's position (TryUnscaledParts scale), verified by the stored images in v1/i4. Refusals are generic parse diagnostics, which the rule does not constrain. No dedicated golden -> test-ref empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The one-point and not-rightmost halves hold for both '.' and ',' (including `(1.)`, `1.+ 2`, `(1,)`). But the 'anywhere, including leftmost' half fails for the comma under DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA: the leftmost-comma literal `,5` is not kept as its own literal when a space and an integer come before it. The parser fuses `1 ,5` into an interior-point literal 1,5 (value 1.5), so a wrong answer is produced and illegal source is accepted. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the formation/value rules are unchanged across editions; only the digit ceiling moves: 18 at COBOL-85, 1 through 31 from 2002 per the clause's lead paragraph)]

notes: kb/Work PB1415 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'A figurative constant may be used whenever 'literal' appears in a format or when a rule allows it, with the following restrictions: a) If the literal is restricted to a numeric literal, the only figurative constant permitted is ZERO (ZEROS, ZEROES) without the ALL phrase. b) A figurative constant shall not be specified where a syntax rule prohibits it.' SR1 main clause / b) are whole-language admission rules (PB780 shape): sampled positions admit (STRING, INSPECT, EVALUATE, VALUE, PERFORM FROM ZERO) and STRING SR2's prohibition of ALL figuratives is enforced (p6.cob first run: COBOLNET1757); the unsampled remainder is covered by PB780's generated-check argument.
