subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB1093 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'At runtime, when referenced outside the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, the high-value format represents the character, or multiple-character combination, that has the highest ordinal position in the runtime collating sequence.' + 'If the context of the figurative constant requires national characters, the national program collating sequence is used' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.6.4 -> OK 6) both). The native alphanumeric and national sequences are 65,536 positions (D-N1/D-N3; DOC-A.1-188; CollatingTable.Repertoire = 0x10000; FUNCTION CHAR(20000) yields ordinal 20000), so the highest-ordinal character is U+FFFF. The code pins HIGH-VALUE to U+00FF: AlphabetDef.HighValue '?? (char)0xFF' for the native alphanumeric sequence; FillChar/Fill 'H' -> '\u00ff' for a national anchor with no national PCS; the literal-phrase CollatingTable computes the alphanumeric HighValue 'over the Latin-1 block' although §12.3.7.4 GR7 k3 puts every unspecified native character above the specified ones in native order; AlphabetFigurative (SPECIAL-NAMES, §12.3.7.4 GR10 native extreme) returns U+00FF for alphanumeric while returning U+FFFF for national. The design docs call it 'the flagged §8.3.3.6 GR6/GR7 divergence ... kept byte-stable' (COBOLNET_DESIGN §14 item 14; PHASE4_RECONCILIATION) — no owner decision or kb/Work note owns it. PROBES (probe/figurative-constant-values): p1.cob native: ORD(HIGH-VALUE in PIC X) = 256, ORD(HIGH-VALUE in PIC N) = 256, 'IF NX"4E00" > HIGH-VALUE' TRUE (expected FALSE), 'NA = NX"FFFF"' after MOVE HIGH-VALUE TO NA FALSE (expected TRUE); p2.cob: CHAR(20000) > HIGH-VALUE TRUE (expected FALSE); p3.cob PCS 'ALPHABET AL IS "B" "A" "C"': ORD(HIGH-VALUE)=256, CHAR(20000) > HIGH-VALUE TRUE (expected: HIGH-VALUE = U+FFFF, ordinal 65536, comparison FALSE); p7.cob 'CLASS HVC IS HIGH-VALUE': CHAR(65536) IS HVC FALSE, CHAR(256) IS HVC TRUE (expected the reverse, §12.3.7.4 GR10). CONFORMING ARMS: an explicit national PCS (p5.cob: HIGH-VALUE = NX"FFFF" under a literal-phrase national alphabet, NX"4E00" > HIGH-VALUE FALSE) and a LOCALE PCS (p4.cob: ORD(HIGH-VALUE)=63894, CHAR(20000) > HIGH-VALUE FALSE; determination L7). See finding 'HIGH-VALUE native U+00FF pin'. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the LC_COLLATE sentence and the national-sequence sentence from 2002)

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: kb/Work PB1414 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'At runtime, when referenced outside the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, the low-value format represents the character, or multiple-character combination, that has the lowest ordinal position in the runtime collating sequence.' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.6.4 -> OK 7)). U+0000 IS the lowest position of both 65,536-position native sequences, so the native pin is correct here (unlike GR6); a literal-phrase sequence takes its first-specified lowest character. PROBES (probe/figurative-constant-values): p1.cob native ORD(LOW-VALUE)=1; p3.cob PCS 'B' 'A' 'C' -> LOW-VALUE = 'B', ORD 1; p5.cob national PCS N"B" N"A" N"C" -> MOVE LOW-VALUE TO PIC N = N"B" while the alphanumeric LOW-VALUE stays ordinal 1 (national context uses the national PCS); p4.cob LOCALE PCS ORD(LOW-VALUE)=1 (U+0000, completely ignorable rank, determination L7); SPECIAL-NAMES arm AlphabetFigurative -> U+0000 native (§12.3.7.4 GR10). Goldens da1_alphabet_hex_thru and pb297_figurative_sizing_categories derive LOW-VALUE='Z' from GR7. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — The value is correct in MOVE, VALUE, comparison, STRING, DISPLAY, INITIALIZE and EVALUATE, but INSPECT ignores the program collating sequence. Under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS AL (ALPHABET AL IS "B" "A" "C"), GR7 makes LOW-VALUE the lowest-ordinal character, 'B'. The INSPECT emitter instead hard-codes the native U+0000 for LOW-VALUE in both its TALLYING and REPLACING arms. That is a wrong answer at runtime, outside SPECIAL-NAMES, which is exactly what GR7 governs. INSPECT SR3 (§14.9.22) says a figurative operand 'refers to an implicit one character data item' of alphanumeric class, so it carries the GR7 value. The adjudicator's probes never put LOW-VALUE under a non-native PCS in any verb except MOVE. This looks like the two-arm pattern: FigurativeConstants.Fill/FillChar honour the PCS, and the INSPECT literal path does not route through them. The HIGH-VALUE sibling is presumably the same, but GR6 is already DIVERGES. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the LC_COLLATE sentence and the national-sequence sentence from 2002)

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: Rule: 'The quote format represents one or more of the quotation mark character ' " ' in the computer's runtime coded character set. The word QUOTE or QUOTES shall not be used in place of a quotation symbol to bound a literal.' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.6.4 -> OK 8)). First half: FillChar 'Q' -> '"' (both classes); probe probe/figurative-constant-values/p1.cob MOVE QUOTE TO PIC X(3)/PIC N(3) -> '"""|"""', DISPLAY QUOTE -> '"'. Second half: the lexer recognizes literal delimiters only as quotation symbols (§8.3.5 SR5); QUOTE is a figurative token (KindOf) with no delimiter role anywhere in the grammar, so it cannot bound a literal. No spec-derived test isolates the quote character; test-needed.

subject: Lexical elements
Lexical elements
notes: kb/Work PB1394 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'The COBOL characters comma and semicolon, immediately followed by a space, are separators' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 2)). Legal half CONFORMS (COMMA_SEP/FNARG_SEPARATOR/SEMICOLON; probe lgsep). Illegal half UNDER-REJECTED: a comma NOT followed by a space lexes as COMMA, which the parser admits as an operand separator in ~12 list rules (`(COMMA? x)*` in CobolParserCore.g4:642/670, CobolData.g4:774/833-835/887, CobolExpressions.g4:620, CobolIO.g4:332/338, CobolReportWriter.g4:219-220); and SEMICOLON : ';' -> skip discards a semicolon regardless of what follows. Probes: probe/lexical-elements/commanosp.cob `MOVE 1 TO N,M.` compiles and runs (001001); probe/lexical-elements/semicnosp.cob `MOVE 1 TO N;M.` compiles and runs (001001). Expected: 'N,M' / 'N;M' contain no separator (the comma/semicolon is not followed by a space) so the character-string is not a valid COBOL word — a compile-time error. Inconsistent sibling: FUNCTION MAX(N,M) IS rejected (probe fnmaxcomma). See finding 'bare comma/semicolon'. [code-location note: (dataReference (COMMA? dataReference)* lists, line 670)] || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators)

subject: Lexical elements
notes: kb/Work PB1394 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'The COBOL character period, when followed by a space, is a separator. The separator period shall be used only to indicate the end of a sentence, or as shown in formats.' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 3)). Second half CONFORMS: a period mid-statement is rejected (probe probe/lexical-elements/periodmid.cob `MOVE 1 TO N. M.` -> COBOL0001). First half DIVERGES: DOT : '.' matches a period whatever follows it, so a period NOT followed by a space still acts as the separator period. Probe probe/lexical-elements/periodnosp.cob `DISPLAY N.DISPLAY M.` compiles and prints 005 / 007; expected: 'N.DISPLAY' has no separator after the period, so it is not a sentence end and the character-string is not a valid word — compile-time error. PICTURE-string periods are handled separately in PICMODE (not this defect). See finding 'period not followed by space'. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators)

subject: Lexical elements
notes: kb/Work PB1394 (registrar 15b). Rule (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 5)): delimiter set + 'The opening delimiter shall be immediately preceded by a space, left parenthesis, or opening pseudo-text delimiter. The closing delimiter shall be immediately followed by one of the separators space, comma, semicolon, period, right parenthesis, or closing pseudo-text delimiter.' Delimiter-set half CONFORMS: STR_BODY takes " or ' with the matching closer, HEX/NAT/BOOL_BODY take X"/N"/NX"/B"/BX" in both quote spellings. Adjacency half DIVERGES: the lexer skips whitespace and no rule or post-lex pass checks the character before an opening delimiter or after a closing one. Probes: probe/lexical-elements/litclose.cob `DISPLAY "AB"N.` compiles and prints AB005; litopen.cob `MOVE"AB" TO A.` compiles and prints AB; litcloseequal.cob `IF "AB"=A` compiles. (litclosecolon `"AB":N` and hexlitopen `MOVE"X"X"41"` are rejected only by accident of the parse.) Expected: each is a compile-time error — the closing delimiter is followed by 'N' / '=' (not a listed separator) and the opening delimiter is preceded by 'E'. See finding 'literal delimiter adjacency'. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators); the prefixed opening delimiters B"/N"/X"/BX"/NX" exist with their literal kinds (2002+ for boolean/national)

subject: Lexical elements
notes: kb/Work PB1353 (registrar 15b). Rule: 'Pseudo-text delimiters are separators. An opening pseudo-text delimiter shall be immediately preceded by a space; a closing pseudo-text delimiter shall be immediately followed by one of the separators space, comma, semicolon, or period. Pseudo-text delimiters may appear only in balanced pairs delimiting pseudo-text.' (cite.py --check 8.3.5 OK §8.3.5 6)). ReadReplaceOperand recognizes '==' with no check of the preceding or following character, and when no closing '==' exists it silently takes the rest of the source text as the operand. Probes: probe/lexical-elements/repl_closenosep.cob `REPLACE ==XX==BY ==DISPLAY==.` accepted (prints OK); copyclose.cob `COPY LXC REPLACING ==XX==BY ==DISPLAY==.` accepted (prints CP); repl_opennosp.cob `REPLACE ==XX== BY==DISPLAY==.` accepted; repl_unbal.cob `REPLACE ==XX== BY ==DISPLAY.` (no closing delimiter) compiles rc=0 and the program prints NOTHING — the rest of the procedure division was swallowed into the operand. Expected: compile-time error in all four. WRONG-ANSWER for the unbalanced case. See finding 'pseudo-text delimiter'. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.3.5 is common to all editions; Annex E lists no change to separators)

subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB1280 (registrar 15c). cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.1 "It is unique within the context of a REDEFINES clause" -> OK §8.4.2.2.1 2). The REDEFINES operand is never resolved through the qualification resolver: DataBinder's REDEFINES pass binds data-name-2 to the NEAREST PRECEDING same-named entry among the redefiner's own siblings (Parent.Children), or among the owning scope's roots for a level-01/77 entry (method roots per section; program Roots), per §13.18.44.3's placement rule, so a name that is non-unique in the source unit but unique in the REDEFINES context needs no qualification. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, --run): b1 - G1 and G2 each hold 05 A + 05 B REDEFINES A, plus a level-01 A and 01 C REDEFINES A (three entries named A in one program) -> B1=12,34,56 at --std 85 and 2023: each B/C overlays its own context's A with no ambiguity diagnostic. b3 - a LINKAGE SECTION 01 L1 + 01 C REDEFINES L1 in a called program -> B3=78 at 85 and 2023. Negative corpus pb93-redefines-later-sibling/-undefined-target pin the placement half (the REDEFINES clause's own rules, not this row). No spec-derived golden pins the 'non-unique name, unique in REDEFINES context' exemption itself, so test-ref is empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Rule 2 lets a non-unique data-name-2 go unqualified because the REDEFINES placement makes it unique in context. Â§13.18.44.3 NOTE 1 says the same, and SR7 says which entry the placement picks: 'the data-name of the entry that originally defined the area'. ResolveRedefines binds the NEAREST PRECEDING same-named sibling instead. When a redefinition reuses the original's name, the context is misresolved: 05 A / 05 A REDEFINES A / 05 C REDEFINES A is legal (C names the original's data-name), but the resolver picks the second A and rejects the program under SR7 (COBOLNET1656). The ordinary shapes conform (adjudicator b1/b3; my r1 with one A in WS and one in LOCAL-STORAGE, each redefined in its own section, gives WW,LL). Also noted for the REDEFINES-clause adjudication, not this rule: r6 (01 A, 01 G{05 A}, 01 C REDEFINES A) and r2 (a LOCAL-STORAGE 01 redefining a WORKING-STORAGE 01) are accepted. The 'context' lookup reaches past intervening storage (SR10) and across sections. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the REDEFINES exception is present in every edition's qualification rules; the REDEFINES clause exists in all four)]

subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB1306 (registrar 15c). cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.1 "It is unique within the context of a VARYING clause" -> OK §8.4.2.2.1 3). The VARYING context is fixed by §13.18.64.3 SR2 (--check OK): "Data-name-1 shall not be defined elsewhere in the source element, except as data-name-1 in another VARYING clause of an entry not subordinate to the subject of the current entry" and (--check OK) "This definition of data-name-1 may be referenced only within the current entry or a subordinate entry"; §13.18.64.4 GR4 NOTE (--check OK) names use "as a source data item, as a subscript to a source data item". VERIFIED HALF: two non-subordinate entries of one report group may each declare VARYING K, and each entry's own unqualified SOURCE K binds its own counter - probe c1 (DET-A: two LINE entries, OCCURS 3 STEP 3, `VARYING K FROM 2 BY 3 SOURCE K` and `VARYING K FROM 1 BY 1 SOURCE K`) compiles at 2002/2023 and prints `2  5  8` / `1  2  3`. DIVERGENT HALF: the counter is visible ONLY to the declaring entry's own SOURCE (the varyings list is per-entry and FieldVaryingSource matches only `varyings` of the same entry), so a SUBORDINATE entry's unqualified reference - legal and unique in the VARYING context - is rejected: probe c2 (`03 OCCURS 2 TIMES STEP 10 VARYING K FROM 1 BY 1.` / `04 COLUMN 1 PIC 9 SOURCE K.`) -> error COBOLNET0899 "SOURCE 'K' does not resolve to a data item (ISO §13.18.53.3 SR4)" at --std 2002 and 2023; spec-derived expected: compiles and prints `1` at column 1 and `2` at column 11. (A subscript use, SOURCE WS-E(K), is refused by the separate staged-loud 'subscripted SOURCE operand not yet implemented' COBOLNET0899 stage that CONFORMANCE.md A.4.11 already itemizes as a staged SOURCE leg - not this mechanism.) No kb/Work note owns the subordinate-entry scope gap (PB565 landed the repetition vehicle; PB215 is the class screen). Test-ref empty: no golden exercises a reused or subordinate-referenced VARYING name. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the VARYING clause of §13.18.64 is a report-writer/VALIDATE clause first standardized in ISO/IEC 1989:2002; the VALIDATE use is a declined module, A.4.14)]

subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB1476 (registrar 15c). cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.1 "Any other definition of the name is subordinate to a type declaration entry for which the type-name is not referenced in any TYPE clause in the source unit" -> OK §8.4.2.2.1 4). A TYPEDEF template's entries are registered in TypeDecls and kept OFF the name index (DataBinder.cs ~834), so a member of an UNREFERENCED type declaration is never a candidate of QualifiedCandidates; a TYPE clause clones the subtree onto the name index, which is what makes the name non-unique again when the type IS referenced. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, --run): a1 (01 T1 TYPEDEF with 05 X; 01 G with 05 X "G"; DISPLAY X) -> A1=G at --std 2002 and 2023 (unqualified reference legal, resolves to the only non-template X). a2 (same + 01 R TYPE T1; DISPLAY X) -> COBOLNET1639 'X' does not uniquely identify a data item (2 declarations) at 2023 - the exception correctly lapses once the type-name is referenced. a3 (DISPLAY X OF R X IN G) -> A3=TG at 2002/2023. Both halves (exempt when unreferenced / not exempt when referenced) verified. No spec-derived golden pins the unreferenced-typedef exemption, so test-ref is empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The exemption holds only while the type-name is 'not referenced in any TYPE clause in the source unit'. A TYPE clause inside ANOTHER TYPEDEF (itself unreferenced) is still a TYPE clause in the source unit, so the type's members lose the exemption and an unqualified reference must be diagnosed as ambiguous. The implementation keys the lapse on the clone reaching the name index (only a TYPE clause on a real data item puts it there), so it keeps exempting a type referenced only from another type declaration. The unreferenced half and the referenced-by-a-data-item half conform (adjudicator a1/a2; my t2 with the TYPE clause in LOCAL-STORAGE correctly lapses with COBOLNET1639). [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the TYPEDEF/TYPE clause facility this exception is about first exists in ISO/IEC 1989:2002; the rule text is §8.4.2.2.1 rule 4 of the 2023 standard)]

subject: Qualification
notes: cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.1 "the names of any group items superordinate to both the data-name and the subject of the data description entry clause are used as implicit qualifiers" -> OK §8.4.2.2.1 5). EntryClauseCandidates walks the subject's ancestors innermost-first and returns the candidate set under the FIRST group that holds any candidate (every survivor there shares the same implicit qualifiers, so two survivors stay ambiguous), falling back to the scope-wide QualifiedCandidates set; explicit qualifiers are still applied by QualifierChainMatches. Callers: OCCURS DEPENDING ON and SAME AS - the data description entry clauses whose operand is a data-name that can share a group with the subject (OCCURS KEY resolves within the table's own subtree; RENAMES is level 66 and never subordinate; REDEFINES is rule 2; VALIDATE-module clauses and SELECT WHEN are declined modules). BOTH HALVES PROBED (pinned cobol.exe, --run): d1 - G1{CNT=2, T ODO CNT}, G2{CNT=3, T ODO CNT}, G{A{CNT=2}, B{CNT=4}, T ODO CNT OF B}, H{HB{CNT=3}, HA{CNT=1, HT ODO CNT}} -> D1=3,4,6,2 at --std 85 and 2023 (spec-derived: 1+2, 1+3, 1+1+4, 1+1 - each unqualified CNT implicitly qualified by the shared group; the explicit CNT OF B supplies the within-group uniqueness). d2 - G{A{CNT}, B{CNT}, T ODO CNT} -> COBOLNET1639 '2 declarations match' at 85 (implicit qualifier G does not establish uniqueness within the group, so the explicit qualifier the rule requires is demanded). d3 (SAME AS, 2014/2023) - G1{S X(3), U SAME AS S}, G2{S X(5), U SAME AS S} -> D3=3,5. Out of scope and noted: report group description entries are a distinct entry kind from data description entries (§13.15; the standard lists 'a data description entry, a report group description entry, or a screen description entry' separately), so SOURCE/SUM references to same-report sum counters are not this rule's population (see dossier_gaps for the unregistered SOURCE-of-a-sum-counter lead). No golden pins the implicit-qualifier leg (pb885_odo_depending_qualified / pb978 write EXPLICIT qualifiers across records), so test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the implicit-qualifier rule governs data description entry clauses in every edition; the OCCURS DEPENDING leg exists at 85, the SAME AS leg only where SAME AS exists, 2014+)]

subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work/PB466.md - rule 6, the paragraph-specific excuse from qualification: 'The name is a paragraph-name and the section containing the reference also contains the named paragraph.' Implemented as the FIRST unqualified arm of the one resolution algorithm - the referencing section's own map is consulted before the source element's, so a duplicated paragraph-name resolves locally without a qualifier, and only a reference the excuse does not reach falls through to the rule-1 uniqueness count. The excuse is CONDITIONED on the containing section declaring the name once (SR-8.4.2.2.3-7), which the same arm now enforces. Witnessed positively by conformance:85/pb466_procedure_name_uniqueness, where two textually IDENTICAL unqualified PERFORM COMMON-P sentences written in two different sections print different lines - the whole content of rule 6, and the observation a first-definition-wins resolver cannot produce - and at all four editions by the drift test; the complementary reject is conformance:negative/pb466-ambiguous-procedure-name, where the referencing section declares neither copy.

subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB919, wave 57. SR1 is now enforced for EVERY 8.4.2.2.2 qualified-name format through a named resolution each: data-name (QualifiedCandidates, counted by UniqueOrReportAmbiguous / ReportUnidentified), condition-name (ConditionBinder.ConditionOf), index-name (NEW: ReferenceResolver.ResolveIndexName over SymbolTable.IndexCandidates, counted by the same generic UniqueOrReportAmbiguous<T> verdict, COBOLNET1639), procedure-name (ResolveProcedureWord), LINAGE-COUNTER (LinageFileOf), LINE-/PAGE-COUNTER (CounterReportOf); screen-name and record-key-name are declared only by DECLINED facilities (A.4.2 SCREEN SECTION, A.3 item 40). QualifiedNameClassDriftTests derives the format list from the standard's own 8.4.2.2.2 text and fails on an unrouted format. Before: index-names were keyed name -> cell, de-duplicated on insert, so two tables' INDEXED BY IX shared one cell and a bare IX compiled clean.

subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB1454 (registrar 15c). cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.3 "A name may be qualified even though it does not need qualification" -> OK §8.4.2.2.3 2). QualifierChainMatchesFrom consumes qualifiers inner -> outer with GAPS allowed and a trailing file-name, and QualifiedCandidates counts survivors, so any written combination that names superordinate levels resolves, needed or not. VERIFIED (pinned cobol.exe, --run, 85 and 2023), all on UNIQUE names: probe e1 `X OF M OF G`, `X OF G`, `X OF M`, `X IN M OF G` -> X; `FC OF FR OF FA`, `FC OF FA` -> F; `SET IX OF T OF G`, `IX IN G`; `PERFORM P2 OF S1` / `P2 IN S1` (unique paragraph, section qualifier not needed); `GO TO P3 OF S2`; condition-name `X-ON OF X OF M OF G` / `X-ON OF G`; probe g1 `PAGE-COUNTER IN R1` with one RD. DIVERGENT: a REPORT SECTION SUM COUNTER accepts only the bare name or ONE report-name qualifier - ReferenceResolver.SumCounterFor returns null for more than one qualifier and diagnoses any single qualifier that is not a report-name. Probe f3/f4 (unique sum counter TOT1 at level 03 under 01 CF1 TYPE CF FINAL of RD R1): `TOT1` and `TOT1 IN R1` -> 14 14, but `TOT1 OF CF1` -> error COBOLNET2145 "a sum counter may be qualified only by the report-name of the report that defines it (ISO §8.4.2.2.2 Format 1)"; probe f1 `TOT OF CF2 OF R2` -> COBOLNET1639 'not defined'. Spec-derived expected: both compile and read the counter (14), because Format 1 is `data-name-1 [ data-qualifier ] ... [ file-report-qualifier ]`, a report group's entry name is a data-name (§13.18.20 entry-name clause, 'data-name-1 or FILLER' in a report group description entry), and the SUM entry is subordinate to its 01 group - see findings. subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB1454 (registrar 15c). cite.py --check 8.4.2.2.3 "Qualifiers shall be specified in the order of successively more inclusive levels in the hierarchy" -> OK §8.4.2.2.3 4). The rule has three parts: (a) each data-name-2 names a level to which the item is subordinate; (b) qualifiers in successively more inclusive order; (c) a level-88 item's hierarchy includes its conditional variable. QualifierChainMatchesFrom walks ancestors inner -> outer, each qualifier consumed at the first matching ancestor ABOVE the previous one, with only the outermost remaining qualifier allowed to be the owning file. VERIFIED by probe n1 (--std 2023), each refused COBOLNET1639: `X OF G OF M` (reversed order, (b)); `X OF T` (a sibling group, (a)); `X OF X-ON` (a condition-name as qualifier - not a level to which X is subordinate); `FC OF FA OF FR` (file not outermost); `X OF M OF G OF FA` (WS item qualified by a file); `W77 OF G` (level-77 has no superordinate); `X OF FA`. Part (c): ConditionQualifierChainMatches starts at the conditional variable - pb567 golden Q1/Q2/Q5 and probe e1 `X-ON OF X OF M OF G` -> T. DIVERGENT on part (a)'s permission side: a report-section SUM COUNTER may not be qualified by the report group (data-name) to which its entry is subordinate - `TOT1 OF CF1` refused COBOLNET2145, `TOT OF CF2 OF R2` refused COBOLNET1639 (probes f1/f3), where the rule makes CF1 exactly 'the name associated with a level number to which the item being qualified is subordinate' - see findings (same mechanism as SR-8.4.2.2.3-2). subject: Subscripts
notes: PB1016 LANDED 2026-09-22: the DATA DIVISION reference - CONSTANT AS LENGTH OF data-name-2 (SS13.10) - now reaches the same ReferenceResolver.ScreenSubscriptArity every procedure-division reference takes; before, `01 KL CONSTANT AS LENGTH OF PLAIN(1).` over a non-table item compiled and KL was 7. The constant binder's private suffix walk is gone (ReadWritten), so a subscript hung off a qualification is screened too. SR2 has two halves - 'shall contain an OCCURS clause OR SHALL BE SUBORDINATE TO a data description entry that contains an OCCURS clause' - and the compiler wrote down only the first, as DataItem.IsTable. Both halves are now one predicate, DataItem.IsTableElement (= SubscriptArity > 0), read by the ONE declaration-informed '(' rule the three subscript-splitting callers share. POSITIVE: the 85 golden subscripts X, which carries no OCCURS clause of its own and is subordinate to one, in every reference position - a receiving operand of MOVE / ADD / COMPUTE / STRING / UNSTRING / INITIALIZE, a sending operand, a relative subscript, a reference-modification leftmost position, an intrinsic-function argument and a SEARCH ALL identifier-1. NEGATIVE: a subscript on an item satisfying NEITHER half is COBOLNET2096 at all four editions. Before kb/Work PB877 that violation drew COBOLNET0899 'not yet implemented' on the receiving side - a promise about permanently illegal source - and compiled clean and aborted at run time on the sending side, where 4.2.2 requires a compile-time mechanism.

subject: Subscripts
notes: The COUNT and the ORDER. DataItem.SubscriptArity is the count - one per OCCURS clause in the item's description, fixed or dynamic - and DataItem.SubscriptLevels() is the same walk as a list, outermost first, which is SR3's 'order of successively less inclusive dimensions'. Five hand-written copies of that ancestor walk were in the compiler; the drift test pins it to one. POSITIVE: the 85 golden writes one subscript per dimension in every position, including the two-dimensional Y2 OF Y-REC (X(1), 2) and the nested SEARCH ALL T-E (T-N (1), TX) whose witness value discriminates the outer occurrence. NEGATIVE: X (1, 2) on a one-dimensional element is COBOLNET2097 at all four editions. SR5's seven exceptions are all about OMITTING the subscript list and are decided by the owning binders (a SEARCH subject, a REDEFINES clause, an OCCURS KEY IS phrase, a SORT key or table subject, a screen entry's FROM/TO/USING phrase, a report SUM addend), so the screen deliberately fires only on a reference that WRITES subscripts.

subject: Subscripts
notes: kb/Work PB1472 (registrar 15c). DISPLAY FUNCTION SUM(E2(IXA, ALL)).` compiles clean and prints `0` at 2023; spec-derived expected: a compile-time SR4 diagnostic (COBOLNET1961), IXA is in T1's INDEXED BY, not in E2's hierarchy. subject: Subscripts
notes: GAP -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB681). Rule text validated: cite.py --check 8.4.2.3.3 "Each table element reference shall be subscripted except when such reference appears" -> OK 5). An OMITTED subscript list on a table element is COBOLNET2270 at all three identifier entries (Resolve, ResolveForItem for a condition-name's conditional variable, ResolveForAddressOf); before, each returned an unreported null (or the first occurrence's address) and MOVE E TO B aborted at run time. The seven exception contexts a)-g) never reach the screen: the SEARCH subject resolves through ResolveTableOperand, the SORT table subject and keys through SortBinder's own data-description walk, REDEFINES / OCCURS KEY / SUM through the data binder; the screen's summary records that boundary.

subject: Subscripts
notes: kb/Work PB1473 (registrar 15c). Rule (cite.py --check 8.4.2.3.3 'The subscript ALL may be used only' -> OK §8.4.2.3.3 6); --check 'as the rightmost or only subscript of a table in the table format of a SORT statement' -> OK §8.4.2.3.3 6)). Two halves. (a) INTRINSIC-ARGUMENT half CONFORMS: ALL outside a function argument fails the subscript-segment parse and draws COBOLNET2363 naming SR6 (MOVE receiver - pb1030 witness; IF relation sr6h; `FUNCTION MAX(E1(ALL) + 1)` sr6d - the subscripted identifier is not itself the argument; `FUNCTION MAX(E1(E1(ALL)))` sr6e - ALL on the inner subscript identifier); IntrinsicBinder.TryBindAllArgument admits it only for a sole-data-reference argument (and §15.3's repeatable-argument condition, COBOLNET1645); `FUNCTION SUM(E1(ALL))` = 06 at 85/2002/2014/2023 (sr6_85); UDF arguments refuse it (UdfBinder, §9.4). (b) SORT half: `SORT E1(ALL) DESCENDING` over a one-dimensional table is accepted and sorts (sr6j -> 321, sr6k ASCENDING -> 123, at 2002 and 2023) = 'equivalent to omitting the ... only subscript'. ⛔ But SortBindTable reads only ResolveTableOperand(...).Item and never the written subscript segments (TableOperand carries their count, unread), so the 'rightmost or only' POSITION is never screened: scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/subscripts/sr6g.cob `SORT E2(ALL, 1) DESCENDING` over `05 R2 OCCURS 2. 10 E2 PIC 9 OCCURS 3.` compiles with only the COBOLNET1756 nested-table DEFERRAL warning (kb/Work PB1055, open - owns SR-14.9.40.3-13) and aborts at run time; spec-derived expected: a compile-time refusal - ALL is not the rightmost subscript. The legal twin `SORT E2(1, ALL)` (sr6c) draws the identical deferral, so the two are indistinguishable today and PB1055's landing will not by itself add the position screen. Aside (not decided here, SR5/SR3 territory): `SORT E1(2)` over a one-dimensional table (sr6i) is accepted and sorts the WHOLE table. [editions as adjudicated: 85 (intrinsic-argument half only - intrinsic functions via the ISO 1989:1985/Amd 1 intrinsic function module, Annex E bibliography [6]), 2002, 2014, 2023 (both halves; the table format of SORT is absent from 1985 and rejected COBOLNET0870 at --std 85)]

subject: Subscripts
notes: kb/Work PB201 (2026-09-04) closed the last unevidenced arm and kb/Work PB877 (2026-09-13) closed a hole INSIDE a closed arm. All THREE determinations of GR1 are pinned separately. a) ALL - pb62 covers all three ranges GR1a defers to (a fixed OCCURS count, an OCCURS DEPENDING object, a dynamic-capacity current capacity) and the multi-dimension rightmost-varies-fastest order; the arm is vacuous at 85, which has no functions for which the subscript ALL is allowed. b) arithmetic-expression-1 - pb136 (compound expressions), pb41 (the integrality condition itself: a non-integer result raises EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT under checking ON, via CobolTable.OccScaled/CobolNum.HasFraction), pb201_position_operand_carriers (the CARRIER axis) and, since PB877, pb877_subscripted_subscript - the OPERAND-SHAPE axis none of the other four touched, an identifier that carries its own subscripts. Five goldens had pinned this arm CONFORMS while that whole shape was refused, which is why the witness list now names the shape as well as the value. c) index-name-1 [+/- integer-1] - pb170 (E(IX)), pb50 (E(IX + 1)) and 85/index_name_r7_windows (T(IX + 1) at the 85 edition). The implementor-defined index-to-occurrence mapping GR1c reserves is the identity (an IndexCell holds the occurrence number). The renderer is not the adjudicator: any operand PositionRead cannot render routes to the D18 materializer, whose arithmetic-expression grammar decides admissibility - so a shape 8.8.1.1 does not admit cannot parse, and the drift test pins the carrier set to the runtime overload set in both directions.

subject: Subscripts
notes: kb/Work PB201 (2026-09-04). CobolTable.At is the ONE occurrence-number to element mapping and it is edition-independent - no edition branch - so the 1..n bound holds identically at every edition; ec_bound_subscript pins the NAMED condition under >>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON with a USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION declarative and RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT. With checking OFF the reference continues into a re-defaulted scratch slot, the implementor choice 13.18.38.4 GR7 leaves open by making out-of-bounds occurrence content undefined, and the only posture COBOL-85 can take since it has no exception conditions. PB201 added the piece that was missing on the way IN: every wide carrier (an Int128 >18-digit item, an unsigned BINARY-CAPACITY container, and an alphanumeric image FromAlphanumeric decodes to up to 38 digits) now narrows through CobolNum.Position, which SATURATES. A plain (long) cast wraps, and a wrapped position can land back inside 1..n - turning a condition this rule requires to be detected into a silent wrong answer.

subject: Identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1407, PB1425 (registrar 15b). SR1 (cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.3 1) OK): any identifier slot of an identifier format admits any identifier format. Probes p1.cob: function-identifier inside a function argument that is itself ref-modified `FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (FUNCTION LOWER-CASE (A OF G (N))(1:3))` -> G2G; function-identifier in a ref-mod leftmost position `W (FUNCTION LENGTH (W) - 1 : 2)` -> ef; function-identifier as a subscript `A OF G (FUNCTION INTEGER (N))(1:1)` -> G; ref-mod identifier as a function argument -> C. Inline invocation chained on its own temporary is pinned by the spec-derived golden pb428 item 6, which cites this rule. Recursion through Format 5 is impossible only because Format 5 does not exist - that defect belongs to SR-8.4.3.1.3-6, not to this rule. Probes under out/probe/ident with the pinned cobol.exe. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — SR1 makes every identifier slot inside another identifier format accept ANY identifier format. subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: kb/Work PB922 (wave 42) - RULE (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.3 'EXCEPTION-OBJECT shall not be specified as a receiving operand'): OK, SR1. SR1 is a rule about EVERY receiving operand in the language, and only SET had an arm for it, so MOVE U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT drew COBOLNET1639 ('is not defined - Check the spelling, or declare the item') beside COBOLNET0901 ('is a reserved word and cannot be used as a user-defined word') - two diagnostics that contradict each other, and neither of them the rule the program broke. Now screened at the ONE general receiving chokepoint, ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving, as COBOLNET2196 quoting SR1; SET's own arm draws the SAME code and its clause number was repaired from 8.4.3.6 (where cite.py --check FAILS) to 8.4.3.6.3. THE EDITION IS PART OF THE RULE and is measured on both sides: 8.9 reserves the word only from COBOL-2002, so at --std 85 EXCEPTION-OBJECT is an ordinary user-defined word and '01 EXCEPTION-OBJECT PIC X(4).' + 'MOVE "ABCD" TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT' is conforming source that runs (conformance:85/pb922_exception_object_user_word_85); the one predicate ReferenceResolver.IsExceptionObjectRegister carries spelling, form (8.4.3.6.2's general format is the bare word) and edition together, so no caller can hold a different opinion. editions names 2002 and later because that is where the prohibition applies at all.

subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: kb/Work PB922 (wave 42) - RULE (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.3 'EXCEPTION-OBJECT is implicitly described as class object and category object reference, as an external data item, and as a universal object reference'): OK, SR2. The STANDARD declares this name and no data description entry does, so a resolver that does not know it answers 'is not defined' about a name that is defined - which is what every sending reference got. DataBinder.ExceptionObjectRegister now carries SR2's implicit description (PicInfo.ObjectReferenceItem(ObjectRefDescriptor.Universal)) and ReferenceResolver resolves the bare word to an ExceptionObjectPlace over it, beside the CAPACITY and DEBUG-ITEM registers, so every class/category screen reads it like any other object-reference item and every caller inherits the answer. It is a VIEW, never storage: 8.4.3.6.4 GR2 gives the run unit ONE instance, which is the runtime's ExceptionState, and PlaceRenderer renders the read (fully qualified, because a reference to it needs neither the EC model nor a class and the conditional 'using' would otherwise leave the backend with CS0103 on generated C# the user cannot see). MEASURED at 2002 and 2023: IF EXCEPTION-OBJECT = NULL is legal source and true when no exception object is associated with the current exception (GR1); SET U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT copies that reference; two references denote the same instance (GR2). SR2's 'as an external data item' is deliberately NOT carried as HasExternalClause - that flag drives the 13.18.22 EXTERNAL-store re-basing of a DECLARED record, and what the phrase asserts (one instance per run unit) is already realized by the single ExceptionState. ExceptionObjectPlace is registered in PlaceStorageFormSwitchDriftTests' storage-form roster, so a switch that meets it in a catch-all is a failing test.

subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: GR1: "EXCEPTION-OBJECT references the current exception object. If an exception object is not associated with the current exception, EXCEPTION-OBJECT is set to null." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.4 OK). Both halves verified. Object half: SetObject (RAISE identifier-1, §14.9.29.4 GR2 --check OK; GOBACK/EXIT RAISING staging) stores the object; probe p1.cob RAISE E then `IF EXCEPTION-OBJECT = E` answers DECL-SAME inside the USE AFTER EXCEPTION OBJECT declarative and AFTER-SAME after return (identity, not merely non-null). Null half: no exception -> null (golden pb922 SR2-NULL=YES); Set (every named raise, §14.6.13.1.1 'the predefined object reference EXCEPTION-OBJECT is set to null' --check OK; SetIo delegates to Set) nulls it - probe: RAISE E then an EC-SIZE raise under >>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING ON / ON SIZE ERROR answers NAMED-NULL; Clear (SET LAST EXCEPTION TO OFF, §14.9.39.4 GR28 --check OK) nulls it - probe OFF-NULL. Same output at --std 2002/2014/2023. Test-ref left empty: pb922_exception_object_reference pins only the no-exception null arm and oo_ec_raise_object only asserts NOT = NULL (no spec derivation header, no identity check); no existing spec-derived test pins identity with the raised object or the null-after-named-raise arm - test-needed.

subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: GR2: "There is one instance of EXCEPTION-OBJECT in a run unit." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.4 OK). The register is not storage in any program: every read renders to ExceptionState.ExceptionObject, a facade over RunUnit.Current.Exceptions - one ExceptionEngine owned by the run unit (AsyncLocal RunUnit, one per run unit, concurrently-hosted run units each get their own). Probe p1.cob: main RAISEs object E, then CALLs a separately compiled program EXOBJS1 (own PROGRAM-ID, same run unit) which reads EXCEPTION-OBJECT and answers SUB-SHARED (not null) at 2002/2014/2023. Test-ref empty: golden pb922's GR2-ONE=SAME compares two null reads inside one program, which cannot distinguish one instance from per-program instances; a cross-program witness with a non-null object is test-needed. [code-location note: (static facade E => RunUnit.Current.Exceptions); code-location note: (ExceptionObjectRegister, one shared per program model, ~l.298-314)]

subject: NULL object reference
notes: "NULL shall not be specified as a receiving operand." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.7.3 -> OK, SR1). At 2002 and later NULL is a reserved token, not a cobolWord, so it cannot head a dataReference in any receiving slot. SetFormatSelection.KindOf's comment records that SR1 is enforced by the grammar. Probed at 2023, and at 2002 for SET: `SET NULL TO G`, `SET NULL G TO NULL`, `MOVE G TO NULL`, `INVOKE CN1 "NEW" RETURNING NULL` and `INITIALIZE NULL` are all refused with COBOLNET0901. A bare `USING NULL` bound BY REFERENCE (the formal's mode) is refused COBOLNET0828, which §14.9.23.3 SR9 also requires. Every receiving position is refused. The diagnostic cites §8.9 (reserved word) rather than this SR, which is a message-quality point, not a missed rejection. At 1985 NULL is an ordinary user word and the rule does not apply. No spec-derived negative test covers this SR by name. Probe files: scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/null-object-reference/n1,n2,n3,n6,n7.cob

subject: NULL object reference
notes: kb/Work PB1137 (registrar 15c). "NULL is implicitly described as class object and category object reference, and is not a universal object reference." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.7.3 -> OK, SR2). The NOT-UNIVERSAL half CONFORMS. `INVOKE NULL MNAME` is refused COBOLNET0866, citing §14.9.23.3 SR7 ("Identifier-2 may be specified only when identifier-1 is a universal object reference", --check OK). The CLASS-OBJECT / CATEGORY-OBJECT-REFERENCE half DIVERGES, and there is no object-reference model of NULL outside SET and the relation condition. Wherever NULL is an operand it binds to BoundFigurative('N'), and IntrinsicArgumentRules classifies that node as [CobolClass.Pointer] only, i.e. the §8.4.3.10 predefined address and never the §8.4.3.7 object. Measured consequences at 2023: (a) `INVOKE G "TAKE" USING BY CONTENT NULL` with an OBJECT REFERENCE CN1 formal is refused COBOLNET0828 "argument form ... is not yet carried across a method activation" (p3.cob). identifier-5 under BY CONTENT is legal per §14.9.23.2, and §14.9.23.3 SR5a is satisfied by a BY REFERENCE formal. (b) `USING BY VALUE NULL` is a parse error (see FMT). (c) `INVOKE NULL "TAKE" USING G` is refused COBOLNET0823 "the predefined NULL object reference cannot be a receiver (ISO §14.9.23.3)". No §14.9.23.3 rule says that: SR1 requires only "an object reference", and SR2 here makes NULL one. The standard excludes NULL by name where it means to, in §8.4.3.4.3 SR2 (inline invocation) and §8.4.3.9.3 SR2 (object property), and INVOKE has no such exclusion. §14.9.23.4 GR5 ("If identifier-1 is null, the EC-OO-NULL exception condition is set to exist") gives the runtime outcome. Two halves, one defective => DIVERGES. Probe files: scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/null-object-reference/p3.cob, n4.cob, n5.cob

subject: NULL object reference
notes: "Predefined object reference NULL contains the null object reference value; this is a unique value defined by the implementor such that it is guaranteed to never reference an object." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.7.4 -> OK). In the typed-native model NULL is the .NET null reference, which by construction references no object. Probed at 2002 and 2023 (p4.cob): a NEW instance compares NOT = NULL. After `SET G H TO NULL`, G = NULL and H = NULL (both operand orders, NULL = G). A universal reference set TO NULL equals NULL and equals a typed reference holding NULL, so there is one unique null value across categories. INVOKE on a null reference raises EC-OO-NULL (conformance:2023/ec_oo_null_invoke, §14.9.23.4 GR5). conformance:2002/oo_universal_relation derives its expected values from this GR: the initial U = NULL, and after NEW U NOT = NULL.

TO SELF (OoCurrentClass null -> 0867), RAISE SELF (EcBinder 0848). subject: SELF and SUPER
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (registrar 15c). Rule (--check 8.4.3.8.3 'This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand' -> OK §8.4.3.8.3 2)). Enforced structurally: no receiving slot (SET receivers are dataReference+, RETURNING, MOVE targets) admits the SELF/SUPER tokens. Probes probe/self-and-super/PSSETR.cob (`SET SELF TO O`) and PSRET.cob (`INVOKE PSRETA "NEW" RETURNING SELF`) both rejected. The diagnostic is the generic COBOLNET0901 "reserved word ... cannot be used as a user-defined word" rather than an SR2 citation (quality, not conformance). No spec-derived negative fixture found for this SR (SetFormatSelection.cs:232 comment only). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — No SR2 mechanism exists. Nine receiving-position probes each fail with COBOLNET0901 "'SELF' is a reserved word ... cannot be used as a user-defined word (ISO §8.9)": SET SELF TO NULL, RETURNING SELF, INITIALIZE SELF, SET SELF O / O SELF TO NULL, MOVE .. TO SELF, SET ADDRESS OF SELF, SET SUPER TO NULL and ACCEPT SELF. The source is rejected only because SELF/SUPER are not identifiers at all, which is the rejects-legal-source defect F2. The stated reason is also false: the source does not use SELF as a user-defined word, it uses a predefined-object identifier as a receiving operand. Nothing tests it. When F2 is fixed by admitting SELF/SUPER as identifier Format 6, every one of these positions would start compiling without a diagnostic. A verdict that depends on a separate defect staying unfixed, with no rule-owned diagnostic, is not CONFORMS. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO predefined object references; absent from COBOL-85)]

notes: kb/Work PB1425 (registrar 15c). Rule (--check 8.4.3.8.3 'are not universal object references' -> OK §8.4.3.8.3 7)). subject: SELF and SUPER

subject: SELF and SUPER
notes: Rule (--check 8.4.3.8.4 'ignores all the methods defined in the class containing the invocation' -> OK §8.4.3.8.4 3)). For SUPER, searchRoot = cur.Base and the call renders non-virtual `base.M()`, ignoring the containing class and its subclasses; SUPER in a root class -> COBOLNET0827. oo_super: DOG.SPEAK override INVOKE SUPER "SPEAK" prints ANIMAL then DOG (no recursion). Probe probe/self-and-super/PGR3.cob: C INHERITS B INHERITS A, B has no M; C.M's INVOKE SUPER "M" runs A.M (skips C, finds grandparent), and C.N's SUPER "N" runs B.N not C.N - output C.M/A.M/C.N/B.N as derived. || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref emptied: oo_super pins only the 'ignore the containing class' half; the 'and all the methods defined in any subclass of that class' half and the grandparent skip are probe-verified only — The behaviour conforms. I probed the half nobody had tried. In RSUB.cob, B.X does INVOKE SUPER "M" on a C object while both B and C override M, and it prints A.M. The factory flavor (INVOKE SUPER "FM" from B's factory, run on the C factory) prints A.FM. So base.M() is non-virtual and ignores the subclass overrides, as GR3 requires. The adjudicator's PGR3 never exercised this half: no SUPER there runs from a class that has an overriding subclass. The cited golden oo_super is only two levels deep (DOG over ANIMAL, invoked on a DOG). It cannot tell a non-virtual base call apart from a virtual one, and it has no subclass. Closing the row on it over-claims what it proves. This is the same reasoning the adjudicator used to leave GR1's test-ref empty. notes: kb/Work PB1427 (registrar 15c). Rule (cite.py --check 8.4.3.10.3 'it may be used only as a sending operand in an INITIALIZE or a SET statement; as an argument in a program-prototype format CALL statement' -> OK §8.4.3.10.3 1) a); '... or in a pointer-or-object-reference relation condition' -> OK; b) message-tag half -> OK). Two halves. a) POINTER HALF -- DIVERGES in BOTH directions. Correctly screened (probes in E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/null/): MOVE NULL TO X / TO P -> COBOLNET0809; IF P = X -> 0869; Format-1 CALL USING NULL -> 0899 (not program-prototype format, correct); SET N TO NULL -> 0867; STOP ... STATUS NULL / DISPLAY NULL have negative witnesses (pb216, pb148). UNDER-REJECTS (NULL treated as LOW-VALUE, compiles and runs): IFX.cob `IF X = NULL` (X PIC X(4)) -> 'NE'; IFN.cob `IF N = NULL` (N PIC 9(4)) -> 'NE'; EVALX.cob `EVALUATE X WHEN NULL` -> 'W OTHER'; INSP.cob `INSPECT X TALLYING T FOR ALL NULL` -> '0000'; STRG.cob `STRING NULL DELIMITED SIZE INTO X` -> writes a NUL into X; LEN.cob `FUNCTION LENGTH(NULL)` -> '0001' (an intrinsic activation is not the function-prototype format SR1 a) names; §8.4.3.2.2 prints function-prototype-name-1 and intrinsic-function-name-1 as distinct arms). Every one must be rejected: the associated item is not of class pointer, or the context is not in SR1 a)'s list. REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE: INITIALIZE P REPLACING DATA-POINTER DATA BY NULL -> COBOLNET1982 'BY the literal NULL: identifier-2 shall be specified' although NULL IS an identifier (§8.4.3.1.2 Format 8 -> OK) and SR1 a) admits it as an INITIALIZE sending operand; CALL prototype USING BY VALUE NULL -> COBOLNET1762 'literal-2 shall be a NUMERIC literal'. CRASHES: CALL prototype USING BY CONTENT NULL to a pointer / program-pointer formal compiles and aborts at run time with EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH (PROTOC3.cob, PROTOPP.cob). Not probed: NULL as a function-prototype activation argument and as a method-invocation argument -- same routing, sweep targets. b) MESSAGE-TAG HALF: unreachable -- the MCS facility is declined (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §4 item 1; COBOLNET1943/2205); no derived selector covers it (see GR-8.4.3.10.4-4). PB939 (open) owns only the VALUE-clause arm of the under-rejection; the other contexts are unowned.

subject: NULL address pointer and message tag content
notes: 'When associated with a function-pointer, the predefined address NULL references a data item of category function-pointer that contains the NULL function address. The null function address is an implementor-defined value that is guaranteed not to represent the address of any function.' The value is the NULL NAME - FunctionPointer.Null, the struct default - and the guarantee holds because no FUNCTION-ID paragraph can name a function null, so no registered function can ever compare equal to it. It is also the item's initial state (PicInfo.DefaultInitializer) and the INITIALIZE SET-NULL target (14.9.20.4 GR4/GR6c). Witnessed at both polarities by the 2014 golden's NULL1/NOTNULL3 pair and by the 2023 golden's B-NULL. NOTE THE CLAUSE: this is GR2, not the GR3 that the PROGRAM twin takes - the first draft of this landing inherited GR3 from ProgramPointer.cs and audit_doc_citations caught it.

GR2 "If identifier-1 is a strongly-typed group item or a restricted data-pointer, the data-address-identifier is a restricted data-pointer that is restricted to the type of identifier-1" (cite.py OK 2)); Annex D.9.2.2 (cite.py --check D.9.2.2 OK): restricted pointers exist so data of one type cannot be treated as another. The level-1 strong-group arm works (G2N: SET plain P TO ADDRESS OF S -> 0869; G4 likewise). But AddressOfRestriction returns the WRONG type in two arms: (a) identifier-1 a restricted data-pointer RP TYPE PT (PT TYPEDEF USAGE POINTER TO T-REC): the code restricts ADDRESS OF RP to T-REC (PointerRestriction = the pointer's TARGET) instead of RP's own type PT. Probe G3: `SET ADDRESS OF BS TO ADDRESS OF RP` with BS TYPE T-REC BASED compiles and runs (ACCEPTED) - a T-REC view over a pointer cell; expected COBOLNET0869 per §14.9.39.3 SR19 second sentence. Probe G5 (legal): PPT TYPEDEF USAGE POINTER TO PT, PP TYPE PPT, `SET PP TO ADDRESS OF RP` is REFUSED 0869 ('restricted to type PT, so the sender shall be ... restricted to the same type') - rejects legal source. (b) identifier-1 a strongly-typed SUBORDINATE group (T-G of S, T-REC STRONG with T-X at offset 0-1, T-G at 2): restricted to 'T-REC' (StrongGroupType -> TypedItemType -> the enclosing anchor's name), so probe G7 `SET ADDRESS OF BS TO ADDRESS OF T-G OF S` compiles and only fails at run time with EC-BOUND-PTR; the address of T-G is not a T-REC. See finding 'restriction type of ADDRESS OF'.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'Identifier-1 shall be of category alphanumeric or national.' COBOLNET1960. The braced operand of ADDRESS OF FUNCTION arrives as ONE dataReference and the two arms are told apart at BIND, where the REPOSITORY function-specifier table and the item's resolved category are both facts: a word that is a declared function-prototype-name takes the prototype arm, anything else must resolve to an alphanumeric or national identifier. The positive leg is witnessed too - the 2023 golden drives the whole run-time lane through a PIC X(12) identifier-1.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'Function-prototype-name-1 shall be a function prototype specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph.' Resolved through DataBinder.UserFunctionNames - the REPOSITORY FUNCTION specifiers WITHOUT the INTRINSIC phrase - plus 8.4.6.6's other leg, 'the user-function-name of the containing function definition', so a self-referential function-pointer inside a function definition needs no repository entry. The SAME two legs the USAGE clause's TO phrase resolves, written once per operand kind. A word in neither leg is not silently accepted: it falls to SR1's identifier test and is refused COBOLNET1960.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'This identifier format shall not be specified as a receiving operand.' STRUCTURALLY SATISFIED, and the structure is the point: the function-address-identifier has exactly ONE grammar home, setFunctionAddressStatement's `TO ADDRESS OF? FUNCTION dataReference` tail, which is a SENDING position by construction. It appears in no receiving-operand rule anywhere in the grammar, so the rule cannot be violated by a parsable program and no screen is needed - the SR18/SR19 lesson in reverse (a rule with a structural answer needs no second copy of that answer in the binder). Compare 8.4.3.13's PROGRAM twin, whose SR4 is the same sentence and whose grammar home setEntryStatement is likewise sender-only.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'Function-address-identifier creates a unique data item of class pointer and category function-pointer that contains the address of a function identified by one of the following: a) the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 b) function-prototype-name-1.' BOTH arms are live and both are witnessed: the 2014 golden takes the PROTOTYPE arm and the 2023 golden drives the IDENTIFIER arm three times. The 'unique data item of class pointer and category function-pointer' is the resolved FunctionPointer value the emitted site computes once and stores into every receiver - it is a value, never a declared item, which is why it has no PicInfo and why SR3 keeps it out of receiving positions. GR1's trailing sentence ('Identifier-1 shall reference a function prototype specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph') is a RUN-TIME fact about the identifier's CONTENT, not a compile-time screen on the identifier, and it is exactly what GR4 answers when the content names nothing.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'For a COBOL function, the address is that of the function identified by the externalized function-name in its FUNCTION-ID paragraph' - this implementation's function-pointer representation IS that name (ProgramTable.Node.CallName, the 11.5.4 GR1 AS literal when one is written and the declared word otherwise, kb/Work PB303), so the rule is satisfied by construction rather than by a conversion. 'For a non-COBOL function, the relation between the address and the associated function is defined by the implementor' - this implementation declares support for no non-COBOL function, which is published under A.1 item 210 (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 DOC-A.1-210, the allowable-languages half); such a function has no run-unit registration, so GR4 - EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND and the predefined address NULL - is the defined answer for one.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'When function-prototype-name-1 is specified, the function-address-identifier has the characteristics of a function-pointer restricted to function-prototype-name-1.' The rule's whole observable consequence is that the sender then enters 14.9.39.3 SR20's same-signature compare as a restricted function-pointer, and that is exactly how it is implemented: the prototype arm of BindSetFunctionAddress runs the SAME PrototypeSignatures.Same test the pointer-to-pointer arm runs, against the receiver's own prototype, and COBOLNET1959 names the mismatch. It is ALSO why the prototype arm needs no run-time GR14 screen of its own - the characteristics are known at bind - while the identifier-1 arm does.

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: 'If the runtime system cannot locate the function, the EC-FUNCTION-NOT-FOUND exception condition is set to exist and the value of the address-identifier is the predefined address NULL.' BOTH halves are measured by the 2023 golden's NF-RAISED/B-NULL pair: the declarative runs AND the receiver takes NULL. The value is DEFINED by the rule, so the store happens whether or not checking is enabled and only the raise is checking-gated (14.6.13.1.4) - the opposite arrangement from 14.9.39.4 GR14, which NAMES its no-change outcome and therefore skips the store unconditionally. The two legs are written separately for that reason. EcBinder.QueryFor gained the BoundSetFunctionAddress arm in the SAME change set as the raise site, after the same gap was MEASURED on its BoundSetEntry sibling (a >>TURN EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND CHECKING ON over SET pp TO ENTRY 'NOSUCH' printed only 'AFTER SET' - the 8.4.3.13 GR4 raise had been dead since P10 Step 7).

notes: cite.py --check 8.4.3.13.4 'creates a unique data item of class pointer and category program-pointer' OK (GR1). a) identifier content: emitted as `(read).Trim()` into ProgramRegistry.EntryOf at statement time; b) literal value decoded at bind (STRINGLIT/HEXLIT/NATLIT/concatenation); c) prototype -> its externalized name. subject: Program-address-identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1453 (registrar 15c). cite.py --check 8.4.3.13.4 'the EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND exception condition is set to exist and the value of the address-identifier is the predefined address NULL' OK (GR4). EntryOf returns ProgramPointer.Null with notFound; with checking on each surface raises the EC (SET: NULL stored, then ExceptionState.Set + declarative dispatch; CALL argument: pre-transfer CobolCallException -> ON EXCEPTION; relation/INVOKE operand: fatal raise), unchecked it is NULL (14.6.13.1.4). Probed: unchecked SET -> NF-NULL, unchecked relation -> REL-NULL (ok2); checked SET with USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND -> 'DECL EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND', AFTER, NF-NULL (ec1). pb239_call_program_address_not_found pins the set-to-exist half (CALL argument); pb239_call_address_identifier pins the NULL value (Q=NULL). Both spec-derived. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The NULL-value half conforms on every surface. The 'EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND is set to exist' half is broken on two surfaces. (1) Relation operand: with >>TURN EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND CHECKING ON, the IF emits EntryOfOperand("NOSUCHP", false), so the condition is never set. EXCEPTION-STATUS stays blank, no declarative runs and execution continues. The adjudicator's note says this surface raises the fatal condition; the probe shows it does not. PtrEmitter.ProgramAddressText reads ecState.Info for the carrying statement, and inside a condition that yields no enabled entry. (2) SET surface: the condition is set, but it is processed as nonfatal. EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND is Fatal in Table 13, so §14.6.13.1.3 items 5 and 7 require abnormal run-unit termination once checking is enabled, whether the USE declarative completes normally or no declarative applies. Instead SET continues with the next statement. Only the CALL-argument surface (pb239) behaves correctly (declarative, then abnormal termination). [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the program-pointer family; absent from COBOL-85 - Annex E covers only 2014->2023, the introduction is the 2002 address-identifier; probe: --std 85 draws COBOLNET0900)]

subject: LINAGE-COUNTER
notes: kb/Work PB1431 (registrar 15b). SR1: "LINAGE-COUNTER may be referenced only in procedure division statements." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.14.3 -> OK 1)). Every data-name clause operand passes the ONE screen ScreenDataNameShape, which refuses the register with COBOLNET2024 citing SR1. Probed (probe/linage-counter): OCCURS DEPENDING ON LINAGE-COUNTER (S1), FILE STATUS (E1), ASSIGN USING (E2), RELATIVE KEY (E3), LINAGE FOOTING AT LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF (E4), RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON (E6) -- all rejected with COBOLNET2024 naming SR1. Report section SOURCE LINAGE-COUNTER (S2b) and SUM LINAGE-COUNTER (S2c) are ALSO rejected (correct outcome) but by the resolver's Deferred(UnroutedSpecialRegister) path, drawing COBOLNET0899 report-source-operand-unresolved / report-sum-addend-unresolved: "SOURCE 'LINAGE-COUNTER' does not resolve to a data item (ISO §13.18.53.3 SR4)" -- the outcome conforms, but the sentence names a different rule and an 0899 (recognized-not-implemented band) id where §8.4.3.14.3 SR1 forbids the reference outright (the PB489 shape: right outcome, wrong sentence). Screen section FROM is COBOLNET1560 (optional module not claimed, CONFORMANCE.md §5). Procedure-division references bind (Q1/Q5/g4). Test-ref covers the FD-clause position. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — SR1 (cite.py --check 8.4.3.14.3 -> OK 1) forbids ANY reference outside procedure division statements. The adjudicator probed only bare/data-name clause operands. Two report-section references with the register inside an expression or condition COMPILE CLEANLY (exit 0, dll emitted) and read the live counter at run time: SOURCE LINAGE-COUNTER + 1 (arithmetic-expression SOURCE, accepted at --std 2023 AND --std 85) and PRESENT WHEN LINAGE-COUNTER > 1 / PRESENT WHEN LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF = 2 (accepted at 2023; at 85 only the PRESENT WHEN edition gate fires, not SR1). The generated C# confirms binding, not a dropped clause: D2.g.cs line 40 `CobolFile.LinageCounter("D2::LPF") + 1L`, D1.g.cs line 40 `if ((CobolFile.LinageCounter("D1::LPF") > 1L))`. So the SR1 screen covers data-name clause operands (ScreenDataNameShape) but not the report-section expression/condition path, which goes through the procedure ExpressionBinder (LINAGE_COUNTER arm of RefExpr) with no data-division check. Also the bare SOURCE LINAGE-COUNTER / SOURCE LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF rejection comes from COBOLNET0899 ('SOURCE LPF does not resolve to a data item') rather than from SR1, which is incidental (the D3 message even misreads the qualifier as the source item). The rule's reach is not whole, so PARTIAL. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85 2002 2014 2023

subject: LINAGE-COUNTER
notes: kb/Work PB1199 (registrar 15b). GR1: "LINAGE-COUNTER references a temporary unsigned integer data item of class and category numeric whose size is equal to the page size specified in the LINAGE clause." (cite.py --check 8.4.3.14.4 -> OK 1)). The NUMERIC half works: NumericRenderer reads CobolFile.LinageCounter(file) at scale 0, so MOVE to a numeric item, arithmetic and numeric relations are right (probe g4: MOVE LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF TO PIC 9(4) after OPEN OUTPUT + one WRITE prints 0002, per §13.18.34.4 GR7 d) set to one at OPEN OUTPUT + GR7 c)3 incremented by one). The capacity half (HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC fold = page size) is the documented CONFORMANCE.md determination. The DATA-ITEM half DIVERGES: FieldOperand wraps the register as BoundComputedOperand(BoundLinageCounterRef), and OperandText.AsString intercepts only intrinsic calls and BoundBinary, so every CHARACTER-context use of a legal numeric integer item falls to Visit(BoundComputedOperand) = EmitText.LoudValue("computed expression in a string context"): compiles clean, then throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time. Measured at --std 85 and 2023 (probe/linage-counter/g2, g3, T1, T2, T3): DISPLAY LINAGE-COUNTER; MOVE LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF TO PIC X(5); STRING LINAGE-COUNTER DELIMITED SIZE INTO WX; IF LINAGE-COUNTER = WX (alphanumeric comparand) -- all crash. Expected: the value of a numeric unsigned integer item (2 after one WRITE) displayed / moved / compared like any other unsigned integer item; nothing in §14.9.11.3 (only message-tag, object, pointer excluded; cite OK 14.9.11.3 1)) or §8.4.3.14.3 excludes it. No covering spec-derived test for the character contexts. Finding: linage-counter-character-context-crash. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85 2002 2014 2023

subject: Report counters
notes: 'In the report section, PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER may be referenced only in a SOURCE clause. In the procedure division, PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER may be referenced in any context where an integer data item may appear.' TWO halves, and each has its own evidence. PROCEDURE DIVISION: the rule names no statement, so the counter is a receiving-capable PLACE resolved at the ONE receiving chokepoint rather than a permission granted per verb — ReportPageCounterPlace, reached from ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving, which every receiver funnels through; the positive golden exercises ten integer-data-item contexts (MOVE, ADD TO, SUBTRACT FROM, MULTIPLY BY, DIVIDE INTO, COMPUTE, ADD GIVING, INITIALIZE, INSPECT TALLYING, UNSTRING WITH POINTER) plus the sending direction in COMPUTE. Before kb/Work PB429 the receiving direction was refused wholesale (COBOLNET0899, 'legal ... not yet implemented'), and four verbs (INSPECT TALLYING, ACCEPT, UNSTRING's POINTER/TALLYING, STRING's INTO/POINTER) resolved their receivers through the SENDING resolver, so the chokepoint could not have reached them either; they now ask ResolveReceiving. REPORT SECTION: ReportSectionNameIn admits a counter only in a SOURCE clause and refuses it elsewhere - the negative golden writes one into a SUM addend, which SR6 of 13.18.54.3 refuses in its own words ('any identifiers it contains may reference entries in any section of the data division other than the report section') while the same program keeps a legal SOURCE IS PAGE-COUNTER in view.

subject: Report counters
notes: kb/Work PB1456 (registrar 15c). SR2 (--check 8.4.3.15.3 "Qualification requirements for PAGE-COUNTER and LINE-COUNTER are defined by 8.4.2.2" -> OK 2)) delegates to §8.4.2.2.3 SR9/SR10 (--check 8.4.2.2.3 "In the report section, an unqualified reference to the PAGE-COUNTER is qualified implicitly by the name of the report in whose report description entry the reference is made" -> OK 10); "Whenever the PAGE-COUNTER of a different report is referenced, PAGE-COUNTER shall be qualified explicitly by the report-name associated with the different report" -> OK 10); LINE-COUNTER twin -> OK 9)). Conforming halves: procedure division qualified refs resolve per report (rcq7 LC1=0004 LC2=0005); unqualified with 2 RDs rejected (rcq2 - wording/code owned by open kb/Work PB1049); qualifier naming a non-report data item rejected (rcq4); a bare SOURCE LINE-COUNTER/PAGE-COUNTER in the 2nd RD takes its own report (rcq7 '05 01'); SOURCE (PAGE-COUNTER OF R2 + 100) in R2 -> 101 (rcq8). Diverging (rejects legal source): (a) SOURCE PAGE-COUNTER OF R1 inside RD R2 -> COBOLNET0899 'a counter of another report ... is not yet implemented' (rcq3) - SR9/SR10's last sentence is the rule that makes it legal and the code comment concedes 'legal'; design doc lists it as staged-loud; NO kb/Work note owns it. notes: kb/Work PB1133 (registrar 15c). CANCEL resolves through the same ResolveVisible (probe:false). Recursive attribute inherited per §11.10.4 GR4 in MakeUnit so a containee of a RECURSIVE container self-calls. Probed (pinned cobol.exe, probe/scope-of-names/r1.cob, --std 2023 and r1_85.cob --std 85): O->A, A->A1 resolve; A1->A (containee calling its non-COMMON container), A1->B (sibling of container), B->A (sibling), O->A1 (grandchild) all EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND via ON EXCEPTION; contained RECURSIVE SNR self-call prints R1 R2. subject: Levels
notes: kb/Work PB1246 (registrar 15b). Rule (cite.py --check 8.5.1.3.2 OK: 'Three types of entries exist for which there is no true concept of level' / '1) Entries that specify elementary items or groups introduced by a RENAMES clause.'). The binder's BindEntries walk handles lvl==66 BEFORE the nesting stack: BindRenames records the alias on the owning record and `continue`s, so a 66 entry neither opens nor closes a group and is never numerically compared to 1-49 levels (66 > 05 would otherwise nest it). The 66 is also the 'entry describing the item' for a following 88 (SR24 b exclusion) without entering the stack. Probe p1 (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): `01 G. 05 GA PIC X VALUE "Y". 88 GA-YES ... 05 GB PIC X VALUE "Z". 66 GR RENAMES GA THRU GB. 01 H. ...` -> FUNCTION LENGTH(G)=2, DISPLAY GR='YZ', following record H unaffected (LENGTH 2) - spec-expected. The level-66 <-> renames-format pairing is LevelNumberPass (§13.18.33.4 GR2b). Covering test pb485_level_number_legal_forms (COBOL-85) writes `66 R-ALL RENAMES H10 THRU H2.` after record H followed by 77/88/01 entries and asserts R-ALL='XYZPQ' and the later items intact - expected values derived from the spec. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The levelless half holds. BindEntries takes lvl==66 before the nesting stack, so a 66 neither opens nor closes a group. But the adjudicator's evidence also leaned on the renames-format pairing (§13.18.33.4 GR2b: a 66 'may be used only as described by the renames format'), and the constraints that make a 66 legitimately levelless are not enforced. (1) SR2 placement: a 66 written in the middle of a record, followed by a further 05, compiles silently, and the 05 is re-attached to the still-open record (LENGTH(R)=2). (2) SR5: a 66 after a 77 attaches to the 77 as its 'owning record', because _lastRoot counts a 77 as a record. `66 RX RENAMES X` over a 77 compiles and runs. BindRenames' _lastRoot model treats a 77 as a record, and a 77 is exactly the entry that has no record. Those defects belong mainly to the sibling rules §13.18.45.3 SR2/SR5, but they show that the 66's 'no concept of level' is modelled as 'transparent to the stack', not as 'a trailing alias of the preceding 01 record'. The golden pins only the legal trailing-66 shape. [code-location note: (lvl == 66 arm: BindRenames, never pushed on the level stack); code-location note: (66 <-> renames format)] || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85,2002,2014,2023

notes: kb/Work PB1246 (registrar 15b). Rule: item 3 (condition-names have no true concept of level) plus the three level-number assignment sentences (cite.py --check 8.5.1.3.2 OK for each: '...for the purpose of re-grouping data items have been assigned the special level-number 66.'; 'Entries that specify noncontiguous data items that are not subdivisions of other items, and are not themselves subdivided, have been assigned the special level-number 77.'; '...condition-names to be associated with particular values of a conditional variable have been assigned the special level-number 88.'). VERIFIED: 88 is outside the hierarchy - BindEntries' lvl==88 arm records the association against lastDescribed and never touches the level stack; probe p1 `01 H. 88 H-AB VALUE "AB". 05 HA PIC X VALUE "A". 05 HB PIC X VALUE "B".` -> LENGTH(H)=2 and H-AB true; `05 GA ... 88 GA-YES ... 05 GB` -> LENGTH(G)=2, GA-YES true (the 88 neither made GA a group nor closed G). 66/88 format pairing enforced by LevelNumberPass (§13.18.33.4 GR2b/GR2c). 77 'not subdivisions of other items' verified (p1: 77 after an open 05 is a root). NOT VERIFIED / DIVERGES: 77 'are not themselves subdivided' has no failure branch. Probe p4 (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): `01 R. 05 A PIC X. 77 X PIC X VALUE "X". 05 B PIC X VALUE "B".` compiles clean and runs (LENGTH(R)=1, DISPLAY B='B'): the 05 entry written under the 77 is silently promoted to a standalone ROOT because BindEntries pops the stack to empty (77 >= 5) and an empty stack makes ANY entry a root, whatever its level. Probe p2 (`77 X PIC X. 05 Y PIC X.`) is identical at --std 85 and 2023. The spec leaves such an entry no legal reading: it is either a subdivision of the 77 (forbidden by this sentence and §13.13 'provided they do not need to be further subdivided', cite OK) or the first entry of a record description, which §13.11.1 requires to have level-number 1 (cite OK: 'the first of which shall have level-number 1'); §13.5.2's WS general format admits only 77-level, constant, record-description and type-declaration entries. Expected: a compile-time diagnostic. Only the p3 shape (`77 G.` with no PICTURE, then `05 A`) is rejected, and only incidentally by COBOLNET0881 (§13.16.3 SR8, no PICTURE on the now-elementary G). Two halves, one failing -> PARTIAL; finding 'levels-root-entry-level-unchecked'. No existing spec-derived test covers the subdivision half. subject: Computer independent data description
notes: Rule: 'The non-combining character and the following combining characters of a composite sequence defined in ISO/IEC 10646 are each treated as a single character position.' (cite.py --check 8.5.1.4 -> OK §8.5.1.4 1)). The typed-native substrate stores alphanumeric and national text as .NET UTF-16 code units, one char per character position (D-N1; CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-188), with no grapheme/StringInfo/normalization anywhere on the character-position path (searched src for StringInfo/TextElement/EnumerateRunes/Normalize: only the ISO 14651 collation engine and CLDR builder walk codepoints, which is the STANDARD-COMPARE algorithm, not character-position processing). All as the rule requires (base and mark each one position). subject: Computer independent data description
notes: Rule: 'The high-half 2 octets and the low-half 2 octets of a four-octet sequence defined in the UTF-16 format of ISO/IEC 10646 are each treated as a single character position.' and the NOTE: 'Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character' (cite.py --check 8.5.1.4 -> OK §8.5.1.4 2) for both). Code: one .NET char per character position; REVERSE is Array.Reverse over chars (splits the pair, as the rule requires); NationalCollation native order = code-unit order. subject: Alignment of data items in storage
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 8.5.1.6.4 "By use of the SYNCHRONIZED clause." -> OK §8.5.1.6.4 1)): synchronization is accomplished by the SYNCHRONIZED clause. The same clause says "The way in which data is stored is determined by the runtime module, and need not respect these natural boundaries" (--check OK) and lists byte boundaries among natural boundaries; §13.18.55.4 GR9 "The effect of this clause is defined by the implementor" (--check OK) and GR3 leaves positioning to the implementor. COBOL.NET accepts SYNC/SYNCHRONIZED [LEFT|RIGHT] on elementary items in every edition, records it on DataItem.Synchronized, and per the documented determination DOC-A.1-195 performs NO physical alignment (natural boundary = byte), so a synchronized item is trivially aligned and generates no FILLER. subject: Dynamic-capacity tables
notes: kb/Work PB1411 (registrar 15b). Rule: 8.5.1.9.1 1) 'its occurrences are created dynamically' (cite.py --check 8.5.1.9.1 "its occurrences are created dynamically" -> OK 8.5.1.9.1 1)). CobolDynTable<T> is an out-of-line growable store; GrowTo creates and seeds occurrences [old..new) on demand, RefReceiving grows on a receiving subscript past the current capacity (8.5.1.9.3, --check OK 'a new element is automatically created and the capacity of the table is increased to the value given by the subscript'), SetCapacity grows/shrinks explicitly. Probe p3: MOVE 8 TO LZ(100000) in LOCAL-STORAGE -> LC=0000100000, LZ(100000)=8; 7-level nested dynamic tables grow on demand (p4 A7=4). Covering golden dyn_implicit_grow (expected values derived from 8.5.1.9.2/.9.3 in its header). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Occurrences are NOT created dynamically when the receiving operand is an element of a dynamic-capacity table that is a VARIABLE-LENGTH GROUP (an element containing a nested dynamic table). The variable-length-group MOVE emitter renders the receiving element through RefSending instead of RefReceiving (the two-arm dispatch shape), so a MOVE to such an element past the current capacity does not create it, does not raise the capacity, and writes into the benign scratch slot -- the data is silently discarded (wrong answer, no diagnostic). All elementary/fixed-group receiving shapes I probed DO grow correctly (MOVE, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE, COMPUTE, STRING INTO, UNSTRING INTO, ref-mod receiver, INITIALIZE, INSPECT REPLACING, ACCEPT, SET 88 TO TRUE, CALL BY REFERENCE, nested dyn in dyn, dyn in fixed OCCURS, LOCAL-STORAGE, arithmetic subscripts), so the rule is half-verified => PARTIAL. The cited golden dyn_implicit_grow pins only an elementary MOVE and also asserts undefined content (E3 without INITIALIZED per 8.5.1.9.5) and a checking-off sending-past-capacity read, so it does not pin this branch. subject: Dynamic-capacity tables
notes: kb/Work PB1269, PB1144 (registrar 15b). Rule (--check OK 8.5.1.9.6 1)): EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW 'shall exist when a dynamic-capacity table has an expected capacity and an operation causes this expected capacity to be exceeded. If the change in capacity was implicit and the expected capacity had already been exceeded before the operation, no exception shall exist.' + 'If checking ... results in the execution of a declarative procedure ... that executes a RESUME statement with the NEXT STATEMENT phrase, the operation shall be allowed to continue, thus exceeding the receiving table's specified expected capacity' (--check OK). VERIFIED CONFORMING: subscript-driven implicit growth raises on the FIRST crossing only (RefReceiving `occ > exp && _count <= exp`), growth proceeds with checking off or a declarative completing normally; golden conformance:2014/ec_bound_overflow pins that half. DEFECT A (wrong-answer), probe p1: >>TURN EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW CHECKING ON, FROM 2 TO 4, declarative USE AFTER EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW doing RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT, MOVE 22 TO WS-E(6) -> observed DECL=EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW, CAP=0000000002, E6=000; spec: the operation continues and the table exceeds its expected capacity -> CAP=0000000006 (E6=022). Cause: RefReceiving raises BEFORE GrowTo and NonfatalIfEnabled throws RaiseResumeSignal for RESUME NEXT STATEMENT, unwinding past the growth. DEFECT B (silent), probe p2: sender group with a TO-less dynamic table grown to 6, MOVE S TO R where R's table is FROM 1 TO 4 -> R recreated at capacity 6 (RC=0000000006) but FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS blank; spec: the MOVE (14.6.9.2 'recreates or overwrites the receiving table', --check OK) exceeds the expected capacity 4 from 1 -> EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW. Cause: GroupImageCodec FromVarImage -> CobolDynTable.FromCurrentImage -> SetCapacity, the explicit-SET primitive, which raises EC-BOUND-SET (14.9.39.4 GR30, --check OK) - a condition whose checking gate binds only on SET nodes (EcBinder SetCapacityNames) - so under the MOVE's ambient EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW gate nothing is recorded; and even with EC-BOUND-SET on it would name the SET-statement condition and ignore GR1's implicit 'already exceeded' exemption. OPEN READING (not asserted as a defect): probe p6 SET K UP BY 5 over TO 4 with EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW on -> no EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW (EC-BOUND-SET only, by design, EcBinder.cs ~line 359 comment). GR1's 'If the change in capacity was implicit' qualifier implies explicit changes are within GR1 too; whether an explicit SET raises EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW in addition to GR30's EC-BOUND-SET needs adjudication. ec_bound_overflow covers only the conforming half, so test-ref is empty (test-needed). notes: kb/Work PB1410 (registrar 15b). Rule (--check OK 8.5.1.9.6 2)): 'The fatal EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT exception condition shall exist when an operation attempts to increase the capacity of a dynamic-capacity table to a value higher than the maximum capacity of the table based on the resources available at runtime.' 8.5.1.9.1 defines the maximum capacity as the limit 'imposed by the implementor and by current resource availability' (--check OK).
