DEFECT (crashes), probe p5c: element group of 40 x PIC 9(18), SET K TO 1000000000 (below MaxOccurrences) with EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT checking on -> the process dies with the .NET message 'Out of memory.' and no COBOL exception; spec: the request exceeds the maximum capacity 'based on the resources available at runtime', so the fatal EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT shall exist (abnormal termination naming EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT, or a USE declarative for it runs). subject: Variable-length data items
notes: PERMISSIVE rule: §8.5.1.11.3 says the resources 'MAY be freed automatically when' the listed event occurs, and 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' (Annex A item 220: required, need not be documented). The only binding content is that freeing is unobservable ('this has no effect on the results of the execution of the program') and persistence equals a fixed-length item's. COBOL.NET's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Editions: the facility is ISO 2014+ (Annex E item 17 of 2023 records only the SET SIZE enhancement as new, so the items pre-exist in 2014). Event 1 (object finalized): OBJECT working-storage variable-length items are per-instance managed fields; they become unreachable with the instance and are collected with it. Probe probe/vldi/p2.cob (CLASS-ID CDYN, OBJECT WS with OCCURS DYNAMIC + DYNAMIC LENGTH; two instances, FILL on O1, SHOW both, SET O1 TO NULL): output 'CAP=0000000006 D=[HELLO]' / 'CAP=0000000001 D=[]' -- per-instance storage, no sharing, released with the instance. No spec-derived test pins OO-instance variable-length data (none exists; the freeing itself is unobservable).

COBOL.NET's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Editions: the facility is ISO 2014+ (Annex E item 17 of 2023 records only the SET SIZE enhancement as new, so the items pre-exist in 2014). Event 5 (fatal exception): a fatal exception not handled terminates the run unit (§14.6.13), and with it every managed object; release at run-unit termination is within the implementor-defined timing. Not separately observable.

subject: Variable-length data items
notes: PERMISSIVE rule: §8.5.1.11.3 says the resources 'MAY be freed automatically when' the listed event occurs, and 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' (Annex A item 220: required, need not be documented). The only binding content is that freeing is unobservable ('this has no effect on the results of the execution of the program') and persistence equals a fixed-length item's. COBOL.NET's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Editions: the facility is ISO 2014+ (Annex E item 17 of 2023 records only the SET SIZE enhancement as new, so the items pre-exist in 2014). Event 6 (reduced in size): a dynamic-length shrink returns current[..n], a NEW string, so the old buffer is garbage immediately. A dynamic-capacity table shrink (SetCapacity n<_count) only lowers _count: the T[] backing array is not trimmed and the vacated slots keep their element values (and any string references) until the table itself is collected or the slots are re-seeded by GrowTo. That is RETENTION, which the permissive 'may be freed' plus implementor-defined timing admits; the binding half -- no observable effect -- holds because GrowTo re-seeds every slot in [old,new) through _seedAt before exposure. Probe probe/vldi/p1.cob: MOVE 'AB' TO E(4); SET CP TO 2; SET CP TO 4 -> 'E3=ZZ E4=ZZ' (the VALUE seed, not the stale 'AB'); dynamic-length MOVE 'HELLO', SET SIZE 2, SET SIZE 4 -> 'D=[HE  ]' (§14.9.39.4 GR39 spaces, truncated content not resurrected). Implicit reduction (MOVE of a shorter value) is the Store path, a new string. At --std 2014 SET SIZE is correctly COBOLNET0900 (Annex E item 17). Observation for the owner, not a defect: the untrimmed array means a table shrunk from a huge capacity keeps its peak memory for the table's lifetime -- a quality-of-implementation choice inside the latitude.

subject: Variable-length data items
notes: PERMISSIVE rule: §8.5.1.11.3 says the resources 'MAY be freed automatically when' the listed event occurs, and 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' (Annex A item 220: required, need not be documented). The only binding content is that freeing is unobservable ('this has no effect on the results of the execution of the program') and persistence equals a fixed-length item's. COBOL.NET's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Event 7 (overwritten with a new value) + the implementor-defined timing sentence: CobolDynString.Store returns the sender string (or its truncation) and the field is re-assigned, so the previous string is unreachable at once and collected by the GC at a GC-chosen time; a table overwrite (FromCurrentImage/element store) replaces element values in place. Probe probe/vldi/p1.cob: after 'HE  ' a MOVE 'Q' gives 'D=[Q] 1'. The second sentence ('The actual time ... is implementor-defined') is Annex A item 220 'required ... does not have to be documented', so no CONFORMANCE.md row is owed; COBOL.NET's answer is 'when the CLR garbage collector reclaims the unreachable object'.

subject: Variable-length groups
notes: Condition 1 of the compatibility determination - 'For each dynamic-capacity table in either group there is a corresponding table in the other group as specified in 8.5.1.12.2, Positional correspondence' - is the dynamic-capacity arm of the ONE positional walk (kb/Work PB204). Correspondence is 8.5.1.12.2 sentence 2's 'at least one of them is a dynamic-capacity table and they occupy the same relative byte positions within their groups', computed over DataItem.ByteWidth, which already carries 8.5.1.12.3's two collapse conventions by construction (a dynamic-length item is zero bytes; a dynamic-capacity table carries no Occurs so a parent sums one element). The relation is CONSULTED at the activation boundary 14.8.2.2 / 14.8.3.2 name, through OoConformance.DescriptionMismatch - the one comparator shared by the Format-2 CALL, CALL RETURNING and INVOKE. POSITIVE: pb204_vlg_boundary crosses a matched dynamic-capacity pair at position 3 and the callee's growth returns to the caller. NEGATIVE: pb204-nested-vlg-table-correspondence puts a dynamic-capacity table opposite a non-table at the same position and is rejected naming this rule. 8.5.1.12.2's last-sentence latitude (a dynamic-capacity table beyond the shorter group's last character corresponds to a space-filled fixed-length table) is implemented in VariableLengthCompatibility.Tail.

subject: Variable-length groups
notes: Condition 2 - 'For each pair of corresponding tables, these tables match, as specified in 8.5.1.12.3, Matching' - is the same walk's matching arm: 8.5.1.12.3 sentence 2's 'the byte length of their elements is equal and their elements are compatible', the second conjunct RECURSING into the same relation (VariableLengthCompatibility.Elements) because a table of variable-length groups is exactly the shape the condition exists for. Sentence 3's 'the dynamic-capacity table is considered to be the same length as the corresponding table' when only one side is dynamic, and sentence 4's single-element length when both are, are applied as the pair's position advance - a fact about a PAIR, which is why it cannot live on either item. POSITIVE: pb204_vlg_boundary's 3-byte elements match and the crossing recovers the callee's capacity by dividing the carried content by that element width. NEGATIVE: pb204-nested-vlg-element-width corresponds two tables of 3- and 4-byte elements and is rejected naming this rule.

subject: Variable-length groups
notes: Condition 3 - 'For each dynamic-length elementary item in either group there is a corresponding dynamic-length elementary item in the other group as specified in 8.5.1.12.2' - with 8.5.1.12.2 sentence 1's 'start at the same relative byte positions within their groups' as the correspondence and 8.5.1.12.3 sentence 1's 'Two dynamic-length elementary items always match, regardless of their definitions' as the matching. POSITIVE: pb204_vlg_boundary and pb204_vlg_invoke each pair a dynamic-length item across the boundary against a group whose FIXED members are split differently (1+2 against X(3), and 2+1 against X(3)), so the rule is observed to key on byte position and not on the declaration tree. NEGATIVE: pb204-nested-vlg-position (an argument/formal pair) and pb204-nested-returning-incompatible (a RETURNING pair, through 14.8.3.2) each displace the item by one byte and are rejected naming this rule.

notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB129): the _outermost final-transfer flag is now cleared by EVERY recursion - BoundNegate, BoundPower and BoundComputedOperand join BoundBinary - so a division under a unary minus, an exponent base or an operand wrapper computes at the D2 guard scale with truncation and the receiver's ROUNDED mode binds to the final transfer only (14.7.4.3 GR3-GR10; 8.8.1.2 r1's treated-as-a-single-operand). Pinned twice: (1/3) ** 0 under PROHIBITED is exactly 1.00 (the CA5 sibling - the leak reinstated the pre-CA5 spurious EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION), and (A/B) ** 2 = 1 * (A/B) ** 2 = 11.1111 (the leak made multiplying by one change the value).

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is GR2's four-rank hierarchy (1st unary +/-, 2nd exponentiation, 3rd multiply/divide, 4th add/subtract). The IMPLEMENTATION was already correct and is unchanged: powerExpression puts a full unaryExpression in its base position, so `- 2 ** 2` binds as (-2)**2. What was PARTIAL was the EVIDENCE - rank 1 over rank 2 was pinned NOWHERE, and it is the one rank whose answer differs from every mainstream language, so a regression would have looked like normal behaviour. tests/conformance/2023/pb158_arith_precedence_spine now pins all four ranks in one labelled golden with every expected value derived from GR2/GR3 rather than from a run: R1 `- 2 ** 2` = 4 (rank 1 over 2), R2 `2 ** 3 * 4` = 32 (2 over 3), R3 `2 + 3 * 4` = 14 (3 over 4), R4 `2 ** 3 ** 2` = 64 (GR3 left fold), R7 `8 / 4 / 2` = 1 (GR3 left fold on /), and R5/R6 as the parentheses-vs-precedence discriminator. It also replaces the previous evidence's dependence on pb69 T11, where the precedence fact was INCIDENTAL to a golden about the Int128 carrier and would have vanished silently if that expression were ever rewritten.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: Citation re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.8.1.2 "the order of execution of consecutive operations of the same hierarchical level is from left to right"` => OK §8.8.1.2 3). || UPHELD, with my own evidence rather than the adjudicator's. Derived first: every level left-folds, exponentiation included — the standard states no right-associativity exception for `**`, so `2 ** 3 ** 2` = (2**3)**2 = 64, not 512. READ: `ExpressionBinder.BindChain` is `foreach (var child in StatementBinder.Children(node)) { if (child is AddOpContext or MulOpContext) op = child.GetText()[0]; else { var x = BindExprCore(child, context); acc = acc is null ? x : new BoundBinary(acc, op, x); } }` — a strict left fold serving BOTH AdditiveExpressionContext and MultiplicativeExpressionContext; and `ExpressionBinder.BindPower` is `acc = BindExprCore(bases[0], context); for (int i = 1; i < bases.Length; i++) acc = new BoundPower(acc, BindExprCore(bases[i], context));` — the same left fold for rank 2. I ALSO CHECKED THE CHILD ENUMERATOR the adjudicator took on trust: `StatementBinder.Children` is `for (int i = 0; i < node.ChildCount; i++) yield return node.GetChild(i);` — plain index order, no filtering, so no operand can be skipped and no pair re-ordered. `CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith`, the only other walker of this tree, left-folds identically over `node.ChildCount`. || TEST EVIDENCE VERIFIED BY READING BOTH GOLDENS AND THEIR .out FILES, not by trusting the citation: (a) tests/conformance/2014/func_expr_arg.cob header says verbatim '** folds LEFT per 8.8.1.2 r3', its body has `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MAX(2 ** 3 ** 2, 1)` and func_expr_arg.out asserts `POW=00064` — right-folding gives 512, so it discriminates rank 2 and cites this exact rule; (b) tests/conformance/2002/arith_standard.cob has `COMPUTE W1 = 2 / 7 * 7` into PIC 9V9(5) with hand-derived §8.8.1.5 arithmetic in the header, and arith_standard.out asserts `W1=200000` — `2/(7*7)` = 0.0408 would print 004081, so rank 3 left-to-right is pinned, in the SDIDI lane. Both are spec-derived (hand-derived expectations, ISO citations in the headers), neither is a differential, neither is nist:/characterization:/MatchesLegacy. Rank 4 (`A - B - C`) has no golden, but it is the SAME `BindChain` loop already discriminated at rank 3 by (b) — associativity is decided once, in the binder, and no renderer re-associates (I verified `CombineCore` emits self-parenthesized forms only). Rank 1 is prefix-unary, where 'left to right' has no content. || I ALSO CHECKED THE SUBSCRIPT FAST PATH, a second evaluator the adjudicator did not consider: `ReferenceResolver.RenderSegment` splices `+ - * / ( )` into C# text, and C# gives those operators the same precedence and the same left associativity as COBOL, and `**` has no case arm so it routes to the D18 materializer — so rule 3's ORDER holds there too. (That path's VALUE defect — C# integer division — is recorded against GR-8.8.1.2-1; it is not an ordering defect.) The `_outermost` leak recorded against GR-8.8.1.2-1 likewise does not touch associativity. Editions: no Annex E change item for §8.8.1.2 (scanned); batch default.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is Table 3's symbol-adjacency matrix. WHICH CELLS THE GRAMMAR CAN STILL PRODUCE WAS MEASURED, one probe program per cell, parsed through the real compiler rather than reasoned about: ten of the thirteen invalid cells are already hard parse errors ((ident,ident), (binop,binop), (binop,')'), (unary,binop), (unary,')'), ('(',binop), ('(',')'), (')',ident), (')',unary), (')','(')), and two more - (ident,'(') and its sibling - cannot form as an arithmetic PAIR at all because COBOL reads a '(' after an identifier as a subscript or reference-modifier. Exactly ONE cell was producible: (unary, unary). It is now screened by ExpressionFormationPass over the shared frontend rule, covering all THREE evaluating arms (ExpressionBinder.BindExprCore, CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith, and its SoleNumericLiteral reclassification probe, which used to fold `- - 5` to the literal 5). The screen reads TOKEN POSITIONS, not the tree, because SS8.3.3.3.2 rule 2 makes an ADJACENT sign part of the numeric literal - `- -2` is the PERMISSIBLE (unary, literal) pair while `- - 2` is the invalid one, and in the default lexer mode both emit MINUS MINUS INTEGERLIT. A grammar tier would have rejected both, i.e. rejected legal source. The over-rejection guard is pinned positively (golden R10/R11/R12 and three unit cases).

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB136): both defects of the D10 transitional subscript evaluator closed. (1) The splitter's new-segment logic now handles a depth-0 '(' - after ')' or a literal it always opens a NEW subscript; after an IDENTIFIER the split is DECLARATION-INFORMED (a name with no OCCURS cannot be subscripted, so its '(' begins the parenthesized-expression subscript the spec's own NOTE 2 prints, while `DOG (BAKER (I) 3)` keeps BAKER's paren as its own subscript) - the rule-5 restructuring the batch-8 note asked for, threaded as an optional predicate so the intrinsic-argument caller keeps its exact behavior. (2) A quotient-bearing segment routes to the D18 exact evaluator UNCONDITIONALLY: the old token splice was C# integer division over long reads, so an all-integer quotient truncated silently where GR1b evaluates the exact result - (3+4)/2 = 3.5 now raises the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT fatal when checking is on (probed verbatim) and takes the documented lenient truncation otherwise. PB41's scaled-operand routing caught only segments with scaled OPERANDS; the all-integer quotient was exactly the case it could not see.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: CONFORMS as of 2026-08-03 (fix-queue PB28, landed this session). Rule 6 has three parts. r6a (zero base requires exponent > 0) and r6c (negative base requires an integer exponent) are mandatory 'shall' requirements setting EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION, Fatal in Table 14. BEFORE the fix the STANDARD-DECIMAL arm enforced both (CobolDec.Pow) and EVERY NATIVE arm enforced neither, so the same program answered differently depending only on whether an ARITHMETIC clause was present: 0 ** 0 returned 1 (IEEE's convention, not COBOL's) and -2 ** 0.5 returned 0 (Math.Pow yields NaN and the quantizer made it zero), both with an ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken. subject: Simple boolean condition
notes: Rule: 'Boolean-expression-1 shall reference only boolean items of length 1.' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.3.3 OK). BoolExprAllLengthOne walks every leaf; a violation is COBOLNET1511. Probed n1.cob: IF B8 (PIC 1(8)), NOT B8, B8 B-AND B8, BW B-AND B8, B8(1:2), G2 (GROUP-USAGE BIT of 2 bits -- §13.18.29.4 GR1b PICTURE 1(m), cite.py --check OK), BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(1,2), B-NOT B8, PERFORM UNTIL B8 all -> COBOLNET1511; EVALUATE TRUE WHEN B8 -> COBOLNET1634 (Table 15). Legal side: every length-1 form in p1.cob accepted; a run-time-length ref-mod (B(1:N)) fails open, correct for a syntax rule (pb589_bool_refmod_width.cob covers that acceptance). Note (not a divergence): the code also refuses a boolean LITERAL longer than 1 (`IF B"10"`, `IF BW B-OR B"10"`); the SR's words name only items, but such an expression's result is not 1 or 0, so GR1 assigns it no truth value -- refusing it is the only reading under which the condition is defined. Shift with a long operand (`IF B8 B-SHIFT-L 1`) is refused, but by the wrong diagnostic (COBOLNET2318, the FMT finding's HasBoolOp mechanism). No spec-derived NEGATIVE test exists for the procedure-division SR1 refusal (CompileTimeBooleanCceTests covers the >>IF CCE path only) -- test-needed. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85 -- boolean data/operators arrive at 2002; the 2023 Annex E.2 item 3 adds ONLY the B-SHIFT-* operators at 2023, so a shift-form boolean-expression-1 is 2023-only)]

subject: Simple boolean condition
notes: kb/Work PB1412 (also PB1464, PB1465) (registrar 15c). Rule: 'Boolean-expression-1 evaluates true if the result of the expression is 1 and evaluates false if the result of the expression is 0.' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.3.4 OK, rule 1). BoundBooleanCondition renders as value==1 (ConditionRenderer, CobolBool truth value). Probed p1.cob: BW=1 -> T1, BZ=0 -> F3, BW B-XOR BW -> F13, B-NOT BZ -> T11, USAGE BIT/NATIONAL/GROUP-USAGE BIT/ref-mod/BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(1,1)/literal B"1" all true, PERFORM UNTIL BW does not loop, EVALUATE TRUE WHEN BZ/WHEN BW selects the BW arm; same output at 2002/2014/2023. The shift-form and parenthesized-bare-operand inputs never reach this rule (refused at bind -- owned by the FMT-8.8.4.3.2 finding, not a truth-value defect). boolean_ops.cob's simple-condition block (IF F / IF G / F B-OR G / F B-AND G / B-NOT G) is spec-derived (its header cites the Annex A Table A.2 oracle). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR1 covers every legal boolean-expression-1, and three legal shapes never reach evaluation. (a) The 2023 shift-only forms (IF BW B-SHIFT-L 1, B-SHIFT-LC, (BW B-SHIFT-RC 1)) are refused with COBOLNET2318, which calls them an arithmetic expression. The cause is in the cited file: ConditionBinder.BindPrimaryBoolean dispatches to BindSimpleBooleanCondition only when HasBoolOp(be[0]) is true, and HasBoolOp recognizes only B_AND/B_OR/B_XOR/B_NOT, not the four B-SHIFT tokens. A shift-only expression therefore falls into the 'defensive' bare-operand arm, where UnwrapBareBool returns null because of the shift suffix, and it is refused. COMPUTE BR = BW B-SHIFT-L 1 works (0) and IF BZ B-OR BW B-SHIFT-L 1 compiles, so the defect is only in the condition dispatch. (b) A parenthesized bare operand IF (BW) / IF ((BW)) is refused with 2318 through the same arm. (c) A parenthesized sub-expression after a binary operator or B-NOT (IF BZ B-OR (BW B-AND BW), IF B-NOT (BW B-XOR BZ)) fails to parse (COBOL0001), which Table 4 of 8.8.2 permits; it also fails in COMPUTE, so that is a grammar defect. Where the rule is reached the truth mapping is right, but an edge is unverified, so the verdict is PARTIAL. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85 -- boolean data/operators arrive at 2002; the 2023 Annex E.2 item 3 adds ONLY the B-SHIFT-* operators at 2023, so a shift-form boolean-expression-1 is 2023-only)]

subject: Simple boolean condition
notes: kb/Work PB1412 (also PB1464, PB1465) (registrar 15c). Rule: 'The condition NOT boolean-expression-1 evaluates to the reverse truth-value of boolean-expression-1.' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.3.4 OK, rule 2). NOT is the condition-level `NOT primaryCondition` and applies to the WHOLE boolean expression, since B-operators bind inside booleanExpression. Probed p1.cob: NOT BW -> F2, NOT BZ -> T4, NOT BW B-OR BZ = NOT(1) -> F5, NOT BZ B-AND BW = NOT(0) -> T6, NOT B-NOT BZ -> F12, NOT B8(1:1) -> T10, NOT (BW B-AND BZ) -> T15, NOT BW AND BZ = (NOT BW) AND BZ -> F16, EVALUATE NOT BW WHEN TRUE/WHEN FALSE -> FALSE arm. `NOT NOT BW` is refused (COBOL0001), which is correct: §8.8.4.11.3 Table 5 NOTE 'the pair 'NOT (' is permissible while the pair 'NOT NOT' is not permissible' (cite.py --check OK). `IF NOT (BZ)` is refused by the FMT-row paren mechanism (finding), not by NOT handling. l1_search_when_boolean_omitted.cob WHEN NOT WS-B(IX) cites this GR and expects occurrence 1. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR2 has the same domain as GR1, 'NOT boolean-expression-1' for every legal boolean-expression-1. The reversal is correct wherever it is reached, and the adjudicator's probes plus mine (r1/r2 NOT BW OR BZ -> F, BZ OR NOT BZ -> T, BZ AND NOT BZ -> F, r4 NOT (BW B-XOR BZ) -> F) confirm it. But legal NOT forms are refused before evaluation: IF NOT BW B-SHIFT-L 1 at 2023 (COBOLNET2318, the HasBoolOp dispatch hole in ConditionBinder that omits the B-SHIFT tokens), IF NOT (BZ) (2318, the bare-paren arm), and NOT over a B-op followed by a parenthesized sub-expression (COBOL0001). The NOT-over-shift edge (2023) and the NOT-over-parenthesized-operand edge are unverified, so the verdict is PARTIAL. The test-ref l1_search_when_boolean_omitted pins only NOT over a bare subscripted item. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85 -- boolean data/operators arrive at 2002; the 2023 Annex E.2 item 3 adds ONLY the B-SHIFT-* operators at 2023, so a shift-form boolean-expression-1 is 2023-only)]

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB571. All three arms of SR1 are screened at the ONE class-condition operand screen, which every spelling of the condition reaches (the IF form, 14.9.13.3 SR5's identifier-less form, and the EVALUATE selection subject's own class test, which used to be bound by a separate copy). The class list is asked through ItemCategory.IsIndexMessageTagObjectOrPointer for a data-item reference - the population that also answers for MESSAGE-TAG and FUNCTION-POINTER, whose entries never gain a PicInfo - and through IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf for the operand shapes that are not one (an index-NAME, an intrinsic of 15.2 item 6's index class, the NULL predefined address). The variable-length group arm delegates to ReferenceResolver.HasVariableLengthSubordinate, which IS 8.5.1.12.1's definition. The strongly-typed-group arm keeps the COBOLNET1533 strong-typing family's own code (that family is split by rule) and the other two are COBOLNET2200; the split is stated in the code so it is not re-argued.

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB590. SR3's list - alphabet-name-1, ALPHABETIC, ALPHABETIC-LOWER, ALPHABETIC-UPPER, BOOLEAN, class-name-1 - is the set of ClassConditionModel rows carrying ClassOperandRule.UsageDisplayOrNational, and NUMERIC is deliberately absent from it because SR8 states the same rule with a category escape. The predicate reads the operand's OPERAND picture (DataItem.OperandPic), so a bit or national GROUP answers as the elementary item 13.18.29.4 GR1b/GR2b makes it; a null picture is an ordinary alphanumeric group or a picture-less leaf and fails OPEN, which is the direction a screen must fail. Measured: `01 BT PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT. IF BT IS BOOLEAN` draws COBOLNET2202 where it previously compiled. The rule has no edition axis - the class condition and every alternative in its list except BOOLEAN exist at COBOL-85, and BOOLEAN is unreachable as a keyword below 2002 because it is not a reserved word there.

notes: Rule: 'If the data item referenced by identifier-1 is a zero-length item, the truth value of the class condition without the word NOT is false.' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.4.4 -> OK §8.8.4.4.4 1)). notes: Rule: 'If the word NOT is specified, the truth value is reversed.' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.4.4 -> OK §8.8.4.4.4 2)). All three class-condition bound shapes render `c.Negated ? !(test) : (test)` over the GR1/GR3 test, so the reversal applies after the zero-length FALSE as the rule order requires. Probed: ZL NOT NUMERIC -> T, ZL NOT ALPHABETIC-UPPER -> T, AX(1:0) NOT HEXC -> T, READ '12A' NOT NUMERIC -> T, 'ABC' NOT ALPHABETIC -> F. pb590 case D asserts the NOT reversal derived from GR2; ca7_class_zero_length asserts it at zero length.

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB225 + PB823 (wave 45 A) closed the two residues on this row. (1) PB225, items g)-m): g)/m) FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO / NEAREST-TO-ZERO read AlgebraicRanges, the extremes HIGHEST-/SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC and SET format 15 already share (Annex D.32), compared through the one relation renderer for a fixed-point item; DETERMINATION: 'whether that value is positive or negative' admits EITHER direction's extreme (it differs only for a two's-complement container, 13.18.60.4 GR12 - PIC S9(4) COMP-5 is FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO at -32768 and at 32767). h)-k) and every float question are decided by CobolFloatClass on the carrier's RAW ISO/IEC 60559 bits (the typed field, or a REDEFINES window's bits), never a widened value - a binary32->binary64 widening quiets a signaling NaN. l) compares the item's range with ArithmeticModes.IntermediateExtremes exactly; every declarable description is contained, so it reduces to 'a numeric value' (finite for a float). n) 1. b. is now implemented: NUMERIC over a STANDARD float usage is true only for a finite value (a FLOAT-BINARY-64 infinity was folded to TRUE). (2) PB823, item n): which of n) 1./n) 2. applies is decided by the OPERAND's category through THE ONE reader, so a reference-modified signed DISPLAY item (category alphanumeric, 8.4.3.3.4 GR6 c) takes n) 2.'s all-digits test and the over-punched image 123M is NOT numeric (it answered TRUE). Items a)-f) as before (PB109, PB64 T5, PB590); the ALPHABETIC classification selector is PB760's ObjectComputerEmit.ClassificationArg.

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB1466 (registrar 15c). Rule (GR3 n)1): numeric-category operand - a. display/national: sign presence agrees with the description and the rest is digits 0-9; b. standard float: true only if finite; c. otherwise: 'consists entirely of a valid representation for the usage and, if a PICTURE clause is specified, the numeric value is within the range of values implied by the PICTURE clause'. cite.py --check 8.8.4.4.4 for 'If the category of the data item referenced by identifier-1 is numeric', the a. text and the c. text -> OK (the tool labels them '3) d) 2.' - a transcription-numbering artifact). What conforms: windowed leaves (REDEFINES view / StoreAsImage) go through CobolNum.IsNumericImage (zoned sign-aware via ZonedSign, packed nibble + range, binary range) - pinned by conformance:85/pb230_class_numeric_image and conformance:2023/pb803_sign_valid_set; b. via FloatTest(Finite) - conformance:2014/pb225_float_class_conditions; DISPLAY leaves under group MOVE / READ / BY REFERENCE linkage are promoted to StoreAsImage and answer correctly (probed READ 'ABC' -> F, group 'AB1' -> F, linkage 'AB1' -> F, S9(3) '12+' -> F). DEFECTS (both wrong-answer, silent): (1) RenderClass folds IS NUMERIC to the constant `true` for every non-windowed numeric leaf, on the premise 'a native long can only hold a valid value' - but PACKED, BINARY and USAGE NATIONAL numeric leaves are never promoted to StoreAsImage, and their content arriving through an image boundary is decoded (normalised/truncated) by ParseImage. Probes (p2/p3/p5/p6): MOVE X"96" TO G2 (05 G2B PIC 99 COMP, 1-byte) -> G2B IS NUMERIC T (value 150 outside 0..99; expected F by n)1.c; DISPLAY shows 50); MOVE X"ABCD" TO group over PIC 9(3) COMP-3 -> T (nibbles A,B,C invalid; expected F); READ of a record whose PIC 9(3) COMP-3 field holds X"ABCD" -> T (expected F); CALL USING X(2) X"ABCD" into LINKAGE PIC 9(3) COMP-3 -> T (expected F); MOVE N"AB1" TO a GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL group over PIC 9(3) USAGE NATIONAL -> T (expected F by n)1.a). Generated code is literally `if ((true))`. (2) A NUMERIC-category function-identifier (§15.2 4) 'Numeric functions. These are of the class and category numeric', cite OK; SR8 admits it, cite OK) has no BoundFieldOperand, so numericCategory is false and it takes n)2's all-digits test over its display text: IF FUNCTION INTEGER(-5.5) IS NUMERIC -> F, IF FUNCTION NUMVAL("1.5") IS NUMERIC -> F (emitted CobolClass.IsNumeric(NumvalDec("1.5").ToFunctionText())); expected T for both (n)1.c: a valid value of a numeric temporary). Neither mechanism has a kb/Work note (searched open notes). test-ref empty: no spec-derived test covers the defective arms. [editions as adjudicated: a. 85, 2002, 2014, 2023; b. 2014, 2023 (standard floating-point usages); c. 2002, 2014, 2023 (non-display numeric usages in the class condition); 2023 text]

The misrouting of a numeric-category FUNCTION into this test is a defect of n)1 (GR-8.8.4.4.4-L2.1), not of this rule's predicate. Also pinned by conformance:85/pb823_refmod_class_numeric.

subject: Simple condition-name condition (conditional variable)
notes: cite.py --check 8.8.4.5.3 "including the end values" -> OK §8.8.4.5.3 1). A THRU range renders as inclusive >= lo && <= hi (numeric scaled, float double, string via CobolString.Compare or ThruMember under checking); multiple ranges OR together. Probed (probe out/probe/cn/p1.cob (--std 2023), p3.cob (--std 85), p2.cob/p4.cob (2023/2002)): S9(3)V99 VALUE -10 THRU -1.5 true at -10 and -1.5, false at -1.49; VALUE 1 THRU 2, 5, 7.25 THRU 8 true at 2, 5, 7.25, 8, false at 2.01 and 8.01; COMP-3 100 THRU 200 true at 200, false at 201; PIC X(5) "B" THRU "D" true at B and D, false at A and DA. Identical under --std 85. The golden derives FTTTTTFFFF / FTTFFFFFTT from GR1 + §14.7.8 rule 1. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.8.4.5 carries no edition marking; the simple condition-name condition is base COBOL in every edition)]

subject: Simple condition-name condition (conditional variable)
notes: kb/Work PB1477 (registrar 15c). cite.py --check 8.8.4.5.3 "The rules for comparing a conditional variable with a condition-name value are the same as those specified for relation conditions" -> OK §8.8.4.5.3 2). RenderCondition88 classifies the conditional variable once with StringCategoryOf (the relation-surface reader) and takes the collating sequence from ctx.CollateArgFor(cat,cat) — the same comparison-class rule relation conditions use. Probed: alphanumeric short literal space-extended ("AB" vs X(5) 'AB   ' -> T, 'ABC' -> F); PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE with "A" ALSO "a": 88 VALUE "AB" true for 'ab' exactly as the relation A1 = "AB" (both T); unlisted 'c' vs "C" F; numeric algebraic compare across P-scaling (99PP VALUE 1200 T), COMP (VALUE ZERO T), COMP-2 (VALUE 0.5 T), numeric-edited ZZ9.99 VALUE 10 compared to the edited image (T; landed PB97/PB920), national N(3) T, alphanumeric group and group with numeric subordinate compared as alphanumeric (T). A numeric literal with more fraction digits than the item scale would be truncated by UnscaledAtScale, but §13.18.63.3 SR2 makes such source nonconforming (no truncation of nonzero digits), so the path is unreachable for legal source. pb728 golden derives the group/national/boolean class discriminator from GR2 + §8.8.4.2.1. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The comparison is NOT the relation-condition comparison for a conditional variable that is a group containing an OCCURS DEPENDING ON table (legal: SR1 of 13.18.63.3 excludes only strongly-typed and variable-length groups, and 8.5.1.12 defines variable-length group as one with a dynamic-length item or dynamic-capacity table, not ODO). StringMembershipValue sizes a figurative (ALL literal, ZEROS, SPACES...) to parent.ImageWidth = the MAXIMUM extent, while the operand read is the CURRENT extent; the relation IF GV = ALL "X" sizes the figurative to the current operand and answers TRUE where the 88 answers FALSE. Every other probed shape (PIC A, AE, NE, P-scaling, DECIMAL-POINT COMMA, 31-digit, FLOAT-LONG, boolean pad, PCS ALSO range) agrees with the relation rules. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.8.4.5 carries no edition marking; the simple condition-name condition is base COBOL in every edition)]

subject: Simple switch-status condition
notes: GR1: "The result of the test is true if the switch is set to the specified position corresponding to condition-name-1." (cite.py --check 8.8.4.6.3 OK, General rule 1). Renderer emits ExternalSwitches.Get(name) for an ON-STATUS name and !Get(name) for an OFF-STATUS name; SwitchStore holds per-run-unit state, initial from COBOL_<NAME> env (implementor-defined, absent = off), SET overrides. Probe at 85 and 2023: initial OFF -> S1-ON F, S1-OFF T, S2-ON F/S2-OFF T, S3-OFF T; after SET ON -> S1-ON T, S1-OFF F, NOT S1-ON F, S3-OFF F; PERFORM UNTIL S1-OFF loops once; env COBOL_SWITCH_2=ON flips S2-ON T/S2-OFF F. Both halves (ON name and OFF name, true and false) covered: pb400 (SWON/SWOFF subject true/false) and l1_search_when_condition_forms (SW1-ON false then true).

subject: Simple sign condition
notes: kb/Work PB1471 (registrar 15c). SR1: 'Arithmetic-expression-1 shall be any single numeric data item described with a usage other than a standard floating-point usage, or any form of arithmetic expression' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.7.3 1) OK). The operand-closure half is enforced. A non-numeric item is refused: probe p3.cob, IF X IS POSITIVE with X PIC X(3), gives COBOLNET0844, although the message cites §8.8.1.1 rather than the SR1 text the binder passes. Also refused: a non-numeric literal (PB171 landed), an ALL literal (PB218 landed) and an address-identifier (PB1021). The operand is the whole expression, breadth-first (pb171 AB-P/AB-N). The NOTE's parenthesized standard float (FB) is Format 1 (probe: +0 NOT POSITIVE). The PARTITION half diverges. A single FLOAT-SHORT/-LONG/-EXTENDED item has a 'usage other than a standard floating-point usage' (§3.166/§3.167), so it is an arithmetic-expression-1, but IsFormat2FloatSign (Pic.IsFloat) classifies it as Format 2 (see the finding). pb171 is spec-derived for the closure shapes it pins. Its FL=-2 FLOAT-SHORT line passes under either format, so it does not witness the partition.

subject: Simple sign condition
notes: kb/Work PB1471 (registrar 15c). SR2: 'Data-name-1 shall be the name of a single data item in the data division described with a standard floating-point usage, and that name shall not be enclosed in parentheses' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.7.3 2) OK). §3.166/§3.167 define the standard floating-point usages as float-binary-32/-64/-128 and float-decimal-16/-34 only. The 'not enclosed in parentheses' half conforms: SoleDataReference returns null for a parenthesized, unary or operator form, so (FB) is Format 1 (probe). The usage half DIVERGES. IsFormat2FloatSign is ctx.Refs.Probe(dref) is { Item.Pic.IsFloat: true }, and PicInfo.IsFloat includes Float/Double (COMP-1/COMP-2), FloatShort, FloatLong and FloatExtended. PicInfo.IsStandardFloat, the correct §3.166/§3.167 set, exists but is not used. Probe p2.cob: FLOAT-LONG 0 IS POSITIVE gives true, -0 IS NEGATIVE gives true, and FLOAT-EXTENDED 0 IS POSITIVE gives true. Spec (Format 1, GR1): all false. Edge not verified: a subscripted or qualified data-name-1 (SoleDataReference admits subscripts).

subject: Simple sign condition
notes: kb/Work PB1471 (registrar 15c). GR1a: 'If the POSITIVE phrase is specified, the result is true if the value is greater than zero, and false if the value is zero or less than zero' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.7.4 OK, 1) a)). RenderSign's Format-1 arm (algebraic >0/<0/==0, CompareU for unsigned-wide, DecSign for SDIDI after PB84 landed) is correct and was probed: N=-5 NEGATIVE true, N - N ZERO true, unsigned M=0 NOT POSITIVE true, N*-2 POSITIVE true (--std 85); (FB) with FB=+0.0 NOT POSITIVE. DIVERGES because SR1 makes a single FLOAT-SHORT / FLOAT-LONG / FLOAT-EXTENDED item a Format 1 operand (§3.166/§3.167 exclude those usages from the standard floating-point usages), but it is routed to the Format-2 sign-BIT test. IsFormat2FloatSign tests Item.Pic.IsFloat, which includes FloatShort/FloatLong/FloatExtended and COMP-1/COMP-2, instead of PicInfo.IsStandardFloat. Probe p2.cob (2023 and --std 2002): after MOVE 0 TO FL (FLOAT-LONG), IF FL IS POSITIVE prints FL0 POS (spec: false, because zero is not greater than zero). FLOAT-EXTENDED and FLOAT-SHORT behave the same way. After COMPUTE FL = FL * -1, IF FL IS NEGATIVE prints NEG (spec: false). EVALUATE FL WHEN POSITIVE selects POSITIVE for 0. The answer is wrong in every edition from 2002 on: FLOAT-LONG exists since 2002, but Format 2 not until 2014. The golden conformance:2002/ca8_float_sign_format2 PINS this wrong answer (F2-PZERO-POS / F2-NZERO-NEG on FLOAT-LONG). It is not spec-derived and must be corrected with the fix.

subject: Simple sign condition
notes: kb/Work PB1471 (registrar 15c). GR2a/b: POSITIVE/NEGATIVE is true iff 'the sign of the content ... is positive/negative as specified for its basic floating-point interchange format ... regardless of whether the content ... would evaluate to true in a NUMERIC class test or a ZERO sign test'. GR2c: ZERO is true for a valid representation of zero 'regardless of whether the sign ... is positive or negative' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.7.4 2) OK). RenderSign's Format2Float arm emits !double.IsNegative(v) / double.IsNegative(v) / v == 0.0. That reads the sign bit (NaN and Inf included; widening binary32 to double preserves the sign), keeps ZERO sign-agnostic, and gives false for NaN. SendingRef.SignCondition suppresses EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE per §14.6.13.2 rule 3. Probed with p1b.cob: FLOAT-BINARY-64 +0 POSITIVE true, +0 ZERO true, -0 NEGATIVE true, -0 ZERO true, -0 NOT POSITIVE true, -2.5 NEGATIVE true and NOT ZERO; FLOAT-BINARY-32 +0 POS, -0 NEG; EVALUATE FB WHEN POSITIVE with +0 selects POSITIVE. FLOAT-BINARY-128 and FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/-34 are refused with COBOLNET1564 as processor-dependent (Annex A.3 items 17/19), so their GR2 behavior is outside the claim, not a divergence. PARTIAL for two reasons: (1) the NaN and infinity edges the NOTE singles out were verified by reading only; no probe constructed a NaN or Inf. (2) The SAME predicate over-applies this rule to FLOAT-SHORT/-LONG/-EXTENDED, which the GR-8.8.4.7.4-1 / SR-8.8.4.7.3-2 finding owns.

subject: Simple omitted argument condition
notes: kb/Work/PB757.md landed w46i2. data-name-1 resolves against the formals of the source element containing the condition: the method's own USING formals inside a method body (OoMethodScope.Formals), else the program/function's LinkageFormals. A non-formal is COBOLNET1686 on both arms (negative pb133 for a program, test for a method).

subject: Simple omitted argument condition
notes: kb/Work/PB757.md landed w46i2. One presence fact (OmittedProbe: a program/function formal's null carrier, a method formal's bool presence parameter), rendered by CallEmitter.OmittedTest for the condition and for every forward. a) OMITTED specified - golden TAKE / SUB / PB757F; b) trailing argument omitted - golden TWO and F(W4); c) the argument is itself an omitted formal - golden FWD (method formal forwarded by INVOKE SELF and by CALL), SUB2 (program formal forwarded by INVOKE), and a universal forward (test). All three activation kinds: program, function, method.

notes: kb/Work/PB757.md landed w46i2. NOT and OMITTED form ONE condition: BoundOmittedCondition carries Negated and renders !(test) over the presence fact - golden method TWO's `IF B IS NOT OMITTED` takes both branches (B=WXYZ / B OMITTED).

subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1390 (registrar 15b). Rule: any relation condition except the first may be abbreviated by 1) the omission of the subject. cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.1 "any relation condition except the first may be abbreviated by" -> OK. Binder: BindAbbreviatedRelation inserts carry.Subject and records the newly stated operator (correct; conformance-test covers `A > B OR > C`, `A > B AND > D`, `A < B OR < C OR < D`). Probes: `A = B OR > C OR D`, `A = B OR C AND < D`, `A > B OR < C AND NOT > D` all equal their hand expansions over 81 value tuples. DEFECT: the subject-omitted form is unparseable directly after XOR/EXCLUSIVE-OR (`A = B XOR < C` -> COBOL0001) and after an OR-led abbreviated chain followed by XOR (`OR < C XOR = D` -> COBOLNET0901) — rejects-legal-source at 2023; see the grammar-tier finding.

subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1390 (registrar 15b). Rule: 2) the omission of the subject and relational operator; "Within a sequence of relation conditions, both forms of omission may be used." cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.1 "Within a sequence of relation conditions, both forms of omission may be used." -> OK. Binder: BindSoleOperandCondition makes a bare operand a relation with the carried subject+operator when it is not itself a condition-name/switch/simple-boolean condition (correct; `A = B OR C`, `A < C AND D`, `A = D AND > B AND C` covered by the conformance-test; probe `A = B OR > C OR D` and `A < B AND NOT = C OR D` --std 85 correct). DEFECT: mixing the two forms fails when a bare (or NOT-bare) object follows an AND after an OR-led subject-omitted relation: `A = B OR < C AND D` -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'D' at 85 and 2023; `A = B OR < C AND NOT D` -> COBOL0001; `A = B OR < C XOR D` -> COBOLNET0901. Spec-derived result for A=1,B=2,C=3,D=1: (A=B) OR ((A<C) AND (A<D)) = F. Rejects legal source.

subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1391 (registrar 15b). Rule: "Relation-condition-1 shall not be a boolean relation condition." cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.3 -> OK. A comparison of boolean items/literals is necessarily Format 2 (boolean): §8.8.4.2.3 SR2/SR3 close Format 1 operands to classes alphabetic/alphanumeric/index/national/numeric (cite.py --check 8.8.4.2.3 "All literals shall be of class alphanumeric, national, or numeric." -> OK). Code: only the boolExprAhead() path (a B-operator present) resets the carry (BindPrimaryBoolean); a B-op-free boolean relation goes through BindComparison's relation arm, which sets carry.Subject/Op like any relation. MEASURED (B1 PIC 1 VALUE B"0", B2/B3 PIC 1 VALUE B"1", --std 2023): `IF B1 = B2 OR = B3` compiles clean and prints F; `IF B1 = B2 OR <> B3` compiles clean and prints T (the abbreviation was expanded to B1 <> B3). Expected: a compile-time diagnostic naming §8.8.4.12.3 SR1. (A bare trailing length-1 boolean object — `B1 = B2 OR B3` — is legitimately read as a §8.8.4.3 simple boolean condition and printed T, which is correct.) With a B-operator present (`B1 B-AND B2 = B"0" OR = B3`) the source IS rejected, but only by COBOLNET2319 'refused without a diagnostic naming the rule it breaks; this is a COBOL.NET internal error' — the rule is not named. Under-rejects. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (boolean relation conditions are a 2002 introduction; vacuous at 85)

subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: Rule: "The result of implied insertion shall comply with the rules of Table 5, Combinations of conditions, logical operators, and parentheses." cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.3 -> OK. The inserted relation is bound through the SAME CheckedRelational construction as a written relation and nested in the ordinary logical tiers, so Table 5 adjacency is enforced by the condition grammar: probes `A = B AND NOT NOT C` and `A = B AND NOT NOT < C` -> COBOL0001 (NOT NOT not admitted); `A = B OR NOT` -> COBOL0001; a parenthesized sub-condition starts a fresh scope (BindPrimary) so no insertion crosses a parenthesis. No spec-derived test targets the rejection side (test-needed).

subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1390 (registrar 15b). Rule: insert the last preceding stated subject and the last stated relational operator; "The insertion of an omitted subject and/or relational operator terminates once a complete simple condition is encountered within a complex condition." cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.4 (both sentences) -> OK. Code: AbbrevCarry threaded left-to-right through BindFlatSequence; a fully stated relation sets Subject+Op, an abbreviated relation updates Op only, class/sign/omitted/condition-name/boolean and parenthesized conditions Reset() the carry. MEASURED: probe ab1.cob runs ALL SIX NOTE examples (a > b AND NOT < c OR d; a NOT EQUAL b OR c; NOT a = b OR c; NOT (a GREATER b OR < c); NOT (a NOT > b AND c AND NOT d); NOT (a NOT > b XOR c AND NOT d)) plus three extra chains against their spec expansions over all 81 tuples of A..D in 1..3 -> N=0729 BAD=0000. Termination: `A = B OR C IS NUMERIC OR D` and `A < B AND (C = D) OR D` are rejected (D has no carried subject) with COBOLNET2318. Shapes the parser cannot reach (XOR-led / OR-then-AND-bare tails) are FMT/SR defects, not a failure of the insertion semantics. Conformance-test covers insertion, NOT-in-operator carry, the first NOTE example and the paren fresh scope; the termination-by-class/88 half is not in a spec-derived test. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The insertion semantics are correct on every shape the compiler ACCEPTS: a randomized differential of 270 accepted chains, each with 81 value tuples, gave 0 mismatches against a Python evaluator of the spec expansion (NOT > AND > XOR > OR). The same differential shows the GR is not delivered for a large class of legal abbreviated conditions. Every chain where AND follows an OR-led abbreviated relation is rejected with COBOL0001, and so is every chain where an abbreviated relation follows XOR. That holds whether the AND's right side is a bare object (the adjudicator's OR-then-AND-bare case) or a fully STATED relation. The adjudicator did not report the stated case: `A = B OR < D AND C = 1` is rejected at (11,32) 'unexpected C'. That source is exactly this GR's termination half (a complete simple condition ends the insertion and starts a new subject), and it can never be exercised. About 18 of 290 random AND/OR chains (6%) and 31 of 80 chains with XOR were rejected. The GR has two halves (insert, then terminate at a complete simple condition). The insert half is verified on the reachable shapes. The terminate half is unreachable for OR-abbrev-AND-stated and has no spec-derived test (the adjudicator concedes the class/88 termination is untested). Calling the unreachable shapes only 'FMT/SR defects' is not enough for a CONFORMS on the semantic rule: the rule's effect never occurs for legal source. By the two-halves rule this is PARTIAL. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the XOR example 2023 only)

subject: Conditional expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1432 (registrar 15b). Rule (cite.py --check 8.8.4.13 "evaluation of that hierarchical level terminates as soon as a truth value for it is determined" -> OK §8.8.4.13 1)): the connected conditions within a hierarchical level are evaluated left to right, and evaluation stops once the level's truth value is known. Code: ConditionBinder.BindFlatSequence binds every OR/AND/abbreviated-AND chain (full and EVALUATE partial-expression spines) in source order into BoundLogical("||"|"&&"), and ConditionRenderer.Visit(BoundLogical) emits the parenthesized C# short-circuit operators, so each parenthesized or implied level becomes one C# sub-expression that is evaluated left to right and short-circuits. Side-effecting operands in non-first positions (user-function activations) are attached per evaluation (UdfAttachPerEvaluation), so they are not hoisted ahead of the short-circuit. XOR is rendered with ^ and evaluates both operands, which is correct because an XOR level's truth value is never known from one operand. Probe with the pinned cobol.exe under >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON (out/probe/cond-expr/p1.cob): a skipped OR/AND operand holding an out-of-range subscript T(0), a divide by zero 10/Z, a reference modification S(1:0), FUNCTION SQRT(-4) and FUNCTION MOD(10 0) raised nothing (A1 A2 B1 B2 G1 J1 J2). Negative controls n1/n2/n3 with the operand reached raised EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT, EC-SIZE-ZERO-DIVIDE and EC-BOUND-REF-MOD, so the probe is not vacuous. Tracing UDF activations: A AND B AND C -> ABC; G=0 OR (H=1 AND I=0) OR J=1 -> GHIJ; (K=0 AND L=1) OR M=1 -> KM (L skipped); WS-A = 5 OR TRC("O") abbreviated -> no activation; WS-A = 6 OR 5 OR TRC("Q") -> no activation; NOT (P=1 OR R=1) -> P; EVALUATE TRUE WHEN S=0 AND T=1 / WHEN U=1 OR V=1 -> SU; W=1 XOR Y=0 -> WY (both, left to right). All match the rule. Covering test: conformance:2002/udf_per_eval (C3/C4 prove an AND right operand is skipped when the left is false and an OR right operand is skipped when the left is true, which also shows the left operand is evaluated first). No existing golden covers nested levels or skipped exception-raising operands. That would be a coverage improvement, not a defect. The register note PB987 (landed) covers rule 2 object-property refetch, not this rule. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Rule 1 (cite.py --check 8.8.4.13 "evaluation of that hierarchical level terminates as soon as a truth value for it is determined" -> OK) holds for the evaluation ORDER in every shape probed, but the mechanism that defers a non-first operand until the short-circuit reaches it (the per-evaluation lambda wrapping of a hoisted subscript / reference-modification operand) does not compile under >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON when that operand's subscript or ref-mod position is a user-defined function activation: the lambda body carries the size-error RESUME dispatch 'goto __xfer', which C# forbids inside a lambda (CS0159). Legal source (IF WS-A = 0 OR EL(TRC("C", 1)) = 1) is therefore rejected by the backend, only in the non-first-operand position (the same subscript in the first operand compiles and runs). A rule whose implementing mechanism fails on a legal operand shape is PARTIAL, not CONFORMS. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause 8.8.4.13 rule 1 carries no edition qualifier; the XOR hierarchical level is 2023-only because the XOR operator is a 2023 addition)

subject: Conditional expressions
notes: CONFORMS (kb/Work PB987, w54f). 'Values are established for arithmetic expressions and functions if and when the conditions containing them are evaluated': arithmetic expressions and intrinsic functions render inline inside the C# condition, so C#'s && / || short-circuit (8.8.4.13 1)) and the loop's re-test reach them per evaluation; every HOISTED activation - a user-defined function, an inline method invocation, a function-bearing subscript's temp store (DataBinder.PendingPreOps) and, since PB987, an object-property GET (DataBinder.OoPendingPropertyOps) - is drained by the per-evaluation window it was written in (UdfBinder.Mark marks BOTH lists): a PERFORM UNTIL / VARYING UNTIL condition, a SEARCH WHEN, an EVALUATE object, a non-first AND/OR operand, a VARYING BY / AFTER FROM operand, and runs at each evaluation or not at all. Negated conditions render as C# negation of the inner condition, evaluated when reached. Before PB987 a property reference in PERFORM UNTIL P OF S > 3 was fetched once for the whole loop (K=09 where the rule gives K=03). Witnesses: pb987_property_per_evaluation (UNTIL, AND/OR short-circuit, EVALUATE WHEN order, SEARCH WHEN, VARYING BY), udf_per_eval, pb17_function_subscript.

subject: Files
notes: Rule (9.1.5 item 1): "An external file connector may be referenced from any runtime element that describes that file connector." [cite.py --check PASS 9.1.5]. EXTERNAL FDs key ONE run-unit connector (::EXT:: by FD name). Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\p915\e1.cob (2023) and e85.cob (85): P915E OPENs OUTPUT EF EXTERNAL and writes AAAA; sibling program P915F (own EXTERNAL FD EF, own 01 name) WRITEs FFFF with no OPEN of its own; P915E closes, reopens INPUT; P915G READs -> G-R=AAAA; P915E READs next -> E-R=FFFF. Identical at --std 85 and 2023: one connector shared by three programs, position shared too. Program<->object sharing: conformance:2002/oo_external_file_shared (spec-derived; program opens, object writes through the same connector, R1/R2 read back) covers the 'any runtime element' breadth; conformance:2023/pb673_external_assign_executor covers program<->program. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change; 'runtime element' reaches objects from 2002) || Code sites (adjudicator, verbatim): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/RunUnit.cs#RunUnit (run-unit file-connector registry); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Oo/OoDriver.cs (program<->class sharing is EXTERNAL only); src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/CobolObject.cs

subject: Files
notes: Rule (9.1.5 item 2): "both programs may refer to a common file connector by referring to an associated global file-name either in the containing program or in any program that directly or indirectly contains the containing program" [cite.py --check PASS 9.1.5]. Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\p915\g1.cob (2023) / g85.cob (85, EXIT PROGRAM): A declares FD GF GLOBAL, OPENs OUTPUT, writes AAAA, CALLs contained B which WRITEs BBBB (B-W 00) and CALLs C (contained in B, i.e. INDIRECTLY contained in A) which WRITEs CCCC (C-W 00); A CLOSEs, reopens and reads R=AAAA R=BBBB R=CCCC then EOF 10. TEST-NEEDED: conformance:85/pb369_global_file_use_selection references the global file-name from B and C but each OPEN fails (35), so it never demonstrates the connector is COMMON; tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/SpecFixTests.NestedProgram_ReadsContainingGlobalIndexedFile_SharesConnector exercises the LEGACY compiler and does not qualify. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (nested programs + GLOBAL are COBOL-85; no Annex E change) || Code sites (adjudicator, verbatim): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/BinderDriver.cs (containers' GLOBAL FDs merged into FilesByName); src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/RunUnit.cs#RunUnit

subject: Files
notes: Rule (9.1.11 item 1): "No valid record position has been established." [cite.py --check PASS 9.1.11]. The state is modelled as LastReadUnsuccessful (base) plus the keyed validity bit (IndexedConnector overrides InvalidateFilePosition); set by every unsuccessful START (StartOpenModeGuard applies GR7), every unsuccessful READ (GR18 via ApplyUnsuccessfulReadPosition / the guards), cleared only by a reposition (OPEN / START / successful READ) — the setter-independence comment names why a WRITE does not clear it. subject: Polymorphism
notes: CONTEXT (applies to every 9.3.5.3 row): the seven items define the METHOD RESOLUTION SIGNATURE. The feature that DISTINGUISHES methods by it (overloading) is optional -- cite.py OK 9.3.5.3 7) 'Parametric polymorphism is an optional feature' -- and is NOT claimed (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 5 A.4.10 item 3; refused COBOLNET0822 in OoClassTable.Build, both instance and factory arms). But the signature is consumed by MANDATORY rules: cite.py OK 8.4.6.5 'The methods declared in an object class definition shall have unique method resolution signatures', OK 11.7.3 3) 'If the OVERRIDE phrase is specified, there shall be a method with the same method resolution signature', OK 11.7.3 9) (conformance of an inherited/implemented same-named method). inventory-schema.json derived-verdicts.oo-optional-items-only deliberately EXCLUDES these rows and asks for per-row adjudication, so no selector covers them. COBOL.NET's signature is the degenerate one (the NAME: roster key ExternalizedName) and the remaining components are enforced as SR9 conformance by OoConformance.ValidateOverrideSignatures -> MethodConformanceMismatches -> DescriptionMismatch (COBOLNET0829); for any program that does not overload, a component is conforming iff that comparator rejects every override the component distinguishes. Probes: out/probe/polymorphism/p*.cob, pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023 default. Rule: cite.py OK 9.3.5.3 1) 'The method name'. The name (the externalized name, PB303 roster key) IS the implemented signature: TryAddMethod/TryAddFactoryMethod refuse a second same-named method (COBOLNET0822 -- for identical parameters that is exactly 8.4.6.5's duplicate-signature error; for differing parameters it is the declined overloading), and MarkRoster pairs an override with its base by that key (0838 when OVERRIDE finds no base, 0837 when a same-named base method lacks OVERRIDE per 11.7.3 SR4a). Probe p1 (sub OVERRIDE M, PIC X(4) vs base PIC 9(4)) pairs by name and is rejected 0829. notes: kb/Work PB1051: Rule (cite.py --check 9.3.6 -> OK §9.3.6 1)): a method of the name defined in the class OF THE OBJECT that is an exact match is bound. Code binds by NAME (the roster is keyed by name; TryAddMethod refuses a second same-named method, COBOLNET0822) and dispatches on the runtime class (C# virtual override for typed receivers; the __CobolInvoke switch chain for universal). Why name-first binding is EQUIVALENT to the exact-match-first algorithm here: parametric polymorphism is optional (§9.3.5.3 'Parametric polymorphism is an optional feature', cite OK) and NOT claimed (CONFORMANCE.md A.4.10 item 3; §2 row 45 N/A), and multiple class inheritance is not claimed (COBOLNET0849), so a class holds at most one method per name and a same-named method in a subclass is an OVERRIDE whose formals ValidateOverrideSignatures (COBOLNET0829) holds identical to the base's. Exactness depends only on the PARAMETERS ('A method invocation is considered to match exactly if all parameters match exactly'; the returning item only enters the tie-break), and identical formals answer exactness identically in base and override — so the class-of-the-object's method wins whenever any does. I checked the one tempting counter-case, a COVARIANT RETURNING override (OoSpineTests.CovariantOverrideReturning_And_SignClauseConformance prints WOOF): it is NOT a divergence, because the returning item is not a parameter. Probe out/probe/objects-p1/p1.cob: A1 (typed OBJA) holding an OBJC ran OBJC's M (M-C). The OVERLOAD half of this rule (several same-named methods, one exact) belongs to the declined optional item — not a verdict of this row. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The class-of-the-object-first half is verified. The golden oo_inherit shows a DOG through an ANIMAL reference printing WOOF; RQ1 shows the typed and universal receivers running RFC's M2. The adjudicator's reduction also holds: with one method per name, §11.7.3 SR9 conformance (§9.3.8.2.3 1)/3)) forces identical formals in an override, so exactness answers identically in base and override. But 'exact match ... as specified below' is defined for BY VALUE parameters too (match rule 5 and the exact-match criteria 'for each parameter that is passed by value or by content'), and that edge is unverifiable. subject: COBOL compilation group
notes: kb/Work PB1086: Rule: 'Compilation of a program prototype definition or a function prototype definition generates information required for the external repository, as specified in 8.13, External repository.' (cite.py --check 10.6.3 -> OK §10.6.3 1)). §8.13: 'Whether the information is taken from a prototype or a definition, the information stored in the external repository about the signature of a program or a function is the same.' (OK §8.13); 'The implementor shall provide a mechanism that allows the user to specify whether to update the external repository when a compilation unit is compiled.' (OK §8.13); and '... whether to flag differences in prototypes and definitions in the compilation group from the information in the external repository.' (OK §8.13). WHAT THE CODE DOES: a prototype's signature (LINKAGE formals + RETURNING) is generated and consumed IN-GROUP only - BinderDriver.BuildProgramDetailsTable (programs, GR10 b)) and the user-function table (functions) - so a caller in the SAME compilation group gets the prototype's details (witnessed by conformance:2002/udf_prototype and PB894's goldens). That half is met. The other half is not: this implementation declares its external repository to be the run-unit program registry (BinderDriver.cs:913/945, PrototypeSignatures.cs:32, docs/COBOLNET_INTERPROGRAM_DESIGN.md), and ProgramEmitter.cs:632 skips every prototype ('a prototype registers no runtime module - the separately-compiled definition does (§10.6.3 GR1)') - so compiling a prototype contributes NOTHING to that repository; the §10.6.3 GR1 citation there is used to justify the opposite of what GR1 says. PROBE proto_only.cob (PROGRAM-ID. CGPO IS PROTOTYPE. with LINKAGE A / PROCEDURE DIVISION USING A. / END PROGRAM CGPO.) compiles clean at 2023 and emits a module with no repository record; a later separately-compiled caller naming CGPO in its REPOSITORY therefore takes §12.3.8.4 GR10 c) with a NULL signature (PrototypeSignatures: 'An UNRESOLVED prototype conforms'), so no compile-time conformance check against that prototype is possible. Neither §8.13 mechanism (update / flag differences) exists: the CLI (--help) has no repository option and src has no repository store. Not owned by any kb/Work note (PB612/PB817/PB989 mention the external repository only as GR10 c)'s fallback). Verdict PARTIAL: in-group generation verified; generation for the external repository across compilations absent. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (prototype definitions and the external repository §8.13 are post-85)

SUM CLAUSE - not routed; ReportWriterEmitter documents (and I re-derived) that a SUM accumulation is one aligned addition of fixed-point values (§13.18.54.3 addends are never float) whose exact result fits both Int128 and a 34-digit SDIDI, so the engines are digit-identical for every reachable SUM. The adjudicator verified the SUM arm by re-deriving the emitter comment, not by probing it. subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152), COBOLNET1727. 'Hexadecimal-alphanumeric literal' is a DEFINED TERM and the screen is written to it, not to a paraphrase: 8.3.3.2.2 gives the alphanumeric literal exactly two general formats - format 1 ("..." / '...') and format 2 (X"..." / X'...') - and 'hexadecimal-alphanumeric' names FORMAT 2, so a one-character format-1 literal such as "Z" is NOT admitted however short it is. One byte is exactly two hexadecimal digits (8.3.3.2.3 SR5). Before the screen the decoder took raw[0] for ANY shape, so INITIALIZE ALL TO "AB" silently became 'A'. The 2026-08-30 analysis that scoped this work carried the paraphrase 'a one-character alphanumeric OR one-byte hex literal', which would have shipped an under-reject; the printed page (PDF 307 / folio 277) was rendered and read to settle it. PB151's own golden pb151_options_fill was written with the format-1 spelling and is repaired to X"51" by this landing - 0x51 IS 'Q', so its expected output is unchanged byte for byte.

subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152). All five GR5 arms. ⛔ GR5 b/d resolve through FigurativeConstants.FillChar - the compiler's ONE definition of the alphanumeric high and low value, which 8.3.3.6.4 GR6 makes a PROGRAM-COLLATING-SEQUENCE-dependent fact rather than a constant - and NOT through a second map. This was measured wrong: PB151's landed ALLOCATE arm carried its own GR5 map spelling HIGH-VALUES as U+FFFF while every other HIGH-VALUE in the compiler is U+00FF under the native sequence. GR5 a is kept SEPARATE from GR5 d on purpose: 'a string of binary zeros' is the literal zero byte while 'the alphanumeric low value character' is the collating minimum - they coincide natively and diverge under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE. pb152_options_initialize_arm_agreement asks all three consuming arms the same HIGH-VALUES question in one program.

subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: kb/Work PB1511: Rule (cite.py --check 11.9.11.2 "If native arithmetic is in effect, the rounding rules that apply to intermediate data items are defined by the implementor" -> OK, rule 1; companion cite.py --check 8.8.1.3 "The implementor shall specify techniques used for native arithmetic" -> OK). What the code defines under NATIVE: (i) fixed-point operands on a scaled Int128, EXACT for the 14.7.7 31-digit composite (no intermediate rounding); (ii) a quotient NESTED in a larger expression computed at receiver/operand scale + DivGuardDigits (14) with TRUNCATION (NumericRenderer.cs ~615-651); (iii) any float operand -> IEEE binary64 (.NET round-to-nearest-even); (iv) a Dec-carried operand (float literal, float numeric-edited sender, integer power) -> the SDIDI lane rounded per the OPTIONS INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING mode (IntermediateMode in CombineCore), so the clause DOES reach native statements on that lane (kb/Work PB274 landed; CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-82 says so). The implementor has defined the rules and the implementation is deterministic. WHY PARTIAL: the published determination the rule depends on (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-123 'Native arithmetic - techniques used, intermediate data item') says 'a nested quotient carries up to 14 guard fraction digits and rounds once, at the final transfer' - the guard-digit TRUNCATION (a second, intermediate rounding) is not stated, nor is the binary64 lane's rounding rule, and the INTERMEDIATE-ROUNDING-on-the-Dec-lane rule is stated only inside DOC-A.1-82 (a floating-literal item). The rule is implemented but only partly stated where a user would look. PB298's IntermediateRounding row is answerable from this read: the field IS consumed (NumericRenderer.IntermediateMode; IntrinsicRenderer 125/127/1031; NumericRenderer 163/568-571/857). No spec-derived test pins a native intermediate ROUNDING decision (l1_native_arithmetic_intermediate pins Int128 exactness, not rounding) -> test-ref empty. Editions follow the clause (2014,2023).

subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: kb/Work PB1510: Rule 3 a-e (cite.py --check 11.9.11.2: 'If the INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause is not specified, the NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO phrase is implied' -> OK a); 'If two such values are equally near, the value farther from zero is chosen' -> OK b); 'the value in which the rightmost digit of the significand is even shall be delivered' -> OK c); 'the EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION exception condition is set to exist and the results of the operation are undefined' -> OK d); 'the value shall be the nearest value in that format that is nearer to zero than the intermediate value' -> OK e)). VERIFIED: (a) OptionsModel.IntermediateRounding defaults to NearestAwayFromZero; (b)/(c)/(e) Round34Wide's switch is right when the dropped digits share the result's sign (pb145_round_away/even/trunc TIE/TIE2/L36/SUB legs, 2023, spec-derived and correct); (d) Round34Wide throws CobolSizeError EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION on any inexact reduction (pb145_round_prohib, pb74_sdidi_intermediate_prohibited_ec). DEFECT (new, no register note): CobolDec.AddSigned aligns operands whose exponents differ by more than the 38-digit scratch head-room by TRUNCATING the low operand (ShiftDownSticky: sig / 10^n, truncation toward zero) and hands Round34Wide an UNSIGNED sticky bit, which Round34Wide treats as a positive excess below the round digit in the RESULT's direction. With OPPOSITE-sign operands the discarded tail REDUCES the result's magnitude, so the kept digits over-state |value|: TRUNCATION delivers a value FARTHER from zero than the intermediate (breaks e), and a round digit 5 whose true tail is below one half rounds up under NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO / NEAREST-EVEN (breaks b/c). PROBE (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/irstk, ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL, R PIC S9 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE): INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING IS TRUNCATION: COMPUTE R = ((1 - 1.0E-50) - 1) * 1.0E+34 owed -1 (1 - 1E-50 truncates to 0.(34 nines)), got +0; COMPUTE R = ((1.0E-50 - 1) + 1) * 1.0E+34 owed +1, got +0; control ((1 - 1.0E-36) - 1) * 1.0E+34 (gap within head-room, no sticky) -> -1 correct. Default mode (rule a/b): COMPUTE R = ((1 - (5.0E-35 + 1.0E-60)) - 1) * 1.0E+34 owed -1 (0.(34 nines)4999... rounds DOWN), got +0; same under NEAREST-EVEN (rule c) owed -1, got +0. Expected values cross-computed with Python decimal at prec 34 per mode. PROHIBITED (d) unaffected (sticky alone makes it inexact). No test covers the opposite-sign far-exponent add; test-ref empty.

notes: Rule = GR7 k)3 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "Any characters of the native collating sequence that are not specified in the literal phrase shall assume a position" -> OK): unspecified characters follow the highest specified position, in unchanged native relative order. CODE: CollatingTable is sparse; an unspecified code unit c takes position NextFree + (c - |specified codes < c|), computed arithmetically at run time (LiteralPhraseCollation), over the full 65,536-unit set for both classes. subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB1093: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "If more than one character has the highest position in the program collating sequence, the last character specified is associated with the figurative constant HIGH-VALUE" -> OK §12.3.7.4 8)): "The character that has the highest ordinal position in the program collating sequence is associated with the figurative constant HIGH-VALUE, except when this figurative constant is specified as a literal in the SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph"; tie -> last character specified. CODE: CollatingTable.Extremes starts the HIGH walk at (char)0xFFFF for the national arm - correct, since GR7 k3 puts every unspecified character above the specified block, so the highest position is the largest UNSPECIFIED code unit, with GR8's tie rule when the whole repertoire is specified - but at (char)0xFF for the ALPHANUMERIC arm ('the documented byte-stability pin'), although the same table places the alphanumeric tail over the full 65,536-unit native set (CollatingTable.Repertoire; runtime LiteralPhraseCollation). MEASURED (probe/snp3/g10a.cob, --std 2023): PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL, ALPHABET AL IS HIGH-VALUE "B" "A" -> MOVE HIGH-VALUE TO Y; Y = X"FF" is FALSE (the walk skipped the specified U+00FF and landed on U+00FE), and MOVE FUNCTION CHAR(257) (U+0100) TO X; X > Y is TRUE - a character collates ABOVE HIGH-VALUE, which GR8 makes impossible. Expected from the spec: HIGH-VALUE = U+FFFF (the last native code unit, k3's highest tail position); no character compares greater. Same shape for every alphanumeric literal-phrase alphabet and for the EBCDIC code-name (whose 256 specified positions make Extremes fall through to the tie rule over the Latin-1 block, while U+0100..U+FFFF sit above them per the implementor's own GR7 i adoption of k3). National half verified correct by reading (alphabet_national golden pins U+FFFF); the tie rule verified by reading only. No open kb/Work note owns this; the pin is described as 'flagged' in docs/COBOLNET_DESIGN.md §14.9/§18 #14 and PHASE4_RECONCILIATION but has no owner decision and no register note. Finding: 'alphanumeric HIGH-VALUE pinned to U+00FF over a 65,536-character native set'. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the national program collating sequence half from 2002)]

CODE: Extremes takes specOrder[0] - the first character specified always occupies position 0 (AlphabetLiteralPhrase assigns positions in source order; a refused duplicate (SR14 a) never enters specOrder; a THRU+ALSO entry refused by COBOLNET2242 contributes nothing), and a position-0 ALSO tie resolves to that same character. Identity sequences (NATIVE / STANDARD-1/2 / UCS-4 / ASCII) -> U+0000, the lowest native code unit. MEASURED (probe/snp3/g9also.cob): ALPHABET AL IS "B" ALSO "A" ALSO "Z", ... -> LOW-VALUE = 'B' (tie, first specified); (probe/snp3/g9loc.cob) ALPHABET LOC IS LOCALE as PCS -> ORD(LOW-VALUE) = 1 and X"01" = LOW-VALUE (U+0000 shares the lowest, completely-ignorable rank with other C0 controls; U+0000 is the lowest code among them - the locale sequence has no 'specified' order, CONFORMANCE.md §3 L7 documents LOW-VALUE U+0000 under a locale sequence). da1_alphabet_hex_thru derives LOW-VALUE = 'Z' for ALPHABET AL IS X"5A" THRU X"41" from the lowest position (spec-derived expected). subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB1093: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "the figurative constants HIGH-VALUE and LOW-VALUE are associated with those characters having the highest and lowest positions" -> OK §12.3.7.4 10)): inside SPECIAL-NAMES, HIGH-VALUE / LOW-VALUE are the highest / lowest characters of the NATIVE national collating sequence under NATIONAL, else of the NATIVE alphanumeric collating sequence. CODE: AlphabetFigurative is the ONE mapping for ALPHABET literal-phrase and CLASS operands (both classes, figurative token or >>COBOL-WORDS synonym): LOW-VALUE -> U+0000 (both classes, correct), national HIGH-VALUE -> U+FFFF (correct: the native national set is the 65,536 UTF-16 code units in code-unit order), alphanumeric HIGH-VALUE -> U+00FF. The native alphanumeric set is ALSO 65,536 code units in code-unit order (measured probe/snp3/g6n.cob: ORD(CHAR(65536)) = 65536, and natively CHAR(257) = U+0100 > HIGH-VALUE), so U+00FF is NOT the highest character of the native alphanumeric collating sequence. MEASURED (probe/snp3/g10a.cob): ALPHABET AL IS HIGH-VALUE "B" "A" as PCS -> X"FF" < "A" is TRUE and ORD(X"FF") = 1: the alphabet placed U+00FF first. Expected from the spec (under the implementor's own GR6 definition): the character at position 1 is U+FFFF; U+00FF stays at its GR7 k3 tail position (above 'A'), so X"FF" < "A" is FALSE. LOW-VALUE and the national HIGH-VALUE halves CONFORM; the alphanumeric HIGH-VALUE half DIVERGES -> row DIVERGES. Same mechanism as GR8 (one finding). Not owned by any open note (PB940, open, concerns only the duplicated WORD-recognition half of AlphabetFigurative, not its value). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the NATIONAL-phrase half from 2002)]
