subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB1094: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "a delimiter shall directly follow the data described with dynamic-length-structure-name-1" -> OK §12.3.7.4 19)): with DELIMITED, a delimiter of one alphanumeric (resp. national) character with all bits zero directly follows the data. CODE: the Delimited flag is recorded on Model/DynamicLengthStructure and read by nothing else (grep 'Delimited' over src/Cobol.Net.*: only the model and its binder); CONFORMANCE.md §3 D-DL3 justifies non-materialization with 'no operation gives it an addressable byte image'. MEASURED, refuting that premise: a dynamic-length item is accepted inside an FD record and WRITE gives the record a byte image. probe/snp3/g19b.cob (--std 2023): DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE DLD IS DELIMITED; FD F. 01 R. 05 D1 PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH DLD. 05 D2 PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH DLD.; MOVE "AB" TO D1, "CDE" TO D2, WRITE R, CLOSE, OPEN INPUT, READ F -> file bytes = 05 00 00 00 'A''B''C''D''E' (no delimiter after either item) and the READ yields D1=[ABCDE] LENGTH 5, D2=[] LENGTH 0. Expected from the spec: record data 'A''B'X'00''C''D''E'X'00' (each item's data directly followed by the binary-zero delimiter), and the round trip gives D1='AB', D2='CDE'. Sibling (GR18, the PREFIXED length field, a p2 row): g19c.cob with SHORT PREFIXED is byte-identical and loses the boundary the same way. Owning note: PB991 (open analysis, inventory_rows [GR-12.3.7.4-19]) - its premise 'not observable in the typed-native carrier' is refuted by this measurement; the finding extends it rather than filing a duplicate. Whether §8.5.1.10.3 ('may be located elsewhere in the computer's memory') licenses omitting the item from the record image entirely is an open latitude question, but the implementation does NOT omit it - it inlines the content with neither the GR18 prefix nor the GR19 delimiter, which no reading licenses and which loses data. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2014, 2023 (the DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE clause arrives with dynamic-length elementary items, spec D.3.8)]

notes: kb/Work PB702 (claimable since kb/Work PB324 landed; the row stayed GAP with an empty verdict while GR-12.4.5.3-3 already named the same goldens). RULE: 'Data-name-1 shall reference an alphanumeric data item and shall not be subordinate to the file description entry for file-name-1.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.2 'Data-name-1 shall reference an alphanumeric data item and shall not be subordinate to the file description entry for file-name-1' -> OK, §12.4.5.2 7)). TWO HALVES, AND BOTH ARMS OF EACH ARE MEASURED. CODE: DataBinder.ResolveAssignUsing is the single site. Half 1 (category) is IsAlphanumericDataItem — an elementary PIC X item, or a group with no GROUP-USAGE clause, which 13.18.29.4 GR3 makes 'an alphanumeric group item'; category-ALPHABETIC (PIC A) is excluded because 8.8.4.2.4's 'A class alphabetic operand shall be treated as though it were an operand of class alphanumeric' is a COMPARISON rule and not a category identity, and bit/national groups are excluded by GroupUsage. An unresolvable name takes the same arm (there is no alphanumeric data item to reference), COBOLNET1810. Half 2 (subordination) walks item.Parent up to the root and fires COBOLNET1811 if any ancestor is one of THIS file's record descriptions — 'subordinate to the file description entry' means anywhere under a record description of that FD, which is the reading 9.1.21 corroborates ('The USING phrase references an alphanumeric data item whose content at the time an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement for that file is executed uniquely identifies the specific physical file to be accessed'), because an operand inside the file's own record area is overwritten by every READ of that file. MEASURED on this worktree's build (c34f01ad): `cobol pb324-assign-using-not-alphanumeric.cob --std 85` -> 'error COBOLNET1810: file ''NF1'': ASSIGN … USING ''WS-NUM'' shall reference an alphanumeric data item - ''WS-NUM'' is a category-numeric item (ISO 12.4.5.2 SR7)'; `cobol pb324-assign-using-in-own-record.cob --std 2023` -> 'error COBOLNET1811: file ''NF2'': ASSIGN … USING ''N2-NAME'' shall not be subordinate to the file description entry for ''NF2'' (ISO 12.4.5.2 SR7)'. Both negative goldens carry `*> reject-at: 85 2002 2014 2023`, so the REJECTING arm is asserted at every edition. The ACCEPTING arm — the complement, which a rejection test can never measure — is conformance:2023/pb324_assign_using_dynamic and conformance:85/pb324_assign_using_85, both of which name a WORKING-STORAGE `PIC X(20)` item outside the FD and run to a spec-derived expected output. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. §12.4.5.2 carries no edition marker on SR7 and Annex E records no change to the ASSIGN clause; the compiler enforces the rule through one ungated site and both negatives are pinned as rejecting at all four editions. It also says content that is empty after space removal, or that carries a character below U+0020, 'names no physical file: the association cannot be made, so the statement is unsuccessful'. The OPEN arm honors this (FileConnector.Associate), and so does a SORT GIVING file, which goes through the implicit OPEN. The sort-merge file ITSELF does not. notes: kb/Work PB692. "The DYNAMIC and RANDOM phrases shall not be specified for a sequential file" is a FILE CONTROL ENTRY rule, so it is enforced on the entry, in DataBinder.BindFileControl beside the clauses it relates, and not on any verb: it constrains the entry whether or not the file is ever read, written or started. BOTH PHRASES are screened, not just the one the repro wrote (negatives pb692-access-random-organization-sequential and pb692-access-dynamic-organization-sequential are the same entry with RANDOM and with DYNAMIC). ALL THREE SEQUENTIAL SPELLINGS are under it: an explicit ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL, LINE SEQUENTIAL (12.4.5.10.3 GR2 puts the phrase in the ORGANIZATION clause, that clause is written only in the Format 3 entry, and 12.4.5.2 SR11 says "Format 3 shall be specified only for a sequential file or a report file"), and the OMITTED clause, which 12.4.5.10.3 GR6 makes "sequential organization with the RECORD SEQUENTIAL phrase" - the omitted case is the shape a screen keyed on a written clause would miss, and negative pb692-access-dynamic-organization-omitted pins it. subject: General
notes: Rule: "If the access mode is dynamic, records in the file may be accessed sequentially, randomly, or both." (cite.py --check 12.4.5.5.3 -> OK §12.4.5.5.3 4)). subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: RE-SITED 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB699); rule unchanged. RULE (--check 12.4.5.6.3 1): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses." Same move as the RECORD KEY twin: the screen is a row of FileControlKeyRules' table, run at the ENTRY from DataBinder.ResolveFiles, and its subject list is FileModel.AlternateKeyNames - the clauses AS WRITTEN - rather than the resolved AlternateKeys, because a clause whose data-name-1 resolves to nothing is absent from the resolved list. subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB743). RULE (--check 12.4.5.6.3 2): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall be defined as a data item of category alphanumeric or national within a record description entry associated with the file-name to which the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is subordinate." The prime key's twin, worded the same way with the same two obligations, and landed in the same change for the same reason. The asymmetry this closes was visible inside ONE method: KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile already wrote a CATEGORY screen for the RELATIVE key (12.4.5.13.3 SR2, an unsigned integer) and none for either record key. Both arms are now rows of FileControlKeyRules sharing this rule-id, screened at the ENTRY from DataBinder.ResolveFiles, over the clauses AS WRITTEN (FileModel.AlternateKeyNames) rather than the resolved AlternateKeys - a clause whose data-name-1 resolves to nothing is absent from the resolved list and is exactly the case the location arm speaks about. Boundary measured: a category-alphanumeric alternate key WITH DUPLICATES inside the record is accepted at all four editions, and the relative key's own category rule (which REQUIRES the unsigned integer this rule forbids) is measured beside it so the two cannot leak into each other.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: CONFORMS, unchanged in substance and re-homed by kb/Work PB802 - the ALTERNATE-key twin of GR-12.4.5.12.4-3, carrying a SECOND requirement that one does not: 'The number of alternate record keys for the file shall also be the same as that used when the physical file was created.' Both halves are recorded and compared. IndexedConnector.DeclaredKeys puts every alternate key's window, DUPLICATES phrase, 12.4.5.6.4 GR6 SUPPRESS WHEN value and collating sequence into the FRAMED STORE'S HEADER in declaration order (the order key numbers are assigned in) - no longer into a .cbattr sidecar beside the file, but into the file itself, which is where GnuCOBOL's ISAM format keeps the same information. The SUPPRESS WHEN value is length-prefixed in the header rather than delimiter-separated, because GR6 admits any figurative-constant or literal value, including one carrying a NUL or a line ending; a legal COBOL program therefore cannot write a store its own next OPEN refuses. FixedFileAttributes.Conflicts compares the key COUNT before the descriptors, so an added or missing alternate index is itself the 14.9.27.4 GR10 file attribute conflict condition and the OPEN is unsuccessful with '39'. The descriptor's scope and its derivation are the same as GR-12.4.5.12.4-3's, and so is the COBOLNET_KEYCHECK=OFF opt-out (on by default; documented at DOC-A.1-129). Pinned by open_fixed_attribute_conflict_ix step I3 (a connector whose prime key agrees but which declares an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY the file was never built with gives '39') and by the unit test for the count requirement on its own - a description that simply OMITS the alternate, every key it does declare agreeing.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.6.4 "If the DUPLICATES phrase is not specified, the value of the associated alternate record key shall not be equal" -> OK GR4; cross-checked §14.9.51.4 GR42 c) (WRITE '22', --check OK) and §9.1.13.2 2) c) ('02' for a duplicate on a DUPLICATES key). Probe gr4.cob (2023): unique alt key duplicate WRITE -> INVALID KEY '22'; REWRITE creating a duplicate -> '22'; WITH DUPLICATES key duplicate WRITE -> '02'. The collating-sequence half: file G with `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF G-ALT IS FOLD` (ALPHABET FOLD "A" ALSO "a" "B" ALSO "b") - keys "Ab" and "aB" are equal under that sequence and the second WRITE -> '22', so equality is judged under the file's collating sequence (KeyEq -> KeyCompare with the key's weights). Both halves verified. No existing spec-derived test pins the '22'/'02' on an alternate key (grep of tests/conformance ALTERNATE goldens: none asserts 22 on a unique alternate), so test-ref is empty. NOTE: the duplicate check is also where the GR6 suppression defect surfaces (spurious '22' between two records whose keys equal a figurative/short SUPPRESS WHEN value) - that is GR-12.4.5.6.4-6's mechanism, not this rule's.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.6.4 "are implicitly referenced as keys for all other record description entries of that file" -> OK GR5. Keys are registered as a byte WINDOW (offset,length) over the shared record area, so every record description of the FD is keyed at those positions by construction. Probe gr5.cob: FD with 01 R (R-ALT at bytes 3-5) and 01 S; records WRITTEN THROUGH S are indexed on bytes 3-5 (READ KEY IS R-ALT "CCC" finds the S-written record 02; a second S-written record with the same bytes 3-5 -> '22'; the START/READ NEXT walk orders S-written and R-written records by those bytes). The covering test writes through REC-A and STARTs by a sibling-record operand at the same byte position, expected record derived from the spec.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: kb/Work PB1072: cite.py --check 12.4.5.6.4 "shall not be provided when the value of data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 in that record is equal to literal-1" -> OK GR6 (NOTE: "It is as if they did not exist", --find OK GR6). The EXACT-LENGTH alphanumeric case works (goldens altkey_suppress_when, pb695_alternate_suppress_no_when, l1_rewrite_alt_key_suppress). TWO defects in one mechanism: (1) DataBinder.BindFileControl stores `CobolLiteral.Decode(literal.GetText())`, and Decode returns a non-quoted token UNCHANGED, so a figurative constant (SPACES, ZERO, HIGH-VALUES, ...) or ALL "x" becomes its SOURCE TEXT ("SPACES", "ALL\"*\""); (2) IndexedConnector.IsSuppressed -> KeyEq -> KeyCompare is string.CompareOrdinal when the key has no collating weights - no space-extension of a shorter literal (the method's own summary claims space-extension) and no figurative repetition to the key's length. Probe gr6b.cob (2023, SUPPRESS WHEN SPACES on PIC X(6)): key "SPACES" is suppressed (READ KEY "SPACES" -> '23', spec: found, record 01) while an all-space key is NOT (READ KEY spaces -> FOUND 02, spec: '23'), and the third all-space record's WRITE -> '22' (spec: '00', a suppressed key provides no access path, §14.9.51.4 GR41). Probe gr6.cob: SUPPRESS WHEN "X" on PIC X(3) key "X  " not suppressed; SUPPRESS WHEN ALL "*" on "***" not suppressed; SUPPRESS WHEN N"Q" on PIC N(2) "Q " not suppressed; a spurious '02' on WRITE of a record whose DUPLICATES key equals the suppression value. Wrong answers, silent. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2023 (Annex E.3.3 item 42)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1074: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.3 "Alphabet-name-1 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric collating sequence" OK. alphabet-name-1 is validated only LAZILY, when ResolveKeyCollating reaches it for some key. subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: Only one file-level (Format 1) COLLATING SEQUENCE clause per file control entry. CaptureFileCollating counts the Format-1 clauses on the FileModel (FileLevelCollatingCount) and ResolveFileCollating rejects a count above one with COBOLNET1582. The clause is a COBOL-2002 addition (constructs.json file-collating-clause-2002), so 85 is the gate lane, not a behaviour lane.

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: Data-name-1 shall be a name specified as the data-name in an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY or RECORD KEY clause of the file control entry. ResolveFileCollating builds the declared key-name set from FileModel.RecordKeyName plus AlternateKeyNames and rejects any Format-2 name outside it with COBOLNET1582. SR5 (the record-key-name spelling) is NOT claimed by this row: the test names a data-name.

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.3 "Record-key-name-1 shall be a name specified as a record-key-name" OK. ResolveFileCollating builds keyNames from RecordKeyName + AlternateKeyNames and refuses any Format-2 name outside it (COBOLNET1582, 'SR4/SR5'). record-key-name-1 can only be defined by the `record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS` key form, which CONFORMANCE.md row 40 declares Not claimed and DataBinder.DeclineRecordKeySource refuses by name (COBOLNET1954) at every edition — so no accepted program can hold a record-key-name, and every Format-2 name that is not a declared key's data-name is refused. The SR5 arm is therefore enforced (vacuously) for all accepted source; no open note needed (row 40's witnesses are PB358, landed). FileCollatingSequenceSpecTests.KeyLevel_NameThatIsNotAKey_Diagnosed covers SR4's data-name arm, not SR5 — test-ref left empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.3 "Data-name-1 and record-key-name-1 shall not be subscripted" OK. No spec-derived test. subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1074: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.3 "When the class of data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 is national, alphabet-name-3 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national collating sequence" OK. The key's class is never compared with the alphabet's class. Probe p5: national prime key PIC N(1) with `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF IX-KEY IS REV` (alphanumeric alphabet) compiles clean AND applies REV (reads Z,M,A) — under-reject + wrong answer. Probe p6: alphanumeric key with a NATIONAL alphabet-name-3 is refused, but only via COBOLNET1584 'not yet implemented' (not SR7). Probe p10: the LEGAL pairing (national key, `OF IX-KEY IS NREV`) is refused with COBOLNET1584 as an error — the declared P14 GAP of CONFORMANCE row 41-42 (catalog lists 1584 as Warning 'the key orders natively', yet compilation fails). Undeclared alphabet-name-3 (p12) is refused with COBOLNET1583 citing SR1 (should be SR7). Finding M1. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: Neither data-name-1 nor record-key-name-1 shall be specified in more than one COLLATING SEQUENCE clause. The unit the rule counts is the CLAUSE: 12.4.5.7.2's Format-2 figure prints the ellipsis immediately right of the closing brace of { data-name-1 | record-key-name-1 }, so per 5.2.7 the repeated portion is the brace group and one clause may list the same key twice - one clause is never more than one. Enforced by the shared ConstructOperandRegister with the Format-2 clause as its construct (kb/Work PB703); both arms are pinned, plus the one-violation-one-diagnostic count.

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1093: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.4 "Each collating sequence is a fixed file attribute" OK. Each key's collating sequence is persisted as a KeyDescriptor.Collation fingerprint at creation and compared at OPEN: probe p13 opened the REV-collated p8.dat with a no-clause program -> FS=39 (correct fixed-attribute conflict). Unverified edge: Fingerprint hashes only the weights of U+0000..U+00FF, so two sequences that differ only above Latin-1 (national keys now exist per PB327; ALPHABET literals above Latin-1 per pb770; LOCALE collations) fingerprint equal and a conflicting OPEN would not be detected; also an un-probeable sequence answers UNKNOWN which never conflicts. Half verified -> PARTIAL. No spec-derived test pins the 39. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1074: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.4 "An alphanumeric collating sequence referenced by alphabet-name-1 applies to any record keys of class alphanumeric" OK. Alphanumeric keys: correct (conformance:2002/file_collating_seq; probe p8 prime X key under REV reads Z,M,A). But ResolveKeyCollating never consults the key's class: `alphabet ??= file.FileLevelCollating?.Alnum` applies alphabet-name-1 to EVERY key not named key-level, national keys included. Probe p1 (national prime key PIC N(1), `COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS REV`, write A,M,Z) reads back Z,M,A; per GR2 (alnum keys only) + GR5 (national key with no alphabet-name-2 -> native national) the expected order is A,M,Z. Wrong answer, silent. Finding M1. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1074: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.4 "A national collating sequence referenced by alphabet-name-2 applies to any record keys of class national" OK. CaptureFileCollating stores alphabet-name-2 in FileLevelCollating.Nat and NOTHING reads it (only .Alnum is consulted in ResolveKeyCollating). Probe p2 (national prime key, `COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL IS NREV`, NREV = N"Z..A") compiles with NO diagnostic and reads A,M,Z; expected Z,M,A. docs/CONFORMANCE.md row 41-42 declares national-key collating 'NOT claimed — a documented P14 GAP' diagnosed by COBOLNET1584, but the file-level alphabet-name-2 path never emits 1584 — the declared non-support is not even the observed behavior (silent wrong answer). A.3 item 41's latitude covers only alphabets defined with LOCALE or literals, not a code-name national alphabet (e.g. UCS-4). No open kb/Work note owns this row. Finding M1. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.4 "the native alphanumeric collating sequence applies to any record keys of class alphanumeric" OK. When alphabet-name-1 is absent and no key-level clause names the key, `alphabet` stays null -> native ordinal (null weights). Probe p2 (only FOR NATIONAL written): the alphanumeric alternate key IX-ALT read A,M,Z (native); probe p5 (key-level on the prime only): IX-ALT A,M,Z native. No-clause files take the early return to native. No spec-derived test isolates this rule. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1074: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.4 "the native national collating sequence applies to any record keys of class national" OK. With alphabet-name-2 absent but alphabet-name-1 present, a national key receives alphabet-name-1's ALPHANUMERIC sequence instead of the native national one: probe p1 national prime key under `FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS REV` reads Z,M,A, expected A,M,Z (native national). Same class-blind resolution as GR2. Finding M1. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: Alphabet-name-3 applies to record keys identified by data-name-1 or record-key-name-1. ResolveKeyCollating resolves each key's weight table from the Format-2 clause naming it before falling back to the Format-1 default (GR2) and then to native (GR4/GR5). The golden gives the prime key the alphabet REV and the alternate key DREV in the same file control entry and reads the file back on each key: the two halves order DIFFERENTLY (Z,M,A against 3,2,1 = A,Z,M), so neither can pass with the other's sequence applied and neither can pass with native ordinal weights.

subject: FILE STATUS clause
notes: kb/Work PB1080: cite.py --check 12.4.5.8.3 "Data-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses." -> OK SR1. ResolveFiles resolves the FILE STATUS operand and runs no screen on it (compare ResolveLinage, which screens its own OCCURS SR via RecordLayout.IsSubjectToOccurs). Probe p1b.cob: `01 T. 05 FS PIC XX OCCURS 3.` + `FILE STATUS IS FS` compiles clean and the OPEN dies at run time with CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "FILE STATUS item 'FS' is not resolvable to storage (ISO §12.4.5.8)" (the LoudStmt at SequentialIoEmitter.cs:799) — an unhandled process kill where the standard requires a compile-time rejection. The written-subscript form FS(1) IS refused (COBOLNET2024). Finding F1. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023]

subject: FILE STATUS clause
notes: kb/Work PB1080: cite.py --check 12.4.5.8.3 "Data-name-1 shall reference a two-character data item of the category alphanumeric, defined in the working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section." -> OK SR2. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): p2 `PIC 99` -> backend crash `error CS0029: Cannot implicitly convert type 'string' to 'long'` (generated C# fails); p3 `PIC X(3)` compiles, runs, FS='35 '; p4 `PIC X` compiles, runs, FS='3' (also at --std 85/2002/2014); p6 `PIC N(2)` (national) compiles, runs; p9 FS declared as a record of ANOTHER file's FD (FILE SECTION) compiles and runs. Positive halves verified: WORKING-STORAGE (ok.cob) and LOCAL-STORAGE (lsx.cob) PIC XX both work. Finding F1. subject: LOCK MODE clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 6) 'Execution of any I-O statement except START releases any previously locked record in that file for that file connector' OK. Mode selection: MapLockMode sets Multiple only when the MULTIPLE token is present. So both `LOCK ON RECORD` (explicit single) and an omitted LOCK ON phrase (implicit single) give single locking, as the rule states. Release: ReleasePriorRecordLocks is the one site (skipped only when meta.Multiple). It runs at the top of ReadShared, ReadKeyedShared (l.1396), WriteShared (l.1428), RewriteShared (l.1455, except target) and DeleteShared (l.1499, except target), so it is tied to execution, not success (PB338 landed). The mutating verbs' 'except target' comes from their own statement rules (§14.9.35.4 GR12 a), §14.9.10.4 GR7 a)): the target's lock is released at completion instead. START is not routed through any release. CLOSE and UNLOCK release everything. Probe rt1.cob phase 1: A (AUTOMATIC single) read 1, then read 2, and B's read of 1 went from '51' to '00' (READ releases). A re-locked 1 and then did a WRITE of record 21; B's read of 1 was '00' (WRITE releases). subject: ORGANIZATION clause
notes: kb/Work PB1098: Rule: 'The ORGANIZATION clause specifies the logical structure of a file. The file organization is established at the time a physical file is created and cannot subsequently be changed.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.10.3 -> OK §12.4.5.10.3 1) General rules). Half 1 (clause specifies structure): DataBinder.MapOrganization maps LINE SEQUENTIAL / RECORD? SEQUENTIAL / RELATIVE / INDEXED and the absent clause (GR6) to FileOrganization. Half 2 (established at creation, unchangeable): RecordFraming.WriteHeader stamps the organization byte ('I'/'R') into the store header when a new RELATIVE/INDEXED physical file is created; KeyedConnector.FixedAttributeConflict compares it on every later OPEN. PROBED with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/org/mk.cob + sw.cob): an INDEXED store opened through a RELATIVE description -> '39', a RELATIVE store opened through an INDEXED description -> '39'; the golden's S13 pins a sequential file opened as RELATIVE -> '39' and S6 shows OPEN OUTPUT creating a new physical file. The reverse direction (a keyed store opened through a SEQUENTIAL description succeeds, and probe/org/ex.cob showed OPEN EXTEND appending raw bytes that the relative reader then ignores as trailing bytes while the file stays relative) is the §14.9.27.4 GR10 implementor-defined validated set, fixed by owner decision PB802 and pinned by unit FixedFileAttributeFormatTests.AKeyedStoreOpenedThroughASequentialDescription_IsNOTAConflict; the organization recorded in the file is not changed by it. The golden does not pin the relative<->indexed swap (probed only). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — First half (the clause specifies the structure; organization established at creation, OPEN OUTPUT re-creates) holds, and relative<->indexed and sequential->keyed OPENs answer '39'. But 'cannot subsequently be changed' is breachable: a RELATIVE store opened I-O through a SEQUENTIAL FD succeeds ('00'), its first READ returns the store HEADER bytes as a record, and a REWRITE overwrites the header; the file can then no longer be opened as RELATIVE ('39'), i.e. the organization recorded at creation was destroyed by a later program. The adjudicator's claim that the non-validated sequential direction 'does not change the organization recorded in the file' is falsified. PB802 only contemplated INPUT (and EXTEND appends) through a sequential FD, not I-O REWRITE over the header; §14.9.27.4 GR10 latitude governs which attributes OPEN validates, not whether a later program may rewrite the file's organization. Also the cited golden pins only sequential->RELATIVE; relative<->indexed is probe-only. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (version-invariant general rule)]

subject: ORGANIZATION clause
notes: kb/Work PB688 (LANDED 2026-09-05). RULE: "The LINE SEQUENTIAL phrase specifies that the file organization is line sequential. Line sequential organization is a permanent logical file structure in which a record is identified by a predecessor-successor relationship established when the record is placed into the file. Each record in a line sequential file is terminated by an implementor-defined line delimiter. The range of allowable characters in a line sequential file is implementor-defined." cite.py --check 12.4.5.10.3 'The LINE SEQUENTIAL phrase specifies that the file organization is line sequential' -> OK 12.4.5.10.3 2). THE EDITION: the phrase is a COBOL-2023 introduction - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization" (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, the Foreword; Annex E carries no item for it, and it is NOT derivable from VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md, which has no 85->2002 row set). It is a PHRASE of the sequential organization and not a fourth organization: cite.py --check 9.1.7.1 'There are three file organizations: sequential, relative, and indexed' -> OK, and 9.1.7.2 splits the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types - the { LINE | RECORD } inner choice of the 12.4.5.10.2 general format. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe: before, a SELECT with ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL compiled CLEAN at --std 85 (exit 0, .dll emitted); after, COBOLNET0900 at 85, 2002 and 2014 and clean at 2023. DataBinder.MapOrganization is the one recognition site (both grammar parents - the file control entry and the FD clause list - flow through the ONE VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitOrganizationClause arm, pinned by the two negatives). The delimiter and the allowable-character-range determinations this rule leaves to the implementor are answered at docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-115 and by LineSequentialCharacterSet.

notes: kb/Work PB1098: Rule: 'Relative organization is a permanent logical file structure in which each record is uniquely identified by an integer value greater than zero, that specifies the record's logical ordinal position in the file.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.10.3 -> OK §12.4.5.10.3 4)). MapOrganization maps the RELATIVE phrase to FileOrganization.Relative; RelativeConnector is a sparse 1-based slot model (slot = RRN). PROBED (probe/org/mk.cob, ACCESS DYNAMIC): random WRITE with RELATIVE KEY 0 -> '34' (spec §14.9.51 GR29 b: 'If the relative key data item contains a value that is less than 1 ... the I O status ... is set to 34'), READ key 0 -> '23', WRITE key 7 then READ 7 -> '00' seven, READ 2 / READ 5 (no record) -> '23', START >= 0 then READ NEXT -> RRN 0007 (the ordinal position). Sequential-access WRITE numbering from 1 is §14.9.51 GR29 a) (the slot ordinal code at RelativeConnector.cs:376-379). No spec-derived golden located that pins RRN>0 / ordinal identity directly; test-needed. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The identification half holds on every probe I built: RRN numbered from 1, key 0 -> '34' on WRITE / '23' on READ, sparse slots, sequential READ in ordinal order (2,5,9), EXTEND assigns highest+1 (10), DELETE leaves 9 in place, START > 1 then NEXT -> 2,9, OPEN OUTPUT sequential numbers 1,2, duplicate RRN -> '22'. That is the same defect as GR-12.4.5.10.3-1. One half verified, one breached, so PARTIAL. No spec-derived test pins RRN identity either (the adjudicator says so too). subject: ORGANIZATION clause
notes: kb/Work PB1098: Rule: 'Indexed organization is a permanent logical file structure in which each record is identified by the value of one or more keys within that record.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.10.3 -> OK §12.4.5.10.3 5)). MapOrganization maps INDEXED to FileOrganization.Indexed; IndexedConnector keys records by the prime RECORD KEY window and each ALTERNATE RECORD KEY window of the record image (key descriptors also recorded in the store header, FixedFileAttributes.KeyDescriptor). PROBED (probe/org/mk.cob): a duplicate prime key WRITE -> '22'; READ KEY IS prime K002 -> '00' K002AAAAsecond; READ KEY IS alternate AAAA (WITH DUPLICATES) -> '00' the first-written K003 record, READ NEXT continues in the alternate key of reference -> K002; READ of an absent prime K009 -> '23'. No spec-derived golden identified as pinning the identification rule itself; test-needed. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The identification half holds on my probes: an alphanumeric prime key and an alternate key without DUPLICATES identify records (duplicate alternate -> '22', READ by alternate -> the right record, delete removes it from the alternate index -> '23', START LOW-VALUE then READ NEXT walks prime order, REWRITE with a changed prime key in dynamic mode -> '23'). The adjudicator's evidence for permanence (the header key-table check on OPEN) is exactly the header that this path destroys. PARTIAL, and no spec-derived test pins identification. subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "The RECORD DELIMITER clause may be specified only for variable-length records" is NOT enforced, and the licence is express rather than inferred. §4.2.6 ¶3, second sentence: "Although this warning mechanism shall identify processor-dependent elements that are not supported, it is not required to diagnose syntax errors within this unsupported syntax" (cite.py --check OK). The clause is unsupported whole — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26 for the STANDARD-1 arm (Annex A.3 item 26) and §7 A.1 item 150 for the feature-name arm — and COBOLNET1778 names it at every edition, which is the obligation §4.2.6 ¶3 does impose. Enforcing SR1 anyway was considered and REJECTED as a rejects-legal-source risk, not skipped: SR1's own NOTE makes variable-length-ness partly an implementor determination (A.1 items 147-148, both still open), and §9.1.7.2 makes a LINE SEQUENTIAL file's records variable with no RECORD clause written at all, so a test keyed on FileModel.Varying would refuse legal source in order to enforce a rule the standard excuses. The golden's four files are all SR1-legal (RECORD IS VARYING), so nothing here depends on the unenforced case.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "The implementor shall specify the names available for use as feature-name-1" is DISCHARGED, and discharged in the negative: the set specified is EMPTY, filed as docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 Annex A.1 item 150. That is a specification and not an omission — A.1's preamble classes item 150 as optional and defines the class as "Optional: The element may be provided at the implementor's option" (cite.py --check A.1 OK). The compiler agrees with the register: every spelling written in the feature-name-1 position draws COBOLNET1778 naming the clause as unsupported, so no word is silently accepted as a delimiter selector and §12.4.5.11.4 GR4 never has a method to look up. The DOC row for the same obligation is DOC-A.1-150, whose verdict differs by design — that row asks whether the OPTIONAL ELEMENT is provided (it is not), this row asks whether the implementor answered the question (it did).

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "Any method used shall not be reflected in the record area or the record size used within the function, method, or program" is the rule that makes this implementation's method admissible, and the golden measures it directly. Records of 3 and 8 bytes are written to four variable-length files and read back; §13.18.43.4 GR15 stores the byte count of the record just read into the DEPENDING item, and the count read back is 03 then 08 on every file — the 4-byte little-endian length prefix (Annex A.1 item 151) is stripped before the record area is filled and never enters a record size the program can see. The DEPENDING item is deliberately forced to 99 before each READ so the measurement is GR15's stored count and not the leftover MOVE that sized the WRITE, and the displayed text is reference-modified to the reported length so nothing depends on what a short READ leaves in the tail of the area.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If STANDARD-1 is specified, the external medium shall be a tape drive" is unsatisfiable here and the non-support is documented: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26, whose ground is Annex A.3 item 26 — "The STANDARD-1 phrase of the RECORD DELIMITER clause is dependent upon a reel type of device" — and §4.2.6, which makes the decision to claim a processor-dependent element the implementor's, requires the absence to be specified in user documentation (this row), and adds that "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" (all cite.py --check OK). COBOL.NET provides no reel device at all — the same determination §2 rows 28-30 and 33-34 already record for CLOSE REEL/UNIT and OPEN WITH NO REWIND. The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS, not on silence: COBOLNET1778 is raised at bind for every occurrence at 85/2002/2014/2023, in both the IS and the optional-word-omitted spelling.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If STANDARD-1 is specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record shall be that specified in ISO/IEC 1001:2012, 7.1.2" rides GR2's decline: the method is the tape-interchange framing of a standard this implementation neither implements nor could exercise, having no reel device (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26, Annex A.3 item 26). §4.2.6's "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" is the carry-over licence — the §4.2.6 analogue of Annex A.4.1's second paragraph, and it is what reaches from item 26's PHRASE to this rule. What happens instead is §12.4.5.11.4 GR5's implementor method, documented as Annex A.1 item 151 in §7. Witnessed by the named decline at every edition rather than by silence.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If feature-name-1 is specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record is that associated with feature-name-1 by the implementor" has an EMPTY domain here, and that is a documented posture rather than a gap. The licence is NOT Annex A.3 — item 26 reaches only the STANDARD-1 phrase — but Annex A.1 item 150, which the standard classes as optional ("This item is optional"), read with A.1's preamble ("Optional: The element may be provided at the implementor's option") and §4.2.7's obligation to identify what is claimed. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 A.1 item 150 records the determination as "Not provided.", which is exactly the shape owner decision kb/Work PB280 Q1 (2026-09-02) closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT through the `a1-optional-not-provided` selector. The row closes on a diagnosis: a feature-name written anyway draws COBOLNET1778 by name at every edition.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If the RECORD DELIMITER clause is not specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record is specified by the implementor" — specified, and now documented, as Annex A.1 item 151 in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7: a 4-byte little-endian binary length prefix per record for record sequential, relative and indexed files (one implementation, RecordFraming, shared by every organization), and the line delimiter for LINE SEQUENTIAL, which is §9.1.7.2's own rule. The licence to add a header at all is §9.1.7.2 ("In record sequential files the length of each record is determined by any information the implementor may add to the record on the physical storage medium (such as record length headers)"); the §9.1.13.6 "externally-defined boundaries" sentence that RecordFraming's header used to cite is the I-O status 34 rule about writing past a FILE's end and was corrected in this change set. GR5's ANTECEDENT is witnessed directly: golden file F4 writes no RECORD DELIMITER clause, draws no diagnostic (asserted as the complement) and reads its 3- and 8-byte records back at those lengths.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "At the time of a successful execution of an OPEN statement, the record delimiter is the one specified in the RECORD DELIMITER clause in the file control entry associated with the file-name specified in the OPEN statement" — no delimiter is established at OPEN, because neither alternative of the clause is supported (GR2/GR3 by Annex A.3 item 26 and §4.2.6; GR4 by Annex A.1 item 150 and §4.2.7). §4.2.6's "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" carries the decline to this rule. What the OPEN does establish is §12.4.5.11.4 GR5's implementor method, and the golden shows it holding across an OPEN OUTPUT / CLOSE / OPEN INPUT round trip on all four files — identically whether the clause was written or not, which is what §12.4.5.11.4 GR1 guarantees a program can see. Nothing is captured on FileModel for this clause, deliberately: a stored delimiter nothing reads would be a lookup no test could ever contradict.

subject: RECORD KEY clause
notes: RE-SITED 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB699); rule unchanged. RULE (--check 12.4.5.12.3 1): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses." The screen MOVED from KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile - which ran on the first KEYED VERB naming the file, so an entry whose prime key sat under OCCURS compiled with zero diagnostics when the procedure division only OPENed and CLOSEd it (measured) - to FileControlKeyRules, one table keyed by organization and key role, run from DataBinder.ResolveFiles over every declared file. conformance:negative/pb699-record-key-occurs-entry-only is the discriminator against the older pb354 case, which contains a READ. DATA-NAME-2 is the SOURCE phrase's operand and has no reachable spelling: the grammar's recordKeyClause is `RECORD KEY? IS? dataReference` with no SOURCE alternative, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md 2 row 40 declines A.3 item 40, so honouring the ban on data-name-1 is the whole of what this rule can require here.

subject: RECORD KEY clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-06 (kb/Work PB743) - the CATEGORY arm, which is what earns the verdict PB699 deliberately withheld. RULE (--check 12.4.5.12.3 2): "Data-name-1 and data-name-2 shall reference a data item of category alphanumeric or category national within a record description entry associated with the file-name specified in this file control entry." ONE sentence, TWO obligations joined by the word "within": a CATEGORY and a LOCATION. PB699 implemented the LOCATION half and left the row without a verdict rather than over-claiming; measured with only that half live, an indexed file whose RECORD KEY was PIC 9(5) compiled clean, ran, and wrote '00' - it built an index on an operand the standard forbids as a key. Now TWO ROWS carry this rule-id, one per arm, and FileControlKeyRuleDriftTests.ARuleWithTwoObligations_HasARowForEachArm re-derives the split FROM THE PRINTED SENTENCE so a rule that grows a third obligation reddens instead of shipping two thirds. The category predicate is ItemCategory.IsAlphanumericOrNational - the ONE 8.5.2 category reader, extracted from DataBinder in the same change and now shared with 12.4.5.2 SR7's ASSIGN ... USING screen - which admits an alphanumeric group item (13.18.29.4 GR3: "If a GROUP-USAGE clause is not specified or implied ... that group item is an alphanumeric group item") and a GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL group, and refuses alphabetic (PicInfo.IsAlphabetic; the storage model folds PIC A into PicCategory.Alphanumeric, so a bare category comparison would have passed it), numeric, numeric-edited, boolean and the PICTURE-less usages. Alphanumeric-edited has no PicCategory member and is therefore admitted - the established posture for a category screen here (RecordLayout.CategoryOfItem, 14.9.41.3 SR6 b) 2.): the screen rejects what the rule NAMES, never what the model cannot classify. DATA-NAME-2 is the SOURCE phrase's operand and has no reachable spelling (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 2 row 40 declines A.3 item 40), and SR2's third sentence ("All occurrences of data-name-2 shall be of the same category") is about it alone.

notes: kb/Work PB1074: cite.py --check 12.4.5.12.4 "The value of the associated record key shall not be equal to the value of the same record key in another record in the file" -> OK GR1; --check 12.4.5.12.4 "The equality or inequality is based on the collating sequence used for the file according to the rules for a relation condition" -> OK GR1; consequence --find "to write a record that would create a duplicate prime record key in a physical indexed file" -> §9.1.13.5 2) b) (status 22). subject: RECORD KEY clause
notes: CONFORMS, unchanged in substance and re-homed by kb/Work PB802. The rule - 'The data description of data-name-1 or data-name-2 as well as their relative location within a record shall be the same as that used when the file was created' (note: 'the file', not 'the physical file'; 12.4.5.6.4 GR3 is the one worded 'the physical file', and the inherited quotation that gave both the same wording is corrected here) - states a requirement and no consequence where it is written; 14.9.27.4 GR10's file attribute conflict condition is the mechanism that detects a violation. WHAT CHANGED: the prime key's descriptor is no longer written into a .cbattr catalog sidecar beside the data file but into the framed store's own HEADER, which RecordFraming.WriteStore stamps from the writing connector's DeclaredAttributes on every persist - so the file itself carries its key geometry, as a real ISAM file does, and nothing exists beside it that could outlive it. FixedFileAttributes.Conflicts compares it on every later OPEN and a mismatch is the unsuccessful OPEN with I-O status '39' (9.1.13.6 item 7). THE RECORDED DESCRIPTOR IS THE KEY'S WINDOW PLUS ITS COLLATING SEQUENCE, and that is the whole of 'the data description ... as well as their relative location' this implementation can act on: 12.4.5.12.3 SR2 confines a record key to category alphanumeric or category national, 12.4.5.12.4 GR1 makes key equality a relation condition under the file's collating sequence (recorded by weights - FixedFileAttributes.Fingerprint), and both native sequences are one code-unit ordinal over the UTF-16 substrate (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-33 / DOC-A.1-188), so two descriptions sharing a window and a sequence order every key value identically whatever their category. NEW: the comparison of the key table alone can be turned off for a run by COBOLNET_KEYCHECK=OFF, GnuCOBOL's COB_KEYCHECK opt-out under this repository's naming, documented as part of the A.1 item 129 determination (DOC-A.1-129) - by default it is on, so the rule is enforced unless a run explicitly asks otherwise. Pinned by open_fixed_attribute_conflict_ix step I2 (a six-byte prime key window over a file created with a four-byte one gives '39') and by the unit theory's prime-window arm.

notes: kb/Work R43 (owner, 2026-09-24): an unsupported facility is unsupported entirely — item 2: a rule HALF inside a declined facility takes its LIVE half's verdict; the declined half (data-name-2, the record-key SOURCE form, A.3 item 40, refused COBOLNET1954) is non-support. The data-name-1 half is witnessed by pb354_start_generic_key_ok, whose key is described in one of three record description entries. || kb/Work PB1099: cite.py --check 12.4.5.12.4 "are implicitly referenced as keys for all other record description entries of that file" -> OK GR4. The prime key is registered as a BYTE WINDOW (offset,length) over the file's shared record area (KeyedIoEmitter, 'THE KEY WINDOW IS IN BYTES', kb/Work PB327; FileRegistry.RegisterIndexed), so every record description entry of the FD is keyed at those positions by construction; the key need be described in only one record (first sentence). Probe gr4.cob (2023): FD with 01 R (R-KEY = bytes 2-3) and 01 S (no key described): records WRITTEN THROUGH S are indexed on bytes 2-3 - 'QZZ111' 00, 'XAA222' 00, then R with R-KEY 'ZZ' -> 22 (duplicate of the S-written key), 'QZY444' 00; READ KEY IS R-KEY='ZZ' returns the S-written 'QZZ111'; START >= LOW-VALUES + READ NEXT walks AA, ZY, ZZ (byte-position order). Covering test: conformance:2002/pb354_start_generic_key_ok case K2 STARTs by an item at the prime key's identical byte positions in a SECOND record description and its expected record is derived from this GR (and §14.9.41.3 SR6 a). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The data-name-1 half is verified and holds in every shape probed, but the rule names 'data-name-1 OR data-name-2'. The data-name-2 half (the SOURCE key form) is refused by COBOLNET1954 as the Annex A.3 item 40 decline. subject: RELATIVE KEY clause
notes: GR1: 'The first logical record has a relative record number of 1, and subsequent logical records have relative record numbers of 2, 3, 4, ...' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.13.4 "The first logical record has a relative record number of 1" -> OK). The runtime store is keyed by 1-based RRN (RelativeConnector.cs:24 slot store, :522 `into.Put(i + 1, rec)`). Probe rk4 (pinned cobol.exe): ACCESS SEQUENTIAL OPEN OUTPUT, three WRITEs with RELATIVE KEY preset to 77 -> key item reads 0001, 0002, 0003 after each (FS 00); sequential READs return AAAA K=0001, BBBB K=0002; DYNAMIC random READ with key 0 -> INVALID KEY, FS=23; random WRITE with key 0 -> FS=34, which is what §14.9.51.4 GR29 b) requires for a value less than 1 (cite.py --find located it: §14.9.51.4 29) b)). subject: SHARING clause
notes: GR1 (cite.py --check 12.4.5.15.3 OK): "The SHARING clause specifies the sharing mode to be used for the file unless it is overridden by the SHARING phrase of the OPEN statement. This clause also specifies whether record locks have an effect. Additional details are specified in 9.1.15". THREE halves, each verified: (a) clause sets the mode — DataBinder MapSharing -> FileModel.Sharing -> EmitSharingRegistration -> FileRegistry.RegisterSharing; SharedOpenAttempt uses `sharingOverride ?? registered meta.Sharing ?? ImplementorDefaultSharing`. Probe p1.cob: clause NO OTHER on A -> second connector's OPEN INPUT = 61; clause READ ONLY on B -> another INPUT = 00, EXTEND = 61 (§9.1.15 1)/2), cite.py OK). (b) override — OpenShared passes hasSharingOverride ? sharingOverride : null (§9.1.15 "The SHARING phrase on an OPEN statement overrides the SHARING clause", cite.py OK). Probe: clause NO OTHER + OPEN INPUT SHARING WITH ALL OTHER -> other INPUT open 00; clause ALL OTHER + OPEN SHARING NO OTHER -> other INPUT open 61. (c) record-lock effect — LocksEffective returns false when the EFFECTIVE (post-override) open sharing is NoOther (§9.1.15 1) "Record locks are ignored"; 2)/3) "Record locks are in effect"). Probe p2.cob: READ ONLY + LOCK MODE MANUAL, A READ WITH LOCK then B plain READ -> 51 (locks in effect under READ ONLY); ALL OTHER in-effect covered by conformance:2002/file_sharing (READB=51). The NO OTHER 'ignored' arm is verified by reading only — it is essentially unobservable, since exclusive access excludes any second connector that could meet the lock. Side note (not this rule's defect): FileModel.cs line 13 doc comment says the implementor default is 'COBOL.NET: ALL OTHER' while the runtime's ImplementorDefaultSharing is null/undetermined (kb/Work PB321/PB322) — stale comment. No kb/Work note owns open rows here; PB319 (landed) removed a duplicated §14.9.27.3 SR8 check from the SELECT binder; re-confirmed absent (DataBinder.cs ~1110-1125) and the SR8 check fires only at OPEN (probe: COBOLNET1512 at the OPEN of F-D, not the SELECT).

notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.3 "SORT and SORT-MERGE are equivalent" -> OK SR1. subject: SAME clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "No more than one of these files may be in the open mode at a given time" -> OK GR1. Two halves: (a) the files 'are to use the same memory area' - a storage-ECONOMY permission with no program-observable content for a conforming program: only one member is ever open, and a closed file's record area is unavailable (§14.9.6.4 GR7) so a program cannot observe whether the areas coincide; Annex D (informative) describes it as saving memory space. BindIoControl binds Format 1 as a deliberate no-op (doc comment: 'storage-economy permissions ... bound as conformant no-ops'). (b) the open-mode restriction is a constraint on the PROGRAM with no exception condition or runtime check specified (grep of the spec finds no EC or OPEN rule keyed on SAME AREA), so violating it is outside a conforming program. Probe gr1_filearea (`SAME AREA FOR F1 F2`, write/close F1, write/close F2, read each back) -> F1=AAAAAA, F2=BBBBBB, correct at 2023. No spec-derived test. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the SAME clause is base I-O-CONTROL language in every edition; no Annex E change entry names it)]

subject: SAME clause
notes: cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "A logical record in the shared memory area is a logical record of each file open in the output mode and of the most recently-read file open in the input mode" -> OK GR2; cite.py --check 12.4.6.4.4 "This is equivalent to an implicit redefinition of the area with records aligned on the leftmost byte position" -> OK GR2. BindIoControl chains each listed file's first record as an implicit RedefinitionKind.SameRecordArea redefinition of the first listed file's record (the multi-01 FD mechanism) and records SameRecordAreaPeers for out-of-line records (D-FRA). Probe gr2_mixed (SEQUENTIAL X(4) / RELATIVE X(2)+X(6) / LINE SEQUENTIAL X(10)): MOVE to F3-REC shows F1=ABCD F2A=AB F2B=CDEFGH (leftmost alignment across unequal lengths); MOVE to F1-REC shows F3=WXYZEFGHIJ; after READ F2 F1-REC=1234, after READ F1 F2-A=WX (most-recently-read file's record occupies the area). subject: SAME clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.6.4.4 GR3: "The file and record area of a file subject to commit and rollback may not be shared with another such file or record area unless it has been closed, a commit or a rollback has been executed and the APPLY COMMIT clause for the file has been deactivated." ⚠ ITS SHAPE IS NOT SR-12.4.6.4.3-11'S and it therefore gets its OWN witness: SR11 forbids mixing a commit-subject file with one that is NOT subject, while GR3 says "another SUCH file" — BOTH files subject to commit and rollback. The SAME clause (§12.4.6.4) is CLAIMED and supported; the antecedent is the APPLY COMMIT clause (ISO §12.4.6.3), Annex A.4.3 item 2, refused BY NAME by COBOLNET1709, so no file is ever subject to the facility and the rule cannot be violated. ⛔ NOT DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT: the verdict field would speak about SAME, a claimed facility, and §4.2.7 discharges non-support through user documentation that declines commit and rollback — never SAME. notes:
Rule constrains the PROGRAMS of a run unit: every FD for one external connector shall agree on BLOCK CONTAINS (a), CODE-SET (b), LINAGE literals/external items (c), smallest/largest record size (d), REPORT presence (e) (cite.py --check 13.4.5.4 'all shall have a BLOCK CONTAINS clause specifying the same minimum and maximum size of the physical record' -> OK §13.4.5.4 2) a)). An implementation may, but is not required to, flag violations' (cite.py OK §4.2.2) and §4.4 'The results of violating the formats or rules of standard COBOL are undefined' (cite.py OK §4.4 2)); the only mandated EC check, §14.8.4.4, covers the FILE CONTROL entry (12.4.5 GR1), not the FD (cite.py OK §14.8.4.4). subject: Working-storage section
notes: Owned by kb/Work PB1307. The spec requires it to compile and print REC=01 IN REC=02 IN. This is legal source rejected, and the stage has NO open kb/Work owner: PB168 is landed and only widened the stage to the FILE SECTION. See the finding. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 85/2002/2014/2023 (program); function, factory and object from 2002

subject: Data description entry
notes: kb/Work PB501 LANDED, both arms. GR3 says a format-3 entry carries 'the name of the condition AND the value, values, or range of values associated with the condition-name', and a level-88 entry was never screened against its own general format, so an entry missing EITHER constituent reached the backend. Arm 1 (no value-clause, `88 NOVAL.`) was closed by kb/Work PB485/PB829 -- COBOLNET1747 from LevelNumberPass, re-measured on this worktree. Arm 2 (no condition-name, `88 VALUE 1.`) is closed here, in the same pass and under the same code, because it is the same rule's other half: 13.16.2 was RENDERED from the printed page (folio 364 / PDF p394) and format 3 prints condition-name-1 UNBRACKETED while format 4 brackets condition-name-2; format 4's licence to omit the name is not free-standing, since its value-clause is 13.18.63.2 format 5 whose figure ends in a REQUIRED { INVALID / VALID } choice. So a nameless 88 with no VALID/INVALID phrase is neither format and 13.16.3 SR24 leaves no third possibility. MEASURED on this worktree's own build at 85 and 2023: `88 VALUE 1.` and `88 VALUE 07.` -> COBOLNET1747 naming both formats (both compiled CLEAN and produced a .dll before -- BindCondition returns on a missing data-name and the entry evaporated). Over-rejection measured too: the legal format-3 spellings (single literal, THRU range, literal list, a condition-name over a GROUP conditional variable) all compile and evaluate correctly, and the format-4 spelling `88 VALUE 1 THRU 9 IS VALID.` still draws its own A.4.14 decline (COBOLNET1708), not this screen. RenderCondition88 is now TOTAL over an empty value set -- it rendered the two-character fragment `()`, so the generated source read `if (())` and the user got CS1525 against a .g.cs path; an empty association can only be false (13.16.4 GR3).

subject: Data description entry
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3. Licence: Annex A.4.1, "An implementation shall accept the syntax and provide the functionality for an optional element only when support for that language element is claimed by the implementor", and its second sentence carrying the licence to the module's unlisted rules. Obsolescence (F.2 item 5) is corroboration, never the licence (kb/Work PB198). GR-13.16.4-4 is the Format-4-only general rule of the data description entry ("88 [ condition-name-2 ] value-clause ."). The condition-name is OPTIONAL in this format, and the UNNAMED shape is the one a binder-hook implementation would have dropped in silence (DataBinder.BindCondition returns early without entry.dataName()) — which is why the refusal is a parse-tree pass.

subject: ALIGNED clause
notes: 'The ALIGNED clause may be specified only for a bit group item or an elementary bit data item.' The subject predicate is BitLayout.IsBitItem - the SAME predicate 8.5.1.6.3's layout walk uses, since the rule asks the same question in the same words, so the rule that decides whether ALIGNED is legal and the walk that implements it cannot disagree. Adjudicated in a POST-FOREST pass, not BindEntry, because a group becomes a bit group by 13.16.4 GR1 inheritance which UsageInheritancePass settles. A violation clears IsAligned so the item lays out by the default rules under an already-failed compile. COBOLNET1942. kb/Work PB487.

subject: ALIGNED clause
notes: 'aligned on the first bit of the first available byte boundary. Implicit filler bits may be generated ... as described in 8.5.1.6.3.' One conjunct on THE one placement predicate: an ALIGNED subject never shares its predecessor's byte, and the round-up every caller already performs does the rest. The predicate was previously written out THREE times - BitLayout.ExtentBits, BitLayout.StartBitWithin and DataBinder.AssignClassOffsets - and is now a single method all three call, so an item's OFFSET, the group's EXTENT and a REDEFINES view of it cannot disagree. Golden derivation: 05 B1 PIC 1(4) BIT. 05 B2 PIC 1(4) BIT ALIGNED. occupies 12 bits padded by rule 4 to 16, so FUNCTION LENGTH is 2 where without ALIGNED it is 1 - measured 2.

subject: ALIGNED clause
notes: 'An ALIGNED clause specified for a multiple-occurrence data item applies to each occurrence of that item.' The per-occurrence STRIDE therefore rounds up to a byte while the WIDTH stays the declared bit count; the two were one number at every subscript site (ReferenceResolver, CallBinder, InitializeBinder, OdoModel, GroupValueSlicer) and are now split by BitLayout.StrideBits. RunBits counts stride x (n-1) + width, never stride x n, because 8.5.1.6.3 generates trailing filler only 'to advance alignment ... for the NEXT item'. Golden derivation: 05 T PIC 1(4) BIT OCCURS 3 ALIGNED. places occurrences at bits 0, 8, 16 for an extent of 20 padded to 24, so FUNCTION LENGTH is 3 where without ALIGNED it is 2 - measured 3, with each occurrence read back at its own value.

subject: ALIGNED clause
notes: 'When an ALIGNED clause is not specified, bit data items are aligned in accordance with 8.5.1.6.3.' This is the FALSE arm of the one placement predicate, unchanged by the GR1 conjunct - which is why the golden carries the no-ALIGNED control groups NOALIGN and TBLPLAIN alongside the ALIGNED ones and pins them at 1 and 2 character positions.

subject: ANY LENGTH clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1210, 14d). Rule: 'A PICTURE clause shall be specified ... shall be one instance of the picture symbol N, X, or 1' (cite.py --check 13.18.2.3 OK). The missing-PICTURE and multi-symbol halves are enforced (probe p5.cob: G/L5 no PICTURE -> COBOLNET1542; PIC XX, PIC A -> COBOLNET1542), and positive X/N/1 verified (p4.cob: PIC N ANY LENGTH n=3 'ABC'; PIC 1 USAGE BIT n=5 '10110'). But the check is a closed list of six spellings, so a count-1 repetition in any other spelling is refused: `01 L PIC X(01) ANY LENGTH.` -> COBOLNET1542 (probe p1.cob, --std 2023 and 85). 13.18.40.3 SR6 (cite.py --check OK): 'An unsigned nonzero integer that is enclosed in parentheses indicates the number of consecutive occurrences of the symbol' - X(01) is ONE occurrence, exactly as the code already concedes for X(1); SR6 also admits a constant-name as the integer (X(ONE)), refused the same way. The sibling DYNAMIC LENGTH check in the same file (13.18.19.3 SR1) uses ^[XN](\(0*1\))?$ and accepts X(01) - a two-arm dispatch where only one arm was generalized. Expected: p1 compiles and prints LEN=03 VAL=XYZ / LEN=08 VAL=WXYZABCD. Harm: rejects legal source. negative/any-length-bad-picture covers the reject half only. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (ISO 2023 Annex E lists no substantive change to 13.18.2, so the rule is unchanged from 2014; the 2002 introduction is the project's COBOL-2002 gate and is not derivable from the 2023 text alone - see dossier gap) || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#(ANY LENGTH declaration-shape validation: norm is not ("X" or "N" or "1" or "X(1)" or "N(1)" or "1(1)"))

subject: ANY LENGTH clause
notes: Rule: 'may be specified only in an elementary level 1 entry in the linkage section of a function, of a contained program, or of a method that is not a property method' (cite.py --check 13.18.2.3 OK). Every limb probed: WORKING-STORAGE item (p5 W) -> 1542; level 77 in linkage (p5 L77) -> 1542; group (p5 G - rejected via SR1 first; the IsGroup arm exists in both sweeps); outermost program -> 1542 (negative/any-length-outermost golden); object/factory paragraph arm read (OoIsClassUnit); GET PROPERTY method (p8.cob) -> 1542 'may not be specified in a PROPERTY method'; contained program / function / ordinary method accepted (goldens any_length_contained, any_length_function, oo_any_length). A method's LOCAL-/WORKING-STORAGE root is refused in OoBindMethodData. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (ISO 2023 Annex E lists no substantive change to 13.18.2, so the rule is unchanged from 2014; the 2002 introduction is the project's COBOL-2002 gate and is not derivable from the 2023 text alone - see dossier gap) || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#(ANY LENGTH level-is-not-1 check); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Linkage.cs#AnyLengthValidateUnit; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Oo.cs#OoBindMethodData

subject: ANY LENGTH clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1211, 14d). Rule: contained program or method - the subject 'shall be referenced in its procedure division header as either: a) a formal parameter with the BY REFERENCE phrase, or b) the returning item' (cite.py --check 13.18.2.3 OK for a) and b)). The restriction half is enforced: an unreferenced ANY LENGTH linkage item -> 1542 (p5 L2; p8 U in a method); a BY VALUE formal -> 1542 (p3.cob). Leg a) accepted and runs (any_length_contained, oo_any_length). Leg b) - the RETURNING item, which the rule expressly PERMITS - is refused with the named RecognizedNotImplemented COBOLNET0899 in BOTH arms: contained program `PROCEDURE DIVISION RETURNING L` with `01 L PIC X ANY LENGTH` (p2.cob) -> 'ANY LENGTH on the PROCEDURE DIVISION RETURNING item is recognized ... but not yet implemented'; method RETURNING (p8.cob method RET) -> the same. 8.4.3.4.3 SR4 forbids an ANY LENGTH returning item only for an INLINE method invocation, so INVOKE ... RETURNING / CALL ... RETURNING activations are legal. No open kb/Work note owns this leg (PB428, landed, only notes the 0899 staging). Expected for p2: compiles; per 13.18.2.4 GR1b L has n = 3 (the caller's A3), so it prints A3=ABC. Harm: rejects legal source. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (ISO 2023 Annex E lists no substantive change to 13.18.2, so the rule is unchanged from 2014; the 2002 introduction is the project's COBOL-2002 gate and is not derivable from the 2023 text alone - see dossier gap)

subject: ANY LENGTH clause

subject: ANY LENGTH clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1211, 14d). Rule: the subject shall be 'a) a zero-length item when the corresponding argument or returning item ... is a zero-length item, or b) treated as though there were n repetitions of the picture symbol ... where n is the length of the corresponding argument or returning item' (cite.py --check 13.18.2.4 OK both). ARGUMENT leg verified: b) X via contained CALL (golden LEN=03/LEN=08), function (any_length_function), method (oo_any_length); N via p4.cob (NLEN=03 VAL=ABC; MOVE N"Z" stores 'Z  ' padded to n=3); 1 via p4.cob (PIC 1 USAGE BIT over B"10110" -> BVAL=10110). a) zero-length argument: p7.cob passes a DYNAMIC LENGTH item of length 0 -> LEN=00 VAL=[], then 'HELLO' -> LEN=05. RETURNING-ITEM leg: NOT implemented - every ANY LENGTH returning item is refused at compile time with COBOLNET0899 (see SR-13.18.2.3-3), so n from the activator's returning item is never computed. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL; the test-ref covers the argument leg only. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (ISO 2023 Annex E lists no substantive change to 13.18.2, so the rule is unchanged from 2014; the 2002 introduction is the project's COBOL-2002 gate and is not derivable from the 2023 text alone - see dossier gap)

notes: (kb/Work PB1214, 14d). cite.py --check 13.18.5.4 'The implicit data-address pointer has an initial value of NULL.' OK §13.18.5.4 2); the rule defers the life cycle to §8.6.5 (--check 8.6.5 'when the based entry is defined in the working-storage or local-storage section, at the end of the life cycle of the data items defined in that section' OK) and §8.6.4 makes LOCAL-STORAGE items automatic, 'allocated and set to initial state each time the runtime element containing them is activated'. FIRST HALF CONFORMS: the field is emitted `= ManagedPointer.Null`; WS static persists across CALLs and CANCEL resets it; INITIAL program WS resets each call (probe gr2.cob: WS NULL / WS NOT NULL / after CANCEL WS NULL; INIT NULL twice). LIFE-CYCLE HALF DIVERGES for a PROGRAM's LOCAL-STORAGE based entry: probe E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out13/probe/based/gr2b.cob (LS `01 B PIC X(4) BASED.`, SET ADDRESS OF B TO ADDRESS OF W, GOBACK, CALL again) prints 'LS NULL' then 'LS NOT NULL B=WWWW' (also at --std 2014, gr2e.cob) while the ordinary LS item X re-initialises (X=1 both times). Mechanism: ProgramEmitter's cached-singleton LS re-init loop `continue`s on every StringCanonical cell-backed root, so the implicit pointer field is never re-seeded; OO methods have PtrActivationSeed, programs have no counterpart (two-arm dispatch). Observation not adjudicated as a defect: a LINKAGE based entry keeps its association into the next CALL (gr2c.cob: LK NULL / LK NOT NULL) although §8.6.5 ends the association 'at the end of the execution of the runtime element' - the spec does not state the pointer's value afterwards. subject: BASED clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1216, 14d). cite.py --check 13.18.5.4 'If the subject of the entry is referenced while its address is not NULL and not a valid address of storage, the EC-BOUND-PTR exception condition is set to exist.' OK §13.18.5.4 4). Deref raises EC-BOUND-PTR for a non-window carrier, a FREEd cell, and a window outside the cell (overflow-safe bound, PB465). Probe E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out13/probe/based/gr4.cob (checking on, declarative): reference after FREE P -> HANDLED=EC-BOUND-PTR; SET P UP BY 1000 then reference -> EC-BOUND-PTR; B PIC X(4) over ALLOCATE 2 CHARACTERS -> EC-BOUND-PTR; an in-bounds displaced pointer (UP BY 1 inside W) reads BCDE with no exception. Unit test's expected values (window past end = EC-BOUND-PTR, last position addressable) follow from the rule; Free_ThreeWay_And_DanglingAliasIsLoud covers the freed case. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — GR4 requires EC-BOUND-PTR for any reference while the address is 'not NULL and not a valid address of storage'. §8.6.5 says the association 'may cease to exist because the actual data no longer exists, as specified 8.6.4'. §8.6.4 makes LOCAL-STORAGE items persist only 'while that instance of the runtime element is in active state', and ends static working-storage at a CANCEL of the containing program. A pointer to either kind of storage, used after that storage's life ends, is therefore a non-NULL invalid address. The runtime's only validity notion is the StorageCell.Freed flag, which FREE sets. CobolPtr.Deref checks NULL, non-window carrier, Freed and the window bound, and nothing else. No activation end or CANCEL ever invalidates a cell, so both shapes read stale storage silently with checking on. The adjudicator's FREE, out-of-window, before-start and tail-straddle branches do conform. I re-probed the before-start and tail-straddle branches myself.

subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB566 LANDED 2026-09-20. GR1 blanks on THE VALUE BEING STORED. The determination: 14.9.25.4 GR6 d)'s closing paragraph sends the store to 14.6.8, and 14.6.8.2 r4 transfers 'with zero fill or truncation on either end as required', so a sending value that truncates away to zero at EITHER end stores zero (13.18.8.1 says the same in one line). The guard used to test the raw (value, valueScale) sending pair before the mask rescale, so the MOVE arm rendered digits where the arithmetic arms - whose emitters hand Format a value already at the resultant's scale - blanked on identical items; it now sits AFTER the store rescale in the ONE shared formatter (CobolEdit.Render), testing the stored digit string, which is the same value rule 7 b)'s all-suppressed test beside it already read. Siblings swept the same way: CobolLocaleEdit.Format (r10's short-circuit now runs on r14's aligned value, and r15 b with it, both still before any locale is consulted); CobolEdit.Float's two arms already tested the stored value (the significand's leading digit is nonzero after normalization, and 14.9.25.4 GR6 d) 4 b treats an underflow as zero) and now say so. Measured on the golden at --std 85: low-order truncation (0.4 into PIC ZZZ9 and into PIC 9(3)), high-order truncation (100 into PIC 99 blanks, 101 shows '01'), a negative sender, a floating-currency mask, VALUE 0 initialization (13.18.63.4 GR8's NOTE), the INITIALIZE verb (14.9.20.4 GR6 c), and COMPUTE / MULTIPLY GIVING agreeing with MOVE on the same two items.

subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB508 — The usage-display arm CONFORMS and is measured three ways, not merely by reading the flag: `01 WS-PLAIN PIC 9(5) BLANK WHEN ZERO.` is rejected as an arithmetic RESULTANT with COBOLNET1675 citing ISO 14.9.2.3 SR2 (`ADD 0 TO WS-PLAIN`, probe a6) and as an arithmetic OPERAND with COBOLNET0844 citing ISO 8.8.1.1 (`COMPUTE WS-NUM = WS-PLAIN + 5`, probe a7) - both of which are only correct if the subject really is category numeric-edited - and the item edits and de-edits through the numeric-edited machinery (probes a7/a9). PARTIAL because the predicate hard-codes `usage is Usage.Display` where SR2 expressly admits usage NATIONAL as well: a `PIC 9(5) USAGE NATIONAL BLANK WHEN ZERO` subject would fall through to the plain-numeric return at PictureAnalyzer.cs:356 and never be defined numeric-edited. That arm is presently unobservable - national-form numeric data is refused upstream as a Phase-4a residue (COBOLNET0899 / DiagnosticCatalog.NationalData at PictureAnalyzer.cs:252, probe a5) - so this is a LATENT gap that will surface silently when national numeric lands, not a live wrong answer. See finding bwz-gr2-national-not-promoted. No spec-derived test discriminates the category: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/ValueLiteralClassTests.LegalShapes_StillCompileStrict carries `01 A PIC 999 VALUE "000" BLANK WHEN ZERO.` but its expectation `[000]` is the same under either category, so it does not close this row. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs:342-352 - `if (anyEdit || (blankWhenZero && digits > 0 && !signed && usage is Usage.Display))` returns PicInfo with PicCategory.NumericEdited. || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023 (the national subject is COBOL-2002 and later)

subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB509 LANDED 2026-09-20. BOTH ARMS NOW. The MOVE / de-editing arm was already right (14.9.25.4 GR6 d) 1: every digit position of an all-spaces image contributes zero, which IS GR3's zero). The relation arm was not: ConditionRenderer took the first arm whose operand IsString, and a numeric-edited operand is a string operand, so the whole relation became a character comparison and nothing asked whether the sender was blanked. THE DERIVATION for the reading implemented: GR1 says 'receiving operand' one rule earlier where GR3 says 'the object of an OPERATION', and 8.8.4.2.1 13) calls a relation's two operands its subject and its object; the MOVE receiver case is already legislated by 14.9.25.4 GR6 d) 1, and 8.8.1.1 admits only 'an identifier referencing a numeric data item' into an arithmetic expression - so the relation condition is the operation GR3 adds. GR3 naming a numeric-EDITED object is what settles that the comparison there is BY VALUE (8.8.4.2.4): giving the blanked item 'the value zero' changes nothing in a character comparison. Implemented at the ONE BoundRelational rendering site, so EVALUATE subject/object, SEARCH WHEN, PERFORM UNTIL and the abbreviated relations get it too (they all build BoundRelational through ConditionBinder.CheckedRelational). The test is on the CONTENT and therefore a run-time one: a BLANK WHEN ZERO item holding digits still compares by 8.8.4.2.5/.7, which the golden pins alongside the blanked cases. BOUNDARY, derived not assumed: GR3 requires the object to be a 'data item', so a numeric LITERAL object (IF BWZ-ITEM = 0) and a figurative constant keep the ordinary 8.8.4.2.5 character comparison - pinned as NE-LITERAL in the golden. INTERACTION REGISTERED, NOT FIXED: with EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE checking armed, the value arm de-edits the OTHER operand too, so impossible content in a non-BLANK-WHEN-ZERO numeric-edited partner now raises where a character comparison did not; the arming mechanism is kb/Work PB395's (open).

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: GR1 names the clause's purpose: alphabets used to convert medium-to-native on input and native-to-medium on output. DETERMINATION, documented (CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 27), and it is a PROPERTY OF THE SET rather than a list of phrase names in the file-description binder - CodedCharacterSet.Medium answers it once for every reference site. IDENTITY (claimed, no conversion emitted): NATIVE (12.3.7.4 GR7 d, by definition), STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 (GR7 c - the native set's first 128 characters ARE ISO/IEC 646 IRV), UTF-16 (the D-N1 substrate) and the ASCII code-name (the same set as STANDARD-1). TRANSLATED (claimed, and real - kb/Work PB793): the EBCDIC code-name, whose GR7 i correspondence with the native set is IBM CCSID 37, converts every record crossing the medium. NOT-PROVIDED: a literal-phrase alphabet's remapped ordinals (GR7 k4 leaves that correspondence to the implementor and this one does not define it) and UTF-8 / UCS-4 as variable-width medium encodings are the DOCUMENTED Annex A A.3 item 27 non-support - COBOLNET1672, never a silent identity (the negative). Rule --check verified at 13.18.13.4 1).

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: GR2 - on successful OPEN the coded character set used to represent alphanumeric data on the storage medium is alphabet-name-1's. The set is established for the CONNECTOR and constant thereafter, so it is registered once beside the connector (FileConnector.CodeSet, the FileConnector.NationalRecordArea pattern) rather than re-derived per record; for an identity set nothing is registered at all and the record channel is unchanged byte for byte. The EBCDIC golden observes it in both directions: the same physical file read back through a description carrying NO CODE-SET clause yields the medium's own code units (GR7's default), which is what shows the clause established a DIFFERENT set for the first connector.

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: GR3 - with no SELECT WHEN clause among the record description entries (this grammar has none, so it is EVERY case here), the specified alphabet is used for code-set conversion of ALL data items in each record. The conversion is therefore applied to the whole record image at the medium boundary rather than item by item, which is the same thing for a record whose elementary items are all usage display - 13.18.13.3 SR3 a requires exactly that of a file whose CODE-SET names alphabet-name-1 and which has record description entries, and it is checked (COBOLNET1672). What is NOT converted is the framing this processor adds AROUND the record - the 9.1.7.2 record-length header of a VARYING or keyed file, and a line sequential file's delimiter - because that is not data of the record; the determination is published in CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 27.

COBOLNET1705 is raised at bind for EVERY occurrence and is an Error, not the COBOLNET1560 accept-inert band, because an inert FORMAT changes which bytes reach the medium (§13.18.24.4 GR1) and an inert SELECT WHEN selects the wrong record description entry (§13.18.51.4 GR1) — a wrong answer, not a missing facility.
