subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: GR6 a/b - the character-for-character replacement in both directions, realized for the first time by kb/Work PB793 (before it, every non-identity set was refused at compile time and GR6 had nothing to do). The correspondence is a COMPILE-TIME artifact of the named alphabet (12.3.7.4 GR7 i), emitted into the generated program as a 256-entry char[] literal exactly as a collating sequence's weights are, so the runtime holds no code page and knows no alphabet name. The boundary is the ONE physical transfer point of each organization and nowhere else - SequentialConnector.NextFrame on the read side, its EmitRecord / EmitRecordLine / OverwriteInPlace twins on the write side, and RecordFraming's store payload for RELATIVE and INDEXED - so a record area, a key value, a comparison and a lock identity are always in the native character set, which is what every other rule is written about. The golden proves both directions independently: the round trip restores AB012, and a second file description with no CODE-SET clause reads the same physical file as 194 195 241 242 243, the native ordinals of X'C1 C2 F0 F1 F2'.

notes: Rule: 'The COLUMN clause defines one or more printable items. If a COLUMN clause is not specified, the items are not printed.' (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 -> OK §13.18.14.4 1)). notes: (kb/Work PB1059, 14d). Rule: 'If this rule is violated the EC-REPORT-PAGE-WIDTH exception condition is set to exist, the report line is truncated, and the report line is printed.' subject: COLUMN clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1220, 14d). subject: COLUMN clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1220, 14d). Rule: 'The rightmost column position of each printable item becomes the new value of the horizontal counter.' (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 -> OK 9)). Absolute arm: `__hc = integer-1 + width - 1` (set, not max - so an absolute item left of the counter resets it, as 'becomes' requires); Relative: `__hc += width - 1`; AnchorSeed/AnchorStep likewise. Probe p1 line 5: absolute C at 12 then PLUS 1 -> D at 13 (counter became 12); p5 boundaries exact for every picture kind. Absent items (PRESENT WHEN) not advancing the counter is §13.18.41.4 GR3f, not this rule. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR9 applies to EVERY printable item. The emitter always takes an absolute item's rightmost column as integer-1 + printable-size - 1, the LEFT formula (GR6b). The alignment phrase that GR6c/GR6d give a different rightmost (RIGHT: integer-1; CENTER: integer-1 + size/2) has no grammar surface. CobolReportWriter.g4 reportColumnClause is `(COLUMN|COLUMNS|COL|COLS) (NUMBER|NUMBERS)? (IS|ARE)? reportColumnOperand+`, with no LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT. So legal source such as `COLUMN RIGHT 10 PIC XXX` followed by `COLUMN PLUS 1` cannot be compiled, and the counter update for right- or center-aligned items is not implemented. The left-aligned and relative halves are verified. The 13.18.14.3 SR9 legality of the phrase was checked. PB1059's body records the missing LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT surface with 'no note', so a register note is needed. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (Format 1 multiple/relative/alignment forms); the absolute single-operand COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 form also 85. Annex E records no 2023 change to the clause. || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ReportWriterEmitter.cs#EmitFieldPlacements (all four arms set __hc to the rightmost column)

subject: COLUMN clause
notes: Rule: 'If an entry containing a LINE clause has no subordinate entry defining a printable item, the resultant report line will be blank.' (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 -> OK 11)). subject: COLUMN clause
notes: Rule: a multiple COLUMN clause is functionally equivalent to a single-operand COLUMN plus a simple OCCURS with integer = operand count, except it allows unequal intervals (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 'allows the printable items to be defined at unequal horizontal intervals' -> OK 12)). subject: CONSTANT RECORD clause
notes: kb/Work/PB881.md - SR2 is a rule over an OPERAND ROLE ('shall be specified as a receiving data item'), so it is written once, in ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving (DataBinder.RejectConstantStore, COBOLNET1548), and every verb binder now states each operand's role by calling ResolveReceiving or ResolveSending - never ctx.Refs.Resolve, which screens nothing (ReceivingResolutionDriftTests fails a binder under Verbs/ that does). The sweep moved every receiving operand that had bypassed the chokepoint: INSPECT identifier-1 under REPLACING/CONVERTING (14.9.22.3 SR8 keeps Format 1's TALLYING-only identifier-1 SENDING), READ INTO (sequential and keyed) and RETURN INTO, the CORRESPONDING receiving group, SEARCH VARYING identifier-2 (14.9.37.4 GR1), INVOKE RETURNING (three arms) and BY REFERENCE arguments (typed and universal), the SET object-reference / data-pointer / program-pointer / function-pointer receivers, SET ... TO LOCALE's save target, ALLOCATE RETURNING, FREE and SET UP/DOWN pointer receivers. ACCEPT (the note's second site) had already been routed by PB429 (3fffacb61). The negatives pin four of the formerly bypassing arms at 2002/2014/2023; the positive pins the SENDING roles that stay legal (INSPECT TALLYING of a constant -> CN=0004 unchanged, MOVE CORRESPONDING from a constant group). The CONSTANT RECORD clause is COBOL-2002, so the rule has no population at 85.

subject: CONSTANT RECORD clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1233, 14d). Rule: content is "as though the clause had been omitted and the record had been the subject of an INITIALIZE statement" with FILLER, VALUE ALL, DEFAULT (cite.py --check 13.18.15.4 OK). Per §14.9.20.4 GR5c/GR6c (cite OK: "The DEFAULT phrase is specified", "| Numeric-edited | Figurative constant ZEROES |", "A data-item format VALUE clause is specified in the data description entry of the elementary data item") every elementary item without its own VALUE clause receives the category default. The code does NOT implement INITIALIZE semantics: DataItem.IsConstantRecord's remark asserts the ordinary VALUE/default initial state "already produces" it. VALUE half verified (golden constant_record; VALUE ALL "Q" -> QQQ; FILLER VALUE honoured; D.21 REDEFINES example correct; numeric/binary/packed/sign-separate VALUE-less items -> zero; alphanumeric/edited-X -> spaces). DEFAULT half diverges: (a) `05 E1 PIC ZZ9.99.` (no VALUE) displays 6 spaces, spec: MOVE ZEROES -> "  0.00" (probe gr1a.cob, 2014 and 2023); (b) with `OPTIONS. INITIALIZE WORKING-STORAGE SECTION TO X"5A".` VALUE-less A1 PIC X(3), FILLER PIC X(2), E1 PIC ZZ9 in the CONSTANT RECORD hold 'Z' fill (`[ZZZZZZZZOK]`), spec: spaces/spaces/"  0" -> `[       0OK]` (7 spaces, probe gr1b.cob) - InitialStateBackground.FillFor even carves CONSTANT RECORD INTO the fill (GR7 external exception) instead of out of it; (c) a group VALUE inside the record (`05 GV VALUE "WXYZ". 10 GA PIC XX. 10 GB PIC XX.`) keeps WXYZ, whereas INITIALIZE's receiving operands are elementary items and GA/GB carry no VALUE clause, so DEFAULT gives spaces (probe gr1c.cob) - the most literal consequence; Annex D.21 (informative) speaks of "applicable VALUE clauses". See finding constant-record-content-is-initial-state-not-initialize.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: The one grammar rule accepts both spellings - (CONTROL IS? | CONTROLS ARE?) - and nothing downstream can tell them apart, so they are synonyms by construction. Witnessed both ways: rw_suppress writes CONTROL IS, pb205_control_ref_mod writes CONTROLS ARE. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): the golden moved from tests/conformance/2002 to tests/conformance/2023 - it observes the report by re-reading the report file through ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL, which is a COBOL-2023 introduction (12.4.5.10.3 GR2; the Foreword's main-changes list over ISO/IEC 1989:2014), so the program is not expressible at 2002. The RULE's editions are unchanged.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB205. Previously rejected as a side effect under the WRONG rule: report-section names are not in the storage forest, so the operand failed ordinary name resolution and drew the 8.4.2.1 unresolved-operand diagnostic. SR2 now has its own arm on COBOLNET1699, asked only AFTER resolution fails - a name also declared in ordinary storage resolves there (8.4.2.1) and is not an SR2 reference, which is the 13.15.3 SR16 scan's own reasoning; both consumers share the one report-section-exclusive name set.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: The shape arm (kb/Work PB177 arm C) rejects an operand subject to any OCCURS clause, recognised with DataItem.IsTable so both dynamic-capacity shapes are covered. kb/Work PB205 added the WRITTEN half: a subscript on the operand was dropped at capture, and since SR3 bars the OCCURS case and 8.4.2.3.3 SR2 bars a subscript on an item without one, no subscripted control operand is legal - it is now rejected on the spelling, not only on the item.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB205 - both halves of SR4. The PERMISSION: a reference-modified operand now binds as its slice, because the capture keeps the ref-mod (ReadOperandSuffixes reads both source carriers lexically) and the emitter builds the 8.4.3.3.4 GR5 unique data item through the one ref-mod view builder (ResolveItemRefMod over RefModView), so 13.18.16.4 GR3's prior control is the slice; before this the ref-mod was dropped and CONTROL IS CX(1:3) broke on all six characters, a silent wrong answer. The RESTRICTION: a leftmost-position or length that is not an integer literal is rejected (COBOLNET1699) - unscreenable while the ref-mod never reached the binder. The omitted length CX(4:) is 8.4.3.3.2's bracketed form and runs to the rightmost position (GR5c).

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB177 arm C: OdoModel.TableUnder finds an occurs-depending table anywhere under the operand. It is a separate arm from SR7 on purpose - an occurs-depending table does NOT make a group variable-length (8.5.1.12 defines that over dynamic-length elementary items and dynamic-capacity tables), so SR7 cannot reach this shape.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB205. Uniqueness is of the WRITTEN reference (ReportControlRef.SameOperandAs over name + qualifiers + ref-mod), which is what SR6's own second sentence forces: two operands may 'refer to the same physical data item or to overlapping data items', so the referenced item cannot be what distinguishes them - and 13.18.57.3 SR10 could not name a level unambiguously if it were. The positive golden is the legal shape the second sentence permits (CONTROLS ARE CX(1:3) CX(4:)); the negative is the same reference twice.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB177 arm C: the variable-length-group test is 8.5.1.12's - a dynamic-length elementary item or a dynamic-capacity table subordinate to the group - read through the one predicate the reference resolver already uses for 8.4.3.3.3 SR1.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: The operands are captured in written order into ReportModel.Controls and emitted in that order as AddControl calls, so index 0 is the major control and the last is the minor. The golden proves the ordering behaviourally: its first operand CX(1:3) is the level whose footing prints last at a break and whose SUM covers both minor groups, while its second operand CX(4:) breaks on its own.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: cite.py --check 13.18.16.4 "Therefore FINAL, if specified, is associated with the highest level in the hierarchy" -> OK §13.18.16.4 2). FINAL is registered as a control whose value never changes (get = "", set = no-op) and DetectBreakLevel skips IsFinal, so it never breaks during GENERATE; its CF prints only at TERMINATE's most-major break (probe gr4/f3: `CFF B` once, after CFN/CFX, at TERMINATE). For every format-legal CONTROL clause FINAL is written first, so model.Controls[0] (the highest level) is FINAL. The out-of-position FINAL the grammar also admits is a FORMAT violation owned by FMT-13.18.16.2 / finding 1, not a GR2 defect. No spec-derived test isolates FINAL; test-ref empty. || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Reports.cs#BindReportDescriptionClauses; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ReportWriterEmitter.cs (FINAL AddControl); src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/ReportWriter.cs#DetectBreakLevel

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: The prior control is a saved character image per control operand (the emitted get/set pair over the operand's place); the chronologically first GENERATE saves without testing, later ones test major to minor and stop at the first change, and break processing runs for that level and every lower one. kb/Work PB205 made the SAVED item the right one for a reference-modified operand: GR3 gives the prior control 'the same data description as the corresponding data item', which for such an operand is the 8.4.3.3.4 GR5 unique data item - the slice - and the golden's two overlapping-item controls could not be told apart otherwise. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): the golden moved from tests/conformance/2002 to tests/conformance/2023 - it observes the report by re-reading the report file through ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL, which is a COBOL-2023 introduction (12.4.5.10.3 GR2; the Foreword's main-changes list over ISO/IEC 1989:2014), so the program is not expressible at 2002. The RULE's editions are unchanged.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1234, 14d). cite.py --check 13.18.16.4 "the corresponding prior controls are stored in the control data items before any control footing is printed" -> OK 4) a); "If no control footing is defined for the report, the new current values of the control data items are stored in the corresponding prior controls" -> OK 4) b); "the value produced is similarly the prior value" -> OK 4) a). GenerateCore on a break saves every current value, Sets every control to its prior, prints CFs minor->break, then restores current and makes it the prior, then prints CHs. VERIFIED by probe gr4.cob (CONTROLS FINAL CX CN, COMP-3 CN, page 8): CFN shows A 001 / A 002 / A 005 (priors), CFX shows A 005, USE BEFORE REPORTING CFX DISPLAYs CX=A CN=005 (prior), the CF-caused page advance prints `PF  A 005` and `PH  A 005` (prior), CHX then shows B 003 (new), and DISPLAY after GENERATE shows the new values. 4b (no CF) is observationally identical: the swap-and-restore has nothing between it, and priors end equal to the new values. DEFECT HALF: a legal FLOAT-LONG (or any IsFloat) control operand cannot be restored - the emitter writes a runtime NotImplemented loud, and the program dies at activation at 2002/2014/2023 (probe flt.cob). No syntax rule bars a float control item, so the GR4a save/restore mechanism is missing for a legal category -> finding 2. Existing spec-derived test covers the DISPLAY 4a path only. || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/ReportWriter.cs#GenerateCore; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ReportWriterEmitter.cs (CONTROL get/set delegates, float limb)

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: TERMINATE runs the same control-break processing as a highest-level break, so every defined control footing prints minor to major. subject: CONTROL clause
notes: cite.py --check 13.18.16.4 "Data-name-1 shall not reference a zero-length group item" -> OK 6). Zero-length group per §8.5.4 (cite.py --check 8.5.4 "A group data item containing only an occurs-depending table in which the number of occurrences is zero" -> OK 1)): item 1 (group of only an ODO table) and item 2 (group of only a zero-length subordinate, recursively ODO or DYNAMIC LENGTH) are always rejected at bind by ControlOperandShapeViolation's SR5 arm (OdoModel.TableUnder, cite OK §13.18.16.3 5)) and SR7 arm (HasVariableLengthSubordinate, cite OK §13.18.16.3 7)); items 3/4 are elementary, not groups; item 5 (a variable-length logical record whose runtime length is zero) is a run-time state the GR constrains the PROGRAM against with no exception condition or specified outcome, so no implementation action is required. Existing negatives pb177-control-occurs-depending / pb177-control-variable-length-group are SR5/SR7 witnesses whose groups have nonzero minimum length, so they do not witness GR6 as such; test-ref empty. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (text as in 2023; Annex E carries no edition note for it)

subject: DYNAMIC LENGTH clause
notes: cite.py --check 13.18.19.3 "The character-string specified in that PICTURE clause shall be one instance of the picture symbol 'N', or 'X'." OK (SR1). Both halves (a PICTURE shall be specified; exactly one N or X) verified by probe against the COBOLNET1561 check (regex ^[XN](\(0*1\))?$ over the upper-cased string): no PICTURE -> COBOLNET1561 (+0881); PIC XX, PIC N(2), PIC 1, PIC A -> COBOLNET1561; lower-case PIC x(001) accepted and runs; PIC X, PIC N accepted. || Editions (adjudicator): 2014, 2023 (COBOL-2014 introduction per VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE; the 2023 Annex E lists only the 2023 SET enhancement for dynamic-length items, E.3 item 17)

subject: DYNAMIC LENGTH clause
notes: kb/Work PB829. dynamic-length-structure-name-1 must correspond to a DYNAMIC LENGTH STRUCTURE declaration of the source element or a containing one (8.4.6.1 - the golden's contained program uses its container's DS-SS); an undeclared name is COBOLNET2258. It used to be refused whether declared or not (COBOLNET1562, retired).

subject: DYNAMIC LENGTH clause
notes: cite.py --check 13.18.19.3 "If dynamic-length-structure-name-1 is not specified, the structure of the dynamic-length elementary item is defined by the implementor." OK (SR3); cite.py --check 8.5.1.10.2 "In the absence of a dynamic-length-structure-name the internal structure is defined by the implementor." OK. The implementor structure is the native .NET string carrier (StorageForm.DynamicString, no length prefix or delimiter, DynStructure null, max = MaxLength); every unnamed-structure golden (dynamic_length_item, dynamic_length_limit) compiles and runs. cite.py --check A.1 "Dynamic-length elementary items (structure if dynamic-length-structure-name-1 is not specified). This item is required. This item need not be documented" OK (A.1 item 63): the item is REQUIRED but NEED NOT BE DOCUMENTED, so kb/Work PB991 (open, claims this row) rests on a false premise where it says the row 'Needs the A.1 documentation row' - documentation is optional, and the binder path already applies the structure. Where the structure becomes byte-observable (a file record) is determination D-FRA (PB981). Recommend PB991 close this row on this adjudication; its GR-12.3.7.4-19 half is unaffected. || Editions (adjudicator): 2014, 2023 (COBOL-2014 introduction per VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE; the 2023 Annex E lists only the 2023 SET enhancement for dynamic-length items, E.3 item 17)

subject: DYNAMIC LENGTH clause
notes: kb/Work PB829. LIMIT above the maximum length associated with the structure (its PREFIXED field capacity bounded by the implementor maximum) is COBOLNET2258: SHORT PREFIXED accepts 65535 and refuses 65536; SIGNED SHORT PREFIXED refuses 40000.

subject: DYNAMIC LENGTH clause
notes: cite.py --check 13.18.19.4 "The minimum length of the data item is zero. The picture symbol determines the class." OK (GR1). Three sentences, all verified: (a) length varies - dynamic_length_item golden and probe; (b) minimum zero - initial FUNCTION LENGTH of `PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH` with no VALUE is 0000 and displays [], MOVE "" gives length 0 (CobolDynString.Store never pads); (c) class from the picture symbol - StorageFormPass (1b) builds DynamicString(item.Pic.Category): a PIC N item is national (MOVE WN TO PIC X(4) refused COBOLNET0819 per the MOVE table; LIMIT 4 kept 4 national characters), PIC X alphanumeric. FUNCTION LENGTH of a PIC N dynamic item returns bytes (N"AB" -> 4), which is CORRECT per cite.py --check 15.50.4 "If argument-1 is a dynamic-length elementary item, the current length of argument-1 in bytes is returned." OK - not a defect. Unit cover also in CobolDynStringTests (min-zero). || Editions (adjudicator): 2014, 2023 (COBOL-2014 introduction per VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE; the 2023 Annex E lists only the 2023 SET enhancement for dynamic-length items, E.3 item 17)

subject: DYNAMIC LENGTH clause
notes: cite.py --check 13.18.19.4 "If the LIMIT phrase is not specified, the maximum number of characters that can be contained by the subject of the entry is implementor-defined." OK (GR2). Both halves verified: integer-1 is the maximum character count (MaxSizeOf = min(LIMIT, PREFIXED max, 0x3FFFFFDF)); probes: LIMIT 5 / LIMIT 3 / X(001) LIMIT 2 truncate MOVE "ABCDEFG" on the right to 5/3/2 characters; PIC N LIMIT 4 keeps 4 national CHARACTERS (not bytes). No LIMIT -> implementor maximum 1,073,741,791, documented as DOC-A.1-62 in docs/CONFORMANCE.md; a LIMIT above it warns COBOLNET2027 and clamps. Stale comment only: tests/conformance/2014/dynamic_length_limit.cob header calls the no-LIMIT item 'unbounded within the native string' - the bound is MaxLength; comment-level, not behavior. || Editions (adjudicator): 2014, 2023 (COBOL-2014 introduction per VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE; the 2023 Annex E lists only the 2023 SET enhancement for dynamic-length items, E.3 item 17)

subject: Entry-name clause
notes: "Data-name-1 shall not be qualified or subscripted." (cite.py --check 13.18.20.3 OK, rule 1). dataName is a single cobolWord/FILLER token with no qualifier or subscript alternative, so the declaration slot cannot carry either: probe/entry-name-clause/p4.cob `05 A OF G PIC X(3).` -> COBOL0001 near 'OF'; p5.cob `05 A(1) PIC X(3).` -> COBOL0001 near '('. Report group name (cobolWord) likewise. Rejection is a generic parse error, not a named diagnostic — acceptable for a syntax rule. No spec-derived negative test pins it. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause's own text; Annex E records no change to the entry-name clause)

subject: Entry-name clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1226, 14d). "If the entry-name clause is not specified in a data description entry, a report group description entry, or a screen description entry, the word FILLER is assumed." (--check 13.18.20.3 rule 2 OK). Data description: dataName? optional; probe/entry-name-clause/p1.cob `05 PIC X(2) VALUE "DE".` inside a group behaves as a filler (DISPLAY G -> ABCDEF) at 2023 and 85; LevelNumberPass.EntryName maps a missing name to FILLER. subject: EXTERNAL clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1236, 14d). §13.18.22.3 SR2: "In the same source element, the externalized name of the subject of the entry that includes the EXTERNAL clause shall not be the same as the externalized name of any other entry that includes the EXTERNAL clause." (cite.py OK §13.18.22.3 2)). The screen exists (COBOLNET2159) and fires for SR2DUP (two AS "Q"), SR2DEF (default name A vs AS "A") and SR2FD (two FDs AS "ZZ"). DEFECT: the screen compares with StringComparer.Ordinal while the run-unit store it protects (ExternalTable._cells) keys with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase, so two entries whose externalized names differ only in case pass SR2 and are then silently ALIASED onto one cell. Probe SR2ALIAS: `01 A PIC X(3) EXTERNAL.` + `01 B PIC X(5) EXTERNAL AS "a".`; MOVE "ABC" TO A; MOVE "12345" TO B; DISPLAY -> observed `A=[123] B=[123  ]`. Spec-derived expected: the implementation must apply ONE formation/mapping of externalized names (§8.3.2.2 2), so either the names are distinct (expected `A=[ABC] B=[12345]`) or they are the same externalized name and SR2 rejects the source; the observed truncated shared storage satisfies neither. The negative fixture covers only the exact-duplicate edge. || Editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (violable only once the AS phrase exists; at 1985 every externalized name is the entry's own unique name)

subject: EXTERNAL clause
notes: (kb/Work PB1236, 14d). §13.18.22.4 GR6: "...each name that is externalized to the operating environment for the record description entries shall be the same; the VALUE clause specification, if any, for each record name of the associated record description entries shall be identical; and the records shall define the same number of bytes. (cite.py OK §13.18.22.4 6)); §14.8.4.3 routes it to EC-EXTERNAL-FORMAT-CONFLICT. DEFECT: the VALUE identity is `RawValue.ToUpperInvariant()` (OoEmitter.EmitExternalDescribes), which case-folds the LITERAL CONTENT: probe G6CASE, `01 XV PIC X(4) IS EXTERNAL VALUE "ABCD".` vs `... VALUE "abcd".` -> NOEXC. Expected: "ABCD" and "abcd" are different VALUE clause specifications, so the condition is raised (EXC=[EC-EXTERNAL-FORMAT-CONFLICT]). subject: JUSTIFIED clause
notes: kb/Work PB737 (adjudication). THE RULE: 'When the receiving data item is described with the JUSTIFIED clause and the sending operand is larger than the receiving data item, the leftmost character positions or boolean positions of the sending operand shall be truncated' (cite.py --check 13.18.32.4 => OK 1)). ONE MECHANISM, ONE PLACE: every character store into an alphanumeric/alphabetic/national receiver routes through RuntimeApi.StrStoreAligned (MOVE, STRING, the INVOKE formal copy-back, ACCEPT temporal - kb/Work PB139's one-rule-one-place extraction of six hand-rolled ternaries), a boolean receiver through StrStoreBoolean, and BOTH end at CobolString.Store, whose justifiedRight arm is 'value.Length > width ? value[^width..]' - the RIGHTMOST width positions kept, i.e. the LEFTMOST truncated, which is the rule read literally. THE RULE NAMES TWO POSITION KINDS AND FOUR USAGES, AND EACH WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM THE ALPHANUMERIC ARM. Sending five positions into three: PIC X(3) JUSTIFIED gets 'CDE' (pb339_into_current_record leg B, whose sender is a 5-byte current record); PIC A(3) JUSTIFIED gets 'CDE'; PIC N(3) JUSTIFIED gets national CDE; PIC 1(3) JUSTIFIED and USAGE BIT PIC 1(3) JUSTIFIED both get '001' - the boolean-position half of the rule's own wording, and the USAGE BIT carrier answers the same way as the DISPLAY carrier because GR1 truncates POSITIONS, not bytes. Right truncation (the non-JUSTIFIED 14.6.8.5/14.6.8.6 rule) would give ABC/ABC/ABC/110/110, so every leg discriminates. JUSTIFIED is legal on exactly these categories by 13.18.32.3 SR3 (alphabetic, alphanumeric, boolean, national), so the four measured usages are the rule's whole domain; a numeric or edited receiver cannot carry the clause. New test conformance-test:NationalBooleanDataTests.JustifiedRight_SenderLarger_TruncatesLeftmostAcrossUsages carries the national/alphabetic/boolean/bit legs, which were implemented but unevidenced before this adjudication; the DISPLAY-alphanumeric leg is pb339_into_current_record leg B, corroborated by the ACCEPT temporal receiver. A reference-modified receiver stays exempt by 8.4.3.3.4 GR6 and a screen item's JUSTIFIED is a separate clause (13.18.32 in ScreenFacility's staged band), neither of which is this rule. EDITION-INVARIANCE WAS DERIVED, NOT ASSUMED: no docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row touches 13.18.32. The national and boolean legs are written at 2002 because PIC N and PIC 1 are themselves 2002+ language elements, not because the rule changes. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 . 2002 . 2014 . 2023

subject: JUSTIFIED clause
notes: kb/Work PB737 (adjudication). THE RULE IS ONE SENTENCE PLUS THREE PER-USAGE FILL SENTENCES, and the verdict rests on all four. (cite.py --check 13.18.32.4 'the data is aligned at the rightmost character position or boolean position in the data item with zero fill for the leftmost boolean positions and space fill for the leftmost character positions' => OK 2); --check 13.18.32.4 'For data items implicitly or explicitly described as usage national, national zeros shall be used for zero fill and national spaces shall be used for space fill' => OK 2); --check 13.18.32.4 'For data items implicitly or explicitly described as usage bit, bit zeros shall be used for zero fill' => OK 2).) THE ALIGNMENT is CobolString.Store's justifiedRight arm 'value.PadLeft(width, pad)', reached through the ONE dispatch RuntimeApi.StrStoreAligned for character receivers and StrStoreBoolean for boolean ones. THE FILL CHARACTER is that method's pad parameter and it is the ONLY thing the three usage sentences differ in: ' ' for a character receiver, '0' for a boolean/bit one (RuntimeApi.StrStoreBoolean pins pad: '0'). MEASURED, one leg per usage sentence: DISPLAY - a five-byte current record into PIC X(10) JUSTIFIED gives '     ABCDE' (pb339_into_current_record leg A at all four editions); NATIONAL - N"AB" into PIC N(4) JUSTIFIED gives national spaces then AB (NationalBooleanDataTests.JustifiedRight_NationalAndBoolean_LeftFill, whose '!' sentinel keeps the right end observable); BOOLEAN - B"11" into PIC 1(4) JUSTIFIED gives '0011' (conformance:2002/boolean_data leg JR, and the same test); USAGE BIT - B"11" into USAGE BIT PIC 1(4) JUSTIFIED gives '0011', the leg added by this adjudication because GR2 states its fill PER USAGE and a PIC 1(4) DISPLAY carrier therefore does not stand in for the bit one. The 'national zeros' and 'bit zeros' clauses are the ZERO-fill half; zero fill arises for a boolean/bit receiver, which is the case measured, while a national receiver's fill in an alignment is national spaces, also measured. JUSTIFIED's legal categories are fixed by 13.18.32.3 SR3 (alphabetic, alphanumeric, boolean, national), so these four usages are the whole domain of the rule. EDITION-INVARIANCE WAS DERIVED, NOT ASSUMED: no docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row touches 13.18.32; the national and boolean legs sit at 2002 because PIC N and PIC 1 are 2002+ elements, not because the rule changes. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 . 2002 . 2014 . 2023

subject: JUSTIFIED clause

(cite.py --check 13.18.32.4 -> OK §13.18.32.4 3); --check 14.6.8 "Alignment" -> OK). Probes: P1 A5 PIC X(5) (no JUSTIFIED) <- "AB" = [AB   ]; P10 PIC N(4) <- N"XY" = [XY  ], PIC 1(4) <- B"11" = [1100] — left alignment with right space/zero fill per §14.6.8, across alphanumeric, national and boolean. The substance of §14.6.8 is owned by its own rows; this row only requires that absence of JUSTIFIED leaves the standard rules in force, which holds. No test names this rule -> test-ref empty.

subject: Level-number
notes: Enforced STRUCTURALLY: every grammar rule that spells an entry opens with a mandatory levelNumber (dataDescriptionEntry, linkageProcedureParameter, reportGroupEntry, screenDescriptionEntry), so an entry with no level-number cannot parse. Witnessed because a rule enforced by the grammar's shape has no code site to point at, and an unwitnessed structural claim is indistinguishable from an unchecked one.

subject: Level-number
notes: The FileRecord arm: an entry subordinate to an FD or SD takes {66, 88, 1-49} and NOT 77, which SR5 admits. The witness is a 77 under an FD -- the case a flat section-blind range test accepts, and the reason the screen classifies from the entry's section ancestry. kb/Work PB485.

subject: Level-number
notes: A spelling permission, not a set: the screen parses the level-number TEXT to its VALUE and tests the value, so 01 through 09 and the bare 1 through 9 are the same level and both pass. The positive golden writes all of 01..09 plus a bare 1 and must still compile.

subject: Level-number
notes: The ReportGroup arm: a report group description entry subordinate to an RD takes 1-49 and no special level at all. reportGroupEntry is a distinct grammar rule reaching a distinct binder, which is why the screen sits on the shared levelNumber node instead of in each binder. kb/Work PB485.

subject: Level-number
notes: The NoncontiguousCapable arm: working-storage, local-storage and linkage take {66, 77, 88, 1-49}. Witnessed three ways -- the MicroFocus/GnuCOBOL 78 constant (which ISO does not define; the conforming spelling is the 13.10 CONSTANT entry), an ordinary out-of-range 50, and a twelve-digit level that used to become a silent lvl = 0 in DataBinder -- plus the positive over-rejection guard proving 66, 77, 88 and 1-49 still compile. kb/Work PB485.

subject: Level-number
notes: Annex A.4.2 (ACCEPT and DISPLAY screen handling) is an OPTIONAL module for which no support is claimed - docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 5 row 'A.4.2 | ACCEPT/DISPLAY screen handling | Not claimed' and section 4 item 4. A.4.1: an implementation shall accept an optional element's syntax ONLY when support is claimed, so the construct is REFUSED by name (COBOLNET1560 data/environment surface, COBOLNET1707 procedure surface); A.4.1 paragraph 2 extends the licence from the 27 printed items to the syntax and general rules hanging off them. subject: Level-number
notes: (kb/Work PB1246, 14d). GR1: "The level-number 1 identifies the first entry in each record description, type declaration, or report group." (cite.py --check 13.18.33.4 rule 1 -> OK); its obligation form is §13.11.1 "A record description entry consists of a set of data description entries, the first of which shall have level-number 1". Arms: (a) Level 1 STARTS a record: BindEntries pops the nesting stack on level <= open level, so each 01 opens a new root (probe p5: `01 G ... 01 H ...` -> two records, prints ABC) - conforms. (b) Type declaration: `05 T TYPEDEF.` is refused COBOLNET1529 (probe p7) - conforms. (c) Report group: an RD whose first entry is `02 DL TYPE DETAIL` is refused (probe p6), via ReportGroupBefore01 whose descriptor sits in the COBOLNET0899 NotImplemented band citing ISO §13.15 - the refusal is right, the code band says not-implemented. (d) Record description: DEFECT. BindEntries' `if (stack.Count == 0)` makes ANY first entry a root whatever its level, and no screen tests that the first entry of a record description is level 1. Probes: p2 WORKING-STORAGE `05 A PIC X VALUE "A". 05 B PIC X VALUE "B".` with no 01 compiles clean and prints AB at 85/2002/2014/2023; p3 `FD F. 05 R PIC X(4).` compiles clean. Harm: under-rejects. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (type declaration arm 2002+ with TYPEDEF; report group arm with Report Writer A.4.11)

subject: Level-number
notes: All three special-level assignments, each with its own witness: GR2a (77 may be used only as described by the data description format) by a 77 written as a renames entry; GR2b (66 only as the renames format) in BOTH directions -- a 66 with no RENAMES clause and a RENAMES body at another level, the latter of which reached the emitter and produced uncompilable C# before this screen; GR2c (88 only as the condition-name or validation format) by an 88 carrying a PICTURE. The format is read from the entry BODY and never from the level-number, or every one of these rules would be vacuous. kb/Work PB485.

subject: Level-number
notes: kb/Work PB836 LANDED; kb/Work PB981 LANDED (determination D-FRA, docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3). Sentence 1 - 'Multiple level 1 entries subordinate to a FD or SD entry represent implicit redefinitions of the same area': DataBinder.LinkImplicitRecordArea, the ONE linker for the FD and SD arms, joins every later CHARACTER-WINDOW level-1 record to the first through DataItem.SetRedefinition(first, RedefinitionKind.ImplicitFileRecord); the storage layout reads the one class for both constructs, while the 13.18.44.3 REDEFINES-clause screens read RedefinesKind == Clause only. Since PB981 a dynamic-length record, a variable-length group or a pointer-class record - legal source that used to be staged loud as COBOLNET0899 - is an OUT-OF-LINE record (FileModel.IsOutOfLineRecord): 8.5.1.10.3 lets its storage be located elsewhere, so it is never linked into the class and shares the area at the transfer boundary instead - a READ/RETURN makes the current record available in it (SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRecordAreaStore; a variable-length group through the one split rule CobolVarGroup.FromContiguous), and a WRITE/REWRITE/RELEASE sends its contiguous image (8.5.1.11.2). The 2014 golden writes and reads back a variable-length group, a dynamic-length record and a character record of one FD, a SAME RECORD AREA peer and an SD; the 2002 golden a pointer record beside a character record. Residue stated in D-FRA: an EXTERNAL file whose area has an out-of-line record, and a SORT/MERGE key that follows a variable-length member, are refused by name. Sentence 2 - report description level-1 entries are not implicit redefinitions: the report binder never calls SetRedefinition. EDITIONS 2002/2014/2023 as before; the FD rule is COBOL-85 base language and the same binder arm serves 85.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB489 LANDED. SR1 now HAS a site - DataBinder.ResolveLinage, the FD-clause twin of ResolveFileCollating, run post-build because an operand's OCCURS ancestry is unknown until the data forest is indexed - and it reports COBOLNET2025 naming SR1's own sentence. Both spellings of the violation are screened, at the two places they are decidable: the WRITTEN subscript at the capture (a subscript is not part of 8.4.2.2.2 Format 1's qualified-data-name, COBOLNET2024), and the RESOLVED table element in ResolveLinage. Before this, neither existed: `LINAGE IS T-LINES LINES` over `05 T-LINES PIC 99 OCCURS 3 TIMES` compiled CLEAN and killed the process at OPEN OUTPUT with an unhandled NotImplementedCobolFeatureException whose text cited SR2 for what is SR1's obligation - a run-time crash where 4.2.2 requires a compile-time indication. The sibling message at SequentialIoEmitter.LinageOpExpr remains as the 1.4 backstop only; it is no longer the enforcement. SR2 (elementary unsigned numeric integer) and SR3 (integer-2 not greater than integer-1) are one more test each in ResolveLinage and stay with kb/Work PB524; the method names them in a comment so the next fixer adds a test beside these rather than a screen elsewhere.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB524 (landed): ResolveLinage screens every resolved LINAGE data-name operand against all four conjuncts of SR2 and names the first one broken under COBOLNET2025 - a group item (not elementary), a non-numeric item or an index item (class index), a non-integer (PicInfo.IsIntegerDescription: fixed-point with no fraction; a floating-point item is refused), a signed item. Measured on the implementer's build: group, PIC X(3), PIC S9(3), PIC 9V9 and alphanumeric FOOTING/BOTTOM operands each rejected at every edition; the positive golden binds a DISPLAY PIC 9(3) page and USAGE COMP PIC 99 margins and pins the GR7/GR26b counter/EOP sequence.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB524 (landed): with integer-1 and integer-2 both literals, FOOTING greater than the page size is refused at compile time under COBOLNET2025 (it used to reach run time and throw a CLR InvalidOperationException); the equality boundary (FOOTING AT 4 on a page of 4) compiles and runs in the positive golden. A data-name on either side makes the relation a run-time value governed by 13.18.34.4 GR3, outside this syntax rule.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: Zero margins are accepted (the permission — tested by the fixture compiling at all) and, per §13.18.34.4 GR1, must behave as an omitted phrase: LINAGE-COUNTER steps 1,2,3,4 identically on the explicit-zero file and the phrase-less control (GR7d, GR7c3). The columns pin GR7, NOT margin handling — a zero margin is the identity, so column equality is blind to how a margin is treated. Every WRITE is preceded by its own MOVE because §14.9.51.4 GR4 empties the record area on each successful WRITE.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB523 LANDED - THE LOGICAL PAGE SIZE IS THE SUM, AND THE SUM IS ON THE MEDIUM. All four conjuncts now hold, and the one that did not is the one this row was PARTIAL for. (a) 'The logical page size is the SUM of the values referenced by each phrase except the FOOTING phrase': SequentialConnector no longer keeps a counter over an untouched print stream - it keeps a PHYSICAL-POSITION model of the logical page (top margin, page body, bottom margin) and derives a page transition's travel from that page (BeginNextLogicalPage: the unwritten rest of the body, then the bottom margin, then exactly one line onto the next page, which is what 13.18.34.4 GR8's contiguity makes it) rather than from the WRITE's own ADVANCING amount. MEASURED on LINAGE IS 2 LINES LINES AT TOP 3 LINES AT BOTTOM 2: the logical page is 3 + 2 + 2 = 7 lines, page 1 occupies physical lines 1-7 and page 2 begins at physical line 8, so a record on page-1 body line 2 and the next on page-2 body line 1 stand FIVE lines apart (bottom margin 2 + top margin 3) where the old code wrote one. Pinned byte-for-byte by the named 2023 golden (which writes, closes and reads the file back AS LINE SEQUENTIAL so each DISPLAYed index is a physical line number: A05 / A11 / A12) and by its 85 twin (which reads the medium one character at a time and pins LEN=0036, A@=0009, B@=0025, C@=0031 against the counter-only reading's LEN=0020, A@=0003, B@=0009, C@=0015). (b) 'If the LINES AT TOP or LINES AT BOTTOM phrases are not specified, the values of these items are zero' - LinageOpExpr renders the literal 0 for an absent operand, and Bytes_NoMarginPhrases_LeaveThePrintStreamUnchanged pins that a zero margin is the IDENTITY on the medium, which is the half no test could reach while the margins produced no bytes at all. (c) 'If the FOOTING phrase is not specified, no end-of-page condition independent of the page overflow condition exists' - the footing arm is guarded by _footing > 0 and Gr1_NoFooting_EopIsOverflowOnly covers it. (d) 'There is not necessarily any relationship between the size of the logical page and the size of a physical page' - a permission, and now honoured with content rather than vacuously: the model never consults a physical page.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB489 LANDED - THE REFUTATION IS REPAIRED. The row was held at PARTIAL by one operand spelling: when data-name-1 was QUALIFIED the compiler used the value of a DIFFERENT data item, silently, so GR2's 'the value of the data item referenced by data-name-1' was the page size of whatever item of that name happened to be declared first. The mechanism was in the binder, and the row's code-location now names it: BindLinageClause kept only the first word of the operand's dataReference and ResolveFiles resolved that bare word with `ByName.TryGetValue(n) -> list[0]`. Both are gone. The operand keeps its IN/OF qualifiers and resolves through DataBinder.QualifiedCandidates - the ONE 8.4.2.2 candidate-set matcher, shared with the procedure division's ReferenceResolver, which knows the file-name qualifier of 8.4.2.2.2 Format 1 and returns the SET so that the NUMBER of survivors is the answer 8.4.2.2.1 demands. MEASURED, on the probe the refutation named: `LINAGE IS SZ OF GRP-B LINES` over GRP-A.SZ=3 and GRP-B.SZ=9 with `WRITE ... AFTER ADVANCING 4 LINES` reported EOP / LINAGE-COUNTER 1 (a 3-line page) before and reports NO-EOP / LINAGE-COUNTER 5 (the correct 9-line page) now, at every edition. The third spelling - an AMBIGUOUS unqualified operand - is now REJECTED (COBOLNET1639) instead of resolved by declaration order. The row's cost disclosure about the page body's POSITION under a top margin is GR4's obligation and is recorded there; GR2's own sentence is clean.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB525 LANDED - THE 'GREATER THAN ZERO' HALF IS NOW ENFORCEABLE, BECAUSE ZERO IS NO LONGER THE ABSENT-PHRASE SENTINEL. The footing AREA was always right ([footing start, page size] INCLUSIVE - pinned at the boundary by Gr26ab_CounterEqualsBody_IsFootingEopNotOverflow and its goldens). What was not implemented was GR3's 'The value shall be greater than zero and not greater than integer-1 or the value of the data item referenced by data-name-1', because ONE integer slot carried two different facts: 'the footing start' and 'there is no FOOTING phrase', with 0 encoding the second. The fix is the SHAPE, not the guard: LinagePage.Footing is int?, SequentialIoEmitter.LinageOpExpr renders null for an OMITTED phrase (TOP and BOTTOM stay int - GR1 says their values ARE zero when absent, so only FOOTING had a collision), EvaluateLinage applies GR6 b) 2 to every footing start that IS specified including 0, and the GR26 b) end-of-page arm's guard became `_footing is { } f` - a test of PRESENCE rather than of value. THE DISCRIMINATING PAIR is on disk: Gr6b2_FootingPhraseHoldingZero_IsAViolation_NotAnAbsentPhrase and Gr1_NoFootingPhrase_SamePageAndWrite_IsAnOrdinarySuccessfulWrite are the same page size, the same WRITE, differing only in whether the FOOTING phrase is written - a model that encodes absence as 0 cannot tell them apart, which is exactly what used to happen (the first one printed NO-EOP / LC=005 like the second). A specified footing of 0 is now the §13.18.34.4 GR6 b) 2 violation, reported as I-O status '90' with the EC-I-O-LINAGE condition - see GR-13.18.34.4-6.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB523 LANDED - THE TOP MARGIN IS A LINE OF THE LOGICAL PAGE AND REACHES THE MEDIUM. _top is read by EmitTopMarginIfPending, which every travel (PositionOnLogicalPage) and every presentation (Present) calls FIRST, so no record can reach a page body without the top margin ahead of it and no write arm can be added that skips it. MEASURED on LINES AT TOP 3 with page size 2: the first record lands on physical line 5 (three margin lines, then body line 1, then the AFTER ADVANCING 1 travel to body line 2) and the record after the page wrap on physical line 11, three lines past the start of page 2. The ADVANCING PAGE arm is fixed with it: 14.9.51.4 GR25 g) requires the repositioning to be 'to the first line that may be written on the next logical page as specified in the LINAGE clause', so BeginNextLogicalPage runs there too and the bare form feed is gone (GR25 h) is the NO-LINAGE arm, and Advance's form feed is now reachable only from it) - Bytes_AdvancingPage_RepositionsToTheNextLogicalPage_NotAFormFeed pins eight leading blank lines and no 0x0C. Both WRITE arms were fixed, not one: the LINE SEQUENTIAL twin (Bytes_LineSequentialLinageFile_GetsTheSameMargins) had emitted its record and a bare newline, which is the two-arm dispatch this repository's rule 4 sweep looks for. THE ONE LATITUDE, and the rule that grants it: the margin is materialized at the first thing written on the page rather than at OPEN OUTPUT, which 14.9.27.4 GR18 permits ('the positioning of the output medium with respect to physical page boundaries is implementor-defined following the successful execution of the OPEN statement, whether or not the LINAGE clause is specified'); it makes an OPEN OUTPUT + CLOSE with no WRITE leave an empty file (14.9.51.4 GR12 released nothing) and is byte-identical to the eager reading whenever any record is presented. GnuCOBOL defers it the same way. NIST corroboration, independent of this implementation: SQ201M's own visual-check text asks for 50 body lines 'FOLLOWED BY 16 TOP AND BOTTOM BLANK LINES' on LINAGE 50 TOP 10 BOTTOM 6, SQ209M's for 'TWO BLANK LINES SHOULD FOLLOW ... IT SHOULD BE THREE LINES BELOW THE PREVIOUS LINE' on TOP 2 BOTTOM 0, and SQ210M's for pages 'SEPARATED BY 5 BLANK LINES' on TOP 5 - all three now hold and none did before.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB523 LANDED - THE BOTTOM MARGIN, THE SAME WAY AND IN THE SAME PLACE. _bottom is read by BeginNextLogicalPage, the ONE page transition shared by 14.9.51.4 GR25 g)'s ADVANCING PAGE and GR26 a)'s page overflow, whose first act is to travel the rest of the current page: max(0, page size - LINAGE-COUNTER) unwritten body lines plus the bottom margin. Recorded separately from GR-13.18.34.4-4 because a fix that reserved only the top margin would have left this row open; it is closed by evidence that isolates it. MEASURED on LINAGE IS 2 LINES LINES AT TOP 3 LINES AT BOTTOM 2: a record on page-1 body line 2 (the LAST writable line, so the bottom margin is the whole remaining travel) and the next record on page-2 body line 1 are five lines apart, of which two are this margin. Bytes_OverflowWithBeforePhrase_PresentsThenRepositions isolates it further by presenting ON the last body line with a BEFORE phrase and then measuring the travel out of the page. The 85 twin's byte-offset form gives the same quantity arithmetically: without the two bottom-margin lines the file would be 4 characters shorter and C@ would move.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB525 + PB526 LANDED - THE EXCEPTION CONDITION IS AN EXCEPTION CONDITION. The timing half was already right and still is (GR6 a) a literal's value is always that literal; GR6 b) 1 read at the completion of OPEN OUTPUT; GR6 b) 2 re-read during a WRITE ADVANCING PAGE; GR6 b) 3 re-read during a page-overflow WRITE, after the overflow decision was taken against the OLD body; 'the value applies to the next logical page'). WHAT LANDED is the whole second half. (i) Both VALUE RULES are now enforceable and enforced: GR6 b) 1 'The page size shall be greater than zero' and GR6 b) 2 'The footing start shall be greater than zero and not greater than the page size' - the latter applied exactly when the FOOTING PHRASE IS SPECIFIED, which required making the absent phrase ABSENT in the model (LinagePage.Footing is int?, SequentialIoEmitter.LinageOpExpr renders null for an omitted phrase) instead of encoding it as the value 0. (ii) A violation is no longer a raw System.InvalidOperationException that kills the process: EvaluateLinage returns false and the connector reports an unsuccessful I-O status '90' (§9.1.13.11's implementor-defined value; docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 DOC-A.1-110) together with the exception-name GR6 b) 2 NAMES, through FileConnector.SetIoCondition - and the raise itself goes through the ONE EC-I-O channel, the emitted __IoCheckEc hook, which owns the USE format-1 and format-3 tiers, the exception-checking PERFORM frames and the fatal default. The name has to travel beside the status because §9.1.13.1's status->EC correspondence has no entry for EC-I-O-LINAGE and reads a '9x' as EC-I-O-IMP; §14.6.13.1.1's 'Unless otherwise specified, if more than one exception is detected during the execution of a statement, the one that is set to exist is undefined' is the licence for the specific rule to win, and FileRegistry.IoConditionName is the ONE place the named condition and the correspondence are combined. (iii) ALL THREE consequences of GR6 b) 2's closing sentence are realized and witnessed: execution continues with the statement following the WRITE (measured: the DISPLAY after the failing WRITE runs); the LINAGE-COUNTER is set to 0 and remains at that value until the file is closed (measured: LC=000 at the violation, at every later WRITE, and back to 001 only after a CLOSE + fresh OPEN OUTPUT); and all subsequent WRITE statements referencing the file cause the condition to continue to exist until the file is closed (the _linagePageBroken latch, checked by BOTH write entries because a plain WRITE on a LINE SEQUENTIAL LINAGE file does not route through WriteAdvancing). The file connector STAYS OPEN at an OPEN-time violation - GR6 b) 2's 'until the file is closed' and 'all subsequent WRITE statements referencing the file' both presuppose it - so the OPEN reports the status and nothing else about it changes. With checking for EC-I-O-LINAGE enabled the standard fatal protocol applies unchanged (§14.6.13.1.3 4)-7)): 2023/pb526_linage_ec_checking runs a format-3 USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-I-O-LINAGE declarative whose FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS reads EC-I-O-LINAGE (not EC-I-O-IMP - that is the assertion the name override exists for) and RESUMEs; with no handler the run unit terminates abnormally with a named diagnostic instead of a CLR stack dump. The 85 twin exists because the whole behaviour is reachable with no construct newer than 1985 - the status and the format-1 declarative carry it - so a regression making it depend on the EC subsystem being present cannot stay green.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB489 LANDED - BOTH HALVES OF GR7 b)'s RESTRICTION NOW HOLD. (i) 'may be referenced only in PROCEDURE DIVISION statements' is enforced: a LINAGE-COUNTER written in a file description entry's LINAGE clause is refused at bind with COBOLNET2024 naming 8.4.3.14.3 SR1, where it used to compile clean and die at OPEN with the nonsense message "LINAGE operand 'LPF' is not resolvable to storage" - the binder had taken the FILE-NAME QUALIFIER for the data-name. (ii) 'only the input-output control system may change the value' now rejects by its OWN rule: ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving grew the missing third arm, COBOLNET2026 citing 8.4.3.14.3 SR2 and 13.18.34.4 GR7 b). It was the two-arm-dispatch shape with the third arm absent - LINE-COUNTER had a rule-citing rejection and PAGE-COUNTER a correctly-labelled not-yet-implemented, while LINAGE-COUNTER, the only one of the three that is flatly ILLEGAL as a receiver, inherited the generic COBOLNET0899 catch-all and told the user that permanently illegal source was a feature awaiting implementation; the named test asserts COBOLNET0899 is no longer among the diagnostics. Everything the adjudication recorded as already implemented and covered is unchanged: GR7 a)'s per-file counter, the counter's meaning under GR7 c), and both arms of GR7 b)'s qualification requirement including the PB123 GLOBAL-FD sweep.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB578 — THE RESET IS IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED; THE IMPLICIT-INCREMENT SENTENCE HAS NO IMPLEMENTATION AND ITS UNOBSERVABILITY IS A DERIVATION WITH A HOLE. Sentence 1 ('automatically reset to one') is the `lines < 0` arm and the named test pins it. Sentence 2 ('during the resetting ... the value of LINAGE-COUNTER is implicitly incremented to exceed the value specified by integer-1') is modelled nowhere: the arm sets EndOfPage = false and returns. The argument that this costs nothing runs: (a) the only consumer of 'exceeds the page size' is 14.9.51 GR26a's page-overflow condition; (b) its observable effects are the reposition-and-reset (already done) and GR6b3's re-evaluation, which GR6b2 already performs on this same arm (:163); (c) its END-OF-PAGE flag cannot be seen, because 14.9.51.3 SR18 forbids ADVANCING PAGE and END-OF-PAGE in one statement and the compiler enforces it (conformance-test:CobolNet.Tests.Conformance.LinageConformanceTests.Sr18_AdvancingPageWithEop_IsRejected). THE HOLE: step (c) assumes no user code observes LINAGE-COUNTER mid-statement, and a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR declarative entered from inside this WRITE could. That path is currently unreachable only because of a separate defect (p18_use.cob: the declarative never fires), so the derivation rests on a bug rather than on the language. PARTIAL under 'an unverified edge => PARTIAL'; it is a candidate for the PB386 no-observable-obligation close once the EC path exists. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs:159-165 (the ADVANCING PAGE arm: LinageCounter = 1, then EvaluateLinage)

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: BOTH OPERAND FORMS MEASURED. The integer form is the named test (1 + 3 = 4) and the zero case is conformance-test:CobolNet.Tests.Conformance.LinageConformanceTests.Gr25c_AdvancingZero_CounterUnchanged. The IDENTIFIER form - the half the rule states separately and no repo test exercises - was probed: <lane3 scratch>/out-b3/probe/linage/p24_ident.cob does `WRITE ... AFTER ADVANCING WS-N LINES` with WS-N = 3 then `BEFORE ADVANCING WS-N LINES` with WS-N = 2 on a 9-line body and reads back LINAGE-COUNTER 4 then 6, i.e. the item's CURRENT contents at each write, and BEFORE and AFTER both count. || CORRECTED 2026-09-06 by kb/Work PB712. notes: BOTH SENTENCES MEASURED. 7c4 (reset to one at each succeeding logical page) is the named test - an advance of 4 from line 4 of a 5-line body lands on 1, not on the modulo carry 3. 7d (set to one at OPEN OUTPUT) is conformance-test:CobolNet.Tests.Conformance.LinageConformanceTests.Gr7d_CounterIsOneAtOpenOutput, and the OPEN arm is guarded on FileOpenMode.Output so INPUT / EXTEND / I-O do not reset it (14.9.27.3 SR2 forbids EXTEND on a LINAGE file outright). subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB523 LANDED - CONTIGUOUS, ON BOTH TRANSITIONS, WITH NOTHING ADDITIONAL. The rule was PARTIAL for two reasons and both are gone. (1) The ADVANCING PAGE transition used to write a form-feed character, which is neither a line of the logical page nor 'no additional spacing'; it now goes through BeginNextLogicalPage like the overflow transition, and Advance's form feed is reachable only from 14.9.51.4 GR25 h), the arm for a file with NO LINAGE clause. Bytes_AdvancingPage_RepositionsToTheNextLogicalPage_NotAFormFeed asserts the whole file byte-for-byte, so a 0x0C anywhere fails it. (2) The code comment that cited THIS rule as licence to drop the top and bottom margins is deleted and replaced with the derivation: GR8 forbids spacing ADDITIONAL to the logical page, it does not delete the margins 13.18.34.4 GR1/GR4/GR5 define the page to contain - under the old reading GR4 and GR5 had no content at all and GR1's 'sum ... except the FOOTING phrase' was a sum of one term. WHAT CONTIGUITY NOW MEANS, MEASURED: a page transition adds exactly (page size - LINAGE-COUNTER) + bottom margin + 1 lines and not one byte more, so the next page's line 1 is the line immediately after the current page's last line; on a 7-line logical page written from body line 2, page 2 starts at physical line 8. The zero-margin case is the same code path with both margins zero and Bytes_NoMarginPhrases_LeaveThePrintStreamUnchanged pins that it costs exactly one line, i.e. that no filler was introduced by the new model.

notes: Owned by kb/Work PB1266. cite.py --check 13.18.38.3 "Index-name-1 may be specified only in the following contexts" -> OK. The five contexts work: subscript T(IX) and T(IX - 1), PERFORM VARYING IX, SEARCH VARYING IX, SET, IF IX = 2 -> probe/occurs-p1/sr7_ok ('QQ', 'F'). Outside them the index-name is rejected: DISPLAY, MOVE, COMPUTE and a ref-mod bound -> COBOLNET1637 (sr7_display, sr7_move, sr7_compute, sr7_refmod). ADD 1 TO IX and CALL ... USING IX are also rejected, but by COBOLNET1639 "'IX' is not defined — no declaration in this source element gives the name 'IX'" (sr7_add, sr7_call). The verdict is right, the message is false: that is the defect SetBinder.cs:391's comment names ('false about a name INDEXED BY declared, and it sends the reader hunting a typo'), fixed there but not at these sites. EVALUATE IX WHEN 2 is accepted (sr7_evaluate) because a selection subject/object pair is evaluated as a relation. Many landed notes cover this rule (PB170/172/215/219/221/223/224, R29). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — EVALUATE IX WHEN 1 THRU 3 compiles and runs (r7_evaluate_subject rc=0 'E'; the adjudicator's sr7_evaluate showed the same). A selection-subject is identifier-1 / literal-1 / arithmetic-expression-1 / boolean-expression-1 / condition-1 / TRUE / FALSE (§14.9.13.2) - an index-name is none of these (the compiler itself refuses IX as an identifier, §8.4.3.1.2, and as an arithmetic operand, 1637). SR7 restricts where index-name-1 may be SPECIFIED; the EVALUATE general rule that evaluates the subject/object pair 'as a relation' is semantics, not a relation condition written in the source, so the adjudicator's rationale is a real clause answering a different question. Everything else holds: DISPLAY (also --std 85), MOVE, COMPUTE, FUNCTION ABS(IX), DIVIDE, STRING, refmod bound -> 1637; PERFORM IX TIMES -> 1646; GO TO DEPENDING ON IX -> 2324; INITIALIZE IX / INSPECT TALLYING IX / ADD / CALL -> 1639 with the false 'not defined' message. Legal contexts (subscript, PERFORM VARYING/AFTER, SEARCH VARYING, SET, relation incl. EVALUATE TRUE WHEN IX = 2) accepted. The cited test-ref conformance:negative/display-index-name pins only the DISPLAY branch.

notes: kb/Work PB201 (2026-09-04). REJECTED side: DataBinder.Odo screens data-name-1 as Category Numeric, IsFloat false, Scale 0 and raises COBOLNET0852 otherwise - a PIC 9V9 control item is rejected at every edition (pb201-odo-depending-not-integer; OCCURS DEPENDING is COBOL-85 and rule 17 has no introduction axis). ACCEPTED side: rule 17 asks for an INTEGER and nothing narrower, so a 20-digit COMP item and an unsigned BINARY-DOUBLE are both legal control items; pb201_odo_count_carriers exercises both and asserts the 13.18.38.4 GR8a current-count part each one sends. That golden is what proved the SECOND emitter of the position-carrier defect: RuntimeApi.TableOcc renders the current-count read at CODEGEN time from a Place and cannot decline a carrier and re-route the way the subscript renderer can, so MOVE <odo-group> TO X failed the backend with four CS1503s (System.Int128 and ulong to long) in the DEFAULT strict lane. Rule 17 is exactly what bounds that emitter's carrier universe to long/Int128/ulong/UInt128 plus the promoted string image - all five of which CobolTable.Occ now declares a parameter for - which is why the rejection has its own negative golden rather than resting on the accept side.

subject: RECORD clause
notes: THE RULE HAS TWO HALVES AND BOTH ARE PINNED. notes: kb/Work PB537 LANDED (wave 58). ONE subject screen, COBOLNET2422: an elementary entry (data description OR report group description - SR1's first two bullets are one test, DataBinder.SignClauseElementaryDefect) must be category numeric with an 'S' in its WRITTEN picture character-string; a group must be an alphanumeric, national or strongly-typed group item (ItemCategory.GroupKindsOf - a GROUP-USAGE BIT group, declared or inherited by 13.16.4 GR1, and a variable-length group are refused). The data-description arm is the post-forest CheckSignClauses pass (after UsageInheritancePass, before InheritSignClauses) over the entries that WROTE the clause - a TYPE copy or a SAME AS ancestor clause (13.18.49.4 GR5) is not re-screened. The former float-edited special case (COBOLNET1658) is this rule's numeric-edited arm and was deleted. The SCREEN description entry bullet is owner-declined A.4.2 non-support (COBOLNET1560, kb/Work PB260). Refused before: PIC 9(3), PIC X(3), PIC N(3), PIC ZZ9, USAGE INDEX, FLOAT-LONG, a bit group, a nested bit group, a report entry PIC 9(3) - each compiled clean at every edition.

notes: kb/Work PB537 LANDED (wave 58). A SIGN clause on a GROUP is not SR2's subject (it names 'an elementary item for which the SIGN clause is specified'), so 01 G USAGE COMP SIGN LEADING. is legal and GR1 applies the clause only to display/national subordinates (ApplyEffectiveSign). notes: kb/Work PB547 — TWO OF THE THREE OBLIGATIONS HOLD OUTRIGHT; THE UNIFORM-SIZE CLAUSE HOLDS ONLY OVER THE LATIN-1 SUBSET OF WHAT THE ITEM ACTUALLY ADMITS, AND THE EXCESS IS LOST SILENTLY. HOLDS: "an alphanumeric coded character set shall be used" and "the data item is aligned on a character boundary" - probe q9 (--std 2023) gives BYTE-LENGTH == LENGTH == the declared positions for X(5), 9(5), S9(5) (an unseparate sign shares a digit position), A(5) and ZZ9; probe q71 shows a DISPLAY leaf never shares a byte and never pads (`X(1) 9(1) 1(1)BIT X(1)` is 4 bytes and G(1:1)/G(2:1)/G(4:1) read P/7/Q, i.e. the character leaves sit on byte boundaries and only the BIT leaf takes 8.5.1.6.3's own byte). HOLDS: "Each implementor shall specify the size and representation of characters stored for usage DISPLAY" - A.1 item 209 is the required item and docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-209 states it (one byte per character position, uniform at every length, no per-compilation-unit option), pinned by the spec-derived golden conformance:2023/l1_usage_display_character_size whose UNI leg measures 1/5/9 for X(1)/X(5)/X(9). WHAT IS PARTIAL - "Alphanumeric characters shall be represented in the storage of the computer as characters of UNIFORM SIZE equal to or less than the size of characters in the computer's national character set": the item admits characters the documented size cannot represent, so the size is not uniform across the item's own content. Measured (probe q50, --std 2023): `01 G. 05 A PIC X(3).` with `MOVE "A(U+00E9)(U+2603)" TO A` compiles, and FUNCTION ORD of A(1:1)/A(2:1)/A(3:1) returns 66/234/9732 - the item is holding U+00E9 and U+2603 as UTF-16 CODE UNITS, one per position, and the group image returns the same three values - while FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(A) is 3. At the byte boundary the third character is not represented at all: probe q72 writes that record to a SEQUENTIAL file and the file is exactly 3 bytes, 41 E9 3F - the snowman became '?'. Probe q80 repeats it under `>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON` and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS comes back BLANK, so the loss is SILENT. That contradicts the implementation's OWN decided disposition, which docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-33 records for the same substitution ("the serialization substitutes '?' (0x3F) and sets EC-DATA-CONVERSION ... never silent") - the CONVERT leg was given the EC and the record/file leg was not, the two-arm shape. The rule's own words are the test: a character in an alphanumeric item is either represented at the uniform size or it is not admitted; here it is admitted, carried at 2 bytes in memory and written at 1 with a substitution nobody is told about. See finding usage-p3/F1. NOTE the neighbouring tension the row does not itself resolve: DOC-A.1-209 says the alphanumeric character is ONE byte while DOC-A.1-188 and DOC-A.1-33 say "the native alphanumeric and national repertoires are UTF-16, one code unit per character position" - the two determinations disagree about the size of the very character GR7 asks the implementor to specify. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth (the `_ => ElementaryImageWidth` DISPLAY arm - one byte per character position); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ByteForm (Usage.Display -> NumericByteForm.Zoned); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/BitLayout.cs#BitsPerCharacter; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-209; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-33 (the '?' substitution disposition) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85,2002,2014,2023 (USAGE DISPLAY, explicit or implied, is a COBOL-85 element and the implied default at every edition - 13.18.60.3 SR13 b)

subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB546 — THE SIZE THE IMPLEMENTOR SPECIFIED IS NOT THE SIZE THE STORAGE USES, AND THE DISAGREEMENT DISPLACES EVERY LEAF AFTER A NATIONAL ONE. What conforms: the head of the rule and the alignment - `01 N PIC N(4) USAGE NATIONAL.` reports FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 8 and FUNCTION LENGTH 4 (probe q11), i.e. 2 bytes per national position, and 2 IS "a multiple of the size of characters in the computer's alphanumeric character set" (1, DOC-A.1-209); `01 M PIC N(4).` reports the same, so SR13 a's implied USAGE NATIONAL agrees; national values store, compare and display (conformance:2002/national_data). THE DIVERGENCE, minimal repro (probe q73, --std 2023): `01 G. 05 N PIC N(2) USAGE NATIONAL. 05 A PIC X(2).` with `MOVE N"AB" TO N` and `MOVE "YZ" TO A`. FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(G) = 6 and FUNCTION LENGTH(G) = 6 - so A is DECLARED at positions 5-6 - yet `G(3:2)` reads "YZ" and `G(5:2)` reads two spaces. The same wrong layout crosses a CALL: probe q52 passes G BY REFERENCE to a program whose linkage is `01 W PIC X(6)` and the callee reads ORD 66 67 90 91 33 33 = A,B,Y,Z,space,space; probe q25/q27 show the identical thing through a group MOVE. MECHANISM, located and named by the code itself: DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth answers `2 * ElementaryImageWidth` for Usage.National (the documented D-N1/D-N3 model) while DataItem.IsCharacterImage's comment says a national leaf "contribute[s] their CHARACTER positions to a group image (ImageWidth = Length - never byte-doubled for national)". Two widths for one item, and the consumers split: BYTE-LENGTH / LENGTH / the declared group size take ByteWidth, the image codec and every channel built on it take ImageWidth. DataItem.IsImageCapable's own doc comment asserts the opposite - "Width-wise the codec uses ImageWidth, which IS ByteWidth for every item that reaches an image - the ONE-WIDTH invariant" - and the drift test that guards it, ImageWidthIsStorageWidthTests, carves national out by name (NationalLeaf_IsExactlyTwoBytesPerPosition asserts ImageWidth 4 / ByteWidth 8 and calls it "the ONE sanctioned divergence"), so the invariant cannot catch this and never has. THE IMPLEMENTATION ALREADY KNOWS: the FILE-record channel refuses the same shape LOUD - probe q60 gives COBOLNET0899 "national data in a file record ... the record codec is single-byte and the national character is two bytes (Phase 4a residue; ISO 8.1.2 / 13.18.60.4 GR8)" - so one of the four byte channels is honest and three are silently wrong. What the rule requires: "National characters shall be represented in the storage of the computer as characters of a UNIFORM SIZE equal to or a multiple of the size of characters in the computer's alphanumeric character set" - one size, everywhere, and the implementor's specified size is 2. EXPECTED for the repro: BYTE-LENGTH(G) = 6 with N occupying bytes 1-4 as UTF-16 (00 41 00 42, the form DOC-A.1-33 names for the storage channel) and A at bytes 5-6, so G(5:2) reads "YZ". OWNERSHIP: no kb/Work note covers this. PB327 (open) owns the FILE channel only - the EXTERNAL FD record, the national key and the national space fill - and PB231 (open) the BASED/ALLOCATE refusal; both are REJECTS-LEGAL-SOURCE shapes, whereas this is the silent WRONG-ANSWER shape, and its exact twin PB188 (landed) is the same defect for a byte-form numeric leaf: "seeds a FOUR-character window over a TWO-byte item, silently shifting every following member of the group image". SECOND, SEPARATE GAP IN THIS ROW: the rule's closing sentence ("Each implementor shall specify the size and representation of characters stored for usage NATIONAL") is A.1 item 213, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md has NO DOC-A.1-213 row - the ledger runs 208, 209, 211, 215 and DOC-A.1-209 forward-references "row 213" for the 2-bytes-per-position figure it relies on. See finding usage-p3/F2. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth (`Usage.National => 2 * ElementaryImageWidth`) vs src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.IsCharacterImage / DataItem.ImageWidth (a national leaf contributes its CHARACTER positions - "never byte-doubled for national"); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/DataDivision/GroupImageCodec.cs; tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/ImageWidthIsStorageWidthTests.cs#NationalLeaf_IsExactlyTwoBytesPerPosition (the divergence asserted as sanctioned) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 2002,2014,2023 (USAGE NATIONAL and category national are post-1985: probe q65 gives COBOLNET0900 "national data (PICTURE symbol N / USAGE NATIONAL) requires COBOL-2002" at --std 85)

notes: RE-RECORDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB598) — the SUBJECT of each sentence, which this row had right for what SR4 forbids and wrong for what it admits. SR4 is three sentences: a category sentence, then 'Alphanumeric literals in the VALUE clause of an elementary item shall not exceed the size indicated by an explicit PICTURE clause' and 'Alphanumeric literals in the VALUE clause of an alphanumeric group item shall not exceed the size of the group item'. The 2026-09-04 landing (PB206) closed both size sentences, which had silently TRUNCATED, and this row was recorded CONFORMS on that evidence — but the screen it landed was reached by the three level-88 call sites in BindCondition carrying the CONDITIONAL VARIABLE's size, so it also applied the elementary-item sentence to a subject neither sentence names. `01 XV PIC X. 88 XC VALUE "cd".` became COBOLNET1740, legal source rejected, and GnuCOBOL differential case syn_misc:388 flipped from AGREE_ACCEPT to WE_REJECT_THEY_ACCEPT. A Format-3 entry is `88 condition-name-1 value-clause .` (13.16.2), which admits no PICTURE clause, so no EXPLICIT picture indicates a size; SR33 makes that level-88 entry the subject of the entry; 8.5.1.3.2 item 3 gives a condition-name entry 'no true concept of level', so it is neither of 8.5.1.3.1's record subdivisions; and 13.18.63.4 GR19 gives it its conditional variable's characteristics only IMPLICITLY, which is exactly what 'explicit' excludes. The three subjects the rule addresses are now a TYPE, ValueSubject, built only by ForElementary / ForGroup / ForConditionName, so a call site cannot compose a size the standard does not give it. The category sentence is unaffected and still binds a condition-name (SR4 is an ALL FORMATS rule). And the standard defines what an oversize condition-name literal MEANS, which a size rule would make dead text: 8.8.4.5.3 item 2 sends the comparison to the relation-condition rules, so it never compares equal; 14.9.39.4 GR6 -> 13.18.63.4 GR7 -> 14.6.8.5 places it 'with space fill or truncation to the right'. The 85 golden pb598_condition_name_value_size derives every one of those answers from the rules before measuring them; the pb206 negatives and ConditionNameValueSizeTests.TheSizeSentencesStillBindAnElementaryAndAGroupSubject are the drift proof that withholding the size from a condition-name did not withhold it from the two subjects the sentences do name (that test was measured RED against a deliberately over-withholding build). A FIGURATIVE operand remains exempt by rule (8.3.3.6.4 GR2). Error at every edition: Annex E.2 item 27's 2023 size change is scoped to numeric-edited items (COBOLNET1570).

notes: LANDED 2026-09-13 (kb/Work PB506). THREE DELEGATIONS: TWO NOW CONFORM, THE THIRD IS VACUOUS IN FORMAT 4. SR17 (VALUE and VALUES are equivalent) — CONFORMS, one grammar production accepts both spellings and the 2023 golden writes `VALUES ARE`. SR11 sentence 1 (editing characters ARE used for a numeric-edited item when the literal is numeric) — CONFORMS: `03 COLUMN 46 PIC ZZ9 VALUE 12.` prints ` 12`. SR11 sentence 2 (editing characters for an alphanumeric-edited or national-edited item do NOT cause editing of the initial value) — NOW CONFORMS, and this was the divergence: `03 COLUMN 26 PIC XXBXX VALUE "AB CD".` printed `AB  C`, the literal run through the alphanumeric EDIT, and now prints `AB CD` as written. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS A ROUTING, NOT A MISSING CHECK: ReportWriterEmitter.FieldImage turned a FieldValueSource into move.ConvertSource(source, PrintItem) — the SOURCE clause's implicit MOVE, 13.18.53.4 GR1, a real clause answering a different question — and a MOVE applies exactly the transforms a VALUE excludes. A format-4 VALUE operand now renders through ValueInitializer.InitializerFrom, the SAME 13.18.63 recipe the working-storage (format 1) lane uses, reached via DataEmitter.ValueImageOf; the 2023 golden prints the report item AND its identical WORKING-STORAGE twin on adjacent lines for each shape, so the two lanes cannot drift apart unseen. SR25 (no format 3/4/5 VALUE in or under a CONSTANT RECORD entry) is VACUOUS in format 4: CONSTANT RECORD is a data-description clause (13.18.15) and the report group description entry's clause list does not contain it, so the shape SR34 imports SR25 to forbid cannot be written in the report section at all; SR25's own row owns its format-3/5 legs. EDITIONS: MEASURED at 2002, 2014 and 2023 (the three goldens); FieldImage and InitializerFrom carry no version predicate and the 85 leg is reasoned from that, the repetition and COLUMNS/SOURCES spellings used to reach it being 2002-gated (COBOLNET0900). Annex E carries no 2023 change to SR34.

notes: LANDED 2026-09-13 (kb/Work PB506). BOTH SENTENCES ENFORCED, AND THE OPERAND LIST EXISTS TO ENFORCE THEM AGAINST. Sentence 1 (a multi-operand VALUE requires a repeating entry or an entry subordinate to one) and sentence 2 (the operand count shall equal the entry's repetitions, or that number multiplied by the repetitions of successive higher repeating entries) are screened by ONE reader, ScreenRepeatingOperandCount, which computes the admissible counts as the PREFIX PRODUCTS of the repetition chain RepetitionChain reads off the report-entry scope stack — the entry's own count per 13.15.4 GR3 (EntryRepetitions: a COLUMN clause with more than one operand, else 1) then each enclosing entry's. A non-repeating frame contributes a factor of 1, so sentence 1 is exactly 'the full product is 1' and needs no separate special case, and the rule generalizes without edit on the day the report-group OCCURS and multiple LINE vehicles land (both stage COBOLNET0899 today, and an entry that staged loud is skipped rather than double-diagnosed). Diagnostic COBOLNET2012. MEASURED: `03 COLUMN 1 PIC X(3) VALUE "AAA" "BBB" "CCC".` (a non-repeating entry) and `03 COLUMNS ARE 1 6 11 PIC X(3) VALUES ARE "AAA" "BBB".` (3 repetitions, 2 operands) each draw COBOLNET2012 at 85, 2002, 2014 AND 2023 — SR35 carries no version proviso and Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change, so at 85 the COBOLNET0900 introduction gate for the multiple COLUMN vehicle is reported ALONGSIDE it, not instead of it. The LEGAL three-operand form compiles and prints AAA/BBB/CCC (the 2023 golden). BEFORE: both illegal shapes compiled clean and printed the same `AAA  AAA  AAA` as the legal one, because DataBinder.ExtractValue collapsed the whole list to item.GetText() and FieldValueSource held ONE string — no count could be compared with a repetition count because no count existed. The SIBLING ARM, 13.18.53.3 SR6, is the same rule written for the SOURCE clause and now rides the same reader (COBOLNET2013).
