subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: an explicit scope terminator terminates 'the most-recently preceding unterminated statement having the statement-name for which that scope terminator is defined' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.2 -> OK §14.5.3.2 1)). Implementation is structural: every Table-12 statement rule ends in an optional END_x token (END_ADD?, END_IF?, END_READ?, ...) and ANTLR's greedy optional binds the terminator to the INNERMOST open statement of that name. Probes: nested ADD ... ON SIZE ERROR ADD ... END-ADD END-ADD binds innermost (sc1 T5 -> 'T5 B-SE','T5 IN-A-SE','T5 END'); an inner ADD already implicitly terminated by the outer's NOT ON SIZE ERROR phrase is skipped and END-ADD closes the outer (sc1 T1); nested inline PERFORMs (sc4 U3 -> 8); END-IF closes the innermost IF only (sc1 T7, sc4 U9); an END-ADD whose ADD was already implicitly terminated by ELSE is rejected COBOL0306 (sc5). The golden's S2/S4 pin END-IF-to-nearest-IF (IF instance only). Observation, not a verdict change: the grammar/lexer also accept END-SORT and END-MERGE as terminators of SORT/MERGE (Core/CobolIO.g4:846,921) and END-INVOKE for INVOKE (PB758) although Table 12 defines none; `SORT E ASCENDING END-SORT` compiles and runs at 2023 with no diagnostic (sc2). The reservation is documented (CONFORMANCE.md D-RW1, §4.2.10) but no §4.2.10 3) warning flags the extension - see finding F1. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]

subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: the explicit terminator also terminates 'any unterminated statements that appear between that statement-name and the explicit scope terminator' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.2 -> OK §14.5.3.2 2)). Mechanism: statementBlock : statement+ stops at any END_x token that cannot start a statement; each intervening rule's own END_y? is absent, so it closes implicitly and control returns up the rule stack to the rule owning END_x. Probes: IF ... ADD ON SIZE ERROR ... END-IF closes the ADD (sc1 T3 -> 'T3 SE','T3 AFTER-IF'); ADD ON SIZE ERROR IF ... END-ADD closes the IF (sc1 T4); PERFORM ... IF ... END-PERFORM (sc4 U1); EVALUATE WHEN IF ... END-EVALUATE (sc4 U2); SEARCH WHEN IF ... END-SEARCH (sc4 U7) - all as the rule requires, at 85 and 2023. (U1/U2/U7 place an undelimited conditional where a format writes imperative-statement; that acceptance is PB351's open under-reject, not this row.) subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: a single imperative statement not contained in another is terminated by 'a) any element that follows the exhaustion of the statement's syntax, or b) the next-encountered statement-name, or c) a separator period' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 1) a)). Mechanism: sentence : statement+ DOT, each statement rule consumes exactly its own syntax, so the next statement keyword (b), the DOT (c), or a following element such as ELSE (a) ends it. Probes: 'DISPLAY "T8 A" DISPLAY "T8 B" MOVE 1 TO A DISPLAY A.' -> three separate statements (sc1 T8); every sentence in sc1/sc4 ends at its period. Reserved statement names cannot be absorbed as operands (§8.9 reservation), so no adversarial operand/statement-name collision exists. No spec-derived test targets this rule specifically: test-needed. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]

subject: Scope of statements

MOVE 6 TO N.' -> ELSE ends the THEN-arm MOVE (sc4 U8 -> 'U8 ELSE','U8 6'); (b) the DISPLAY inside ON SIZE ERROR ends when END-IF ends the containing IF (sc1 T3) and when the period ends the containing ADD (sc4 U5 -> both DISPLAYs inside the phrase); (a) statement-name boundaries inside phrases (sc4 U5 'DISPLAY "U5 SE" DISPLAY "U5 SE2"'). subject: Scope of statements
notes: Rule: a contained conditional statement is terminated by the termination or next phrase of a containing statement; 'Any phrase encountered is the next phrase of the most-recently preceding unterminated statement with which that phrase may be syntactically associated. If all permitted occurrences of a phrase have already been specified for a given statement, a subsequent occurrence of that phrase is not syntactically associated with that statement' (cite.py --check 14.5.3.3 -> OK §14.5.3.3 4)). Mechanism: each conditional-phrase group allows each phrase at most once (e.g. arithmeticOnSizeError, readAtEnd, ifStatement's single ELSE), and ANTLR's greedy optional attaches a phrase to the innermost open rule that can still take it, returning outward otherwise - the rule's association order. Probes: nested IFs, second ELSE goes to the outer IF (sc1 T6 'T6 OUTER-ELSE', T6B 'T6B INNER-ELSE'); END-IF-terminated inner IF lets ELSE go outer (sc1 T7); ADD conditional inside IF ended by ELSE (sc1 T9); SEARCH inside IF ended by ELSE, both WHENs to SEARCH (sc4 U6 'U6 FOUND'); exhausted inner NOT ON SIZE ERROR passes the second NOT to the outer ADD (sc1 T1/T2). The golden's S1/S3 pin association and the 'already matched with an ELSE' exhaustion for IF. Reach note: §14.5.1 makes a conditional statement imperative only when delimited, and every Table-12 conditional phrase and EVALUATE/PERFORM body is written imperative-statement-n, so in a CONFORMING program the only containing statement a conditional can sit in unterminated is IF (§14.9.19.2 statement-1/-2), whose only later phrase is ELSE. The grammar over-admits phrase repetition/merging elsewhere (SEARCH ALL WHEN+ - PB446; READ Format 1 AT END with Format 2 INVALID KEY on one statement; WRITE EOP with INVALID KEY; CALL 'NOT ON OVERFLOW'), which could steal a phrase from an outer statement - but only in programs already non-conforming under PB351 (undelimited conditional in an imperative position). Those rows are owned by PB351/PB446; no separate scope defect. probe dir out/probe/scope-of-statements (sc1/sc4/sc5, pinned cobol.exe; sc1 identical output at --std 85/2002/2014/2023, sc4 at 85 and 2023) || REFUTED: CONFORMS with test-ref EMPTY (test-needed) — Implementation conforms: adjudicator sc1 T6 (IF IF ELSE ELSE, second ELSE to outer), refuter R2 (ELSE terminates a contained undelimited EVALUATE, both truth values), R3 (ELSE terminates contained READ AT END/NOT AT END), R8, E5 (third ELSE with both IFs exhausted rejected COBOL0307). But the golden does not pin the rule load-bearing branches: branch b) "next phrase of any containing statement" terminating a contained CONDITIONAL, and the exhaustion sentence, are never reached - in S2/S3/S4 every inner IF is END-IF terminated before the ELSE (so S3 is decided by the END-IF, not by the already-matched-ELSE exhaustion the adjudicator credits it with), and in S1 the inner IF is ended by the period. Only the association sentence (S1 dangling ELSE) is pinned. A deciding test: IF T IF F DISPLAY 1 ELSE DISPLAY 2 ELSE DISPLAY 3. with no END-IF (expect 2), plus IF F IF .. ELSE .. ELSE DISPLAY 3. (expect 3). [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (explicit/implicit scope termination is COBOL-85 surface; Annex E records no change to 14.5.3)]

subject: Initial and last-used states of data
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152). Action 1 is the consumer point 11.9.10.4 GR2/GR3/GR4 route to, and its ORDER against action 2 is structural: the fill is a BACKGROUND laid down first and then OVERWRITTEN by VALUE clauses, never a per-item substitute for a missing VALUE. pb152_options_initialize_background pins the ordering with an item that HAS a VALUE beside one that does not. No sequencing code was added - a field initializer is one expression, and only the expression's no-VALUE case changed - so the re-application sites (RecordStructEmitter's field initializers and __ResetStatics, the LOCAL-STORAGE per-activation re-seed, the OO instance cell) inherit it by construction. DETERMINATION recorded in CONFORMANCE.md and COBOLNET_DATA_MODEL_DESIGN D23: 'the storage ... is set to the specified-fill-character' over a typed-native model means CHARACTER-FORMED storage takes the fill, while a NATIVE-NUMERIC carrier and an INDEX cell take their zero - licensed by 13.18.63.4 GR4 c), whose own sentence leaves a VALUE-less item 'undefined and set to a value that may or may not be allowed for that data item or index'. Class object/message-tag/pointer take NULL instead, because that same sentence states it as a positive requirement; USAGE BIT keeps its packed ceil(n/8) zero seed (D19) because its storage is packed bytes rather than character positions.

notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.6.2.3.2 OK, case 2): static data is placed in initial state 'The first time the program in which it is described is activated after the execution of an activating statement referencing a program that possesses the initial attribute and directly or indirectly contains the program.' subject: Alignment and transfer of data into data items
notes: kb/Work PB77 (2026-08-18): a fixed-point numeric receiver takes the sending value aligned by decimal point 'with zero fill or truncation on either end' — for EVERY sending magnitude, including one past the Int128 carrier. Every carrier's landing now has two forms chosen by the LANDING: the CHECKED landing (ON SIZE ERROR / EC-SIZE) saturates so the capacity check raises (PB13); the UNCHECKED landing (MOVE, the no-phrase store, INVOKE BY CONTENT) keeps the low-order digits — the native exact family through CobolNum.RescaleStoreCap (Rescaled's unchecked arm), the float family through the exact binary64 expansion (CobolFloat.LowOrderDigits) — where before both saturated and the MOVE stored the sentinel's low digits (MOVE FUNCTION NUMVAL-F("5E+30") TO PIC V9(9) stored 884105727 for 000000000). The SDIDI carrier had the two forms since PB74. In-carrier MOVEs are unchanged.

notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1110 (open). Rule: 'If the receiving data item is described with a FLOAT-SHORT, FLOAT-LONG, or FLOAT-EXTENDED usage, the implementor specifies any exception conditions that might be set to exist during data conversion. If no fatal exception conditions have been set to exist during data conversion, the content of the receiving operand is set to the algebraic value of the sending operand.' cite.py --check 14.6.8.3 -> OK §14.6.8.3 1). HALF 1 (implementor-specified EC) VERIFIED: docs/CONFORMANCE.md (the 'EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE / EC-DATA-OVERFLOW applied to EVERY floating-point usage' determination) specifies EC-DATA-OVERFLOW (fatal) and EC-DATA-NOT-FINITE for every float usage including this trio; MoveEmitter routes FLOAT-SHORT through StoreSingleChecked / StoreChecked(CobolDec) which raise it; pinned by conformance:2023/ec_data_overflow and conformance:2023/pb271_float_receiver_overflow. Probe p3.cob: MOVE PIC 9V9(16) 1.0000000596046448 TO FLOAT-SHORT stores 1.0 where the value lies ABOVE the binary32 midpoint 1+2^-24 = 1.000000059604644775390625, so the nearest binary32 is 1+2^-23 = 1.00000011920928955078125 (COMP-1 identical, p4.cob). PARTIAL: the EC half and the binary64 arms verified; the binary32 value arm fails the nearest-value reading. subject: Alignment and transfer of data into data items
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1110 (open). Rule: 'If the receiving data item is described with a standard floating-point usage, the algebraic value is converted and transferred to the receiving data item in a manner consistent with the specifications of ISO/IEC 60559:2020, Clauses 3 and 5.' cite.py --check 14.6.8.3 -> OK §14.6.8.3 2). ISO/IEC 60559 Clause 5 conversions are correctly rounded per the rounding-direction attribute (default roundTiesToEven) - ONE rounding of the exact value. FLOAT-BINARY-64: correct - probe out/probe/alignment/p3.cob MOVE 9007199254740993 -> 9007199254740992 (tie to even), MOVE PIC 9(16)V9(10) 9007199254740993.0000000001 and the same literal -> 9007199254740994 (ScaledToDouble is correctly rounded). FLOAT-BINARY-32: WRONG - MoveEmitter's float arm renders a fixed/Dec sender through NumericRenderer.Real (ScaledToDouble / CobolDec.ToDouble, a correctly-rounded binary64) and then CobolFloat.StoreSingleChecked / StoreChecked(CobolDec, single:true) casts that double to float: two roundings. Probe p3.cob/p4.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023 and 2014): MOVE 1.0000000596046448 TO FLOAT-BINARY-32 (fixed literal), MOVE 1.0000000596046448E0 (float literal, Dec lane), MOVE of a PIC 9V9(16) item holding it, MOVE 1.00000005960464478, and COMPUTE B32 = SRC ALL store 1.0 (displayed via MOVE to PIC 9V9(23) as 100000000000000000000000); expected, derived from 60559 roundTiesToEven: the value exceeds the midpoint 1.000000059604644775390625 between binary32 neighbours 1 and 1+2^-23, so the result is 1.00000011920928955078125 -> 100000011920928955078125. Contrast in the same program: VALUE 1.0000000596046448E0 on a FLOAT-BINARY-32 seeds the CORRECT 1.00000011920928955078125, so the VALUE landing and the MOVE/COMPUTE landings of one literal disagree. Single-rounding cases pass (0.1 -> 0.100000001490116119384765625; 16777217 -> 16777216; 16777219 -> 16777220), which is why nothing caught it. FLOAT-BINARY-128 / FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/-34 are refused COBOLNET1564 (CONFORMANCE.md §2 rows 17/19 Not claimed, Annex A.3) - not adjudicated here. No existing kb/Work note owns this (searched kb/Work for double rounding / binary32; PB961 is the NaN-payload widening, PB271 the overflow EC). subject: Alignment and transfer of data into data items
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB66 / D21). The store normalizes EXACTLY in integer arithmetic: the value a×10^e is rescaled so the significand's leading digit position is nonzero (S = a×10^k / a÷10^-k, E = digits + e + scale − sigDigits) — -12345.678 into -9.9(5)E+99 → -1.23456E+04, 0.00012345 into 9.99E+9 → 1.23E-4, 1234 into 9(3)E+99 → 123E+01, 6.02214076E+23 (a binary64 sender) into -9.9(5)E+99 → 6.02214E+23; a zero value takes §13.18.40.5 r8's zero image (no normalization).

subject: Alignment and transfer of data into data items
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB66 / D21). After normalization the significand aligns at the mask's point, truncates to the mask's digit count (-12345.678 into +9(3).9(2)E+999 → -123.45E+002 — six digits truncated to five) and zero-fills (1.5E+3 into +9.9(3)E+99 → +1.500E+03); the significand's simple / special / fixed insertion symbols (B 0 / , . +/-) render per §13.18.40.5 Table 7 and the exponent takes none; DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA exchanges the point and the grouping character in the image (-1,23456E+04; 1.234E+00 for 9.999E+99 in comma mode).

notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.6.9.2 "superfluous elements are not moved and no exception exists" -> OK §14.6.9.2 1)): when the receiving table is NOT dynamic-capacity and the sender's current capacity is higher, superfluous elements are not moved, no exception. §14.6.9.1 (checked OK) makes an ODO receiver a table of capacity = DEPENDING value. Code: GR9 MOVE (MoveEmitter.VariableLengthGroupMove) routes a fixed receiving group through VarCarrierWrite -> RuntimeApi.VarGroupToFixedImage -> CobolVarGroup.ToFixedImage, which CobolString.Store-fits each carried component to its span width (truncation = superfluous elements dropped). Probe out/probe/dyncap/p1.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023 and 2014 identical): dyn sender capacity 4 -> OCCURS 2 fixed receiver gives A=[HH][AAA][BBB] (elements 3,4 not moved, no exception); dyn sender capacity 3 -> ODO receiver with N=2, then N raised to 4, gives C=[AAA][BBB][OL3][OL4] (element 3 beyond the DEPENDING count untouched). No spec-derived MOVE golden exercises the superfluous arm (conformance:2014/pb393_move_varlen_table covers only the shorter-sender arm; BoundaryGroupCorrespondenceTests exercise the CALL boundary, not MOVE) -> test-ref empty. The element-wise MOVE-rule defect (finding 2, filed under GR-14.6.9.2-2) also runs through this path but is the other sentence's obligation. || editions as adjudicated: 2014, 2023 (dynamic-capacity tables / variable-length groups arrive with ISO/IEC 1989:2014; 2023 Annex E lists no change to 14.6.9)

subject: Operations on dynamic-capacity tables
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1144 (open). Three sentences (cite.py --check 14.6.9.2 each OK): (a) "all the remaining elements of the receiving table are space filled" (non-dynamic receiver, shorter sender); (b) "further elements are created and filled with spaces until the current capacity of the table is equal to its minimum capacity" (dynamic receiver whose FROM minimum exceeds the copied capacity); (c) "Correspondingly numbered elements are moved according to the rules of the MOVE statement". (a) CONFORMS: ToFixedImage space-pads the component; probe p1 D=[AAA][   ][   ][OL4] for an ODO receiver N=3, and conformance:2014/pb393_move_varlen_table F= for a fixed OCCURS 3. (b) DIVERGES: CobolDynTable.FromCurrentImage calls SetCapacity(parts.Length), whose shrink arm clamps to _min WITHOUT re-seeding or space-filling, and the store loop writes only i < parts.Length, so the elements between the copied capacity and the minimum keep the receiver's OLD content. Probe p1: receiver MT FROM 3 holding OL1/OL2/OL3, sender capacity 1 AAA: expected (spec) CM=3 [AAA][   ][   ]; observed B=  3[AAA][OL2][OL3] (2014 and 2023). (c) DIVERGES: the carrier moves each element as a character image, not by elementary MOVE rules; §8.5.1.12.3 compatibility as implemented (VariableLengthCompatibility: equal element byte length) admits PIC 9(4) -> PIC 99V99 elements, and probe p2: ST(1)=1234 -> RT(1) shows [1234] (12.34) where MOVE 1234 TO a 99V99 item yields 34.00 (displayed 3400); same for a fixed OCCURS receiver (F=[1234]). Either the element pair is compatible and the MOVE rules apply, or it is not and SR9 must reject: the byte copy is wrong under both readings. No register note owns either (PB393/PB965 landed; neither covers the minimum-capacity arm nor element MOVE rules).

notes: Rule: 'When the data items are described by the same data description entry, the result of the statement is the same as if the data items shared no part of their respective storage areas.' (cite.py --check 14.6.10 -> OK, rule 2). Items described by the SAME entry can only share storage by being the same occurrence (full overlap), so the obligation is that a statement reads its sending value before it stores. Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d1\out\probe\ovl\ovl.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023) - every result equals the no-overlap result: ADD A TO A (7) -> 0014; MULTIPLY B BY B (3) -> 9; COMPUTE C = C*2 + C/5 (5) -> 11.00; MOVE E(I) TO E(J), I=J=2 -> XYZ042 unchanged; MOVE G TO G -> ABCD1234; SUBTRACT N FROM N GIVING N -> 0; DIVIDE N INTO N -> 1; ADD N N N TO N (10) -> 40; ADD 1 TO N GIVING N N -> 11. Arithmetic is also covered by §14.7.7 rule 4 a)/NOTE 3 (the intermediate is complete before any store; cite.py --check 14.7.7 -> OK). The reference-modification sentence ('not considered to be the same data description entry ... undefined') imposes no result. No existing spec-derived test names this rule.

notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB603 (open). Rule: 'An implicit CLOSE statement without any phrases is executed for each file that is in the open mode. These implicit close statements shall be executed for all open files in the run unit, even when an error occurs during the execution of one or more of the CLOSE statements. Any exception processing procedures associated with these files are not executed.' (cite.py --check 14.6.11 -> OK, rule 2). Three halves: (1) every open file in the RUN UNIT - RunMain's finally calls _owner.Files.CloseAll() on normal, STOP RUN and abnormal exits (§14.6.12 path too), over the run-unit registry incl. instance-file connectors (DrainPendingObjectCloses) and files opened by a separately compiled module; pinned by RunUnitTerminationTests.ImplicitClose_ReachesFileOpenedBySeparatelyCompiledSub and AbnormalTermination_StillClosesOpenFiles (spec-derived: on-disk content is the observable). (2) 'even when an error occurs': FileConnector.Close maps IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException to status '30' and returns, so one failing close does not stop the loop - verified by reading, no test. (3) 'exception processing procedures ... are not executed': CloseAll calls the connector's Close directly, never the emitted CLOSE statement path that selects USE declaratives - verified by reading, no test. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The half that says the implicit CLOSEs 'shall be executed for all open files in the run unit, even when an error occurs during the execution of one or more of the CLOSE statements' is broken. FileConnector.Close contains only IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException. Any other close-time failure escapes FileRegistry.CloseAll's loop, which has no per-file guard, so every connector after it is never closed, its buffered data is lost, and the process dies with an unhandled .NET exception. I reached this with a user-level program: an indexed file with CODE-SET IS EBCDIC defers its CODE-SET conversion to the persist in IndexedConnector.CloseCore, and a record holding U+20AC makes CodeSetConversion.ToMedium throw InvalidOperationException. The implicit close of every open file and the not-running of the exception procedures do hold. The adjudicator verified the 'error' half only by reading, which missed the narrow catch. Separate lead: WRITE IX returned '00' for a record its CODE-SET cannot represent, because the conversion is deferred to CLOSE (§13.18.13.4 GR1/GR6 b).

notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1069 (open). Rule: 'Any storage obtained with an ALLOCATE statement and not yet released by a FREE statement is released.' (cite.py --check 14.6.11 -> OK, rule 3). ALLOCATE yields a managed StorageCell (CobolPtr.Allocate) with no process-static registry, so storage becomes unreachable when the run unit's program registry is dropped (ProgramTable.Reset via RunUnit.ResetCurrent; staticReset re-seeds RECURSIVE static WS at run-unit start) and is released at process exit on the CLI path. Unverified/defective edge: In a host that runs several run units in ONE process (RunUnit.Run / the conformance test host), the FACTORY object of every class is a process-lifetime singleton - OoEmitter emits `public static readonly <Factory> __Instance = new();` (src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/OoEmitter.cs, the FACTORY-class extras) - which RunUnit.ResetCurrent / ProgramTable.Reset cannot reach, so any instance object, ALLOCATEd cell or dynamic table/string referenced from factory data survives the run unit's termination and is visible to the next run unit. Same mechanism class as kb/Work PB1069 (open: run-unit state not scoped to the run unit), which names Switches/ReportFlow/Locale/Scratch but not the factory singletons. Decided by reading, not probed (the CLI runs one run unit per process, where process exit releases everything). || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (ALLOCATE/FREE)

subject: Exception conditions
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1122 (open). Rule: §14.6.13.1.2 1) (cite.py --check 14.6.13.1.2 "An EXIT PROGRAM, GOBACK, RESUME, or STOP statement that is specified in this function, method, or program is executed" -> OK 1)). A declarative completes normally only if none of EXIT PROGRAM/GOBACK/RESUME/STOP is executed and no fatal exception occurs in its scope. Code: the EC-model __RunUse (DispatchEmitter.EmitRunUseBody) returns -1 ONLY when the bounded __Dispatch falls off its end; RESUME unwinds as ResumeSignal and is converted to the resume action (-2 / pc), and GOBACK/EXIT PROGRAM/STOP RUN/CobolFatalException unwind through the finally (guard reset + checking restore) without producing -1, so every caller's 'completed normally' arm (EmitArgOrPlain '__r != -2 -> throw', EmitRaise, __IoCheckEc) is never reached for a non-normal completion. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/exc-normal): n1 fatal EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT in a CALLed program whose USE AFTER EC declarative executes GOBACK -> 'B-DECL / A-AFTER', exit 0 (no abnormal termination: GOBACK made it not-normal, so 14.6.13.1.3 #5's terminate-after-normal-completion does not fire); n2 same with STOP RUN -> 'B-DECL', exit 0 (normal STOP, not abnormal); n3 control (declarative falls off) -> abnormal termination exit 1; n4 nonfatal EC-USER-X declarative that itself raises a checked fatal EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT -> 'DECL-START' then abnormal termination, exit 1, DECL-END/AFTER-RAISE never shown; n6 EXIT PROGRAM in a nonfatal declarative of a called program -> 'DECL / A-AFTER', statement after RAISE not executed. RESUME half pinned by the golden (DECL-RAN / AFTER-SORT). All halves verified. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Only the statement half holds. Normal completion is decided solely by whether __Dispatch falls off its end (DispatchEmitter.EmitRunUseBody returns -1). Nothing records that a fatal exception occurred within the scope of the declarative. A fatal exception that is handled inside the declarative's scope (a second declarative that RESUMEs AT NEXT STATEMENT) therefore lets the first declarative be treated as completing normally, which contradicts the second half of 14.6.13.1.2 1). || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §14.6.13 exception-condition model and its USE-completion definition arrive with ISO 2002; COBOL-85 has no RESUME/GOBACK/EC model)

notes: kb/Work PB75 (2026-08-18) + the EC waves: with checking enabled and no WHEN / USE / PROPAGATE that resumes, execution of the run unit is terminated abnormally (§14.6.12): the guard rethrows the (dispatched) fatal to ProgramTable.RunMain, which writes 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-… (fatal): …' to stderr and exits 1 — the size-error family included, which used to escape as a raw CLR crash.

subject: Exception conditions
notes: kb/Work PB77 + PB75 (2026-08-18): with checking for a fatal exception condition NOT enabled 'the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and how any receiving operands are affected'. COBOL.NET's determination for the arithmetic size error condition without a SIZE ERROR phrase (EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, §14.7.5 no-phrase rule 4; A.1 item 70): execution continues and the resultant identifier receives the LOW-ORDER digits of the result aligned at its scale (CobolNum.Store's high-order truncation), for EVERY value carrier — SDIDI (CobolDec.ToUnscaled, PB74), the native exact family (Rescaled's unchecked arm), a binary64 (ToScaledUnchecked / FromDouble's unchecked form — the exact decimal expansion past the Int128 carrier). A non-finite binary64 landing in a fixed-point receiver stores ZERO. An INTERMEDIATE that cannot be formed at all (a standard-decimal intermediate past decimal128, a native value past the Int128 escape boundary in a value-semantics position, an exponentiation-rule violation, a zero divisor) has no result: execution does NOT continue — the run unit terminates abnormally, exit 1, naming the condition (PB75; it used to be a raw CLR crash, exit 127). Documented on CONFORMANCE.md (the item-70 row).

subject: Common phrases and features for statements
notes: || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

subject: Common phrases and features for statements
notes: kb/Work/PB401.md - rule 1, 'When the range of values is defined by numeric literals, the range of values includes literal-1, literal-2, and all algebraic values between literal-1 and literal-2'. A numeric range lowers to the inclusive ALGEBRAIC pair `subject >= lo && subject <= hi` over the numeric channel, names no collating sequence, and sets NO exception condition in either direction - which is what makes rule 1 observably different from rule 2 and is measured as such: PBR10 (inverted numeric identifier ends: empty, no EC), PBR11 (arithmetic-expression ends 1+1 THRU 8+2 containing 5 algebraically), PBR12/PBR13 (literal ends both directions), and the golden's NUMINV/ARITH arms. The rule-1/rule-2 split is written down ONCE, as CollatingSelection.IsCollatedThroughRange over the range's class, so a site cannot implement one rule and leave the other to a second author; before it, an arithmetic-expression-ended range was classified ALPHANUMERIC (its operand answered 'no category') and took rule 2's collating treatment.

subject: Common phrases and features for statements
notes: kb/Work/PB401.md - rule 2, all four of its sentences, for BOTH clauses 14.7.8's opening sentence governs ('This specification applies to THROUGH phrases specified in the VALUE clause and the EVALUATE statement'). (1) No IN phrase: the sequence is the implementor's, and this implementation's is the PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, reached through the ONE comparison-class rule over both ends. (2) IN alphabet-name-1: TryResolveRangeAlphabet is the single resolver both clauses take, it registers the named sequence as a runtime carrier and it DISPLACES the program sequence - measured both directions against a reversed alphabet on the EVALUATE range (probe pM) and on the level-88 VALUE range (probe pN). (3) The inclusive ascending membership, and (4) the EC-RANGE-INVALID raise on an inverted range followed by 'execution proceeds as if the range of values were empty' - now keyed on the range's CLASS rather than on its operands' written form, so an identifier-, function-result-, group- or national-ended range raises exactly as a literal pair does. A figurative end is materialized to the tested item's own width first (8.3.3.6.4 GR2, CobolString.ThruMember's loFig/hiFig overload); a signed numeric operand drops its operational sign as 8.8.4.2.5 -> 14.9.25.4 GR6a require of the alphanumeric comparison this rule orders. || RESIDUAL, recorded elsewhere: `identifier-4 IN alphabet-name-1` is parsed as 8.4.2.2 qualification and rejected COBOLNET1639, so the phrase is reachable only when the range's ending operand is a literal - a general-format defect owned by FMT-14.9.13.2 (DIVERGES).

subject: RETRY phrase
notes: kb/Work PB1163 (registrar 14c). cite.py --check 14.7.9.3 "If the FOREVER phrase is specified, the mass storage control system shall attempt to gain access to a locked resource until the input-output operation has been completed" -> OK 3). RetryLoop's Forever arm makes exactly ONE re-attempt and then lands the conflict's own status (or '52' for a record lock). That is defended only for a holder inside the executing run unit (DOC-A.1-109; D8). But since PB860 the file-sharing conflict on OPEN (FileConnector.Open IsSharingRefusal -> '61') and DELETE FILE (HostFile.IsHeldByAnother -> '62') is also raised by a holder in ANOTHER run unit — which CAN release, as FileRegistry.DeleteFile's own comment says ('another run unit CAN close mid-loop'). Probe (out/probe/retry-phrase/forever.cob, openforever.cob; pwsh holds held.dat FileShare.None and releases after 4 s): `DELETE FILE F RETRY FOREVER` -> '62' after 72 ms, file NOT deleted; `OPEN INPUT RETRY FOREVER F` (SHARING WITH NO OTHER) -> '61' after 72 ms. Spec-derived expected: the statement keeps attempting until the holder releases, then completes successfully — '00' (file deleted / opened) after ~4 s. The in-run-unit record case ('52' deadlock) is a documented A.1-109 determination and not contested here. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the RETRY phrase is a COBOL-2002 facility; 2023 Annex E lists no change to 14.7.9)]

subject: Parameters
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1112 (open). RULE (cite.py --check 14.8.2.2 OK, rule 1): under the lead-in 'If either the formal parameter or the argument is an alphanumeric group item and neither of them is strongly typed', 'If the argument is passed by reference, that argument or the formal parameter corresponding to that argument shall be an alphanumeric group item or an elementary item of category alphanumeric, and the formal parameter shall be described with the same number or a smaller number of bytes as the corresponding argument.' TWO HALVES: (a) the category of the other side; (b) formal bytes <= argument bytes. 14.9.4.3 SR25 (--check OK) 'The rules for conformance specified in 14.8.2, Parameters and 14.8.3, Returning items apply' makes both a compile-time syntax rule for Format-2 CALL; 14.8.2.1 NOTE (--check OK) 'A bit group or national group is treated as an elementary item'; 8.5.2.2 / 8.5.2.4 (--check OK) make alphabetic and alphanumeric-edited categories DISTINCT from alphanumeric. CODE: CallBinder's BY REFERENCE arm and OoBinder's INVOKE arm both call OoConformance.DescriptionMismatch(formal, arg, byRefGroupPrefix: true). Its group arm tests `arg.IsGroup || arg.Pic?.Category is PicCategory.Alphanumeric`, and its group-argument arm tests `f.Category is PicCategory.Alphanumeric`; the size half compares ImageWidth (formal <= argument). StrongTypeMismatch runs first (the lead-in's strong-type exclusion and the separate same-type sentence). PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023, CALL "S" AS NESTED USING BY REFERENCE ARG; out/probe/parameters/*.cob via gen.py): CONFORMING HALVES OK: pa formal group 4 vs arg group 10 accepted, callee sees F=ABCD, write-back ARG=WXYZEFGHIJ (prefix + tail preserved); pb formal group 10 vs arg group 4 -> COBOLNET1688 'the formal (10 ...) exceeds the argument (4)'; pc group formal 5 vs arg PIC X(10) F=ABCDE ARG=VWXYZFGHIJ; pd group formal vs PIC 9(10) -> 1688; ph PIC X(5) formal vs group 10 accepted, ARG=12345FGHIJ; pi PIC X(12) vs group 10 -> 1688; pj PIC 9(4) vs group -> 1688; pm/pn/po/pp COMP-5 leaves counted at 4 storage bytes, 4<=4 accepted, 4>3 and 5>4 rejected. DEFECT HALF (a) CATEGORY, UNDER-REJECTS: pe arg PIC A(10) into alnum group formal -> accepted, runs F=ABCDE (expected 1688: alphabetic is not category alphanumeric); pf arg PIC X(3)BX(3) (alphanumeric-edited) -> accepted F=ABC D (expected 1688); pk/pl formal PIC X(3)BX(3) / PIC A(5) against a group argument -> accepted (expected 1688); pg arg GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL group into alnum group formal -> accepted, callee reads the UTF-16 bytes ' A B'; pg2 alnum group into GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL formal -> accepted, callee reads U+4142 U+4344 garbage (expected 1688 both: a national group is treated as an elementary national item, 14.8.2.1 NOTE). Cause: PicCategory.Alphanumeric also carries alphabetic (PicInfo.cs: 'Alphanumeric (X) or alphabetic (A)') and alphanumeric-edited ({Category: Alphanumeric, EditMask: not null}); DataItem.IsGroup is true for a GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL/BIT group. DEFECT HALF (b) BYTES: the size compare uses ImageWidth, which counts a national leaf at ONE unit per position while D-N1 (CONFORMANCE.md, 13.18.60.4 GR8 implementor choice) fixes 2 bytes: ps arg `01 ARG. 05 N1 PIC N(4)` (8 bytes, an alphanumeric group) into formal `05 F1 PIC X(8)` (8 bytes) -> REJECTED 1688 'the formal (8 ...) exceeds the argument (4)' (legal source refused); pt same with X(5) -> rejected (legal); pr/pu formal `05 F1 PIC N(2)` (4 bytes) vs arg X(3) (3 bytes) -> ACCEPTED (expected 1688), and the callee's store corrupts the caller (ARG=[ XC]). This is kb/Work PB546's (open) two-widths mechanism reaching the 14.8.2.2 size compare; PB546 claims GR-13.18.60.4-8 only, so this row is a further consumer to extend it with. RUN-TIME LANE (Format 1, no AS NESTED): pq formal group 10 vs arg group 4 runs silently: the callee reads 'ABCD      ' (space-padded) and its store splices back 4 characters (ARG=QQQQ). 14.9.4.4 GR3 d) (--check OK) raises EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH only 'If a violation of these rules is detected', so undetected adaptation is within the text; noted, not filed. Not re-reported: PB204/PB818/PB965 (variable-length-group arms, landed), PB427 (strong-type sentence, landed), PB480 (OO universal descriptor, open, different crossing). Verdict DIVERGES: the size half rejects legal source (ps/pt) and both halves under-reject. [code-location note: (the BY REFERENCE arm, byRefGroupPrefix: true, ~line 618); code-location note: (INVOKE BY REFERENCE, ~line 790)] || editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E records no change to 14.8.2.2; the compile-time lane is 14.9.4.3 SR25, Format-2 CALL and INVOKE, where those formats exist; a Format-1 CALL is the 14.9.4.4 GR3 d) run-time lane)

(cite.py --check 14.8.2.3.2 -> OK §14.8.2.3.2 1)). Code: BY REFERENCE arguments (INVOKE: OoBindInvocationArg byReference arm; CALL AS NESTED/prototype: CallBinder's Reference arm) go through OoConformance.DescriptionMismatch, whose ObjectReference arm requires ObjectRefDescriptor.SameDescriptionAs (Kind, Name, Factory, Only all equal) — Kind equality makes universal<->universal the only pairing. Rule: "If either the argument or the formal parameter is described with an interface-name, the corresponding formal parameter or argument shall be described with the same interface-name." Code: SameDescriptionAs requires Kind==Interface on both sides and case-insensitive name equality (§8.3.2.2). Probe r2a: I1 arg -> I1 formal BY REFERENCE accepted and runs (IN-M); kind mismatch refused by the same comparator (r1a/r1b show the Kind compare). conformance:negative/oo-interface-arg-mismatch does NOT cover this rule (it pins a PIC 9(6)/9(4) digit mismatch through an interface receiver), so test-ref empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Same defect in the function arm. A class-typed argument into an interface-named formal of a user-defined function is not diagnosed at compile time, even though §8.4.3.2.3 SR13 applies. subject: Elementary items
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1115 (open). Rule: same object-class-name, "and the FACTORY and ONLY phrases shall be the same". SameDescriptionAs compares Kind, Name, Factory and Only. Probes: r3a (subclass C2 arg -> C1 formal BY REF) refused 0828; r3b (C1 ONLY -> C1) refused; r3c (FACTORY OF C1 -> C1) refused; r3d (C1 -> C1) accepted and runs; r3e (C2 -> C1 BY CONTENT) accepted — correct, BY CONTENT is §14.8.2.3.3's SET regime, not this rule. Caveat, recorded under GR-14.8.2.3.2-4: rule 3 read literally forbids an object-class-name argument at an ACTIVE-CLASS formal, which rule 4 b) expressly permits; the comparator applies rule 3 without rule 4 b)'s exception — that defect is filed against rule 4, not here. No spec-derived parameter-rule test (pb389 negatives are SET format 5) -> test-ref empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — This is a silent acceptance of non-conforming source. A user-defined function argument described 'OBJECT REFERENCE C1 ONLY', passed BY REFERENCE into a formal described 'OBJECT REFERENCE C1', compiles and runs with no diagnostic and no exception. Rule 3 requires the ONLY phrase to be the same on both sides, and §8.4.3.2.3 SR13 makes that a syntax rule for function activation. The INVOKE arm (r3a-r3d) is correct, but the function arm never calls the comparator, and the runtime carrier check cannot see ONLY because both sides share a carrier.

The row also carries the class-pointer paragraph (same category; both restricted and of the same type) and the class object-reference sentence. Code: DescriptionMismatch's ObjectReference arm is plain SameDescriptionAs identity; no arm consults the INVOKE receiver. DEFECT 1 (rejects-legal-source, 4 b)): probe ac_ref_legal (pre-edit form) — `01 X USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE C1 ONLY` + `INVOKE X "M" USING BY REFERENCE X` where M's formal is `USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE ACTIVE-CLASS` -> COBOLNET0828 'object-reference description mismatch (formal ... ACTIVE-CLASS (containing class C1), argument ... C1 ONLY)'. Expected: accepted (4 b) is met — C1 ONLY argument, no FACTORY on either side, invoked with a reference described C1 ONLY). subject: Elementary items
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1112 (open). Rule: BY CONTENT/VALUE to an ACTIVE-CLASS formal — alternative 1) "The method to be activated shall be invoked with the predefined object references SELF or SUPER, or with an object reference described with the ACTIVE-CLASS phrase, and a SET statement shall be valid ...". Code: ContentMismatch's ObjectReference arm asks ObjectRefAssignmentMismatch (SET format 5, SR14 for an ACTIVE-CLASS receiver: ACTIVE-CLASS sender with equal FACTORY presence) — the SET half is right, but the INVOKE receiver (the invocation-target half) is never consulted. Probe ac_con_bad4a: in C1 method N, `INVOKE O2 "M" USING BY CONTENT Y` (O2 `USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE C1`, Y ACTIVE-CLASS) compiles and prints IN-M. Expected: rejected — O2 is not SELF/SUPER/ACTIVE-CLASS, so alternative 1) fails, and alternative 2) fails because Y is not SET-valid into a C1 ONLY receiver (§14.9.39.3 SR12 b)1.). Legal form ac_con_legal (INVOKE SELF) runs. Two halves, one verified -> the rule diverges (under-rejects).

subject: Elementary items
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1112 (open). Rule (cite.py --check 14.8.2.3.3 -> OK §14.8.2.3.3 2)): alternative 2) for an ACTIVE-CLASS formal — invoked with an object-class-name or a reference described with that class and ONLY, and a SET valid from the argument into a reference described with that object-class-name and ONLY. The row also carries: "If the formal parameter is of class pointer or an object reference described without the ACTIVE-CLASS phrase, the conformance rules shall be the same as if a SET statement were performed". Code: ContentMismatch sends every object-reference formal, ACTIVE-CLASS included, to ObjectRefAssignmentMismatch with the FORMAL as receiver, so an ACTIVE-CLASS formal is always SR14 (ACTIVE-CLASS sender only) and alternative 2) is unreachable. Probe (ac_con_legal pre-edit form): `01 X USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE C1 ONLY` + `INVOKE X "M" USING BY CONTENT X` -> COBOLNET0828 'an object reference described C1 ONLY does not conform to a receiver described with the ACTIVE-CLASS phrase (SR14)'. Expected: accepted — invoked through a C1 ONLY reference, and SET X-to-(C1 ONLY) is valid (SR12 a)1.). Rejects legal source. The pointer/object-without-ACTIVE-CLASS SET paragraph: the object half conforms (probe r3e: C2 subclass BY CONTENT into C1 formal accepted = SR12 a)2.); the pointer half checks category only and not restriction — the open kb/Work PB1063 (restricted data-pointer BY CONTENT into an unrestricted formal accepted) owns that leg; not re-reported.

(3) under-rejects b) — c_num_idx (PIC 9(4) identifier into a USAGE INDEX formal) and c_lit_idx (literal 3) accepted; SET's §14.9.39.3 SR2 "Identifier-2 shall reference a data item of class index" and SR3 (no arithmetic-expression-1 into class index) refuse both (index items carry PicCategory.Numeric, so the numeric COMPUTE arm answers). c_idx_idx accepted (correct). subject: Returning items
notes: kb/Work PB1164 (registrar 14c). Rule: 'If the returning item in the activated element is not described with an ACTIVE-CLASS phrase, the conformance rules are the same as if a SET statement were performed in the activated runtime element with the returning item in the activated element as the sending operand and the corresponding returning item in the activating element as the receiving operand.' (cite.py --check 14.8.3.3 -> OK §14.8.3.3 1)). THREE activation lanes, only one follows the rule. (a) INVOKE: OoBindResolvedInvoke routes an object-reference pair to OoConformance.ObjectRefAssignmentMismatch (the §14.9.39.3 SR8/SR10/SR12/SR14 table) - CONFORMS; pinned by conformance-test:OoSpineTests.ReturningWidening_SubclassIntoBaseAndUniversalReceivers (subclass into base and universal receivers). (b) Format-2 CALL (AS NESTED / program prototype): CallBinder.BindCall runs OoConformance.DescriptionMismatch(cr, rr.Item, anyLengthActivationRelax:true), whose ObjectReference arm demands SameDescriptionAs (the §9.3.8.2.3 rule-2 IDENTITY rule), not the SET rules. Probe probe/returning-items/p5.cob: nested MKR5 'PROCEDURE DIVISION RETURNING L-O' with L-O 'USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE RID5' (RID5 INHERITS FROM RIB5), caller 'CALL "MKR5" AS NESTED RETURNING B' with B 'OBJECT REFERENCE RIB5' and again RETURNING U (universal): both refused COBOLNET1736 'object-reference description mismatch ... §9.3.8.2.3 rule 2'. Spec: SET B TO <RID5-typed> is §14.9.39.3 SR12 a)2. (same class or a subclass - cite OK) and a universal receiver constrains nothing (SR8), so both compile and the run prints DERIVED then U-SET. (c) FUNCTION-ID: UdfReturningResidue refuses an object-reference RETURNING item outright (COBOLNET1510 'not yet carried ... a named residue') - no register note owns it. Two-arm dispatch: the INVOKE arm was fixed (DEVLOG 603 adversarial review), the CALL arm was not. Rejects legal source. test-ref left empty: the OoSpine test covers the INVOKE half only. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause 14.8.3 Returning items exists from ISO/IEC 1989:2002, where RETURNING on CALL/INVOKE/functions was introduced; not applicable to 1985)]

subject: Returning items
notes: kb/Work PB1165 (also PB1166) (registrar 14c). Rule 2) (cite.py --check 14.8.3.3 'If the activated method is invoked with any other object reference, the sending operand has the same description as that object reference' -> OK §14.8.3.3 2) b) 4.; b) 1. 'described with that same object-class-name and an ONLY phrase' -> OK). An ACTIVE-CLASS returning item is NOT a sender description by itself: the sending operand is RE-DESCRIBED from how the method was invoked (class-name -> that class ONLY; SELF/SUPER -> ACTIVE-CLASS; interface-typed ref -> universal; otherwise the invoking reference's description), with FACTORY presence copied from the returning item. OoBindResolvedInvoke passes m.Binding.Returning.Pic (ObjectRefDescriptor.ActiveClass(<declaring class>)) straight to ObjectRefAssignmentMismatch; no code re-describes it (grep ActiveClass in OoBinder.cs: only the NEW/SELF delivery at :253 and the inline-invocation screen at :499). Probe p2.cob: RIB2 method MK 'RETURNING R' R 'OBJECT REFERENCE ACTIVE-CLASS'; main 'INVOKE D "MK" RETURNING D2' with D and D2 'OBJECT REFERENCE RID2' (RID2 INHERITS FROM RIB2) -> COBOLNET0828 'the class containing the ACTIVE-CLASS sender (RIB2) is not RID2 or one of its subclasses (SR12 b)2.)'. Spec: rule 2 b) 4. makes the sender RID2-typed, SR12 a)2. admits it; expected run output DERIVED. Probe p3.cob: RIB3 FACTORY method MAKE returning ACTIVE-CLASS, 'INVOKE RID3 "MAKE" RETURNING DO' with DO 'OBJECT REFERENCE RID3 ONLY' -> COBOLNET0828 'the receiver is described with the ONLY phrase, so an ACTIVE-CLASS sender is not permitted (SR12 b)1.)'. Spec: rule 2 b) 1. makes the sender 'RID3 ONLY', SR12 a)1. admits it; expected DERIVED. The interface-typed leg (b)3.) is not statically reachable (an interface prototype cannot carry ACTIVE-CLASS, §13.18.60.3 SR16) and the SELF/SUPER leg coincides with the code's behavior. The row's trailing lead-in sentence ('the receiving operand shall have the same ALIGN, BLANK WHEN ZERO, DYNAMIC LENGTH, JUSTIFIED, PICTURE, SIGN, and USAGE clauses' - cite OK) also under-rejects: probe p13.cob, nested SA13 returning 'PIC A(5)' into caller 'PIC X(5)' compiles and prints [ABCDE] - DescriptionMismatch's Alphanumeric arm treats alphabetic and alphanumeric as one category with a null EditMask, so two different PICTURE clauses pass; ALIGN and DYNAMIC LENGTH are never compared (not probed). Rejects legal source (ACTIVE-CLASS legs) and under-rejects (PICTURE A vs X). [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (clause 14.8.3 Returning items exists from ISO/IEC 1989:2002, where RETURNING on CALL/INVOKE/functions was introduced; not applicable to 1985)]

notes: kb/Work PB1166 (registrar 14c). 'Period picture symbols match if and only if the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause is in effect for both the activating and the activated runtime elements or for neither of them.' (cite.py --check 14.8.3.3 -> OK §14.8.3.3 2)). Probe p9p.cob: class RIC9P with SPECIAL-NAMES DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA returns LR PIC Z9.99 ('.' = insertion there), main (no DPC) receives into R PIC Z9.99 ('.' = decimal point) -> accepted, prints [12.34]. Contained units share SPECIAL-NAMES (§12.3.7.4 GR1, cite OK), so the divergence is reachable only across separately-defined units (class, prototype-activated program, function) - measured on the INVOKE lane. Under-rejects. The REPORTED side stays this negative determination on both directive branches'), and Annex A.1 item 111 cross-references 14.9.1 GR11 to that same determination, so the fact that AcceptSource.Time never reads DataBinder.LeapSecond (unlike IntrinsicRenderer.LeapSecondFlag, which every section 15.3 date/time function receives) is a documented choice rather than a gap. subject: ACCEPT statement
notes: 'DAY-OF-WEEK ... unsigned elementary numeric integer ONE digit ... usage display. 1 represents Monday ... 7 represents Sunday.' AcceptSource.DayOfWeek() returns `((int)Now().DayOfWeek + 6) % 7 + 1`. Checked the remap against .NET's DayOfWeek (Sunday=0 .. Saturday=6) for every value: Sunday 0 -> (6%7)+1 = 7; Monday 1 -> (7%7)+1 = 1; Tuesday 2 -> 2; Wednesday 3 -> 3; Thursday 4 -> 4; Friday 5 -> 5; Saturday 6 -> (12%7)+1 = 6. That is exactly the standard's Monday=1 .. Sunday=7 numbering, and the result is always 1..7 so the one-digit unsigned width holds. EmitAcceptTemporal maps the kind to width 1 (`_ => ("AcceptSource.DayOfWeek()", 1)` -- the default arm, which is safe because AcceptKind.Device is dispatched away by EmitAccept before EmitAcceptTemporal is reached). Both endpoints of the remap -- the two values a naive Sunday=0 mapping would get wrong -- are pinned by the theory AcceptDifferentialTests.DayOfWeek_MondayIs1_SundayIs7 (2026-06-08 -> '1', 2026-06-14 -> '7'). || UPHELD: I recomputed all seven remap values independently and they match; and I verified the safety claim about the `_ =>` default arm by reading EmitAccept (AcceptDisplayEmitter.cs:37-41), which is `if (a.Kind == AcceptKind.Device) EmitAcceptDevice(a.Target); else EmitAcceptTemporal(...)`, so AcceptKind.Device genuinely cannot reach the ternary's default -- the arm receives DayOfWeek only. The test is a spec-derived theory pinning exactly the two boundary values a Sunday=0 error would corrupt. CONFORMS with qualifying closing evidence.

notes: READ: the grammar alternative `ADD (CORRESPONDING | CORR) dataReference TO dataReference roundedPhrase? arithmeticOnSizeError? END_ADD?` (CobolParserCore.g4:851) and CorrespondingBinder.BindAddCorresponding (25-29), `add.CORRESPONDING() is not null || add.CORR() is not null ? Bind(CorrVerb.Add, add.dataReference(), ...) : new BoundUnsupported(...)`. The two spellings are ONE grammar alternative and ONE boolean disjunction feeding ONE Bind call, so there is no second dispatch arm that could carry different behaviour -- the equivalence is structural rather than a pair of parallel code paths (the two-arm-dispatch failure shape does not apply here). Neither token is edition-gated: no ConstructRegistry row in tests/version-matrix/constructs.json mentions CORR or CORRESPONDING, and Annex E carries no ADD entry, so the batch default editions stand. TEST HONESTY: the golden cited exercises the CORRESPONDING spelling on ADD; the CORR spelling is exercised on SUBTRACT (conformance-test:CorrespondingDifferentialTests.SubtractCorr_TargetMinusSource_CorrToken), through the sibling alternative at CobolParserCore.g4:890 and the identical `sub.CORRESPONDING() is not null || sub.CORR() is not null` disjunction -- so the CORR-on-ADD spelling specifically has no test of its own. Adding `ADD CORR SRC TO DST` to an existing CORR golden would make the coverage exhaustive; nothing about the code makes it a risk. || UPHELD, with evidence the record did not have. The structural argument is only sound if the two spellings are also indistinguishable to the LEXER, which I checked rather than assumed: Core/CobolLexer.g4:455 `CORR : 'CORR' ;` and :459 `CORRESPONDING : 'CORRESPONDING' ;` are both UNCONDITIONAL token rules -- no `{isXXXX()}?` version predicate on either -- and ANTLR's maximal-munch keeps CORRESPONDING whole rather than splitting it into CORR + a word, so neither spelling can degrade into a data-name at any edition. Had CORR been edition-gated or context-sensitive, `ADD CORR X TO Y` would have fallen to grammar alternative 2 and bound CORR as an ADDEND -- a silent wrong answer -- which is the failure mode this check rules out. Also verified: alternative 1 precedes alternative 2, so the Format-3 parse always wins, and BindAddCorresponding's `else` arm is unreachable (BindAdd routes here only when `addOperandList()` is null, which only alternative 1 produces). I also independently confirmed the edition claim per ground rule 4: Annex E (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42847 onward) lists no ADD substantive change, and the rule text carries no edition qualifier, so the batch default 85,2002,2014,2023 is the derived answer, not a copied one. CONFORMS-but-thinly-tested is the correct outcome here (ground rule 3), and the record's own honesty note about the CORR-on-ADD spelling stands.

notes: READ: ArithmeticEmitter.EmitInPlace (lines 26-44), NumericRenderer.Fold (319-332), NumericRenderer.CombineCore/CombineAdditive, ArithmeticEmitter.Snapshot (208-215), and the bind side ArithmeticBinder.BindAdd:43-47 (`BoundAddTo(addends, recv, sizeErr)`). UNVERIFIED HALF -- the rule's SECOND paragraph, 'When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the result of the initial evaluation is equivalent to (operand-11 + ... + operand-1n)': STANDARD-BINARY is rejected outright at bind (DataBinder.cs:318-320, COBOLNET0806, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 2 records it 'Not claimed'), so that leg has no implementation; the STANDARD-DECIMAL leg does exist -- NumericRenderer.CombineCore's `if (StandardDecimal)` branch lifts every ADD operand through `DecOperand`/CobolDec -- but NO golden exercises an ADD under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` (2014/arithmetic_standard_decimal is a COMPUTE, pb84_standard_decimal_intermediate_consumers is DIVIDE/REMAINDER). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` golden whose multi-addend ADD has an SDIDI-visible answer the native Int128 lane would give differently (e.g. an addend list whose intermediate needs more than the receiver's digits). || UPHELD. Additional independent evidence FOR the first half: the code computes `identifier-2 + initial-evaluation` where GR1 prints `(initial-evaluation + identifier-2)` -- not a defect, addition is commutative in Int128, in CobolDec (decimal128 add is commutative and correctly rounded) and in IEEE binary64, so no rounding difference can arise from the swap; and NumericRenderer.Fold saves/restores the ambient `_rcv` so the initial evaluation is receiver-INDEPENDENT, matching GR4a ('the initial evaluation ... is placed in an intermediate data item'). subject: CONTINUE statement
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.9.3 "If the AFTER phrase is not specified, then the statement is processed as if an AFTER phrase were specified with arithmetic-expression-1 specified as zero."` -> OK, SR 2). Derived expectation first: bare CONTINUE must be EXACTLY equivalent to `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS`, which by GR1 means (a) no suspension, (b) no exception -- 0 is not less than zero, so EC-CONTINUE-LESS-THAN-ZERO cannot be set even under CHECKING ON -- and (c) execution continues with the next executable statement. The failure shape to look for is a bare CONTINUE that behaves OBSERVABLY differently from the AFTER-0 spelling under some ambient state. READ: ControlFlowBinder.BindContinue (ControlFlowBinder.cs:57-62) -- `if (cont.arithmeticExpression() is not { } secs) return new BoundNop();` -- and StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundNop) (StatementEmitter.cs:147) returns false emitting nothing, so control simply falls to the next emitted statement. COMPARED the two spellings for OBSERVABLE difference rather than assuming: the AFTER-0 leg emits `CobolTiming.ContinueAfter((double)(0L), true)` (checked-in generated output, tests/conformance/2023/continue_after.g.cs), and ContinueAfter with 0.0 takes neither the `seconds < 0.0` arm nor the `secs == 0` sleep -- it returns having touched nothing. Under `>>TURN ... CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION` the AFTER form additionally wraps itself in `ExceptionState.EnterStatement("CONTINUE", loc, ...)` / `ExitStatement` (exception_statement_ambient.g.cs:151-156), but that pair is SAVE-and-RESTORE (ExceptionState.cs:79-88) and nothing raises inside it, so LastStatement/LastLocation are identical afterwards to what a bare CONTINUE leaves -- FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION cannot tell the spellings apart. EcBinder gives BoundNop no EC wrapper and BoundContinueAfter one (EcBinder.cs:379-381), but since neither can raise, that is not observable either. So all three of (a)(b)(c) hold STATICALLY and the equivalence looks exact. EDITION: 2023 -- this syntax rule exists only because the AFTER phrase does (Annex E.3.3 item 14, specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43957); at 85/2002/2014 bare CONTINUE is the only form and 14.9.9.1 already governs it, so no per-edition split exists. || UPHELD, the code half: I re-ran the cite check myself and re-read BindContinue (ControlFlowBinder.cs:57-62), Visit(BoundNop) (StatementEmitter.cs:147) and ExceptionState.EnterStatement/ExitStatement (Runtime/Exceptions/ExceptionState.cs:79-88) independently; the save/restore argument holds, and I confirmed the one thing that could break it -- that EnterStatement touches ONLY _stmtName/_stmtLoc/_stmtLocNames and nothing raises between it and ExitStatement, so no ambient state differs. I also checked the sibling defect I raised on SR-14.9.9.3-1 for an ASYMMETRY between the two spellings and found none: ProcedureTableBuilder.DeclIsTrivialExit tests `st.continueStatement() is not null`, which is true for BOTH forms, so it mis-classifies them equally. || REFUTED, the EVIDENCE half -- VERDICT DOWNGRADED CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The rule's entire content is an EQUIVALENCE between two spellings, and neither cited test pins it. (1) `conformance:85/wavef_dbg_proc` is MISATTACHED and I removed it: SR-14.9.9.3-2 is 2023 text, there is no AFTER phrase at edition 85, so an 85 golden cannot exercise a rule that is not in force there -- it evidences 14.9.9.1's no-op, not this rule. (2) `conformance:2023/continue_after` does NOT contain a bare CONTINUE at all -- I read tests/conformance/2023/continue_after.cob in full: its PROCEDURE DIVISION is DISPLAY "A" / `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS` / DISPLAY "B" / `CONTINUE AFTER WS-N SECONDS` / DISPLAY "EC=" ..., so it pins only the AFTER-0 leg. The bare leg at 2023 is exercised by 2023/ec_range_search (SEARCH WHEN bodies) and 2023/pb86_perform_times_function_count, which pin (c) 'control continues' -- so I substituted ec_range_search for the 85 golden. WHICH HALF IS UNVERIFIED: (b), the bare leg's 'no exception even under CHECKING ON', and the equivalence itself. No golden anywhere puts a BARE CONTINUE inside a `>>TURN EC-CONTINUE-LESS-THAN-ZERO CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION` window, so nothing would fail if a future change gave BoundNop an EC wrapper or an ambient EnterStatement -- exactly the shape that makes a green gate no evidence. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS ROW: one 2023 golden under `>>TURN EC-CONTINUE-LESS-THAN-ZERO CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION` that executes `CONTINUE.` and then `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS.`, DISPLAYing FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS, FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION after each and asserting the two triples are byte-identical (and that EXCEPTION-STATUS is empty after both). Note this is an evidence downgrade, not a claim that the code is wrong: the static read says the spellings agree, but 'nothing raises' is a reachability claim, and reachability is measured, not deduced.

The claim was that 'COMMIT lexes as a facility IDENTIFIER' so 'APPLY COMMIT ON F' is absorbed by genericClause and silently dropped. It is not: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4 line 436 defines a dedicated token 'COMMIT : 'COMMIT' ;', and genericClause (CobolExpressions.g4) is 'IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER | literal)*' over the IDENTIFIER TOKEN -- not over cobolWord, which is the rule that lists COMMIT as a context-sensitive user word (CobolWords.g4). So in 'ioControlParagraph : I_O_CONTROL DOT (ioControlClause DOT?)*', genericClause consumes only 'APPLY' (no APPLY token exists, so it lexes as IDENTIFIER), the COMMIT token matches no alternative of ioControlClause, the loop exits and COMMIT is left unmatched -> a syntax error. 12.4.6.3.2's format is 'APPLY COMMIT ON [ [ file-name-1 ] [ identifier-1 ] ]...', so the clause is LOUDLY REJECTED, not silently swallowed. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: no program this compiler accepts can be subject to an active APPLY COMMIT clause, so GR7's guard 'the file is not subject to an active APPLY COMMIT clause' is VACUOUSLY SATISFIED and the unconditional releases are correct for everything that compiles. The gap is a 12.4.6.3 NOT-IMPLEMENTED (consistent with StatementBinder routing the COMMIT and ROLLBACK STATEMENTS to BindUnsupportedFacility), not a GR7 divergence. || REMAINING UNVERIFIED HALF (why PARTIAL still stands): GR7's OTHER antecedent conjunct, 'If record locks are in effect', is never evaluated on this path. DeleteShared performs ReleaseAllExcept and ReleaseSingle without consulting LocksEffective, unlike its own siblings RewriteShared ('if (phrase == FileRecordLock.WithLock && LocksEffective(meta, st, name))') and WriteShared. It is benign TODAY only because LocksEffective's first line is 'if (meta.LockMode == FileLockMode.None) return false;' so a SHARING-only connector can hold no lock to release -- an accident of another method's guard, not a check on this one. And no test drives DELETE through DeleteShared with a lock held: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/CobolFileLockTests.cs exercises ReleaseSingle/ReleaseAllForConnector as PRIMITIVES, and file_sharing_mutate never locks a record through the deleting connector. What would close the row: gate the GR7 releases on the same LocksEffective predicate the sibling verbs use, and add a 2002 golden that READs a record WITH LOCK, DELETEs it, and shows a second connector can then lock the same id.

subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: DERIVED FIRST: leg (a) is chunking - repeat the transfer leftmost-first until the item is exhausted - when the sending size exceeds the device's single-transfer size; leg (b) is left-alignment when the device is the wider of the two. READ: AcceptDisplayEmitter.EmitDisplay is one `sink.Write(image)` / `sink.WriteLine(image)` with no length test, no loop, no wrap and no padding, over a `System.Console` / `System.Console.Error` byte stream. LEG (b) HOLDS trivially: the stream write deposits the characters left-to-right starting at the current position and adds nothing, which is 'the transferred data is stored aligned to the left in the receiving device'. LEG (a) IS UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: there is no device transfer size for the sending item to exceed. THAT VACUITY IS THE UNVERIFIED HALF - it is sound only if GR2's determination genuinely is 'unbounded', and that determination is nowhere written down (see GR-14.9.11.4-2: Annex A.1 item 58 has no docs/CONFORMANCE.md row). Nor is it pinned by any test: no corpus program displays an operand long enough to prove no chunk boundary or wrap is inserted. So the larger half of this rule rests on an undocumented premise and on zero evidence => PARTIAL, not CONFORMS. The phrase-NOT-specified arm is WriteLine, whose platform line terminator is exactly GR10's 'reset to the leftmost position of the next line of the device'. The arm selector is faithful to the phrase: AcceptDisplayBinder.BindDisplay sets NoAdvancing = 'display.displayNoAdvancing() is not null', one-for-one with the optional grammar sub-rule, so absence of the phrase can only take the WriteLine arm. BOTH sinks are covered identically -- 'string sink = d.ToStdErr ? "System.Console.Error" : "System.Console"' is chosen before the terminator decision, so the SYSERR route resets the line the same way (checked because feedback_two_arm_dispatch is the repeat defect shape here; the sink axis and the advancing axis are independent and both were read). B-SYSOUT
C-CONSOLE' (each statement reset the position to the next line), and the golden comp5_display_beyond_picture.out carries two lines produced by two DISPLAY statements. subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: CONFORMS BY VACUITY, and the vacuity is a documented determination rather than an accident. READ EmitDisplay: the only two devices this compiler can emit to are System.Console and System.Console.Error -- the 14.9.11.4 GR8 standard display device and the SYSERR routing established by AcceptDisplayBinder.DisplayOutputDevices / BindDisplayUpon and written up in docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.1 item 59. Both are line-structured streams on which vertical positioning IS applicable (WriteLine performs it), so GR11's antecedent -- 'vertical positioning is not applicable on the device' -- is FALSE for every device the implementation offers, and there is no positioning to ignore. The claim is recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 24 ('DISPLAY positioning ignored when N/A | 14.9.11 | Claimed | Console device; positioning is a no-op where inapplicable'), which matches spec A.3 item 24 -- 'If positioning is not applicable on the hardware device, the operating system will ignore the positioning specified or implied by the DISPLAY statement' (cite.py --check A.3 OK). NO TEST-REF, deliberately: the antecedent is unpopulatable by declaration, so no spec-derived test can exist for this row; it is CONFORMS-but-untestable, not CONFORMS-but-untested. What would change the verdict is the arrival of a device (a printer / reel mnemonic) for which vertical positioning is inapplicable -- at that point GR11 needs real code and this row must be re-adjudicated. || UPHELD with my own reads. I re-located A.3 item 24 in the spec independently (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, Annex A.3 'Processor-dependent language element list' begins at the section-a-3 anchor; item 24 is the DISPLAY positioning row, text verbatim as quoted) and confirmed it is the A.3 counterpart of GR11 rather than of GR9. I re-derived the device closure from the code rather than from the doc: AcceptDisplayBinder.BindDisplayUpon admits ONLY names in DisplayOutputDevices and errors COBOLNET0817 otherwise, and EmitDisplay's sink expression is a two-valued ternary over System.Console / System.Console.Error -- there is no third sink expression anywhere in the emitter, so no unread arm can reach a non-line-structured device. This is the one row where a CONFORMS legitimately costs nothing further, because the antecedent is closed by the implementation's own device set, and the note already names the single event that would reopen it. NOTE the vacuity is contingent, not permanent: it is voided the moment DisplayOutputDevices grows a name, so the eventual Format-2 / printer work must re-adjudicate this row rather than inherit the Claimed.

DERIVED FIRST: in EVERY format the dividend is the id-2/lit-2 slot and the divisor the id-1/lit-1 slot — which means INTO's first operand is the DIVISOR and BY's first operand is the DIVIDEND, the one role-mapping a compiler can silently invert. READ: BindDivide binds `var a = host.Expr.BindExpr(aCtx)` with the comment 'INTO: the divisor; BY: the dividend', then INTO-with-GIVING returns `BoundDivideGiving(dividendX, a, ...)` where dividendX = BindExpr(into.divideIntoOperand()) and BY-with-GIVING returns `BoundDivideGiving(a, divisorX, ...)` where divisorX = BindExpr(byPhrase.divideOperand()); the record is `BoundDivideGiving(BoundExpr Dividend, BoundExpr Divisor, ...)`, so both map correctly. The REMAINDER branch repeats the same mapping through its two conditional expressions (`dividend = intoPhrase ? BindExpr(i.divideIntoOperand()) : a` / `divisor = intoPhrase is not null ? a : BindExpr(b.divideOperand())`) — checked arm by arm, both arms correct. Format 1 (no GIVING) makes each identifier-2 both dividend and receiver: EmitDivide is called with dividend null and reads `num.FieldNum(r.Place)` per receiver — the identifier-2-as-dividend reading. GR2c (literal value) — a literal operand binds through ExpressionBinder.NumLiteral to BoundNumLiteral, and the literal-after-INTO case (`DIVIDE 3 INTO 10 GIVING Q`) reaches it through BindOperandExprCore's LiteralContext arm. subject: GENERATE statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1131 (open). GR3: "each execution of the GENERATE statement causes the specified control data items to be saved and subsequently compared so as to sense for control breaks. This processing is described by the CONTROL clause." (cite.py --check 14.9.16.4 OK, 3)). The first GENERATE saves Prior = Get() for each control. Each later GENERATE calls DetectBreakLevel, which walks major to minor, skips FINAL and returns the first change. On a break the priors are replaced by the new current values. Verified for a three-level hierarchy (FINAL K1 K2) in probe out/probe/generate/g1.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023). Unverified edge, which belongs to the §13.18.16 rows: §13.18.16.4 GR3 tests 'for equality with the corresponding prior control' (cite.py OK), but the engine compares the character images ordinally. Two values that are equal but have different images would therefore break, for example ALSO-equivalent characters under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE. The CONTROL-clause adjudication should probe that edge. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR3 is the save-and-COMPARE step, and the compare is wrong. §12.3.6.4 GR11 c) says the program collating sequence determines the truth value of alphanumeric comparisons 'Implicitly specified by the presence of a CONTROL clause in a report description entry'. §13.18.16.4 GR3 makes the test one 'for equality with the corresponding prior control'. CobolReport.DetectBreakLevel instead compares the character images with string.Equals(..., StringComparison.Ordinal). So under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE with ALSO, or a locale-based one, two values the program itself treats as equal still sense a control break. subject: INSPECT statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1128 (open). Rule: zero-length identifier-1 -> a) identifier-1 and identifier-2 unchanged, b) successful, c) control to end of statement (cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 'the contents of the data items referenced by identifier-1 and identifier-2 are unchanged' -> OK 2) a)). No explicit short-circuit exists, but the runtime loops run zero times over an empty image, every count is 0 and the emitter ADDs 0 into identifier-2, and the replaced/converted image is the empty string stored back over a zero extent - observationally identical. Probe p3.cob with CNT=0 (G zero-length): N PIC 99 VALUE 7 TALLYING N FOR ALL 'A' CHARACTERS -> N=07 unchanged; REPLACING ALL 'A' BY 'B' and CONVERTING 'A' TO 'C' then CNT=5 -> G='AAAAA' unchanged; no EC, execution continues (b). Second route probed too: p7.cob under >>REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH, INSPECT S1(1:L) with L=0 TALLYING N FOR ALL 'A' CHARACTERS / REPLACING ALL 'A' BY 'B' -> N=07, S1='AAAA', EXCEPTION-STATUS blank. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR2 a) requires identifier-2 to be UNCHANGED when identifier-1 is zero-length, and c) requires control to go straight to the end of the statement. The implementation has no zero-length short-circuit. It still runs the counter store counter := counter + 0 (ArithmeticEmitter.StoreArith through CobolNum.Store/FormatImage), and that store rewrites identifier-2 whenever its content is not already in canonical form. The adjudicator probed only a canonical counter (PIC 99 VALUE 7), where adding 0 happens to leave the value alone. Identifier-1 unchanged (half a) and no EC set (half b) were confirmed. Identifier-2 unchanged fails for a non-canonical counter, so the rule is PARTIAL, and in fact a defect for that shape. || editions as adjudicated: 2023 text (applies wherever a zero-length identifier-1 can exist; Annex E lists no INSPECT change for it)

subject: INSPECT statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1124 (open). cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 "If the LEADING adjective applies to literal-1 and literal-1 is a leading occurrence as defined in General rules 12 and 17" -> OK GR8 a) 2.; GR12 b) "provided that the first such occurrence encountered is at the point where comparison began in the first comparison cycle in which literal-1 was eligible to participate" -> OK; GR17 c) same proviso -> OK; GR9 a) "is first eligible to participate in matching at the leftmost character position" -> OK. The runtime anchors a LEADING run at expectedPos, set lazily at the first cycle in which the loop REACHES the operand in its region — not the first cycle in which it is ELIGIBLE. When an earlier operand matches at the eligible start, the LEADING operand is never tried in that cycle, expectedPos stays -1, and the run anchors at a later position. REPLACING twin: Z='ABBC' REPLACING ALL "A" BY "a" LEADING "B" BY "b" -> abbC; spec aBBC. Wrong answer, silent. The existing shared-cycle test only covers the case where LEADING is reached at the eligible start and fails there. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023

subject: INSPECT statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1125 (open). Rule: 'Both the ALL and LEADING phrases are transitive across the operands that follow them until another ALL or LEADING phrase is encountered.' (cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 -> OK 10)). The binder half is right: a bare operand inherits the last adjective (InspectBinder 'last' seed); probe p1.cob T4 'ABAB' TALLYING N FOR ALL "A" "B" -> 04. The DEFECT is in the parse that decides where the transitive operand list ENDS: inspectCountPhrase's bare alternative is guarded by IsBareInspectOperand() => TokenStream.LA(2) != FOR, which only recognizes the next identifier-2 when it is a single bare word. A subscripted, qualified or reference-modified identifier-2 (C(1) FOR / M OF G FOR) is swallowed as a transitive ALL operand of the previous counter, and its FOR clause is re-attached to the previous counter. Probe p6.cob: S1='AAB', INSPECT S1 TALLYING N FOR ALL "A" C(1) FOR ALL "B" -> N=3 C=000; with M OF G -> N=3 M=0. Spec-derived: C(1)/M OF G can only be identifier-2 (an operand is never followed by FOR in the tallying-phrase format), so expected N=2, C(1)=1 / M=1. Silent wrong answer, all editions. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023

notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1124 (open). subject: INSPECT statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1128 (open). Rule: format 4 executes as a format 2 with one ALL phrase per character of literal-4, literal-3 the ordinally corresponding character of literal-5 (cite.py --check 14.9.22.4 -> OK 20)). Every such operand is one character over the same single region, so the shared cycle degenerates to CobolInspect.Convert's per-character map inside Region(before, after); figurative literal-5 is expanded to literal-4's size at bind time. Probes: p1.cob T15 'ABCABC' CONVERTING "ABC" TO "XYZ" AFTER "C" -> 'ABCXYZ'; Annex D.25 EXAMPLE 6 (AFTER QUOTE BEFORE "#") -> 'AC"XEYXFYZX#AB"D' exactly as printed (p4.cob); BACKWARD p5.cob 'ABCABC' AFTER "C" -> 'XYZXYC'. The size-mismatch (GR22) and duplicate-character (GR23) behaviour belong to sibling part rules. No spec-derived test pins the equivalence directly (conformance:2023/inspect_backward C= covers only the BACKWARD boundary). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR20 makes a format 4 behave as a format 2 with one ALL c BY d pair per character. The per-character map in CobolInspect.Convert is right for alphanumeric and national ELEMENTARY items and for alphanumeric groups. W1 PIC N(5) and W2 alphanumeric group GA both give 'ZZYZZ'. The BEFORE delimiter case W4 gives 'XYCABC'. The duplicate-from case W5 gives 'XYCXYC'. A plain figurative TO QUOTE, W3, expands correctly. Two shapes fail. (1) A NATIONAL GROUP identifier-1 (GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL, which SR1 allows) is CORRUPTED. On a fixed 5-occurrence national group, CONVERTING N"A" TO N"Z" gives '婚婚娠††' where 'ZZZZZ' is expected. On a national ODO group the live positions become mojibake. The emitter stores the converted UTF-16 character string through the group byte-image path (GF.FromImage(__ins) / SpliceInto(GN.AsImage(), ...)). REPLACING corrupts the same way (X3), so the defect is in the shared store; the format 2 equivalence holds, but its result is wrong. (2) A figurative constant beginning with ALL is legal as literal-5: SR3 bars ALL only for literals 1-4, and GR22 sizes a figurative literal-5 to literal-4. The binder still rejects 'CONVERTING "ABC" TO ALL "Q"' with COBOLNET1757, so that legal format 4 source never executes. The claim that a figurative literal-5 is expanded at bind time holds only for the non-ALL figuratives. || editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (BACKWARD half 2023 only - Annex E.3.3 item 34)
