subject: INVOKE statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1136 (open). Rule: 'Identifier-1 shall be an object reference.' (cite.py --check 14.9.23.3 -> OK §14.9.23.3 1)). The data-item half is enforced: OoBindInstanceInvoke rejects a non-OBJECT-REFERENCE receiver (probe pa2: INVOKE X5 "GREET" with X5 PIC X(5) -> COBOLNET0824) - but the message cites 'ISO §14.9.23.3 SR3' (SR3 is the class-name-1/factory rule; the rule is SR1). The other half - which IDENTIFIERS may be identifier-1 - is not met: invokeTarget -> objectReference admits only dataReference | NULL | SELF | SUPER, and NULL is refused. (1) INVOKE NULL "GREET" -> COBOLNET0823 'the predefined NULL object reference cannot be a receiver (ISO §14.9.23.3 -)', a rule with no number because none exists: §8.4.3.1.3 7) makes NULL an identifier (predefined-object reference), §8.4.3.7.3 2) (OK) makes it 'class object and category object reference ... not a universal object reference', so SR1 holds and SR4 applies vacuously; §14.9.23.4 5) (OK) is the runtime answer (EC-OO-NULL); and §8.4.3.4.3 2) (OK) bans NULL as identifier-1 of the INLINE form only - the statement form has no such ban. (2) An object-view (§8.4.3.1.3 6), identifier Format 5) has no grammar anywhere: INVOKE U AS CP2 "GREET" -> COBOLNET0901 'AS is a reserved word' + COBOL0301 (probe pc1). (3) An inline method invocation (Format 4) returning an object reference: INVOKE O :: "ME" "GREET" -> COBOL0001 unexpected '::' (probe pc4). EXCEPTION-OBJECT works (probe pc2 -> EC-OO-NULL at run time, correct). The qualified [object-class-name-1 OF] SUPER spelling is also a parse error (probe pb1) - owned by the §8.4.3.8 rows (PB285 measured it; SR-8.4.3.8.3-4/-6 open NOT-IMPLEMENTED). No spec-derived test for SR1. Finding F1 + F9 (citation). || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (INVOKE and the OO module are a COBOL-2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule, so the 2023 text is also the 2014 text)

subject: INVOKE statement

Probes: "" -> 0823 zero-length (pa7); N"" -> 0823 (pa16); X"" -> 0823 (pa18); 12 -> 0823 class (pa9); B"1" -> 0823 class (pa15); N"GREET" runs HI (pa8); X"4752454554" runs HI (pa10); "GR" & "EET" runs HI (pa17); "greet" runs HI (pa12, §8.3.2.2 case-insensitivity). OoDecodeMethodNameLiteral decodes NX"..." by stripping the N and running the ALPHANUMERIC hex codec, so every hex digit pair becomes one character. subject: INVOKE statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1136 (open). Rule: 'If object-class-name-1 is specified, literal-1 shall be specified. The value of literal-1 shall be the name of a method defined in the factory interface of object-class-name-1.' (--check OK §14.9.23.3 3)). OoBindClassInvoke resolves non-NEW literal-1 via cls.FindFactoryMethod (walks INHERITS); a miss is COBOLNET0825 citing SR3 (probe pbn7: INVOKE BASEC "FRUN" where FRUN is a SUBC factory method -> 0825). Positive: INVOKE SUBC "FRUN" runs (probe pb2), predefined NEW binds the ctor. First half: INVOKE CP2 MA (identifier-2 with a class-name) is rejected (probe pa5) - but by the resolver's COBOLNET1639 "'CP2' is not defined", which is false (CP2 is in the REPOSITORY); the program is correctly refused, the diagnostic misnames the cause (recorded in finding F9). oo_factory golden exercises the factory-interface resolution positively. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Neither half of the rule is enforced as a rule. (1) 'Literal-1 shall be specified' with class-name-1: INVOKE CP2 MA is refused only because the identifier-2 branch resolves CP2 as a data item. The resolver's COBOLNET1639 then falsely says 'CP2' is not defined, although CP2 is in the REPOSITORY and is a class. No code tests the class-name-1 plus identifier-2 shape. (2) 'The value of literal-1 shall be the name of a method defined in the factory interface': OoBindClassInvoke short-circuits "NEW" before any factory-interface lookup. A class with no INHERITS clause has no BaseFactoryInterface New (§11.3.4 GR2, §16.2), yet INVOKE CQ "NEW" is accepted. The same compiler's SR4 a) arm (INVOKE F "NEW" through FACTORY OF CQ) says CQ's factory interface has no NEW. So the two arms disagree about one interface, and INHERITS BASE itself fails (COBOLNET0821). The FindFactoryMethod path for non-NEW names is correct, and the oo_factory golden pins it. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (INVOKE and the OO module are a COBOL-2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule, so the 2023 text is also the 2014 text)

subject: INVOKE statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1136 (open). Rule: SR4 a)-i) method-name placement by receiver description (--check 14.9.23.3 on the b) text -> OK §14.9.23.3 4) b)). Verified every arm by probe (pb2 / pbn1-6): a) FACTORY OF SUBC receiver resolves the factory roster, instance name 'HELLO' refused 0825; b) typed SUBC receiver resolves instance roster incl. inherited, factory name refused; c) FACTORY OF ACTIVE-CLASS (method LS) resolves factory roster of the containing class, instance name refused; d) ACTIVE-CLASS resolves instance roster, factory name refused; e) interface receiver resolves the prototype closure (code path + oo_interface_conformance golden); f)/g) SELF in factory/instance method selects factory/instance roster (SELF "RUNALL" in a factory method refused); h)/i) SUPER starts at the base, factory/instance by context (SUPER "RUNALL" refused, BASE HELLO / BASE FHELLO printed). Universal receivers bypass (correct - SR4 is non-universal only). Behaviour conforms; the COBOLNET0825 message cites 'SR4d' for EVERY typed receiver (SR4d is the ACTIVE-CLASS arm; a class-name receiver is SR4b, FACTORY OF is SR4a) - finding F9. The [class OF] SUPER spelling is owned by §8.4.3.8 rows. Covering test pins arm b) only. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Arm a) (FACTORY OF object-class-name → the factory interface) disagrees with SR3's arm about the SAME factory interface. INVOKE F "NEW", with F FACTORY OF CQ, is refused with 0825 because FindFactoryMethod never sees the predefined New. Yet INVOKE CQ "NEW" and SELF "NEW" in a factory method (oo_factory golden) treat NEW as a member of that factory interface. Under the compiler's own model this rejects legal source, and the same gap exists for arm c) FACTORY OF ACTIVE-CLASS, which uses the same FindFactoryMethod call. This is a two-arm dispatch: the NEW special case exists in OoBindClassInvoke and OoBindByReceiver but not in OoBindInstanceInvoke. Arms b) and d)-i) look correct for ordinary method names. The diagnostic also cites SR4d for every typed receiver. The covering test pins arm b) only. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (INVOKE and the OO module are a COBOL-2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule, so the 2023 text is also the 2014 text)

subject: INVOKE statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1137 (open). Rule: 'Identifier-5 and any identifier specified in arithmetic-expression-1 or boolean-expression-1 is a sending operand.' (--check OK §14.9.23.3 21)). BY VALUE identifier-5 is unreachable (PB1051) but its role would be the same sending resolution. No dedicated test. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — SUPERSEDES the earlier SR21 line and adds evidence. The rule covers identifier-5 (any identifier) and expression identifiers under BOTH the BY CONTENT and BY VALUE branches of §14.9.23.2. (1) The BY VALUE half is unexercisable: every BY VALUE argument is refused, and a BY VALUE method formal is COBOLNET0899 (open PB1051, rejects legal source). (2) Within BY CONTENT, identifier-5 formats that are legal sending operands are refused. A BY CONTENT object-view (O AS UNIVERSAL), whose only role bar is §8.4.3.5.3 SR2 (not receiving), is refused with a false 'AS is a reserved word' COBOLNET0901. The ordinary data-item and expression cases are correct: ResolveSending (pe3), BindExpr/BindBoolExpr, no write-back (pd9), and BY CONTENT EXCEPTION-OBJECT is accepted (re9). || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (INVOKE and the OO module are a COBOL-2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule, so the 2023 text is also the 2014 text)

subject: INVOKE statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1051 (open). Rule: 'An argument that consists merely of a single identifier or literal is regarded as an identifier or literal rather than an arithmetic or boolean expression.' (cite.py --check 14.9.23.4 OK, GR4). OoBindInvocationArg recovers a sole data reference (ConditionBinder.SoleDataReference), a sole numeric literal (SoleNumLiteral), a bare boolean node (UnwrapBareBool), a sole inline method invocation and a sole function-identifier from the expression nodes the grammar produced, so each rides the identifier/literal arm (§14.8.2.3.3 rule 2d MOVE lane) rather than the expression arm. The golden pins `BY CONTENT N`, `BY CONTENT 42`, `BY CONTENT A` (alphanumeric formal — would be refused on the expression arm). The separate defect that keyword-less EXPRESSIONS do not parse as one argument is GR6's (finding F1), not this rule's. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR4 (cite OK §14.9.23.4 4)) applies to EVERY argument: keyword-less, BY CONTENT, and BY VALUE (whose operands are also {arithmetic-expression-1 | identifier-5 | literal-2}). Two lanes are verified: the keyword-less and BY CONTENT reductions (qualified, subscripted, sole literal, keyword-less literal) ride the identifier/literal arm. The BY VALUE lane is unreachable: any BY VALUE argument is refused (COBOLNET0828 'formal parameter is BY REFERENCE ... header BY VALUE formals are a later slice'), and a method header BY VALUE formal is COBOLNET0899. So GR4's effect there is unverified — a single BY VALUE identifier is identifier-5, subject to SR15's class message-tag/numeric/object/pointer test, not an arithmetic expression. A second observation points the same way: `BY CONTENT -5` is classified as a literal, but a signed integer literal into a PIC X formal is refused. Table 16 (Numeric Integer -> Alphanumeric = Yes), via §14.8.2.3.3 rule 2 d) (cite OK), makes it legal, and `MOVE -5 TO X` compiles. The literal lane GR4 selects therefore answers wrong for signed literals (OoConformance.ContentNumericLiteralMismatch; the emitter comment says 'moves an UNSIGNED integer literal'). One half verified -> PARTIAL. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (INVOKE / OO is a COBOL-2002 introduction)

notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1141 (open). Rule: 'If an output procedure is specified, control passes to it during execution of the MERGE statement. The compiler inserts a return mechanism after the last statement in the output procedure. When control passes to that return mechanism, the mechanism provides for termination of the merge, and then passes control to the next executable statement after the MERGE statement. ... The RETURN statements in the output procedure are the requests for the next record.' (cite.py --check 14.9.24.4 -> OK §14.9.24.4 9)). Code: EmitMerge performs the merge (Merge) BEFORE entering the procedure (the 'point at which it selects the next record ... when requested'), then SortEnterProcedure(output:true) and Statements.EmitProcedureRange(op) - a bounded __Dispatch(start,end) whose bounded return IS the inserted return mechanism; after it SortClose ends the merge and control falls to the next statement. RETURN -> CobolSort.ReturnStatement pulls the next record from the cursor. Probe probe/merge-p2/m1.cob: OUTPUT PROCEDURE OUT-P (a paragraph after STOP RUN) runs, its RETURNs yield the 9 records in merged order, and 'AFTER CNT=09' shows control resumed at the statement after MERGE (85 and 2023). Note: the USING files' as-if CLOSE (GR7 c), 'not performed until after control passes the last statement in the output procedure') is performed BEFORE the procedure in this implementation - that is GR7's timing (part 1 / not in this part), not GR9's return mechanism. pb837/pb349/pb678 goldens run MERGE output procedures but assert other rules; no golden is derived from GR9 - test-needed. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR9 says the inserted return mechanism, reached after the last statement of the output procedure, 'provides for termination of the merge'. GR7 c) defines part of that termination: the as-if CLOSE of each USING file, which 'is not performed until after control passes the last statement in the output procedure'. EmitMerge instead runs EmitInputFile, including its FileClose and CLOSE USE hook, for every USING file BEFORE SortEnterProcedure and the output procedure. So the termination the mechanism provides is missing the USING CLOSE, which has already happened, and the difference is observable. Inside the output procedure the USING file's FILE STATUS holds the as-if CLOSE's '00' instead of the at-end '10' left by the as-if READ with AT END. Any CLOSE USE procedure also runs before the output procedure instead of after it. The adjudicator named this timing and sent it to GR7 c). But it is the same event GR9's mechanism is required to perform, so the half of GR9 about what happens on entry and on RETURN is verified and the termination half is not.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB319 LANDED, after kb/Work PB316 (landed). ONE SITE, FULL ANTECEDENT. The rule (cite.py --check 14.9.27.3, both its leading conjunct and its two disjuncts: OK, rule 8) is a syntax rule of the OPEN STATEMENT about file-name-1, which 14.9.27.2's general format defines as that statement's operand; 12.4.5.15.3 has exactly ONE general rule and NO syntax rules, so SR8 is the standard's only source of a LOCK MODE requirement anywhere. It was enforced in TWO places. The second copy, in DataBinder.BindFileControl, fired off the SELECT clause alone and had to DROP the antecedent, because a file control entry sees no OPEN statement and the I-O-CONTROL paragraph is not bound until after it. That copy is DELETED (the extraction IS the fix), leaving StatementValidation.CheckOpenSharingAllOther, called from BindOpen once per file-name, as SR8's only site; its two disjuncts collapse onto the effective sharing mode 'sharing ?? file.Sharing' (14.9.27.4 GR23), which after PB316 is the file's OWN open group's phrase. MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER on this worktree's cobol.exe at --std 2002. sr8ovr.cob (SELECT F1 ... SHARING WITH ALL OTHER, no LOCK MODE, and OPEN OUTPUT SHARING WITH NO OTHER F1) was REJECTED COBOLNET1512 at the SELECT line 6 and now compiles and runs. sr8none.cob (the same SELECT, the file NEVER opened) was REJECTED and now compiles and runs. sr8dup.cob (the same SELECT, plain OPEN OUTPUT F1) drew the SAME rule TWICE in two spellings and now draws exactly ONE diagnostic, from the OPEN. sr8phr.cob (no SHARING clause; OPEN OUTPUT SHARING WITH ALL OTHER F1) is still rejected - disjunct 2 intact. THE LEADING CONJUNCT IS NOW MODELLED AND IS NOT VACUOUS. 'When file-name-1 is not subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause' reads FileModel.SubjectToApplyCommit, set by DataBinder.BindIoControl from the 12.4.6.3 APPLY COMMIT clause. The row's earlier claim that the exemption was harmless because APPLY COMMIT is a parse error does NOT hold: the clause parses and is DECLINED (COBOLNET1709), and that descriptor is PermissiveInert, so under --permissive it is a warning and the program compiles - measured, an APPLY COMMIT file with SHARING WITH ALL OTHER and no LOCK MODE was rejected COBOLNET1512 by BOTH sites at --std 2023 --permissive and now compiles. The exemption is load-bearing rather than decorative: 12.4.5.9.3 SR1 forbids writing a LOCK MODE clause 'for a file that is the subject of an APPLY COMMIT clause', so without it SR8 would demand the one clause another rule forbids. WITNESSES. conformance:2002/pb319_sr8_antecedent pins the antecedent falsified in both compilable ways (a non-ALL sharing phrase on the OPEN; a file never opened) and prints Table 19 statuses - OVR=00, RIV1=61 (row SHARING WITH ALL OTHER / INPUT against column 'sharing with no other' = Unsuccessful open, 9.1.13.9 item 1 a), RIV2=00 after the conflicting connector closes - so a compiler that passed it by IGNORING the sharing phrase would print 00 where 61 is required; it does not compile at all on the pre-fix compiler. conformance:negative/sharing-all-no-lockmode is RE-POINTED: it used to have no OPEN statement anywhere and so pinned the over-rejection as intended behaviour (a green test holding the gap open), and now carries an OPEN with no sharing phrase, which is disjunct 1, with the OPEN-site diagnostic as its .err. conformance:negative/pb316-open-sharing-all-no-lockmode covers disjunct 2. conformance-test:OpenSharingLockModeTests carries the two assertions no .cob corpus can make - that ONE violation draws exactly ONE COBOLNET1512 (a substring-matching .err is blind to a duplicate, which is how the second copy survived), and the APPLY COMMIT exemption with its falsifying control arm (the same program minus the I-O-CONTROL paragraph is still rejected). Design: docs/COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN.md D13. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 / 2014 / 2023 - the SHARING clause, the OPEN sharing phrase and LOCK MODE are Annex A.4.7 items and are gated out at 1985 (COBOLNET0900); Annex E records no 2014-to-2023 change.

notes: kb/Work PB323, LANDED. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 'insufficient authority exists to open the file': OK, 3)): 'If the file associated with file-name-1 is present and insufficient authority exists to open the file, the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, and the I-O status value in the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is set to \'37\''. The status is §9.1.13.6 6) b) (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'insufficient authority exists to access the file': OK) — 'A permanent error exists because an OPEN statement or DELETE FILE statement is attempted on a file and insufficient authority exists to access the file. The ability to detect this is processor dependent.' WAS: every OpenCore decided presence with File.Exists, which swallows every access error and answers false, so a PRESENT-but-refused file classified as ABSENT and never reached the '37' mapping. Probed on a worktree build at 000b6242 (a file under a directory whose DACL denies the running user, icacls /deny :(RX)): non-optional sequential OPEN INPUT = '35'; SELECT OPTIONAL over the same path = '05' — a SUCCESSFUL open — with the first READ reporting AT END '10'; relative and indexed non-optional OPEN INPUT = '35'. NOW: the presence question has ONE site and THREE answers — HostFile.Probe (IO/FileSupport.cs) returns FilePresence.Absent / Present / Unauthorized from File.GetAttributes, whose FAILURES distinguish a missing file (FileNotFoundException / DirectoryNotFoundException → §9.1.13.6 5)'s '35') from a refused one (UnauthorizedAccessException → GR3's '37'); every other IOException propagates so §9.1.13.6 1)'s '30' stays mapped in one place. FileConnector.Open takes that probe ONCE per OPEN, answers GR3 from it, and hands the result to OpenCore(mode, presence), so no organization re-asks the host and no two probes in one statement can disagree. The same probe now serves §14.9.10.4 GR14/GR16 in FileRegistry.DeleteFile, which had carried the only correct copy of the rule since kb/Work PB140 (this row was the OPEN arm of that two-arm dispatch, unfixed for five months). RE-PROBED after the fix on the same denied path: sequential non-optional '37', sequential OPTIONAL '37', relative non-optional '37', indexed non-optional '37'; a genuinely ABSENT file inside the same denied directory still answers '35', so the probe does not over-fire. OUTPUT IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE SHORT-CIRCUIT and that is required, not a convenience: GR18 makes OUTPUT a creation that never consults presence, §9.1.13.6 5) is defined only 'for an OPEN statement with the INPUT, I-O, or EXTEND phrase', and a directory the process may write but not list legitimately accepts a NEW file (measured: create OK, truncate-existing UnauthorizedAccessException) — so a blanket '37' would reject an OPEN OUTPUT the operating environment carries out. An OUTPUT over a present-and-refused file still reaches '37' through the creating stream's own exception and Open's catch. COVERING TESTS: unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests establishes the GR3 precondition for real (a DACL deny ACE on Windows, mode 000 on Unix) and verifies the denial with a raw File.OpenRead rather than with the subject under test — the conformance runner compiles a .cob and compares output with nowhere to express 'first make this file unreadable', so no golden can reach this arm; its GR3 assertions were shown to FAIL (8 of them) with the short-circuit disabled. conformance:2023/pb323_open_presence_arms pins the probe's OTHER two answers — Absent and Present across all three organizations and both OPTIONAL states, expected values derived from §9.1.13.6 5) ('35'), §14.9.27.4 13) + Table 18 ('05' then §9.1.13.4 1)'s at-end '10') and §14.9.27.4 17) (an absent OPTIONAL EXTEND is created, '05') — because a refactor that got Absent wrong would be louder than the defect it fixed. unit:HostFileProbeDriftTests keeps the probe singular: File.Exists, .Exists and File.GetAttributes are banned everywhere under Runtime/IO but FileSupport.cs (it flags all 10 pre-fix sites at 000b6242, including the var-named FileInfo the first draft of its regex missed). || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 — GR3's explicit '37' sentence is the 2023 clarification (Annex E.2 item 18, 'The OPEN statement may return a file status \'37\' for insufficient authority to open a file'), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 determines it is emitted at EVERY edition and not gated, so the rule is adjudicated at all four. notes: RE-DERIVED at kb/Work PB740, because the CONFORMS this row already carried was CONTRADICTED by measurement and its evidence could not have seen it. The row's clause-less witness (conformance:2023/pb321_default_sharing_arbitration) has two legs, OPEN INPUT + OPEN INPUT (permitted) and OPEN INPUT + OPEN OUTPUT (refused BY THE ARBITER, before the operating environment is consulted); both hold the ACCESS axis fixed, so neither is a cell where Table 19 says 'Normal open' and the host handle says no. subject: OPEN statement
notes:
kb/Work PB325 (landed). RULE (--check 14.9.27.4 "'X' at an intersection indicates that the specified statement, used in the access mode given for that row, may be used with the open mode given at the top of the column"): Table 20 licenses each (statement, access mode, open mode) triple; every BLANK cell is an unsuccessful execution whose status 9.1.13.7 names -- item 7 '47' for READ/START not open input or I-O, item 8 '48' for WRITE (a: access sequential and not open extend/output; b: access random or dynamic and not open I-O/output), item 9 '49' for REWRITE/DELETE RECORD not open I-O. Table 20 was read from the PDF (page 709) as well as the transcription, because the load-bearing signal here is a BLANK CELL and the OCR of a blank is not self-evident: Random x WRITE and Dynamic x WRITE carry X under Output and I-O only, and the Extend column of both rows is empty.
IMPLEMENTATION. The ACCESS MODE is the sole branch discriminator and lives in ONE place, KeyedConnector.Access (the abstract base RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector now share); the open mode is only ever the screen that follows. Each connector's Write opens with 'bool sequentialRelease = Access == KeyedAccess.Sequential', takes item 8 a)'s arm when true and item 8 b)'s when false; SequentialConnector.Write carries item 8 a) directly (12.4.5.5.2 SR2 admits only ACCESS SEQUENTIAL for a sequential file); READ/START answer item 7 and REWRITE/DELETE item 9 in both keyed connectors and in SequentialConnector; the blank Random x START row is enforced one level up, at bind, by KeyedIoBinder.BindStart's 14.9.41.3 SR1 screen (COBOLNET0862).
EVIDENCE. conformance:2023/l1_table20_seq_relative and conformance:2023/l1_table20_indexed walk EVERY cell of Table 20 that conforming source can reach -- 4 open modes x {READ, WRITE, REWRITE, START, DELETE RECORD} over sequential, relative and indexed organizations at all three access modes, 139 observations, each expected value derived from Table 20 plus 9.1.13.7 items 7/8/9 and every one observed. conformance:negative/pb325-start-random-access pins the blank Random x START row on BOTH keyed organizations at all four editions. The Random/Dynamic x WRITE x Extend cell is UNREACHABLE from conforming source -- 14.9.27.3 SR2 confines the EXTEND phrase to sequential access -- so it is pinned at the runtime by unit:Table20WriteOpenModeTests, whose four defect facts go RED if the open mode is put back into the branch predicate (measured) while its eight control facts stay green.
WHAT WAS FIXED. RelativeConnector.Write and IndexedConnector.Write selected the branch with '_access == KeyedAccess.Sequential || Mode == FileOpenMode.Extend'; the disjunct routed a random- or dynamic-access connector opened EXTEND into the sequential-release branch, whose own screen accepts extend, so the WRITE appended a record and reported '00' where item 8 b) requires '48'. That made a run-time answer depend on a bind-time syntax rule (SR2) that is enforced nowhere -- kb/Work PB318 -- so the runtime is now correct independently of it.
EDITIONS: Table 20 is version-invariant; the DELETE RECORD row for a sequentially-accessed relative/indexed file and the dynamic access mode ride the relative/indexed I-O modules present at every edition adjudicated here, and the negative fixture was observed rejecting at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: CONFORMS, and RE-DECIDED without a change of verdict (kb/Work PB802, owner decision 2026-09-07 verbatim: 'Let's match GNUCobol's implementation in spirit. No sidecar of any type.'; it supersedes the catalog PB193 landed). GR10's comparison still runs on FileConnector.Open BEFORE OpenCore (GR25 leaves an unsuccessful OPEN's file unaffected and the creation arms truncate), still returns FileStatusCode.FixedAttributeConflict '39' (9.1.13.6 item 7), and both OPEN dispatch arms still reach it (the plain registry Open and the sharing-active SharedOpenAttempt). WHAT CHANGED IS WHERE THE FILE'S ATTRIBUTES COME FROM: there is no catalog and no sidecar of any type (NTFS alternate data streams were considered and rejected with it), so a physical file's 9.1.6 fixed file attributes are whatever ITS OWN BYTES record. THE VALIDATED SET IS THEREFORE A RULE RATHER THAN A TABLE - exactly what each organization's format encodes - realized as three overrides of ONE virtual, FileConnector.FixedAttributeConflict, each beside the format it reads, so an organization added later brings its own answer instead of needing a row in a switch (the hand-kept MediumFixesRecordLayout classification is deleted). (1) Fixed-length record sequential and line sequential encode NOTHING, so nothing is validated - 9.1.7.2 puts those lengths in the data and in the reading program, and 9.1.13.2 items 3, 5 and 7 answer the disagreement with the SUCCESSFUL '04', '06' and '09'; a uniform set was MEASURED WRONG in 2026-08 (six conforming corpus programs red, one into an infinite READ loop). (2) A RECORD VARYING record-sequential file encodes its record type in 9.1.7.2's own 'record length headers' - COBOL.NET's 4-byte little-endian prefix, by the method 12.4.5.11.4 GR5 leaves to the implementor - so a first prefix naming more bytes than the file holds is not a framed file and the declared VARIABLE record type contradicts the medium: '39'. A prefix that PARSES but falls outside the RECORD clause's bounds is NOT a conflict; that is item 3's '04' on the READ, which a '39' at the OPEN would make unreachable (golden step 16 pins exactly that boundary). (3) RELATIVE and INDEXED encode the organization, record type, minimum and maximum logical record size and the key table in the framed store's HEADER, which is IN the data file as GnuCOBOL's ISAM key definitions are; a store with no readable header is '39' (loud) rather than a silent misread, and a zero-byte file is the one tolerated exception. The key check has a documented runtime opt-out, COBOLNET_KEYCHECK=OFF (GnuCOBOL's COB_KEYCHECK), read once per run unit and registered in RuntimeConfig. HONEST COST, PINNED AS A DECISION: PB193's original probe - a RELATIVE file reopened INPUT through a SEQUENTIAL or LINE SEQUENTIAL FD - no longer answers '39' but '00' (golden step 3, with its READ and its comment), because a sequential file's format states nothing for the store to contradict; the reverse direction still answers '39' (golden step 13) and RecordLayoutNotice still reports the byte-count disagreement on stderr. Surveyed, not assumed: GnuCOBOL's testsuite has exactly two status-39 cases, 'variable-length SEQUENTIAL data integrity' and 'INDEXED undeclared keys' with its COB_KEYCHECK=OFF opt-out, and both are reproduced.

MEASURED after, and re-measured 2026-09-22 on the merged entry: 07, 07, 07. notes: kb/Work PB317. RULE: 'If the storage medium for the file permits rewinding, the following rules apply: a) When neither the EXTEND, nor the NO REWIND phrase is specified, execution of the OPEN statement causes the file to be positioned at its beginning. b) When the NO REWIND phrase is specified, execution of the OPEN statement does not cause the file to be repositioned ...' subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB328, LANDED. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode': OK, 16)): 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode. If the file does not support those statements, the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to '37' and the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful. The successful execution of an OPEN statement with the I-O phrase sets the open mode of the file connector referenced by file-name-1 to open in the I-O mode.' TWO halves. HALF 2 (the open mode is set) was already conforming: FileConnector.Open assigns Mode and sets _openMode from the success family. HALF 1 (the '37') was the defect. WAS: the only producer of '37' for a write-incapable file was the shared catch (UnauthorizedAccessException) around OpenCore, which fired for SEQUENTIAL only because that organization's I-O and EXTEND arms open write-capable streams; the relative and indexed I-O arms merely Attach() (a READ of the store), so writability was never probed. Probed on a worktree build at 17c11fd4 with three files created by the compiler and then made read-only (a real host attribute, not a simulation): OPEN I-O answered SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' on the SAME condition; the keyed successes were then believed downstream (READ '00', REWRITE '00') and the loss surfaced only as a '30' at CLOSE on a file whose MD5 was unchanged. The identical omission made OPEN EXTEND answer SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' where 9.1.13.6 6) a) 1. requires '37' (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the EXTEND or OUTPUT phrase is specified but the file will not support write operations': OK, 6) a) 1.); OPEN OUTPUT was already '37' on all three because its keyed arm eagerly calls RecordFraming.WriteStore. NOW: the write-capability question is an OPEN-CONTRACT question, asked ONCE above the organizations. HostFile.PermitsWrite (IO/FileSupport.cs) asks the host for a writable handle (FileMode.Open + FileAccess.Write + FileShare.ReadWrite, nothing written) and answers false only on UnauthorizedAccessException; every other IOException propagates so 9.1.13.6 1)'s '30' stays mapped in the one place. FileConnector.Open calls it for I-O, EXTEND and OUTPUT on a Present file, after GR10's '39' and before OpenCore, so every organization -- including one added later -- inherits the answer instead of re-earning it. GR16 names no organization and Table 20 is why it cannot: REWRITE sits under the I-O column for sequential, random AND dynamic access, so 'supports the statements permitted in the I-O mode' entails write capability whatever the organization. RE-PROBED after the fix on the same three read-only files: OPEN I-O 37/37/37, OPEN EXTEND 37/37/37, OPEN OUTPUT 37/37/37 -- nine cells. OVER-FIRE MEASURED, not assumed: the same read-only files still OPEN INPUT '00' and READ their record on all three organizations (a read-only file supports everything Table 20 permits in the input mode), and a WRITABLE file still opens I-O '00' and rewrites on all three. GR25 ('If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, the file is not affected', cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK, 25)) holds through the probe: content MD5 and last-write time are identical after the refused open. INPUT IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE PROBE and the exclusion is required, not an optimization -- probing write for INPUT would refuse an OPEN the operating environment carries out perfectly, and 9.1.13.6 6) a) 3.'s read-capability question is answered by the organization's own eager read (measured on all three: see GR-9.1.13.6-6). BOTH HALVES OF GR16 ARE COVERED, not just the one that was defective: the rule says the file must support the input AND output statements the I-O mode permits, and Table 20 lists READ under the I-O column beside REWRITE, so a file this process may WRITE but not READ is equally '37'. Measured with icacls /deny :(RD) -- read DATA only, so a raw write open still succeeds and HostFile.PermitsWrite accepts the file -- OPEN I-O answered '37' on sequential, relative and indexed, produced by the organization's own eager read rather than by the write probe; unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests.OpenIo_PresentAndWritableButNotReadable_Is37 asserts the write-probe premise first so the two halves cannot be confused. COVERING TESTS: unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests establishes the precondition for real (a read-only attribute on Windows, mode 0400 on Unix) and verifies it with a RAW write open rather than with the subject under test; its nine GR16 cells were shown to FAIL (7 of them -- the four keyed I-O/EXTEND cells, the two keyed OPTIONAL cells and the GR25 inertness assertion) with the check disabled, and the three sequential cells and three OUTPUT cells stayed green, which is exactly the two-arm fingerprint the defect had. unit:HostFileProbeDriftTests keeps the question singular: PermitsWrite is banned outside FileConnector and its call count in the OPEN contract is pinned at one. No conformance golden can reach this arm -- the corpus runner compiles a .cob and compares its output, with nowhere to express 'and first make this file read-only'. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 -- GR16 is version-invariant and docs/CONFORMANCE.md determines the '37' family is emitted at every edition, ungated.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: RULE: 'Upon successful execution of the OPEN statement, the current volume pointer is set: a) To point to the first or only reel/unit in the physical file if INPUT or I-O is specified. b) To point to the reel/unit containing the last record in the physical file if EXTEND is specified. c) To point to the newly created reel/unit in the physical file for an unavailable file if EXTEND, I-O, or OUTPUT is specified.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 19)). DERIVATION: §9.1.10 (Current volume pointer) states 'The current volume pointer is a CONCEPTUAL ENTITY used in this document to facilitate exact specification of the current physical volume of a sequential file. The status of the current volume pointer is affected by the CLOSE, OPEN, READ, and WRITE statements.' (cite.py --check 9.1.10: OK) — it is not a programmer-visible register and has no COBOL surface. Its only observable consequences are reel/unit swaps (§14.9.30.4 GR23 READ, §14.9.51.4 GR24 WRITE) and CLOSE unit processing (§14.9.6.4 Table 14). COBOL.NET's storage medium is single-unit mass storage, asserted in code at FileRegistry.CloseReelUnit ('CLOSE … REEL/UNIT on a disk medium: a no-op … the file is on a non-reel/unit medium') and CloseNoRewind, so every physical file has exactly ONE reel/unit and arms a), b) and c) all designate that same and only unit whichever mode is specified. There is nothing the rule can require that a single-unit medium does not already satisfy, and no state a program can observe that would disagree. TEST: unit:FileStatusDisciplineTests.CloseReelUnit_AbsentOptional_NoUnitProcessing is the spec-derived test that pins the single-unit medium model (§14.9.6.4 GR6 / §9.1.13.2 6)) this verdict rests on. ⚠ THE PREMISE IS APPLIED INCONSISTENTLY ELSEWHERE: the same non-reel/unit medium that makes GR19 vacuous is what makes GR11's '07' MANDATORY, and that arm is missing (see GR-14.9.27.4-11 and finding open-no-rewind-07-arm-missing). The medium model is also asserted only in code comments — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 33-34 states the opposite ('no reel device'). || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB316 LANDED. GR20's normal form is now the bound tree's shape rather than a property of it: BindOpen flattens the repeated groups into one BoundOpenFile per file-name, in source order, each carrying its OWN group's open mode, sharing-phrase and retry-phrase - which is literally 'a separate OPEN statement ... for each file-name in the same order as specified in the OPEN statement ... each hav[ing] the same open mode specification, the sharing-phrase, retry-phrase, and REWIND phrase as specified in the OPEN statement' (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4, both sentences: OK). The statement node carries NO phrase state at all, so no consumer can re-broaden a phrase's scope; EmitOpen decides its sharing-aware routing per file from that file's own entry, where it previously computed one 'bool shared' for the whole statement. The two leaks the row recorded are gone and both were re-probed on today's tree first: REPRO A (rejects legal source) - 'OPEN OUTPUT SHARING WITH ALL OTHER F1 OUTPUT F2', F2 with neither a SHARING clause nor a LOCK MODE clause, was rejected COBOLNET1512 naming F2 while the same two groups in the other order compiled clean; both orderings now compile, and the complement (the ALL phrase on F2's OWN group) still rejects - conformance:negative/pb316-open-sharing-all-no-lockmode. REPRO B (wrong answer) - a second group's SHARING phrase destroyed the first group's file-control sharing at run time; conformance:2002/pb316_open_group_scope writes that arbitration twice, once as separate OPEN statements and once as one two-group statement, and requires the two to print the same I-O statuses (Table 19, row SHARING WITH ALL OTHER / INPUT against column 'sharing with no other' = Unsuccessful open = '61', 9.1.13.9 item 1). The RETRY phrase is pinned the same way, through its own observable: a file in a phrase-less group is no longer made a sharing participant, so a LATER open arbitrates against the same set it does in the reference form. The row's previously VERIFIED-CONFORMING halves (per-file decomposition in source order; the RESUME NEXT STATEMENT sentence, probe openresume/OPRES01) are untouched. The REWIND-phrase half of GR20's second sentence remains vacuous because the phrase is still discarded - that is kb/Work PB317's GR-14.9.27.4-11/-12, not this row.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB322. 'The SHARING phrase is effective only for files that are shareable.' The predicate 'shareable' is defined by §9.1.15: 'A shared physical file shall reside on a device that allows concurrent access to the file. The implementor shall specify which devices allow concurrent access to a physical file' (cite.py --check 9.1.15 OK). notes: kb/Work PB370. The emitted sequence is exactly the rule's order. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a — the value is placed in the I-O status), then EmitUseHook. Inside the generated __IoCheckEc the body runs: `ExceptionState.SetIo(__ec!, IsFatalIoStatus(__st), ...)` when the name's checking bit is on (b — the level-3 EC-I-O condition associated with the status value, mapped by ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus per §9.1.13.1), then `__EcPerform(__ec!, __f)` consults the installed Format-3 PerformFrame FIRST (c), and only if that returns NoMatch do the F1 file-name / open-mode USE tiers and the outward GLOBAL walk run (d). §14.9.28.4 GR17's 'Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored' is what makes c) exclude d), and the emitter's own comment states it. PROBE (out-b1/probe/open-gr25): OPEN INPUT of an absent non-optional file with a `USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION PROCEDURE ON FN` declarative → the declarative runs and reports status 35, and the file is NOT created (a + d, and 'the file is not affected'); the same OPEN inside `PERFORM ... WHEN EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR ... END-PERFORM` → the WHEN body runs and the declarative does NOT (c), after which the run unit terminates abnormally naming EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR — which is §14.9.28.4 GR20's own tail ('If the exception condition was fatal, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.3'), not a defect. CONFORMS-but-untested: no existing spec-derived test pins the OPEN-specific a-b-c-d ordering (conformance:2023/f3_perform_handler_turn_off_all covers the Format-3 machinery but not through an I-O statement). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, downward to PARTIAL. The rule has a leading requirement and then four ordered actions: 'If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, THE FILE IS NOT AFFECTED and the following actions take place in the following order: a) ... b) ... c) ... d)'. VERIFIED HALF -- the a-b-c-d machinery is right and I could not break it. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a), then EmitUseHook; inside __IoCheckEc the order is SetIo (b), then the F3 PerformFrame via RunTopFrame (c), then, only when no WHEN matched, the F1 file-name and open-mode USE tiers, the F3 __EcDispatch tier and the outward GLOBAL walk (d) -- which is what 14.9.49.4 GR6 requires. I also closed the leg the adjudicator left unexercised: its probe ran a FORMAT 1 USE only, but GR25 d) names 'USE FOR EXCEPTION or USE AFTER EXCEPTION', so I probed a FORMAT 3 declarative (USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR under >>TURN ... CHECKING ON) on an unsuccessful OPEN INPUT: it runs, with FS=35, EXCEPTION-STATUS=EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR and EXCEPTION-FILE=35FN. The 9.1.13.1 status->EC map in ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus matches the standard's list digit for digit. UNVERIFIED-AND-VIOLATED HALF -- 'the file is not affected'. The adjudication tested this in the only direction that cannot lose data (an absent file is not CREATED by a failing OPEN INPUT). I tested the destructive direction and it fails. Connector FA holds po.dat open INPUT under SHARING WITH NO OTHER; connector FB, a plain SELECT on the same physical file, executes OPEN OUTPUT. 9.1.13.9 1) a) and Table 19 (whose 'sharing with no other' existing column is 'Unsuccessful open' in EVERY request row) make that OPEN unsuccessful with status 61, so GR25's own consequent applies and the file shall not be affected. The compiler reports 00 and TRUNCATES po.dat to zero bytes -- the record 'KEEPTHIS01' is gone. That is wrong-answer-with-data-loss on legal source, and it is GR25's own text that is violated, not merely the detection rule's. I checked the counter-hypothesis before charging it: every unsuccessful OPEN the implementation DOES recognise leaves the file intact -- 61 on a sharing-active incoming connector returns before c.Open(mode) is ever called, 41 returns at the top of FileConnector.Open, and 35/37/30 all return before or from the failing stream construction (I confirmed 61 and 41 by probe with the content re-read intact, and the OS-level conflict variant gives 30 with the file intact). So the failure is confined to spec-unsuccessful opens the implementation misclassifies as successful, whose ROOT cause (FileRegistry.Open consults the physical-file table only when the INCOMING connector is sharing-active) is already booked DIVERGES under GR-14.9.27.4-22/-23 -- I am not re-booking that defect, I am recording that GR25's leading clause is therefore unsatisfied and was never measured. If it is any other value, the execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to 47.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to 47' -> OK 14.9.30.4 2). All five READ entries open with the SAME two-part guard: `if (!IsOpen ...) return 47` and `if (Mode is Output or Extend) return 47`, so all four not-input/not-I-O states are covered -- never opened, closed, open OUTPUT, open EXTEND. SequentialConnector.Read splits the guard over two statements plus a third `_reader is null` arm, all three yielding 47; the keyed connectors fold it into one expression. Matches 9.1.13.7 item 7 ('a file connector that is not open in the input or I-O mode'). ADVERSARIAL EDGES CHECKED: (i) after CLOSE the connector is not open -> 47, and the named test asserts exactly that plus that AT END does NOT fire (47 is not the 1x family) and the record area is unchanged; (ii) a governed (sharing-active) READ cannot pre-empt the 47 -- FileRegistry.ReadShared consults SequentialConnector.ReadEligible, which requires IsOpen and Mode input/I-O, so a mode failure keeps its own 47 instead of a premature 51; (iii) an ABSENT OPTIONAL file opened I-O is created and opened, so its first READ is at-end 10 and not 47 (conformance-test:SequentialFileIoSpecTests.OptionalSequential_OpenIoAbsent_Creates05_ThenFirstReadIsAtEnd10). notes: Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "the content of any data item, where any part of that data item lies beyond the range of the current record, is undefined" => OK 3)). The rule imposes NO requirement: it declares the content UNDEFINED, and it is registered as such in Annex A.2 item 41 (Undefined language element list — unlike A.1, A.2 carries no documentation obligation). COBOL.NET makes the choice DETERMINATE: FileConnector.Fit pads/truncates the physical record to the record-area width with SPACES, and SequentialIoEmitter.EmitImageInto stores that full-width image into FileModel.AreaRecord (the LARGEST record description, §13.4.2), so every position past the current record reads as a space. subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB346. RULE (three halves): (i) a record identified for access locked by ANOTHER file connector => the operation's result depends on the presence or absence of the RETRY phrase; (ii) RETRY present => 'additional attempts may be made to read the record as specified in the rules in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase'; (iii) 'The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules for the RETRY phrase.' VALIDATED: `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules for the RETRY phrase"` -> OK 14.9.30.4 9); `--check 14.9.30.4 "If the RETRY phrase is not specified or the record is not successfully accessed as specified by the RETRY phrase, the record operation conflict condition exists"` -> OK 14.9.30.4 9); `--check 14.7.9.3 "the result of the evaluation of arithmetic-expression-1 or arithmetic-expression-2 is negative or zero, the statement is unsuccessful"` -> OK 14.7.9.3 4) a); `--check 9.1.13.8 "an attempt to access a record that is currently locked by another file connector"` -> OK 9.1.13.8 1); `--check 9.1.13.8 "The implementor shall specify under what conditions a deadlock is detected"` -> OK 9.1.13.8 2). IMPLEMENTATION: FileRegistry.ConflictOnLockedRecord is the ONE GR9 conflict check, reached from ReadShared (Format 1, pre-read peek leg on the sequential walk and post-read leg on a keyed walk) and from ReadLockGovern (Format 2), for all three organizations; it contributes only the conflict predicate and the status assignment and delegates BOTH of GR9's second and third sentences to RetryLoop, whose landing goes through ExhaustionStatus. RULE: 'For an indexed file being sequentially accessed, records having the same duplicate value in an alternate record key that is the key of reference are made available in the same order, or, in the case of PREVIOUS, in the reverse order, in which they are released by execution of WRITE statements, or by execution of REWRITE statements that create such duplicate values.' VALIDATED: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "records having the same duplicate value in an alternate record key that is the key of reference are made available in the same order" -> OK 26). WAS DIVERGES: KeyedRec carried ONE Arrival for the whole record and IndexedConnector.Rewrite collapsed its per-key loop into one altChanged bool, so a REWRITE that changed ANY alternate key repositioned the record last in the duplicate set of EVERY alternate key - contrary to 14.9.35.4 GR24 a) ('When the value of a specific alternate record key is not changed, the order of retrieval when that key is the key of reference remains unchanged', --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)). NOW: KeyedRec.Ordinals is a VECTOR - slot 0 the prime key, slot i+1 the i-th alternate; Write stamps one fresh ordinal into every slot (the record is released under every key at once, 14.9.51.4 GR40); Rewrite re-stamps ONLY the keys whose value or SUPPRESS WHEN state actually changed, and the changed test is KeyEq under the key's collating sequence per GR24's closing sentence ('The comparison used for determining changes to the key is based on the collating sequence for the file according to the rules for a relation condition', --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); Ordered(keyIndex) ties on THAT key's ordinal; PersistOrder writes the physical file in a topological order of the per-key duplicate orders so a reload - which can only give every key the file's own order - reproduces all of them. RESIDUE (a NEW, separate defect, not this rule's): the per-key orders can be made mutually CYCLIC by a REWRITE that moves one record into another's duplicate set under key A while both stay duplicates under key B, and no single sequence of record images can then carry both orders across a CLOSE - the physical framing has one order and the model has one per key. PersistOrder appends the cyclic residue in release order, which loses one key's repositioning.

notes: kb/Work PB348 LANDED. RULE (`--check 14.9.32.3 "If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric or national function."` => OK). WHAT WAS ABSENT: nothing screened the function's result class in this position. The FROM phrase of RELEASE, WRITE and REWRITE alike bound its operand through SequentialIoBinder.WriteSource, an unconditional three-way hand-off that INSPECTED NOTHING, so each verb's own phrase rule was applied by no one. WHAT IS THERE NOW: MoveBinder.BindFromPhrase applies the rule from a FromPhraseRules row, ONE PER VERB, because the three verbs name DIFFERENT SETS and a scalar column would reject legal source: RELEASE (14.9.32.3 SR2) and WRITE (14.9.51.3 SR4) admit an alphanumeric or national function, REWRITE (14.9.35.3 SR9, the FILE phrase not specified) also admits a boolean one. The FILE-phrase readings (14.9.51.3 SR10, 14.9.35.3 SR8) are unreachable: the FILE arm is Annex A.4.13 item 2 and is declined COBOLNET1706 earlier. The class is read off the BOUND operand through the SAME Table-16 sender position the category screen uses (MoveBinder.SenderPosition), which is what makes a folded FUNCTION LENGTH -- it reaches the binder as a plain numeric literal -- answer 'numeric' rather than 'unknown'. DIAGNOSTIC COBOLNET1914. MEASURED before: `RELEASE SRT-REC FROM FUNCTION LENGTH(WS-A).` compiled clean at 85, 2002 and 2023 and released R=[8       ]. MEASURED after: refused at every edition, and the WRITE and REWRITE siblings with it. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 . 2014 . 2023

notes: kb/Work PB348 LANDED. RULE (`--check 14.9.32.3 "Identifier-1 or literal-1 shall be valid as a sending operand in a MOVE statement specifying record-name-1 as the receiving operand."` => OK). WHAT WAS ABSENT: the MOVE statement's own screens. They run at BIND time in MoveBinder -- the 14.9.25.3 Table-16 legality arms, the SR1 class-index test, the SR5 figurative edition gates and CheckStrongMove -- and RELEASE reached none of them, because SortBinder.BindRelease only bound the OPERAND and the implicit MOVE was FIRST CONSTRUCTED AT EMIT TIME (`SortEmitter.EmitRelease: move.Emit(new BoundMove(from, [rl.Record]))`), downstream of every one. DECISIVE PAIR, measured: `MOVE WS-NUM TO SRT-REC` (PIC 9(3) into PIC A(8)) drew COBOLNET0819 while the equivalent `RELEASE SRT-REC FROM WS-NUM` compiled clean and printed R=[123     ]. WHAT IS THERE NOW: BindFromPhrase routes the operand through MoveBinder.BindMoveOf -- THE one application of the MOVE statement's rules to a sender/receiver pair, shared with the explicit MOVE statement -- so the same rules reach the phrase by construction rather than by an edit, and the diagnostic names the statement the programmer wrote ('the implicit MOVE of RELEASE ... FROM to SRT-REC (ISO 14.9.32.4 GR4 a); 14.9.32.3 SR3)'). The drift test ImplicitMoveConstructionDriftTests keeps `new BoundMove` out of the I-O and sort emitters. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 . 2002 . 2014 . 2023

It was a missing APPLICATION, not a missing capability: the same BoundStringLiteral { Value.Length: 0 } predicate is applied in ControlFlowBinder (the STOP RUN / GOBACK status literal, COBOLNET1704), IntrinsicBinder, DataBinder.Switches and CallBinder, and the premise was proved rather than assumed -- `STOP RUN WITH ERROR STATUS "".` is rejected, so the compiler both lexes and models "" as a zero-length literal. notes: kb/Work PB349 (landed, wave 56). RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.32.4 'the EC-FLOW-RELEASE exception condition is set to exist' -> OK 14.9.32.4 1)). The sort store now carries the executing statement's procedure PHASE (CobolSort.Store.Phase, set by the emitted EnterProcedure before the INPUT PROCEDURE range and cleared by the sequence phase); the RELEASE STATEMENT renders CobolSort.ReleaseStatement, which raises EC-FLOW-RELEASE through ExceptionState.FlowReleaseError before releasing whenever no store exists for the SD or its phase is not Input. FatalAmbientGates row (EC-FLOW-RELEASE, FlowReleaseChecking) + QueryFor(BoundRelease) give the statement its >>TURN guard, so the condition reaches a USE declarative (14.6.13.1.3 item 5) or terminates (item 7). The implicit USING release keeps the unchecked Release primitive (it is not a RELEASE statement). Checking OFF: nothing is raised (14.6.13.1.1) and the release proceeds, except that a RELEASE with no SORT executing has no store to release to - the 14.6.13.1.3 item 8 implementor choice. Golden pb349_sort_merge_flow_ec: MAIN's RELEASE outside any SORT -> HANDLED=EC-FLOW-RELEASE, the record is not released, and the two RELEASEs inside IN-P raise nothing (negative control).

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: RULE (`--check 14.9.32.4 "The execution of a RELEASE statement causes the record named by record-name-1 to be released to the initial phase of a sort operation."` => OK 14.9.32.4 2). WHAT THE CODE DOES: SortEmitter.EmitRelease renders record-name-1's own character image and calls `CobolSort.Release(sd, image)`, which appends it to that SD's per-file image buffer in release order (CobolSort.cs:77) -- the buffer the SORT's sequence phase then orders and the RETURN phase drains, i.e. exactly the initial phase. The image is a C# string, so the store holds a snapshot: a later mutation of the record area cannot alter an already-released record. THREE LENGTH SHAPES READ AND VERIFIED, all three per 13.18.43.4 GR13 (`--check 13.18.43.4 "During the execution of a RELEASE, REWRITE, or WRITE statement, the number of bytes in the record is determined by the following conditions"` => OK 13.18.43.4 13): (a) fixed SD -- the named record's own width (probe out-b1/probe/base/base.cob returns AAAaaaaa / BBBbbbbb / CCCccccc in key order); (b) RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON -- GR13a's length, emitted as `StrRefMod(image, 1, (int)dep)` (`--check 13.18.43.4 "If data-name-1 is specified, by the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1."` => OK 13.18.43.4 13) a)); (c) GR13c, a variable-occurrence record with no DEPENDING ON in the RECORD clause -- probe out-b1/probe/odo/odo.cob generates `CobolSort.Release("RELODO::SRTF", SRT_REC.AsImage().Substring(0, CobolTable.OdoExtentChars(CobolTable.Occ(WS_OCC), 1, 9, 6, 2, 1)))`, i.e. fixed portion 6 + 2 occurrences x 2 = 10 bytes, not the maximum. COVERING TEST is spec-derived (AssertSpec with expectations computed from the standard, not from the legacy oracle) and cites 14.9.32 GR2 in its own section header. EDITIONS: Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32; the rule is edition-neutral in its own text.

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB322. RULE (`--check 14.9.32.4 "If the number of bytes to be released to the sort operation is greater than the number of bytes in record-name-1, the content of the bytes that extend beyond the end of record-name-1 are undefined."` => OK 14.9.32.4 6). The latitude is explicit: Annex A.2 (Undefined language element list) item 45 repeats the sentence for the RELEASE statement, so any content is conformant PROVIDED the release still happens and the run continues -- a crash or an unsuccessful release would NOT be, because GR6 presumes the over-long release occurs. WHAT THE CODE DOES: the varying arm emits `CobolString.RefMod(image, 1, (int)dep)` where the image is record-name-1's own width; CobolString.RefMod space-extends rather than throwing. PROBE out-b1/probe/gr6/gr6.cob -- `SD SRTF RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 8 TO 20 DEPENDING ON WS-LEN` with `01 SRT-SHORT PIC X(8)` and `01 SRT-LONG PIC X(20)`; the shared area is filled with 20 'L's, WS-LEN is set to 12, and `RELEASE SRT-SHORT` releases 12 bytes from an 8-byte record-name-1. OBSERVED: `RELEASED-OK` then `LEN=0012 R=[LLLLLLLL            ]` -- the first 8 bytes are record-name-1's content and the 4 bytes past its end are spaces. No exception, no truncation of the released length, and the four extension bytes are exactly the ones A.2 item 45 leaves undefined. NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST covers the over-length release, so this row is CONFORMS-but-untested and stays a GAP. EDITIONS: Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32; the rule is edition-neutral in its own text. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — GR6's antecedent -- 'the number of bytes to be released ... greater than the number of bytes in record-name-1' -- has TWO realizations under 13.18.43.4 GR13, and only ONE of them exists in this compiler. VERIFIED (GR13a, DEPENDING ON): the adjudicator's gr6 probe, and my own harder variant probe/ref-gr6/v.cob (RECORD VARYING 8 TO 20 DEPENDING ON WS-LEN with only an 8-byte 01 present, WS-LEN=20) -- 'RELEASED-OK', returned 'LEN=0020 R=[SSSSSSSS]', no exception, the run continues. Conformant, within Annex A.2 item 45. NOT VERIFIED (GR13b + 13.18.43.4 GR5a): with no RECORD clause the implicit clause is implementor-defined, and if format 1 is implied its size is 'the record size of the LARGEST record description entry in this file description entry' (cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 => OK 13.18.43.4 5) a)), which is precisely the fixed-length sort file 14.9.40 GR7 presupposes. In that model releasing a SHORT 01 of a multi-01 SD IS GR6's case. This compiler never produces it: SortBinder.BindRelease releases at record-name-1's OWN description size (SortBinder.cs:238-240 + BoundSort.cs:71). MEASURED at probe/ref-gr6/w.cob -- SD with 01 SRT-SHORT PIC X(4) and 01 SRT-LONG PIC X(10), no RECORD clause -- the sort store ends up holding a 4-byte record and a 10-byte record for ONE SD, and SORT ... GIVING writes a 4-character record into an FD whose 01 OUT-REC is PIC X(10) (output file lines '[AAAA]' and '[ZZZZZZZZZZ]'). That may be legitimate implementor latitude (13.18.43.4 GR5 lets the implementor imply FORMAT 2 instead, min=smallest, max=largest, under which 4 bytes is in range and GR6 is vacuous) -- but the implementation nowhere DECLARES that choice, and 13.18.43.4 GR5 is on the implementor-defined list that 'shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation' (docs/rearchitecture/spec-rule-catalog.json:39386). Worse, the two code comments that justify the choice both cite '14.9.40 GR7c space-fills a short record into a fixed-length sort file' -- and GR7 is a rule about file-name-2, the USING file ('any record in the file referenced by file-name-2 ...'), not about a RELEASE statement in an input procedure. A real clause answering a different question, inherited straight into the GR6 adjudication. CONFORMS asserts conformance in BOTH realizations on evidence from one; PARTIAL is what the evidence supports. Not DIVERGES: nothing measured contradicts GR6 itself -- the release happens, the run continues, and record-name-1's own bytes occupy the leading positions in every over-length case I could build. No test-ref, correctly.

subject: RESUME statement
notes: Rule: 'The RESUME statement may be specified only in a declarative or in an imperative statement in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM statement. In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified.' (cite.py --check 14.9.33.3 'In the latter case, the NEXT STATEMENT phrase shall be specified' -> OK §14.9.33.3 1)). BindResume asks the ONE bind-position probe ctx.Enclosing: InPerformWhen admits NEXT STATEMENT and refuses procedure-name with COBOLNET1610; outside any declarative (ordinary paragraph, imperative-statement-1, FINALLY) it refuses with COBOLNET0712. Both halves verified: the theory PBRS01-05 covers a WHEN phrase, a statement nested inside a WHEN phrase, imp-1 and FINALLY (rejected) and a plain paragraph (rejected), all with SR1-quoted expectations; Resume_AtProcedureNameInAWhenPhrase_IsRejected covers the second sentence; ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.Resume_OutsideDeclaratives_Diagnosed and PerformFormat3Tests' imp-1 case also pin 0712. PROBED in addition: RESUME NEXT STATEMENT in WHEN OTHER and in WHEN COMMON (both WHEN phrases of the general format) is admitted and runs (sr1w.cob -> SIZE / COMMON / END). A RESUME inside a WHEN phrase that is itself inside a declarative is treated under the WHEN branch (NEXT STATEMENT required) - a reading the text supports, since the statement is then 'in a WHEN phrase'.

subject: RESUME statement
notes: kb/Work PB1160 (registrar 14c). Rule: 'The RESUME statement shall not be specified in a declarative procedure for which the GLOBAL phrase is specified in the associated USE statement.' (cite.py --check 14.9.33.3 -> OK §14.9.33.3 2)). The prohibition is flat: it names the declarative procedure, with no exception for a statement nested in it. BindResume tests `where.InPerformWhen` FIRST and returns BoundResume for NEXT STATEMENT before the `decl.Global` test is ever reached, so a RESUME written in a WHEN phrase of an exception-checking PERFORM that sits inside a USE GLOBAL declarative is admitted. PROBED (probe/resume-statement/sr2w.cob): G SECTION. USE GLOBAL AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON F. G1. PERFORM ADD 1 TO N WHEN EC-SIZE RESUME NEXT STATEMENT END-PERFORM. -> compiles clean at 2023; expected COBOLNET0713. The direct case (RESUME as a statement of the GLOBAL declarative) IS refused with COBOLNET0713 and is pinned by ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.Resume_InGlobalDeclarative_Diagnosed and ExitPlacementContextDriftTests.Resume_InADeclarative_FollowsTheGlobalPhrase (PBRS07/PBRS08) - one half verified, the nested half under-rejects, so the row cannot close. The sibling screen PlacementRules.RefusedInGlobalDeclarative (GOBACK/EXIT, PB404/PB409) asks InGlobalDeclarative irrespective of the WHEN frame; RESUME's own arm should ask the same question before its WHEN branch.

subject: RESUME statement
notes: Rule: 'Procedure-name-1 shall be a procedure-name in the nondeclarative portion of the function, method, or program.' (cite.py --check 14.9.33.3 -> OK §14.9.33.3 3)). BindResume resolves procedure-name-1 through the ONE procedure-operand resolution (scoped to the source element, so a name of another program does not resolve) and refuses a target whose SECTION is declarative (target.IsDeclarative, PB433) with COBOLNET0714. PROBED with the pinned cobol.exe: RESUME AT a declarative paragraph (sr3_D2.cob) and RESUME AT the declarative section itself (sr3_D.cob) -> COBOLNET0714; RESUME AT an undeclared name (sr3_X9.cob) -> COBOLNET1639; RESUME AT a nondeclarative paragraph compiles and transfers (gr3b.cob). pb1010_method_declaratives exercises the method arm. No test asserts COBOLNET0714 (searched tests/ for 0714: none), so the row is CONFORMS-but-untested; the needed negative is a declarative RESUME AT one of its own paragraphs.

subject: RESUME statement
notes: kb/Work PB1160 (registrar 14c). Rule: 'If the RESUME statement is executed within the scope of execution of a global declarative, it is the equivalent of the execution of a CONTINUE statement.' (cite.py --check 14.9.33.4 -> OK §14.9.33.4 1)). SR2 forbids RESUME written statically in a GLOBAL declarative, so GR1 is reached DYNAMICALLY: a GLOBAL declarative may PERFORM a procedure of another declarative section (cite.py --check 14.9.49.3 'Procedure-names within a declarative section may be referenced in a different declarative section or in a nondeclarative procedure only with a PERFORM statement' -> OK §14.9.49.3 4)), and a RESUME executed there is within the global declarative's scope of execution, so it shall be a CONTINUE: execution proceeds with the statement after the RESUME. Code: EcEmitter.EmitResume unconditionally emits `throw new ResumeSignal(...)`; the only GR1 realization is EmitRunGlobalUse DISCARDING the resume action after the throw has already unwound the declarative (its comment cites GR1 for that), which ends the declarative instead of continuing it, and the LOCAL tier (a global declarative selected for its own program's statement) does not even discard - it honors the action. The run-time `__useActive[global ids]` test the emitter already has (EmitterState.InGlobalDeclarativeRangeTest, used for EC-FLOW-GLOBAL-GOBACK) is never consulted by EmitResume. PROBED with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/resume-statement): gr1a.cob - G SECTION USE GLOBAL AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON F; G1: DISPLAY 'G-START' PERFORM D DISPLAY 'G-END'; D SECTION USE AFTER ... ON OUTPUT; D1: DISPLAY 'D-START' RESUME NEXT STATEMENT DISPLAY 'D-AFTER-RESUME'; main OPEN INPUT F (missing file) then DISPLAY 'MAIN-AFTER-OPEN ' FS. Expected (GR1): G-START / D-START / D-AFTER-RESUME / G-END / MAIN-AFTER-OPEN 35. Observed: G-START / D-START / MAIN-AFTER-OPEN 35. gr1b.cob (same, with the OPEN in a contained program, so __RunGlobalUse runs G): observed G-START / D-START / INNER-AFTER-OPEN 35 / MAIN-END (expected D-AFTER-RESUME and G-END too). gr1c.cob (gr1a with RESUME AT M2): observed G-START / D-START / M2-JUMPED - a GO TO where GR1 requires CONTINUE. subject: REWRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1193 (registrar 14c). "If record-name-1 is defined in a containing program and is referenced in a contained program, the file description entry for the file associated with record-name-1 shall contain a GLOBAL clause." A GLOBAL FD's records join the GLOBAL roots (DataBinder.Linkage) and its file-name joins the contained program's FilesByName (BinderDriver); a non-GLOBAL FD's records are not visible, so the reference fails resolution. Probe pe.cob (FD F without GLOBAL, contained program does `REWRITE R1`) -> error COBOLNET1639 'R1' is not defined; pf.cob (FD F GLOBAL) compiles and runs. The rule is enforced by the scope mechanism rather than a REWRITE-specific diagnostic; the message cites 8.4.2.1, not this SR. cite.py --check 14.9.35.3 SR3 -> OK. No spec-derived negative fixture for REWRITE. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator's premise is false: it says 'a non-GLOBAL FD's records are not visible, so the reference fails'. But §13.18.27.3 SR1 b) lets a file-section 01 record carry its OWN GLOBAL clause, which makes it a global name even when the FD has no GLOBAL. SR3 exists for exactly that case, and it has no mechanism of its own. REWRITE R1 is rejected only because the compiler silently DROPS the GLOBAL clause on a file-section 01 record (a separate defect): a plain MOVE to that global record in the contained program is also rejected with 'R1 is not defined', although it is legal. So the rejection is an accident of that defect, and the diagnostic gives the wrong reason (§8.4.2.1 undefined name instead of §14.9.35.3 SR3). Fix that defect and SR3 is no longer enforced at all. The simple case (neither the FD nor the record GLOBAL) is correctly rejected, so this is PARTIAL. [editions as adjudicated: 2023; ISO 1989:2023 Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule (E.3.3 item 41 touches GR10 only), so 2014 identically; the 1985/2002 wording is not derivable from the 2023 text]

subject: REWRITE statement
notes: A successful REWRITE releases the record to the operating environment, not to a buffer, and the OBSERVABLE content of that is what ANOTHER file connector over the same physical file then reads: OverwriteInPlace is the ONE in-place overwrite for both sequential framings (the record-sequential GR16/GR20 arm and the line-sequential GR17 arm validate differently and release identically), and it seeks to the record's byte anchor, writes, FLUSHES, and announces the release on the physical file's shared state (NoteRelease -> PhysicalFileTable.State.ReleaseGeneration) so no sibling connector's read-ahead can keep serving the superseded image. The keyed organizations release into the per-physical-file shared record store, which every attached connector sees the instant the mutation happens (kb/Work PB143). MEASURED, both goldens: over 300 records, reader R takes record 1, sibling W rewrites a later record to NEW and reports '00', and R's next reads are OLD then NEW on record-sequential FIXED width, RECORD VARYING, LINE SEQUENTIAL (2023 only), a CLAUSE-LESS pair, RELATIVE and INDEXED. The SHARING WITH ALL OTHER legs close W before R reads on, which is the reported shape; the CLAUSE-LESS leg instead re-fills R's read-ahead AFTER W's OPEN and reads with W STILL OPEN, because a change in the 9.1.15 union repostures - and therefore rebuilds and empties - the other connectors' handles, which for the undetermined-default spelling would hide the defect (measured: with the coherence rule injected out, that leg still printed NEW while the three ALL OTHER legs printed OLD). Before kb/Work PB753 the four sequential legs all read OLD while the physical file held NEW, with '00' from every statement. COBOL-85 has no file sharing, so the sibling observation cannot be made there; the release itself is the same code on every edition.

subject: REWRITE statement
notes: Rule: previous I-O statement on the connector must be a successfully executed READ, else '43'; a successful REWRITE replaces the record the READ accessed. cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 5). Probe probe/rewrite-statement-p2/p1.cob: indexed ACCESS SEQUENTIAL REWRITE with no READ -> NOREAD=43; second REWRITE after a successful one -> TWICE=43; relative ACCESS SEQUENTIAL no READ -> RQNOREAD=43, after READ -> RQOK=00, again -> RQTWICE=43. Replacement half: p2.cob sequential REWRITE read-back BACK lines show the READ's record replaced in place. Dynamic/random access correctly skip the gate (p1 DYNNOREAD=00). file_sharing_seq (2002) pins the '43' after an unsuccessful READ for the sequential organization; the relative/indexed arms are probe-verified only. Ordering note: IndexedConnector checks GR20 '44' before '43' while RelativeConnector checks '43' first; the spec states no precedence between them, so not a divergence. notes: kb/Work PB1168 (registrar 14c). notes: kb/Work PB702 (the row PB341 made true and did not claim). RULE — all six obligations of GR24, each re-derived on this tree, never inherited: (a) 'When the value of a specific alternate record key is not changed, the order of retrieval when that key is the key of reference remains unchanged' (cite.py --check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (b) 'When the value of a specific alternate record key is changed … the record is logically positioned last within the set of duplicate records where the alternate record key value is equal to the same alternate key value in one or more records in the file based on the collating sequence for the file' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (c) the FIRST SUPPRESS WHEN sub-rule, 'If the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase is specified in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause and the value of the alternate record key is no longer equal to the literal specified in that phrase: 1. an access path to this record using this key of reference shall be provided, and 2. the record shall be logically positioned so that it will be found when accessed using the alternate record key' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (d) the SECOND SUPPRESS WHEN sub-rule, 'If alternate record key suppression is specified for this alternate record key and the value of this alternate record key is now equal to its key suppression value: 1. the access path to the record using this alternate record key shall no longer be provided, and 2. the record shall be logically repositioned so that it will not be found when accessed using this alternate record key' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (e) 'The comparison used for determining changes to the key is based on the collating sequence for the file according to the rules for a relation condition' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)); (f) 'Any number of records may have the same alternate key value equal to its key suppression value without requiring the DUPLICATES phrase to be specified for that key. Key entries that are suppressed shall not cause a duplicate key condition to exist' (--check 14.9.35.4 -> OK 24)). CODE: IndexedConnector.Rewrite runs TWO passes over _alts and the order is load-bearing — pass 1 validates only (an early '22' must leave nothing repositioned), pass 2 applies GR24 while target.Image is still the REPLACED record so AltChanged compares against it. (a)/(b): the local AltChanged(i) is the ONE definition of 'this REWRITE changed alternate key i', and only the keys it answers true for take a fresh release ordinal off the monotone mint (Stamp(target, i, repositioned)), so an untouched key keeps its ordinal and Ordered(i) keeps its order, while a changed key sorts after every existing member of its new duplicate set. (e): AltChanged is KeyEq, the file's collating sequence, not an ordinal string compare. (c)/(d): AltChanged also returns true when IsSuppressed(image, i) != IsSuppressed(target.Image, i), so entering OR leaving suppression is a change of its own and re-stamps the key; the access path itself is Ordered(keyIndex)'s Where(r => !IsSuppressed(r.Image, keyIndex)) (12.4.5.6.4 GR6), which withdraws and restores the path from the key VALUE with no separate state to drift. (f): pass 1 does `if (IsSuppressed(image, i)) continue;` before the uniqueness test and also excludes suppressed records from the `exists` scan, so a suppressed entry can neither raise '22' on a non-DUPLICATES key nor be duplicated by one. MEASURED on this worktree's build (c34f01ad + this change) by conformance:2023/l1_rewrite_alt_key_suppress, whose 20 expected lines were WRITTEN FROM THE SPEC BEFORE THE FIRST RUN and matched byte for byte: leg B REWRITEs record 01's R-A1 to the suppression value 'XX' and the R-A1 walk drops from 01,03,02 to 03,02 at status '00' (d); leg C REWRITEs it back to 'AA' and the walk becomes 03,01,02 — the access path is restored (c 1.) and 01, which was FIRST in the AA set on release, comes back LAST (c 2. + b), with the REWRITE itself reporting '02' per 9.1.13.2 2 c); leg D REWRITEs two records to 'ZZ', the suppression value of an alternate key with NO DUPLICATES phrase, and both report '00' rather than the '22' a real duplicate would raise, after which the R-A2 walk finds only the one unsuppressed record (f); leg E re-walks after CLOSE/OPEN and both the restored position and the two withdrawn paths survive the physical file. conformance:2023/l1_rewrite_alt_key_order (kb/Work PB341) independently pins (a), (b) and (e) on two DUPLICATES alternate keys without suppression. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 for (a), (b) and (e) — ALTERNATE RECORD KEY and its DUPLICATES phrase are ungated in this compiler (no constructs.json row), the clause carries no edition marker, and Annex E lists no change to 14.9.35; this matches the band the sibling rows GR-14.9.30.4-26 and GR-14.9.30.4-32 were landed at on the same golden. Sub-rules (c), (d) and (f) are 2023-ONLY: they exist only where SUPPRESS WHEN is writable, and SUPPRESS WHEN is a COBOL-2023 addition (cite.py --check E.3.3 'The SUPPRESS WHEN phrase may be specified as part of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause' -> OK, item 42), gated by constructs.json row 'alternate-key-suppress-when-2023' (COBOLNET0900 below 2023) — so the 2023 golden is the only edition at which they CAN be measured, and they are vacuous, not unverified, at 85/2002/2014.

notes: kb/Work PB451 — WAS PARTIAL on a REFUTED reading; the refutation is itself refuted here, from the standard, and the row CLOSES. Rule: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "if the SET statement is contained in a method within the factory definition of the class, that factory definition shall be described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-1"` -> OK 10) (SR10 d)1.). THE INTERPRETIVE QUESTION, DECIDED FROM THE SPEC: is 'described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-1' a LITERAL claim about the clause's operand list, or the standard's prose for the SS11.4.4 GR2 relation? It is the relation, on four independent grounds. (1) SS11.4.4 GR1: 'The IMPLEMENTS clause specifies the names of the interfaces that are implemented by the factory object of the containing class ACCORDING TO 9.3.11, Interface implementation' - the clause is defined in terms of implementation, not the reverse. (2) SS9.3.8.2.3 rule 5 b)2.a. states the SAME obligation about the SAME objects with the OTHER phrasing: 'if described with the FACTORY phrase, the factory object of the specified class shall be described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references int-r', where SET SR10 b)1. writes 'the factory object of the specified class shall implement int-1'. Two phrasings, one rule. (3) Annex D (SS D.19.5) paraphrases SS13.18.60.4 GR22 c) - normatively 'the object referenced by this data item shall IMPLEMENT interface-1' - as 'the data item can only be used to reference an object DESCRIBED WITH AN IMPLEMENTS CLAUSE THAT REFERENCES the interface specified': the standard glosses its own rule with the other spelling. (4) The reductio: under the literal reading, in a subclass whose own definition carries no IMPLEMENTS clause, `SET R TO SELF` would be illegal while `SET T TO SELF` (T typed at the containing class) followed by `SET R TO T` is legal under SR10 b)2. - identical semantics, one statement apart. MEASURED (pb451_set_format5_self_sender): the FMK method's `SET JR TO SELF` exercises GR2 a)+b) (FACTORY IMPLEMENTS PB451K, which INHERITS PB451J, the receiver's int-1) -> FPING-P; PB451Q's QFMK exercises GR2 c) (PB451Q's FACTORY carries NO IMPLEMENTS clause at all; only its base's does) -> FPING-Q. The REFUSING arm is pinned for the first time by pb451-self-sender-factory-not-implements, whose discriminator is the factory/instance axis - the INSTANCE definition implements the interface and the FACTORY definition does not, so a screen keyed on the wrong definition accepts it. || CODE SITE: OoBinder.OoBindSetObjectRef, the SELF arm's ObjectRefKind.Interface case -> OoClassTable.ImplementsClosure(cur, host.OoInFactory), which is exactly SS11.4.4 GR2 a)+b)+c).
