A period may be missing at the end of the previous sentence.` - a bare syntax error with a misleading hint, not a named refusal. With no restricted data-pointer declarable, identifier-9 can never be 'a data-pointer restricted to a type described with the STRONG phrase' and the rule has no input.

I CHECKED THE COMPLEMENT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT: the omission is in the USAGE grammar, not in a binder screen, so it is invisible to the dossier's 14.9.39 citation regex and to its 'SET' keyword derivation - neither the grammar block nor the source block returns CobolData.g4:445. `grep -n "POINTER (TO\|POINTER TO" src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4` returns only the PROGRAM-POINTER and FUNCTION-POINTER rules.

HARM: rejects legal COBOL-2002+ with an unnamed COBOL0307, which is worse than the 0899 staged-loud posture PROGRAM-POINTER TO and FUNCTION-POINTER TO get for the same shape - three sibling usages, two of them refused by name and one by a parse error.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:445 - usageKeyword's alternative is the bare token `POINTER`, with no `(TO cobolWord)?` tail (contrast programPointerUsage at :455 and functionPointerUsage at :461, which both carry one). PicInfo.PointerItem (src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs:314-316) is a singleton with no restriction field, so the model cannot represent a restricted data-pointer either. No STRONG-phrase test appears anywhere in the SET path.

notes: kb/Work/PB464.md — Citations validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "the length of data-name-3 is set to 0 and an EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL exception condition is set to exist" -> OK (General rules 37) and "the result of arithmetic-expression-5 is truncated to the nearest integer" -> OK (same rule). THE RULE IS TWO SENTENCES AND ONLY THE FIRST IS SETTLED. Sentence 1 (not a nonnegative number -> length 0 + EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL) is implemented at CobolDynString.cs:53-57 and is closed by a spec-derived golden: tests/conformance/2023/ec_storage_not_avail.cob drives WS-FRAC = -0.5 and WS-NEG = -1 under '>>TURN EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL CHECKING ON' and pins 'FRAC LEN=00 EC[EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL...]' / 'NEG LEN=00 EC[...]' plus an in-range negative control that raises nothing -- and the fractional-negative case is the one that proves the ORDER is right (the sign test is on the evaluated value at full precision, before truncation, which is why SetEmitter.cs:119 renders the amount as a double rather than casting to long in generated code). Gating the raise on checkStorage is CORRECT, not a shortcut: 14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3 (re-derived -- cite.py --check 14.6.13.1 FAILED and --find placed it at 14.6.13.1.1) says 'An exception condition is set to exist only if checking for that condition is enabled by default or by the TURN compiler directive.' SENTENCE 2 IS THE UNVERIFIED EDGE. The standard's words are internally in tension -- 'truncated to the NEAREST integer' -- and this is the phrase's ONLY occurrence in the whole document (grep of specs/ISO_COBOL.md), so there is no sibling use to calibrate it against. The code picks toward-zero truncation ((long)newLen at :65). MEASURED at --std 2023 (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set-p5/gr37-nearest): with LIMIT 9 and a nine-character value, WS-A = 2.7 gives L(2.7)=02 and WS-B = 2.2 gives L(2.2)=02 -- so 2.7 truncates DOWN, where a 'nearest integer' reading would give 3. Toward-zero is the defensible reading (the operative verb is 'truncated', and the negative half of the domain is already consumed by sentence 1 so toward-zero and floor coincide here), but it is a CHOICE: there is no determination for it in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (whose only SET SIZE determination covers GR38's third sentence) and no test drives a fractional POSITIVE amount -- ec_storage_not_avail.cob's fractional case is -0.5, which sentence 1 catches before sentence 2 is reached. PARTIAL on the strict reading: two halves, one verified. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a determination line beside the existing GR38 one, plus a positive-fraction row in the ec_storage/set_size golden.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs:402 BindSetSize (explicit SIZE OF) and :421 DynTrySetSize (the SIZE-OF-absent bare re-route) -> BoundSetSize -> src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/SetEmitter.cs:112 EmitSetSize -> src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Roslyn/RuntimeApi.cs:148 DynSetSize -> src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Text/CobolDynString.cs:49 SetSize -- the negative leg at CobolDynString.cs:53-57 (n = 0 plus the nonfatal EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL under checkStorage), the non-integer leg at :65 ((long)newLen).  || EDITIONS (verbatim from the adjudication): 2023 only (READ, not inferred: Annex E.3.3 item 17 -- 'Dynamic-length elementary items. The SET statement was enhanced to allow the setting of the length of a dynamic-length elementary item.' -- cite.py --find -> E.3.3 17). The 2023 introduction gate is enforced on the BoundSetSize node (src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ConstructRegistry.g.cs:28 set-dyn-length-size-2023 -> COBOLNET0900), so the 85/2002/2014 compilers refuse it by name, which is right.

notes: kb/Work PB463 LANDED - ALL THREE OF GR38'S LEGS, AND THE MAXIMUM SIZE THEY ARE ALL STATED AGAINST. Citations re-checked on this tree: cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "If integer-2 is specified, the length of data-name-3 is set to integer-2" -> OK (General rules 38); "If the amount of storage required to expand the size of data-name-3 is not available, the size of data-name-3 is not changed" -> OK (same rule); cite.py --check 8.5.1.10.1 "The maximum size of a dynamic-length elementary item is smallest of:" -> OK (General); cite.py --check 13.18.19.4 "If the LIMIT phrase is not specified, the maximum number of characters that can be contained by the subject of the entry is implementor-defined." -> OK (General rules 2). WHAT WAS WRONG: every leg of GR38 is stated against "the maximum size of data-name-3", and for an item written WITHOUT a LIMIT phrase this compiler had no such thing. DataItem.DynLengthLimit was the LIMIT phrase with -1 meaning "no phrase", CobolDynString.SetSize's clamp was guarded by `limit >= 0`, and so an unbounded item skipped the clamp and fell into two UNCHECKED long->int narrowings. MEASURED on this worktree's own build before the fix, at --std 2023 with EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL CHECKING ON: `01 WS-D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH.` with SET SIZE OF WS-D TO 4294967306 (= 2**32 + 10) printed LEN=000000000010 and 31 spaces for FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS - a ten-character item nobody asked for, exit 0 - and the same declaration with 3000000000 (> int.MaxValue, < 2**32) narrowed NEGATIVE and threw System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException out of _PRG_...__Dispatch. WHAT LANDED: 8.5.1.10.1's "smallest of" is now a real computation in ONE place, CobolDynString.MaxSizeOf(Int128?) - the LIMIT phrase read WIDE (so a literal past int is compared at its written value instead of being dropped by an int.TryParse that left the item unbounded) bounded by CobolDynString.MaxLength = 0x3FFFFFDF, the implementor maximum (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 row DOC-A.1-62; the PREFIXED candidate cannot apply because a dynamic-length-structure-name is refused by COBOLNET1562). DataItem.DynMaxSize carries it to every emitter and defaults to the implementor maximum, so no site can see "no maximum". With that, leg 2 (clamp to the maximum + EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL) is the ONE path for an over-large request - both probes now print LEN=001073741791 EC[EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL] - and the (int) narrowings are exact by construction rather than by inspection. LEG 3 IS IMPLEMENTED RATHER THAN DECLARED UNREACHABLE: the maximum is the carrier's ceiling, not a promise the host can allocate two gigabytes, so an OutOfMemoryException at the growth site returns the item UNCHANGED with the condition set to exist (raised once per statement - a request that already took the clamp leg has set it). Leg 1 (integer-2 -> that length) is unchanged and still pinned by 2023/set_size. The section 7 determination that used to read "always allocatable ... the branch is unreachable ... that third leg never raises" has been rewritten to what the code does; audit_annex_a1.py --check reports no findings.

Both procedure phrases are `(INPUT|OUTPUT) PROCEDURE IS? procedureName ((THRU | THROUGH) procedureName)?` — one alternative, one parse node, and SortRange reads procedureName()[1] without looking at which token was written, so the two spellings cannot bind differently. PROBE fmt1.cob --std 2023: `INPUT PROCEDURE IS IP-1 THROUGH IP-2` + `OUTPUT PROCEDURE OP-1 THRU OP-2` ran and returned R7r,Q5q (both input paragraphs executed; the THRU output range reached OP-2's RETURN loop). conformance:2023/pb440_sort_procedure_range exercises only the THRU spelling, so it does not witness the equivalence; test-ref left empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Format 1).]

subject: SORT statement

(ISO §14.9.40.3 SR8)` -> COBOLNET1757; PROBES s8usd (USING SW2, an SD) and s8gsd (GIVING SW2) rc 70 COBOLNET1757 — conforms. subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB994 (registrar 14c). cite.py --check 14.9.40.3 "the first specification of data-name-1 shall be associated with an ASCENDING phrase" OK (SR9). No code screens the first key's direction or its byte location/length against an indexed GIVING file's prime RECORD KEY. The rule is currently UNREACHABLE only because SortMapIoFiles refuses every non-sequential USING/GIVING file (COBOLNET1757 'the G5 keyed slice'): PROBE s9idxg `SORT SW ASCENDING SK USING OU1 GIVING KFL` (KFL INDEXED, RECORD KEY RK at the same bytes as SK — a CONFORMING program) -> rc 70 COBOLNET1757. So today every indexed GIVING, legal or not, is refused; the legal half is kb/Work PB994's harm (open, rejects-legal-source), but PB994's inventory_rows are GR-14.9.40.4-15 and SR-14.9.40.3-12 only and its title does not mention SR9 — when PB994 lifts the blanket refusal, SR9 must land in the same change or DESCENDING-first / misaligned keys will be accepted. See findings. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Format 1; no Annex E change recorded).]

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB1139 (registrar 14c). cite.py --check 14.9.40.3 "No pair of file-names in the same SORT statement may be specified in the same SAME SORT AREA or SAME SORT-MERGE AREA clause" OK and "File-names associated with the GIVING phrase shall not be specified in the same SAME AREA clause" OK (SR10). subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB1055 (registrar 14c). cite.py --check 14.9.40.3 "Data-name-2 shall have an OCCURS clause in its data description entry. Subscripting shall be specified in accordance with 8.4.2.3, Subscripts" OK (SR13); §8.4.2.3.3 5) e) "As the subject of a SORT statement that references a table" OK and 6) "This is equivalent to omitting the rightmost or only subscript in this context" OK. Two halves. (1) OCCURS required: SortBindTable resolves the written reference (ReferenceResolver.ResolveTableOperand) and `table?.Occurs is null` -> COBOLNET1757 naming SR13 — probe t13plain (`SORT PLAIN ASCENDING PLAIN`, no OCCURS) rc 70; control t13ok rc 0 and ran (TK 3,1,2 -> 123). (2) subscripting per §8.4.2.3: the single-level forms conform — t13ok (unsubscripted) and t13all (`SORT TE(ALL)`, SR6's equivalent of omission) both ran -> 123. But a data-name-2 nested under another OCCURS, which §8.4.2.3 requires to be subscripted for its outer dimension, is DEFERRED: SortArrayPath returns null for any OCCURS ancestor and the binder emits BoundUnsupported -> COBOLNET1756 warning + run-time abort — probe t13nestsub (`SORT E(2) ASCENDING EK`, E OCCURS 3 under ROW OCCURS 2) rc 0 with the warning; t13nestall (`SORT E(2, ALL)`) compiled and ABORTED at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException. This half is OWNED by kb/Work PB1055 (open, inventory_rows [SR-14.9.40.3-13]) — not re-reported. Edge left unadjudicated: t13nestnosub (`SORT E` with its outer subscript OMITTED — too few subscripts for §8.4.2.3.3 SR3/SR5e) gets the same deferral warning instead of a rejection, so the illegal and legal nested spellings are indistinguishable today (noted for PB1055's fixer); t13oversub (`SORT TE(1)`, a full-count subscript on a one-level table) compiles and sorts the whole table — whether that reference is legal is not settled by SR5e's text, so no verdict is drawn on it. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (Format 2 is a 2002 introduction; gated table-sort-2002 COBOLNET0870).]

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB1173 (registrar 14c). cite.py --check 14.9.40.3 OK for a) "The data item identified by a key data-name shall be the same as, or subordinate to, the data item referenced by data-name-2", b) "Key data names shall not be subscripted", c) "Key data items shall not be of class boolean, object, or pointer", d) "A key data item shall not reference a variable-length group or an occurs-depending group item". Five arms, measured --std 2023 over SortBindTable: a) CONFORMS — SubtreeCandidates(table, base, quals) + COBOLNET1757 'SR14a'; probe t14a (`SORT TE ASCENDING OTHER-K`) rc 70. b) DIVERGES — the key reference is reduced to DataBinder.KeyReference (base name + qualifiers) and any subscript is DROPPED without a diagnostic: probe t14b `SORT TE ASCENDING TK(1)` rc 0 and ran -> 123, identical to the unsubscripted key. c) DIVERGES — no class screen: probe t14cbool (`SORT TE ASCENDING TB`, TB PIC 1 USAGE BIT, class boolean) rc 0. d) DIVERGES — probe t14vg (`SORT VE ASCENDING VG`, VG a group whose only child is `VD PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH` — a variable-length group per §8.5.1.12.1, cite OK) rc 0. (Control: t14d, a dynamic-length ELEMENTARY key, rc 0 — correct, SR14 d) names only groups.) e) CONFORMS on the explicit-key path — KeyUnderInnerOccurs -> COBOLNET1757 quoting SR14 e); probe t14e (`SORT TE ASCENDING TIN`, TIN OCCURS 2 under TE) rc 70. On the GR21 path (KEY phrase omitted, keys from the table's OCCURS KEY phrase) an unbuildable key still returns TableSortKeyUnsupported (a deferral), the conflation kb/Work PB599 (open) owns; PB996 (open) owns that message's stale 'SR14e' cite. Harms: under-rejects (b, c, d); b) also silently ignores the written subscript. See findings. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (Format 2). The d) variable-length-group arm applies from 2014 (dynamic-length items / dynamic-capacity tables).]

subject: SORT statement
notes: Rule: 'The words ASCENDING and DESCENDING are transitive across all occurrences of data-name-1 until another word ASCENDING or DESCENDING is encountered.' (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR1). The general format braces {ASCENDING|DESCENDING} inside each repeated key phrase, so every phrase opens with its own direction word; both binders apply `phrase.DESCENDING() is not null` to every data-name of that phrase's dataReferenceList, which is exactly GR1. Spec-pinned test: 'ON ASCENDING KEY S-K1 ON DESCENDING KEY S-K2 S-K3' -> S-K3 descends too (R=1BB5R1 before R=1BB2R4). Table arm: pb846 leg X (conformance:2002/pb846_sort_table_occurs_keys). [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (file format); 2002, 2014, 2023 (table format); no 2014->2023 change in Annex E]

subject: SORT statement
notes: Rule: 'The data items referenced by the specifications of data-name-1 are the key data items ... The order of significance of the keys is the order in which they are specified in the SORT statement, without regard to their association with ASCENDING or DESCENDING phrases.' (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR2). Keys are appended in statement order (file: List<BoundSortMergeKey>; table: List<BoundTableSortKey>), and both comparators walk the list first-to-last returning on the first non-zero result. The spec-pinned test orders S-K1 (ASC, first phrase) above S-K2/S-K3 (DESC, second phrase): R=2AA3R3 last. Table arm: conformance:2002/pb846_sort_table_occurs_keys leg X (KA major, KB minor across two phrases). Both halves (file order of return, table storage order) verified. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (file format); 2002, 2014, 2023 (table format)]

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB704 (2026-09-06): the phrase that BUYS this rule was unusable above COBOL-85 until this landing - ORDER is the format's own optional word (measured: on the printed page only DUPLICATES is underlined) but the grammar spelled it as a `cobolWord`, and the 8.9 funnel, which screens IDENTIFIER occurrences position-blind, refused it as a user-defined word from 2002 (8.9 reserves ORDER since 2002). ORDER is now a lexer token with a cobol-words.json nameSlot row, so the phrase parses at every edition and `01 ORDER PIC X.` still draws COBOLNET0901 at 2002+ (conformance:negative/pb704-order-as-data-name). All three arms are evidenced: a) the USING-file order and, within a file, the access order; b) the input procedure's RELEASE order; c) the table elements' pre-sort relative order. Both formats realize it as an unconditional STABLE sort - CobolSort.Sort ties on the buffer index (Format 1) and EmitTableSort emits a stable comparer (Format 2) - so GR4's undefined order is safely refined to the same one. Arm c) needs Format 2, which is 2002+; arms a) and b) hold at 85.

subject: SORT statement
notes: Rule: 'If the DUPLICATES phrase is not specified and the contents of all the key data items ... are equal ..., the order of return of these records or the relative order of the contents of these table elements is undefined.' (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR4; also listed as undefined item 52 in Annex B). CobolSort.Sort breaks ties by release index (stable) and CobolTable.Sorted uses stable OrderBy regardless of the phrase; any order satisfies 'undefined', so the stable refinement conforms. Nothing observable to pin with a spec-derived expected value (the rule defines no result), hence no test-ref. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (records); 2002, 2014, 2023 (table elements)]

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB678 (2026-09-05): the TWO sequences GR5 determines separately are now resolved as a pair (SortCollation) and selected per key by the key's CLASS through the one classifier CollatingSelection.Of - alphabet-name-1 (GR5a) or the alphanumeric program collating sequence (GR5b) for keys of class alphabetic and alphanumeric, alphabet-name-2 (GR5a) or the national program collating sequence (GR5b) for keys of class national, and NO sequence for the two classes GR5 names neither of (numeric, boolean). Both formats take the same selection: the Format-1 file sort carries the class on its runtime key descriptor (CobolSort.KeyClass) and the Format-2 table sort chooses the comparer's carrier argument. Before this the statement carried ONE sequence, the alphanumeric weights were applied to a national key's UTF-16BE record bytes, and the table-sort form staged loud on recognition. Below 2002 the national half is unreachable (alphabet-name-2 and the FOR forms draw COBOLNET0872 - the negative case), so the alphanumeric half is what conforms at 85.

subject: SORT statement
notes: Rule: 'Additional rules affecting the execution of the SORT statement are given in 12.4.5, File control entry, General rules 3 and 4.' (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR6). 12.4.5.3 GR3: 'The association occurs at the time of execution of an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement that referenced file-name-1' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 OK). Code: every implicit USING/GIVING OPEN renders seqIo.ExecutingElementArgs(file) -- the literal ASSIGN target (GR3 a) or the CURRENT content of the ASSIGN USING data item (GR3 b) evaluated at the SORT. PROBE out/probe/sort-statement-p2/passign.cob: ASSIGN USING FI-NAME / FO-NAME, names changed to passign-in2.dat / passign-out2.dat before the SORT; the SORT read passign-in2.dat and wrote passign-out2.dat (OUT=AAA, OUT=BBB), and no -in1/-out1 file was created. GR4's content/consistency rules are implementor-defined. The 'association cannot be made -> SORT unsuccessful' arm is the implicit OPEN's status path (pb714/pb837 goldens). No golden witnesses ASSIGN USING through a SORT (pb673_external_assign_executor exercises OPEN only), so test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the ASSIGN USING form of 12.4.5.3 GR3 b is a 2002 addition)]

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB1140 (registrar 14c). Rule: a record of file-name-2 shorter than a fixed-length file-name-1 'is space filled on the right to that fixed length ... when that record is released to the file referenced by file-name-1, as follows: a) If there is only one record description entry associated with the file referenced by file-name-2 and that record is described as a national data item or as an elementary data item of usage national and of category numeric, numeric-edited, or boolean, the record is filled with national space characters. b) [SELECT WHEN] ... c) Otherwise, the record is space filled with alphanumeric space characters.' (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR7 and GR7 a). Code: the fixed-SD arm of EmitInputFile releases RuntimeApi.StrStore(tmp, sdWidth) -- CobolString.Store's default pad ' ' -- whatever file-name-2's record description is; no national arm exists. PROBE out/probe/sort-statement-p2/pfill.cob: FD FN with ONE record 01 FN-REC PIC N(2) (4 bytes), SD SN 01 SN-REC (SN-K PIC N(2), SN-T PIC N(1), 6 bytes), SORT SN ... USING FN OUTPUT PROCEDURE; FUNCTION ORD(SN-T) of every returned record = 8225 (U+2020, the two alphanumeric 0x20 bytes read as one national position). Spec-derived expected (GR7 a): SN-T = the national space, ORD = 33. Arm c) verified: FA (01 FA-REC PIC X(3)) into SA (X(6)) -> SA-T = SPACES. Arm b) is unreachable: SELECT WHEN is declined (A.4.8 Not claimed, COBOLNET1705, derived selector format-select-when-only). [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the c) alphanumeric fill); a)/b) national arms 2002, 2014, 2023]

subject: SORT statement
notes: Rule: 'To determine the relative order in which two records are returned from the file referenced by file-name-1, the contents of corresponding key data items are compared according to the rules for comparison of operands in a relation condition, starting with the most significant key data item.' a) ASC lower first, b) DESC higher first, c) equal -> next key (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR8). KeyColumns dispatches on the key's class: numeric -> algebraic via the leaf's own NumProfile (8.8.4.2.4, incl. IEEE float and unsigned 128-bit lanes), national -> decoded national positions under the GR5 national sequence (8.8.4.2.9), boolean -> no sequence (8.8.4.2.8), alphanumeric/group -> byte window under the GR5 alphanumeric sequence (8.8.4.2.7); Compare walks keys in significance order and negates for DESCENDING. a/b/c all pinned by the spec-pinned multi-key test; algebraic numeric by conformance-test:SortMergeDifferentialTests.Sort_SignedNumericKeys_CompareAlgebraically; national by conformance:2023/pb678_sort_national_key_collating; float by conformance:2023/pb164_float_sort_key. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023]

subject: SORT statement
notes: Rule: 'If an input procedure is specified, control is passed to the input procedure before the file referenced by file-name-1 is sequenced by the SORT statement. The compiler inserts a return mechanism after the last statement in the input procedure. When control passes to that return mechanism, the records that have been released ... are sorted.' subject: SORT statement
notes: Rule: 'If an output procedure is specified, control passes to it after the file referenced by file-name-1 has been sequenced ... The compiler inserts a return mechanism after the last statement in the output procedure ... passes control to the next executable statement after the SORT statement ... The RETURN statements in the output procedure are the requests for the next record.' (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR14). EmitSort emits SortSort, then SortEnterProcedure(output: true) + the bounded dispatch of the output range, then the end label and SortClose, falling through to the next statement; RETURN pulls the next record by cursor (CobolSort.Return). Sorted records are delivered one per RETURN in pb440 (OUT=A/B/C) and in the spec-pinned conformance-test SortMergeDifferentialTests.Sort_InputOutputProcedures_MultiKeyMixedDirections; conformance:2023/pb367b_sort_use_not_normal shows control reaching the statement after the SORT. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023]

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB1140 (registrar 14c). Rule: a record of file-name-1 shorter than a fixed-length file-name-3 is space filled 'when that record is returned to the file referenced by file-name-3, as follows: a) If there is only one record description entry associated with the file referenced by file-name-2 and that record is described as a national data item or as an elementary data item of usage national and of category numeric, numeric-edited, or boolean, the record is filled with national space characters ... c) Otherwise ... alphanumeric space characters.' (cite.py --check 14.9.40.4 OK, GR16). ⚠ The printed standard (PDF page 782, extracted) really says file-name-2 in a) and b); the MERGE twin 14.9.24.4 GR13 a) names the GIVING file (file-name-4), so this adjudication reads GR16's a)/b) as file-name-3 -- the text slip is a dossier gap. Code: the implicit WRITE pads through the GIVING connector's FitRecord, which uses the national space only when EmitNationalAreaRegistration registered the area: `file.Records.Any(r => r.OperandPic is { Category: PicCategory.National })` -- ANY record (not 'only one'), and category NATIONAL only (not usage national of category numeric, numeric-edited or boolean). subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 1): 'The access mode of the file referenced by file-name-1 shall be either sequential or dynamic.' CODE: BindStart -- if (file.AccessMode == FileAccessMode.Random) ctx.Edition.Error('COBOLNET0862', ... 'the access mode shall be sequential or dynamic (ISO 14.9.41 SR1)'). FileAccessMode is {Sequential, Random, Dynamic}, so the single Random test is the exact complement of the rule's permitted pair, and FileModel.AccessMode DEFAULTS to Sequential -- a SELECT with no ACCESS clause (the implicit arm a check written against an explicit clause would miss) does not false-fire. ctx.Edition.Error is unconditional, so the diagnostic fires at every strictness and every edition, right for a rule with no edition delta.
PROBED on BOTH keyed organizations, because the check sits before the organization split and a one-organization probe would not have shown that: indexed ACCESS RANDOM (out-b1/probe/sr1-sr8) and relative ACCESS RANDOM (out-b1/probe/sr1-rel) each report COBOLNET0862 SR1.
ONE EDGE NOT REACHED, and it is benign: the check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)', so a sequential-organization file never reaches SR1. 12.4.5.2 admits only ACCESS SEQUENTIAL for sequential organization, so no conforming program can exercise that arm -- the hole is in the diagnostic for an already-illegal file control entry, and 12.4.5.2 owns it, not this rule.
TEST: NONE. grep for COBOLNET0862 across tests/ returns zero hits -- no negative fixture, no unit test -- so a green suite proves nothing about this row. conformance:2002/file_collating_seq exercises only the ACCEPT side (ACCESS DYNAMIC) and would still pass with this check deleted. Closing needs a negative fixture pinning COBOLNET0862 on ORGANIZATION INDEXED + ACCESS RANDOM + START, and its relative twin. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator's own note names an unreached edge -- the SR1 check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)' at KeyedIoBinder.cs:208, so a sequential-organization file never reaches it -- and then argues the edge away with a premise I MEASURED AND BROKE: 'no conforming program can exercise that arm ... 12.4.5.2 owns it, not this rule'. The premise is half right and the conclusion is wrong. Half right: I read the file control entry general formats (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 12.4.5.1) rather than trusting the paraphrase, and Format 3 (sequential) does carry only '[ ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ]' -- ACCESS RANDOM on a sequential file is indeed not conforming. Wrong: nothing in this compiler diagnoses it. ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL + ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM + START SQF FIRST compiles CLEAN -- exit 0, prb.dll written, ZERO diagnostics -- so the rule that was supposed to own the hole owns nothing, and a program that violates SR1 ('the access mode of the file referenced by file-name-1 shall be either sequential or dynamic') is accepted in silence and becomes NotImplemented.Run at run time. SR1 is therefore enforced over two of the three organizations START can name and unenforced over the third; that is PARTIAL by the stated burden (an unverified edge => PARTIAL, and this one is worse than unverified -- it is verified to miss). I did NOT charge SR1 with the sequential-file rejection itself: that mechanism is already recorded as DIVERGES on SR-14.9.41.3-2, and if it is fixed the SR1 test, sitting below it, would start covering sequential files unchanged. What I charge is the CONFORMS claim, whose sole justification for the uncovered half was an escape hatch that does not exist. Everything else in the record I re-derived and it held: FileModel.cs:10 'enum FileAccessMode { Sequential, Random, Dynamic }' makes the single Random test the exact complement of the rule's permitted pair; FileModel.cs:54 'AccessMode { get; set; } = FileAccessMode.Sequential' makes the implicit arm safe; EditionContext.cs:109 'Error(...) => Diagnostics.Add($"{Prefix()}error {code}...")' is unconditional. Citation re-run and OK. Test-ref is empty, which is expected and not what moved the verdict.

LANDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB352). The one edge the adjudication named as unreached is gone: the `if (file.IsSequential) return BoundUnsupported(...)` early return that sat AHEAD of the SR1 test was removed, so a sequential-organization file now reaches SR1 like the other two organizations. The complement is measured, not assumed: conformance:negative/pb325-start-random-access pins the reject side (COBOLNET0862 on ACCESS RANDOM) and the accept side runs at every open mode the rule permits in conformance:2002/pb352_start_sequential_first_last (ACCESS SEQUENTIAL) and conformance:2023/l1_table20_seq_relative.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 4): 'Data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses.' The rule has two operand legs (indexed and relative) and they behave differently.
INDEXED LEG -- ENFORCED, but only as a SIDE EFFECT and reported under the WRONG RULE. RecordLayout.OffsetOf bails to null when the item or any ancestor carries OCCURS ('if (p.Occurs is not null) return null;   // subject to OCCURS => no single fixed position'), so KeyIndexByPosition returns null and BindStart emits COBOLNET0862 '<name> neither names a record key nor begins at the leftmost character position of one with a length not greater than that key (ISO 14.9.41 SR6)'. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr4-occ) with '05 IX-KEY. 10 IX-ELEM PIC X(3) OCCURS 2 TIMES.' and 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-ELEM (1)': rejected with exactly that message. The source IS refused, so no illegal program compiles -- but the message asserts something FALSE about this operand: IX-ELEM(1) DOES begin at IX-KEY's leftmost character position and IS shorter than it. The rule actually violated is SR4; OffsetOf's null collapses two distinct rejection reasons into one sentence, and a user reading it would look for the wrong problem.
RELATIVE LEG -- NO CHECK AT ALL. BindStart's relative arm tests only ReferenceEquals(operand.Item, file.RelativeKeyItem) (that is SR5), which is TRUE for a SUBSCRIPTED reference to the same DataItem. PROBED (same file): with '01 WS-RKT. 05 WS-RK PIC 9(4) OCCURS 3 TIMES.' and 'RELATIVE KEY IS WS-RK', the statement 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK (2)' compiles with NO diagnostic. That shape is reachable only through a file control entry that already violates 12.4.5.13.3 SR1 (--check: 'Data-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses') -- and KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile implements 12.4.5.13's SR2 (unsigned integer, no P) and SR3 (not within a record of the file) but NOT its SR1, so nothing anywhere in the chain diagnoses it. The two missing checks cover for each other.
UNDER-REJECTS. TEST: none.

LANDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB354). SR4 has its own named check, on BOTH arms, ahead of the position walk: RecordLayout.IsSubjectToOccurs is the one predicate for the phrase "subject to an OCCURS clause" and BindStart calls it before either organization arm. The indexed leg no longer reports an OCCURS violation under SR6's message (a sentence that was FALSE of an operand which does begin at the key's leftmost position), and the relative leg - which never called OffsetOf and therefore had no check at all - now reports it too. Both legs are pinned by their own negative fixture.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB602 (wave 42) - THE REFUTED HALF IS CLOSED. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.3 5): 'For relative files, data-name-1, if specified, shall be the data item specified in the RELATIVE KEY clause in the associated file control entry.' 'Shall BE the data item' is an IDENTITY OVER DATA ITEMS, and the screen was asking Place.Item - which answers about the ATTRIBUTES and STORAGE a reference reads, not about which item it is. Place now answers both questions, as 13.18.45.4 GR1 writes them ('all of the data attributes of data-name-2 become the data attributes of data-name-1 AND the storage area occupied by data-name-2 becomes the storage area occupied by data-name-1'): Place.Item is unchanged, and Place.DenotedItem is null for a reference-modified place (8.4.3.3.4 GR5 - 'Reference modification creates a unique data item that is a subset of the data item referenced by identifier-1', which no data description entry declares) and is the level-66 item for a non-THROUGH alias (recorded by the ONE resolver in Place.DenotesAs, so nothing about the ACCESS changes). MEASURED at 2023 on this tree: START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK(1:2) and START RLF KEY IS = RK-ALIAS both now draw COBOLNET0862 naming SR5, where both compiled clean and positioned the file on the relative record number the key's first two characters spell (12.4.5.13.4 GR1 makes 1 the first legal one). SR6's indexed arm asks the same question and refuses IX-KEY(1:2) the same way. POSITIVE CONTROLS in the same golden: the plain RELATIVE KEY item and the prime record key START successfully and READ the record, and both RENAMES forms remain legal MOVE / ADD receivers with the renamed item's attributes and storage. The clause number in this screen's four diagnostics was repaired in the same change set: they said 'ISO 14.9.41 SR5/SR3/SR8/SR1' and every one of those syntax rules is in 14.9.41.3. The PB128 route-around this note named - a hand-written 'p is not RefModPlace' beside a p.Item test, i.e. one caller's private copy of 8.4.3.3.4 GR5 - was written out at twenty sites and all twenty now read DenotedItem; PlaceDenotedItemDriftTests holds the roster so a new Place kind is a failing test rather than a silent inherit.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 6 and 6) b) 1.): for indexed files data-name-1 shall reference either a) a prime or alternate record key associated with file-name-1, or b) a data item whose 'leftmost character position WITHIN A RECORD OF THE FILE corresponds to the leftmost character position of a prime or alternate record key that is associated with file-name-1 and that is defined without the SOURCE phrase in the RECORD KEY clause or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause'.

SR6's two arms are two methods. a) RecordLayout.KeyIndexOfKeyItem: the operand IS a record key - by reference identity, or by 12.4.5.12.4 GR4's identical BYTE POSITIONS in another record description entry OF THE SAME FILE. b) RecordLayout.GenericKeyIndex: SR6 b)'s three conditions together. The missing premise of b) 1. - "within a record of the file" - is required by RecordLayout.IsInRecordOfFile, so a WORKING-STORAGE 01 at offset 0 no longer collides with offset 0 in the record (conformance:negative/pb354-start-operand-outside-record). The COMPLEMENT is measured, not assumed: conformance:2002/pb354_start_generic_key_ok walks all five accepting shapes (declared prime key, a GR4 implicit key in a second record description, a shorter generic prime key, the declared alternate, and a shorter generic alternate) and each returns the record the rule selects.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB358 LANDED 2026-09-09 - the decline is now NAMED, and this row is the one PB697's adjudication put the 4.2.6 paragraph 3 obligation on. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.3 -> OK, SR7): 'Record-key-name-1 shall be specified with the SOURCE phrase in the RECORD KEY clause or in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause in the file control entry for file-name-1.'
THE RULE'S SUBJECT IS THE DECLINED ELEMENT ITSELF, which is what makes this row DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT where its four siblings below are CONFORMS: SR7 says nothing about the START statement except where record-key-name-1 has to be declared, and record-key-name-1 is declared ONLY by the SOURCE phrase (8.4.6.2.4, 'Scope of record-key-names'; the name class is 8.3.2.2.24). The same discriminator the owner set on SR-12.4.5.9.3-1 (kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02): a rule whose subject is a CLAIMED facility conforms with a witness pinning the refusal of a declined operand, and a rule whose subject IS the declined element is DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT.
THE DECISION REFERENCE is docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 40, the conformance claim's own record of the decline, standing on Annex A.3 item 40 (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK item 40): 'The capability of specifying the SOURCE phrase of the RECORD KEY clause and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' kb/Work PB293 recorded on 2026-09-05 that the posture is settled and the owner question withdrawn under the owner-decision protocol; providing the form is not proposed. The same decision reference and the same evidence shape as A.3 item 26 (kb/Work PB292, row 26).
WHAT CHANGED, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THIS ROW'S DEBT. Until 2026-09-09 the SOURCE phrase matched NO grammar alternative anywhere, so 'RECORD KEY IS IX-COMPOSITE SOURCE IS IX-A IX-B' answered COBOLNET0312 'unexpected SOURCE. Unexpected token in FILE-CONTROL paragraph. Check SELECT/ASSIGN TO syntax. A period may be missing at the end of the previous sentence.' - a generic parse error that names a token instead of the determination and points at the wrong repair - and NO fixture pinned the rejection, so a later widening that swallowed SOURCE and ignored it would have broken nothing. 4.2.6 paragraph 3 (cite.py --check 4.2.6 -> OK) makes the indication mandatory: 'An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism at compile time to indicate use of syntactically-detectable processor-dependent language elements not supported by that implementation.'
BOTH CLAUSES, ONE RULE, ONE CODE. CobolIO.g4 now carries recordKeySourcePhrase (record-key-name SOURCE IS dataReference+) used by BOTH recordKeyClause and alternateKeyClause, and DataBinder.DeclineRecordKeySource refuses it through the one EditionContext.Declined seam as COBOLNET1954. A.3 item 40 names both clauses in ONE sentence and 12.4.5.12.2 and 12.4.5.6.2 print the SAME brace group, so a second code would put one rule in two places; the original finding named only the prime key, which is the two-arm defect shape this repository reproduces most often.
REFUSED (Error), NOT ACCEPT-INERT like COBOLNET1778 on the same annex: 12.4.5.12.4 GR2 / 12.4.5.6.4 GR2 (both --check OK) make the form 'a record key consisting of the concatenation of all occurrences of data-name-2 in the order specified', and record-key-name-1 names no data item, so an inert compile would leave the file with NO key. 4.2.6 paragraph 3's closing sentence is the licence: 'The implementor is not required to produce executable code when unsupported processor-dependent language elements are used.'
WITNESSES: five negatives (both clauses; the printed spelling, the optional-word minimum spelling that 8.3.2.4.3 makes equivalent, and the trailing WITH DUPLICATES phrase that proves the clause is recognized WHOLE rather than up to the SOURCE token - it used to draw a SECOND unexpected-token error at WITH), each rejecting at 85/2002/2014/2023 with exactly ONE diagnostic; plus two FileControlKeyRuleSpecTests methods carrying what the corpus cannot say - that the refusal does not also report the clause MISSING (a measured regression on the first build of the surface: 12.4.5.1 Format 1's requiredness row inferred absence from a null data-name, so the program was told both that the form is not provided and that its indexed file 'has no RECORD KEY clause'; the row now reads FileKeyOperand.Written).
EDITIONS unchanged: the SOURCE phrase is absent from the COBOL-85 RECORD KEY clause and Annex E records no 14.9.41 change from 2014, so 2014 and 2023 are certain and 2002 is the conventional third. The negatives reject at 85 as well, which is right either way - at 85 the construct does not exist at all.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 8): 'If the LENGTH phrase is specified, file-name-1 shall reference a file with indexed organization.' CODE: BindStart -- 'if (length is not null && file.Organization != FileOrganization.Indexed) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET0862", ... "the LENGTH phrase requires indexed organization (ISO 14.9.41 SR8)");'. The predicate itself is right (Indexed is the only permitted organization), but the STATEMENT IS UNREACHABLE for one of the two organizations it exists to exclude.
RELATIVE LEG VERIFIED (out-b1/probe/sr1-sr8): 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK WITH LENGTH 2' on ORGANIZATION RELATIVE reports COBOLNET0862 SR8.
SEQUENTIAL LEG NOT REACHED: the check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)'. notes: kb/Work PB370. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR9 and GR9 b) / c)). GR9 a) FORWARD SEARCH: RelativeConnector.Start walks the SortedDictionary keys ascending for '==' (ContainsKey), '>' and '>=' and breaks on the first hit. GR9 b) REVERSE SEARCH: '<' and '<=' walk the same ascending key order but KEEP the last satisfying key and break on the first non-satisfying one — which is the largest RRN satisfying the relation, i.e. the first record found searching the file in reverse. ConditionBinder.MapOperator maps NOT LESS -> '>=', NOT GREATER -> '<=', GREATER OR EQUAL -> '>=', LESS OR EQUAL -> '<='; '!=' is unreachable here (SR3 rewrite in BindStart), and no other spelling can fall through the switch, so there is no silent no-match arm. PREVIOUS raises COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 (VersionConformancePass.cs:254, Constructs.ReadPrevious2002) -- and gates every other post-85 element of START (start-first-last-2002, start-with-length-2002, both with constructs.json rows). notes: kb/Work PB370. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR17 e) 1.): 'The file position indicator is set to the value of the key of reference in the first logical record whose key satisfies the comparison'. IMPLEMENTATION: IndexedConnector.Start builds `Ordered(keyIndex)` — records sorted by (key-of-reference value under KeyCompare, then Arrival) with SUPPRESS WHEN records filtered out — then iterates FORWARD for '==','>','>=' and BACKWARD for '<','<=' (GR17 c/d) and stops at the first satisfying record, setting `_fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex)` (the key VALUE, as the rule states) plus `_fpiArrival` (the duplicate-key disambiguator 9.1.8.2 needs to make arrival-order retrieval work; it adds resolution, it does not contradict the rule). GR17 e)'s operand orientation is right: `KeyCompare(part, value, keyIndex)` puts the RECORD'S extracted key on the left, matching 'with the second temporary area on the left hand side' (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK). The suppression sentence is honored by Ordered's `Where(r => !IsSuppressed(r.Image, keyIndex))`, and IsSuppressed returns false for keyIndex < 0 so the prime key is never suppressible. The partial-key truncation uses the WITH LENGTH count when present, else the operand's ImageWidth (EmitStart). OBSERVED (probe/idx-start/STPRB3, keys AAA100/BBB200/CCC300): implicit EQUAL 'BBB200' -> BBB200; '> BBB200' -> CCC300; '< BBB999' -> BBB200 (the LARGEST key below, proving the reverse search); 'NOT GREATER BBB999' -> BBB200; '>= AAA000 WITH LENGTH 3' -> AAA100. probe/idx-dup/STPRBB (alternate key WITH DUPLICATES, MM written by 05, 03, 09 in that arrival order): '>= MM' positions at 05 — the EARLIEST arrival of the duplicate set, and the walk gives 05, 03, 09; '< NN' positions at 09 — the LATEST arrival, i.e. the first satisfying record in reverse order. TESTS: conformance:2002/file_collating_seq pins START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV (expected 'START >= M UNDER REV:' then K=M, K=A, derived from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, not from any oracle); conformance:2023/altkey_suppress_when pins START KEY IS >= LOW-VALUES on a SUPPRESS-WHEN alternate key (expected 01/AA then 03/BB); conformance-test:KeyedOffsetSpecTests.Start_KeyOperandInSiblingRecord_MatchesByBytePosition asserts GOT=01 for START KEY = via a sibling-record operand, reasoned from 12.4.5.12.4 GR4 + 14.9.41.3 SR6b. All three compute their expected values from the standard. EDITIONS: the GR17 e) suppression sentence depends on SUPPRESS WHEN, a COBOL-2023 addition (cite.py --check E.3.3 OK, item 42), and the WITH LENGTH count in GR17 b) is a post-85 phrase; the rule itself is present in every edition. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, on the same defect as GR9 and for the same reason: the record claims edition 85 for a branch COBOL-85 does not have and the compiler does not gate. The BEHAVIOUR survived everything I threw at it. I re-derived the ordering from source rather than from the notes: IndexedConnector.Ordered (:510-513) sorts by (key-of-reference value under KeyCompare, then Arrival) with IsSuppressed filtered out, and Start (:444-481) walks seq[i] for '=='/'>'/'>=' and seq[Count-1-i] for '<'/'<=', which is exactly 9.1.8's reverse order (descending key, reverse arrival); KeyCompare(part, value, keyIndex) puts the RECORD's extracted key on the left, matching GR17 e)'s 'second temporary area on the left hand side'; _fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex) is the key VALUE the rule names. I verified BOTH cited conformance goldens by reading them, not by trusting the note: 2002/file_collating_seq computes START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV -> 'K=M','K=A' from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, and 2023/altkey_suppress_when computes the SUPPRESS-WHEN skip from 12.4.5.6.4 GR6 -- both spec-derived, both genuinely pinning the FPI-setting branch (a mis-set FPI changes the printed walk). I then probed the edges neither test reaches. Nothing broke. What breaks is editions '85,2002,2014,2023': the record's own notes claim the BACKWARD arm for COBOL-85 ('iterates FORWARD for ==,>,>= and BACKWARD for <,<= ... < BBB999 -> BBB200, proving the reverse search'), and that operator set is A.3 item 39's other half of READ PREVIOUS, which the compiler does gate at 2002. subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: The three per-format DETERMINATIONS are each implemented at their own call site and read correct. (a) format 1 `all of the operands in the statement`: CheckComposite("SUBTRACT", minuends, recv) superimposes the sending operands AND the identifier-2 receivers. (b) format 2 `excluding the data item that follow the word GIVING`: CheckComposite("SUBTRACT", [minuends, fromX], []) passes an EMPTY receiver list - pinned by the spec-derived golden conformance:2023/ca4_giving_composite, whose SUBTRACT leg (`SUBTRACT B FROM D GIVING C` over 25-digit operands and a 16-digit GIVING receiver) is legal only because the receiver is excluded. (c) format 3 `the two corresponding operands for each separate pair`: the check runs inside CorrMatch's per-pair loop with exactly [source] + [target]. notes: The emitted shape is literally the rule's `(operand-2 - (operand-11 + ... + operand-1n))`: Fold builds the SUM node first and Combine subtracts it from the rendered FROM operand as one nested subtrahend - not a left-to-right `((op2 - op11) - op12)`. THE PARENTHESISATION IS MEASURED, NOT ONLY READ, and the measurement is spec-derived: under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL every operation rounds to 34 significant digits (8.8.1.5 / decimal128), so the two shapes disagree at the boundary. subject: UNLOCK statement
notes: RULE (two halves): 'Any record locks associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1 are released by the execution of the UNLOCK statement. The presence or absence of any record locks does not affect the success of the execution of the UNLOCK statement.' - cite.py --check 14.9.47.4 (first sentence) -> OK §14.9.47.4 1). CODE: FileRegistry.Unlock calls `PhysicalFileTable.ReleaseAllForConnector(st, name)` - keyed on the CONNECTOR name, which is exactly 'associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1' - then unconditionally `c.SetStatus(FileStatusCode.Success)`, so held locks and no locks give the same 00. The RECORD/RECORDS word is deliberately dropped (`_ = records;`), which is right: GR1 releases ALL locks and its NOTE routes single-record release to READ ... NO LOCK. BOTH HALVES MEASURED. (a) release: conformance:2002/file_sharing has A lock record 1 (READA=00), B blocked (READB=51), then `UNLOCK F-A` and B reads 00 (AFTER=00); file_sharing_seq shows the converse - B's UNLOCK does not disturb A's own lock (UNLB=00 then REWA=00/REWB51=51). (b) presence-or-absence: p1.cob UNLOCKs an OPEN sequential file that never held a lock -> 00, and p6.cob UNLOCKs twice in a row (AUTO-UNLA=00 then AUTO-UNLA2=00 with nothing left to release). (c) ALL LOCK MODES, not just MANUAL: p6.cob uses `LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC` on two RELATIVE connectors - the auto-lock taken by A's READ blocks B (AUTO-READB=51) and is released by `UNLOCK F-A` (AUTO-READB2=00), matching Table A.1's UNLOCK row, cite.py --check D.2.4.3.2 '| UNLOCK | Automatic -single - multiple Manual - single - multiple | | for all lock modes: - on all locked records |' -> OK (informative corroboration; GR1 is the normative source). NOT DOWNGRADED by the unregistered-connector path of findings [unregistered-keyed-connector]/[unlock-registry-entry-is-the-one-silent-fall-through]: a connector that was never registered was never opened, so it holds no record locks and GR1 is vacuous there - the observable failure on that path is the I-O status, which is why GR2 and GR3 carry it and this row does not.

What the record misses is the RULE'S SCOPE: GR5 is 'Within a given procedure division', and ISO 14.2.2 SR10 says Format 1 -- the procedure-division format that CARRIES the DECLARATIVES portion (14.2.1) -- 'may be specified in a source element if and only if that source element is a function definition, a function prototype definition, a METHOD DEFINITION, a program definition, or a program prototype definition'. A method definition therefore has a procedure division that may legally hold Format-1 USE statements (14.9.49.3 SR1 puts the USE statement in exactly that declaratives portion), and the compiler rejects EVERY declarative part inside a method unconditionally: StatementBinder.cs:239-242 -> COBOLNET0899 'DECLARATIVES inside a method (ISO 14.2.1) are recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 3, OO port)'. That is a deferral rejecting legal source, not owner-documented non-support, so the rule is implemented for the program and function procedure divisions and NOT IMPLEMENTED for a method's. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL. (The record's code-location, editions and empty test-ref are otherwise accurate and should be kept.) || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985/2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 1). subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the first one that occurs in the order of evaluation of the statement that causes the exception to exist" -> OK, GR 11). There is no explicit 'first condition' latch; the property is emergent - every raise site dispatches inline at the point the condition occurs, and a fatal raise throws out of the statement, so the first condition in evaluation order is the one that reaches __EcDispatch. `__af.Dispatched` additionally guarantees one dispatch per raise across nested guards (14.6.13.1.3 #7). PARTIAL because the adversarial shape is unverified and the emergent property is not robust to it: a statement in which the FIRST condition is nonfatal and a LATER one is fatal would dispatch on the later one, and there is no mechanism preventing it, because an enabled nonfatal condition raised from a runtime site never dispatches at all (ExceptionState.Set only records the last exception status - the nonfatal ambient gates EC-DATA-CONVERSION / EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW set a flag and nothing more). Whether a nonfatal condition must run the declarative is 14.6.13.1.4's rule, not this one, but it is what makes GR11 untested here. No spec-derived test asserts the ordering. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 3). No Annex E entry touches it.

subject: USE statement
notes: CLOSED 2026-09-09 by the PB365/PB366 reconciliation - the row carried TWO measured defects, each mechanism owned one, and this is the first tree on which both cures exist together. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 'A declarative is selected for execution by analyzing the USE statements in a source element in the order in which they are specified' -> OK GR 14; 'is a factory object or instance object of object-class-name-1 or of a subclass of object-class-name-1' -> OK GR 14 a); 'all of the USE statements in the source element are analyzed again' -> OK GR 14 a) (its otherwise-clause); 'described with an IMPLEMENTS clause that references interface-name-1' -> OK GR 14 b)). || DEFECT 1, GR14 a)'s FACTORY arm, FIXED by kb/Work PB366: the factory object of class X is a distinct emitted type X__FACTORY deriving from the BASE class's factory (OoEmitter.EmitClassUnit / OoClassSymbol.FactoryCsName), never from X, so the selector's single `__obj is X` test was false for every factory exception object - silently, no declarative and no diagnostic. Measured before (probe: `01 FR USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE.` / `SET FR TO CF1.` / `RAISE FR.` against `USE AFTER EXCEPTION OBJECT CF1`) -> `AFTER` alone where the spec requires `F4-HANDLER / AFTER`; the instance control reached the handler. The cure is the census OoClassSymbol.FactoryOrInstanceCsTypes rendered as one C# or-pattern per entry, `__obj is X or X__FACTORY`; 'or of a subclass' rides C#'s `is` in EACH hierarchy because both mirror INHERITS. Witness conformance:2002/pb366_use_exception_object_factory walks five arms - an exact-class factory, a factory two declaratives match (source-order first-match plus 'no other declaratives are executed'), a SUBCLASS factory naming no declarative of its own, an INSTANCE object, and an unmatched factory falling to the 14.6.13.1.5 tail - and on the pre-fix tree arms 1, 2 and 3 printed no handler at all. || DEFECT 2, GR14 b) absent, FIXED by kb/Work PB365: an interface operand was rejected at bind with COBOLNET0859 (SR16's diagnostic answering SR17's question) and there was no second analysis pass over the USE statements at all. The selector is now TWO passes - EmitObjDispatchPass emits every object-class-name-1 entry in source order, then, only after all of them, every interface-name-1 entry - which is what 'otherwise, all of the USE statements in the source element are analyzed again and: b) ...' requires and which an interleaved single pass cannot express (an earlier interface entry would beat a later class entry). GR14 b)'s 'described with an IMPLEMENTS clause' is 11.8.4 GR2 (instance objects) / 11.4.4 GR2 (factory objects) as a CLOSURE - own IMPLEMENTS, an implemented interface's INHERITS, an inherited class's IMPLEMENTS - and the emitter renders each emitted HALF of a class with exactly that closure as its C# interface list, so one test against OoInterfaceSymbol.ImplementedCsTypes realises all three legs for both object kinds. Witness conformance:2002/pb365_use_eo_interface_two_pass, whose interface declarative is written FIRST and whose expected output (CLASS-CY, AFTER-1, IFACE, AFTER-2) is produced only by a selector that honours the pass boundary. || THE RECONCILED SHAPE (this change set): BoundDeclarative.Eo is the discriminated BoundEoOperand - BoundEoClass(OoClassSymbol) | BoundEoInterface(OoInterfaceSymbol) - carrying the RESOLVED SYMBOL, never a rendered C# type name, and each GR14 pass renders its own alternative's census. Both goldens were re-measured on the merged tree and match their .out byte-for-byte. pb366_use_exception_object_factory itself needed repair, not exemption: two of its class definitions inherited from PBFBASE with no REPOSITORY paragraph, which 11.3.3 SR2 forbids and PB365's 8.4.6.4 funnel now enforces. Format4UseObjectSelectorDriftTests asserts against the GENERATED C# that each alternative's census equals what the backend actually emits, that the selector tests every member, and that the class pass precedes the interface pass; both new detectors were fired against a deliberately broken census and a deliberately swapped pass order before being trusted. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 4 - the exception-object / OO facility). No Annex E entry touches it.

subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the predefined object reference EXCEPTION-OBJECT references the exception object" -> OK, GR 15). On BOTH paths that can enter a Format-4 declarative the register is set before the selector runs: EmitRaiseObject emits `ExceptionState.SetObject(<the RAISE operand>)` and then `__EcObjDispatch(ExceptionState.ExceptionObject)`; EmitPropagationPickup emits `SetObject(__po)` and then the selector. The covering case tests/conformance/2002/oo_ec_raise_object.cob enters the selected declarative and executes `SET U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT` / `IF U NOT = NULL`, and the committed golden requires `BASE-HANDLER EXCEPTION-OBJECT` + `REGISTER-SET` - so the register is proven non-null and carrying the raised object on entry. Note the register is a run-unit-scoped single slot (ExceptionState.ExceptionObject) and a NAMED raise inside the declarative nulls it (Set sets ExceptionObject = null); that is 14.9.29.4 GR1's rule, and GR15 constrains only the state on ENTRY, which holds. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Two independent defects in the record. (1) THE TEST-REF DOES NOT PIN THE RULE. GR15 says EXCEPTION-OBJECT 'references the exception object' -- an IDENTITY claim (ISO 8.8.4.2.15: the relation is true 'if the object referenced by identifier-3 is the same object that is referenced by identifier-4'). The cited conformance:2002/oo_ec_raise_object asserts only 'IF U NOT = NULL DISPLAY "REGISTER-SET"'; its golden line 'REGISTER-SET' is satisfied by ANY non-null object, so a regression that set the register to the wrong object -- SELF, a fresh instance, the activating program -- keeps that golden green. The row is NOT closed by it and the test-ref must be emptied; the missing assertion is one line (IF U = E). I measured the identity claim myself and it HOLDS on every entry path, so the program-level half of the rule is genuinely correct -- this is a coverage correction, not a behaviour finding. (2) A HALF THAT CANNOT BE ENTERED AT ALL. 'the associated declarative' is a declarative in a procedure division, and ISO 14.2.2 SR10 permits the DECLARATIVES-bearing Format 1 (14.2.1) in a METHOD DEFINITION; StatementBinder.cs:239-242 rejects every declarative part inside a method with COBOLNET0899 'recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 3, OO port)' at both 2002 and 2023, so a Format-4 USE in a method -- the natural home for EC-OO handling -- is legal source the compiler refuses. Unlocated/unreachable half + verified half => PARTIAL. (Contributing, already owned by the record for GR14: the interface-name-1 arm of the associated declarative is rejected COBOLNET0859, so even in a program only the object-class arm of GR14 can ever deliver an entry for GR15 to constrain -- I confirmed that rejection. It does not by itself move GR15, because the register is written BEFORE the selector runs and is therefore arm-independent.) || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 4). No Annex E entry touches it.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: 'The write file is the file referenced by file-name-1 or by the file-name associated with record-name-1.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 OK, SR1). ResolveRecordName's identity test returns the FileModel whose Records contain the item (own files, then inherited GLOBAL FDs via FilesByName); that FileModel is the write file every later check (SR12/SR13/SR19/SR22, org reroute) and the BoundWrite/BoundKeyedWrite node use. The FILE file-name-1 arm is Annex A.4.13 declined (COBOLNET1706) so only the record-name arm is reachable. pb347_record_name_identity writes OUT-REC / OUT-REC OF OUTF and reads the records back from OUTF. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base WRITE statement; the 2023 text records no change to this rule in Annex E)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GAP -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB691). Rule text validated: cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 "If the organization of the write file is sequential, format 1 shall be specified" => OK 2). The rule is a FORMAT-SELECTION rule, and what it forbids is read off the formats: Format 1 (sequential) of 14.9.51.2 carries no INVALID KEY bracket at all -- only Format 2 (random) does -- so a WRITE on a sequential-organization file may not carry the phrase. It was PARSED AND DROPPED: SequentialIoBinder.BindWrite never called w.writeInvalidKey(), so the program compiled clean at every edition and NEITHER imperative ran, with no diagnostic on either severity axis. Measured with a CLI probe before the fix (WRITE ... INVALID KEY DISPLAY "W-IK" NOT INVALID KEY DISPLAY "W-NIK" on ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL printed only 'DONE 00' at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive), not inferred. It is the THIRD arm of one silent drop: PB144 screened REWRITE (SR-14.9.35.3-2), PB334 READ, and this one hid because the writeInvalidKey sub-rule was consumed by the KEYED binder only. Now screened through the ONE severity seam (StatementValidation.ScreenForbiddenPhrase -> COBOLNET1720, no new code): an ERROR under strict at all four editions, a WARNING under --permissive -- and, unlike the REWRITE arm as PB144 left it, the phrase is BOUND rather than dropped, because 9.1.14's final rule item 2 (cite.py --check 9.1.14 "If the I-O status indicates a successful completion, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement or to the imperative-statement specified in the NOT INVALID KEY phrase if it is specified" => OK 2)) gives the NOT INVALID KEY imperative a live meaning even here. The INVALID arm is provably dead on this organization: 9.1.13.5's four invalid-key statuses '21'-'24' each name a relative or indexed file, so the emitter's status-first '2' branch can never fire -- dead, never rerouted. D9 CORPUS SWEEP RUN, NOT REASONED: a record-name -> FD -> SELECT organization mapping over all 459 NIST programs finds 77 WRITE ... INVALID KEY sites, every one of them on an INDEXED or RELATIVE file and ZERO on a sequential-organization file; all 459 then compiled at --std 85 with the screened compiler and NOT ONE drew COBOLNET1720; and the ~Nist conformance leg is byte-identical across the change (Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 352, Total: 352, before and after). The screen is edition-invariant by construction (Removed keys on Permissive, never on edition) and measured so at 85/2002/2014/2023.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GAP -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB909). Rule text validated: cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 "If the organization of the write file is indexed or relative, format 2 shall be specified" -> OK 3). Format 2 differs from Format 1 only by lacking the ADVANCING and END-OF-PAGE phrases (and admitting INVALID KEY, which SR2 screens on the other arm), so refusing those two phrases on a relative/indexed WRITE IS the rule. COBOLNET1720 in both lanes (Format 2 gives a print-control phrase no meaning to bind under --permissive); it used to be a COBOLNET1756 deferral and a run-unit abort.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: SR4: 'If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric or national function.' (--check OK). FromPhraseRules.Write = {Alphanumeric, National}; BindFromPhrase reads the function's category through MoveTable16.SenderPosition (so a constant-folded LENGTH still reads numeric) and raises COBOLNET1914. Same row serves the sequential and keyed arms. Probes: numeric (NUMVAL), integer (INTEGER, LENGTH) and boolean (BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER) rejected 1914; alphanumeric (UPPER-CASE, CURRENT-DATE) and national (NATIONAL-OF to PIC N) accepted. The screen is deliberately not applied to an inline method invocation (not a function-identifier, §8.4.3.1.2). pb348-write-from-integer-function rejects FUNCTION LENGTH at all four editions; the paired positive is conformance:2023/pb10_function_identifier_sending. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 wherever a function-identifier can be written as identifier-1 (the national/boolean categories are post-1985)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB347. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 'Record-name-1 is the name of a logical record in the file section of the data division and may be qualified.' -> OK, 14.9.51.3 5). This is RELEASE 14.9.32.3 SR1 and REWRITE 14.9.35.3 SR1 written a third time, and all three now share ONE implementation, StatementValidation.ResolveRecordName. BOTH HALVES ARE WITNESSED. Name-of-a-logical-record: a subordinate item is refused (`WRITE OR-DATA` -> COBOLNET1757, naming OUT-REC as the record to write instead), a reference-modified record is refused (record-name-1 is a user-defined word per 8.3.2.2.25 and 5.2.4, not an identifier position per 8.4.3.3.3 SR5), and a WORKING-STORAGE 01 is refused with 14.9.51.3 SR1's reason -- 'The write file is the file referenced by file-name-1 or by the file-name associated with record-name-1' (--check OK) -- there being no file to name. May-be-qualified: `WRITE OUT-REC OF OUTF` binds and writes, pinned in both positive goldens. BEFORE THIS: all three were accepted with NO error. The subordinate and reference-modified forms drew nothing at all and emitted CobolFile.Write with the wrong operand and so the wrong record WIDTH; the WORKING-STORAGE form drew only the COBOLNET1756 DEFERRAL WARNING, which announces the COMPILER's gap for what is the source's error, and the program compiled. ISO 4.2.2 makes the compile-time indication mandatory. Edition-invariant: the sentence is identical in 1985, 2002 and 2014, so no gate exists and each negative carries `*> reject-at: 85 2002 2014 2023`.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: SR6: 'If record-name-1 is specified, identifier-1 or literal-1 shall be valid as a sending operand in a MOVE statement specifying record-name-1 as the receiving operand.' (--check OK). BindFromPhrase ends in BindMoveOf(source, [record], phrase) - the MOVE statement's own screen, with the phrase named in every message. Probes: index item sender -> COBOLNET0809 (ws3snd2); national function to alphanumeric record -> 0819 (ws3fnatof); SPACE to a numeric record at 2023 -> 0902 (the edition-dependent Table 16 cell, ws3snd5); alphanumeric literal, numeric-edited item and 3.5 to PIC 9(5) accepted, all legal MOVEs (ws3snd1/3/4). Both arms (sequential and keyed) call the same helper. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base WRITE statement; the 2023 text records no change to this rule in Annex E)]

subject: WRITE statement

The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS: conformance:negative/a413-write-file-format-1; conformance:negative/a413-write-file-format-2; conformance:85/a413_declined_phrase_positive_control, with conformance:85/a413_declined_phrase_positive_control proving the mandatory record-name arm still compiles and RUNS. subject: WRITE statement
notes: SR11: 'If identifier-1 references a function and the FILE phrase is not specified, identifier-1 shall reference an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function.' (--check OK). SR4 of the SAME clause is unconditional: 'If identifier-1 is a function-identifier, it shall reference an alphanumeric or national function.' (--check OK). Both are syntax rules a conforming WRITE must satisfy together, so the admitted set without FILE is their intersection {alphanumeric, national}; FromPhraseRules.Write enforces exactly that (COBOLNET1914). Probes: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE / CURRENT-DATE accepted (ws3fupper, ws3fcurdate); NUMVAL, INTEGER, LENGTH rejected 1914 (ws3fnumval/ws3fintf/ws3flength); NATIONAL-OF into a PIC N record accepted (ws4nat rc=0); BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER into PIC 1(8) rejected 1914 citing SR4 (ws4boo). So every function SR11 forbids is rejected; a boolean function, which SR11 alone would admit, is refused by SR4 - the literal conjunctive reading, documented in the MoveBinder comment and pb348-write-from-integer-function's header. NOTE the tension: REWRITE's twin §14.9.35.3 SR9 admits boolean and has no SR4-style unconditional rule, so the WRITE text is internally inconsistent; no docs/CONFORMANCE.md determination records the SR4-over-SR11 reading (see dossier_gaps). No spec-derived test pins the SR11 no-FILE arm itself (the boolean rejection or the national acceptance), so test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 for the boolean/national arms (boolean and national categories do not exist in 1985); the function-identifier-in-FROM restriction applies at every edition that admits a function-identifier]

subject: WRITE statement
notes:
kb/Work PB1171 (registrar 14c). SR12: 'The file description entry associated with the write file shall not contain the REPORT clause and shall not be a sort-merge file description entry.' (--check OK). SORT-MERGE HALF conforms: `SD S. 01 SR ... WRITE SR` -> COBOLNET1692 via UnsupportedOrg -> ScreenSortMergeFile (probe probe/write-statement-p1/ws2sd.cob); the keyed arm (which does not call UnsupportedOrg) is unreachable for an SD because §12.4.5.2 SR9 rejects ORGANIZATION RELATIVE/INDEXED on a sort-merge entry first (ws4sdr COBOLNET1900). No negative test pins WRITE of an SD record (pb140 covers CLOSE/DELETE only). REPORT HALF DIVERGES: nothing in BindWrite or the keyed arm tests file.IsReportFile; the only IsReportFile screen is OPEN's mode check. `FD P REPORT IS RP. 01 PR PIC X(10).` + `INITIATE RP / GENERATE DL / WRITE PR / GENERATE DL / TERMINATE RP` compiles clean and runs; the report file receives 'HELLO
INJECTED
HELLO
' (probe ws4rpt.cob) - a record written into a report file by a statement SR12 forbids. The record description itself is already illegal (§13.4.5.3 SR8 'No record description entries or constant entries shall be associated with the file description entry for a report file.' --check OK) and is also accepted (ws3rpt0 rc=0) - the root mechanism. Expected: a compile-time error for the WRITE (SR12) and for the FD's record entry (§13.4.5.3 SR8). No register note owns this (PB345/PB677/PB694 are different defects). [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base WRITE statement; the 2023 text records no change to this rule in Annex E)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: SR13: 'If the file description entry associated with the write file contains the LINAGE clause, mnemonic-name-1 shall not be specified.' (--check OK). CheckWriteAdvancingMnemonic errors (COBOLNET0862) when file.Linage is set and the ADVANCING dataReference resolves in the unit's mnemonic registry. Probe ws1mnlin (LINAGE + AFTER ADVANCING TOP-OF-FORM, C01) -> 0862; ws1mnok (same, no LINAGE) compiles. Keyed files never reach it but Format 2 has no ADVANCING at all (SR3, COBOLNET1720). Both BEFORE and AFTER share the one adv context, so both words are covered. subject: WRITE statement
notes: RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 'The BEFORE and AFTER phrases shall not both be specified if the PAGE phrase is specified' -> OK 14.9.51.3 17). BOTH DIRECTIONS OBSERVED. The prohibition: tests/conformance/negative/pb712-write-before-after-page.cob writes `WRITE P-REC BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING PAGE` and is refused COBOLNET1910 at 2023. subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1193 (registrar 14c). SR21: 'If record-name-1 is defined in a containing program and is referenced in a contained program, the file description entry for the file-name associated with record-name-1 shall contain a GLOBAL clause.' (--check OK). Enforced by scope: a non-GLOBAL FD's record-name is not visible in the contained program, so `WRITE R` there fails name resolution (probe ws3nest0: COBOLNET1639 'R' is not defined, rc=70); with `FD F IS GLOBAL` the contained WRITE resolves through FilesByName to the container's one connector and runs (ws3nest1 prints DONE). The diagnostic is the generic undefined-name one rather than an SR21-specific message, which is adequate (§8.4.2.1). No spec-derived golden writes a GLOBAL FD's record from a contained program (pb123_exception_file_global_fd has no WRITE), so test-ref is empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator's premise is false: it says a non-GLOBAL FD's record is not visible in the contained program, so WRITE R fails name resolution. But 13.18.27.3 SR1 b) lets a file-section 01 record carry its OWN GLOBAL clause, and SR21 exists for exactly that case: the record is visible, yet the FD has no GLOBAL, so WRITE must be rejected. The pinned compiler rejects that shape only because it ignores record-level GLOBAL in the file section entirely: MOVE "HELLO" TO R is refused too, with a false 'R is not defined' message. So the SR21 outcome depends on a separate defect, and there is no SR21-specific check. Once record-level GLOBAL is honoured, WRITE R would pass silently. Same finding as the REWRITE twin, SR-14.9.35.3-3. A separate wrong-rejection defect also needs a note: a GLOBAL 01 under a non-GLOBAL FD is not visible to contained programs. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base WRITE statement; the 2023 text records no change to this rule in Annex E)]

Half 1, 'no longer available': the standard leaves the content after release undefined, and the emitted WRITE neither clears nor preserves the area by rule; the typed field keeps its last value, as CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-24 documents for CLOSE. So there is nothing to enforce. notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'The same WRITE statement without the FROM phrase' -> OK 5) b)): WRITE ... FROM is equivalent to MOVE identifier-1/literal-1 TO record-name-1 followed by the WRITE. Code: both emitters start with `if (wr.FromMove is { } fromMove) move.Emit(fromMove);`, which emits the BOUND implicit MOVE built by the binder under the MOVE screens (kb/Work PB348), and then emit the plain WRITE. subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'The figurative constant SPACE when specified in the WRITE statement references one alphanumeric space character' -> OK 6)). The only place a figurative constant can appear in WRITE is literal-1 of the FROM phrase. With the FILE phrase it is forbidden (--check 14.9.51.3 'literal-1 shall be an alphanumeric, boolean, or national literal and shall not be a figurative constant' -> OK 7) b)), and the FILE phrase is declined anyway (A.4.13, COBOLNET1706). A national record under SPACE is not probed, but MOVE's figurative rule governs it. No test is aimed at this rule, so test-ref is empty.
