subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the information in the area referenced by identifier-1 is available, provided that identifier-1 is not one or part of one of the record descriptions subordinate to the file-description' -> OK 9)). Code: the FROM phrase emits only a MOVE that READS identifier-1, and the connector call receives a copy of the record-area image. Nothing writes back to identifier-1. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). from1.cob: after WRITE R1 FROM WS-SRC, WS-SRC shows '[HELLO]'; after the indexed WRITE K-REC FROM WS-KSRC, WS-KSRC shows '[K01DATA1]'. The record-area half ('not available except as specified by SAME RECORD AREA') is GR4's and is decided there. No test is aimed at this rule, so test-ref is empty.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR10: 'If the locking mode of the write file connector is single record locking, any record lock associated with that file connector is released by the execution of the WRITE statement.' Every WRITE (sequential and keyed emitters both render FileWriteShared unconditionally) calls ReleasePriorRecordLocks before the operation; it returns early only for meta.Multiple (multiple record locking keeps its locks), otherwise ReleaseAllForConnector. Released 'by the execution' regardless of the write's outcome, which matches the rule text (no success condition). Organization-independent. The unit test asserts WA's WITH LOCK record 2 is released by the next WRITE under single locking. cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'any record lock associated with that file connector is released by the execution of the WRITE statement' -> OK rule 10. Record locking is a COBOL-2002 introduction (LOCK MODE clause).

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR11: 'If record locks have an effect for the write file connector and the WITH LOCK phrase is specified or implied, the record lock associated with the record written is set when the execution of the WRITE statement is successful.' WriteShared: wantLock = phrase==WithLock && LocksEffective (LOCK MODE not None, not SHARING NO OTHER); lock set only when status[0]=='0' via _physical.LockRecord on c.LastWrittenRecordId. The 'implied' arm: the only source of an implied WITH LOCK is §9.1.16's 'implicit LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC WITH LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS' for files subject to commit and rollback (cite.py --check 9.1.16 -> OK); APPLY COMMIT is refused by name (COBOLNET1709, CONFORMANCE.md A.4.3 Not claimed), so no compilable program reaches that arm — the same vacuity the owner recorded as CONFORMS for commit-antecedent rules (kb/Work PB371). Automatic locking does not lock on WRITE (§14.9.51.3 SR22 forbids the phrase; the concept text locks on READ). cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the WITH LOCK phrase is specified or implied' -> OK rule 11.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: A successful WRITE releases the record to the operating environment, not to a buffer: SequentialConnector.ReleaseRecord is the ONE release point every write arm reaches, and for a file another connector shares it flushes the record out before the statement returns, which is what makes it visible to that connector's read and what stops the next append landing on top of it. The keyed organizations release into the per-physical-file shared record store, which every connector over the path sees. All three write arms release (the print-control arms never did).

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR13: 'the content of the bytes that extend outside the end of record-name-1 are undefined.' An undefined result imposes no observable requirement; the connector pads to the record width (Fit / FitRecord) and any content there is conforming. cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the content of the bytes that extend outside the end of record-name-1 are undefined' -> OK rule 13. Nothing to test.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1190 (registrar 14c). GR14: the record size 'shall not be larger than the largest or smaller than the smallest number of bytes allowed by the RECORD IS VARYING clause ... If this rule is violated, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status of the write file connector is set to '44'.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 14). The plain sequential arm (Write, IsVarying branch) and RelativeConnector/IndexedConnector (Stored -> null -> '44') enforce it: PROBE pa.cob V9/V2 plain -> 44; pb.cob relative random VARYING 3 TO 8, VL=9 and VL=2 -> 44. BUT the print-control arm never sees the length: FileRegistry.WriteAnyOrg calls f.WriteAdvancing(image, advance.Lines, ...) with no length parameter, and SequentialConnector.Write itself reroutes to WriteAdvancing(image, 1, ...) whenever _printControl or a LINAGE page is present, before the IsVarying check. PROBE E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out/probe/write-p2/pa.cob: FD VF RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 3 TO 8 DEPENDING ON VL; VL=9 WRITE VR AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE -> '00' (expected '44'); VL=2 WRITE VR BEFORE ADVANCING 1 LINE -> '00' (expected '44'); then VL=5 plain WRITE -> '00' but the medium holds all 8 X's with no length prefix (the DEPENDING length is dropped on every write once the connector has seen print control). DIVERGES on the print/LINAGE arm; the literal-1/identifier-1 (FILE phrase, A.4.13 Not claimed) and FORMAT clause (A.4.8) halves are outside the claimed surface.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1190 (registrar 14c). GR15: 'If the execution of a WRITE statement is unsuccessful, the write operation does not take place, the content of the record area is unaffected, and the I-O status ... is set' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 15). Every unsuccessful arm returns before any stream/store traffic ('48', '44', '71', '24', '22', '34', '21', and the WITH LOCK preflight '53'/'54' which WriteShared answers before WriteAnyOrg). The runtime receives the record area as an image string and never writes back into it. PROBE pa.cob: after '48' SR still 'BBBBB'/'CCCCC'; after '44' VR still 'XXXXXXXX' and nothing reached wp2a-v.dat for the two plain '44' writes; pb.cob: the refused '21' indexed record never entered the file. Transfer of control: EOP phrases guarded on successful status (SequentialIoEmitter snapshot), INVALID KEY only on '2x' (EmitInvalid), USE hook after the status store. The print-arm GR14 miss is recorded under GR-14.9.51.4-14, not here. Golden conformance:85/l1_open_not_open_statements pins 'write does not take place' but not the record-area half, so it is not named as closing this row: test-needed. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The write-does-not-take-place half fails on the print-control arm. On a record-sequential RECORD VARYING file, a WRITE with an ADVANCING phrase whose DEPENDING length is outside the VARYING bounds is UNSUCCESSFUL under GR14 ('44'), and GR15 then requires that the write operation not take place. The runtime skips the bound check on that arm (the mechanism the adjudicator filed under GR14), so the record reaches the medium. The observable file content therefore breaks GR15 as well as GR14's status. The other unsuccessful arms verified: 48/44 plain/24/22/21/71/53-54. One mechanism (the print arm with no length parameter), so a fix of the GR14 finding closes this too.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR16: 'The RETRY phrase is used to control the behavior of the WRITE statement for files opened for file sharing for the case where resources needed to write a record are locked by another run unit. The I-O status is set in accordance with the rules in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 16). The antecedent is unpopulatable in this implementation: COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN §14.7.9 GR2 determination (CONFORMANCE A.1 items 165/166) — every file and record lock is held by a connector of the executing run unit, and WRITE defines no record operation conflict. WriteShared therefore binds the RETRY phrase (grammar retryPhrase, GateRetryIntro 2002) and makes the first attempt decide. The one resource denial WriteShared CAN return, the §12.4.5.9 GR7 lock ceiling '53'/'54' from PreflightNewLock, bypasses RetryLoop — kb/Work PB707 (open) owns that as a where-the-rule-is-written defect, behaviour-identical today (no re-attempt within one run unit can clear the ceiling). No verdict-changing edge found.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR17: 'The successor relationship of a sequential file is established by the order of execution of WRITE statements when the physical file is created. The relationship does not change except when records are added to the end of a physical file.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 17). The sequential connector appends each record to one forward-only writer (OUTPUT = FileMode.Create, EXTEND = append stream, PB739 made shared append re-seek to the end), so read-back order is write order; REWRITE overwrites in place (never reorders). Golden l1_open_extend_position's sequential leg reads back SEQ001, SEQ002, SEQ003 after an EXTEND append — the order of execution of the WRITEs.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: The EXTEND write-ordinal base is the record count present at OPEN, measured before this OPEN's own writer exists (kb/Work PB713); the goldens read the appended record back as the successor of the existing one on every organization and framing.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Two sharing-active file connectors extending one physical file each append after every record present at the moment of the write: a participant's writer is HostFile.OpenConnectorWriteStream's SharedAppendStream, which repositions at the physical end before every write instead of at the .NET FileMode.Append offset captured once at open. The record's ordinal is minted from the shared PhysicalFileTable.State.ReleasedOrdinal, so the two connectors' releases are 2 then 3 rather than 2 twice. Only the relative ORDER of the two connectors' records is undefined by this rule; both goldens read all three records back on every organization and framing. COBOL-85 has no file sharing, so the rule's antecedent cannot arise there. kb/Work PB740 renamed the role to HostFile.OpenConnectorWriteStream and moved its shared-vs-plain choice onto the 9.1.15 file lock the connector's handle carries (FileLockPosture.AdmitsAnotherWriter) instead of onto whether the SELECT wrote a SHARING or LOCK MODE clause: the same change made two CLAUSE-LESS connectors openable EXTEND on one physical file for the first time, and keying the repositioning stream on a clause would have left exactly that pair anchoring two buffered writers at one offset. The rule and its evidence are unchanged; this row is re-recorded because the symbol it names moved.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1192 (registrar 14c). GR20: 'When an attempt is made to write beyond the externally-defined boundaries of the physical file, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status value of the write file connector is set to '34'.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 20); §9.1.13.6 item 3: 'The implementor specifies the manner in which these boundaries are defined.' (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 -> OK rule 3). Searched src/Cobol.Net.Runtime: FileStatusCode.PermanentBoundary ('34') has exactly one producer, RelativeConnector.Write (GR29 b)); no sequential write arm (SequentialConnector.Write / WriteAdvancing / EmitLineSequentialRecord / ReleaseRecord) can return '34', and none catches IOException — a write that exhausts the host medium surfaces as an unhandled System.IO.IOException from the StreamWriter (or a '30' from the CLOSE flush). IoStatusClass.WriteBoundary consumes a sequential '34' (SORT GR15 / MERGE GR12 loop) that nothing produces. docs/CONFORMANCE.md carries no determination of how the boundaries are defined (DOC-A.1-151 explicitly declines to answer it). Not probed (needs a full volume); the verdict rests on the absence of any producer.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1191 (registrar 14c). GR21: 'For a line sequential file with a file description entry not containing a RECORD clause with the DEPENDING phrase, any spaces to the right of the rightmost non-space character are not transferred to file-name-1. If record-name-1 is specified implicitly or explicitly as alphanumeric, a space is defined to be the alphanumeric space character. If ... as national, a space is defined to be the national space character.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 21). The core case holds (PROBE pc.cob: PIC X(8) 'AB' -> line 'AB'; ' C D' keeps its interior/leading spaces; PIC N(4) N"AB" -> 00 41 00 42; VARYING without DEPENDING -> trimmed). TWO divergences: (1) the alphanumeric arm is string.TrimEnd(), which strips every Unicode White_Space character, not the alphanumeric space character. PROBE E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out/probe/write-p2/pd.cob: LR PIC X(8) = 'AB' + X"A0" (U+00A0, a MEMBER of the line sequential character set per CONFORMANCE DOC-A.1-115, 'every character whose code point is U+0020 or above') -> the file holds 'AB' CRLF; the U+00A0 was dropped (expected 'AB' U+00A0 CRLF). (2) the national flag is per-CONNECTOR (EmitNationalAreaRegistration: any national record description marks the whole FD), while GR21 keys on record-name-1: PROBE pd.cob FD LM with 01 LMN PIC N(4) and 01 LMX PIC X(8); WRITE LMX with 'AB' -> 'AB' + six 0x20 + CRLF (expected 'AB' CRLF). The emitter's own comment records (2) as a known RESIDUAL. LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 introduction (DOC-A.1-115).

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB329 (LANDED 2026-09-05) built this rule's mechanism; kb/Work PB689 gave it a ROW. The row did not exist when PB329 landed -- an interior '## SEQUENTIAL FILES' heading truncated 14.9.51.4's rule block at GR16, so GR17-GR42 were never in the catalog and PB329's implementer had nothing to close. RULE: 'For a line sequential file, if the record area contains one or more characters that are not in the implementor-defined character set defined for a line sequential file, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71.' cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71' -> OK 14.9.51.4 23). MECHANISM: LineSequentialCharacterSet is the one executable copy of the Annex A.1 item 115 determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-115: every character at or above U+0020 is a member, the C0 controls below it are not), and SequentialConnector.RecordAreaOutsideLineCharacterSet is the one call shape. BOTH write entry points consult it -- Write and WriteAdvancing -- ahead of every shape branch, because the rule is organization-scoped rather than shape-scoped, and ahead of any stream traffic because 9.1.13.10 item 1 requires the record area and the medium to be left unchanged. (There were THREE until kb/Work PB712, 2026-09-06, deleted WriteBeforeAndAfter: 14.9.51.2 Format 1 prints ONE ADVANCING operand, so the COBOL-2023 BEFORE AFTER pair is a placement and reaches WriteAdvancing like every other print-control write. The arm count fell; the coverage did not.) The test is CHARACTER-wise, not byte-wise: a national record area is walked two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE, so N"CD"'s 00 43 00 44 is two members and not two control characters. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe before PB329 landed: a line sequential WRITE of a record holding 0x00 reported STATUS=00 and left the byte on the medium; after, STATUS=71 and the file is 0 bytes. Goldens walk 09 (READ, 14.9.30.4 GR16), 71 (WRITE, THIS rule), 71 (REWRITE, 14.9.35.4 GR17d), the unchanged medium, and the set boundary (0x7F -> ordinal 128, 0xFF -> ordinal 256 are members) at 2023, the one edition the LINE SEQUENTIAL organization exists in. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 INTRODUCTION - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization", and 9.1.6 / 9.1.7.1 still name exactly three organizations with 9.1.7.2 splitting the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types. The organization therefore does not exist below 2023 (the pass now rejects it with COBOLNET0900, registry row file-organization-line-sequential-2023), the 2002 and 2014 copies of the golden were deleted as programs no edition below 2023 can express, and this row's editions are 2023 alone.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work R43 (owner, 2026-09-24): an unsupported facility is unsupported entirely — item 3: a rule whose trigger can only arise through an unsupported capability closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT, CONTINGENT: re-adjudicate if the capability is ever added (kb/Work PB1198 Q2). §14.9.51.4 GR24's reel/unit swap needs an end of reel/unit recognized inside a multi-volume physical file; COBOL.NET provides no reel or unit medium (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 A.3 items 26, 28-30, 33-34; A.1 item 24), and the witness pins that every connector kind reports a non-unit or mass-storage category (§14.9.6.4 GR2 (a)/(d)), so no WRITE can recognize an end of unit. The READ twin GR-14.9.30.4-23 was closed earlier by an owner-signed §8 derivation.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB964. The omitted ADVANCING phrase acts as AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE: its ONE advance (one LINAGE-COUNTER step, §13.18.34.4 GR7) is placed by the device's line state (SequentialConnector.ImplicitAdvanceIsBefore) - FIRST when an AFTER-placed record stands on an unterminated line (GR25 f)), so the record lands on the next line; otherwise the stream's record-then-terminator shape already puts it on a fresh line. Every plain-WRITE arm (print/LINAGE reroute, line sequential with and without LINAGE) asks that one property; before PB964 a plain WRITE after an AFTER write welded two records onto one physical line on every sequential organization. a) n lines = n line terminators; c) zero = no travel (overprint = same line); d) mnemonic = implementor-defined zero-line advance, the record always released; e)/f) BEFORE presents then advances, AFTER advances then presents; g) PAGE on a LINAGE file repositions to the next logical page; h) PAGE with no LINAGE = a form feed. Determination: every sequential file supports vertical positioning, so the ADVANCING phrase is never ignored. b) (negative identifier) is undefined.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB686 + PB523 LANDED - THE CONDITION WAS ALREADY MEASURED; ARM a)'s REPOSITIONING SENTENCE IS NOW MEASURED TOO, ON BOTH ORDERINGS. What this row was PARTIAL for was named exactly: arm a) does not stop at the condition, it also says 'the device is repositioned to the first line that may be written on the next logical page and the logical record is presented on that line', and for any file with a LINES AT TOP phrase that first writable line is past the top margin, which 13.18.34.4 GR4's discarded operand made unreachable - the counter landed right and the device did not. Both are now decided in one place: PositionOnLogicalPage computes the condition and calls BeginNextLogicalPage, which travels the rest of the current page (unwritten body lines plus the bottom margin, GR5), re-evaluates the operands (13.18.34.4 GR6 b) 3, 'before the device is positioned and after all positioning on the current page') and steps one line onto the next page, leaving the device on its line 1 with the new top margin still to materialize. Bytes_TopAndBottomMarginsAreLinesOfTheLogicalPage pins the AFTER ordering ('the device is repositioned ... and the logical record is presented on that line' - the record after the wrap is on page-2 body line 1, physical line 11, not on the first line of the page and not on the line after the old body); Bytes_OverflowWithBeforePhrase_PresentsThenRepositions pins the BEFORE ordering ('the logical record is presented and the device is repositioned'), which was previously exercised only by nist:SQ201M and now has a spec-derived fixture. The a)/b) DISCRIMINATION and the c == page size boundary are unchanged and stay adjudicated in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 4 ('DETERMINATION - the 14.9.51.4 GR26 a)/b) boundary at LINAGE-COUNTER = page size'), pinned by conformance:2023/pb686_linage_gr26_boundary and its 85 twin on BOTH arms of the FOOTING dispatch. RESIDUE, deliberately not folded in here: GR27's choice between EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW and EC-I-O-EOP is GR-14.9.51.4-27's row and the EC subsystem is a later slice.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB854. a) PositionOnLogicalPage records WHICH arm caused the end-of-page condition (GR26 a) -> EC-I-O-EOP-OVERFLOW, GR26 b) -> EC-I-O-EOP) and WriteSucceeded reports the name beside the successful '00' through the connector's rule-named condition channel (the one EC-I-O-LINAGE uses); both names now have mask bits. b) the END-OF-PAGE phrase runs on the success guard, and __IoCheckEc's success arm dispatches nothing for an EOP name when the phrase is present, while the condition is still SET (EXCEPTION-STATUS names it inside the phrase). c) the exception-checking PERFORM's WHEN takes it and the matching USE is ignored (2023 golden). d)/e) the USE declarative, or nothing. RELATIVE/INDEXED connectors present no page and raise neither name. COBOL-85 has the phrase but not the names (negative: COBOLNET0878).

subject: WRITE statement
notes: GR28: 'If, during the successful execution of a WRITE statement with the NOT END-OF-PAGE phrase, the end-of-page condition does not occur, then after execution of the input-output operation, control is transferred to imperative-statement-2 of the NOT END-OF-PAGE phrase. If control is returned from imperative-statement-2, control is then transferred to the end of the WRITE statement.' (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 28). EmitWrite snapshots the connector status before the FILE STATUS store and USE hook, then renders `if (successful && EndOfPage) {AT} else if (successful) {NOT}` — the NOT arm runs only on a successful write without the condition, after the operation, and falls to the end of the statement. Both orders of the phrases parse (writeAtEndOfPage choice indicators). Goldens conformance:2023/pb686_linage_gr26_boundary and conformance:85/pb686_linage_gr26_boundary_85 print 'NO-EOP' on exactly the writes that land inside the page body (spec-derived per the PB686 determination).

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1192 (registrar 14c). GR29 a)/b) (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 -> OK rule 29, both items). VERIFIED by PROBE E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out/probe/write-p2/pb.cob: a) OUTPUT with RELATIVE KEY PIC 9 releases 1..9 consecutively, the 10th -> '24' with INVALID KEY run and RK left at 9; OPEN EXTEND after 9 records -> next RRN 10 overflows PIC 9 -> '24'; KeyedIoEmitter moves RelativeSlot into the key item only on success; b) DYNAMIC I-O existing key 2 -> '22' INVALID KEY; key 0 -> '34' (no invalid key). Shared-extend non-consecutive numbering is PB739's (landed). DEFECT on b)'s last sentence: 'If the relative key data item contains a value that is less than 1 or greater than the highest relative record number permitted for the file, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful, and the I O status ... is set to '34'.' RelativeConnector.Write tests only key < 1; there is no highest permitted RRN, so any key is accepted, and RelativeConnector.Persist then allocates `new string?[_st.Highest]`. PROBE E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out/probe/write-p2/pe.cob: ACCESS RANDOM, RELATIVE KEY PIC 9(18), MOVE 999999999999999999 TO RK, WRITE -> '00', CLOSE -> Unhandled System.OverflowException (run unit killed; the file is left at 20 bytes). Expected: the implementation's highest permitted RRN (bounded by what the store can represent) is exceeded -> '34', the record not written, the CLOSE clean. Keys in the tens of millions also allocate an array of that length at every CLOSE.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'Subsequent records released to the operating environment have consecutively higher relative record numbers' -> OK 30)): in extend mode the first record gets highest-existing RRN + 1, later records get consecutive numbers, and the RRN is MOVEd into the RELATIVE KEY item. Code: extend mode can only be reached with ACCESS SEQUENTIAL (§14.9.27.3 SR2), and RelativeConnector.Write's sequential arm takes NextSequentialSlot() = Max(_st.Highest, _lastReleasedSlot) + 1. That is highest-existing + 1 for the first record and consecutive after it, because nothing else releases between two writes on an unshared file (GR31 covers the shared case). KeyedIoEmitter.EmitWrite then StoreArith's FileRelativeSlot into the key item when the status is successful: a MOVE-rule numeric store, with Truncation. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). rel1.cob: OUTPUT writes RRN 1..3; a DYNAMIC connector adds RRN 5; OPEN EXTEND then writes 'E-OK 00 RK=6', 7, 8, 9 (consecutive, starting at highest+1), and the 5th write overflows RELATIVE KEY PIC 9 with 'E-INV 24'. The read-back walks 1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9. The test l1_open_extend_position is spec-derived: it seeds records 1 and 4 sparsely, and EXTEND gives RK=0005. It covers the first-record and MOVE sentences; the consecutive-subsequent sentence is witnessed only by the probe. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: The relative key values two sharing extend connectors receive are ascending: the slot is Highest+1 read from the shared store at the moment of the release, clamped to this connector's own last release so a sibling's DELETE cannot make them regress. Over a file holding RRN 1 the goldens display R-KA=0002 and R-KB=0003, and both records read back. The number used to be captured once at OPEN, which made both connectors mint 2 and the second store write replace the first record. COBOL-85 has no file sharing, so the rule's antecedent cannot arise there.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the value of the relative key data item shall be initialized by the runtime element with the relative record number to be associated with the record that is to be written' -> OK 29); the same sentence is GR32's, rule 32). If that item cannot be resolved it emits a LOUD statement, not a silent write. RelativeConnector.Write's non-sequential arm then puts the record at _pendingKey. subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1192 (registrar 14c). Three arms. a) (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 "When the value of the relative key data item specifies a record that already exists in the file, the I-O status associated with the write file connector is set to '22'" -> OK 33)) CONFORMS: `_slots.ContainsKey(key)` gives DuplicateKey. Probe rel1.cob: RKD=5 a second time gives 'INVDUP 22' and runs the INVALID KEY branch; RKD=2 (a record written sequentially) gives 'INV2 22'. c) (--check 'When the number of significant digits in the relative record number is larger than the size of the relative key data item specified for the file' -> OK 33)) CONFORMS for sequential release: `slot.ToString().Length > _keyDigits` gives '24'. Probe: PIC 9 key, 10th RRN gives 'E-INV 24'; PIC 9(2) COMP key, 100th write gives 'B100 INV 24 RK=99' (key not stored). b) (--check "When an attempt is made to write outside the externally defined boundaries of the file, the I-O status associated with the write file connector is set to '24'" -> OK 33)) is NOT realized. The relative store defines no boundary at all. §9.1.13.5 item 4 (--check 9.1.13.5 'The implementor specifies the manner in which these boundaries are defined' -> OK 4)) requires the implementor to define one, and CONFORMANCE.md has no such determination. Probe rel2.cob: a RANDOM write of RRN 5,000,000 into an empty file gives 'OK 00', and CLOSE writes a 20,000,024-byte store: RecordFraming writes a 4-byte gap tag for every empty slot, and its MemoryStream is flushed with an (int) length. A RELATIVE KEY value in the high hundreds of millions (legal for a PIC 9(9)+ key) therefore gets '00' at WRITE and fails later, at CLOSE, with an allocation/stream-length failure. That is reasoned from the code and was not run, because of its memory cost. Arm b) should have produced '24' at the WRITE. Separately, a key below 1 gets '34' ('Z 34', no INVALID KEY branch). That follows GR29 b)'s explicit sentence (--check 14.9.51.4 'If the relative key data item contains a value that is less than 1 or greater than the highest relative record number permitted for the file' -> OK 29)), while GR33 b) plus §9.1.13.5 4) put a relative-file boundary violation under '24' and §9.1.13.6 3) confines '34' to SEQUENTIAL files. The standard conflicts with itself here, and no determination records which sentence governs. PARTIAL: a) and c) are verified and b) is not implemented. See the finding. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'Successful execution of a WRITE statement causes the content of the record area to be released' -> OK 34)): the record is released, and the operating environment uses its record keys so that later access by any of them works. Code: IndexedConnector.Write appends a KeyedRec holding the whole record image with one release ordinal stamped under EVERY key. Every retrieval path (FindRandom, Ordered, START) derives the key from that image through KeyOf, so every declared key is an access path. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). idx1.cob: a record written through the DYNAMIC connector is found by the prime key ('RK47 d6') and walked under the alternate key ('A K47 d6'); U01 written RANDOM is found by the alternate key ('UZ U01'). No spec-derived golden is aimed at this rule, so test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1072 (registrar 14c). Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'The comparison used for ensuring uniqueness, for ordering records, or for suppressing records' -> OK 35)): the comparison follows the file's collating sequence and the rules for a relation condition. Uniqueness and ordering CONFORM: KeyCompare applies the key's CobolCollation (null means native ordinal, which is §12.4.5.7.4 GR6's default for a clause-less file). Probe idx1.cob, file COLLATING SEQUENCE IS ALPHA ("A" ALSO "a"): after A01, WRITE a01 is refused 'C2 INV 21', because a01 collates EQUAL, so it is not greater. B01 is then accepted. The SUPPRESSING arm DIVERGES. IsSuppressed calls KeyEq(KeyOf(image), lit) with lit = CobolLiteral.Decode(literal text). That value is not space-extended, although a relation condition extends the shorter operand (--check 8.8.4.2.7 'comparison proceeds as though the shorter operand were extended on the right by sufficient alphanumeric spaces to make the operands of equal length' -> OK 2)). A figurative constant or ALL literal is never expanded to the key's length either, although §12.4.5.6.3 SR7 admits both. Re-run of the sibling probe out/probe/alternate-record-key-clause/gr6.dll (SUPPRESS WHEN SPACES / "X" on PIC X(3) / ALL "*"): every alternate walk still returns records 01 and 03, whose key values equal the suppression value. The alternate-record-key-clause and rewrite-statement-p2 adjudications found the same mechanism. PARTIAL would understate it: one of the three comparisons the rule names gives the wrong answer. DIVERGES. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it); the 'suppressing records' arm is 2023 only (SUPPRESS WHEN, Annex E.3.3 item 42)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'The value of the prime record key shall not be equal to the value of the prime record key of any record existing in the file' -> OK 36)). Code: `_recs.Any(r => KeyEq(KeyOf(r.Image, PrimeKey), prime, PrimeKey))` gives DuplicateKey '22', using collation-aware equality, and the record is not added. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). idx1.cob: a DYNAMIC WRITE of K30, which the sequential connector wrote earlier, gives 'D3 INV 22' and runs INVALID KEY. The sequential-access equal-key case gets '21' first (GR42 a), which is the correct precedence: GR38's order test comes before existence. KeyedIoDifferentialTests.Indexed_RandomCrudByPrimeKey is legacy-pinned and does not qualify, so test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'The data item specified as the prime record key shall be set by the runtime element to the desired value prior to the execution of the WRITE statement' -> OK 37)): the program sets the key before the WRITE. Code: EmitWrite passes the record area's current image (OperandText.RecordAreaImage), after any FROM move, and IndexedConnector.Write takes the prime key from that image with KeyOf at execution time. So the value the program placed there before the WRITE is exactly the key used, and nothing is cached from an earlier statement. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). from1.cob: WRITE K-REC FROM WS-KSRC ('K01DATA1') and then READ with key K01 gives 'K=[K01DATA1]'. This shows that the key set by the FROM phrase's implicit MOVE, before the release, is the key used. No test is aimed at this rule, so test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'If the record is not in the sequence above, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful' -> OK 38)). Code: the sequential arm refuses `KeyCompare(prime, _lastWrittenPrime) <= 0` with '21'. OpenCore seeds _lastWrittenPrime with the highest existing prime key under EXTEND, and the comparison uses the file's collating sequence. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). idx1.cob, OUTPUT: K20 is written, then K10 gives 'S2 INV 21', K20 again gives 'S3 INV 21', and K30 and K40 succeed. EXTEND over a file whose highest key is K40: K35 gives 'E1 INV 21', K50 is accepted, and K45 then gives 'E3 INV 21' (it must exceed the highest key written through this connector). With COLLATING SEQUENCE ALPHA ('A' ALSO 'a'), a01 after A01 gives 'C2 INV 21'. The spec-derived golden l1_open_extend_position (K004 as the first record of an extend session over K002/K006/K008 gives 'XW2=21') covers the extend first-record sentence. The unit tests SharedExtendOpenDriftTests and SharedExtendWriteDriftTests cover the shared case. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'WRITE statements may release records to the operating environment through that connector in any order' -> OK 39)). Code: the '21' order test is guarded by `sequentialRelease`, which is Access == Sequential, so random and dynamic access skip it. `_lastWrittenPrime` is updated only on the sequential arm. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). idx1.cob: a DYNAMIC I-O connector writes K05 (below every existing key) and then K47 (between existing keys), with 'D1 02' and 'D2 02' ('02' because alternate AA duplicates, which is correct). No golden is aimed at this rule; pb771_keyed_file_lock cites it only in passing, for lock behaviour. Test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'If the DUPLICATES phrase is not specified and the alternate key value is non unique, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful' -> OK 40)). Code: for each alternate key, `exists && !_alts[i].Dups` gives '22' and the record is not added. With DUPLICATES, the record is added with a fresh release ordinal under every key (ReleaseOrdinals), so a sequential walk returns duplicates in the order they were written. Probe dir: out/probe/write-statement-p3/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). idx1.cob: FU (ALTERNATE U-ALT, no DUPLICATES): U01/ZZ gives 'U1 OK 00', U02/ZZ gives 'U2 INV 22', and a random READ by ZZ still returns U01. Through FX/FR (X-ALT WITH DUPLICATES): K20, K30, K40, K50 are written sequentially and K05, K47 dynamically, all with alternate key AA, and START KEY = R-ALT then READ NEXT walks K20, K30, K40, K50, K05, K47. That is the write order, not prime-key order. The '02' of §9.1.13.2 2c accompanies each duplicate. The '22' that a SUPPRESSED alternate key raises today is a GR41 defect, not this rule's. No spec-derived golden is aimed at the WRITE side (l1_read_alt_dup_walk is a READ GR26 golden), so test-ref is empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is in every edition's relative/indexed WRITE text; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change to it)]

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1072 (registrar 14c). Rule (cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'Key entries that are suppressed shall not cause a duplicate key condition to exist' -> OK 41); --check 'the record shall be logically positioned so that it will not be found when accessed using the alternate record key' -> OK 41)). Code: Write skips a suppressed key in the uniqueness loop (`if (IsSuppressed(image, i)) continue;`). The structure is right, but IsSuppressed only matches a literal that is exactly the key's length. The binder stores CobolLiteral.Decode(literal text), which leaves a figurative constant or ALL literal as its source text, and KeyCompare with no collation is string.CompareOrdinal, with no space-extension (§8.8.4.2.7 2)). Measured by re-running out/probe/alternate-record-key-clause/gr6.dll: R-A1 (no DUPLICATES) has SUPPRESS WHEN SPACES, and the second record whose R-A1 is SPACES gets 'W2 22'. The spec requires '00', because both entries are suppressed and 'shall not cause a duplicate key condition'. The record is LOST. The walks under R-A2 (SUPPRESS WHEN "X", PIC X(3)) and R-A3 (SUPPRESS WHEN ALL "*") return 01 and 03, whose values equal the suppression value, which violates a) and b). A quoted literal of exactly the key's length does suppress (the l1_rewrite_alt_key_suppress golden exercises REWRITE with such a literal). DIVERGES, wrong answer. The sibling adjudications alternate-record-key-clause (GR-12.4.5.6.4-6) and rewrite-statement-p2 (GR-14.9.35.4-L4.x) filed the same mechanism, and no kb/Work note in the dossier owns it yet. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 (SUPPRESS WHEN is new in 2023: Annex E.3.3 item 42; VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 230)]

subject: WRITE statement

That is reasoned from the code, not measured. PARTIAL: a), b), c) and the lock sentence are verified and d) is not implemented. This is the same mechanism as GR33 b); see the finding. notes: UPHELD after varying the RECEIVER as well as the argument. Repertoire appends exactly one character per input character (a substitution replaces, never expands or drops), so the returned string's length is always argument-1's character count, and under D-N1 one national position is one UTF-16 char and one usage-display position. RAN MYSELF at --std 2023: FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(PIC N(5))) -> 005; the same over a PIC N(3) containing a SUBSTITUTED U+4E16 -> 003, so substitution does not change the length; the ZERO-LENGTH national literal FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N"") -> LENGTH 000 and an all-space receiver, which is correct since 15.26.3 carries no zero-length-literal prohibition (its 15.66.3 r3 twin does); a SUPPLEMENTARY-plane national literal in a PIC N(2) -> LENGTH 002 and '??', consistent with the declared D-N1 one-code-unit-per-position model; a reference-modified argument N-SRC(1:3) -> 3; a national GROUP of two PIC N(2) items -> 4. subject: E function
notes: Verdict SURVIVES; the note is corrected and the SPEC BASIS the adjudicator missed is supplied. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'standard-binary arithmetic is in effect' -> OK (rule 2). THE PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER, re-verified by me on the built CLI: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode with COBOLNET0806 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL' - a HARD error at --std 2002 (alongside COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'), 2014 and 2023, and NOT downgradable by --permissive (2023 adds the COBOLNET0903 obsolescence warning and still errors). Nothing in the tree computes 14114126198520207781233383725636853 / (2 ** 112); CobolIntrinsics.E() is the only body and is Math.E in every mode. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and it is F.2 ITEM 3 - not Annex E - that records the non-implementation: '3. STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' (cite.py --check F.2 'STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item' -> OK). CITATION REPAIRED 2026-08-31, and the error was worse than a wrong annex letter: the sentence as previously quoted here ('it has not been implemented ... by any COBOL provider', singular) is F.2 ITEM 5's, which is about the VALIDATE FACILITY - a real clause answering a different question (feedback_a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question). Item 3 also carries the reevaluation note that makes the decline REVISITABLE: 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: the STANDARD-BINARY keyword of the ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only; the compiler's own edition gate agrees - 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode. The honest cover is a negative case pinning that FUNCTION E under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE; a mode-only rejection test that never names E would not cover this row. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

(b) NATIVE x FLOAT-BINARY-32/-64 -> must be ACCEPTED, because §11.9.5.2 GR4 makes the absent ARITHMETIC clause NATIVE and r2's antecedent is then false. (c) STANDARD-DECIMAL x COMP-1/COMP-2 -> must be ACCEPTED, because neither is a §3.166 usage. subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → NOT-IMPLEMENTED, same two grounds as rule 2. (1) EDITIONS: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` (§11.9.5/§8.8.1.4) and the §3.167 standard decimal floating-point usages (float-decimal-16, float-decimal-34 — USAGE per §13.18.60.4 GR17/GR18) are both COBOL-2014 additions; the rule as worded does not exist at COBOL-2002. (2) VERDICT: no code implements this rule anywhere — the prohibited combination is doubly unreachable through two INDEPENDENT non-supports that have nothing to do with §15.43, so nothing has ever evaluated the rule's condition. Both non-supports are conformance-legal and I re-derived them rather than inheriting them: DataBinder rejects STANDARD-BINARY with COBOLNET0806, and Annex A.3 item 2 reads 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (NOTE 1 adds that the mode is obsolete); FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/34 are rejected at ParseUsage with COBOLNET1564 under A.3 item 19. Worth recording for whoever revisits this: A.3 item 3 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL processor-dependent TOO, so COBOL.NET's support for it is a choice, not an obligation — which is why rule 2's combination is writable and rule 3's is not. Vacuous truth is not implementation: if either half is ever supported, nothing enforces this. No spec-derived test, and none constructible. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. subject: MAX function
notes: VERDICT UPHELD, on stronger evidence than the original, with one citation corrected. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. CONTINGENCY WORTH RECORDING: this rule governs which of the TIED arguments is returned; whether the tie is real is RV-15.59.4-1's question, and at the boundaries documented there the 'greatest value' premise is itself wrong. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. REFUTER'S DECISIVE CASE - an equal-value tie between DIFFERENT contents, on the non-identity-PCS weights overload: E:/Temp/rfmax/tiew.cob (RFMAXTIEW) `OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL.` / `SPECIAL-NAMES. ALPHABET AL IS "A" ALSO "B", "C", "D".` with P1 PIC X VALUE "A", P2 PIC X VALUE "B" prints REL=A-EQ-B (the program's own relation condition confirms the tie is real), then `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(P1 P2) TO R1` -> T1=A and `MOVE FUNCTION MAX(P2 P1) TO R1` -> T2=B. The selection follows ARGUMENT POSITION over two operands that are equal but not identical, which is leftmost-wins in the form the rule states it. Corroborating, from the original adjudication (size-tie form): E:/Temp/pbmax/maxsize.cob `01 S3 PIC X(3) VALUE "AB". 01 S6 PIC X(6) VALUE "AB".` -> `STRING FUNCTION MAX(S3 S6) ... INTO R12` = C1=[AB |********] (size 3) and the reversed order C2=[AB    |*****] (size 6); national, E:/Temp/pbmax/maxnat3.cob `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(N3 N6))` -> L1=000C (3) and `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION MAX(N6 N3))` -> L2=000F (6); zero-length leftmost, maxzl2.cob `FUNCTION MAX("" SP)` -> Z=[|***********]. Refuter's alphabetic-item repeat, E:/Temp/rfmax/cats.cob: `FUNCTION MAX(AL1 AL2)` over PIC A(3)/PIC A(6) both VALUE "ABC" -> ALPHA1=[ABC|********], reversed -> ALPHA2=[ABC   |*****]. CONTROL: E:/Temp/rfmax/ctl.cob compiles and runs (CTLNUM=0099, CTLSTR=XYZ). subject: MODULE-NAME function
notes: Verdict SUSTAINED after an independent attempt to make the gate reject LEGAL source, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 4 forbids and which a containment predicate is most likely to produce. `InNestedProgram = unit.Parent is not null` is read off the BOUND unit at binder construction (BinderDriver.BindUnitProcedure), so I probed the containment shape most likely to leave Parent unset: a program NESTED INSIDE A FUNCTION DEFINITION. It is accepted and correct, which is the answer the rule requires (the rule says 'within a nested program', not 'within a nested program of a program'). The runtime half cannot desynchronise from the compile-time half either: ProgramTable.CallProgram sets the frame flag from the same registry containment fact (`isNested: n.ParentPath is not null`) that produced BoundUnit.Parent. Rejection inside a METHOD body is the spec answer and not an accident — a method is not a nested program. Also confirmed the cited test is SPEC-DERIVED despite living in a file named ...DifferentialTests: AssertSpec/AssertRejected compare against a fixed expected string and a named diagnostic code, never against the legacy oracle or GnuCOBOL, so the test-ref is admissible. EVIDENCE: New probe E:/Temp/mnref/fnnest.cob: PROGRAM MNRFNN-IN nested inside FUNCTION-ID MNRFNN, called from MNRFNMAIN via `MOVE FUNCTION MNRFNN TO W`. Compiles and runs: 'FI-NST=[MNRFNN-IN]', 'FI-CUR=[MNRFNN]', 'FI-ACT=[MNRFNN]', 'FI-STK=[MNRFNN;MNRFNMAIN; ]', 'W=[OK]'. subject: PI function
notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-binary arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-binary-2014', IntroducedIn 2014, ObsoleteIn 2023), so this rule cannot apply at 2002 - confirmed empirically, the sibling STANDARD-DECIMAL clause is rejected at --std 2002 with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'. The rule's precondition can never hold: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is rejected at bind time with COBOLNET0806 (DataBinder.BindDeclarations), re-verified on the built CLI as a HARD error at both --std 2014 and --std 2023 and NOT downgradable by --permissive. No code computes the exact binary128 value 16312081666030376401667486162748272 / 2**112, and none can while the mode is refused. The non-support is already recorded in CONFORMANCE.md SS2 row 2 ('ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1)') and licensed by ISO Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' BARE QUESTION: should SS15.73.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by that existing Annex A.3 item-2 non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? TEST-REF STRUCK on review: the previously cited StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported exercises the MODE rejection and never references PI or any returned value, so it does not cover this rule - test-needed (a test pinning that FUNCTION PI under STANDARD-BINARY is refused by name would be the honest cover). || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

subject: SQRT function
notes: CLOSED by kb/Work PB246. Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.84.4 'the returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1' -> OK, rule 4 - and the rule's own lead-in is 'When native arithmetic is in effect', so CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt IS this rule's site and the SDIDI lane answers to r2 instead. THE APPROXIMATION HALF WAS ALREADY CONFORMING (Math.Sqrt is IEC 60559 correctly-rounded, and SQRT's Codomain.None is correct because 15.84.4 states no bound, so the FromDoubleBounded clamp must not apply). THE ABSOLUTE-VALUE HALF WAS NOT IMPLEMENTED AT ALL, only unreachable-by-argument: grep Abs over the file returned nothing. The rule does not say 'made non-negative when negative'; it says the returned value IS the absolute value, and IEEE abs clears the sign bit - |-0.0| is +0.0 while IEC 60559 mandates sqrt(-0) = -0 EXACTLY so that sqrt is not the absolute value there. Negative zero is therefore the unique input on which r4's phrase does work, it is a LEGAL argument-1 (15.84.3 r2 admits zero) that a COMP-1/COMP-2 item reaches by ordinary native underflow, and the receiver-less/float arm renders it unquantized through CobolFloat.Display, which is IEEE-faithful and prints the sign. Math.Abs on the result IS r4. OBSERVABILITY MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED - the row's predecessor reported this as an unverified edge because it was read-only: 2002/pb246_sqrt_absolute_value_and_domain DISPLAYs the argument first (NZ=-0, so the probe demonstrably IS a negative zero and not a plain zero) and then SQL=0 on the receiver-less arm, SQR=0 into a COMP-2 receiver that stores the signed zero bit for bit, and SQ4=00200 on a fixed-point receiver. SIBLING SWEEP: ABS's own body is already Math.Abs; STANDARD-DEVIATION now composes 15.86.4 r1's expression literally - FUNCTION SQRT of FUNCTION VARIANCE - in both carriers, so neither re-decides this rule through a bare Math.Sqrt or CobolDec.Sqrt. float_intrinsic and pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage are retained as the binary64-pipeline evidence they are.

subject: SUM function
notes:
Citation re-derived mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.88.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"` => OK, §15.88.3 rule 1 (Argument rule). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Verified row `["SUM"] = Uniform('n', "§15.88.3 r1")` (line 693, in the 'statistical trio' block beside STANDARD-DEVIATION and VARIANCE); IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Uniform builds an ArgSchema with EMPTY positional kinds and a TAIL rule, so `schema.At(i)` yields the 'n' rule for EVERY argument position — which is what §15.88.2's repeated `{ argument-1 }` needs, since every written argument IS argument-1. Enforcement: IntrinsicBinder.cs#CheckArgumentClasses (line 1652) is called on the generic path at line 587, AFTER arity and BEFORE every per-function arm; it loops all positions and calls IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation. For kind 'n', Violation reads CandidateClasses(op) and Admissible('n') = [CobolClass.Numeric] — so a numeric-EDITED item (Table 2 class alphanumeric, mapped to CobolClass.NumericEditedDeEditing) is rejected too, which the arm's comment derives from §8.8.1.1 ("an identifier referencing a NUMERIC DATA ITEM"). VERIFIED EDGES: (a) a GROUP argument — ClassOfPlace returns Alphanumeric for `Item.IsGroup` (National/Boolean for an as-if-pic group), so `FUNCTION SUM(grp)` is rejected; (b) an INDEX item — the usage-keyed arm returns CobolClass.Index before the category table, so it cannot pass as numeric; (c) a table(ALL) argument — TableAllPlace is a `PlaceDecorator(Element)` (Place.cs:158), so `p.Item` is the ELEMENT and the element's class is screened, i.e. `SUM(alphaTable(ALL))` is rejected, not failed open; (d) the figurative ZERO is admissible here by §8.3.3.6.4 GR4 (CandidateClasses gives it Numeric among four), correct behavior per the batch's rule 8. FAIL-OPEN residue, deliberate and documented at the Violation head: an operand whose class is not statically decidable (candidates empty) is not screened — that can only miss a rejection, never invent one. TESTS: tests/conformance/negative/pb58-sum-alpha.cob (`COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(N9 X3)`, header cites "ISO 15.88.3 r1", reject-at 2002 2014 2023, expected diagnostic COBOLNET1627 in the .err, registered in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json:192) and the positive twin tests/conformance/2023/pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob line 75 (`FUNCTION SUM(N9 I2 3.5)` — registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:124). Nothing missing for this rule.

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): citation re-derived independently — `cite.py --check 15.88.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"` => OK, §15.88.3 rule 1; spec text re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33501-33504. Attacked on four axes and each held. (1) TWO-ARM DISPATCH (the shape that has recurred five times in this repo): both `functionCall` alternatives that can spell SUM — the FUNCTION-keyword arm (IntrinsicBinder.cs:89) and the reserved-word keyword-omitted arm `SUM(…)` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:78, CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn) — converge on the SAME BindIntrinsicCore (line 438), whose generic path calls CheckArgumentClasses; there is no unscreened second route, and KeywordOmittedFunction cannot reach SUM at all because a reserved word never arrives in the cobolWord name slot. (2) ArgSchema.At(i) (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:172) returns the Tail rule for EVERY i when Positions is empty, so Uniform('n') genuinely screens all n positions of the repeated argument-1, not just position 1. (3) The two classifier holes I probed are closed: a ref-modified numeric item resolves through RefModPlace.Category (Place.cs:292ff), which implements §8.4.3.3.4 GR6 c) — numeric under display usage is considered class alphanumeric — so `FUNCTION SUM(N9(1:2))` is rejected; and a nested USER-DEFINED function result does NOT fall into the fail-open `BoundComputedOperand => CobolClass.Numeric` catch-all, because UdfBinder.UdfBindCall returns `new BoundNumRef(tempPlace)` over a temp cloned from the RETURNING item's description (§8.4.3.2.4 GR1), so it reaches the screen as a BoundFieldOperand carrying the real category and an alphanumeric-returning UDF is rejected. (4) EDITIONS: CheckArgumentClasses is gated only on `ctx.Edition.Permissive`, never on the edition, so the screen fires at --std 85 as well; the negative fixture's `reject-at: 2002 2014 2023` omits 85 only because that same fixture declares `01 TDEF TYPEDEF STRONG` and `01 NAT PIC N(2)`, both COBOL-2002+ constructs that would make an 85 run reject for the wrong reason — not because the rule is edition-gated. subject: SUM function
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB252). THE PRIOR RECORD'S OWN LANE (b) DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, and that is what this landing corrects. It read: '`case "SumScaled" or "RangeScaled"` takes AlignedArgs ... and calls CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled (`Int128 s = 0; foreach (x) s += x`) ... the alignment is escape-checked (CobolNum.RescaleEscape), so an argument that cannot be represented in the Int128 intermediate raises the size-error condition instead of wrapping.' RescaleEscape bounds each ALIGNED ARGUMENT and says nothing about their SUM: `Int128.Abs(value) > Int128.MaxValue / Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)`. MEASURED on the compiler's own exe before the fix, inside the 31-digit cap: `P PIC S9(31) VALUE ALL '9'` beside `Q PIC SV9(7)`, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(P P P Q) ON SIZE ERROR ...` -- each aligned argument (9.99e37) passes the per-argument bound (1.70e31 at scale 7), their sum 2.9999e38 exceeds Int128.MaxValue and wrapped to -4.028e37, which at scale 7 fits a 31-digit receiver, so the phrase was NOT taken and a SIGN-FLIPPED value was stored silently. The EAE's true value (3x10^31 - 3) needs 32 digits, so Sec.14.7.5 rule 3 makes the size error condition exist there with NO implementor latitude at all. FIX: the accumulator is now `checked` under one try for the whole loop and escapes through CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SizeEscape -> CobolSizeError/EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, which ArithmeticEmitter lands on the ON SIZE ERROR arm leaving the receiver unchanged (Sec.14.7.5 rule 1). GOVERNING CLAUSE CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE: the message text had carried PB32's inherited 'ISO Sec.8.8.1.2 rule 7', which is a REAL clause answering a DIFFERENT question (arithmetic expressions are exempt from the composite-of-operands limit); the rule that makes this the size error condition is Sec.14.7.5 rule 5 -- 'if native arithmetic is in effect and the implementor defines that the range of values allowed for the intermediate data item is to be checked, when an arithmetic operation on the intermediate data item would cause the new value to be outside of the allowed range' (--check 14.7.5 -> OK). ALL THREE LANES NOW READ AND EACH IS THE Sec.15.88.4 r1 EAE: (a) standard modes -> SumDec on the SDIDI, left to right; (b) NATIVE fixed-point -> the checked Int128 accumulator, exact until the D1 boundary and then LOUD; (c) NATIVE with a float argument -> SumReal. Left-to-right accumulation is normative (Sec.8.8.1.2 rule 3, --check OK), so a partial sum that escapes the carrier IS an r5 size error even when later terms would bring the total back inside -- the modular cancellation the old unchecked `s += x` happened to deliver was two's complement's answer, not the standard's. CLOSING EVIDENCE: conformance:2002/pb252_native_carrier_boundary pins the r3 case (no latitude) and a control well inside the carrier; the drift test closes the whole exact-carrier entry-point set by reflection, so a new variadic exact function cannot ship unguarded. Both were verified to FAIL on the pre-fix build (SUM-R3-SIZE-ERROR=NO, RANGE-SIGN=NEGATIVE). EDITIONS: carried forward as adjudicated; the witness itself needs 31-digit items so it lives in the 2002 corpus (COBOL-85 caps fixed-point at 18 digits, COBOLNET0802).

subject: TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB254). The PARTIAL was leg a's UPPER half, defeated above 2**63 by the intake, not by the body. CITATIONS RE-DERIVED MECHANICALLY, none inherited: cite.py --check 15.90.4 "less than 16 010 000 or greater than 99 999 999" -> OK (15.90.4 1) a)); --check 15.90.4 "The year is not within the range 1601 to 9999" -> OK (1) a) NOTE 1); --check 15.90.4 "The date is valid" -> OK (1) d) NOTE 4); --check 15.90.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer" -> OK (15.90.3 rule 1); --check 15.3 "results in an incorrect value for that argument" -> OK (15.3 rule 14); --check 8.3.3.3.2 "fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits" -> OK. THE DERIVATION. 15.90.3 r1 is the WHOLE argument rule and constrains nothing but integer-ness; 15.90.4 r1a is a CATCH-ALL over both directions, so the function is TOTAL over the integers and every integer argument has a defined verdict. 15.3 rule 14 sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION only when evaluation 'results in an incorrect value for that argument or for the returned value according to the rules specified in the function definition' - there is no such value here, so a conforming program may pass any integer and must receive a verdict, never an abort. THE DEFECT, re-probed on this tree before the fix, not inherited from the note: (a) FLOAT lane - 01 FBIG USAGE COMP-2, COMPUTE FBIG = 1.0E19, FUNCTION TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD(FBIG) printed 00, i.e. 1) d) 'The date is valid', where r1a requires 1; the body was CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#TestDateYyyymmddReal = 'TryIntegerArg(...) ? CobolDate.TestDateYyyymmdd(n) : 0' and the literal ': 0' tail is the verdict for VALID. (b) CHECKING-ON lane - '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' with 01 BIG19 PIC 9(19) VALUE 9999999999999999999 terminated the run unit: 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): the intrinsic integer argument 9999999999999999999 is outside the range the function can represent (ISO 15.3)' - on CONFORMING source. (c) NATIVE/Dec lane printed 01, the right code by COINCIDENCE ONLY: CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArg substituted the checking-off default 0 for the ARGUMENT and 0 lands in the same r1a arm (0 < 16 010 000); the coincidence evaporates under checking, which is lane (b). THE FIX is at the validator, never at the shared narrowing: CobolDate.TestDateYyyymmdd now takes Int128 and answers r1a before any conversion (past the guard the value is eight digits, so the int narrowing is exact); IntrinsicRenderer's 'case "TestDateYyyymmdd" or "TestDayYyyyddd"' arm takes the WIDE intake IntArgWide -> AsIntWide, which has no raise point and, unlike AsInt, carries the U (UInt128) carrier arm as well; TestDateYyyymmddReal classifies by r1a on the VALUE, so +/-infinity and every magnitude past the window answer 1 without narrowing, and the one input that is the value of no integer (a NaN) routes to the shared 15.3 raise site and substitutes the documented implementor-defined result 1, never the 0 that would call a non-date a valid date. ", digitCap: 34" : ""`, and NvScan's parameter takes 31 or 34 and nothing else; the renderer's own comment at line 263 records the omission ("standard-binary's 35 rides the P12/P13 STANDARD-BINARY wave"). I do not record that verdict, because the established adjudication of the identical shape is an owner question, not a defect: RV-15.27.3-2 (FUNCTION E) and RV-15.73.3-2 (FUNCTION PI) are both open at NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION on exactly this precondition, on the grounds that Annex A.3 item 2 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY processor-dependent, Annex F.2 makes it obsolete, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2 already records the non-support — the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, which decision D13 reserves to the owner; plan §4678 still carries "STANDARD-BINARY (2014 pending row)" as unresolved. BARE QUESTION: should §15.93.4 rule 1 sub-note 3 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence), as proposed for its FUNCTION E / FUNCTION PI siblings, rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? One decision should settle the whole family. EDITIONS derived independently of IntrinsicCatalog: the STANDARD-BINARY alternative of the OPTIONS ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only — the derivation recorded and re-verified on RV-15.27.3-2), so the precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; the two load-bearing claims were the kind a refuter must not take on trust — an INHERITED precedent and an asserted diagnostic — and both check out): (1) The claimed precedent is REAL, not remembered. I read tests/version-matrix/traceability-inventory.json directly: RV-15.27.3-2 (§15.27.3, subject "E function") and RV-15.73.3-2 (§15.73.3, subject "PI function") both carry verdict NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION, editions "2014,2023" and an EMPTY test-ref, and RV-15.27.3-2's note independently records the same COBOLNET0806 mechanism re-verified on the built CLI. This row's verdict, editions and empty test-ref are consistent with the family, so the adjudicator is not inventing a third disposition. (2) The diagnostic is a hard Error, not a warning: DataBinder.cs:318-320 reads exactly as quoted, `Edition.Error("COBOLNET0806", ...)`, and the surrounding comment (306-320) confirms the mode is documented-unsupported at EVERY edition that has it. (3) I re-confirmed the absence of any 35 independently: DigitCapFlag is the only producer of a digitCap argument, it is two-valued, and NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal (line 394) resolves to StandardDecimal-or-Standard, never StandardBinary — so no path can pass 35. NOT-IMPLEMENTED would be the code-only verdict, and I considered recording it, but batch rule 6 reserves the documented-non-support disposition to the owner and the sibling rows fix the family's shape; the bare question stands as put. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'Argument-1 shall be a data item of class alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national.' -> OK (r1). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified["TRIM"] = Schema("§15.96.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: MatchArgument1) — position 0 declares kind 's', and Admissible('s') = {Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National} (IntrinsicArgumentRules.Admissible), so Violation() rejects class numeric, boolean, index, object and pointer for argument-1. §8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts alphabetic and numeric-edited under alphanumeric, so 's' is exactly r1's three classes in this model (PicCategory folds PIC A into Alphanumeric — the CobolClass enum comment). The screen is REACHED on this bespoke path: IntrinsicBinder.BindTrim calls CheckArgumentClasses(sig, operands) at line 1010 before building the node (the generic path returns earlier), and CheckArgumentClasses walks schema.At(i). Positive coverage in both admitted rows: intrinsics_trim (PIC X(10) argument-1) and pb15_result_type_follows_argument (PIC N(8) and PIC X(8) argument-1, TRIM-N=[CDE] / TRIM-X=[CDE]). Figurative ZERO passes (candidate classes include alphanumeric — §8.3.3.6.4 GR4, PB48) and pb48_figurative_zero_intrinsic_argument pins it.
