Deliberate latitude recorded, NOT scored as a defect: r1 says 'a DATA ITEM', and the implementation also admits an alphanumeric/national LITERAL argument-1. That is what §15.6 Table 21 types TRIM's argument-1 as (Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1) and what §15.3 type 2 admits ('A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal'), and §15.96.4's own NOTE writes TRIM("aabbcc" "c" "b") — rejecting a literal would reject the standard's own example. Editions from Annex §E.3.3 item 31 (--check OK: 'The TRIM function has been enhanced…', i.e. TRIM predates 2023) plus kb/Work R28's landed primary-source decision (WG4/J4 CD 1.2 Annex D.2 lists TRIM among the 2014 introductions); NOT derived from the IntrinsicCatalog row. REFUTED: verdict SUSTAINED — attacked on three axes and it held. (a) The load-bearing latitude citation was NOT inherited: I re-ran cite.py --check 15.3 'A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal shall be specified' -> OK (§15.3 2), and read §15.6's own legend in the transcription ('A digit immediately following the argument type indicates the argument's position in the list of arguments') beside the Table 21 TRIM row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md — 'Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1, Alph2 … or Anum2 … or Nat2 … or Key2 or Key2 and Alph2 …'. The literal admission is the standard's, and the Key2-then-Alph2 ordering independently corroborates the FMT-15.96.2 order finding. (b) The REJECT half was re-read rather than accepted: IntrinsicArgumentRules.CandidateClasses/ClassOf1 return a FIXED class for every operand shape that could carry a forbidden argument-1 — BoundComputedOperand{Expr: BoundIntrinsicCall} → ClassOfCategory(ic.ResultCategory), BoundComputedOperand{Expr: BoundIndexRef} → Index, bare BoundComputedOperand → Numeric, BoundFigurative 'N' (NULL) → Pointer, and ClassOfPlace keys USAGE INDEX before the category table — none is in Admissible('s'), so Violation() REPORTS instead of the candidates.Length==0 fail-open. FUNCTION TRIM(FUNCTION ABS(N)) is a compile-time §15.3 rejection, not the run-time StrArgVisitor LoudValue abort (the wrong-stage family). (c) The ALL shape was checked, since FUNCTION TRIM(ALL T) puts a TableAllPlace at position 0: ClassOfPlace reads p.Item, so argument-1's class is still screened there. The editions claim was chased to its source rather than inherited — kb/Work/R28.md's 'LANDED 2026-08-08' section names the WG4/J4 CD 1.2 (2009-08-23) Annex D.2 item 4 list verbatim, and R28's earlier body explicitly warns the 2023 PDF cannot settle a 2002 window; the adjudicator used the landed half, correctly.

notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS, re-verdicted by the kb/Work PB245 golden round (2026-09-09). THE RULE: §15.96.4 r1 'If LEADING is specified, the returned value is a character string that consists of the characters in argument-1 beginning from the leftmost character position that does not contain any argument-2' (cite.py --check 15.96.4 on that sentence -> OK, rule 1). DERIVED BEFORE THE RUN, and the derivation is the row's whole point: read alone, r1's 'does not contain ANY argument-2' is a SET UNION over the argument-2s, which is what this compiler used to compute; r5 ('each argument-2 is processed completely in the order that they are specified') and its NOTE (TRIM(a b c) = TRIM(TRIM(a b) c)) make r1 a rule about ONE argument-2 applied at each level of a nesting. The two readings differ whenever the argument-2 characters INTERLEAVE at the edge. Hand-derived: TRIM('bbxbb' LEADING 'b') = 'xbb' (r1's base case); TRIM('bcba' LEADING 'b' 'c') = 'ba' where the union gives 'a'; the order-reversed TRIM('bcba' LEADING 'c' 'b') = 'cba', a DIFFERENT answer over the same argument-2 set, which no order-blind reading can produce; TRIM('abcb' LEADING 'a' 'b' 'c') = 'b' where the union gives a zero-length result. MEASURED: all four as derived. WHAT CLOSED IT: kb/Work PB117 replaced the one char[] union and single TrimStart(set) with the sequential fold. The pre-existing witness pb117_trim_sequential holds ONE LEADING case and is kept; this row's rule is now measured with one argument-2 and with several, against the union answer written beside every line.

Rule: 'If resources needed to create a new object are not available, the returned object reference is set to NULL, and the EC-OO-RESOURCE exception condition is set to exist and is propagated back to the runtime element that invoked the New method.' (cite.py --check 16.2.1.2 -> OK §16.2.1.2 2)). BASE__FACTORY.__New catches the allocation failure of __Create (the one resource a managed object's creation can lack) and raises EC-OO-RESOURCE through ExceptionState.OoResourceError — FatalIfEnabled over the new OoResourceChecking flag, which EcEmitter's gate table sets for EC-OO-RESOURCE — and otherwise returns NULL. Every emitted New site stores NULL into the receiving item before the call (OoEmitter.EmitNew), so the item is NULL on both legs, including when the raised condition is handled by a declarative. Witnessed through the creation seam (a golden cannot exhaust memory).

subject: FactoryObject method
notes: kb/Work PB1506, LANDED (wave 59). Rule: 'When invoked on an instance object, the FactoryObject method determines the class of the object and returns a reference to the factory object associated with that class.' (cite.py --check 16.2.2.2 -> OK §16.2.2.2 1)). The runtime BASE.FACTORYOBJECT() returns __FactoryOfClass, which every emitted BASE-derived class overrides with its own factory singleton, so the most-derived override is the runtime class's factory. pb1548_standard_class_base: an object of D held in an A-typed reference answers D's factory (line 3 'D-FACTORY'), SELF "FactoryObject" in an inherited method likewise (line 7), and through a reference described BASE into a universal item (line 8). Not FINAL (§16.2 declares no FINAL), so a subclass may OVERRIDE it and redefining it without OVERRIDE is §11.7.3 SR4a's COBOLNET0837 (StandardClassBaseTests).

subject: COPY statement
notes: kb/Work PB1354 (registrar 15a). General format: COPY {literal-1|text-name-1} [{OF|IN} {literal-2|library-name-1}] [SUPPRESS PRINTING] [REPLACING {==pt-1== BY ==pt-2== | {LEADING|TRAILING} ==pw-1== BY ==pw-2==}...] . -- cite.py --check 7.2.3.4 'If the SUPPRESS phrase is specified, library text incorporated as a result of COPY statement processing is not listed' OK. COPY is not in the ANTLR grammar; the whole statement is a hand scan in ResolveOneCopy: name/literal, optional IN|OF qualifier, then REPLACING is recognised ONLY as the very next word, and everything up to the next '.' is skipped. Verified OK: text-name (cc_in_copy), literal-1 (pb82 golden), OF/IN literal-2 and library-name-1 (p03/p04 -> LIBAA), SUPPRESS alone and SUPPRESS PRINTING without REPLACING (p04/s05), multiple operand pairs (q07), LEADING/TRAILING (q09 TRAILING ==-X== BY ==-Q== -> AA-Q), lowercase (q10). DEFECT (wrong-answer): p01 'COPY BK1 SUPPRESS PRINTING REPLACING ==AA-X== BY ==BB-Y==.' -- the legal SUPPRESS-before-REPLACING order the format prints -- silently DROPS the whole REPLACING phrase (BB-Y undefined; with both names declared it would silently run the unreplaced text); expected: BB-Y declared, DISPLAY BB-Y prints HELLO (same as p02 without SUPPRESS). Under-rejects: s01 'COPY BK1 GARBAGE MORE.', s02 missing BY, s03 'REPLACING.' with no operand, s06 'PRINTING' without SUPPRESS all compile silently. Finding F1. || editions (adjudicator): all four editions (1985/2002/2014/2023) per the 2023 clause text; Annex E.2 item 1 bullet 4 changes only the non-pseudo-text REPLACING operands; the pre-2023 texts of this rule are not in-repo, so no earlier edition boundary is asserted

subject: REPLACE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1357 (registrar 15a). Rule: Format 1 REPLACE [ALSO] {==pseudo-text-1== BY ==pseudo-text-2== | {LEADING|TRAILING} ==partial-word-1== BY ==partial-word-2==}... . ; Format 2 REPLACE [LAST] OFF . (cite.py --check 7.2.4.2 "REPLACE [ ALSO ]" -> OK; "Format 2 (off)" -> OK). Code: ApplyReplaceStatements recognizes REPLACE OFF (MatchWord OFF) and otherwise ParseReplacements reads pairs, LEADING/TRAILING honoured, empty ==== accepted. DEFECTS: (1) ALSO and LAST are never recognized -- ParseReplacements reads the word ALSO/LAST as a non-pseudo-text operand and COBOLNET1641 fires; probe out/probe/replace-statement-p1/also.cob (REPLACE ==XX1== BY ==AAA==. / REPLACE ALSO ==XX2== BY ==CCC==. / REPLACE LAST OFF.) -> two COBOLNET1641 errors at lines 12 and 14; also2.cob (REPLACE LAST OFF. alone, legal per 7.2.4.4 6) b) 'A format 2 REPLACE statement has no effect') -> COBOLNET1641. The replace state is a flat list cleared at every REPLACE, so the 7.2.4.4 GR4/GR7 LIFO queue (part 2 rules) has no representation. (2) The required word BY is optional in ParseReplacements (if MatchWord BY): probe noby.cob 'REPLACE ==XX1== ==AAA==.' compiles and runs silently (AAA). Positive half verified: pseudo-text pairs, repetition, LEADING/TRAILING (conformance:2002/replace_partial_pseudo_text), REPLACE OFF, terminating period. Mixed -> DIVERGES (rejects-legal-source for ALSO/LAST). || editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 for the pseudo-text Format 1 and REPLACE OFF (the 2023 text; Annex E.2/E.3 record no REPLACE change 2014->2023). ALSO, LAST, LEADING/TRAILING partial-words: post-85 additions whose introducing edition the 2023 spec does not state (Annex E covers only 2014->2023) -- present in 2023.

subject: Compiler directives
notes: §7.3.2 general format '>>compiler-instruction' (cite.py --check 7.3.2 ">>compiler-instruction" OK). ONE parse of a directive line (CompilerDirectiveLine.TryParse: indicator, optional space, the compiler-directive word, operand) feeds every stage; the word is looked up in the constructs.json-derived CompilerDirectiveCatalog, and an unrecognized word is left in the text so the parser rejects it. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2\out\probe\cd): F1 '>>FOO BAR' -> COBOL0001; F3 bare '>>' -> COBOL0001; V1/V2 every 2023 directive word (LEAP-SECOND, COBOL-WORDS, FLAG-14, DEFINE, EVALUATE/WHEN/END-EVALUATE, PUSH, POP, TURN, PROPAGATE, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH, CALL-CONVENTION, DISPLAY, LISTING, PAGE, SOURCE) recognized with and without the space. Rejection of a non-directive '>>' is a generic parse error rather than a directive-specific diagnostic, which is acceptable. Operand shape per directive is SR-7.3.3-6's question, not this format row's. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the >> compiler-directive facility is absent from X3.23-1985; per-directive introducing editions are the §7.3.x rows' own, e.g. PUSH/POP added in 2023 per Annex E.3.3 item 38 and E.2 item 5)

subject: Defined condition
notes: Rule: 'compilation-variable-name-1 IS [ NOT ] DEFINED' (cite.py --check 7.3.8.4.2 OK). Grammar `definedCondition : cobolWord IS? NOT? DEFINED` matches the diagram (IS optional/not underlined, NOT optional, DEFINED required); DEFINED is a token only in a primed directive-expression fragment, so it stays a legal user word in source. Reachable from ccePrimary so it composes with AND/OR/NOT and parentheses. Probe p1.cob (2002/2014/2023): `VAR-A IS DEFINED`, `var-a DEFINED` (IS omitted, lower case), `VAR-B IS NOT DEFINED`, `VAR-A NOT DEFINED`, `X IS DEFINED AND NOT Y IS DEFINED`, `(X IS DEFINED) OR ...` all parse and select correctly; --std 85 rejects every >> directive with COBOLNET0900 (facility is 2002+). Unit test covers the IS and IS NOT spellings. Probe dir E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2\out\probe\defined-condition || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 compiler-directive facility incl. >>DEFINE/>>IF is not in ISO 1989:1985; no 2023 Annex E change to §7.3.8.4)

subject: CALL-CONVENTION directive
notes: The >>CALL-CONVENTION general format { COBOL | call-convention-name-1 } is the call-convention-directive-2002 row's directiveOperand column: plain braces, so exactly one shall be written, COBOL being one admissible word and any COBOL word an implementor-defined call-convention-name-1 (7.3.9.3 GR2 b). A literal or a missing operand is COBOLNET1911. The directive's EFFECT is the 7.3.9.3 GR1 default in every case - this implementation maps program-names one way - so the format, not the semantics, is what this row records.

subject: COBOL-WORDS directive
notes: kb/Work PB1373 (registrar 15a). Format: >>COBOL-WORDS { EQUATE literal-1 WITH literal-2 | UNDEFINE literal-3 | SUBSTITUTE literal-4 BY literal-5 | RESERVE literal-6 } (cite.py OK §7.3.10.2). TryParseOption switches on exactly one of the four option words (case-insensitive); TryBinary demands exactly 4 tokens with WITH/BY in slot 3 (wrong join word rejected), TryUnary exactly 2 tokens; any other shape is COBOLNET1623. Probed: all four options accepted, lowercase '>>cobol-words equate ... with ...' accepted (probe lower_kw), apostrophe-quoted literals accepted (apos_lit), unknown option / missing WITH / BY-for-WITH / no option rejected (unit theory). Literal-content defects are SR2/SR4 rows, not the format. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The four options, join words and arity are parsed correctly, but the operand tokenizer only splits on whitespace: a separator comma or semicolon between elements (legal anywhere a separator space is, §5.2.8 / §8.3.5 SR2) is rejected with COBOLNET1623, so legal source is rejected; and an UNTERMINATED quoted literal (no closing quote) is silently accepted as literal-6 (ReadQuoted returns end-of-string) instead of being diagnosed as a malformed literal. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 only (new in COBOL-2023: Foreword list 'Additional compiler directives were added: COBOL-WORDS directive'; Annex E.3.3 item 12, cite.py OK §E.3.3 12)); below 2023 the directive word is COBOLNET0900

subject: DEFINE directive
notes: kb/Work PB1367 (registrar 15a). Format: >>DEFINE compilation-variable-name-1 [AS] { {arith-expr-1|boolean-expr-1|literal-1|PARAMETER} [OVERRIDE] | OFF }. cite.py --check 7.3.11.2 "OVERRIDE" -> OK (general format). Every LEGAL form is accepted (probes p1b/q7/r1/t6: AS omitted, AS OFF, bare OFF, PARAMETER, PARAMETER OVERRIDE, value OVERRIDE, arith/boolean/literal). SplitDefine is a string splitter that under-rejects two ILLEGAL shapes: (1) '>>DEFINE X AS OFF OVERRIDE' compiles clean (probe n1.cob) - OVERRIDE belongs only to the value group, never to OFF (figure notes: outer brace = value group [OVERRIDE] | OFF); SplitDefine strips a trailing OVERRIDE before testing for OFF. (2) a bare '>>DEFINE' with no compilation-variable-name-1 compiles clean (probe t1.cob) - ApplyDefine 'if (name.Length == 0) return;' and the registry row's DirectiveOperandForm.Stage delegates the operand check to this stage. Expected: both rejected (COBOLNET1619-class directive-syntax error). Other malformed shapes ARE caught (t2 'OVERRIDE OVERRIDE', t3 'PARAMETER OFF', t4 '1 2', n8 missing operand -> COBOLNET1619). || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 - §7.3 compiler-directive facility; ISO/IEC 1989:2023 Annex E lists no change to §7.3.11 against 2014 (the 2002 introduction is not stated in the 2023 text itself; below 2002 the directive is COBOLNET0900)

subject: DISPLAY directive
notes: kb/Work PB807 (registrar 15a). cite.py --check 7.3.12.2 "PARAMETER" -> OK §7.3.12.2 (General format); cite.py --check 5.2.6.4 "Choice indicators" -> OK. Format: a REPEATED choice of arithmetic-expression-1 | boolean-expression-1 | literal-1 | PARAMETER compilation-variable-name-1, then an optional UPON phrase whose braces carry §5.2.6.4 choice indicators (compile-time-device-1 and/or LISTING, each at most once). Code: the row is {Form=Text, OperandRequired=true}; CheckOperand only tests operand.Length==0. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, 2023): dd4 '>>DISPLAY' -> COBOLNET1911 (presence half correct); dd2 '>>DISPLAY )( 3 +' -> exit 0, no diagnostic; dd5 '>>DISPLAY "A" UPON' -> clean; dd6 '>>DISPLAY "A" UPON LISTING LISTING' (LISTING twice, §5.2.6.4 at most once) -> clean. Presence half verified, operand grammar unimplemented -> under-rejects. Also the COBOLNET1911 text for the bare case says 'the general format admits no operand' (Admissible() over an empty Choice list) -- self-contradictory. Owned by open kb/Work PB807 (inventory_rows FMT-7.3.12.2). Probe dir E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/display-directive/ || editions (adjudicator): 2023 only (Foreword list of 2023 additions: 'Additional compiler directives were added: ... DISPLAY directive'); absent 1985/2002/2014

subject: EVALUATE directive
notes: kb/Work PB1363 (registrar 15a). Both formats: `{ >>WHEN ... [text-1] } ...` is a REQUIRED repeated group (figure note, cite.py --check 7.3.13.2 "shall be specified one or more times" OK), followed by ONE optional `[ >>WHEN OTHER [text-2] ]` and a required `>>END-EVALUATE`. The preprocessor is a flat frame stack with no phrase-order/cardinality state: WHEN, WHEN OTHER and END-EVALUATE arms each act on whatever frame is on top. Probes (probe dir out/probe/evaluate-directive-p1 (pinned adj-d2 cobol.exe, --std 2023)): A `>>EVALUATE 1 / >>WHEN 2 / >>WHEN OTHER (DISPLAY O1) / >>WHEN OTHER (DISPLAY O2)` compiles clean and prints `O1 | O2` (also at --std 2002) -- the second OTHER re-computes Emitting = ParentActive && !BranchTaken, so text-2 is included TWICE; B `>>WHEN OTHER (O1) / >>WHEN 1 (W1)` prints `O1 | W1` -- OTHER does not set BranchTaken, so a WHEN after it still matches and both branches' text is included, contrary to §7.3.13.4 GR4 ("all lines of text-2 associated with a WHEN OTHER phrase are omitted" when a WHEN is TRUE); C `>>EVALUATE 1 / text / >>END-EVALUATE` with no WHEN compiles clean (text silently omitted); D an EVALUATE unclosed at end of source compiles clean (frame stack never checked at EOF); E a stray `>>END-EVALUATE` / `>>WHEN 1` with no open EVALUATE compiles clean (arms guard on `_stack.Peek().Kind == Evaluate` and otherwise do nothing). What conforms: EVALUATE TRUE vs. subject dispatch, WHEN / WHEN OTHER / END-EVALUATE recognized, nesting via the stack, required subject (`>>EVALUATE` alone -> COBOLNET1619 malformed). Edition gate: evaluate-directive-2002 row, COBOLNET0900 below 2002 (pb725 negative). The END-EVALUATE trailing-operand half is PB806's (open). Finding: EVALUATE-directive phrase structure unvalidated. || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 compiler-directive facility, absent from 1985; Annex E E.2 item 8 shows the EVALUATE directive already in the previous standard)

subject: FLAG-02 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1374 (registrar 15a). Printed format (PDF p.100 / folio 70, rendered and inspected: ALL and ON carry NO underline; FLAG-02, the five option words and OFF are underlined). cite.py --check 5.2.3 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats' OK; --check 5.2.6.3 'If one of the alternatives contains only optional words, that alternative is the default and is selected unless another alternative is explicitly specified' OK; --check 5.2.6.4 'but any single alternative shall be specified only once' OK. So the outer braces' ALL alternative (optional words only) is the DEFAULT: `>>FLAG-02`, `>>FLAG-02 ON`, `>>FLAG-02 OFF` are legal and mean ALL ON / ALL ON / ALL OFF (GR2's 'a FLAG-02 directive ... that turns off all flagging options'). Code: TryParse returns 'no option or ALL is named' / 'no option and no ON/OFF phrase' -> COBOLNET1622 ERROR. Probes a/b/c.cbl: all three rejected (a.cbl(12,1): error COBOLNET1622). Opposite half: `>>FLAG-02 I-O-STATUS-07 I-O-STATUS-07 ON` and `>>FLAG-02 ALL ALL ON` are ACCEPTED (TryParse dedups silently, comment cites 5.2.6.4 but applies it as a merge, not a rejection) -> under-rejects (probes d/f). Verified correct: ALL alone, several options any order, trailing ON omitted = ON, ALL+option rejected, unknown word rejected, 2002 rejects (COBOLNET0900), 2023 warns obsolete (COBOLNET0903). Sibling (rule 4): FlagDirectiveLine.TryParse also REQUIRES ON/OFF for FLAG-14 though §7.3.15.2 prints ON bare too (outside this row set). probe dir: scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/flag02/ (pinned adj-d2 cobol.exe, --std 2014) || editions (adjudicator): 2014 (introduced: §7.3.14.1 — incompatibilities between ISO 1989:2002 and ISO/IEC 1989:2014); 2023 (obsolete element, §7.3.14.1 NOTE); not in 1985/2002

subject: FLAG-14 directive
notes: kb/Work PB1374 (registrar 15a). The printed format is >>FLAG-14 { ALL | { |option...| } } { ON | OFF }, with ALL and ON NOT underlined (spec figure note, PB808's glyph measurement against page 102, and errata D1). cite.py --check 5.2.3 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats' OK; --check 5.2.6.3 'If one of the alternatives contains only optional words, that alternative is the default and is selected unless another alternative is explicitly specified' OK. So ON is the default of the trailing braces (GR2 says 'explicitly or implicitly specified' -- cite.py --check 7.3.15.4 'If ON is explicitly or implicitly specified for an option' OK) and ALL is the default of the outer braces (which also resolves errata D1: omitting ALL means the same as writing it). FlagDirectiveLine.TryParse instead returns 'the ON or OFF phrase is required' for FLAG-14 and 'no option or ALL is named' when only ON/OFF is written. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/flag14/): FA '>>FLAG-14 VALUE-ZERO' -> COBOLNET1622 error (expected: accepted, VALUE-ZERO ON); FB '>>FLAG-14 ALL' -> 1622 (expected ALL ON); FC '>>FLAG-14 OFF' -> 1622 (expected ALL OFF); FD bare '>>FLAG-14' -> 1622 (expected ALL ON); FI '>>FLAG-14 ON' -> 1622 (expected ALL ON). Correct: explicit ALL ON/OFF, several options in any order (FF), lowercase words (FJ), unknown word and ALL-plus-option rejected. Second defect, under-rejection: FE '>>FLAG-14 VALUE-ZERO VALUE-ZERO ON' compiles clean because TryParse silently de-duplicates, but 5.2.6.4 says 'any single alternative shall be specified only once' (cite.py --check 5.2.6.4 OK). The green unit test FlagDirectiveTests.Parse_Flag14_MissingOnOff_IsError PINS the divergence, and DESIGN-flag-directives.md says 'FLAG-14 requires the choice', which contradicts the spec's own figure note. No open kb/Work note owns this (PB808 is the LISTING transcription note only). The spec figure note's closing sentence ('The trailing ON/OFF braces are a separate, required one-of-two selection') contradicts its own first paragraph; see dossier_gaps. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 (FLAG-14 is new in 2023 per 7.3.15.1 / Annex E new-features item 21; below 2023 COBOLNET0900 fires, verified with --std 2014)

subject: IF directive
notes: kb/Work PB1363 (registrar 15a). Format: '>> IF constant-conditional-expression-1 [ text-1 ] [ >> ELSE [ text-2 ] ] >> END-IF' (cite.py --check 7.3.16.2 "constant-conditional-expression-1 [ text-1 ]" OK). The format admits AT MOST ONE >>ELSE, only after an >>IF, and a REQUIRED >>END-IF. Render's switch handles the three words over a frame stack but never diagnoses a mismatch: case ELSE and case END-IF do nothing when the stack top is not an If frame, a second ELSE re-evaluates Emitting=ParentActive && !BranchTaken, and after the loop the stack is never checked for unclosed frames. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, probe/if-directive/): p02 orphan >>ELSE -> compiles, prints A and B; p03 orphan >>END-IF -> compiles, prints A; p04 >>IF V = 1 with no >>END-IF -> compiles, prints A; p05 two >>ELSE arms (V=1, IF V = 2) -> compiles, prints B then C; p12 >>ELSE inside >>EVALUATE TRUE -> ignored, prints W1 and EL. Expected: each is a violation of the general format and must be diagnosed. The well-formed shape conforms (p01: T1/U2 at 2002/2014/2023; conformance:2002/conditional_compilation) but the DEFECTIVE verdict forbids closing the row with it. Harm: under-rejects (p05/p12 also silently pick arbitrary text). New finding (no kb/Work note owns unbalanced IF/ELSE/END-IF; PB806 owns only trailing junk on ELSE/END-IF). || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §7.3 compiler-directive facility, incl. conditional compilation, is absent from COBOL-85; the pinned compiler gates >>IF at --std 85 with COBOLNET0900, probe p01)

subject: LEAP-SECOND directive
notes: { ON | OFF } with ON un-underlined in the printed format, so per 5.2.3 a bare >>LEAP-SECOND selects ON - the 'specified or implied' case 7.3.17.4 GR2/GR4 presuppose. Any other operand is COBOLNET1911. The 7.3.17.3 SR1 PLACEMENT rule is a different row and stays with the stage as COBOLNET1650.

subject: LISTING directive
notes: { ON | OFF } with ON un-underlined (rendered from the printed page, folio 78), so a bare >>LISTING selects it - which is what 7.3.18.3 GR4/GR5 call 'specifying or implying the ON phrase'. Any other operand is COBOLNET1911. The directive itself is a no-op under 7.3.18.3 GR1: this compiler produces no source listing.

subject: PAGE directive
notes: >> PAGE [ comment-text-1 ] - the operand is bracketed, so it is optional, and 7.3.19.3 SR2 states that comment-text-1 'is not checked syntactically'. The row's directiveOperand records that as form 'text' with the citation, so the absence of a content check is the standard's decision on the record rather than a gap. The directive is a no-op under 7.3.19.4 GR3 with no listing produced.

subject: POP directive
notes: { directive-name | ALL }, plain braces - exactly one shall be written. The admissible directive-names are DERIVED from the catalog itself minus 7.3.20.3 SR1's exclusions (EVALUATE, IF, PAGE, POP, PUSH), by ROW: >>POP WHEN is refused because WHEN is a word of the excluded EVALUATE directive. Anything else is COBOLNET1911.

subject: PROPAGATE directive
notes: { ON | OFF } with ON un-underlined, so a bare >>PROPAGATE selects ON; 7.3.21.4 GR4's OFF default is about omitting the DIRECTIVE, not about which alternative the format implies. Any other operand is COBOLNET1911 (kb/Work PB794 retired this directive's own COBOLNET0883). The runtime propagation SEMANTICS are separate rows and remain PHASE-13 residue; this row is the format.

subject: PUSH directive
notes: { directive-name | ALL }, plain braces - exactly one shall be written, with the admissible directive-names derived from the catalog minus 7.3.22.3 SR1's exclusions, by row. Anything else is COBOLNET1911.

subject: REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH directive
notes: { ON | OFF } with ON un-underlined, so a bare >>REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH selects ON. Any other operand is COBOLNET1911 (kb/Work PB794 retired this directive's own COBOLNET1576).

subject: SOURCE FORMAT directive
notes: >> SOURCE FORMAT IS { FIXED | FREE }, verified against the PRINTED page (folio 84): SOURCE, FIXED and FREE are underlined required words, FORMAT and IS are 5.2.3 optional words, and the braces are a plain required choice. The optional words are the row's optionalWords, so >>SOURCE FREE and >>SOURCE FORMAT IS FREE both select FREE; an operand that is neither, or none at all, is COBOLNET1911 and the line is still consumed (the reference format in effect carries on, since the directive selected none). kb/Work PB794.

subject: TURN directive
notes: kb/Work PB1365 (registrar 15a). Rendered PDF p115 (the printed diagram): ON is NOT underlined, so it is an optional word, and WITH is not underlined either; OFF, CHECKING, TURN and LOCATION are. GR6 says so again: 'If the ON phrase is specified or implied' (cite.py --check 7.3.25.4 "If the ON phrase is specified or implied" OK). ParseTurn sets on=true ONLY when the word after CHECKING is literally ON, otherwise on stays null -> COBOLNET0718 'malformed directive'. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/turn/): TRNP1 '>>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING' -> error COBOLNET0718 (expected: compiles, checking ON; the ADD's ON SIZE ERROR shows EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION as TRNP2 with explicit ON does); TRNP3 '>>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING WITH LOCATION' -> COBOLNET0718 (expected: ON implied + LOCATION). Under-rejection in the other direction: the parser 'break's after ON/OFF and never looks at the rest — TRNP5 '>>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING ON JUNK' compiles clean and runs; TRNP4 '>>TURN EC-SIZE CHECKING OFF WITH LOCATION' compiles clean (the format has no [WITH LOCATION] under OFF). TRNP6 'CHECKING ON LOCATION' (WITH omitted) is accepted — correct, WITH is an optional word. The exception-name/file-name ellipses are parsed correctly (TRNF3 'EC-I-O-AT-END F1 F2' two files; multiple exception-names). || editions (adjudicator): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the TURN directive is a COBOL-2002 introduction; §7.3 compiler directives)

subject: Alphanumeric literals
notes: Format 1 quote/apostrophe with character-1 optional (STR_BODY `(...)*`), Format 2 X"..."/X'...' with the hex sequence optional (HEXDIGITS `*`, caseInsensitive so x"4a" also lexes; 3.98 makes A-F equivalent to a-f). cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.2 "hexadecimal-alphanumeric" OK. Probe p1 (probe dir E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/anlit): 'it''s', "a""b", X'4142', x"4a4b", X"" all lex and decode ([it's][a"b][AB][JK][    ]). r03 golden rows 13/15/17/18 pin X"", X"4142", X'', X'4142' (both delimiters of Format 2, zero length); Format 1 apostrophe/quote parity is also pinned by conformance-test:ApostropheValueDifferentialTests.EmbeddedDelimiter_DecodesToOneCharacter_PerForm. The X"GG" (non-hex body) lexing hole is SR5's defect, recorded there. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (Annex E itemizes the 2014->2023 delta and lists no change to 8.3.3.2, so the rule stands in both; the 1985/2002 edge is NOT derivable in-repo -- no 2002 or 1985 text is held)

subject: Boolean literals
notes: Format 1 B"[0|1]..."/B'...' and Format 2 BX"[hex]..."/BX'...' with the character sequence OPTIONAL under both delimiters. BOOL_BODY = 'B' '"' [01]* '"' | 'B' apostrophe [01]* apostrophe | 'BX' '"' HEXDIGITS '"' | 'BX' apostrophe HEXDIGITS apostrophe, HEXDIGITS=[0-9a-f]* (caseInsensitive lexer). Probes out/probe/boolean-literals/bl1 (B"0101", B'10', BX"...", BX'f0', VALUE BX'0f') and bl12 (B"", B'', BX'', BX"") all accepted with correct values. cite.py --check 8.3.3.4.2 "hexadecimal-boolean" OK. No spec-derived test exercises the apostrophe spelling of either format (r03 covers BX"..." only) -> test-ref empty. Doc drift (not a verdict issue): CobolLexer.g4 comments above BOOLLIT and near line 979 still say 'BX"..." (hex boolean) is deferred', and the HEXDIGITS comment says Format 1 is '[01]+' while the rule is [01]*. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (boolean literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction, gated COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 - probe bl7; the zero-length-literal introduction edge is not derivable from the in-repo 2023 text, whose Annex E lists only the 2014->2023 delta)

subject: National literals
notes: Format 1 N"[character-1]..." / N'...' and Format 2 NX"[hex-character-sequence-1]..." / NX'...' are all one NATLIT token (NAT_BODY: 'N' STR_BODY | 'NX' '"' HEXDIGITS '"' | 'NX' '\'' HEXDIGITS '\''), HEXDIGITS is `*` so both formats admit zero length as the brackets require; lexer is caseInsensitive so n".." also lexes (prefix is not literal content, §8.1.3 case-equivalence). Probe p1: N"A""B", N'A''B', N"", n"xy", NX"00410042" in VALUE all compile and run correctly. The r03 golden pins NX both delimiters, zero-length NX"" and the F1 control N"CD". Content that is NOT hexadecimal inside NX".." is SR4's defect (silent split), not this format row. cite.py --check 8.3.3.1 "Hexadecimal digits are used to specify the value of the literal" -> OK. [editions as adjudicated: COBOL-2002, COBOL-2014, COBOL-2023 (national literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85, where the construct is rejected COBOLNET0900 via Constructs.NationalData2002)]

subject: Figurative constant values
notes: Formats 1-6 (ZERO/SPACE/HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE/QUOTE with the optional ALL, ALL literal-1) are the figurativeConstant rule; Format 7 (symbolic-character-1) binds through the SPECIAL-NAMES SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS path. kb/Work PB71 made Format 6 total over the literal kinds.

subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB1454 (also PB1455) (registrar 15c). Eight formats plus the data-qualifier and file-report-qualifier sub-formats. QualifiedNameClasses.All carries one row per format (drift-tested against the standard's text). PER FORMAT (pinned cobol.exe, --run, 85 and 2023): F1 qualified-data-name - probe e1 data-qualifier chains with gaps and the file-report-qualifier `FC OF FR OF FA` / `FC OF FA` resolve; report-name-1 half: `TOT1 IN R1` reads the sum counter (f4 -> 14) and `GENERATE DET OF RPT` via reportGroupReference (golden pb365); F2 qualified-condition-name - `condition-name [ data-qualifier ]... [ file-name-1 ]`, golden pb567 incl. the file-name leg; F3 qualified-index-name - `SET IX OF T OF G`, `IX IN G`, and (probe p1) an index in an FD record qualified by the FILE, `SET IX OF FA TO 3` / `FE (IX OF FR)` -> P1=54, golden pb919; F4 qualified-procedure-name - `PERFORM P2 OF S1`, `GO TO P3 OF S2`; F7 qualified-linage-counter - `LINAGE-COUNTER IN/OF file-name` (LinageConformanceTests); F8 qualified-report-counter - `LINE-COUNTER OF R1` / `IN R2` (probe h3 -> 002 003). F5 (qualified-screen-name) and F6 (qualified-record-key-name) belong to facilities docs/CONFORMANCE.md declares Not claimed - A.4.2 screen handling (refused by name COBOLNET1560/1707; derived selector `screen-handling-only`) and A.3 item 40 RECORD KEY SOURCE (refused COBOLNET1954) - so no screen-name or record-key-name is ever declared and those formats have no population; recorded here, not decided (owner decision D13; both are already covered by derived determinations). DIVERGENCES (see findings): (1) UNDER-REJECT - the grammar's `dataReferenceSuffix*` and `qualification : (OF | IN) cobolWord (subscriptPart | refModPart)*` admit subscripts and reference modifiers BETWEEN qualifiers, so probe n2 `MOVE 7 TO E (2) OF T`, `DISPLAY E (1) OF T E (2) IN T OF G` -> N8=57 and `S (2:2) OF G` -> N9=BC compile and run with NO diagnostic at 85 and 2023, where Format 1 carries no subscript and the identifier is `qualified-data-name-with-subscripts-1` (§8.4.3.1.2, --check OK) = `qualified-data-name-1 [ ( subscript … ) ]` (§8.4.2.3.2, --check OK), reference modification following the whole identifier; no CONFORMANCE.md extension row and no dialect gate records this leniency. (2) REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE - a sum counter's Format 1 data-qualifier (its report group's data-name) is refused (`TOT1 OF CF1` COBOLNET2145; `TOT OF CF2 OF R2` COBOLNET1639). (3) the Format 8 cross-report reference in the report section is staged COBOLNET0899 (rows SR-8.4.2.2.3-9/-10). [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Formats 1-4 and 7-8 in every edition; Format 5 qualified-screen-name belongs to the screen section, 2002+; Format 6 qualified-record-key-name to the RECORD KEY SOURCE phrase, 2002+)]

subject: Subscripts
notes: The subscript general format has exactly THREE alternatives and each now has a witness. ALL - pb62 (the three ranges GR1a defers to; vacuous at 85, which has no function for which the subscript ALL is allowed). index-name-1 [{+|-} integer-1] - 85/index_name_r7_windows and pb170. arithmetic-expression-1 - pb136 for compound expressions and pb877_subscripted_subscript for the shape that had no vehicle until kb/Work PB877: an identifier operand carrying its OWN subscripts. 8.8.1.1 admits 'an identifier referencing a numeric data item' and 8.4.3.1.2 Format 2 makes that identifier a qualified-data-name-WITH-SUBSCRIPTS, so X(1) is an arithmetic-expression-1 - but the declaration-informed '(' splitter asked DataItem.IsTable, which is only the first half of 8.4.2.3.3 SR2, so the identifier's own '(' opened a SECOND subscript and every such reference failed arity. It was loud on the receiving side (COBOLNET0899) and a run-time abort on the sending side. Format 1 (qualified-data-name-with-subscripts) and Format 2 (qualified-condition-name-with-subscripts) are both covered: the golden subscripts data-names, and ResolveForItem - the condition-name path, whose subscripts identify the occurrence of the CONDITIONAL VARIABLE - applies the same SR2/SR3 screen.

subject: Identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1425, PB1199 (registrar 15b). Eleven identifier formats (cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.3 6)/7) OK). There is no single identifier rule; the formats are spread over dataReference (F2, F3, F10 LINAGE_COUNTER (OF|IN) word, F11 LINE_/PAGE_COUNTER (OF|IN) word), functionCall with refModPart* (F1+F3), inlineMethodInvocation (F4), objectReference NULL|SELF|SUPER plus the EXCEPTION-OBJECT resolver name (F6), the object-property binder in ReferenceResolver (F7), NULL (F8), addressIdentifier (F9). Probe p1.cob (--std 2023): A OF G (N) -> G2G2; A OF G (N)(2:2) -> 2G; FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (W)(2:3) -> BCD; SET P TO NULL / IF P = NULL / IF P = ADDRESS OF W all TRUE. Probe o2.cob (--std 2002): NM OF D -> ABCDEF, INVOKE SELF / INVOKE SUPER dispatch correctly. l5.cob: LINAGE-COUNTER OF F1 / IN F2 resolve the right file (04 / 02). THREE DEFECTS: (1) FORMAT 5 object-view has NO surface: `SET U TO D AS UNIVERSAL` and `INVOKE D AS KBASE "SPEAK"` (o3/o4.cob) draw COBOLNET0901 "'AS' is a reserved word" - rejects legal source; (2) Format 6's `[object-class-name-1 OF] SUPER` arm: `INVOKE KBASE OF SUPER "SPEAK"` with a single INHERITS class (legal per 8.4.3.8.3 SR6, cite OK) draws COBOLNET0901 "'SUPER' is a reserved word" at 2002/2014/2023; (3) Formats 10/11 compile clean and ABORT at run time in every string-rendering context: `DISPLAY LINAGE-COUNTER`, `DISPLAY PAGE-COUNTER OF RPT1`, `DISPLAY LINE-COUNTER`, `MOVE PAGE-COUNTER OF RPT1 TO WA` (PIC X(4)) each emit NotImplemented.Value<string>("computed expression in a string context") (l2/l4/r1.cob) - ExpressionBinder binds a counter as BoundComputedOperand(BoundLinageCounterRef) and OperandText.AsStringVisitor.Visit(BoundComputedOperand) is loud on the premise that no general format admits one there; 8.4.3.15.3 SR1 (cite OK) admits the counters 'in any context where an integer data item may appear'. No open kb/Work note owns any of the three (searched object-view, OF SUPER, the string-context stub). Probes under out/probe/ident with the pinned cobol.exe. || editions as written by the adjudicator: Formats 1-3 and 10-11: 1985 (intrinsic functions via the 1989 amendment); Formats 4-9: 2002, 2014, 2023

subject: Function-identifier
notes: [FUNCTION] {function-pointer-name-1 | function-prototype-name-1 | intrinsic-function-name-1} [ ( [ {argument-1 | OMITTED} ] ... ) ] - rendered PDF p157: the arguments are bracketed INSIDE the parentheses, so the empty list is legal on both the keyword route (functionCall's functionArgList?) and the keyword-omitted route (subscriptOrRefMod : subToken*, kb/Work PB969). An empty group after a DATA reference is refused by name, COBOLNET2309 (ReferenceResolver.ScreenEmptyParentheses).

subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB1458 (registrar 15c). Format (cite.py --check 8.4.3.3.2 OK): identifier-1( leftmost-position : [ length ] ) - leftmost-position REQUIRED, length optional. Accept side verified at --std 85 and 2023 (out/probe/refmod-fmt/fmt1.cob): X(3:2)=CD, X(L + 1:L * 2)=CDEF, X(8:)=HIJ, X (2 : 3)=BCD, A OF G(2:3)=LMN, T(I)(2:2)=UV, T (I) (3:)=VW, X(L ** 2 - 1:(L + 1) / 3)=C, MOVE "zz" TO X(9:) writes positions 9-10; FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(X)(2:3)=BCD, T OF G(I)(1:2)=PQ, FUNCTION REVERSE(X) (1:) whole result. Reject side: X(1:2)(1:1) -> COBOLNET1630 (SR3), X(1:2:3) -> COBOLNET2363 (SR4), X() -> COBOLNET2309 naming §8.4.3.3.2. DEFECT (the PARTIAL): X(:2) - the REQUIRED leftmost-position omitted - is refused only by the PB1029 safety net COBOLNET2362 'refused without a diagnostic naming the rule it breaks; this is a COBOL.NET internal error', because ReferenceResolver's ref-mod arm calls RenderSegment(tokens.GetRange(0, colonIdx), SegmentPosition.RefMod) on an EMPTY token range and returns (null, true) with no Edition.Error; the same holds for T(1)( :2). Nonconforming source is still rejected (no under-reject), but the user is told it is a compiler bug instead of the §8.4.3.3.2 format violation. The golden cited covers both the length-specified and length-omitted forms at 85 (G (1:7), G (4:)); nothing spec-derived pins the missing-leftmost refusal. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (reference modification is a COBOL-85 facility; the format is unchanged since)]

subject: Inline method invocation
notes: kb/Work PB1430 (registrar 15b). Format: {object-class-name-1 | identifier-1} :: literal-1 [ ( {arith-expr-1|bool-expr-1|identifier-2|literal-2|OMITTED} ... ) ]. cite.py --check 8.4.3.4.2 'the inner braces select exactly one argument form, and the' OK (figure notes: '...' repeats the brace group inside ONE paren pair, so at least one argument). Both receiver arms, chaining, ref-mod tail and all five argument forms are present (golden pb428 + MethodOmittedArgumentTests OMITTED; probes p11 comma list N=0007, p13 arithmetic arg N=0006). DEFECT: inlineInvocationSegment is `COLONCOLON literal (LPAREN argumentList? RPAREN)?`, so an EMPTY list `A1 :: "GETNAME" ()` is accepted and runs (probe p2_emptyparens: W=ACCOUNT) - the format admits no empty parenthesis pair; expected a compile-time rejection. The drift test TheRuleMatchesThePrintedGeneralFormat only asserts 'argumentList' is present, not its cardinality. Sibling (not this row, §8.7.4): cite.py --check 8.7.4 'shall be immediately preceded and followed by a separator space' OK, yet conformance-test MethodOmittedArgumentTests.InlineInvocation_Omitted_ConditionTrueInMethod pins spaceless `O::"CHK"(OMITTED)` as accepted. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO facility; §8.4.3.4 absent from 85)

subject: Object-view
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (registrar 15c). NOT-IMPLEMENTED. Own search of src (the dossier found nothing): no grammar rule for object-view anywhere in src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar -- dataReference (CobolParserCore.g4:673) is cobolWord dataReferenceSuffix* with no AS arm, the token UNIVERSAL is not lexed, and no binder/codegen code names object-view. Probe with the pinned cobol.exe --std 2023 (probe/object-view/OV1-OV4): 'SET B TO U AS OVB', 'INVOKE U AS OVD "SPEAK"', 'SET D TO B AS UNIVERSAL' all refused COBOLNET0901 ('AS' is a reserved word ... cannot be used as a user-defined word) -- the identifier Format 5 (§8.4.3.1.2 'Format 5 (object-view)', cite.py OK) is unwritable. EC-OO-CONFORMANCE exists only as a catalog entry (Runtime/Exceptions/ExceptionCatalog.cs:166); no raise site. OO core is claimed mandatory surface (CONFORMANCE.md A.4.10 row), so this is not declined-module debt. Format: identifier-1 AS { [FACTORY OF] object-class-name-1 [ONLY] | interface-name-1 | UNIVERSAL } -- none of the three arms parses. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO introduced in 2002; §8.4.3.5 absent from 1985)]

subject: EXCEPTION-OBJECT
notes: Format: the bare word <u>EXCEPTION-OBJECT</u> (cite.py --check 8.4.3.6.2 "EXCEPTION-OBJECT" OK). IsExceptionObjectRegister = edition>=2002 AND no dataReferenceSuffix AND spelling EXCEPTION-OBJECT, so only the bare form is the register; resolver returns ExceptionObjectPlace, rendered as CobolNet.Runtime.Exceptions.ExceptionState.ExceptionObject from every sending position (relation condition, SET source). At --std 85 the word stays a user word (conformance:85/pb922_exception_object_user_word_85). Probe out/probe/exception-object/p1.cob compiles and runs at 2002/2014/2023 with the bare word in IF relations, in a declarative and in a separately compiled program. The spec-derived golden pb922_exception_object_reference exercises the bare word in sending positions at the introducing edition. [code-location note: (ExceptionObjectPlace arm, ~l.460); code-location note: (ExceptionObjectPlace => RuntimeApi.ExceptionObjectRead)] || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (object-orientation facility introduced in ISO/IEC 1989:2002; at 85 the spelling is an ordinary user-defined word)

subject: NULL object reference
notes: kb/Work PB1137 (registrar 15c). Format: underlined NULL (cite.py --check 8.4.3.7.2 "NULL" -> OK). §8.4.3.1.3 SR7 makes it identifier Format 6 (a predefined object reference). NULL_ is one lexer token, a reservedGatedWord (reserved 2002+). Probed: at --std 85, `01 NULL PIC X(3)` + DISPLAY NULL compiles and runs (ABC). At 2002 the same program is refused COBOLNET0901 (reserved word). At 2002 and 2023 the word parses in objectReference (SET ... TO NULL, INVOKE target, RAISE) and in the relation-condition operand (figurativeConstant): probe p4.cob prints G-NOT-NULL/G-NULL/H-NULL/NULL-EQ-G/U-NULL/U-EQ-G. PARTIAL: an identifier-5 slot does not admit it. `INVOKE G "TAKE" USING BY VALUE NULL` is COBOL0001 "unexpected '.'" because invokeArgument's BY VALUE arm is (addressIdentifier | arithmeticExpression) and has no NULL/objectReference arm. §14.9.23.2 prints identifier-5 under BY VALUE, and NULL is an identifier. See the finding on NULL as an INVOKE argument. Probe files: scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/null-object-reference/p1.cob [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (object orientation is new in 2002; NULL is not reserved in 1985)]

subject: SELF and SUPER
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (registrar 15c). Rule: `{SELF | [object-class-name-1 OF] SUPER}` (cite.py --check 8.4.3.8.2 "object-class-name-1 OF" -> OK), and it is identifier Format 6 (predefined-object) of §8.4.3.1.2 (cite.py --find 'predefined-object' -> §8.4.3.1.2 General format). Code: `objectReference : dataReference | NULL_ | SELF | SUPER` is the only production naming SELF/SUPER and it is reachable only from INVOKE's receiver, the inline-invocation receiver, SET ... TO (Format 5 sender) and RAISE. (1) The `object-class-name-1 OF` prefix has NO grammar surface: probe probe/self-and-super/PSOF.cob (DOG INHERITS FROM ANIMAL; `INVOKE PSOFA OF SUPER "SPEAK"`) is rejected COBOLNET0901 "'SUPER' is a reserved word" at 2023 - legal source per SR6 with a single base, expected ANIMAL then DOG. (2) SELF/SUPER are identifiers (§8.4.3.1.2 Format 6) but are not admitted where an object-class identifier is legal: `IF O = SELF` / `IF SELF = O` -> COBOL0001 parse error (PSCMP, PSCMP2; legal per §8.8.4.2.15, --check OK 'An operand of class object may be compared with another operand of class object'); `INVOKE SELF "TAKE" USING SELF` / `BY CONTENT SELF` / `BY VALUE SELF` -> 0901 / COBOL0001 (PSSELFU, PSUSEC, PSUSEV); `DISPLAY BAL OF SELF` / `BAL OF SUPER` object-property (Format 7, §8.4.3.9.3 SR2 excludes only universal and NULL, --check OK) -> 0901 (PPROP, PPROP2). Verified working: bare SELF/SUPER as INVOKE receiver, inline `SELF :: "GETN"` / `SUPER :: "GETN"` (PPROP3 prints 7 twice), SET O TO SELF. Half the format is implemented; see finding F1 (OF SUPER) and F2 (SELF/SUPER as general identifier). The negative fixture oo-multi-base-super.cob and landed kb/Work PB285 both record the OF-prefix gap, but no open note owns it. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (OO predefined object references; absent from COBOL-85)]

subject: Object property
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (also PB1449) (registrar 15c). §8.4.3.9.2 prints `property-name-1 OF {object-class-name-1 | identifier-1}` and §8.4.3.1.3 SR1 makes identifier-1 ANY identifier format ('Identifier is defined recursively' — cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.3 OK; §8.4.3.1.2 Format 7 'property-name-1 OF identifier-3' OK). §8.4.3.8.3 SR3 names the property object explicitly: 'SUPER may be specified only as the object in an object-property identifier' (--check OK), SR7 'SELF and SUPER ... are not universal object references' (--check OK). The binder (ReferenceResolver.OoTryBindPropertyReference :96) returns null unless the reference has EXACTLY ONE qualifier that is a bare word resolving to a class-name or a typed object-reference data item; every other identifier-1 form falls to the generic 1639 'not defined'. Probed with the pinned cobol.exe --std 2002 (probe/objprop): bare data-name and class-name forms work (p5, oo_property_ref); `BAL OF A OF T(2)` (STRONG-typedef table of refs, p6) -> 1639; `BAL OF A(2)` (p1) -> COBOLNET2096 naming the compiler temp '__PROP-TEMP-200002' (subscript attached to the temp); `BAL OF SELF` in a method (p7) -> 0901 'SELF is a reserved word'; `BAL OF INNER OF B` chained property (p8) -> 1639; interface-typed receiver `BAL OF I` (p13) -> 0899 + 1639 (:126 'interface-typed receivers ... later refinement'). Legal source rejected -> DIVERGES. The basic forms are covered by conformance:2002/oo_property_ref / oo_property_factory_ref, which do not close a defective row. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the object property is part of the OO facility introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:2002; absent from X3.23-1985)]

subject: NULL address pointer and message tag content
notes: kb/Work PB1427 (registrar 15c). Rule: the general format is the single required word NULL (cite.py --check 8.4.3.10.2 context; §8.4.3.1.2 'Format 8 (predefined-address)' -> OK; §8.4.3.1.3 SR9 'Predefined-address NULL is defined in 8.4.3.10' -> OK). The WORD is recognized: NULL_ token, and SET/IF/INITIALIZE-TO-VALUE probes in E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d2/out/probe/null/NULLOK2.cob compile and run. PARTIAL, not CONFORMS, because §8.4.3.1.2 makes NULL an IDENTIFIER (Format 8) while the grammar carries it only as an arm of figurativeConstant (CobolExpressions.g4 ~776, 'carried in the grammar's figurative rule for parse convenience only' per IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:389) plus the two SET-specific arms; every identifier-only slot therefore sees it as literal-1 (INITIALIZE REPLACING identifier-2, CALL Format 2 BY VALUE identifier-4) and every literal slot admits it as LOW-VALUE. See the findings 'NULL-as-literal' (rejects legal / crashes) and 'NULL-as-LOW-VALUE' (under-rejects). Editions: the pointer category and NULL predefined address are COBOL-2002 introductions (the 2023 Annex E covers 2014->2023 only and lists no change); the message-tag reading is 2023 (E.3.2 item 1 'Asynchronous messaging' -> OK).

subject: Data-address-identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1407 (registrar 15b). Format `ADDRESS OF identifier-1`, only ADDRESS underlined (cite.py --check 8.4.3.11.2 "OF identifier-1" -> OK). Grammar `dataAddressIdentifier : ADDRESS OF? dataReference` is the ONE rule reused by the SET sender, CALL/INVOKE arguments and the relation operand. Probe FM.cob: `SET P TO ADDRESS W` (OF omitted) and `CALL ... BY CONTENT ADDRESS W` compile and run at 2023 and 2002 (DISPLAY via BASED view prints ABC); --std 85 raises COBOLNET0900. The covering golden exercises the OF-present spelling only; the OF-omitted spelling is witnessed only by this probe (and the OptionalWordSubsetDriftTests grammar drift test). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — identifier-1 is a general identifier, and SR4 a) (cite.py OK 8.4.3.11.3 4) a)) speaks of 'subscripting and reference modification in identifier-1', so a reference-modified identifier-1 is legal source. The binder (PtrBinder.PtrBindAddressOf via Refs.ResolveForAddressOf) rejects any reference-modified operand with COBOLNET0869 ('the operand is unresolvable, reference-modified, or mis-subscripted'), with no spec basis. The format therefore rejects legal source for one operand shape. The OF-omitted, qualified, subscripted, relation-operand and CALL/INVOKE shapes do work. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85; the introduction gate COBOLNET0900 fires at --std 85)

subject: Function-address-identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1416 (registrar 15b). RULE: section 8.4.3.12.2 prints 'ADDRESS OF FUNCTION { function-prototype-name-1 | identifier-1 }' with ADDRESS and FUNCTION underlined, OF not (cite.py --check 8.4.3.12.2 "ADDRESS" -> OK). identifier-1 is a full identifier: 8.4.3.1.3 SR1 'Identifier is defined recursively' (OK), so a subscripted identifier-1 is legal. CODE: grammar setFunctionAddressStatement : SET dataReference+ TO ADDRESS OF? FUNCTION dataReference; SetBinder.BindSetFunctionAddress splits the two arms at bind (REPOSITORY/UDF self-name -> prototype arm, else ResolveSending -> identifier arm). VERIFIED (pinned cobol.exe): prototype arm with OF and without OF at --std 2014 runs the golden pb452_set_function_pointer exactly (BOTH-SET/SAME/NULL1/NOTNULL3/OF-OPTIONAL); --std 2002 rejected COBOLNET0900 (correct gate); identifier arm elementary / reference-modified / qualified-then-subscripted (WS-NAME OF WS-NAMES (2) -> REF-SET) all parse. DEFECT: a DIRECTLY subscripted identifier-1 'SET FP1 TO ADDRESS OF FUNCTION WS-NAME(2)' (also with a space before the paren) is a PARSE error 'COBOL0001: missing token before )': the lexer's OnDefaultLParen retypes the '(' after 'FUNCTION <word>' to FNARG_LPAREN, refModPart accepts (LPAREN|FNARG_LPAREN) but subscriptPart accepts only LPAREN. Expected: compiles; with WS-NAME(2)='FAIDBL' (a REPOSITORY function) FP1 is non-NULL (8.4.3.12.4 GR1 a). Probe: out/probe/fai/p1h.cob. ADJACENT (SR1 row, same arm): an alphanumeric group identifier-1 (and a ref-mod of it) is refused COBOLNET1960 'is of category (none)' although 8.5.2.1 'an alphanumeric group item has class and category alphanumeric' (OK) and 8.4.3.3.4 GR6 carries that category into the ref-mod (OK) - see findings. PLACEMENT (not decided here): the phrase exists only as SET Format 8's sender; IF fp = ADDRESS OF FUNCTION f, CALL ... USING BY VALUE ADDRESS OF FUNCTION x and INITIALIZE ... REPLACING FUNCTION-POINTER BY ADDRESS OF FUNCTION f all fail to parse. The printed 8.4.3.1.2 Format 9 (rendered PDF p155) lists only data-address-identifier-1 and program-address-identifier-1 (--check OK), so the normative identifier formats do not include it, while D.9.3.1 (informative) says a function address 'can be used anywhere ... a function-identifier may be used' - recorded as a dossier gap for owner decision, not as this row's defect. Existing covering goldens (conformance:2014/pb452_set_function_pointer, conformance:2023/pb452_function_address_runtime, conformance:negative/pb452-function-address-operand) are spec-derived but do not witness the subscripted arm, so test-ref is left empty for a DIVERGES row. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (function-pointer category and its address-identifier are a 2014 introduction; absent from 2023 Annex E, so unchanged 2014->2023; not in 85/2002)

subject: Program-address-identifier
notes: kb/Work PB1452 (registrar 15c). Printed format `ADDRESS OF PROGRAM { identifier-1 | literal-1 | program-prototype-name-1 }`, ADDRESS/PROGRAM underlined, OF not. Grammar: `ADDRESS OF? PROGRAM (nonNumericLiteral | dataReference)`; one dataReference covers identifier-1 and program-prototype-name-1, split at bind (SetBinder.BindProgramAddressOperand). Reached as the SET Format 9 sender and, as identifier Format 9 via addressIdentifier, in CALL/INVOKE arguments and the relation operand. Probed (out/probe/pai): `ADDRESS PROGRAM "PAISUB"` (OF omitted) compiles; a numeric literal is a parse error; --std 85 rejects with COBOLNET0900. The pb549 golden exercises all three arms plus the OF-omitted spelling with spec-derived expected output. kb/Work PB610 (status open) still claims this format has NO grammar - stale; PB549 (landed) supplied it. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The identifier-1 arm is narrower than the standard allows. The grammar writes it as `dataReference`, which does not admit the other identifier formats. §8.4.3.1.3 SR1 defines identifier recursively: where a format allows another identifier, that identifier 'may be any of the formats for an identifier'. So a function-identifier of category alphanumeric (§8.4.3.13.3 SR1 needs only the category) is legal as identifier-1, and the compiler rejects it with a parse error. The literal arm, the prototype arm, the optional OF, subscripted and reference-modified identifier-1, and the --std 85 gate all behave correctly. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the program-pointer family; absent from COBOL-85 - Annex E covers only 2014->2023, the introduction is the 2002 address-identifier; probe: --std 85 draws COBOLNET0900)]

subject: LINAGE-COUNTER
notes: Format: LINAGE-COUNTER [ {IN|OF} file-name-1 ]. Grammar alternative `LINAGE_COUNTER ((OF | IN) cobolWord)?` is exactly the diagram (qualifier optional, exactly one of IN/OF). LinageFileOf treats the cobolWord as the file-name. Probes (probe/linage-counter/Q1, Q5, g4) at --std 85 and 2023: `LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF`, `LINAGE-COUNTER IN LPG` and bare `LINAGE-COUNTER` all bind and read the right file's counter (Q1/Q5 print their OK line). The covering test writes both `OF LP1` and `IN LP2`. cite.py --check 8.4.3.14.3 "Qualification requirements for LINAGE-COUNTER are defined by 8.4.2.2, Qualification." -> OK. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85 2002 2014 2023

subject: Report counters
notes: kb/Work PB1456 (registrar 15c). Format: {PAGE-COUNTER|LINE-COUNTER} [{IN|OF} report-name-1]. Grammar dataReference alternatives `LINE_COUNTER ((OF | IN) cobolWord)?` and `PAGE_COUNTER ((OF | IN) cobolWord)?` are exactly the diagram (no subscript/refmod suffix admitted, correctly). Probed both qualifier spellings: rcq7.cob `MOVE LINE-COUNTER OF R1` -> 0004 and `LINE-COUNTER IN R2` -> 0005 (correct per-report values); unqualified single-RD form everywhere (a2.cob). cite.py --check 8.4.3.15.2 "report-name-1" -> OK. conformance:85/pb429_page_counter_receiving exercises only the OF spelling of PAGE-COUNTER, so no test pins the whole format (IN, LINE-COUNTER qualified) - test-needed. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The parser accepts every spelling of the format, but the binder rejects one legal instance of the qualified form, report-name-1 naming a DIFFERENT report inside a report section SOURCE clause. SR1 allows counters in a SOURCE clause. §8.4.2.2.3 SR9/SR10 state outright that a counter of a different report is referenced by qualifying it with that report's name. DataBinder.Reports.cs BindSourceReference instead raises ReportSourceOtherReportCounter ('a counter of another report ... is not yet implemented', COBOLNET0899), a staged rejection of legal source. The procedure-division forms all work: PAGE-COUNTER IN/OF and LINE-COUNTER IN/OF, as sender, as the PAGE-COUNTER receiver and in conditions. Same-report qualified SOURCE forms also work. So the format is only partly supported and no test pins it. [editions as adjudicated: 1985 (Report Writer optional module), 2002, 2014, 2023 - clause 8.4.3.15 text]

subject: Condition-name
notes: Rule: §8.4.4.2 Format 1 'condition-name-1' (switch-status, bare word) and Format 2 'qualified-condition-name-with-subscripts-1' (cite.py --check 8.4.4.2 'Format 2 (qualified-condition-name-with-subscripts)' OK; the production is §8.4.2.3.2 'qualified-condition-name-1 [ ( subscript … ) ]', --find OK). Code: ConditionBinder.AnalyzeBareOperand tries level-88 resolution (Format 2, through ctx.Refs.ResolveForItem with qualifiers+subscripts) then SetAlterBinder.SwitchCondOf, which admits a switch-status condition-name ONLY when dataReferenceSuffix() is empty (Format 1 has no qualifier/subscript). Probes (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/condition-name): p1.cob --std 2023 and --std 85 -> 'IF V-ONE OF T OF G (2)' TRUE, 'IF V-ONE (1)' FALSE, 'IF SW-ON' TRUE after SET SW1 TO ON, 'IF SW-OFF' FALSE, EVALUATE TRUE WHEN SW-OFF, and a contained program reading the container's SW-OFF (SPECIAL-NAMES inheritance, DataBinder.InheritConfiguration) all correct. n1 'IF SW-ON OF G' and n2 'IF SW-ON (1)' rejected (COBOLNET1639); n3 'IF SW1' (the mnemonic) rejected COBOLNET2318. Cosmetic only: the 1639 wording says 'no declaration gives the name SW-ON' although SW-ON IS declared as a switch-status condition-name — correct rejection, imprecise message (no harm). Coverage: Format 1 by conformance:85/pb390_procedure_and_condition_operands (SW-ON true after SET SW-M TO ON) and 85/nested_special_names_inheritance; Format 2 by conformance:85/pb567_condition_name_qualification and conformance:85/pb1030_reference_answers (IF C-THREE (I)). No negative golden pins the qualified/subscripted switch-status rejection. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (both kinds of condition-name present in every edition; §8.4.4.1)

subject: Relational operators
notes: kb/Work PB1034 (registrar 15c). §8.7.5.1 prints exactly six simple (Format 1) and thirteen extended (Format 2) spellings; IS/THAN/TO are not underlined (optional), GREATER/LESS/EQUAL/OR/NOT are (cite.py --check 8.7.5.1 'extended-relational-operator' OK; §8.8.4.2.2 figure notes 'the brackets around `NOT` make it optional' OK - that format brackets [NOT] on the first six alternatives only). POSITIVE HALF VERIFIED: every printed spelling (incl. word forms without THAN/TO and without IS) parses and evaluates correctly - probe/relop/relpos.cob (A=5 vs B=3 and B=5, IF with every printed spelling, --std 2023 and 85). EXCLUSION HALF FAILS: comparisonOperator is a SUPERSET that also admits IS NOT >=, IS NOT <=, NOT GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO, NOT LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO and EQUAL THAN; the only screen, ConditionBinder.InGeneralRelationFormat (whose own doc comment states the superset), is asked ONLY by the START KEY phrase (KeyedIoBinder). probe/relop/relneg.cob compiles and runs with NO diagnostic at strict --std 2023 and --std 85 (N1..N5 = F T F T F); relabb.cob 'A > B AND NOT >= C' (§8.8.4.12.4 NOTE: 'NOT cannot immediately precede an extended-relational operator') accepted silently; relcce.cob '>>IF X NOT >= 3' accepted silently. Expected: a strict-mode rejection (warning under --permissive) naming §8.7.5.1 / §8.8.4.2.2. Harm: under-rejects. See finding 'comparisonOperator superset unscreened outside START'. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 (clause text, no edition qualifier); 2014 identical (Annex E, the 2014->2023 delta, lists no change); 1985/2002 text not in-repo, so the edition at which <> (and >=/<=) entered is NOT derivable here - the compiler accepts every spelling at every --std]

subject: Concatenation expressions
notes: kb/Work PB1406 (registrar 15b). General format {literal-1 | concatenation-expression-1} & literal-2 (cite.py --check 8.8.3 "A concatenation expression consists of two operands separated by the concatenation operator" -> OK). The grammar flattens the left recursion to concatOperand (AMPERSAND concatOperand)+ — equivalent for the chain shape (probe: "A" & "B" & "C" & "D" & "E" -> ABCDE). But concatOperand admits only lexical tokens (STRINGLIT/NATLIT/BOOLLIT/HEXLIT) and the keyword figurativeConstant rule, so two things a format 'literal' position must admit are PARSE ERRORS here: (1) a symbolic-character figurative — §8.3.2.2.29 "A symbolic-character is a user-defined figurative constant" (--check OK), §8.3.3.6.3 SR1 "A figurative constant may be used whenever 'literal' appears in a format" (--check OK) and §8.8.3.2 SR1 admits a figurative constant as either operand: `MOVE "X" & SYM-A TO W-X` -> COBOL0309 'A literal value is expected here, not a data-name'; `MOVE SYM-A & "X"` -> COBOL0001 unexpected '&' (the same SYM-A as a plain MOVE/DISPLAY operand works: XA); (2) a constant-name — §13.10.3 SR2 "constant-name-1 may be used anywhere that a format specifies a literal of the class and category of constant-name-1" (--check OK): `01 K CONSTANT AS "Q". MOVE "X" & K TO W-X` -> COBOL0309. Expected: "XA" / "XQ". Finding: concat-operand-word-substitution. Probe dir probe/concat (pinned cobol.exe) CCN1/CCN7/CCN9/c5. No existing golden exercises the word-operand arms. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2002, 2014, 2023 — §8.8.3 is not in the 2023 Annex E (2014->2023) delta, so it predates 2023; the 2002 introduction edge is not quotable from the 2023 text (repo holds no 2002/2014 text) and rides the derived edge concat-operator-2002 (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE decision 1); absent from 1985 (probe: --std 85 -> COBOLNET0900)

subject: Simple relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1034 (registrar 15c). The three general formats (cite.py --check 8.8.4.2.3 SR1-SR5 OK; format diagram read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 8.8.4.2.2). Measured with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/srel1/legal.cob, gen.py): every printed Format-1 spelling is accepted and evaluates correctly — IS [NOT] GREATER THAN, >, LESS THAN, <, EQUAL TO, =, <>, GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO (THAN/TO optional), >=, LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO, <= — over identifier, literal, arithmetic-expression (`IF N3 + 1 > N1 * 2`) and index-name operands (`IF I1 < I2`, `IF I1 = 3`); malformed `IS IS =` and `NOT <>` are refused (COBOLNET2072). Format 2: `IF B1 = B"1010"`, `IS NOT EQUAL TO` accepted, ordering refused COBOLNET0844. Format 3: `=`/`NOT =`/`<>` over pointers/object references/NULL accepted, ordering refused COBOLNET0868/0869; ADDRESS OF is an identifier-3/-4 (PB1021 landed). DEFECT (owned by OPEN kb/Work PB1034, not re-reported): Format 1 prints no `NOT >=`, `NOT <=`, `NOT GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO`, `NOT LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO` or `EQUAL THAN`, yet `IF NI NOT >= 3` and `IF NI EQUAL THAN 3` compile clean at 2023 (probe c_not_ge / c_equal_than, rc=0) — comparisonOperator lists `IS? NOT GTEQUAL`, `IS? NOT LTEQUAL`, `IS? NOT GREATER THAN? OR EQUAL TO?`, `IS? NOT LESS THAN? OR EQUAL TO?` and `IS? EQUAL (TO|THAN)?`. The Format-3 message-tag operand cannot be written (USAGE MESSAGE-TAG refused COBOLNET1943, declined MCS facility, CONFORMANCE.md §5 item 1). [editions as adjudicated: Format 1: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023; Formats 2 (boolean) and 3 (message-tag/object/pointer): 2002, 2014, 2023 (the boolean, pointer and object facilities enter with ISO/IEC 1989:2002)]

subject: Simple boolean condition
notes: kb/Work PB1412 (also PB1464) (registrar 15c). Rule: `[ NOT ] boolean-expression-1` (cite.py --check 8.8.4.3.2 OK). boolean-expression-1 is any §8.8.2 boolean expression, which includes 'a boolean expression and an integer operand separated by a boolean shift operator' and 'a boolean expression enclosed in parentheses' (both cite.py --check 8.8.2 OK). Probed with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/simple-boolean-condition/p1.cob, p2.cob, p3.cob): bare item (PIC 1, USAGE BIT, USAGE NATIONAL, GROUP-USAGE BIT 1-bit group, ref-mod slice), bare literal B"1", BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(1,1), B-AND/B-OR/B-XOR/B-NOT forms, NOT over each, `NOT (BW B-AND BZ)`, and the forms in IF / PERFORM UNTIL / EVALUATE TRUE WHEN / EVALUATE NOT BW all compile and run correctly at 2002/2014/2023, and are gated COBOLNET0900 at --std 85. DIVERGES on two legal shapes: (a) a SHIFT-only boolean expression `IF BW B-SHIFT-LC 1` / `IF BW B-SHIFT-L 1` / `IF (BW B-SHIFT-RC 1)` -> false COBOLNET2318 "'operand' is used as a condition, but it is a literal ..." because ConditionBinder.HasBoolOp recognises only B_AND/B_OR/B_XOR/B_NOT while the parser's boolExprAhead() admits the four shift tokens; the sibling relation `IF BW B-SHIFT-L 1 = B"0"` hits COBOLNET2362 (internal error: refused without a diagnostic). (b) a PARENTHESIZED bare operand `IF (BW)`, `IF ((BW))`, `IF NOT (BZ)`, `IF (BW) AND X1` -> false COBOLNET2318: primaryCondition's comparisonExpression alternative precedes `LPAREN condition RPAREN`, so ANTLR binds `(BW)` as a parenthesized arithmetic operand and the bare-operand analysis does not look through the parens. Same mechanism rejects `IF (X1)` over a level-88 at EVERY edition incl. --std 85 (p4.cob), legal by §8.8.4.11.3 Table 5 ('(' may be followed by simple-condition). See findings. [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85 -- boolean data/operators arrive at 2002; the 2023 Annex E.2 item 3 adds ONLY the B-SHIFT-* operators at 2023, so a shift-form boolean-expression-1 is 2023-only)]

subject: Simple class condition
notes: kb/Work PB225 (wave 45 A): all FOURTEEN alternatives of the printed general format (PDF p224 / printed 194, rendered by PB571: one brace group, no choice indicator, IS not underlined) are offered by the ONE className rule. The seven COBOL-2014 numeric-content alternatives FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO, FLOAT-INFINITY, FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER, FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-QUIET, FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-SIGNALING, IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE and NEAREST-TO-ZERO landed as seven keyword alternatives placed AFTER cobolWord - the BOOLEAN precedent - so the reservation gate is the edition gate: 8.9 reserves the seven from 2014 (reserved-words.json r2002 false / r2014 true; Annex E names none of them, so 2014 is the introducing edition), below that each is a SPECIAL-NAMES class-name (2002 golden) and an undeclared one is COBOLNET1639 (negative, 85/2002). FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-QUIET gained its lexer token with the class condition, its only surface. ClassConditionTableDriftTests pins grammar alternative = binder arm = model row = renderer arm.

subject: Simple condition-name condition (conditional variable)
notes: Format: 'condition-name-1' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.5.2 "condition-name-1" -> OK §8.8.4.5.2 General format). A bare level-88 name binds as BoundCondition88 and renders through ConditionRenderer.RenderCondition88 in every condition context. Probed: bare, NOT-prefixed, subscripted (TE-ODD (1..3) -> T F T), and qualified (R-ONE OF R1V OF R1 -> T; R-ONE OF R2 -> F with a same-named 88 elsewhere) all compile and answer per the spec under --std 2023 and --std 85. l1_perform_until_condition_forms (d) derives the PERFORM UNTIL ST-DONE pass count from §8.8.4.5. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (§8.8.4.5 carries no edition marking; the simple condition-name condition is base COBOL in every edition)]

subject: Simple switch-status condition
notes: kb/Work PB1464 (registrar 15c). §8.8.4.6.2 format is bare condition-name-1 (cite.py --check 8.8.4.6.2 "condition-name-1" OK). SwitchCondOf binds an unsubscripted/unqualified cobolWord found in SwitchConditions (the SPECIAL-NAMES ON/OFF STATUS names) to BoundSwitchCondition; a suffix returns null (a status condition-name takes no subscript/qualifier). Probe p1.cob (probe/simple-switch-status-condition) compiles at --std 85 and 2023 with ON and OFF status names, both orders of ON/OFF phrases, a switch with no mnemonic-name, in IF/NOT/AND/PERFORM UNTIL/EVALUATE; goldens use it in EVALUATE subject/object and SEARCH WHEN. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — A switch-status condition written in parentheses is legal: §8.8.4.2.1 says 'The inclusion in parentheses of simple conditions does not change the simple condition truth value.' (cite.py --check found it in §8.8.4.2.1, not §8.8.4.1). The pinned compiler rejects IF (S1-OFF) and IF NOT (S1-ON) with COBOLNET2318, which says the operand is 'a literal ... or an arithmetic expression' and cites §8.8.4.2.1, the clause that permits the construct. The bare form, lower-case spelling, AND/OR combinations, (S1-OFF AND X-ONE), EVALUATE subject ALSO, and inheritance by a nested program all compile and run correctly at 85 and 2023. The rejection is not specific to switches: (X-ONE), a parenthesized level-88 name, fails the same way. The root cause is the shared path for a parenthesized single-operand condition (§8.8.4.2.1), and the fix belongs there. It still rejects legal source that uses this format. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (switch-status condition present in every edition)]

subject: Simple sign condition
notes: Both printed formats reduce to `operand IS? NOT? (POSITIVE|NEGATIVE|ZERO)`: comparisonExpression alt 3 (written form) and partialComparison alt 2 (EVALUATE SR5 elided operand). The keyword is ZERO only; ZEROS/ZEROES are refused (PB510 landed, COBOLNET2418). IS is optional, NOT is optional, and one of the three keywords is required, which matches both diagrams. Probed with the pinned cobol.exe (probe dir out/probe/sign (p1b.cob, p2.cob, p3.cob, p4.cob)): Format 1 over a signed display item and over expressions (N + 1, N * 0, - N, N * -2 under --std 85), with IS NOT; Format 2 over bare FLOAT-BINARY-64/-32 names; EVALUATE FB WHEN NEGATIVE. All parse and bind. Which FORMAT an operand selects is SR1/SR2's partition and is adjudicated there (it diverges: see SR-8.8.4.7.3-2). test-ref left empty: conformance:2023/pb171_sign_condition_operands covers Format 1 only. conformance:2002/ca8_float_sign_format2 uses FLOAT-LONG, which is not a Format 2 operand at all (§3.166/§3.167), so no golden exercises Format 2 with a standard float usage. cite.py --check 8.8.4.7.3 SR1/SR2 OK. [editions as adjudicated: Format 1: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023. Format 2 (data-name-1 of a standard floating-point usage; the §3.166/§3.167 usages were introduced in 2014): 2014, 2023.]

subject: Simple omitted argument condition
notes: Rule: §8.8.4.8.2 general format 'data-name-1 IS [ NOT ] OMITTED' with NOT and OMITTED underlined and IS not underlined (cite.py --check 8.8.4.8.2 "data-name-1 IS" -> OK; the Markdown form carries the <u> marks), so IS is optional, NOT is an optional bracketed word, OMITTED required. Grammar comparisonExpression alt 1 'comparisonOperand IS? NOT? OMITTED' spells exactly that (superset operand; ConditionBinder.BindComparison then requires the operand text to name a formal of the current element, method formals inside a method, else LinkageFormals, COBOLNET1686 per SR1 -- cite.py --check 8.8.4.8.3 'Data-name-1 shall be a formal parameter defined in the source element in which this condition is specified' OK -- so a subscripted/expression/non-formal operand is refused). NOT yields BoundOmittedCondition(formal, not) -- one condition per GR2 (cite.py --check 8.8.4.8.4 'When used, NOT and the keyword OMITTED specify one condition' OK). Edition gate: VersionConformancePass.VisitComparisonExpression Check(OmittedArguments2002). PROBE (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/simple-omitted/p1.cob): 'l-a OMITTED' (no IS, lower case), 'L-B NOT OMITTED' (no IS), 'L-C IS NOT OMITTED AND L-A IS OMITTED', 'NOT L-C IS OMITTED' against CALL USING W-A OMITTED (+trailing) and USING OMITTED W-A W-A -> A-PRESENT/B-OM then A-OM/B-PRESENT/C-PRES-A-OM/C-PRESENT2, exactly the GR1a/GR1b truth values, at --std 2023 and 2002; --std 85 -> COBOLNET0900 on every condition; p2.cob: working-storage item and a linkage item not in USING -> COBOLNET1686. Covering golden pb133_omitted_args spells IS OMITTED and IS NOT OMITTED (IS-less spellings verified by probe only). [editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the omitted-argument condition is a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from 1985)]

subject: Complex negated conditions
notes: Rule: §8.8.4.10.2 general format `NOT condition-1`; §8.8.4.10.1 'A condition is negated by use of the logical operator 'NOT', which reverses the truth value of the condition to which it is applied. Including a negated condition in parentheses does not change its truth value.' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.10.1 OK). Code: grammar unaryLogicalExpression : NOT primaryCondition | primaryCondition, where primaryCondition includes LPAREN condition RPAREN, so NOT applies to a simple condition or a parenthesized complex condition; NOT sits below AND/XOR/OR tiers, giving §8.8.4.11.3 precedence NOT>AND>XOR>OR. Binder wraps BoundNot; ConditionRenderer emits !(operand). Table 5 / §8.8.4.11.3 NOTE 'the pair 'NOT (' is permissible while the pair 'NOT NOT' is not permissible' (cite.py --check 8.8.4.11.3 OK) is realized structurally (NOT primaryCondition cannot recurse) — probe `IF NOT NOT A = 1` -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'NOT'. Abbreviation interplay §8.8.4.12.4 GR1 'NOT a = b OR c' => '(NOT (a = b)) OR (a = c)' (cite.py --find -> §8.8.4.12.4 1)). Probe (pinned cobol.exe, probe/complex-negated-conditions/negc.cob, --std 2023; negc85.cob at 85/2002/2014) A=1,B=2,C=3,X='Z',88 F-ON false: NOT A=B ->T1; NOT(A=B OR B=C)->T2; NOT(A=1 OR B=C)->F3; NOT cond-name->T4; NOT (X NUMERIC)->T5; NOT A POSITIVE->F6; A=9 OR NOT B=2 AND C=3 ->F7 (precedence); NOT (NOT A=1)->T8; NOT A=2 OR 1 ->T9; NOT A=1 OR 2 ->F10 (NOT scopes only the first relation per §8.8.4.12.4); NOT(A=1 AND B=2) AND C=3 ->F11; A=1 XOR NOT B=2 ->T12 (2023; XOR correctly 0900 below 2023); PERFORM UNTIL NOT A<3 -> A=3; NOT (((A=3)))->F13. All outputs equal the spec-derived expectations at every edition. Covering spec-derived golden: 2023/l1_perform_until_condition_forms (`PERFORM UNTIL NOT (CX IS NUMERIC)`, expected count derived from §8.8.4.4); sibling 2023/l1_search_when_condition_forms (`WHEN NOT (WS-K(IX) < 7)`). No clause-citing source (dossier) — code implements the rule without citing §8.8.4.10; not a defect. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause carries no edition qualification; negated conditions are base COBOL; the XOR operand context is 2023-only per §8.8.4.9)

subject: Complex Combined conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1392, PB1162 (registrar 15b). Rule: condition-1 { {AND|OR|EXCLUSIVE-OR|XOR} condition-2 } ... (braces both levels, one operator per repetition, at least one repetition). cite.py --check 8.8.4.11.2 'condition-1 ┤ ┤              ├ condition-2 ├ …' OK; --check 8.8.4.11.1 "A combined condition results from connecting conditions with one of the logical operators 'AND', 'OR', 'EXCLUSIVE-OR', or 'XOR'." OK; --check 8.8.4.11.3 (Table 5) '| EXCLUSIVE-OR or XOR, OR or AND | No | No | simple-condition, ) | simple-condition, NOT, ( |' OK; --check E.3.2 "Logical operators have been enhanced to include 'EXCLUSIVE-OR' and 'XOR'." OK. Code: grammar condition -> logicalOrExpression (OR loop) -> logicalXorExpression ((XOR|EXCLUSIVE_OR) loop) -> logicalAndExpression (AND loop) -> unaryLogicalExpression (NOT? primaryCondition); ConditionBinder.BindFlatSequence folds each tier into BoundLogical('||'/'^'/'&&'), XOR emitted through RuntimeApi '^' -> CobolBool.Xor. VERIFIED (pinned cobol.exe, probe/ccc/ccc1.cob, --std 2023): XOR truth table T^T=F, T^F=T, F^T(EXCLUSIVE-OR)=T, F^F=F; repetition T XOR T XOR T = T; mixed XOR/EXCLUSIVE-OR 4-operand chain T^T^F^T = T; A OR B XOR C = A OR (B XOR C) (T); F AND T XOR T = T; OR/OR/AND repetition = T; XOR NOT (Table 5 'XOR NOT' pair) = F correctly; AND x4 chain = T. All match the spec. Edition gate VERIFIED (probe g1.cob): `IF A = 1 XOR B = 9` at --std 85/2002/2014 -> COBOLNET0900, at 2023 compiles and runs; XOR as a user data-name at 85/2014 (`01 XOR PIC 9`, `IF XOR = 4 OR A = 9`, `XOR (1:1)`) compiles and runs (probe g2.cob). DEFECT 1 (rejects legal source, all editions where the operator exists = 2023): condition-2 written as a parenthesized condition after XOR / EXCLUSIVE-OR is a raw parse error. Table 5 says an XOR/EXCLUSIVE-OR element 'may be immediately followed by only: simple-condition, NOT, (' - so '(' is explicitly permitted. Probe p.cob --std 2023: `IF A = 1 XOR (B = 9)` -> error COBOL0001: cannot parse construct near 'B'; same for `A = 1 XOR (B = 9 OR C = 3)`, `(A = 1) XOR (B = 9)`, `A = 1 EXCLUSIVE-OR (B = 9)`, and with the '(' on the next line (g6.cob); `A = 1 OR (B = 9 OR C = 3)` and `A = 1 AND (B = 2 OR C = 3)` compile (T); `A = 1 XOR NOT (B = 9)` compiles (F). Spec-derived expected for A=1,B=2,C=3: `A = 1 XOR (B = 9)` -> T; `A = 1 XOR (B = 9 OR C = 3)` -> F. Mechanism: CobolLexer.g4 OnDefaultLParen pushes SUBSCRIPT mode for a '(' whose previous token is in _dataNameTokens (CobolLexerWordSet.g.cs, generated from cobol-words.json subscriptTrigger=true rows); XOR and EXCLUSIVE_OR are in that set (they are user words below 2023) and the decision is edition-blind, so at 2023 - where both are reserved and can only be the operator - the grouping paren is lexed as a subscript and the condition cannot parse. DEFECT 2 (under-rejects): the XOR operator inside an EVALUATE partial-expression (grammar partialXorExpression) is never edition-gated - VersionConformancePass has VisitLogicalXorExpression only, no VisitPartialXorExpression. Probe g4.cob: `EVALUATE A WHEN > 5 XOR B = 2 ...` at --std 2014 compiles and prints W1 with no COBOLNET0900; expected COBOLNET0900 (XOR is a 2023 addition, §E.3.2 4)). Same shape at 85/2002 by the same missing arm.
