subject: Abbreviated combined relation conditions
notes: kb/Work PB1390 (registrar 15b). Printed format (PDF p233 rendered): relation-condition-1 { {AND|OR|EXCLUSIVE-OR|XOR} {NOT | simple-relational-operator | extended-relational-operator} object-1 } ... ; the whole group repeats and each repetition may use any of the four connectives. cite.py --check 8.8.4.12.2 "where simple-relational-operator and extended-relational-operator are described in 8.7.5" -> OK. The grammar spells the abbreviated tail in THREE non-uniform places: logicalAndExpression admits `AND abbreviatedRelation`; logicalOrExpression admits `OR abbreviatedAndChain` where abbreviatedAndChain = abbreviatedRelation (AND abbreviatedRelation)* only; logicalXorExpression's right operand is logicalAndExpression, whose leading element cannot be an abbreviatedRelation. MEASURED with the pinned cobol.exe (scratchpad adj-d2/out/probe/abbrev/): `A = B XOR < C` -> COBOL0001 unexpected '<'; `A = B XOR NOT < C` -> COBOL0001; `A = B OR < C AND D` (--std 85 and 2023) -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'D'; `A = B OR < C AND NOT D` -> COBOL0001; `A = B OR < C XOR = D` / `A = B OR < C XOR D` -> COBOLNET0901 'XOR' is a reserved word. Every one is a legal repetition of the printed group. Shapes that DO parse and run correctly: AND/OR with stated or omitted operator, `OR < C AND = D`, `OR NOT < C AND = D`, `XOR C`, `XOR NOT C AND > D`, IS-prefixed word operators. Separately, comparisonOperator admits `NOT >=`, `NOT <=`, `NOT GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO`, `NOT LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO` (8.7.5 prints none of them; the group's NOT and extended-relational-operator are alternatives) — `A = B AND NOT >= C` compiles and runs; that half is owned by open kb/Work PB1034 (shared comparisonOperator, abbreviated relations named in its body), not re-reported. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (EXCLUSIVE-OR / XOR logical operators 2023 only, §8.8.4.9 / Annex E.2)

subject: COBOL compilation group
notes: kb/Work PB1507: Rule: the §10.6.1 general format (compilation group = zero or more of program-prototype / function-prototype / program-definition / function-definition / class-definition / interface-definition, plus their sub-formats). The printed PDF page 257 (rendered from specs-private, E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\cg\p287.png) was checked because the diagram is load-bearing: program-definition prints '[ procedure-division [ program-definition ] … ]' (cite.py --check 10.6.1 'procedure-division [ program-definition ]' -> OK) and '[ END PROGRAM program-name-1. ]'; function-definition prints '[ procedure-division ]' followed by UNBRACKETED '<u>END</u> <u>FUNCTION</u> user-function-name-1.' (OK §10.6.1) and has NO contained program-definition slot; the PROGRAM-ID attribute group is COMMON and {INITIAL|RECURSIVE} under choice indicators, which §5.2.6.4 reads 'When enclosed by braces, one or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative shall be specified only once.' (OK §5.2.6.4). CONFORMING PARTS (verified): compilationUnit 'compilationGroup* EOF' admits the empty group (empty.cob compiles); class/factory/object/interface/method shapes (IS FINAL / INHERITS FROM? / USING, factory before object, END FACTORY / END OBJECT unnamed, END METHOD [name], no interface or class-level DATA DIVISION) match the figure; the prototype arms are screened by PrototypeUnitRules.ScreenUnitShape (COBOLNET2274: never contained, never containing, END marker required - proto_nested.cob draws 2274) and SR1 order (2273); a class plus a program in one group runs (class_and_prog.cob -> HI); COMMON INITIAL / INITIAL COMMON accepted (common_init.cob, init_common.cob -> OK); INITIAL RECURSIVE refused (COBOLNET0886). DIVERGENT PARTS (all accepted with NO diagnostic by the pinned cobol.exe at --std 2023 and 2002): (1) func_in_prog.cob - a FUNCTION-ID ... END FUNCTION nested inside a PROGRAM-ID definition compiles and runs (program-definition's slot admits only program-definition); (2) func_nested.cob / func_nested_run.cob - a PROGRAM-ID nested inside a FUNCTION-ID definition compiles and the inner program is CALLable (prints INNER); (3) func_no_end.cob - a function definition with no END FUNCTION marker compiles; (4) func_end_program.cob - a FUNCTION-ID closed by END PROGRAM compiles; end_mismatch.cob - a PROGRAM-ID closed by END FUNCTION compiles (endProgramHeader is 'END (PROGRAM | FUNCTION)' for either unit kind and nothing binds the keyword to the paragraph); (5) nested_no_pd.cob - a program with NO procedure division containing a nested program compiles (programUnit / nestedProgram write 'procedureDivision? nestedProgram*'); (6) global_attr.cob - 'PROGRAM-ID. X IS GLOBAL PROGRAM.' compiles and runs (commonProgramAttribute carries GLOBAL, which is not in the figure; MakeUnit reads INITIAL/COMMON/RECURSIVE and silently drops GLOBAL); (7) dup_attr.cob - 'IS INITIAL INITIAL PROGRAM' compiles (choice-indicator 'only once' unenforced; MakeUnit folds repeats into booleans). Root cause is the TWO-ARM shape: the §10.6.1 unit-shape screen was written for the prototype arm only (PrototypeUnitRules.ScreenUnitShape, PB894) and the definition arms - function-definition and program-definition - have no equivalent, while the grammar's shared programUnit/nestedProgram/endProgramHeader rules are a superset over program and function kinds. Side note for the §11.10.3 adjudicator: COBOLNET0886's message cites 'ISO §11.10.3 SR5-6' for INITIAL+RECURSIVE in the SAME paragraph, but SR5/SR6 ('The INITIAL clause shall not be specified if any program that directly or indirectly contains this program is a recursive program.', OK §11.10.3 5)) govern CONTAINING programs; the same-paragraph exclusion is the format's inner brace. No kb/Work note owns these (PB894 / PB303 are landed and scoped to the prototype arm and the AS phrase). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 for the compilation-group format with prototypes, functions, classes and interfaces; the program-definition arm also exists (as a sequence of separately compiled / nested programs) at 1985

subject: End markers
notes: kb/Work PB988: All nine alternatives parse on the pinned cobol.exe: END PROGRAM prog (p1), END PROGRAM prototype (q1), END FUNCTION user-function (p6), END FUNCTION function-prototype (q2), END CLASS / END OBJECT / END METHOD name (o1), END FACTORY and a nameless END METHOD, lowercase names (o5). endProgramHeader folds the PROGRAM and FUNCTION alternatives into one rule, `END (PROGRAM|FUNCTION) programName DOT`, so which keyword goes with which unit kind is left to the syntax rules. That pairing is SR2/SR7 territory: see those rows and PB988. No spec-derived positive test names the format. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The 2023 shape is right: all nine alternatives parse, END FACTORY/END OBJECT with a name are rejected, END CLASS without a name is rejected, and the separator period is required. The edition half fails. The FUNCTION alternatives are COBOL-2002 introductions (the row's own editions field says so), yet with --std 85 `END FUNCTION` is accepted with no diagnostic, even when it closes a PROGRAM-ID unit. endProgramHeader is `END (PROGRAM|FUNCTION) programName DOT` with no edition predicate, and VersionConformancePass has no arm for it. The 2023 Annex E does not list them as changes

subject: OBJECT paragraph
notes: Format `OBJECT. [ IMPLEMENTS { interface-name-1 } ... . ]` (cite.py --check 11.8.2 "OBJECT" -> OK §11.8.2 General format). Grammar: objectParagraph `(IDENTIFICATION DIVISION DOT)? OBJECT DOT implementsClause? ...`, implementsClause `IMPLEMENTS interfaceName+ DOT` - one-or-more repetition and the clause's own trailing period, exactly as printed. IMPLEMENTS IA` / `IC.` spanning two lines compiles and runs (CB8-PA, CB8-PC); p2 missing trailing period -> COBOL0307; p11 `IMPLEMENTS .` (empty list) -> COBOL0001; --std 85 -> COBOLNET0900 (OO gated), 2002/2014 run. subject: OPTIONS paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB1508: Rule (PDF p302, folio 272, rendered and inspected): 'OPTIONS. [ arithmetic-clause ] [ default-rounded-clause ] [ entry-convention-clause ] [ float-binary-clause ] [ float-decimal-clause ] [ initialize-clause ] [ intermediate-rounding-clause ] [.]' - seven SEPARATE brackets in a fixed sequence, NO choice indicators and no ellipsis, and no syntax rule of 11.9.3 relaxes the order. cite.py --check 11.9.2 "[ intermediate-rounding-clause ]" -> OK; --check 5.2.6.4 "The alternatives may be specified in any order." -> OK (any-order is granted ONLY by choice indicators, absent here); --check 5.3.2 "define or clarify the order in which words or elements may be written" -> OK (order is the general format's unless a syntax rule relaxes it); --check 5.2.6.2 "that portion of the general format may be omitted" -> OK. CODE: grammar `optionsParagraph : OPTIONS DOT (optionsClause+ DOT)? ;` with `optionsClause` a 7-way alternation - its own comment calls it 'order-independent (a superset of the spec's fixed clause order)'. OptionsBinder.BindParagraph folds every clause into the model in source order (`model = Apply(model, clause, edition)`), so a repeated clause silently overwrites the earlier one (last wins). Nothing in OptionsBinder, VersionConformancePass or any other consumer checks clause order or repetition (grep of src for optionsClause: OptionsBinder, PrototypeUnitRules only). CONFORMING HALF (verified): every clause keyword set is recognised, the paragraph header `OPTIONS.` is required, the edition gate fires at 85 (COBOLNET0804, probe bare.cob --std 85) and the 2014 clause rows fire at 2002 (COBOLNET0900 for DEFAULT ROUNDED, probe ordered.cob --std 2002); `OPTIONS.` alone compiles at 2002/2014/2023. DIVERGING HALF (measured, pinned cobol.exe, probe dir probe/options-paragraph): reorder.cob (`DEFAULT ROUNDED MODE IS TRUNCATION` BEFORE `ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE.`) compiles clean and runs at 2014 and 2023 (prints 1) - expected a diagnostic, since the format places arithmetic-clause first; dup.cob (DEFAULT ROUNDED written twice, TRUNCATION then NEAREST-EVEN) compiles clean at 2014/2023 and prints 2 (last one wins) - expected a diagnostic, since each bracket is written at most once. Neither is documented in docs/CONFORMANCE.md as a nonstandard extension and neither is flagged (4.2.10: cite.py --check 4.2.10 "An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate use of a nonstandard extension" -> OK). SECOND EDGE: the trailing `[.]` is its own independent bracket, so with zero clauses the format literally derives `OPTIONS. .`; SR-11.9.3-1 constrains only the with-clauses case. twodots.cob (`OPTIONS. .`) and twolines.cob (`OPTIONS.` then a lone `.` line) are REJECTED at 2014/2023 with COBOL0001 unexpected '.', because the grammar ties the second DOT to optionsClause+. See findings. No kb/Work note owns this (searched kb/Work for optionsClause+/clause order: none; PB298 is the producer-only-fields analysis and does not cover order/repetition). No spec-derived test drives the order/repetition half; tests/conformance/2014/options_paragraph.cob and options_default_rounded.cob only exercise the in-order positive form. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (not 85): the OPTIONS paragraph is a 2002 element (its ARITHMETIC clause's Standard Arithmetic was obsolete in 2014 and removed per Annex E.2 item 21); the seven-clause list is the 2023 format - initialize-clause is new in 2023 (Annex E.3 item 33), the other five non-ARITHMETIC clauses 2014

subject: ARITHMETIC clause
notes: Rule: `ARITHMETIC IS {NATIVE | STANDARD-BINARY | STANDARD-DECIMAL}`, ARITHMETIC and the three phrases underlined, IS not underlined, plain braces = exactly one (cite.py --check 11.9.5.1 "STANDARD-DECIMAL" -> OK §11.9.5.1 General format; cite.py --check E.2 "Standard Arithmetic" -> OK §E.2 21)). Code: arithmeticClause = ARITHMETIC IS? arithmeticMethod; arithmeticMethod = NATIVE | STANDARD_BINARY | STANDARD_DECIMAL | STANDARD. Probed with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/arithmetic-clause/p_*.cob) at --std 85/2002/2014/2023: every alternative with and without IS compiles at 2014/2023 and selects the right engine (FUNCTION SQRT(2) into PIC 9V9(30): NATIVE/absent -> binary64 1.414213562373095145474621858738, STANDARD-DECIMAL -> 34-digit 1.414213562373095048801688724209); `ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE STANDARD-DECIMAL` -> COBOL0307 (exactly one); `ARITHMETIC IS.` -> COBOL0001 (one required); STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2002 -> COBOLNET0900; OPTIONS at 85 -> COBOLNET0804; the 2002 STANDARD phrase compiles at 2002, warns obsolete (0903) at 2014, is rejected at 2023 (0807, Annex E.2 item 21 removal) - edition-correct dual window. STANDARD-BINARY is refused by COBOLNET0806 at every edition: a documented processor-dependent decline (A.3 item 2, cite --check A.3 OK; docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2, kb/Work PB198), not a syntax defect; at 2023 it additionally draws the NOTE 2 obsolete warning 0903 (cite --check 11.9.5.2 "The STANDARD-BINARY mode of arithmetic is an obsolete feature" OK). Grammar comment calls bare STANDARD 'a common vendor spelling' - it is in fact the ISO 2002 phrase; the gating is right, the comment is stale. No single existing test exercises the IS-omitted spelling plus each alternative, so test-ref is empty (candidates: conformance:2023/l1_native_arithmetic_intermediate writes ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE; conformance:2014/arithmetic_standard_decimal writes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002 (clause introduced with the OPTIONS paragraph; NATIVE | STANDARD); 2014 (STANDARD-BINARY, STANDARD-DECIMAL added; STANDARD obsolete); 2023 (NATIVE | STANDARD-BINARY | STANDARD-DECIMAL; Standard Arithmetic removed - Annex E.2 item 21); not in 1985

subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1508: Format: INITIALIZE {ALL | {|LOCAL-STORAGE|SCREEN|WORKING-STORAGE|}} [SECTION] [TO] {BINARY ZEROES | HIGH-VALUES | literal-1 | LOW-VALUES | SPACES}; SECTION and TO not underlined. Verified (pinned cobol.exe, probes under out/probe/initialize-clause): ALL SECTION TO HIGH-VALUES -> both sections 0xFF; ALL BINARY ZEROES (SECTION and TO omitted) -> NULs; WORKING-STORAGE LOCAL-STORAGE SECTION X"5A" (reverse order, TO omitted) -> both ZZZZ; singular SPACE refused COBOLNET1727 naming the keyword spelling; ALL mixed with a section name refused (outer braces are exclusive); empty target refused; --std 85/2002/2014 refused COBOLNET0900 (E.3.3 item 33). SCREEN leg refused by name via ScreenFacility (declined A.4.2 module, PB260 owns). DEFECT (the other half of the choice-indicator group): the grammar writes optionsInitializeSection+ and OptionsBinder.InitializeOf ORs the flags with Aggregate, never calling ChoiceIndicators.AtMostOnce, so `INITIALIZE WORKING-STORAGE WORKING-STORAGE TO X"5A".` compiles clean and runs (W=[ZZZZ]); cite.py --check 5.2.6.4 "When enclosed by braces, one or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative shall be specified only once" -> OK; expected COBOLNET2104 choice-alternative-repeated. cite.py --check 11.9.10.2 "INITIALIZE" -> OK. No existing spec-derived test pins the whole format (OptionalWordSubsetDriftTests covers SECTION/TO omission only; pb152 goldens cover semantics), so test-ref empty. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): COBOL-2023 only (Annex E.3.3 item 33: OPTIONS INITIALIZE clause is a 2023 introduction); below 2023 the clause is refused

subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: Rule: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING IS {NEAREST-AWAY-FROM-ZERO|NEAREST-EVEN|PROHIBITED|TRUNCATION}, IS optional (not underlined), exactly one of four (cite.py --check 11.9.11.1 "INTERMEDIATE" -> OK, the general-format line). Grammar: `intermediateRoundingClause : INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING IS? intermediateRoundingMode` with a SEPARATE 4-alternative intermediateRoundingMode (not the 8-mode roundingModeName), so the restricted set is enforced by syntax; RoundingModes.MapIntermediate maps the four keywords 1:1 onto CobolRounding. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/irfmt): `INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING NEAREST-EVEN` (IS omitted) compiles and runs; `... IS PROHIBITED` compiles; `... IS NEAREST-TOWARD-ZERO` and `... IS AWAY-FROM-ZERO` (ROUNDED-phrase-only modes) are rejected COBOL0001; at --std 2002 the clause draws COBOLNET0900 'OPTIONS INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING requires COBOL-2014', at --std 2014 it compiles. Editions: the 2023 Annex E change lists neither introduce nor change this clause, so it is carried from 2014; absent from 2002 (OPTIONS carried only ARITHMETIC NATIVE/STANDARD) and 85 (no OPTIONS paragraph) -> 2014,2023. Test-ref: pb145_round_{away,even,trunc,prohib} (2023) spell the clause with IS and run it (spec-derived expectations); no golden spells the IS-omitted form or a negative for a non-listed mode (probe-verified only).

subject: PROGRAM-ID paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB894. Both formats (PDF p310 rendered): Format 1's attribute group and Format 2's `PROGRAM-ID. program-prototype-name-1 [AS literal-1] IS PROTOTYPE .` are ALTERNATIVES of programIdParagraph, and the IS PROTOTYPE tail is the ONE prototypePhrase rule the FUNCTION-ID paragraph shares (IS unstressed, so optional — the golden writes `PGPR PROTOTYPE.`). Before PB894 Format 2 drew COBOLNET0901 on the reserved word. Format 2 is a COBOL-2002 introduction (program-prototype-2002; below it COBOLNET0900 from the bound arm).

subject: Environment division structure
notes: Rule §12.2.1: 'ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.' (both words underlined, period required) followed by '[ configuration-section ]' then '[ input-output-section ]' -- both optional, in that order. Grammar environmentDivision = ENVIRONMENT DIVISION DOT configurationSection? inputOutputSection? matches exactly (no binder/validation pass narrows it; ClosedFormatPass line 132 only names the node). Probed with pinned cobol.exe at --std 85/2002/2014/2023: empty division, CONFIGURATION only, INPUT-OUTPUT only, both in order, empty section headers alone -> all compile and run correctly; INPUT-OUTPUT before CONFIGURATION -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'CONFIGURATION' (correct rejection, order is fixed by the format); header without period -> COBOL0307 (correct). cite.py --check 12.2.1 '[ configuration-section ]' -> OK; '[ input-output-section ]' -> OK. No spec-derived test targets this format (order rejection has no negative golden) -> test-ref empty = test-needed. Probes: out/probe/env-div/{A,B,C,D,E,G,H,N}.cob. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §12.2.1 format carries no edition gating; unchanged across editions)]

subject: Configuration section
notes: The format is `CONFIGURATION SECTION.` followed by four BRACKETED paragraph names — source-computer-paragraph, object-computer-paragraph, special-names-paragraph, repository-paragraph — and nothing else, RENDERED from the printed page (PDF p313 / printed folio 283). All four are modelled and all four are exercised together by the positive golden. The residue is now DIAGNOSED: the list ended in `vendorConfigurationParagraph -> genericClause`, so a misspelled or misplaced paragraph header was swallowed together with everything written under it (`CONFIGURATION SECTION.` + `WIBBLE WOBBLE.` compiled and ran). It is now the shared `unrecognizedClause` error production, refused by name with COBOLNET1971 — a PARAGRAPH-list code distinct from the clause-list COBOLNET1970, because naming an unrecognized paragraph header a 'clause' sends the reader to the wrong subclause. ⚠ Scope of this verdict: the general format's LIST is closed and complete. Whether a paragraph written TWICE, or out of the printed order, is separately diagnosed is a §5.2.6.2 ordering question over the same format and is not asserted here.

subject: SOURCE-COMPUTER paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB78 (2026-08-18) + PB830 (2026-09-22). RENDERED from the printed page (PDF p314 / folio 284): SOURCE-COMPUTER. [computer-name-1] . and nothing else; SR1 (no name -> the second period may be omitted) is the PB78 witness. The format is CLOSED since PB830: what follows the name used to be the `computerAttributes` `~DOT` token SINK, kept for the deleted '85 WITH DEBUGGING MODE and never gated, so `SOURCE-COMPUTER. IBM-370 WIBBLE WOBBLE.` compiled and ran at every edition (the previous CONFORMS witness answered a different question - the optional name). The '85 clause is now a modelled rule (`debuggingModeClause`, gated debugging-mode-removed-2002 at its node) and the residue is the `unrecognizedClause` error production, refused by name as COBOLNET1970 at every edition (the negative).

subject: OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB78 / PB64 T5 (2026-08-19) + PB830 (2026-09-22). RENDERED (PDF p315 / folio 285): OBJECT-COMPUTER. [computer-name-1] [ | CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION ... | PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE ... | ] . - computer-name-1 is optional and the two clauses may follow the period directly, in any order, each at most once (a duplicate is COBOLNET1652). The '85 format hung the clauses off a REQUIRED name, so the name-less clause form is gated below 2002 (computer-name-optional-2002, COBOLNET0900). CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION is LIVE (T5; an undeclared locale-name is COBOLNET1664). The format is CLOSED since PB830: the clause list ends in the `unrecognizedClause` error production (COBOLNET1970 at every edition - the pb830 negative), replacing the `computerAttributes` `~DOT` sink that swallowed `OBJECT-COMPUTER. IBM-370 WIBBLE WOBBLE.` in silence. The two '85 clauses ISO 2002 deleted, MEMORY SIZE and SEGMENT-LIMIT, are modelled `objectComputerClause` alternatives gated at their nodes; modelling them also fixed a rejects-legal-'85 gap the sink hid - the '85 printed order MEMORY SIZE ... PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE ... SEGMENT-LIMIT ... was COBOL0001 (the 85 golden, whose PCS must still take effect).

subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB829 (wave 48 W). The format was RENDERED (PDF p320-321 / folios 290-291) and every clause is now modelled: the last missing one, the dynamic-length-structure-clause (DYNAMIC LENGTH [STRUCTURE] name [IS] {|[SIGNED][SHORT] PREFIXED| |DELIMITED|} | physical-structure-name-1), was COBOL0001 'unexpected DYNAMIC' and is now dynamicLengthStructureClause (STRUCTURE/IS optional, the choice-indicator pair at-most-once through ChoiceIndicators), bound by DataBinder.DynamicLengthStructureBind and gated below 2014 (dynamic-length-structure-2014). The residue is DIAGNOSED (COBOLNET1970). The two-word switch-entry shape is SR8's semantic rule, owned by kb/Work PB862 (row SR-12.3.7.3-8), not this general format. kb/Work PB977: a FOR phrase written AFTER the definition of an ALPHABET, CLASS or SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS clause — a position no edition prints and no dialect owns — is the grammar's misplacedSpecialNamesForPhrase error production, refused by name at every edition (COBOLNET2315, ClosedFormatPass); the ALPHABET postfix used to compile clean as a 'historical superset' and the CLASS one drew a bare COBOL0001. (Train 51 composition: PB829 landed first and closed the dynamic-length-structure-clause residue this batch was written against, so the row stays CONFORMS.)

subject: REPOSITORY paragraph
notes: Rendered PDF p334-335: every specifier - class [AS literal-1] [EXPANDS ...], interface [AS literal-2] [EXPANDS ...], FUNCTION {intrinsic-function-name-1}... INTRINSIC | FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC, program [AS literal-3], property [AS literal-4], user-defined function [AS literal-5] - now parses as printed (kb/Work PB974: the AS phrase was on PROGRAM only, and the intrinsic list took one name). The REPOSITORY paragraph is a 2002 introduction (VersionConformancePass ParseArm.VisitRepositoryEntry).

subject: Input-output section
notes: Format: 'INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION. [ file-control-paragraph ] [ i-o-control-paragraph ]' (cite.py --check 12.4.2 "INPUT-OUTPUT" -> OK §12.4.2 General format). Grammar `inputOutputSection : INPUT_OUTPUT SECTION DOT fileControlParagraph? ioControlParagraph?` is the format verbatim: both words required, period required, both paragraphs optional, FILE-CONTROL before I-O-CONTROL. environmentDivision places it after configurationSection? (the §12.2 order). Bound by DataBinder.BindFileControl (env.inputOutputSection()?.fileControlParagraph()) and BindIoControl. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec/scratchpad/adj-d1/out/probe/iosec): p1 both paragraphs -> runs 'OK' at 2023; p2 empty INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION. -> runs 'EMPTY' at 2023 and at --std 85; p3 I-O-CONTROL before FILE-CONTROL -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'FILE-CONTROL', exit 65 (correct: the format orders them). Edition note: the 2023 spec carries no edition difference for this format, so the uniform acceptance is what the spec derives; whether COBOL-85 required FILE-CONTROL inside the section is not stated in ISO_COBOL.md and is not a basis for a verdict here. test-ref left empty: goldens exercise the both-paragraph shape (e.g. conformance:2023/l1_release_same_record_area) but none pins the optional-paragraph arms (empty section / I-O-CONTROL only) or the ordering refusal. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E row names the input-output section; the 2023 format is the only one the spec states)]

subject: FILE-CONTROL paragraph
notes: Rule: '<u>FILE-CONTROL</u>. [ file-control-entry ] ...' (cite.py --check 12.4.4.2 "file-control-entry" -> OK §12.4.4.2 General format). Grammar fileControlParagraph = FILE_CONTROL DOT fileControlClauseGroup* : required keyword, required separator period, zero-or-more file-control-entries -- exactly the format; it is optional inside inputOutputSection (FILE-CONTROL? then I-O-CONTROL?), matching §12.4.2. Probes with the pinned cobol.exe at --std 85/2002/2014/2023: (a) FILE-CONTROL. with zero entries compiles and runs (DISPLAY OK1); (b) two SELECT entries compile, write and read back both files (AAAABBBB); (c) FILE-CONTROL without its period is rejected COBOL0307 at every edition. The contents of each file-control-entry belong to §12.4.5 rows, not this one. No spec-derived golden targets the empty-paragraph form or the missing-period rejection, so test-ref is empty (test-needed). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change entry for the FILE-CONTROL paragraph format)]

subject: File control entry
notes: kb/Work PB829. The four formats were RENDERED from the printed pages (PDF p342-344 / folios 312-314); every clause of their union is modelled and the residue is DIAGNOSED (COBOLNET1970, the file-control negative - its residue now follows ORGANIZATION, because words after an ASSIGN operand are further TO operands). The last missing piece is closed (wave 48 W): the ASSIGN TO phrase is the LIST the printed format writes (`assignTarget+`, the ellipsis on the inner brace pair), and which lists are allowable is the 12.4.5.2 SR5 determination DOC-A.1-71 (one operand naming the file, or DISK/PRINTER then one operand), read in ONE place, AssignTargetRule.Resolve; any other list is COBOLNET2256 BY NAME where it used to be the parse error COBOL0308. Positive 85/pb829_assign_device_class proves DISK "x" and "x" name the same file; negative pb829-assign-target-list (two literals, reject-at all four editions).

subject: General
notes: Format: ACCESS MODE IS {SEQUENTIAL|RANDOM|DYNAMIC}, ACCESS/SEQUENTIAL/RANDOM/DYNAMIC underlined, MODE and IS optional words (cite.py --check 12.4.5.5.1 "ACCESS" -> OK). Grammar accessModeClause : ACCESS MODE? IS? accessMode; accessMode : SEQUENTIAL|RANDOM|DYNAMIC -- exact match. DataBinder.BindFileControl maps it via MapAccessMode onto FileModel.AccessMode. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 85 and 2023): 'ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC', 'ACCESS RANDOM', 'ACCESS IS DYNAMIC', 'ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL' all accepted and honoured (gA.cob, gB.cob); 'ACCESS MODE IS' with no mode rejected COBOL0312 (gE.cob); 'MODE IS RANDOM' without ACCESS rejected COBOL0312 (gF.cob). SIBLING (not this row): the FD grammar fileDescriptionClause (CobolData.g4:69-71) also admits organizationClause/accessModeClause/recordKeyClause, which §13.4.5.2's closed formats do not, and nothing reads them -- 'FD SQ ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC.' compiles and runs silently as a plain sequential file (gG.cob, gH.cob); reported as a finding against FMT-13.4.5.2. No spec-derived golden targets the clause's format variants, so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (Annex E lists no substantive change to the ACCESS MODE clause)]

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: kb/Work PB756: Printed format: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS { data-name-1 | record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS {data-name-2}... } [WITH DUPLICATES] [SUPPRESS WHEN literal-1]; underlined ALTERNATE, RECORD, SOURCE, DUPLICATES, SUPPRESS. Grammar: `ALTERNATE RECORD? KEY? IS? (recordKeySourcePhrase | dataReference) (WITH? DUPLICATES)? alternateKeySuppressWhen?`. VERIFIED correct: KEY/IS/WITH/WHEN optional (pb695 golden); DUPLICATES-then-SUPPRESS fixed order (probe fmtord.cob: `SUPPRESS WHEN "A" WITH DUPLICATES` -> COBOL0312, correct, two sequential brackets with no choice indicators); SUPPRESS introduction-gated (probe sr7zero.cob --std 2014 -> COBOLNET0900); SOURCE with no record-key-name refused (fmtsrc.cob -> COBOL0312); the record-key-name SOURCE arm parses and is refused by name COBOLNET1954 (fmtsrc2.cob), which is the Annex A.3 item 40 declined arm (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 40); a subscripted/ref-modded operand refused (fmtrm.cob `R-GRP(1:2)` -> COBOLNET2024). DIVERGENCE: RECORD is UNDERLINED but `RECORD?` makes it optional - probe fmtrec.cob `ALTERNATE KEY IS R-G2` compiles exit 0 with no diagnostic at 2023 (under-rejects). That defect is OWNED by the OPEN note kb/Work PB756 (not re-reported here). Also related open note PB481 (ref-modified key) - on this pin the ref-mod form is refused by COBOLNET2024 for the ALTERNATE clause, so PB481 may be partly stale for this clause (owner of PB481 should re-measure). cite.py --check E.3.3 "The SUPPRESS WHEN phrase may be specified as part of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause" -> OK item 42. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85,2002,2014,2023 (the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase from 2023 only: Annex E.3.3 item 42, cite.py --check OK)]

subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1075: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.2 "COLLATING" OK (diagram); --check 5.2.6.4 "any single alternative shall be specified only once" OK. The grammar parses Format 1's IS form, the FOR-split form (FOR optional per the PB695 underline census, both alternatives in either order: probe p16 `SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL IS NREV ALPHANUMERIC REV` runs) and Format 2's `OF name... IS? alphabet`. Two shape defects: (1) Format 2 takes `OF cobolWord+`, so a QUALIFIED data-name-1 is a parse error — probe p14 `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF IX-KEY IN IX-REC IS REV` -> `COBOL0312: unexpected 'IN'`; data-name-1 is a user-defined word 'including qualification ... if needed' (§5.2 table) and §8.4.2.2 requires qualification where the name is not unique (two FDs sharing a key field name is ordinary), while RECORD KEY itself takes dataReference — rejects legal source. (2) the FOR choice-indicator group is `collatingForPhrase+` and CaptureFileCollating overwrites alnum/nat on each phrase, so `FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS REV FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS DREV` is accepted with last-wins (probe p15 only drew an error because its second name was undeclared) — §5.2.6.4 'any single alternative shall be specified only once' under-rejected. Also: when IS is omitted and SR6 subscripting is written the parse error is generic (p11). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]

subject: FILE STATUS clause
notes: Format 'FILE STATUS IS data-name-1' with only STATUS underlined (cite.py --check 12.4.5.8.2 "IS data-name-1" -> OK; the figure note at the SELECT Format 1 states FILE is not underlined). Grammar `FILE? STATUS IS? dataReference`; ClauseDataName refuses a written subscript (COBOLNET2024, probe p1c.cob) since data-name-1 is a qualified-data-name; qualification resolves through the one §8.4.2.2 resolver (probe qual.cob: `FILE STATUS IS FS OF G1` -> status 35 lands in G1's FS, G2's untouched); bare `STATUS FS` accepted and works (probe gr1.cob). Probes under probe/fs/ [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023]

subject: LOCK MODE clause
notes: kb/Work PB755: cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.2 'Both brace groups are plain' OK: the figure notes say LOCK (both), MANUAL, AUTOMATIC, ON, MULTIPLE, RECORD, RECORDS are underlined and MODE, IS, WITH are not. Grammar: `LOCK MODE? IS? (MANUAL|AUTOMATIC) lockOnPhrase?` / `WITH? LOCK ON? MULTIPLE? (RECORD|RECORDS)`. probe out/probe/lock-mode-clause/gen.py (pinned cobol.exe): these compile at exit 0 as the format requires: a) `LOCK MODE IS MANUAL WITH LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS`, b) `LOCK MODE AUTOMATIC LOCK ON RECORDS`, n) `LOCK IS MANUAL` (--std 2002). These are rejected as required: d) `LOCK MODE IS` with no MANUAL/AUTOMATIC (COBOL0312), e) `... LOCK ON MULTIPLE` with no RECORD(S) (COBOL0312), i) at --std 85 (COBOLNET0900, the 2002 introduction gate). DIVERGES because of c): `LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC WITH LOCK MULTIPLE RECORDS` leaves out the underlined ON and still compiles at exit 0 with no diagnostic (under-rejects). The OPEN note kb/Work PB755 already owns this exact mechanism, so no new finding is filed here. PB755 carries inventory_rows: [] and should claim this row. Spec-derived coverage of the accepted spellings is conformance:2002/pb695_lock_mode_optional_words (the optional words only). No negative covers the ON omission, which is PB755's to add. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause is absent from ISO 1989:1985; it arrives with the 2002 file sharing / record locking facility, D.2.4 / A.4.7; no later change to 12.4.5.9 located)]

subject: ORGANIZATION clause
notes: kb/Work PB706 (2026-09-22). The general format `[ORGANIZATION IS] { {LINE|RECORD} SEQUENTIAL | RELATIVE | INDEXED }` RENDERED from the printed page (PDF p357): ORGANIZATION, LINE, SEQUENTIAL, RELATIVE, INDEXED underlined; IS and RECORD NOT (optional words, --check 5.2.3). Grammar: `organizationType : LINE SEQUENTIAL | RECORD? SEQUENTIAL | RELATIVE | INDEXED` - RECORD SEQUENTIAL used to be a raw COBOL0001/0312 parse error at every edition. The written-out RECORD word is the 2023 inner choice (constructs.json file-organization-record-sequential-2023, COBOLNET0900 below 2023); bare SEQUENTIAL is ungated. The pb706 golden writes and reads back all three spellings (RECORD SEQUENTIAL, bare SEQUENTIAL with ORGANIZATION IS omitted, no clause).

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: The general format is implemented EXACTLY as printed, and the printed page was rendered rather than inherited from the transcription (kb/Work PB292): RECORD, DELIMITER and STANDARD-1 are underlined (required words), IS is not (an optional word), feature-name-1 is a user-defined word, and the braces are a plain required choice of exactly one alternative with no choice indicators. `recordDelimiterClause : RECORD DELIMITER IS? (STANDARD_1 | cobolWord)` is that diagram one-for-one. All FOUR legal spellings are exercised by the golden and each draws the clause's named decline: STANDARD-1 with IS (file F1), feature-name-1 with IS (F2), STANDARD-1 with the optional word omitted (F3); the complement, a file with no clause at all (F4), draws none. The format row is CONFORMS rather than DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT because the syntax IS accepted here — §4.2.6 licenses accepting a declined processor-dependent element and only compels the warning, unlike Annex A.4.1, which forbids accepting an unclaimed OPTIONAL element's syntax (the A.4.8 FORMAT rows are DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT for that reason).

subject: RECORD KEY clause
notes: kb/Work R43 (owner, 2026-09-24): an unsupported facility is unsupported entirely — item 2: a rule HALF inside a declined facility takes its LIVE half's verdict; the declined half (the record-key-name-1 SOURCE alternative, A.3 item 40) parses and is refused by name (COBOLNET1954). The data-name-1 alternative matches the grammar's recordKeyClause. ||

subject: RELATIVE KEY clause
notes: Format: '<u>RELATIVE</u> KEY IS data-name-1' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.13.2 "RELATIVE" -> OK). Underlining MEASURED on the printed page (figure_extract.py 360, main tree PDF): only RELATIVE is underlined; KEY and IS are plain, so both are optional words (cite.py --check 8.3.2.4.3 "uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words" -> OK). Grammar `relativeKeyClause : RELATIVE KEY? IS? dataReference` spells exactly that. data-name-1 is a qualified-data-name: DataBinder.BindFileControl captures name + qualifiers via ClauseDataName, and ScreenClauseOperandShape rejects a subscript, a reference-modifier (cite.py --check 8.4.3.3.3 "reference-modification is not permitted" -> OK) and the special registers. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/relkey): rk1 `RELATIVE KEY IS WS-RK OF WS-G` with a same-named WS-RK OF WS-H compiles and binds the qualified item; rk2 `RELATIVE KEY IS WS-RK(1:2)` -> COBOLNET2024 error (correct rejection, though the message says 'written with a subscript' for a reference-modifier on a non-OCCURS item — wording only); rk3 `RELATIVE WS-RK` (no KEY) compiles clean at --std 2023 and --std 85 — CORRECT, it is conforming source. NB the grammar comment above relativeKeyClause (CobolIO.g4 ~289-297) and the Frontend DiagnosticDescriptors CBL3613/3614 text call the no-KEY form a 'non-standard CCVS leniency ... ISO §12.4.5.13 requires it' — that is false (see finding); behavior is right, the documentation is wrong. Open kb/Work PB481 (ref-modified file key silently accepted) appears SUPERSEDED for RELATIVE KEY by ScreenClauseOperandShape (measured: rk2 rejected) — PB481 should be re-verified/closed by its owner. Syntax rules §12.4.5.13.3 SR1-3 are owned by landed PB699 (not re-adjudicated here). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the RELATIVE KEY clause exists unchanged at every edition; no Annex E delta for its format)]

subject: RESERVE clause
notes: §12.4.5.14.2 prints `RESERVE integer-1 [AREA|AREAS]` (RESERVE underlined, AREA/AREAS optional, one of). Grammar `fileReserveClause : RESERVE integerLiteral (AREA | AREAS)?` matches exactly and is a fileControlClauses alternative. integer-1 is governed by §5.5 1) (cite.py --check 5.5 "shall be unsigned and nonzero unless otherwise specified in the associated rules" -> OK); IntegerOperandRules maps FileReserveClauseContext = Nonzero. Probes with the pinned cobol.exe at --std 85 and 2023: `RESERVE 5 AREAS`, `RESERVE 1 AREA`, `RESERVE 3` compile and run (OK); `RESERVE 0 AREAS` -> COBOLNET2386 citing §5.5 1); `RESERVE -2 AREAS` rejected (COBOL0312); `RESERVE 2.5 AREAS` rejected (COBOL0001); `RESERVE AREAS` rejected. cite.py --check 12.4.5.14.2 "integer-1" -> OK. Side observation (not this rule's shape, a §12.4.5.1 SELECT-format issue): a repeated clause (`RESERVE 2 AREAS RESERVE 3`, and equally `ACCESS SEQUENTIAL ACCESS SEQUENTIAL`) is accepted — reported as a dossier gap/lead against §12.4.5.1. No spec-derived test names RESERVE; test-ref empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the clause and its format are unchanged across editions; no Annex E entry)]

subject: SHARING clause
notes: Format: SHARING [WITH] { ALL [OTHER] | NO [OTHER] | READ ONLY } — SHARING/ALL/NO/READ/ONLY underlined, WITH/OTHER optional (cite.py --check 12.4.5.15.2 "SHARING" OK). Grammar sharingClause = SHARING WITH? sharingMode; sharingMode = ALL OTHER? | NO OTHER? | READ ONLY — exact match, one of three required. Probe (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/sharing-clause/p1.cob, --std 2023 and 2002): `SHARING NO.`, `SHARING READ ONLY`, `SHARING WITH ALL`, `SHARING WITH NO OTHER` all accepted and bound to the right modes (runtime statuses per Table 19: 61/00/61/...). n1.cob: `SHARING WITH READ.` (no ONLY) rejected COBOL0312; `SHARING WITH OTHER.` rejected (COBOLNET2072 — correct rejection, but its message text talks about WHEN OTHER/§5.2.6.2, a misleading diagnostic, not a conformance defect). --std 85: COBOLNET0900 on every SHARING clause (edition gate, VersionConformancePass ParseArm.VisitSharingClause; also conformance:negative/sharing_below_2002). Covering golden pb321_table19_open_arbitration writes all three alternatives (with WITH/OTHER spelled); the optional-word omissions are verified by probe only. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85 — rejected there)]

subject: I-O-CONTROL paragraph
notes: The format is `I-O-CONTROL . subject: File section

subject: Sort-merge file description entry
notes: The format is `SD file-name-1 [ record-clause ] .` and nothing else, RENDERED from the printed page (PDF p376 / printed folio 346) rather than read off the OCR. Both halves hold: the record-clause is modelled and the file-name-only spelling parses (the positive golden writes `SD SF RECORD CONTAINS 10 CHARACTERS.`), and the residue is now DIAGNOSED. The rule used to end in `genericFileDescriptionClause -> genericClause : IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER|literal)*`, a shared vendor-extension catch-all that made `SD SF WIBBLE WOBBLE.` compile and run in silence at every edition (kb/Work PB829); it now ends in the ONE `unrecognizedClause` error production, refused by name with COBOLNET1970. The COBOL-85 DATA RECORDS clause of this format is superset-parsed and removal-gated post-bind. A green witness that the legal clause parses would NOT have been evidence on its own — the row also owes the negative, because an open list can parse every legal clause and still accept anything at all.

subject: Working-storage section
notes: Owned by kb/Work PB1309. §13.5.2 prints WORKING-STORAGE SECTION. (both words underlined, so required) followed by an optional bracket of {77-level-description-entry | constant-entry | record-description-entry | type-declaration-entry} with an ellipsis: any number, any order, possibly none. Grammar: `workingStorageSection : WORKING_STORAGE SECTION DOT dataDescriptionEntry*`. The four kinds all ride dataDescriptionEntry, and the binder separates them by level number and body (CONSTANT / TYPEDEF). Probe probe/ws/p1fmt.cob mixes 77, a CONSTANT AS numeric, a TYPEDEF, a level-01 record using TYPE, another 77, and a CONSTANT AS alphanumeric, and a second program has an EMPTY WS. At --std 2002/2014/2023 it prints `007 42 ABWXYZ Q HI` / `EMPTY-WS-OK`, which is what the spec requires. The non-standard level 78 is refused (negative/pb485-level-78-working-storage). cite.py --check 13.5.2 "record-description-entry" OK. No golden exists that was written for the §13.5.2 interleaving of all four kinds, so test-ref is left empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The format admits exactly four entry kinds (77-level, constant, record-description, type-declaration). A record-description-entry's first entry shall have level-number 1 (13.11.1, cite.py OK). The grammar's `dataDescriptionEntry*` admits any level number as the first WS entry, and nothing downstream screens it: a WS whose first entry is `05 X PIC X` or `02 X PIC X` is none of the four kinds, yet it compiles clean and runs at --std 85, 2002 and 2023. Secondary: the BYTE-LENGTH OF constant-entry form is refused with COBOLNET0899. That form belongs to the 13.10 row, but it means one constant-entry shape the format admits is not accepted in WS. subject: Report group description entry
notes: Owned by kb/Work PB1287. The general format is `level-number [ entry-name-clause ] [type-clause] ... [varying-clause] .`, and entry-name-clause is §13.18.20, whose Format 3 is FILLER (§13.18.20.3 SR3: 'If the entry-name clause is specified in a data description entry or a report group description entry, either data-name-1 or FILLER shall be specified'). The grammar writes `reportGroupEntry : levelNumber reportGroupName? reportGroupClause* DOT` with `reportGroupName : cobolWord`, and FILLER is a reserved token that cobolWord does not admit. So the filler format has no parse path: probe/rgde/filler (`05 FILLER COLUMN 1 PIC X SOURCE WA.`) fails with COBOL0307 "unexpected 'FILLER'" at --std 85, 2002 and 2023. The clause set is otherwise complete. TYPE, NEXT GROUP, LINE, PICTURE, USAGE (SR7 of §13.18.60 limits it to DISPLAY/NATIONAL, screened by ScreenReportUsage), SIGN, JUSTIFIED, COLUMN, BLANK WHEN ZERO, SOURCE/SUM/VALUE, PRESENT WHEN, GROUP [INDICATE], the Format-3 OCCURS (DYNAMIC/KEY/INDEXED refused by ReportOccursOf) and VARYING all parse, in any order (probe fmtorder: `SOURCE WS PIC S9 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE COLUMN 1 USAGE IS DISPLAY` printed `-3`). cite.py --check 13.18.20.3 'either data-name-1 or FILLER shall be specified' -> OK §13.18.20.3 3). Rejects legal source, so DIVERGES; see the finding 'report-group-entry-filler-format'. || Editions (adjudicator's statement, normalized to 85,2002,2014,2023 by registrar 14e): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the report group description entry is Report Writer nucleus syntax at every edition; no Annex E item changes §13.15 between 2014 and 2023)

subject: Level-number
notes: (kb/Work PB1246, 14d). The general format is the single word `level-number`, whose shape §8.3.2.2.13 defines: "A level-number, expressed as a one-digit or two-digit number, indicates the hierarchical position of a data item or the special properties of a data description entry." (cite.py --check 8.3.2.2.13 -> OK); §13.18.33.3 SR3 adds the 01-09 spelling (--check 13.18.33.3 rule 3 -> OK). The grammar takes levelNumber : INTEGERLIT, and INTEGERLIT is INT_BODY = [0-9]+ (any digit count). LevelNumberPass screens only the parsed VALUE (int.TryParse + Arm.Permits), never the digit COUNT, so a three-or-more-digit spelling whose value is in range is accepted. Probe (pinned cobol.exe, probe/level-number/p1.cob): `001 A PIC X VALUE "A".` in WORKING-STORAGE compiles clean and prints A at --std 85/2002/2014/2023. Expected per §8.3.2.2.13: `001` is not a level-number (three digits), so the entry lacks the level-number §13.18.33.3 SR1 requires and a compile-time diagnostic is owed (§4.2.2). The value half conforms: out-of-range values (50, 78, twelve digits) draw COBOLNET1746 and 01-09/1/49/66/77/88 compile (conformance:85/pb485_level_number_legal_forms, negative/pb485-level-number-unparseable). Test-ref left empty because the row diverges on the spelling half. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the general format carries no edition marker; §8.3.2.2.13 defines the word in every edition) || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4#levelNumber; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4#INTEGERLIT; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Validation/LevelNumberPass.cs#LevelNumberPass.VisitLevelNumber

subject: SIGN clause
notes: kb/Work PB486 — THE CLAUSE'S OWN FORMAT IS EXACT; THE ENTRY MAY CARRY IT TWICE. The figure was RENDERED from the canonical PDF (scripts/render-spec-page.py 513 -> printed folio 483), not read from the transcription: `[ SIGN IS ] { LEADING / TRAILING } [ SEPARATE CHARACTER ]`, with SIGN, LEADING, TRAILING and SEPARATE underlined and IS and CHARACTER not, LEADING/TRAILING in BRACES (exactly one, no choice indicators). `signClause : (SIGN IS?)? (LEADING | TRAILING) (SEPARATE CHARACTER?)?` is a token-for-token match and every boundary was probed: all six printed shapes parse and behave (sg_fmt_bare_lead, sg_fmt_is_lead, sg_fmt_nosign_lead, sg_fmt_nosign_trail_sep, sg_fmt_full, sg_fmt_nosign_sepchar); the `SIGN IS` bracket is a UNIT, so `PIC S9(3) IS LEADING` is a parse error (sg_fmt_is_only); the brace is enforced, so `SIGN IS SEPARATE CHARACTER` with neither alternative is rejected (sg_fmt_neither); CHARACTER is optional and non-repeatable (sg_fmt_char_twice rejected). PARTIAL FOR ONE MEASURED OVER-ACCEPTANCE: a data description entry may carry the SIGN clause TWICE and the compiler silently takes the LAST. `01 A PIC S9(3) SIGN IS TRAILING LEADING VALUE -12.` compiles and stores a LEADING over-punch (`}12`) though the program selected TRAILING first (sg_fmt_trail_lead), while `SIGN IS LEADING TRAILING` stores a TRAILING over-punch (`01K`, sg_fmt_both) -- the LAST clause wins in written order either way, and `05 A PIC S9(3) SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE SIGN IS TRAILING VALUE -12.` compiles and DROPS the separate character position -- the enclosing group image shrinks from 5 characters to 4 (`G=[01K|]`; sg_fmt_twice / sg_fmt_sep_then_lead / sg85_dup_85 / _2002 / _2014 / _2023, identical at all four editions). Mechanism: `dataDescriptionClause*` is a plain star and DataBinder.cs:2378 assigns `ownSign` unconditionally on each pass of the clause loop, so a second SIGN clause overwrites the first with no diagnostic. Both enclosing general formats print the slot exactly once (§13.15.2 `[ sign-clause ]`; §13.16.2's own bracket) and §5.2.6.2 makes a bracket 'may be explicitly specified ... or omitted', never repeated. See finding sign-duplicate-clause-last-wins. The SCREEN SECTION alternative (CobolScreen.g4:68) is owner-declined A.4.2 non-support refused by name (COBOLNET1560, ScreenFacility.cs:89 carries the per-clause fact for signClause), owned by kb/Work PB260 -- not adjudicated here. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:647 (signClause); CobolData.g4:276 (dataDescriptionClause alt); CobolReportWriter.g4:94; CobolScreen.g4:68; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2377-2378; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Reports.cs:427-428

subject: SYNCHRONIZED clause
notes: The ANTLR rule is the printed figure token for token: a REQUIRED choice of SYNCHRONIZED|SYNC (no `?`, so one must be written) followed by an OPTIONAL at-most-one LEFT|RIGHT. Measured at all four editions (probe sy_elem_/sy_elem_left_/sy_elem_right_/sy_77_ x 85|2002|2014|2023, all exit 0), and the figure's complement is measured too: `SYNC LEFT RIGHT` -> COBOL0307 (probe sy_fmt_both_lr), a bare `LEFT` with no SYNC -> COBOL0307 (sy_fmt_bare_left), `SYNC IS LEFT` -> COBOL0001 (sy_fmt_sync_is; the figure has no IS). subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: Read the format at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22600-22604 (no 'Figure notes' block accompanies this diagram, so the transcribed <pre> IS the authority): ALLOCATE { arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 } [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ], with ALLOCATE / CHARACTERS / INITIALIZED / RETURNING underlined and no optional noise words. (RETURNING dataReference)?` — arm-for-arm identical to the diagram, both optional phrases optional in both arms, and no scope terminator / conditional phrase (matching Table 12's empty ALLOCATE row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:20867). Alternative order is safe because alt 1 requires the CHARACTERS token, so a bare data-name falls to alt 2 under ALL(*) prediction. The binder's `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` reads `al.dataReference()` (DIRECT children only, so data-names inside arithmeticExpression are not in the list) and indexes drefs[0] for data-name-1 / drefs[^1] for RETURNING — correct for all four legs, and the RETURNING()-null guard precedes the index so the no-RETURNING form cannot index an empty list. (RETURNING dataReference)?` tail matches it in both arms. subject: CONTINUE statement
notes: Re-read the format in specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23190 and validated it mechanically (`cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK, returning the whole format line). Derived expectation BEFORE reading code, from the repaired Figure-notes block: CONTINUE is a required word (the printed missing underline is the C2 typo), the bracket makes the whole phrase optional, and AFTER / SECONDS carry underline rules so they are REQUIRED inside the phrase; the operand is arithmetic-expression-1 (a full 8.8.1 arithmetic expression, not a mere identifier/literal). READ: `continueStatement : CONTINUE (AFTER arithmeticExpression SECONDS)? ;` (CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363). Token-for-token identical to the derived shape: CONTINUE mandatory (so `AFTER 5 SECONDS` alone cannot parse as a CONTINUE, the Figure-notes' second argument), the group is `( ... )?` (bracket), AFTER and SECONDS are hard tokens inside it (not `AFTER?` / `SECONDS?`), so `CONTINUE 5` is rejected. The operand nonterminal is the SHARED `arithmeticExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4:208 -> additiveExpression -> multiplicative -> power), i.e. the same 8.8.1 rule PERFORM VARYING uses, so a parenthesized/compound expression, a literal, an identifier and a function reference are all admitted -- not a narrowed operand. The grammar's own header comment (CobolControlFlow.g4:359-360) records the same page-604-vs-page-732 contradiction the Figure notes do and resolves it the same way (the defining occurrence governs), so the transcription and the grammar agree rather than one having inherited the other's typo. Wired into the single `statement` rule at CobolParserCore.g4:719. EDITION (derived from Annex E, NOT from the registry's own IntroducedIn column): Annex E.3.3 item 14 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43957 -- "Additional functionality added to the CONTINUE statement. The CONTINUE statement has been enhanced to provide the ability to pause runtime execution for a specified period of time" -- so the bracketed phrase is 2023-only while bare CONTINUE is 85-continuous. The compiler gates exactly that split: VersionConformancePass.VisitContinueStatement fires COBOLNET0900 only when `ctx.arithmeticExpression()` is present (Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs:584-589), i.e. on the PHRASE, never on the verb -- confirmed by 85/wavef_dbg_proc.cob and 85/index_name_r7_windows.cob compiling bare CONTINUE at --std 85. I additionally checked the two edges the adjudicator did not: (a) `unaryExpression : addOp unaryExpression | primaryExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4) admits a LEADING SIGN, so `CONTINUE AFTER -1 SECONDS` -- the literal spelling of the GR1a negative case -- parses, and `primaryExpression` admits numericLiteral / ZERO_ARITH / functionCall / dataReference / `( arithmeticExpression )`, so the operand really is the full 8.8.1 rule; (b) the SECONDS terminator cannot be swallowed by the operand, because `additiveExpression` stops at a non-addOp token and `dataReference` is single-word except for OF/IN qualification. I verified the test-refs are LIVE rather than merely present: tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json lists `continue_after` at enabled[22], and tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/VersionMatrixTests.cs:79/:124 are the two named methods; the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` carries source `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS.` with expectDiagnostic COBOLNET0900. || REFUTED (edition-basis citation, verdict unchanged): the adjudicator wrote "E.2's new-reserved-word list at :43951 adds SECONDS". That is WRONG on both counts and I did not inherit it. Line 43951 sits inside Annex **E.3.3 item 13** (heading at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43225 `E.3.3 Not affecting`), whose lead sentence is "**Context-sensitive words.** In order to provide enhanced functionality, the following words have either been added to the list of context-sensitive words or the context in which they are reserved has been expanded" -- SECONDS is in the CONTEXT-SENSITIVE list, not a reserved-word list. The 8.10 context-sensitive-words table at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:9578 confirms it: `| SECONDS | RETRY phrase, CONTINUE statement |`. The compiler agrees with the STANDARD and not with the adjudicator's note: CobolLexer.g4:562-568 comments SECONDS as "8.10 context-sensitive (user-legal at every edition)" and CobolWords.g4:89 re-admits it as a user word. notes: kb/Work/PB396.md — ALL FOUR recorded divergences are closed, and each was re-measured on this tree rather than inherited. (3) imperative-statement-1 sits INSIDE the outer brace group, unbracketed, so §5.2.6.3 makes it required and §5.2.6.2 gives the omission licence to brackets only: `evaluateWhenClause` now reads `evaluateWhenPhrase+ statementBlock` (statementBlock IS statement+), and `EVALUATE X WHEN 3 END-EVALUATE` is refused COBOLNET2072 where it used to compile in silence. The outer `{ … } …` is itself unbracketed, so at least one ordinary WHEN group is required and an EVALUATE whose only clause is WHEN OTHER is no longer a spelling of this statement. (4) `[ WHEN OTHER imperative-statement-2 ]` is ONE bracketed phrase FOLLOWING the repetition — §5.2.7 scopes an ellipsis to the portion between the delimiters immediately to its left, which the OTHER phrase is outside of — so it is a trailing `evaluateWhenOther?` on `evaluateStatement` rather than a second alternative of the repeated clause. A repeated or mispositioned WHEN OTHER is refused COBOLNET2073; it used to be admitted at any position any number of times, with EvaluateBinder's `other = body` discarding all but the last. The positive control at the introducing edition writes every position WITH its imperative and pins the values from the general rules, so the tightening cannot have been "satisfied" by refusing the construct.

subject: GENERATE statement
notes: Format: GENERATE {data-name-1 | report-name-1} (cite.py --check 14.9.16.2 "GENERATE" OK). The grammar parses one operand, `GENERATE reportGroupReference` = cobolWord [(IN|OF) reportName]. The optional qualifier is SR1's "It may be qualified by a report-name". BindGenerate tells the two alternatives apart by resolution. An unqualified name that resolves to a report is report-name-1 (summary reporting); otherwise it resolves through ReportGroupResolution to a report group (data-name-1). A name that matches neither is COBOLNET1757. Both alternatives were compiled and run in probe out/probe/generate/g1.cob (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): `GENERATE DE-1` and `GENERATE R-1`. subject: GO TO statement
notes: kb/Work/PB412.md landed w41. DEPENDING ON identifier-1' -- one or more names (5.2.7), DEPENDING underlined and required (5.2.2), ON optional. The transcription matches the page. THE REPAIR IS STRUCTURAL: goToStatement now carries ONE ALTERNATIVE PER PRINTED FORMAT plus the edition-gated ANSI-85 target-less arm, so the complement is a syntax error in the parser; GoToFormats.Of is the ONE classifier every reader asks (the binder's total three-arm switch, the BareGotoRemoved2002 gate, and the ALTER sole-GO-TO-paragraph test), replacing three separate reconstructions from optional children; and CobolErrorStrategy re-codes the resulting parse error as COBOLNET2172 naming the format's own cardinalities. (procedureName)* (DEPENDING ON? dataReference)?', so 'GO TO A B.' compiled at every edition and the Format-1 bind arm read names[0] and DISCARDED B in silence, while 'GO TO DEPENDING ON X.' compiled clean and aborted the run unit on a BoundUnsupported loud stage -- that stage is now deleted. subject: IF statement
notes: kb/Work/PB387.md — Citations validated mechanically: `cite.py --check 14.9.19.2 "IF</u> condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ <u>ELSE</u> statement-2 ] <u>END-IF"` -> OK (General formats), and `--check 14.9.19.2 "NEXT SENTENCE is an archaic feature"` -> OK. The DIAGRAM is load-bearing here, so I rendered the PRINTED page rather than trusting the OCR: PDF page 665 (printed folio 635) at 300dpi. It confirms the transcription exactly -- rules under IF, ELSE and END-IF only; NO rule under condition-1, THEN, statement-1 or statement-2. (Note the transcription has since been repaired: docs/rearchitecture/spec-reconciliation/agents/verify-p665-incorrect-figure-0.json ledgered this same figure as carrying ZERO <u> markup; specs/ISO_COBOL.md:24334 now carries it and matches the print.) So per 5.2.2 the required keywords are IF/ELSE/END-IF, per 5.2.3 THEN is an optional word, per 5.2.6.2 only the ELSE phrase is optional, and Format 2's THEN and ELSE arms are BRACES -- 5.2.6.3: 'Braces, { }, enclosing a portion of a general format indicate that the syntax element contained within the braces or one of the alternatives contained within the braces shall be explicitly specified'. DERIVED EXPECTATION: statement-1 is REQUIRED in both formats (unbracketed in Format 1; a brace alternative in Format 2), and statement-2 is REQUIRED whenever ELSE is written. GRAMMAR SAYS OTHERWISE: `ifStatement : IF condition THEN? statementBlock* (ELSE statementBlock*)? END_IF?` uses `*` on BOTH arms, and `statementBlock : statement+`, so zero statements is accepted in either arm. MEASURED with the pinned cobol.exe, all accepted rc=0 with no diagnostic: `IF X = 1 END-IF` (probe p1-empty-then); `IF X = 9 ELSE DISPLAY "E" END-IF` (p2-empty-then-else); `IF X = 1 DISPLAY "T" ELSE END-IF` (p3-empty-else); `IF A = 1.` as a complete sentence (u7-empty-format2); `IF A = 1 DISPLAY "T" ELSE.` (u8-else-then-period); and nested (u6-empty-nested). Swept at --std 85 and --std 2023 (probe empty-std85 / empty-std2023): identical acceptance, so the leniency is edition-wide and not a dialect gate. WHAT IS RIGHT: everything else in both formats. IF and condition-1 required; `THEN?` optional per 5.2.3; the ELSE phrase optional per 5.2.6.2; NEXT SENTENCE reachable in BOTH arms via statement -> nextSentenceStatement (measured p6/p7); `END_IF?` is the correct UNION of Format 1 (END-IF required) and Format 2 (no END-IF) -- Format 2 measured period-terminated at all four editions (probe ed, std 85/2002/2014/2023, identical output). A SECOND, much smaller leniency falls out of that same union: because the grammar does not separate the two formats it also admits the cross-format mixture NEXT SENTENCE + END-IF, which no single format shows -- `IF X = 1 NEXT SENTENCE END-IF` is accepted (p11-mix-nextsent-endif) and behaves per GR4. Recorded as one mechanism in finding IF-F1. Not closed by a test: the only named test, tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Unit/Overlenient/M413_OverlenientIfElseTests.cs, has THREE EMPTY [Fact] bodies -- see finding IF-F2.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolControlFlow.g4:136 (ifStatement); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:793 (statementBlock : statement+); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolControlFlow.g4:365 (nextSentenceStatement)

subject: INSPECT statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1125 (open). Formats 1-4 + tallying/replacing/after-before/replacement-item. CONFORMING parts, probed: all four formats bind and run (P76 format 3 multi-counter N=05 M=01 X=xxyyzx; P67 CONVERTING; P79 AFTER+BEFORE either order); BACKWARD runs the spec's own NOTE 1 example = 2 (P77) and is rejected COBOLNET0845 at --std 2014/2002/85 (E.3.3 34 'BACKWARD context sensitive word added' --check OK); tallying FIRST/TRAILING and REPLACING TRAILING rejected COBOLNET2269 (P78; PB909 landed); duplicate AFTER/BEFORE in a TALLYING/REPLACING after-before-phrase is a parse error (P74, P81) because inspectDelimiters admits at most one of each. DIVERGENCES (all under-reject, strict --std 2023): (1) inspectTallyingItem is `dataReference inspectForClause+`, so `INSPECT X TALLYING N FOR ALL 'A' FOR ALL 'B'` compiles and runs N=04 (P70) - the printed tallying-phrase has ONE `identifier-2 FOR` per outer repetition, the middle ellipsis repeats only the CHARACTERS/ALL/LEADING phrase. (2) The bare-operand alternative of inspectCountPhrase and the optional adjective of inspectReplacingItem admit an adjective-less FIRST operand: `TALLYING N FOR 'A'` -> N=02 (P71), `REPLACING 'A' BY 'Z'` -> ZBCZB (P72); the binder seeds All 'for that (ungrammatical) case' (its own comment). The format requires ALL/LEADING (tallying) or ALL/LEADING/FIRST (replacing) before the first operand; GR10/GR16 transitivity covers only operands that FOLLOW an adjective. (3) inspectConvertingPhrase takes `inspectBeforeAfterPhrase*`, so CONVERTING accepts `BEFORE 'E' BEFORE 'C'` (P73 -> abCDEF, the last one silently wins) and `AFTER 'A' AFTER 'C'` (P80); the after-before-phrase's choice indicators (§5.2.6.4 'When enclosed by braces, one or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative shall be specified only once' --check OK) forbid a repeat - the TALLYING/REPLACING arm (inspectDelimiters) is right, the CONVERTING arm is not (two-arm shape). cite.py --check 14.9.22.2 'Format 4 (converting)' OK; 5.2.6.4 OK; E.3.3 OK. Related: PB786 (choice-indicator figure notes untested). probes under scratchpad/adj-d1/out/probe/inspect-p1 (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023 unless noted) [code-location note: BACKWARD (COBOLNET0845)] || editions as adjudicated: 85/2002/2014/2023 (BACKWARD 2023 only: E.3.3 item 34)

subject: INVOKE statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1135 (open). FMT 14.9.23.2: INVOKE {object-class-name-1 | identifier-1} {identifier-2 | literal-1} [USING {[BY REFERENCE]{identifier-3|OMITTED} | [BY CONTENT]{arithmetic-expression-1|boolean-expression-1|identifier-5|literal-2} | [BY VALUE]{arithmetic-expression-1|identifier-5|literal-2}}...] [RETURNING identifier-4]. Each [BY x] bracket is optional as a whole (figure notes; BY un-underlined per PB695). VERIFIED with pinned cobol.exe (probe/fmt-invoke/base.cob): class-name target + RETURNING (factory FM -> R=9), instance target + BY CONTENT N + 1 (6), universal target U + identifier-2 method name MN (5) all compile and run correctly; OMITTED / BY-less phrases are covered by conformance:2002/pb757_invoke_omitted and conformance:2002/pb695_invoke_by_omitted; BY CONTENT expression/boolean by conformance:2023/pb46_invoke_by_content_expression / pb46_invoke_by_content_boolean. DEFECT 1 (rejects legal source): an argument written WITHOUT a BY phrase may be arithmetic-expression-1 or boolean-expression-1 (the [BY CONTENT]/[BY VALUE] brackets are optional; §14.9.23.3 SR14 'If an argument is specified without any BY phrase, BY REFERENCE is implied for that argument when:' a) valid for by-reference ... ; §14.9.23.4 GR4 'An argument that consists merely of a single identifier or literal is regarded as an identifier or literal rather than an arithmetic or boolean expression.' presupposes bare expressions). invokeArgument's bare arms are only OMITTED | addressIdentifier | dataReference | literal — no arithmeticExpression, no {boolExprAhead()}? booleanExpression (CALL's callArgument, CobolParserCore.g4:1338, has both since PB130). Probes: `INVOKE O "TAKEN" USING N + 1.` -> COBOLNET0828 '2 USING argument(s) for 1 formal parameter(s)' (the PB46 silent mis-parse shape); `USING BY CONTENT N N + 1` -> '3 ... for 2'; `USING B1 B-AND B2` -> COBOLNET0901 'B-AND is a reserved word'. Expected: each compiles, one argument, passed by content (SR14 does not imply BY REFERENCE for an expression), value 6. subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB421.md landed w41. Both general formats were already faithfully implemented and the diagram was verified as PRINTED (PDF p.694): Format 1 'MOVE {identifier-1|literal-1} TO {identifier-2}...' and Format 2 'MOVE {CORRESPONDING|CORR} identifier-3 TO identifier-4'. The whole divergence was ONE over-accepting alternative: moveReceivingPhrase carried '(CORRESPONDING | CORR) dataReference TO dataReference', which composed with 'MOVE moveSendingOperand moveReceivingPhrase' to admit 'MOVE <sending-operand> CORRESPONDING id-3 TO id-4' -- a shape neither format prints, which the binder could not build, so MoveBinder fell through to BoundUnsupported and the compiler EMITTED A PROGRAM that died at run time claiming an unimplemented COBOL feature. The alternative is DELETED (Format 2 is spelled whole by moveStatement's first alternative), the shape is now a parse error re-coded as COBOLNET2173 naming both formats, and the fall-through message no longer says 'MOVE CORRESPONDING'. All FOUR spellings of the over-acceptance (identifier/literal sender x CORRESPONDING/CORR) are refused at all four editions, and the six legal spellings still compile. The drift guard is stated over the WHOLE grammar: a format-selecting CORRESPONDING/CORR keyword may be named only by a statement rule, never by a phrase rule it composes with.

subject: MULTIPLY statement
notes: OWNED BY kb/Work PB1142 (open). Both formats parse and bind: F1 `BY {identifier-2 [rounded]}...` (multi-receiver, per-receiver ROUNDED), F2 one sending `BY {identifier-2|literal-2}` + `GIVING {identifier-3 [rounded]}...`; the SIZE ERROR pair in either order and ON omitted (5.2.6.4 choice indicators, cite --check 5.2.6.4 'any single alternative shall be specified only once' OK); a duplicated ON SIZE ERROR is rejected (COBOL0307). subject: PERFORM statement

subject: RAISE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1197 (registrar 14c). Format: RAISE { EXCEPTION exception-name-1 | identifier-1 }, exactly one alternative. The named test covers the EXCEPTION alternative; the identifier alternative is covered by conformance-test:OoSpineTests.RaiseObject_NoDeclarative_ContinuesNextStatement. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — identifier-1 in the general format is ANY identifier (§8.4.3.1.2 Formats 1-9) that is an object reference, but the grammar narrows it to objectReference (dataReference|NULL|SELF|SUPER). Two legal identifier-1 shapes are rejected at the parse. The first is the inline method invocation (§8.4.3.1.2 Format 4). §8.4.3.4.3 SR1 bars it only as a receiving operand, and RAISE SR3 makes identifier-1 a sending operand. The second is the object-view (Format 5, §8.4.3.5.3 SR2, receiving-only ban). The compiler's own inlineMethodInvocation rule exists and parses in SET ... TO, so this is RAISE-specific for the inline invocation. The EXCEPTION alternative and plain data-name object references do conform. subject: READ statement
notes:
kb/Work PB331 LANDED (and PB332's format half rides the same grammar). THE PRINTED FIGURE WAS MEASURED, NOT INHERITED. `clause_page.py 14.9.30.2` -> PDF page 722 / folio 692, RENDERED with `render-spec-page.py 722`; `figure_geometry.py 722` reports, in printed order: Format 1 = a plain bracket y=280.90 h=48.79 over THREE stacked alternatives (ADVANCING ON LOCK / IGNORING LOCK / retry-phrase) and a SEPARATE plain bracket y=339.26 h=31.98 over TWO (WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK); Format 2 = the same pair at y=507.57 and y=547.48, then the KEY bracket at y=589.03. Neither lock bracket carries choice indicators - contrast the AT END group at y=377.08 and the INVALID KEY group at y=634.55, which the same tool flags `<-- CHOICE INDICATORS (5.2.6.4)`.
THREE RULES, ALL THREE NOW MODELLED. 5.2.6.2 (`--check` OK, 'or one of the alternatives contained within the brackets') makes each bracket AT MOST ONE alternative; 5.2.6.1 (`--check` OK, 'a unique combination of possibilities from a series of brackets') makes the two brackets INDEPENDENT; 5.2.1 (`--check` OK, 'shall be written in the compilation group in the sequence given in the general format') makes the printed ORDER normative, so the KEY phrase follows both brackets.
WHAT WAS WRONG, MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER ON THIS WORKTREE'S cobol.exe. (1) ORDER: `READ IXF RECORD WITH NO LOCK KEY IS IX-KEY ...` was `error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'KEY'` (identically with IGNORING LOCK and with RETRY 3 TIMES), because `readKey?` sat BEFORE the lock slots and ANTLR takes the first matching alternative in written order; all three now compile and run, and the unprinted reverse `KEY IS IX-KEY WITH NO LOCK` - which used to compile - is now rejected (negative/pb331-read-key-before-lock). (2) CARDINALITY, INVERTED BOTH WAYS BY ONE MERGED RULE: `recordLockPhrase : IGNORING LOCK | WITH? NO LOCK | WITH? LOCK` reached through three free optionals made the LEGAL pair `IGNORING LOCK WITH NO LOCK` a syntax error (`no viable alternative at input 'WITH'`) while accepting `ADVANCING ON LOCK RETRY 3 TIMES IGNORING LOCK`, three alternatives out of one bracket. Now `readLockContentionPhrase` is bracket 1 and `recordLockPhrase` is bracket 2 - one grammar object per printed bracket - so the legal pair compiles (conformance:2002/pb331_read_lock_brackets, line S1) and the three-alternative spelling is rejected (negative/pb331-read-two-from-one-lock-bracket). (3) THE MERGE LEAKED INTO TWO OTHER STATEMENTS: WRITE and REWRITE reference the same rule, and 14.9.51.2 (pages 815/816) and 14.9.35.2 (page 740) print `[ retry-phrase ]` and `[ WITH LOCK | WITH NO LOCK ]` with NO IGNORING LOCK alternative at all; `WRITE R IGNORING LOCK` and `REWRITE R IGNORING LOCK` compiled and are now rejected (negative/pb331-write-ignoring-lock, negative/pb331-rewrite-ignoring-lock). (4) ONE OPTIONAL WORD: `figure_extract.py 722` measures the underlines as `_ADVANCING_ ON _LOCK_`, so by 5.2.3 ON is an optional word and `READ ... ADVANCING LOCK` is conforming; it was `error COBOL0001: missing token before 'LOCK'` and now compiles (golden line S2). The transcription of this figure was already CORRECT on all four points - the grammar had diverged from it, so nothing in specs/ISO_COBOL.md needed repair.
THE MODEL FOLLOWS THE FIGURE END TO END, which is the part that keeps it fixed: `BoundRecordLock` lost its IgnoringLock member and is now the retention bracket alone, `BoundRead`/`BoundKeyedRead` carry `IgnoringLock` beside `AdvancingOnLock`/`Retry` for bracket 1, and the runtime's `FileRecordLock` / `CobolFile.ReadShared` / `ReadLockGovern` take the two facts separately - because a single enum cannot say `IGNORING LOCK WITH NO LOCK`, which is exactly why that spelling could not reach 14.9.30.4 GR11 b)'s release before. Design: docs/COBOLNET_FILES_DESIGN.md D15. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: the general format itself is present at all four editions; its lock phrases are Annex A.4.7 2002 introductions and are COBOLNET0900-gated at 85 (measured at --std 85 for IGNORING LOCK, WITH NO LOCK and ADVANCING LOCK - the split kept every gate, VersionConformancePass.VisitReadIgnoringLock being the new site the split required).
 (5) ONE MORE OPTIONAL WORD, WRITTEN DOWN TWICE: the statement's single printed RECORD lived in BOTH `readDirection : (NEXT|PREVIOUS) RECORD?` and `readStatement`'s own `RECORD?`, so the grammar accepted it TWICE - `READ SQF NEXT RECORD RECORD ... END-READ` compiled clean, exit 0, no diagnostics. 14.9.30.2 Format 1 prints it once, after the {NEXT|PREVIOUS} braces, and 5.2.3 makes a non-underlined word one that may be omitted, not repeated. `readDirection` is now `NEXT | PREVIOUS` and the word lives in one place (negative/pb331-read-record-word-twice). subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB347 LANDED. FORMAT, rendered from the licensed PDF rather than read from the OCR (scripts/render-spec-page.py, PDF page 734 = printed 704): `RELEASE record-name-1 [ FROM { identifier-1 | literal-1 } ]`, with RELEASE and FROM the underlined required words -- the transcription at 14.9.32.2 is faithful, and the operand IS record-name-1, not identifier-1. THE DIVERGENCE THIS ROW CARRIED (over-acceptance of the record-name-1 POSITION) IS CLOSED: `RELEASE SRT-REC(1:3)` used to compile with NO diagnostic at any --std and emit CobolSort.Release(..., CobolString.RefMod(SRT_REC.AsImage(), 1, 3)), releasing a 3-character record into an 8-byte sort file; it is now COBOLNET1757 at every edition. The rule behind it: a record-name is a user-defined word (8.3.2.2.25) and 5.2.4's operand table gives that operand type 'User-defined word, including qualification and subscripting if needed' and nothing further, while 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 permits reference modification only 'anywhere an identifier referencing a data item of class alphanumeric, boolean, or national is permitted' -- its NOTE drawing the consequence, 'where data-name-n is used in a general format or syntax rule, then reference-modification is not permitted' (all three --check OK). The refusal is at BIND, not in the grammar: `releaseStatement : RELEASE dataReference` stays general because the subordinate-item half of the same rule cannot be decided by a grammar, and one rule belongs in one place. THE ACCEPTED SURFACE IS UNCHANGED and still verified in both positive goldens: FROM omitted; FROM identifier; FROM subscripted identifier; FROM reference-modified identifier (an IDENTIFIER position, where 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 does permit it); FROM alphanumeric literal; FROM figurative constants (8.3.3.6.3 SR1). EDITION LEG unchanged: the literal-1 arm is gated 2002+ (`release-from-literal-2002` -> COBOLNET0871); the functionCall arm (the deliberate PB10 addition, legal by 8.4.3.1.2) carries no gate. Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32, so 2014 and 2023 are identical; the 85/2002 boundary for either FROM arm is not derivable from this document -- a dossier gap, not a verdict.

subject: RESUME statement
notes: General format: RESUME [AT] { NEXT STATEMENT | procedure-name-1 }, with RESUME, NEXT and STATEMENT underlined and AT not underlined (figure notes; the rendered figure's underlining is what the transcription records). Grammar: `resumeStatement : RESUME AT? (NEXT STATEMENT | procedureName)` - AT optional, one of the two operands required, NEXT STATEMENT both required.
