[editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the RESUME statement belongs to the exception model introduced by ISO 1989:2002; absent from 1985)]

subject: RETURN statement
notes: STILL DIVERGES, AND THE RESIDUE IS NOW EXACTLY ONE DEFECT. This row carried TWO independent defects; PB350's is LANDED and PB351's is not, so the verdict stays DIVERGES (a non-resolving verdict, so the row is still a GAP) and PB351 keeps holding it. PB350 (LANDED 2026-09-05) - the AT END phrase of RETURN was optional in the grammar. FORMAT RE-DERIVED FROM THE PRINTED PAGE (CLAUDE.md rule 1 - the diagram is load-bearing): python scripts/render-spec-page.py 738 (printed folio 708) renders 'RETURN file-name-1 RECORD [ INTO identifier-1 ] / AT END imperative-statement-1 / [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 ] / [ END-RETURN ]'; the AT END line carries NO bracket and NO choice indicators, while the two lines under it are bracketed, and the markdown transcription is FAITHFUL here. cite.py --check 5.2.6.2 'may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted' -> OK: brackets are the ONLY convention that makes a portion omissible. cite.py --check 5.2.2 'They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword, subject to the conventions specified in 5.2.6, Options' -> OK. cite.py --check 14.9.34.3 'The AT END phrase and the NOT AT END phrase, when specified, may be written in reversed order.' -> OK: SR4 permits REVERSAL, never omission. FIX: a bind-time screen, not a grammar change. StatementValidation.ScreenOmittedRequiredPhrase (COBOLNET1850, the mirror of COBOLNET1720's forbidden-phrase screen) is called from SortBinder.BindReturn on 'atEnd is null' AFTER PhraseBlocks.Split has normalized position away, so ONE test covers BOTH grammar arms - the absent phrase and the reversed spelling that writes only NOT AT END, whose AT END half the second alternative also made optional. The grammar keeps 'returnAtEndPhrase?' deliberately, with a comment saying so, because a bind-time diagnostic NAMES the omitted phrase, the statement and the clause where a parse error can only report an unexpected token. MEASURED BEFORE: 'RETURN SF RECORD END-RETURN.' and 'RETURN SF NOT AT END DISPLAY ... END-RETURN.' both compiled clean at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 (exit 0, no diagnostic) and the first printed R=ONE / R=TWO / R=TWO - past end-of-data the record area kept the previous record and control fell THROUGH the statement, so a loop written on RETURN never terminated from it. MEASURED AFTER: both are rejected with COBOLNET1850 at all four editions (exit 70), and the legal shapes still compile and run - the minimal AT END-only form and the SR4 REVERSED pair are the two positives, whose expected output is derived from 14.9.40.4 GR8 a) (ASCENDING returns the lower key first), 14.9.34.4 GR4 (no at end condition: control to imperative-statement-2 if specified, otherwise to the end of the statement) and 14.9.34.4 GR3 (at end: control to imperative-statement-1, then to the end of the statement). CORPUS SWEEP before the screen landed: grep -rn 'RETURN' tests/conformance tests/nist --include=*.cob, minus RETURNING/RETURN-CODE/RETURNED - every RETURN statement in both corpora writes its AT END (several on the following line, several with the optional word AT omitted), so nothing legal was newly rejected. SPEC SWEEP for siblings: over every 'General format' <pre> block in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, 14.9.34.2's is the ONLY unbracketed conditional-phrase line in any 14.9 statement format; SEARCH's two WHEN groups are the only other mandatory phrase and the grammar already writes searchWhenClause+ / searchAllWhenClause+. RequiredFormatPhraseDriftTests re-derives that set from the transcription and re-checks each adjudication's stated mechanism, so a transcription repair or a grammar restructure fails loudly. REMAINING - PB351 (open, OWNS the residue): CobolParserCore.g4#statementBlock is 'statement+', so a conditional statement not delimited by its explicit scope terminator is accepted wherever a general format writes imperative-statement-n (14.5.1) - one mechanism under roughly fifteen formats, of which this row is one.

subject: REWRITE statement
notes: General format: REWRITE {record-name-1 | FILE file-name-1} [RECORD] [FROM {identifier-1|literal-1}] [retry-phrase] [WITH LOCK | WITH NO LOCK] [|INVALID KEY| |NOT INVALID KEY| with choice indicators] [END-REWRITE]. Grammar rewriteStatement = REWRITE (recordName | FILE fileName) RECORD? rewriteFrom? retryPhrase? recordLockPhrase? rewriteInvalidKeyPhrase? END_REWRITE? - same order, same optionality; rewriteFrom admits dataReference / functionCall / inlineMethodInvocation (identifier-1) and literal; recordLockPhrase = WITH? NO LOCK | WITH? LOCK (WITH not underlined, one of two); rewriteInvalidKeyPhrase admits either phrase alone or both in either order (5.2.6.4 choice indicators). Probe pl.cob: `REWRITE R1 RECORD FROM "KEY1DATA01" RETRY 3 TIMES WITH NO LOCK NOT INVALID KEY .. INVALID KEY .. END-REWRITE`, `REWRITE R1 NO LOCK`, `RETRY FOR 2 SECONDS LOCK`, `RETRY FOREVER` all compile clean at 2023; pm.cob (FROM identifier + both key phrases) compiles at --std 85. The FILE file-name-1 alternative is PARSED and declined by name (COBOLNET1706, Annex A.4.13 Not claimed per docs/CONFORMANCE.md) - owner decision, landed as kb/Work PB282 which owns SR-14.9.35.3-7/8/10/11/12 and GR-14.9.35.4-9. cite.py --check 14.9.35.2 "retry-phrase is described in 14.7.9" -> OK. No spec-derived positive golden exercises every phrase combination, so test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 2023; ISO 1989:2023 Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to this rule (E.3.3 item 41 touches GR10 only), so 2014 identically; the 1985/2002 wording is not derivable from the 2023 text; retry-phrase and the LOCK bracket are later additions than 1985 (not derivable from the 2023 text)]

subject: ROLLBACK statement
notes: General format is the single keyword ROLLBACK (cite.py --check 14.9.36.2 "ROLLBACK" -> OK, <u>ROLLBACK</u>). Grammar: rollbackFacilityStatement : ROLLBACK, reached from `statement` under {facilityWord("ROLLBACK")}? so it is a statement exactly where §8.9 reserves the word. Editions from the spec: Annex E.3.2 item 2 'Commit and rollback facility' (cite.py --check E.3.2 "Commit and rollback facility." -> OK §E.3.2 2)) - a COBOL-2023 addition; below 2023 ROLLBACK is a user word and there is no ROLLBACK statement. Probed on the pinned cobol.exe (out/probe/rollback/rb9_2014.cob): a bare ROLLBACK statement compiles and runs at --std 2023, and at 85/2002/2014 is rejected as an undefined user word (COBOLNET1639) - correct, no such statement exists there. The goldens pin a bare ROLLBACK parsing as a statement in sentence and imperative positions. FMT under an unclaimed module: the derived selector commit-and-rollback-only excludes FMT rows by KIND and records that the shipped grammar matches the printed format, which this confirms.

subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB450 half 2 - the LAST printed general format of 14.9.39.2 whose grammar shape was not the figure's. The printed Format 7 was RE-RENDERED here (specs-private PDF p760 / folio 730 at 300 dpi) rather than taken from the transcription: `SET { ADDRESS OF data-name-1 | identifier-5 } ... TO identifier-6`, the brace a PLAIN required choice, the `...` OUTSIDE it, ADDRESS and TO underlined and OF NOT - and the figure note says the same in words, "The braces are a plain required choice - exactly one of the two alternatives - and the following `...` repeats the braced receiving operand" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.2 OK). The grammar held TWO fixed productions split on the SENDER's spelling, each hard-coding arity one, so four cells of the printed cross-product were a bare COBOL0001 at every edition. MEASURED on this worktree's own build BEFORE the fix: `SET ADDRESS OF B1 ADDRESS OF B2 TO P1` -> `COBOL0001: unexpected 'ADDRESS'`; `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF REC1` -> `cannot parse construct near 'REC1'`; `SET ADDRESS OF B1 P1 TO P2` -> `unexpected 'P1'`; `SET ADDRESS OF B1 TO ADDRESS OF R1` -> `unexpected 'ADDRESS'`. AFTER: all four compile and answer the values 14.9.39.4 GR12/GR13 and 8.4.3.11.4 GR1 compute (B1A=[AAAA] B2A=[AAAA] / B1A=[BBBB] / B1A=[CCCC] / B1A=[DDDD]). The rule is now ONE production whose repeated unit is a NAMED rule, `setAddressStatement : SET setAddressReceiver+ TO setAddressSender`, and the receiver carries its own kind (`ADDRESS()` present = data-name-1, absent = identifier-5) instead of a binder re-deriving it from token positions - the discipline half 1 landed for Formats 3 and 4, now held for this one by the same drift test. setObjectReferenceStatement moved AHEAD of it in setStatement, pinned by unit:PrintedFormatAlternativeDriftTests.SetObjectReferenceStatement_IsOfferedBeforeSetAddressStatement: Format 7's identifier-6 may be the predefined address NULL (SR19) and Format 5's identifier-4 the predefined object reference NULL (SR9), so `SET X TO NULL` is token-identical and only the receiver's category tells them apart, which is a BIND question. The other sixteen formats' shapes were swept and none carries a hard-coded arity: Formats 8, 9, 15 and the ENTRY extension already write `dataReference+`, Format 16's printed receiving operand IS one operand, and Format 6 is refused by name (COBOLNET1707).

subject: SORT statement
notes: kb/Work PB1175 (registrar 14c). cite.py --check 14.9.40.2 "Format 2 (table)" OK; --check 14.9.40.2 "may BOTH appear, in either order" OK (figure note: FOR ALPHANUMERIC / FOR NATIONAL are a choice-indicator brace, one or more, each once, any order); required words per the measured figure note: SORT, ASCENDING, DESCENDING, DUPLICATES, SEQUENCE, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL, INPUT, PROCEDURE, USING, THROUGH, THRU, OUTPUT, GIVING (COLLATING, ON, KEY, WITH, IN, ORDER, IS, FOR are optional). Grammar: sortStatement = SORT sortFileName sortKeyPhrase* sortDuplicatesPhrase? sortCollatingPhrase? ((USING|INPUT PROCEDURE)(GIVING|OUTPUT PROCEDURE))? END_SORT?; the Format-1 arity (>=1 key phrase, key data-names required, both legs required) and the Format-2 exclusion of USING/GIVING/procedures are screened in SortBinder once the operand's format is known (SortBindFile lines 70-118, SortBindTable 132-138); duplicate FOR ALPHANUMERIC / FOR NATIONAL -> COBOLNET0898 (probe c_dupfor). PROBE fmt1.cob at --std 2023 (multi-phrase keys with ON/KEY present and absent, DUPLICATES, COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL ... FOR ALPHANUMERIC in REVERSED order, USING two files, GIVING two files; second SORT with SEQUENCE IS (COLLATING omitted), INPUT PROCEDURE IS .. THROUGH .., OUTPUT PROCEDURE .. THRU ..) compiled and ran: OU1/OU2 = C1w,B2y,A2z,A1x (REV-A "Z" THRU "A" puts C<B<A; numeric K2 DESCENDING algebraic), OP = R7r,Q5q — the spec-derived order. Edges noted, not defects of this row: (1) END-SORT is not an ISO word; its acceptance is the documented nonstandard extension D-RW1 (docs/CONFORMANCE.md, PB655) — but no §4.2.10 3) warning mechanism flags its use (cite.py --check 4.2.10 "An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism" OK), a compiler-wide gap not specific to SORT; (2) the sortCollatingPhrase grammar comment and DiagnosticDescriptors CBL3617/3618 claim COLLATING is REQUIRED (leniency L5) — the measured figure note says it is NOT underlined, so COLLATING? is correct and the comment is the error (CBL3617/3618 are wired nowhere in Cobol.Net.*, which is therefore right). No spec-derived golden exercises the whole format (pb704_sort_duplicates_in_order covers only the DUPLICATES phrase), so test-ref is left empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The general format admits Format 2 with any table data-name-2 that has an OCCURS clause, and Format 1 USING/GIVING of any FD file. Two legal operand shapes do not compile to working code. (1) SortBindTable returns BoundUnsupported for a table inside a REDEFINES (SortBinder.cs, 'SORT of table ... inside a REDEFINES class ... deferred'). The source compiles with warning COBOLNET1756 and aborts at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException. SortArrayPath also defers a data-name-2 nested under another OCCURS (the SR13 half). (2) SortMapIoFiles refuses every relative or indexed USING/GIVING file ('sequential slice'), which rejects legal Format-1 source (owned by PB994 under SR12). The syntax surface itself checks out: phrase order is enforced (COLLATING before DUPLICATES gives COBOL0307), a Format-1 KEY with no data-name is rejected, Format 2 is gated below 2002 (COBOLNET0870), FOR forms are gated at 85 (COBOLNET0872), DUPLICATES is accepted at 85, and a Format-2 SORT with no key phrase uses the table's OCCURS KEY. But one verified half plus one staged-loud half makes this PARTIAL. [editions as adjudicated: Format 1: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023. Format 2 (table) and the national collating surface (alphabet-name-2 / FOR ALPHANUMERIC / FOR NATIONAL): 2002, 2014, 2023 (ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introductions; 2023 Annex E records no SORT format change).]

subject: STRING statement
notes: General format: STRING {{identifier-1|literal-1}... [DELIMITED BY {identifier-2|literal-2|SIZE}]}... INTO identifier-3 [WITH POINTER identifier-4] [choice-indicator ON OVERFLOW / NOT ON OVERFLOW] [END-STRING]. Grammar: stringStatement : STRING stringSendingPhrase+ stringIntoPhrase stringWithPointer? stringOnOverflow? END_STRING?; stringSendingPhrase : strUnstrOperand delimitedByPhrase?; delimitedByPhrase : DELIMITED BY? (ALL)? (strUnstrOperand|SIZE) (the non-ISO ALL token is parsed only to be rejected at bind under SR2 - verified: sr2b.cob 'DELIMITED BY ALL SPACE' -> COBOLNET1757); stringOnOverflow carries both orders of the choice-indicator pair (5.2.6.4). Underlined/optional words verified by probe gr2.cob ('DELIMITED SIZE' with BY omitted, 'NOT OVERFLOW' with ON omitted, 'DELIMITED BY SPACES') -> C[ABX.......] NOV. identifier-1 admits a function-identifier (§8.4.3.1.2 Format 1) via strUnstrSender; INTO/POINTER are dataReference only (receivers). phrase_order_overflow golden pins the reversed NOT/ON order with DELIMITED BY SIZE runs. SR9 (omission only before INTO) is structurally unviolable by this grammar: any phraseless run merges into the next run. Edition note: whether COBOL-85 already allowed the DELIMITED phrase to be omitted is NOT derivable in-repo (see dossier_gaps); the binder applies it at every edition. [editions as adjudicated: 2023 text (ISO/IEC 1989:2023 §14.9.43); Annex E lists no STRING change 2014->2023; the earlier-edition edge is not derivable in-repo (no 2002/2014 text)]

subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: All three printed formats implemented and measured. PRINTED PAGE RENDERED (licensed PDF p.762, ISO/IEC 1989:2023) and matched against specs/ISO_COBOL.md line-for-line: F1 `SUBTRACT {identifier-1|literal-1}... FROM {identifier-2 [rounded-phrase]}...`; F2 adds `FROM {identifier-2|literal-2}` + `GIVING {identifier-3 [rounded-phrase]}...`; F3 `{CORRESPONDING|CORR} identifier-4 FROM identifier-5 [rounded-phrase]`; each with the bracketed CHOICE-INDICATOR size-error group and `[END-SUBTRACT]`. Underlining measured off the render: ON is NOT underlined in either size-error line (optional word) and the grammar has `ON?` in both arms (CobolParserCore.g4:840,842). MEASURED (probe dir probe/subtract): p1 F1 multi-operand + multi-receiver + per-receiver ROUNDED; p2/g6 F2 with literal-2 and with several GIVING receivers each carrying its own ROUNDED; p3/p4/m3 F3 with both CORR and CORRESPONDING, ROUNDED after identifier-5, both size-error branches, END-SUBTRACT; g7 the REVERSED phrase order (5.2.6.4 choice indicators - zero or more, each at most once, any order); h5 END-SUBTRACT as a scope terminator inside IF; h1 the FROM sender as a data reference; g9/g10 a function-identifier in both sending positions (8.4.3.1.2 makes it an identifier). The format-mixing violations the union grammar admits are narrowed back at bind and REJECTED AT COMPILE TIME with COBOLNET1689: two FROM operands under GIVING (g1), ROUNDED on the F2 sending operand (g2), operands with no FROM (g3), a literal receiver in F1 (g4), GIVING with no FROM (g5), a function-identifier F1 receiver (g11). Verified at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (h2); ROUNDED MODE IS gates 2014+ (h3, COBOLNET0803 - 14.7.4's row, not this one). Additional spec-derived goldens touching this row: conformance:85/optional_on_size_error (ON omittable, SUBTRACT leg), conformance:2023/pb134_giving_sending_operands (F2 one sending literal), conformance:2023/pb45_function_in_sending_operands (F2 function sender). DEFECT ATTACHED (does not change the verdict - it is comment text, not behaviour): the grammar's own section banner for SUBTRACT cites the WRONG clause and UNSTRING's banner claims SUBTRACT's - see finding subtract-clause-citation-drift.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:897 subtractStatement; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:902-923 subtractOperandList/subtractOperand/subtractFromPhrase/subtractFromOperand/subtractGivingPhrase; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:809-817 receivingArithmeticOperand/roundedPhrase; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:839-844 arithmeticOnSizeError; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/ArithmeticBinder.cs:71-99 BindSubtract; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/ArithmeticBinder.cs:215-236 Format2SendingOperand/Format1Receivers; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/CorrespondingBinder.cs:33-37 BindSubtractCorresponding

subject: UNLOCK statement
notes: kb/Work PB236 (landed). SHAPE: unchanged and correct -- `UNLOCK file-name-1 [ RECORD | RECORDS ]` with only UNLOCK underlined, rendered from the printed page (scripts/render-spec-page.py 798) and matched exactly by `unlockStatement : UNLOCK fileName (RECORD | RECORDS)? ;`; RECORD/RECORDS are optional words carrying no semantics (5.2.3), the whole bracketed group is omissible (5.2.6.2), and all three spellings were measured behaviourally identical. Edition identity: recognition-gated at COBOL-2002 (COBOLNET0900 at --std 85). THE OPERAND HALF -- THE ONE REASON THIS ROW WAS PARTIAL -- IS NOW ENFORCED. The format writes file-name-1 and cite.py --check 8.4.2.1 'In order to use a resource, a statement shall contain a reference that uniquely identifies that resource.' -> OK; `UNLOCK NOSUCH.` used to compile clean (exit 0, zero diagnostics) and abort at run time with 'a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented ... UNLOCK of undeclared file'. The finding said the mechanism was shared with six sibling binder sites and the fix was one dispatch change rather than seven -- and that is what landed: StatementValidation.ResolveFile is the ONE file-name resolution step for a statement operand, reporting the EXISTING undefined-reference descriptor COBOLNET1639, and the seven sites now have no BoundUnsupported arm at all. Measured: `error COBOLNET1639: 'NOSUCH' is not defined as a file -- UNLOCK names file-name-1 in its general format ...`. The witness deliberately puts the UNLOCK on a path the flow GO TOs past, because that is the shape on which the defect was worst: the run-time loud never fired either, so illegal source compiled AND ran to normal completion. Witness: conformance:negative/pb236-unlock-undeclared-file-unreached.

subject: UNSTRING statement
notes: kb/Work PB1183 (registrar 14c). Format: `UNSTRING identifier-1 [DELIMITED BY [ALL] {identifier-2|literal-1} [OR [ALL] {identifier-3|literal-2}]...] INTO {identifier-4 [DELIMITER IN identifier-5] [COUNT IN identifier-6]}... [WITH POINTER identifier-7] [TALLYING IN identifier-8] [choice-indicator bracket: ON OVERFLOW / NOT ON OVERFLOW] [END-UNSTRING]`. Verified CONFORMING: BY/IN/WITH/ON optional words (probe ufmtnoby.cob `DELIMITED "," OR "5"` runs A=AB B=CD C=EF); ON/NOT ON OVERFLOW in reversed order accepted and correct (ufmtrev.cob prints OVF); POINTER/TALLYING fixed order enforced (ufmtptrtal.cob TALLYING-before-POINTER -> COBOL0307); literal sender refused (ufmtlitsnd.cob -> COBOL0308, strUnstrSender admits identifiers only); function-identifier sender admitted per §8.4.3.1.2. DIVERGES: the grammar writes `unstringIntoPhrase+` with `unstringIntoPhrase : INTO unstringIntoTarget+`, so the INTO KEYWORD may repeat — `UNSTRING S DELIMITED BY "," INTO A INTO B` (probe ufmtinto2.cob) compiles clean at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and runs A=[AB  ] B=[CD5E], where the general format has exactly one INTO followed by a repeated {identifier-4 ...} group. Under-rejects illegal source. The legacy test tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Unit/Overlenient/M417_OverlenientUnstringTests.cs is an empty-body [Fact] set (kb/Work PB387 owns that). The `DELIMITED BY ALL ALL ","` acceptance is SR1's defect (literal-1 is an ALL figurative), recorded on SR-14.9.48.3-1. cite.py --check 14.9.48.3 (SR1/SR4/SR8/SR9) OK; the FMT itself is the rendered <pre> of §14.9.48.2. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the format is unchanged in shape; national operands 2002+)]

subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB332 (divergence 1) and PB365 (divergence 2), both LANDED. Divergence 1: AFTER and PROCEDURE were REQUIRED where 14.9.49.2 prints them un-underlined, so 5.2.3 / 8.3.2.4.3 make them optional words; PB332 relaxed them after measuring the printed figure. Divergence 2: Format 4's second brace group prints {object-class-name-1 | interface-name-1} and DeclBindUse resolved only the class arm, so half the format's operand alternatives were unreachable; PB365 landed the interface alternative (SR17) and the two-pass GR14 selector behind it. All four formats now parse and bind as printed. Format 2's operand also stopped being spelled `procedureName` in the grammar: identifier-1 references a report GROUP, so it is the shared `reportGroupReference` rule (`cobolWord ((IN|OF) reportName)?` per 8.4.2.2.2 Format 1's file-report-qualifier), which is also GENERATE's operand -- that is what lets ONE funnel own the qualified spelling and the 8.4.2.2 uniqueness rule for both.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB1189 (registrar 14c). Format 1 prints ADVANCING as `{identifier-2 | integer-1} [LINE | LINES]` OR `{mnemonic-name-1 | PAGE}` - LINE/LINES belong ONLY to the count alternative. The grammar writes `(dataReference | integerLiteral | literal) (LINE | LINES)?`, and a mnemonic-name parses as dataReference, so `WRITE R AFTER ADVANCING TOP-OF-FORM LINES` and `WRITE R BEFORE TOP-OF-FORM LINE` compile clean (probe probe/write-statement-p1/ws1mnlines.cob, ws2mnl.cob rc=0); BindAdvancing takes the mnemonic arm and silently ignores the trailing LINE(S). `AFTER ADVANCING PAGE LINES` IS rejected (ws5pgl COBOL0307) - the two non-count alternatives are treated differently. Everything else verified: EOP / NOT EOP both orders and both spellings, AT optional (ws1eop runs); INVALID KEY both orders in grammar; WITH optional on LOCK/NO LOCK, the two lock alternatives mutually exclusive (ws1lock2 COBOL0307); FROM must precede ADVANCING (ws1order COBOL0307); `BEFORE BEFORE` rejected (ws5dup); the BEFORE+AFTER pair rejected at 2014 (COBOLNET0900) and accepted at 2023 (ws1pair); retry-phrase and lock phrase rejected at 85 (ws5lk, ws5rt COBOLNET0900) and accepted in format order at 2023 (ws5rt23). Choice-indicator reading per §5.2.6.4 (cite.py --check 5.2.6.4 'The alternatives may be specified in any order.' OK); §E.3.3 item 2 --check OK; §14.9.51.2 'where retry-phrase is described in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase' --check OK. The FILE file-name-1 alternative is Annex A.4.13, declined (COBOLNET1706, PB282 landed). Format selection by organization is SR2/SR3 (part 2/3). Expected from spec: `mnemonic-name-1 LINES` is outside Format 1 and shall be rejected. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 for the base format; the BEFORE+AFTER word pair is 2023-only (§E.3.3 item 2, 'Both BEFORE and AFTER are allowed together in WRITE ADVANCING'); the retry-phrase and WITH [NO] LOCK bracket are post-1985 (edition of introduction not derivable from the 2023 text; the code gates them at 2002)]

subject: ASIN function
notes: FUNCTION ASIN(1)/(-1)/(0.5) in the printed format. The rule-derived pins are +/-1570796326, from S15.10.4 r1's CLOSED but IRRATIONAL pi/2 bound; the ASIN(0.5) line is the S15.4.1 implementor-quantization contrast, not a rule value.

subject: ATAN function
notes: FUNCTION ATAN(1000000000000000000) in the printed format, the value strictly below S15.11.4 r1's OPEN pi/2 bound, hence floor((pi/2)*10^9). pi/2 is not representable at scale 9, so the open-vs-closed distinction is not observable in this line.

subject: BASECONVERT function
notes: UPHELD after INDEPENDENT re-verification rather than by accepting the prior report. PRINTED PAGE RE-RENDERED AND READ (python scripts/render-spec-page.py 851 = printed folio 821): the format is 'FUNCTION BASECONVERT ( argument-1 argument-2 argument-3 )' with separate underline rules under FUNCTION and under BASECONVERT and none under the parentheses or the arguments -- exactly three arguments, no brackets, no braces, no choice indicators, no ellipsis, so nothing is optional and nothing is repeatable. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:30184 now carries the matching <u>FUNCTION</u> <u>BASECONVERT</u> markup, so the transcription is faithful and the earlier reconciliation defect is repaired. subject: BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER function
notes:
ADVERSARIAL PASS 2 - I tried to overturn this and could not; the CONFORMS is upheld on evidence I generated myself, not on the prior report. SCOPE OF THE CLAIM (stated so this row cannot be misread as 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER is done'): per scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py, an FMT row is 'the unit of verify this diagram against the grammar rule that implements it' - it is the SYNTAX question only. The SEMANTICS of this function DIVERGE; see RV-15.13.4-1, which is DIVERGES on three independent sites.

(a) TRANSCRIPTION - I did not take the prior report's word for it. I extracted the PDF text layer independently (specs-private/ISO+IEC+1989-2023..., 0-based page 851 = printed folio 822) AND RENDERED THE PAGE IMAGE at 300 dpi (scripts/render-spec-page.py 852) because the standing rule is that OCR'd DIAGRAMS were systematically lossy toward falsely-restrictive syntax. The rendered diagram reads 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER ( argument-1  argument-2 )' with FUNCTION and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER UNDERLINED and nothing else underlined, NO brackets, NO braces, NO ellipsis, one Format only. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30217 is faithful. §15.13.2 validated with scripts/spec/cite.py --check.

(b) ACCEPTANCE - every case below re-run by ME on src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe at --std 2023, all yielding 00000101: space-only '(5 8)'; comma '(5, 8)'; semicolon '(5; 8)'; spaces inside the parens '( 5 8 )'; identifier arguments '(IV LN)'; arithmetic-expression argument '(IV - 0, LN)'; SUBSCRIPTED argument '(E(2), 8)'; nested function argument '(FUNCTION INTEGER(5.2), 8)'; and the two forms the prior report did NOT test, which were my best shot at breaking it - SPACE-SEPARATED PARENTHESIZED arguments '((2 + 3) (4 * 2))' and a data-name-headed expression followed by a space-separated parenthesized argument '(N + 0 (4 + 4))', both of which stress the FNARG_SEPARATOR / SUBSCRIPT-mode boundary described in the CobolExpressions.g4 comment. Both accept correctly. Also verified: a USER DATA ITEM NAMED 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER' coexists with 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8)' in the same program and both resolve correctly (the intrinsic-function-name is not wrongly reserved); the format binds in a STRING sending position; and the §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 FUNCTION-omitted form under 'REPOSITORY. FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER INTRINSIC.' works.

(c) REJECTION (the diagram's other half - no bracket means no other arity is legal): 0, 1 and 3 arguments and the bare no-parenthesis form all reject with COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER takes 2 argument(s); n given (ISO 15.3)', emitted in IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore off the IntrinsicCatalog Fixed(2,2) row; OMITTED in an argument position rejects with COBOLNET1544 (§8.4.3.2 SR7). All four re-run by me.

(d) EDITIONS - NOT taken from the IntrinsicCatalog row (I verified that independently of the code). Annex E of the 2023 standard is the SUBSTANTIVE CHANGES list 'between the previous COBOL standard and this Working Draft' (i.e. 2014 -> 2023) and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER appears nowhere in it - its only post-Annex-E occurrence in specs/ISO_COBOL.md is the Index entry - so 2014 and 2023 are identical. The 85 exclusion is EXTERNAL knowledge, honestly flagged: the 2023 text carries no introduction-edition statement, and the COBOL-85 + 1989 intrinsic-function amendment set of 42 functions contains no boolean function (boolean/bit data - PICTURE 1, USAGE BIT, B"..." literals - is a COBOL-2002 addition, and §15.13.1 makes this function's type boolean).

(e) test-needed (partial). tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_boolean_conv.cob exists on disk, is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json AND in tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/ConformanceTests.cs, and is spec-derived (expected values hand-derived from §15.13.4 r1 and the Annex D.10 544 -> low-6-bits example - not a characterization/nist/legacy asset); I re-ran it through the CLI and it reproduces its golden exactly. It covers the format POSITIVELY and only in the comma-separated style. The SPACE-separated form as actually printed in the diagram, and the whole wrong-arity/OMITTED rejection half, appear in NO test asset (COBOLNET1504 and COBOLNET1544 are in no test) - those halves rest on my manual CLI runs above.

(f) CHECKED AND CORRECTLY OUT OF SCOPE (I re-tested the prior report's two dismissals rather than accepting them). (i) 'MOVE BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) TO B8' with NO REPOSITORY entry compiles silently and dies at run time with an UNHANDLED NotImplementedCobolFeatureException instead of a bind-time 'undefined data item'. This is NOT a §15.13.2 leniency: I ran the control 'MOVE ZZ-UNDEFINED-THING(5, 8) TO B8' and 'MOVE UPPER-CASE("abc") TO B8' and BOTH are equally undiagnosed, so the missing diagnostic is the generic undefined-subscripted-reference gap, not this function's. (ii) Reference modification of a function-identifier is a parse error for UPPER-CASE too, so it is a §8.4.3.1.2 / §8.4.3.2 diagram gap, i.e. a different FMT row.

subject: MAX function
notes: VERDICT UPHELD after an independent attack on each of the format's three obligations. `FUNCTION MAX ( { argument-1 } … )`: both words underlined (required), parentheses required, braces-plus-ellipsis = one or more with no upper bound. (1) REQUIRED WORDS AND PARENTHESES - the grammar deliberately parses the parenthesized list as a SUPERSET, `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` (read at source, both symbols exist), and the omission is caught at bind with a COBOL diagnostic rather than a parse error, which is a conforming rejection either way. (2) THE ELLIPSIS IS GENUINELY UNBOUNDED - the original record asserted 'Variadic, 1, inf' from the row; re-derived at source, the row is `Add(new("MAX", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "p", "MaxScaled", ...))` and `const int inf = int.MaxValue;` (IntrinsicCatalog.cs), so no hidden ceiling truncates the ellipsis. (3) THE ARGUMENT SEPARATOR - `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` admits the §8.3.5 comma separator and bare juxtaposition alike. No optional phrase words exist in this format, so there is no unverified half. NOTE ON SCOPE: the FUNCTION-keyword-omitted form is §8.4.3.2's grant, not this format's - §15.59.2 underlines FUNCTION as required - so it is out of scope here and is not what this CONFORMS rests on. subject: MIN function
notes: REFUTER RE-EXAMINED AND SUSTAINED — the one row that survived attack, and the format DIAGRAM was rendered from the PDF rather than trusted from the transcription (CLAUDE.md rule 1: a general format is a load-bearing diagram). Printed folio 888 / PDF page 918 renders as `FUNCTION MIN ( { argument-1 } … )` with FUNCTION and MIN both UNDERLINED and nothing bracketed — exactly what specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.63.2 carries, so the transcription is faithful and no falsely-restrictive OCR residue is in play here. The grammar rule `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` is a deliberate SUPERSET — the parenthesised group is optional there and the per-function arity is the binder's job. For MIN the catalog row is Variadic with a minimum of 1 (`Add(new("MIN", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "p", "MinScaled", ...))`) and the binder enforces it, so the composite behaviour matches the printed format: FUNCTION required, MIN required, the parenthesised list required, at least one argument required, repetition unbounded. The repeat-brace `…` also picks up §15.3's ALL-subscript expansion, which works. ⚠ RESIDUE (unchanged, and it is a corpus gap not a conformance defect): no spec-derived test pins the two REJECTION shapes (bare `FUNCTION MIN`, empty `FUNCTION MIN()`) — test-ref is deliberately left EMPTY rather than closed on the differential. ⚠ SCOPE NOTE the refuter adds: §15.63.1's TYPE TABLE (Index ⇒ Index, All arguments integer ⇒ Integer) is visible on the same rendered page and is NOT covered by any rule in this batch — the catalog hardcodes IntrinsicType.Numeric and the binder only ever re-derives Alphanumeric/National. Whether the Integer and Index rows of that table are honoured is an UNADJUDICATED row, and it should be added to the inventory rather than assumed closed by this FMT verdict. Two attack lines the adjudicator did not run, both of which the format rule actually reaches, come out clean. (1) THE FUNCTION-KEYWORD-OMITTED FORM. §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 and §12.3.8 SR13 make `FUNCTION` omissible for any intrinsic the REPOSITORY declares, and §15.65 carries no rule requiring the keyword — this is the exact shape of the landed PB7/PB9 defects, and MODULE-NAME is not covered by either (it is not a §8.9 reserved name and it is not zero-argument, so it takes the D2 dataReference re-route in KeywordOmittedFunction). It works, including for the reserved-word argument NESTED, under both `FUNCTION MODULE-NAME INTRINSIC` and `FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC`. (2) RESULT REFERENCE MODIFICATION (§8.4.3.3.3 SR2) and lower-case keywords both work. Residual, recorded but not verdict-changing: NEITHER cited test exercises the rule's own content — the arity bound (zero / two / non-keyword arguments) and the NESTED and STACK keywords are pinned by no test at all, so the structural enforcement I verified by hand is undefended against drift. subject: NUMVAL function
notes: CONFORMS SUSTAINED -- and, unlike the adjudication, it now survives the boundaries it had merely asserted. The general format has no optional or repeated element: FUNCTION and NUMVAL are both underlined (required) and there is exactly one parenthesized argument; the catalog row declares `IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1` and BindIntrinsicCore enforces it with COBOLNET1504 in BOTH directions. Three additional attacks were run and all failed to overturn it. (i) PB7's pattern -- a form that compiles and dies at run time: the FUNCTION-keyword-omitted form under `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.` compiles AND RUNS correctly, so the omission license does not strand NUMVAL. (ii) Over-reservation: an intrinsic-function-name is not a reserved word unless the REPOSITORY declares it, and `01 NUMVAL PIC X(6)` is accepted alongside `FUNCTION NUMVAL(NUMVAL)` -- the lexer token does not leak into the user-defined-word space, so no legal source is rejected. (iii) The format has no reference-modification slot and NUMVAL is a numeric function; `FUNCTION NUMVAL("123.45")(1:2)` is rejected with COBOLNET1629 citing §8.4.3.3.3 SR2. test-ref left EMPTY deliberately: no spec-derived test pins the arity diagnostic or the general format, and CONFORMS-but-untested is the honest state. EDITIONS EMPTY: see AR-15.67.3-3's note -- the adjudication's '2014, 2023' was inferred from an Annex E absence and implies a false unavailability before 2014; IntrinsicCatalog's own `85` may not be used as the source. EVIDENCE: Probe pbnv09.cob: `FUNCTION NUMVAL(A1, A1)` -> `error COBOLNET1504: FUNCTION NUMVAL takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (ISO §15.3)`. Probe pbnv17.cob: `FUNCTION NUMVAL` with no argument list -> the same COBOLNET1504 with '0 given'. Probe E:/Temp/rfnv/rfnv04.cob (RFNVW04, --std 2023) with `REPOSITORY. FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC.`: CTRL `FUNCTION NUMVAL("12.5")` = +12.500000 and OMIT `COMPUTE R = NUMVAL("34.25")` = 00000003425000{ (=+34.250000), then REACHED-END. subject: REVERSE function
notes:
Printed folio 908 (PDF page 938) re-rendered and read independently: the format is `FUNCTION REVERSE ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and REVERSE both UNDERLINED (required), one unbracketed required operand, no optional phrase. Grammar: functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? ; REVERSE is NOT a lexer token (only REVERSE_VIDEO and REVERSED are - grep-verified over Grammar/) so it arrives as IDENTIFIER through functionName. The catalog row is Fixed 1..1 and the arity gate was re-run live against the built CLI: `FUNCTION REVERSE` (no parens) -> COBOLNET1504 '1 argument(s); 0 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE()` -> COBOLNET1504 '0 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE(W-A W-B)` -> COBOLNET1504 '2 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE(OMITTED)` -> COBOLNET1544 (8.4.3.2.3 SR7, cite-checked). The parens being syntactically optional in the grammar is harmless: the shape is still REJECTED, at bind time rather than parse time. ⚠ TRANSCRIPTION DEFECT (the prior draft asserted 'the transcription is faithful' - that claim is WITHDRAWN as false): specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.78.2 renders the general format as BARE MARKDOWN TEXT, with no

The required-word underlining the printed page shows is therefore LOST in the transcription. The verdict is unaffected - this format has no optional element, so nothing required-vs-optional turns on the underlining, and the compiler requires both words - but the defect is real and propagating: the Phase-B extractor's rule text for FMT-15.78.2 swallowed the trailing `` anchor precisely BECAUSE there is no 
 block to bound it. Repair 15.78.2 to the 
/ form of its neighbours. ⚠ Test coverage is POSITIVE-ONLY: both test-refs write the correct one-argument format (StringFamily_PinnedToSpec has an InlineData `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE("abc 12") TO T.`; IF134A carries 109 REVERSE references, e.g. `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE("figure") TO WS-ANUM.`), so acceptance is pinned, but NO test pins the four rejection shapes above - they were verified by hand. subject: SIGN function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py OK on §15.81.2 '( argument-1 )' — the general format is the one-line 'FUNCTION SIGN ( argument-1 )' with both words required and no optional bracket, so the historically lossy-diagram risk does not arise. Grammar: functionCall alt 1 'FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*' with SIGN listed in functionName (SIGN lexes as a reserved token and must be admitted explicitly); the parse is a deliberate superset (argument group optional) and BindIntrinsicCore enforces the exact arity from the catalog row (Fixed 1..1) with COBOLNET1504, so FUNCTION SIGN with zero or two arguments is rejected at bind with the §15.3 citation. The §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 keyword-omitted form (cite.py OK: 'the word FUNCTION may be omitted') is carried by the separate reservedIntrinsicArgFn alternative (PB9, kb/Work/PB9.md status landed) whose argument group is structurally REQUIRED — derived from §15.81.2 itself, which has no no-argument form — keeping the SIGN clause (§13.18.53) collision impossible; that form belongs to §8.4.3.2.3, not to this FMT rule, but the golden asserts both forms yield the same value. §8.4.3.2 SR6 paren discipline is honored via FNARG_LPAREN retyping (PB48). subject: SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.83.2 'FUNCTION</u> <u>SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC' -> OK (General format). The format is FUNCTION SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC ( argument-1 ) -- both words underlined and required, one required argument, no optional, alternative or repeating part, so there is nothing bracketed to accept and nothing repeated to count. FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*' -- carries the shape generically, with the 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 argument-list parens retyped by the lexer so a parenthesised argument is never read as a subscript or a grouping paren. subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. The general format, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33307-33309, is `FUNCTION SQRT ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and SQRT both UNDERLINED — required words — and exactly one argument inside required parentheses; there is no optional phrase, no ellipsis, and no second format. READ, GRAMMAR: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 line 333 — `: FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` — so the FUNCTION keyword and the name are both required at this production, and the argument list's '(' is lexed in the dedicated FNARG mode so §8.4.3.2 SR6 ('that ( is ALWAYS the argument list') holds rather than the '(' being read as a subscript or a grouping paren. The optionality of the paren group in the grammar is deliberate (it serves the zero-argument functions) and does NOT leak into SQRT: the arity is the CATALOG's. READ, ARITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 133 — Add(new("SQRT", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "n", "Sqrt", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1, enforced at IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore lines 572-579: `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` -> COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION SQRT takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)'. So a bare `FUNCTION SQRT` (given 0) and `FUNCTION SQRT(A B)` (given 2) are both rejected with the §15.3 citation. The FUNCTION-omitted spelling (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2, a REPOSITORY INTRINSIC declaration) is gated the same way — IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 301 and 339 both refuse to route a name written without an argument list unless sig.MinArgs == 0, which SQRT's is not. The row's IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.84.1's 'The type of this function is numeric'. GOLDEN: conformance:2023/pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage writes the format both ways argument-1 can be spelled (a data item, `FUNCTION SQRT(NI)`, and a literal, `FUNCTION SQRT(4)`), each pinned to 2.00 in the .out. NOT COVERED: there is no SQRT-specific arity negative fixture; the COBOLNET1504 guard is catalog-driven and generic, so a SQRT-specific one could only re-test the shared guard. EDITIONS: the format is unchanged across the four editions (SQRT is a 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment function); batch default.

subject: STANDARD-COMPARE function
notes: kb/Work PB101 T7 (2026-08-18): FUNCTION STANDARD-COMPARE ( argument-1 argument-2 [ ordering-name-1 ] [ argument-4 ] ) — the bespoke binder takes the two operands, then a bare ordering-name and/or an integer level in either order the format admits; ArgKinds ssoi ('o' = §15.3 argument type 12). Below 2002 the function is COBOLNET1502 (standard-compare-2002).

subject: STANDARD-DEVIATION function
notes: Format read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.86.2: `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and STANDARD-DEVIATION underlined (required keywords), the parenthesised list NOT bracketed (required), and the brace-ellipsis making argument-1 one-or-more. Both halves of the format located and read. HALF 1, the keyword/name/paren shape: the grammar carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION production (grep of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend for the name returns nothing) because the form is generic — CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall is `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and CobolExpressions.g4#functionName admits IDENTIFIER. Checked the lexer for the hyphen hazard, since CobolLexer.g4 does carry STANDARD (:536), STANDARD_BINARY/STANDARD_DECIMAL (:264-265) and STANDARD_1/STANDARD_2 (:669-670) but no STANDARD_DEVIATION token: ANTLR maximal munch gives IDENTIFIER the full 18-character 'STANDARD-DEVIATION' over STANDARD's 8, which is the documented behavior at CobolLexer.g4:261-262 ('a bare STANDARD still lexes as STANDARD, and WC-COBOL still lexes as one IDENTIFIER'). The argument-list paren is retyped FNARG_LPAREN per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6, so the list is never read as a grouping or subscript paren. HALF 2, the one-or-more arity: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build:139 declares Add(new("STANDARD-DEVIATION", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "StandardDeviation", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue, matching `{ argument-1 } …` exactly; IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579 computes `given` and raises COBOLNET1504 'takes at least 1 argument(s)' when given < MinArgs, which catches both the bare `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION` and the empty-parens `()` form the grammar's optional group admits. IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.86.1 ('The type of this function is numeric'). Closing test: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 45 writes the format `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION(2, 2, 2)`, it is registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:123, and tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.out line 8 pins SD=0.0 — so the format demonstrably lexes, parses and binds. The fixture is spec-derived (its header derives every line from §15.4.1 r1 and the functions' own EAEs), not a characterization or legacy-match. Editions: Annex E (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42847 onward) carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION entry and the clause has no edition-varying content, so the batch default stands; the editions field was NOT read off IntrinsicCatalog's own IntroducedIn column.

subject: SUBSTITUTE function
notes: kb/Work PB81 (2026-08-18): FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ANYCASE] [FIRST | LAST] argument-2 argument-3 } … ) — the pair repeats, so §15.3's table(ALL) is admissible among the pairs and its elements form the pairs by position at run time (the FLAT form: CobolIntrinsics.SubstituteFlat pairs the enumerated elements; a keyword before an enumeration attaches to the pair its first element opens). Written pairs pair at bind as before (SubstituteModes per pair). The ALL argument was the staged COBOLNET0899 (`substitute-all-subscript-argument`, retired).

subject: SUM function
notes:
Format read directly from specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.88.2 (line 33495-33499): `FUNCTION SUM ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and SUM underlined (required), the argument-list parentheses present, and the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis, i.e. ONE OR MORE. Both halves READ and verified. (1) THE REFERENCE SHAPE: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, with SUM present in CobolExpressions.g4#functionName (line 458) — needed because SUM is one of the §8.9 reserved words that is also a §8.11 intrinsic name. The keyword-omitted twin `SUM(…)` rides CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn (`SIGN | SUM`), and IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsic lines 54-63 enforces §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 on it (COBOLNET1543 unless REPOSITORY declares SUM / FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC) — so the abbreviated form is not accepted unconditionally. Arguments juxtapose or take the §8.3.5 separator via functionArgList. §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is decided from the DEFINITION before binding (DefinitionPermitsArguments("SUM") is true since MaxArgs > 0), so `FUNCTION SUM (1:4)` draws Sr6ArgumentListError, not a bogus arity error; §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 rejects reference-modifying SUM's numeric result (ResultRefMod, COBOLNET1629). (2) THE 1..n MULTIPLICITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 152 `Add(new("SUM", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "SumScaled", …))` — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue; IntrinsicBinder.cs line 573 raises COBOLNET1504 ("takes at least 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)") for `FUNCTION SUM` written with no list or an empty one, and the unbounded max means no upper rejection. The ellipsis also licenses the §15.3 table(ALL) argument: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (MaxArgs == int.MaxValue) gates TryBindAllArgument, and its own diagnostic text names SUM as an example of a `{ argument } …` format. TESTS: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.cs re-reads §15.88.2's `<pre>` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md and asserts the catalog's unboundedness EQUALS the presence of the '…' character — spec-derived in the strict sense (the assertion's oracle is the standard's own text, not a hand list). tests/conformance/2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges.cob exercises the repeated-argument format over ALL (fixed, ODO, dynamic-capacity, two-level, and a mixed `SUM(F(ALL) WS-E(ALL))`); pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob exercises the plain 3-argument written form. NOT covered by a dedicated fixture: a zero-argument `FUNCTION SUM` negative case — the COBOLNET1504 arm was read in source but has no SUM-specific golden; that is a test gap, not a behavior gap (the arm is shared and exercised by other MinArgs rows).

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): the format was re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33494-33499 and §8.4.3.2.3 re-read whole at :6020ff. SR2 ("If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph … the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required") and SR6 ("If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments") both check out against IntrinsicBinder.cs:57 (COBOLNET1543) and :88 (Sr6ArgumentListError, via DefinitionPermitsArguments reading MaxArgs > 0 from the catalog row). The keyword-omitted alternative `reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart*` (CobolExpressions.g4:334-346) REQUIRES the subscript group, so a bare `SUM` can never be read as a function reference — which is correct precisely because §15.88.2 has no zero-argument form, and is what keeps the report-writer `SUM OF` clause and the `SIGN` data-description clause from being swallowed. The drift test was read in full and is genuinely spec-derived: it re-scans every `#### 15.x.2 General format` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, keys on the '…' character, asserts a ≥79-row floor on BOTH the spec scan and the catalog scan so the scanner cannot silently find nothing, and asserts the equivalence in both directions — it closes the UNBOUNDED half of `{ argument-1 } …`. The at-least-one half rests on reading only (IntrinsicBinder.cs:573, MinArgs 1) with no SUM-specific fixture, which rule 3 expressly permits for CONFORMS. ONE RESIDUE FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED AGAINST THIS ROW: with a runtime-ranged table(ALL) the compile-time count is `all.StaticCount ?? 1` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:572), so an OCCURS DEPENDING object of 0 satisfies MinArgs at compile time and the enumerated list reaches the runtime EMPTY — CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#SumDec would then throw IndexOutOfRangeException on `xs[0]` and CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled would return 0. §15.3 makes exactly that case undefined ("The evaluation of an ALL subscript shall result in at least one argument, otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined"), so it is not a violation of this format rule; it is worth a robustness note elsewhere, not a downgrade here. Verdict held at CONFORMS.

subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
THE FORMAT READ OFF THE PRINTED CLAUSE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.92.2, lines 33665-33668): `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ( argument-1 argument-2)`. FUNCTION and the function-name are UNDERLINED, so both are required key words; the two argument operands are unbracketed and carry no ellipsis, so exactly two arguments, both required, and no repetition (feedback_underlining_not_bracketing — I measured the <u> markup, I did not infer from brackets).

GENERIC HALF — the keyword/name/parenthesised-list shape. Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* | ...` and `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`. The separator rule is what matters for THIS format: it admits BOTH the bare juxtaposition §15.92.2 itself prints and the §8.3.5 comma separator, and the corpus exercises both spellings (below). TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME is not a §8.9 reserved word, so it arrives through the ordinary functionName/cobolWord slot; hyphens are COBOL-word characters, so the name lexes whole.

PER-FUNCTION HALF — the name, the arity and the edition window — is the catalog row at IntrinsicCatalog#Build (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:310): Add(new("TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2, "ss", "TestFormattedDatetime", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2014)). ⚠ I READ THE IntrinsicSig RECORD DECLARATION (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:52-57) to confirm the POSITIONAL meaning of `2, 2` (MinArgs, MaxArgs) and of `2014` (IntroducedIn) instead of counting commas. The grammar's paren group is OPTIONAL, i.e. a superset parse; what actually makes both arguments REQUIRED and forbids a third is BindIntrinsicCore's arity gate — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET1504", ...)` — so a bare `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME` (0 given) and a 3-argument call are both rejected against MinArgs=MaxArgs=2.

RESULT TYPE, since the format's clause head fixes it: §15.92.1 "The type of this function is integer" — the row's IntrinsicType.Integer, and IntrinsicRenderer.cs:334 `case "TestFormattedDatetime": return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DateFn(...), 0)` renders it at SCALE 0, i.e. as an integer.

TESTS: both separator spellings of the printed format are pinned by spec-derived programs. conformance:2023/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form writes `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD" "9999W526")` — the exact space juxtaposition §15.92.2 prints, which is the harder half and is easy to leave untested; conformance:2014/formatted_datetime and the AssertSpec theory write the §8.3.5 comma form. ⚠ NOT TESTED under this function's name: the arity REJECTIONS. The COBOLNET1504 gate is generic and catalog-driven (read at IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579) and is exercised elsewhere (tests/conformance/2023/pb24_length_physical_keyword pins it for FUNCTION LENGTH), but no fixture gives TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME one or three arguments.

EDITIONS from the standard: Annex E (the 2014->2023 change record) carries no occurrence of the name, so the general format is unchanged at 2023; 2014 is the introduction edition the family is gated at, and the landed sibling row AR-15.92.3-2 records the same window. Not derived from the catalog row.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK (§15.93.2 General format), the printed form being FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL ( argument-1 ) — one required argument, no optional phrase, no keyword, no repetition. READ: (1) the grammar, CobolExpressions.g4:332 functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* — functionName is the generic word slot, so TEST-NUMVAL needs no bespoke production and the written form parses; (2) IntrinsicCatalog.Build line 276, Add(new("TEST-NUMVAL", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "TestNumval", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002)) — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1 matches the format's single non-optional argument, and IntrinsicType.Integer matches §15.93.1 (cite.py --check 15.93.1 "The type of this function is integer." -> OK); (3) the arity is ENFORCED, not merely declared — IntrinsicBinder.cs:573 raises COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)" for any other count. TEST-NUMVAL is NOT an OptionalTrailing/Variadic row, so no phrase the format does not print can be written. TEST: conformance:2002/intrinsics_test_validators writes the call in exactly the form §15.93.2 prints, ten times, and asserts the §15.93.4 returned values (N1..N10 in the .out). NOT VERIFIED and named honestly: no negative fixture pins the COBOLNET1504 two-argument rejection for THIS function specifically (siblings do), and the format rule itself states nothing about arity beyond the one printed operand, which the catalog row expresses. EDITIONS: batch default, same derivation limit recorded on AR-15.93.3-1 (the compiler's 2002 window and the test-numval-2002 construct row are code, not the spec).

REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; the ZERO-argument path — rule 5's second famous miss, "every zero-argument intrinsic failing at run time" — probed independently and found closed at COMPILE time, which the adjudicator did not check): I traced all three routes by which a TEST-NUMVAL reference with no argument list can arrive. (a) `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL` bare: fc.functionArgList() is null, ArgsOf yields [], given = 0 < MinArgs = 1, so IntrinsicBinder.cs:573-579 issues COBOLNET1504 and returns BoundExprError — a diagnostic, never a LoudValue that survives to run time. (b) `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL ()`: the grammar's optional functionArgList is absent, same arity error. (c) `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL (1:4)`: intercepted BEFORE the bind by IntrinsicBinder.cs:87 (FNARG_LPAREN null + refModPart present + DefinitionPermitsArguments, which is MaxArgs > 0 = true here), so it draws the §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 message COBOLNET1543, not a misleading "takes 1 argument(s); 0 given" — the PB61 misroute does not reach this function. I also confirmed TEST-NUMVAL is NOT diverted to any bespoke binder (BindNumvalCFamily takes "NUMVAL-C" or "TEST-NUMVAL-C" only, line 557), so the generic arity + class path at 565-581 is the ONE path, and PB12's "bespoke binders return above CheckArgumentClasses" hazard does not apply. Test gap restated unchanged: the two-argument rejection has no fixture for this function; the row stays test-needed on that edge.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL-C function
notes:
PB250 LANDED — the format was already correct (the printed page was re-rendered, scripts/render-spec-page.py 958 = printed folio 928, and all eight legal shapes trace through BindNumvalCFamily's positional walk); the PARTIAL was owed to (a) the >>COBOL-WORDS interaction with this format's two keywords and (b) four missing test shapes. Both are closed.

(a) THE DEFECT AND ITS ROOT CAUSE. ANYCASE and LOCALE are ISO 8.9 RESERVED words (cite.py --check 8.9 OK on both; neither is in the 8.10 table) and 7.3.10.3 SR3 therefore admits both as the EXISTING word of a >>COBOL-WORDS directive. The directive was applied by ONE mechanism only — the post-lex token retype (CobolWordsRewriter), which can reach a word solely when the lexer makes it a keyword TOKEN — and both of these words are deliberately left as bare IDENTIFIERs so the 15.94.2 / 15.68.2 phrase parses as ordinary space-separated arguments. So the directive was ACCEPTED and SILENTLY INERT in both directions: `EQUATE "LOCALE" WITH "LOCALITY"` then `TEST-NUMVAL-C(X LOCALITY FR)` rejected legal source with a COBOLNET1504 arity error naming the renamed keyword (measured), and `UNDEFINE "ANYCASE"` still ate the user's own data item as the keyword, switching on case-insensitive currency matching and injecting the compilation-unit currency with no diagnostic (measured: a wrong TEST-NUMVAL-C answer of 1 where 0 is required by 15.94.4 1)a)).

THE FIX IS THE SECOND MECHANISM, ONCE, FOR THE WHOLE CLASS. CobolWordsMap.Resolve is now the ONE reading of 7.3.10.4 GR2/GR3/GR4 (canonical for an EQUATE/SUBSTITUTE synonym, null for an UNDEFINE'd or SUBSTITUTE'd-away word, the word itself otherwise), and every by-name classifier calls it: IntrinsicBinder.KeywordWordOf — the single funnel through which EVERY section-15 phrase word is read, so TRIM, FIND-STRING, SUBSTITUTE, CONVERT, MODULE-NAME, LENGTH and NUMVAL-C/TEST-NUMVAL-C are all covered by one change — plus the parser's text predicates, the SET-statement locale categories, the ALPHABET coded-set names and CALL ... AS NESTED. CobolWordsRewriter.CanonicalWordOf/TokenIs keep the directive applied to a word EXACTLY once (the retype already re-spells what it reaches). Measured population behind the sweep: of the 552 words in 8.9 union 8.10, 447 were in the token map, 17 are lexed but were invisible to it (a multi-spelling rule publishes no ANTLR literal name) and 88 are no token at all.

TWO SIBLING DEFECTS OF THE SAME MECHANISM, ALSO CLOSED. The token map now resolves multi-spelling keywords by asking the lexer itself, and the de-reserve retype matches the token TEXT so `UNDEFINE "ZERO"` frees ZERO without freeing ZEROS and ZEROES (7.3.10.3 SR3 names one COBOL word). And SR3/SR4's category test could only ask the lexer vocabulary, so it rejected every legal directive naming one of the 31 section-8.10 context-sensitive words this compiler does not tokenize (HEX, CURRENT, LC_ALL, ANUM, BYTE, ACTIVATING, STACK, TOP-LEVEL, UCS-4, UTF-8, UTF-16 and the rest) — a generated 8.10 table now answers it, single-sourced from the spec section and drift-tested against it.

(b) TESTS. The three positive shapes the row owed (argument-1 ANYCASE; argument-1 LOCALE ANYCASE; argument-1 LOCALE locale-name-1 ANYCASE) are 2002/pb250_test_numvalc_remaining_shapes, all three verified 0 per 15.94.4 1)a); the stack-exclusion negative under this function's OWN name is negative/pb250-test-numvalc-locale-and-argument2-are-alternatives (15.94.2 + 5.2.6.2, COBOLNET1504). The >>COBOL-WORDS goldens the row asked for are 2023/pb250_cobol_words_phrase_word_equate (GR2 synonym for ANYCASE) and 2023/pb250_cobol_words_phrase_word_undefine (GR3, the user's data item bound as argument-2), with negative/pb250-cobol-words-undefined-keyword-syntax-withdrawn pinning that the withdrawn syntax is no longer available. All eight shapes of the format now have a fixture or a traced derivation, and nothing in the format binds by a rule stated in more than one place.

THE STALE COMMENT the row recorded (IntrinsicBinder.cs, "The LOCALE phrase is the A.4.9 documented non-support") is corrected in the same change set, as is the neighbouring claim that ANYCASE and LOCALE are 8.10 context-sensitive words — they are 8.9 reserved, and the argument-1 exclusion is positional, not a context-sensitivity allowance. EDITIONS unchanged at 2002,2014,2023.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL-F function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.2 "FUNCTION"` -> OK, printing the format verbatim: `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-NUMVAL-F</u> ( argument-1 )` (General format). The format is FUNCTION + the name + a parenthesized list of EXACTLY ONE argument; nothing is bracketed, so both the argument and its parens are required and no second argument is admitted. CODE READ (not sampled): (1) the reference shape comes from the ONE generic rule `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` in src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 — TEST-NUMVAL-F is not a reserved word (it is not in the four-word §8.9 n §8.11 set SIGN/SUM/LENGTH/RANDOM), so it arrives through `functionName` and the FNARG_LPAREN retyping makes the '(' the argument list per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6; (2) the ARITY is the catalog row's, `Add(new("TEST-NUMVAL-F", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "TestNumvalF", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002))` inside IntrinsicCatalog.Build; (3) it is ENFORCED at IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` raises COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)". I traced both degenerate shapes to that arm rather than assuming them: a BARE `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F` (no parens) reaches `FinishIntrinsic(fc, BindIntrinsicCore(name, ArgsOf(fc.functionArgList())), display)` at IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsic:89 with an EMPTY list (the paren group is optional in the grammar), so given=0 < MinArgs=1 -> COBOLNET1504; a two-argument write gives 2 > MaxArgs=1 -> COBOLNET1504. The MinArgs!=0 guards at IntrinsicBinder:301/339 belong to the KEYWORD-OMITTED (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2) route and cannot swallow the FUNCTION-keyword form. (4) The NAME resolves — the catalog row exists, so COBOLNET1501 ("not an intrinsic function of ISO/IEC 1989") does not fire, and the edition window is applied by IntrinsicBinder:493 (COBOLNET1502 below the introduction edition). TESTS: `tests/conformance/2023/pb60_numval_one_scan.cob` writes `COMPUTE T = FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F("1 2")` and its .out pins `ET=000C` (the overpunched +3), and IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.TestNumvalF_Positions_2014 exercises the same one-argument form four more times through AssertSpec (which compares against a HARDCODED spec-derived expectation, not against the legacy oracle or GnuCOBOL — I read the helper at line 26 to confirm that before citing it). EDITIONS: taken from kb/Work R28 (landed), whose evidence is EXTERNAL to this code — the COBOL Consortium's COBOL2002 introduction names NUMVAL-F/TEST-NUMVAL-F among the functions added by COBOL2002, and both are absent from the WG4 2014-cycle new-function lists; the 2023 text itself cannot settle it (Annex E fixes only the 2014->2023 boundary and §8.11 lists names with no edition data). I did NOT derive the window from IntrinsicCatalog's own row. REFUTED: VERDICT SURVIVES (CONFORMS); one qualifying spec-derived test the adjudicator missed is ADDED to test-ref. I did not accept the adjudicator's trace — the citation was re-derived by me (`cite.py --check 15.95.2 "TEST-NUMVAL-F"` -> OK, §15.95.2 General format, `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-NUMVAL-F</u> ( argument-1 )`) and the row was attacked on four axes. subject: VARIANCE function
notes: Rule text re-derived from specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 33974: `FUNCTION VARIANCE ( { argument-1 } ... )` -- FUNCTION and VARIANCE underlined (required), the parenthesised list not bracketed (required), the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis (one or more, repeatable). Each element located: (1) the surface shape is the shared Frontend rule src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall -- `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` -- with functionArgList = `functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`, so space- and comma/semicolon-separated repeats both parse; VARIANCE is not in reservedIntrinsicArgFn (only SIGN and SUM are) so it takes the generic FUNCTION-keyword arm. (2) The VARIANCE-specific half is the catalog row read at IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 140: Add(new("VARIANCE", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "Variance", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) -- MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue. (3) That bound is ENFORCED, not decorative: IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore lines 572-579 compute `given` (a table(ALL) argument counted as its static element count) and raise COBOLNET1504 "takes at least 1 argument(s)" outside [MinArgs, MaxArgs], so the format's minimum-one is a real rejection. (4) The ellipsis itself is mechanically pinned: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 69) is `MaxArgs == int.MaxValue`, and IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.RepeatsAnArgument_IsExactly_TheFormatsEllipsis READS specs/ISO_COBOL.md, extracts the '#### 15.98.2 General format' block and asserts the catalog row agrees with whether that block contains a literal ellipsis -- a genuinely spec-derived test covering VARIANCE (it iterates every catalogued row, floor >= 79). RepeatsAnArgument is also the ISO 15.3 precondition that admits the ALL subscript, and both render lanes consume the enumerated list as one array (IntrinsicRenderer.cs#ArgArray via DecArgList line 517 and the RenderFloat default arm line 403), so `FUNCTION VARIANCE(TBL(ALL))` is structurally supported. Positive exercise of the written format: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 39, `COMPUTE VA = FUNCTION VARIANCE(1, 2, 3)`, registered enabled in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json line 123. Editions: Annex E (spec lines 42847-44200) carries NO VARIANCE or STANDARD-DEVIATION entry, so there is no edition delta; VARIANCE is in the section 8.11 intrinsic-function-name list (spec line 9710) and is an original Intrinsic Function Module name -- editions left at the batch default, NOT read off the catalog row's IntroducedIn. NOT tested for VARIANCE specifically: the table(ALL) form (pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges does not name VARIANCE) and the zero-argument rejection. || REFUTER (independently re-derived; verdict UPHELD as CONFORMS). Format re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 33974 -- FUNCTION and VARIANCE underlined, list unbracketed, `{ argument-1 } ...`. Grammar confirmed at CobolExpressions.g4 line 333 (functionCall) and lines 351-353 (functionArgList); reservedIntrinsicArgFn at line 343 is SIGN and SUM only, so VARIANCE takes the FUNCTION-keyword arm as claimed. The argument-less shape genuinely reaches the arity gate rather than a zero-argument path: BindIntrinsic line 89 calls BindIntrinsicCore(name, ArgsOf(fc.functionArgList())) and ArgsOf returns [] when the optional paren group is absent, so `FUNCTION VARIANCE` draws COBOLNET1504 -- and the section 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 pre-check at line 87 only diverts a `NAME (start:length)` shape. TWO ATTACKS TRIED AND DEFEATED. (i) Reference modification of a NUMERIC function result -- the general format shows none and the grammar's `refModPart*` admits the tokens -- is rejected: IntrinsicBinder.cs#ResultRefMod lines 180-185 admits only ResultCategory Alphanumeric/National/Boolean and reports COBOLNET1629 citing section 8.4.3.3.3 SR2, so `FUNCTION VARIANCE(1 2 3)(1:2)` is loud. (ii) The grammar's OMITTED alternative inside functionArgument is not a hole in the format: IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 2452-2456 report COBOLNET1544 citing section 8.4.3.2 SR7. The ellipsis's real consequence (the section 15.3 ALL subscript) is generic and driven by sig.RepeatsAnArgument at TryBindAllArgument line 2578, the element enumerates row-major in CobolTable.cs#AllArgs, and the zero-occurrence case that section 15.3 leaves undefined is defined LOUD there (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION + CobolFatalException, lines 130-135) -- so no VARIANCE body can be entered with an empty list today. Editions re-checked independently: a scan of the Annex E range finds no VARIANCE or STANDARD-DEVIATION row, so the batch default stands and agrees with the landed sibling rows FMT-15.62.2 and FMT-15.74.2. TEST: IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.WhenCompiled_CompileTimeConstant_PinnedToSpec (tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs:294-303) is spec-pinned, not a legacy differential - it calls AssertSpec (compile + run under CobolNetCompiler and Assert.Equal on the expected output), never AssertSameAsLegacy - and writes `MOVE FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED TO T` plus `IF FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE >= FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED`, so the keyword form with no argument list is exercised in both a MOVE sending field and a relation-condition operand. subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: cite.py --check 15.100.2 'FUNCTION</u> <u>YEAR-TO-YYYY' OK (General format) - the format is 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY ( argument-1 [ argument-2 [ argument-3 ] ] )', both words underlined hence required, with argument-3 NESTED inside argument-2's brackets. READ: there is no bespoke grammar for this function - CobolExpressions.g4's functionCall carries 'FUNCTION functionName' plus a parenthesised argument list of arithmeticExpressions separated by §8.3.5 separators, and IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 205 supplies the shape: Add(new("YEAR-TO-YYYY", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing, 1, 3, "iii", "YearToYyyy", ...)). IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore line 573 enforces it - 'if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)' => COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY takes 1..3 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)'. The BRACKET NESTING needs no separate rule: the arguments are positional, so 1, 2 or 3 written arguments is exactly the language the nested brackets generate (argument-3 cannot be written without argument-2). Result type Integer matches §15.100.1 'The type of the function is integer'. Every arity is live in code - the 3-argument form is pinned end to end by conformance:2002/intrinsics_date_window (11 hand-derived lines), the 1-argument form by unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_DefaultArg3_IsExecutionYear; only the 2-argument form has no test, and no fixture pins the COBOLNET1504 over- or under-arity rejection for this function. The below-2002 edition gate is pinned by conformance:negative/date_window_below_2002 (COBOLNET1502). NOTE for the reader of AR-15.100.3-5: the 1- and 2-argument forms PARSE and COMPILE correctly on every carrier - the divergence recorded there is in the runtime default, not in this format. REFUTED: REFUTED: verdict UPHELD at CONFORMS - the implementation reading survives independent re-derivation - but ONE EVIDENCE CLAIM IS FALSE AND IS WITHDRAWN. cite.py --check 15.100.2 'YEAR-TO-YYYY' -> OK §15.100.2 (General format), rendering '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>YEAR-TO-YYYY</u> ( argument-1 [ argument-2 [ argument-3 ] ] )'. I verified every arity edge by READING, not by sampling: IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 205 gives IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing with MinArgs 1 / MaxArgs 3; IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore computes 'long given = args.Sum(...)' and rejects 'given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs' with COBOLNET1504 before any per-function arm; and I confirmed the binder injects NO default argument for this function (the only injecting arm is BindNumvalCFamily), so the written arity survives to the renderer intact - which is precisely what makes the bracket nesting positional and correct. THE FALSE CLAIM: 'the 1-argument form [is pinned] by unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_DefaultArg3_IsExecutionYear'. It is not. That test (CobolDateWindowingTests.cs line 41) calls 'CobolDate.YearToYyyy(76)' - a direct C# call on the runtime API. It never compiles a COBOL one-argument reference and so exercises none of the grammar, the catalog arity, the binder's COBOLNET1504, or the renderer's arity-dependent emission. The one-argument SOURCE form has no test on any path, and per the REFUTED note on AR-15.100.3-3 it is in fact the broken form on the float carrier. The two-argument source form is likewise untested, and no negative fixture pins the COBOLNET1504 over- or under-arity rejection for this function. That is a test debt, not an implementation gap - rule 3 makes CONFORMS with a thin test-ref a legitimate outcome - so the verdict stands and the claim is struck. EDITIONS (rule 4): '2002,2014,2023' is NOT taken from IntrinsicCatalog's own 2002 field nor from ConstructRegistry.g.cs, both of which are the code under review. Annex E of the 2023 standard carries no §15.100 entry (it lists changes from 2014), and the value matches the landed sibling inventory rows FMT-15.23.2 / FMT-15.25.2 for the same Y2K trio.

notes: kb/Work PB324. A.1 item 10 -- 'ASSIGN clause, USING phrase (meaning and rules for operands; consistency rules). subject: CANCEL statement (result of canceling an active program when EC-PROGRAM-CANCEL-ACTIVE is not enabled)
CANCEL statement (result of canceling a non-COBOL program)
notes: §14.9.5.4 GR10's branch is UNREACHABLE from COBOL source in this implementation, so the row stays a GAP and this record deliberately carries NO test-ref. GR10's premise is a program the runtime system LOCATED per GR2 (§8.4.6/§8.4.6.3); ProgramTable.Cancel resolves every target with probe:false and returns on a null node, so CANCEL performs no locate step that could reach a sibling module and the named module's LANGUAGE is never consulted — a foreign module name and a nonexistent name take the byte-identical not-located path. No CALL-CONVENTION directive exists (§7.3.9), so a non-COBOL program cannot be declared either. A corpus golden therefore cannot exercise this determination: any such program's output is invariant under it. What is observable — GR3 re-initialization and GR7's never-called/not-located/already-canceled no-ops with its control-transfer sentence — is already pinned by conformance:2023/pb154_cancel_scope and conformance:2023/pb154_cancel_cascade and belongs to items 18/other GR rows, not to item 19. Closing item 19 needs an owner decision: re-file the row as an unreachable-branch determination, or add a harness that deploys a companion non-COBOL module and drives ProgramTable.Cancel directly (a unit: ref). || CLOSED 2026-09-04 ON AN OWNER-SIGNED DERIVATION. subject: Dynamic-length elementary items (maximum length)
notes: kb/Work PB463 LANDED - the A.1 item 62 determination is STATED and IMPLEMENTED. 8.5.1.10.1 makes the maximum size of a dynamic-length elementary item "the smallest of" three candidates and A.1 item 62 makes the third of them - "the maximum permitted by the implementor" - required AND documented; 13.18.19.4 GR2 makes it the whole answer when no LIMIT phrase is written. COBOL.NET provides 1,073,741,791 characters (0x3FFFFFDF) for every dynamic-length elementary item, alphanumeric or national: the CARRIER's own ceiling, since the item IS a native System.String whose maximum length is that value - the same "the carrier's headroom IS the implementor maximum" reading CobolDynTable<T>.MaxOccurrences already records for a dynamic-capacity table. A LIMIT phrase below it is the maximum size; one above it cannot raise the maximum and is REPORTED (COBOLNET2027, a warning - 13.18.19.3 bounds integer-1 only when a dynamic-length-structure-name is written too, SR4, so the entry is legal source). The second candidate never applies: the PREFIXED phrase rides a dynamic-length-structure-name, refused by COBOLNET1562. ONE producer computes it (CobolDynString.MaxSizeOf) and DataItem.DynMaxSize carries it, so the value cannot differ between the binder, the emitters and the runtime; DynamicLengthTests.ImplementorMaximum_IsTheNumberPublishedInConformanceSection7 reads the number back out of the section 7 row in both published spellings, so the determination and the constant cannot drift apart. Before this landing the item had no maximum at all and the section 7 register said only that a branch was unreachable - a determination about code nobody had checked, which is how a SET SIZE past 2**32 came to wrap to its low bits.
