notes: A.1 item 115 -- 'Line sequential character set. This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (14.9.30, READ statement, General rule 16, 9.1.13.2, Successful completion, I-O Status = 09; 14.9.35, REWRITE statement, General rule 17d; 14.9.51, WRITE statement General rule 23; and 9.1.13.10, Record with invalid content with unsuccessful completion, I-O Status = 71)'. The determination is made and documented (kb/Work PB329): the set is every character at code point U+0020 or above; the C0 controls U+0000-U+001F are outside it, the two line delimiters CR and LF and the tab HT among them; DEL and the Latin-1 supplement are inside, so an ordinary 8-bit text file reads without 09. The delimiters are FORCED out by 9.1.7.2's definition of a line sequential record's extent; the set cannot be only 'everything but the delimiters' because the reader consumes CR/LF as the framing and GR16's 09 would then be unreachable by construction; the remaining C0 controls are the stream/device repertoire, not text, and a line sequential file exists to be plain text. Surveyed, not assumed: GnuCOBOL's COB_LS_VALIDATE defaults to TRUE 'per COBOL 2022' and validates data read (status 09) and written (status 71) against the same below-SPACE boundary. ONE type carries the set for all four cross-referenced rules, so the READ and WRITE directions cannot disagree; the test is character-wise (national record areas two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE) rather than byte-wise. Pinned at all three editions the LINE SEQUENTIAL organization exists in. kb/Work PB688 (2026-09-05): ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL is a COBOL-2023 INTRODUCTION - the Foreword's list of the main changes this third edition makes over ISO/IEC 1989:2014 names "Line Sequential file organization", and 9.1.6 / 9.1.7.1 still name exactly three organizations with 9.1.7.2 splitting the sequential one into its record- and line-delimited types. subject: SET statement (value in NaN payload)
notes: DOCUMENTED (kb/Work PB452, 2026-09-09) IN THE SAME CHANGE SET AS THE GENERAL RULES IT RIDES. A.1 item 176 is a REQUIRED documentation obligation on 14.9.39.4 GR34 and GR35 - the NaN PAYLOAD a SET CONTENT OF ... TO FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER / FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-SIGNALING stores - and it had no row while the general rules themselves had no implementation at all; a required implementor-definition with no documentation row is not 'implemented'. The determination: payload ZERO for the quiet form and ONE for the signaling form, giving binary32 0x7FC00000 / 0x7F800001 and binary64 0x7FF8000000000000 / 0x7FF0000000000001, with the sign bit set from GR34/GR35's own SIGN phrase and positive when the phrase is absent. Zero is the canonical NaN every IEEE implementation produces; one is the smallest payload that keeps the significand nonzero once ISO/IEC 60559:2020 6.2.1's quiet bit is cleared, which a signaling NaN requires. 14.9.39.3 SR32 confines the receiver to a STANDARD floating-point usage and the two COBOL.NET provides are binary32 and binary64 EXACTLY, so the basic interchange format the rules name IS the carrier. The values are emitted as BIT PATTERNS through BitConverter, never as a CLR constant: double.NaN carries a SET sign bit, so the positive default would otherwise be spelled -double.NaN and depend on constant folding, and the CLR has no signaling-NaN constant at all because every managed arithmetic path quiets one. IeeeSpecials is one table serving as both the documented encoding and the emitted one, and IeeeSpecialsTests asserts the two agree by DECODING them rather than string-matching. The COBOL-observable witness can see that a NaN is unequal to itself but not which kind it is: the class condition that would expose the distinction (8.8.4.4's FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-QUIET / -SIGNALING) is kb/Work PB225 and unimplemented. kb/Work/PB961 (2026-09-22): RE-RECORDED ON THE STORED IMAGE. The prior CONFORMS rested on the emitted EXPRESSION (unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits), while the pipeline stored a binary32 signaling NaN as the QUIET 0x7FC00001 - the JIT carried the inline BitConverter constant as a double, and the binary32 image lane widened through double. The value now reaches the item through CobolFloat.FromBinary32Bits (opaque to the JIT) and CobolNum.FormatImageSingle/ParseImageSingle (no binary64), and a same-usage MOVE copies on the carrier (14.9.25.4 GR6 c)). Witness: conformance:2014/pb961_signaling_nan_binary32 reads 0x7F800001 = 2139095041 back through a BINARY-LONG UNSIGNED REDEFINES and asks GR3 k) of every copy; unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits follows the emitted text to the stored image in both byte orders. IeeeSpecials.Text is deleted (Bits is the one table; RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits spells it). docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-176 corrected in the same change set (the "cannot quiet the value" sentence was true of the expression and false of the pipeline). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/IeeeSpecials.cs#Text (IeeeSpecials.Text was deleted by kb/Work PB961 (the emitted expression is RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits over IeeeSpecials.Bits) and TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits was replaced by TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits, which asserts the stored image rather than the expression) retired-witness: unit:IeeeSpecialsTests.TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits (IeeeSpecials.Text was deleted by kb/Work PB961 (the emitted expression is RuntimeApi.FloatFromBits over IeeeSpecials.Bits) and TheEmittedExpression_EvaluatesToTheDocumentedBits was replaced by TheStoredImage_CarriesTheDocumentedBits, which asserts the stored image rather than the expression)

subject: SIGN clause (valid sign when SEPARATE CHARACTER phrase not present)
notes: DOCUMENTED (kb/Work PB803). The row states the valid sign set as a RULE over the program's convention rather than as a character list: at the sign position a plain digit 0-9 plus both tables of the selected convention, every other position a plain digit. It records the three things a user has to know and could not previously look up -- that a PLAIN DIGIT is valid and means positive (so a group MOVE of raw characters, and every positive value under the `ascii` convention, is well formed); that a punched character carries a DIGIT as well as a sign, so it fixes the value (`12{` is +120, and at the leading position `C23` is +323); and that the SEPARATE characters `+` and `-` are 13.18.52.4 GR6 b)'s and are NOT valid here. GR5 a) is documented alongside b) although it is not latitude, because it is what makes the width answer 3 and a reader looking up the sign set is exactly the reader who needs it. What a numeric operation makes of a character outside the set stays 14.6.13.2's obligation and is not filed here.

subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, code-name-1 (alphanumeric coded character set and collating sequence; ordinal
notes: A.1 item 183 - the code-name-1 coded character set and collating sequence, the ordinal number of characters, and the correspondence with the native alphanumeric character set (12.3.7.4 GR7 i). CONDITIONALLY REQUIRED 'because it is conditioned upon the existence of a code-name', and the condition became TRUE with owner decision kb/Work PB793, so the item is LIVE and the determination is written out in full at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7. ASCII: ISO/IEC 646 IRV, 128 ordinals, ordinal n = native character U+(n-1), the identity correspondence, the native collating positions. EBCDIC: IBM CCSID 37, 256 ordinals, ordinal n = the native character that page assigns to code unit n-1, the correspondence being the page itself and the collating position of a native character being its code unit in it; the 65,280 native characters the page does not spell are not members of the set and take the collating position 12.3.7.4 GR7 k3 gives an unspecified character. Surveyed rather than assumed (survey_compilers_on_latitude): CCSID 37 is the canonical registered complete single-byte EBCDIC page and the z/OS default; GnuCOBOL's own default table corresponds to no registered CCSID and its named alternates are CCSID 500 variants, so its LATITUDE is followed and its tables are not (they are GPL and are not read here). The whole table is DERIVED from Encoding.GetEncoding(37) at bind time, so nothing is transcribed and there is no 256-entry literal to drift.

subject: USAGE BINARY-CHAR, BINARY-SHORT, BINARY-LONG, BINARY-DOUBLE (allow wider range than minimum specified)
notes: OWNER DECISION Q30, 2026-09-09 (kb/Work PB592), verbatim: "provided, the native range." It REPLACES the premise this row previously closed on. The row carried DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT through the `a1-optional-not-provided` derived selector (kb/Work PB280 Q1) because docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 7 said "Not provided. Each usage holds exactly the GR12 minimum range for its width" - and that determination was FALSE for all four SIGNED usages. 13.18.60.4 GR12's printed table is ASYMMETRIC and the asymmetry is the whole content of the rule: every SIGNED row prints a STRICT '<' on BOTH sides (-128 [-2**7] < n < 128 [2**7]) while every UNSIGNED row prints '<=' on the left (0 <= n < 256 [2**8]) - re-rendered from the canonical PDF for this landing (printed page 507), independently of the reading the note inherited. So the minimum SIGNED band EXCLUDES -2**(w-1), which this compiler stores; 15.58.4's NOTE concedes the same thing from inside the standard ("BINARY-CHAR SIGNED | -128 (assuming an 8-bit twos-complement representation)"). The optional element of A.1 item 206 - "allow wider range than minimum specified" - is therefore PROVIDED, by exactly one value per signed usage, and A.1's preamble ("Documentation required: If the element is provided by the implementor, the implementor's user documentation shall document the element ...", cite.py --check A.1 OK) read with 4.2.5 (the conformance clause that governs the A.1 list, cite.py --check OK) makes documenting it an obligation rather than an option. NOTE the ground named here is 4.2.5, NOT 4.2.7: 4.2.7's own first sentence scopes it to A.4 (kb/Work PB593).
